findings.title: AO resolution uses seeing x (1 - Strehl), reporting 0.32 arcsec for Keck+AO at K where the asserted Strehl 0.6 implies 0.055 arcsec (6x-29x too coarse; flips the binary verdict)
findings.evidence: `const correctedSeeingArcsec = seeingArcsec * (1 - strehl);` then `combined = sqrt(diffractionLimit^2 + correctedSeeing^2)`, with `AO_STREHL_DEFAULT = 0.6` (line 6). Strehl is a peak-intensity ratio, not a seeing-reduction factor; an AO-corrected PSF is a near-diffraction-limited core plus a seeing halo, and its FWHM is at the diffraction limit once Strehl exceeds ~0.2. I recomputed for an 8-m at 500 nm: diffraction limit = 1.22 x 5e-5 cm / 800 cm x 206264.8 = 0.0157 arcsec. Model output with 1.0 arcsec seeing: Strehl 0.3 -> 0.700 arcsec, Strehl 0.6 -> 0.400 arcsec, Strehl 0.9 -> 0.101 arcsec. The real AO core is 0.016-0.024 arcsec at all three. At the default Strehl the model is 25x too coarse. The closure is uncited, and apps/demos/src/demos/telescope-resolution/index.html:94 labels the control only "Adaptive optics (AO)" with no caveat, and apps/site/src/content/demos/telescope-resolution.md never mentions Strehl.
findings.scenario: A student ticks "Adaptive optics" on an 8-m aperture at 500 nm in 1 arcsec seeing. The readout drops from 1.00 to 0.40 arcsec, so the student concludes AO buys a factor of 2.5 and that an 8-m with AO cannot resolve a 0.1 arcsec binary. Real AO at Strehl 0.6 delivers ~0.02 arcsec and resolves it with room to spare — a factor of 25 error in the exact capability the demo teaches.
findings.fix: The finding's direction is right but its fix has two gaps and one break it does not flag. Gaps: (a) it leaves apps/demos/src/demos/telescope-resolution/main.ts `drawPsf` drawing a single Gaussian of width `blurFwhmArcsec`, so the canvas would keep showing a wrong-width blob even after the readout is fixed; (b) returning only the core FWHM makes AO look like it always buys the full diffraction limit, which is the opposite error at low Strehl where contrast, not FWHM, is the limit - the halo fraction has to be reported alongside or the demo over-sells AO. Break it does not flag: changing `effectiveResolutionArcsec` from `number` to an object breaks main.ts:186-194, `resolutionStatusFromSeparationArcsec`, the Copy Results export and the test file; that is acceptable but must be done as one cutover, not an added wrapper. What I would apply: model the AO PSF as the two components the physics actually supports, I(theta) = S * Airy(theta; lambda, D) + (1 - S) * Gaussian(theta; FWHM = seeing), and use that same object for the readout, the verdict and the canvas - report `coreArcsec` (the diffraction limit) as the resolution whenever a core exists, with `haloArcsec` and the core light fraction exposed next to it so the halo is visible rather than implied. Also stop hard-coding S: a fixed 0.6 independent of lambda, D and r0 erases the fact that AO works far better in the IR, which is exactly what the Keck/near-IR activity is meant to teach - either expose Strehl as a control or derive it from Marechal with an approved wavefront-error/r0 closure. Per CLAUDE.md the Strehl closure, the core-existence threshold and the halo treatment are Anna's to approve before they become load-bearing, so the honest interim is to stop publishing a number the model cannot support: keep the AO toggle qualitative, state the closure and its validity in the demo's model-notes panel, in the site `model_notes` (content/demos/telescope-resolution.md) and in instructor model.md:79, and amend activities.md:53-63 so the lab no longer asks students to record the AO resolution as evidence. Finally, rewrite telescopeResolutionModel.test.ts:64-72 - that assertion pins the defect and must not be carried over green.
findings.note: CONFIRMED, not refuted. (1) Code exists verbatim: /Users/anna/Teaching/cosmic-playground/packages/physics/src/telescopeResolutionModel.ts:96 is `const correctedSeeingArcsec = seeingArcsec * (1 - strehl);`, fed into the quadrature at :97-100 with `Math.max(diffractionLimitArcsec, combined)` at :101; `AO_STREHL_DEFAULT = 0.6` at :6. (2) Independent recomputation (my own node run, not the finder's): theta_diff = 1.22*lambda/D*206264.806 arcsec. Keck preset, 10 m, its own default near-IR 2.2e-4 cm, "good" seeing 0.8": theta_diff = 0.0554", model theta_eff = sqrt(0.0554^2 + (0.8*0.4)^2) = 0.3248" -> 5.9x the core. 10 m at visible 5.5e-5 cm, "average" seeing 1.0": theta_diff = 0.0138", model theta_eff = 0.4002" -> 28.9x. Custom 8 m at 5.5e-5 cm, 1.0" seeing: 0.0173" vs 0.4004" -> 23.1x. Note a correction to the finder: 500 nm is NOT selectable (packages/data-telescopes/src/wavelengthBands.ts bands are 3e-5, 5.5e-5, 2.2e-4, 1e-3 cm and 21 cm), so the reachable visible case is 550 nm; the finder's 0.0157"/0.400" pair corresponds to 8 m at 500 nm, which I reproduce but which is not reachable. The error magnitude is 6x-29x depending on band, not a flat 25x. (3) The physics claim holds independently: by the Marechal relation S = exp(-sigma^2), S = 0.6 implies sigma = 0.715 rad = 0.114 waves RMS wavefront error, i.e. a well-corrected system whose PSF is unambiguously core-dominated with FWHM at the diffraction limit. The model therefore asserts a Strehl and then reports a FWHM 6-29x wider than that Strehl permits - internally inconsistent, independent of any external benchmark. (Sanity anchor: 0.055" at K on a 10 m is what Keck AO actually delivers, and the model reports 0.325" for exactly that configuration.) (4) Reachable and unguarded: apps/demos/src/demos/telescope-resolution/main.ts:186-189 calls the function live with `aoEnabled: state.includeAtmosphere && state.aoEnabled` and never passes `aoStrehl`, so the fixed 0.6 always applies (grep over the repo finds no other `aoStrehl` caller). The checkbox is at index.html:94-95, enabled whenever "Include atmosphere" is on (main.ts:395). Seeing slider 0.2-3.5", separation log slider 1e-3 to 1e3 arcsec, aperture log slider 0.007-1e7 m, so every configuration above is in range. The value drives the arcsec readout, the resolved/marginal/unresolved verdict (model.ts:112), the Gaussian blur FWHM drawn on the PSF canvas (main.ts drawPsf `blurFwhmArcsec`), and the Copy Results export row `thetaEffArcsec` (main.ts:455). Verdict inversion I recomputed: a 0.1" pair, 10 m, 550 nm, 1.0" seeing, AO on gives sep/eff = 0.250 -> "unresolved", where a Strehl-0.6 core (0.0138") gives ratio 7.2 -> "resolved". (5) Not already fixed: `git log -3` on the file returns only f26ad26 "feat(demo): migrate telescope-resolution instrument"; no guard, no Strehl caveat anywhere in the repo. The existing test at packages/physics/src/telescopeResolutionModel.test.ts:64-72 asserts eff > 0.35 and < 0.6 for S = 0.6 and 1.0" seeing, i.e. it PINS this closure rather than catching it - the repo's known "tests encode defects" pattern. (6) Severity kept at P0, with corrections to the finder's framing in both directions. Mitigators the finder omitted: apps/site/src/content/demos/telescope-resolution.md:6-11 carries `status: draft` and `readiness: experimental` with readinessReason "parity and launch-gate signoff are still pending", so the "Active development" callout and card badge are both showing and there is NO readiness-honesty violation here; its model_notes line does say "Atmosphere (toy model): ... AO reduces the seeing contribution in the demo"; the instructor clicker (instructor/telescope-resolution/assessment.md:77-88) scopes AO to "in the demo's story" and its correct answer is only the qualitative direction, which is right; and AO is not among the demo's stated learning_goals. Aggravator the finder missed, which outweighs those: the published lab protocol at apps/site/src/content/instructor/telescope-resolution/activities.md:53-63 instructs students to pick Keck, "turn on Adaptive Optics (AO) and compare", and then use "your recorded resolutions/status changes" as the Evidence line of a claim-evidence-reasoning paragraph. The wrong number is assigned coursework evidence, not an incidental readout, and a generic "toy model" label does not scope a 6-29x error or excuse a reversed resolved/unresolved verdict. That is a wrong number, a wrong verdict and a wrong drawing a student would believe -> P0 stands.

findings.title: stars-zams-hr shows a Z-blind Hurley main-sequence lifetime beside a Z-dependent ZAMS, so the lifetime readout is up to 2.3x too long (1.67x on the one-click Low-metallicity preset)
findings.evidence: `export const SOLAR_METALLICITY_ONLY = 0.02;` with `HURLEY_ZETA = 0` (line 32), so `mainSequenceLifetimeMyr` (line 59) is Z-independent. hrInferencePopulationModel.ts:227-229 routes L, R and Teff through the Z-dependent Tout fit, while :94 `mainSequenceLifetimeGyr` routes to this Z=0.02 relation; apps/demos/src/demos/stars-zams-hr/main.ts:325 and :924 display that lifetime, and index.html:153 gives Z a live input over [0.0001, 0.03]. I recomputed the model's own Tout luminosities: at 1 Msun, L(Z=0.02) = 0.6977 Lsun and L(Z=1e-4) = 1.586 Lsun, a factor 2.27. Since t_nuc ~ M/L, the metal-poor star's main-sequence lifetime should be ~0.44x, i.e. ~4.8 Gyr, not the 11.003 Gyr the model returns at both metallicities. The same inconsistency holds at 0.8 Msun (L ratio 2.37) and 2 Msun (1.75).
findings.scenario: A student in stars-zams-hr sets Z = 0.0001 to model a halo star. The main sequence visibly brightens (the model's own L more than doubles) while the lifetime readout stays at 11.0 Gyr. The student concludes a metal-poor solar-mass star lives as long as the Sun, when the same model's luminosity implies it lives less than half as long — and the error is in the quantity cluster ages are read from.
findings.fix:
The finder's option A is right and its option B is actively dangerous. Do not implement option B as written.

Why option B breaks things: returning NaN for Z != 0.02 does not fail safe, because neither call site tests finiteness. Traced line by line: `hrInferencePopulationModel.ts:257` `if (ageMyr < mainSequenceLifetimeMyr(massMsun))` is false for NaN, so every star falls through to `postMainSequenceTrack`; `stellarLifetimeModel.ts:357-358` `if (ageMyr < mainSequenceEnd) return null` is false for NaN too, so it continues; `:375-376` then computes `span = giantBranchStart - mainSequenceEnd` = NaN, `f` = NaN, and `:377-378` return NaN luminosity and temperature. At any Z but 0.02 the whole synthetic population would come out NaN and the CMD would silently empty — including on the default "Low metallicity" preset. That converts a factor-2 error into a blank teaching instrument.

What I would apply, in order:

(a) Immediate, no new physics closure and therefore no scientific approval needed. Change the signature to `mainSequenceLifetimeMyr({ massMsun, metallicityZ })`, but add the `Number.isFinite` guards at `hrInferencePopulationModel.ts:257` and `stellarLifetimeModel.ts:357` FIRST, before any out-of-domain return value can reach them. Then, for Z != 0.02, stop asserting a number: suppress the `#evolveMsLifetime` readout and replace it with "lifetime model is solar-metallicity only — set Z = 0.02 to read a lifetime", or keep rendering it explicitly labelled "at Z = 0.02" and drop the three-decimal format at `main.ts:930`, which projects a precision the relation does not have even at Z = 0.02. Also unpin the evolve time axis: `main.ts:326` `endT = 1.2 * tMs` currently scales the x-extent with a Z-blind clock while the track's L, R and T move with Z.

(b) The real fix, which is Anna's to approve because it changes a physics closure: carry Hurley et al. (2000) Appendix-A zeta polynomials for a1-a10 so t_MS tracks Z. Note the structure is already half-present and deliberately disabled — `stellarLifetimeModel.ts:35` computes `HURLEY_X` from the eq. (5) zeta term with `HURLEY_ZETA` hard-coded to 0, giving 0.95 - 0.03*(0 + 0.30103) = 0.9410, which the `Math.max` floor pins to 0.95. At Z = 1e-4, zeta = log10(0.005) = -2.301 and that same expression gives 1.0100, which the `Math.min` ceiling puts at 0.99. So one of the Z dependencies is already written and zeroed out. Gate the result against the existing `stellarStartraxParity.test.ts` fixture at more than one Z, not just at 0.02.

(c) Either way, delete `SOLAR_METALLICITY_ONLY` or make something actually consume it. An exported constant that names a validity limit which no code enforces and no reader ever sees is worse than no constant, because it makes the limit look handled during review — which is plausibly how this shipped.

Do not leave a Z slider, a one-click metal-poor preset, and a Z-blind clock on the same screen.
findings.note:
CONFIRMED on every point, and reachability is worse than the finder claimed. I could not refute it.

1. Code exists verbatim. `packages/physics/src/stellarLifetimeModel.ts:23` is `export const SOLAR_METALLICITY_ONLY = 0.02;`, `:32` is `const HURLEY_ZETA = 0;`, and `mainSequenceLifetimeMyr(massMsun: number)` at `:58` takes mass only. `hrInferencePopulationModel.ts:226-229` (`msProperties`) routes L, R and Teff through `ZamsTout1996Model.*FromMassMetallicity`, while `:94-96` `mainSequenceLifetimeGyr` wraps the Z-blind relation. `apps/demos/src/demos/stars-zams-hr/main.ts:325` and `:924` consume it; `:930` prints it to three decimals. `index.html:152-153` gives Z `min="0.0001" max="0.03"`, and `main.ts:1133-1138` clamps to `ZamsTout1996Model.CONSTANTS.metallicityMin` = 1e-4, so Z = 0.0001 is reachable.

2. Independent recomputation (my own JS re-implementation of the stored Tout and Hurley coefficients, not the finder's arithmetic). At 1 Msun: L(Z=0.02) = 0.6977 Lsun, L(Z=1e-4) = 1.5863 Lsun, ratio 2.274. tMS(1 Msun) = 11003.13 Myr = 11.003 Gyr, identical at every Z. With t_nuc ~ M/L that implies 4.84 Gyr at Z=1e-4 against the 11.003 Gyr displayed. Ratios at 0.8 and 2 Msun are 2.375 and 1.752. Allowing for the metal-poor star's larger hydrogen fraction (X = 0.700 at Z=0.02 vs 0.760 at Z=1e-4, 8.6 percent more fuel) the net error is still 2.09x, i.e. a true lifetime near 5.3 Gyr. Every number the finder quoted reproduces.

3. Reachability is stronger than claimed. The Z input (`index.html:152`) and the "Main-sequence lifetime estimate" readout (`index.html:248`) are inside the SAME `<details id="experimentControls">` block (`index.html:105-253`), so they are on screen together — the brightening main sequence and the frozen clock are simultaneously visible. No typing is even needed: the "Low metallicity" preset chip (`index.html:120`, `logic.ts:279-283`) sets Z = 0.004 in one click, where I compute the lifetime still 1.67x too long at 1 Msun (6.59 Gyr implied vs 11.003 shown). `buildEvolutionTrack` (`main.ts:311-326`) uses `state.metallicityZ` for L, R and T but pins the time axis to the Z-blind `tMs` via `endT = 1.2 * tMs`, so the track's shape and its clock disagree.

4. The turnoff claim holds. Cluster mode is the default (`index.html:158` checkbox `checked`; `main.ts:452-455` passes `modeCluster`, `clusterAge`, `metallicityZ`), and `hrInferencePopulationModel.ts:257` gates stage on the Z-blind lifetime. Solving tMS(M) = age myself: the model's turnoff mass is 0.978 Msun at 12 Gyr, 1.271 Msun at 4.6 Gyr and 2.392 Msun at 0.7 Gyr — the same at every Z, while the plotted turnoff luminosity at 12 Gyr moves 0.626 -> 1.050 -> 1.432 Lsun across Z = 0.02, 0.004, 1e-4. Real isochrones put a 12 Gyr, Z=1e-4 turnoff near 0.8 Msun, not 0.98.

5. Pedagogically aggravated. `apps/site/src/content/demos/stars-zams-hr.md:23` lists "Metallicity only changes spectral lines and not bulk stellar structure" as a misconception the demo exists to correct, and `:19` makes "Connect mass-dependent lifetimes to conceptual stellar-evolution tracks" a learning goal. The demo invites exactly the manipulation that exposes its own inconsistency.

6. Not fixed, not guarded. `git log -3` on all three files shows no related commit (latest touching the physics is e61f76f "Fix the stars-zams-hr colour relation and layout"). `SOLAR_METALLICITY_ONLY` is exported at `:23` and re-exported at `:450` but read by NO caller — I grepped every .ts/.astro/.html outside node_modules and the only hits are its own definition, its doc comment and the export object. The named limit is dead code, not a guard, and no reader-visible text in the demo or its model notes discloses it.

7. One finder scope claim I tried to extend and had to retract: `starClusterModel.ts:186,190,217` has the same Z-dependent-ZAMS/Z-blind-lifetime shape, and cluster-census has a live [Fe/H] slider over [-2.00, +0.50] dex. But cluster-census never passes `metallicityZ` (grep for it in that demo returns nothing), so `starClusterModel.ts:157` keeps the 0.02 default and the [Fe/H] slider only feeds `highMassSlopeFromEnvironment` (the IMF slope). cluster-census is internally consistent at Z = 0.02. The defect is confined to stars-zams-hr, exactly as scoped.

8. Severity. P0 stands under this audit's definition: a wrong displayed number, to three decimals, in a live and one-click-reachable path. The only moderating fact is that `stars-zams-hr.md:3,10-11` is honestly labeled `status: draft`, `readiness: experimental`, "classroom parity and launch-gate QA remain in progress" — so this is NOT additionally a readiness-honesty violation. But that badge warns about QA, not about the physics being wrong, and a student reading "11.003 Gyr" still believes it.

findings.title: eos-lab scaling-detective insight copy is double-escaped, printing literal `—` / `⇒` to the reader
findings.evidence: Source byte-for-byte (verified with `sed -n '530p' | cat -v`): `insight: "$P_{\\rm gas} \\propto T^1$ \\u2014 linear scaling. Double $T$ \\u21D2 double $P$."`. In a double-quoted JS string `\\u2014` is the six characters backslash-u-2-0-1-4, not an em dash. Traced the render path: main.ts:1117 sets `feedbackEl.innerHTML = `${ch.insight}`` then calls `renderMath(feedbackEl)` on line 1118; renderMath (packages/runtime/src/math.ts:28) typesets only `$...$`, `$$...$$`, `\\[...\\]`, `\\(...\\)` delimited spans and leaves all other text untouched. Same defect at logic.ts:543 and :556, five occurrences total.
findings.scenario: A student opens eos-lab, answers "x2" to "Double T. By what factor does P_gas change?" correctly, and the green feedback reads: the KaTeX for P_gas ∝ T^1, then the literal string "— linear scaling. Double T ⇒ double P." The pedagogical payoff line of the activity is visible source-code escape garbage.
findings.fix:
Two edits per line in apps/demos/src/demos/eos-lab/logic.ts (lines 530, 543, 556), treating the em dash and the implication operator differently because CLAUDE.md's KaTeX rule covers operators, not punctuation:

1. Em dash — delete one backslash so the escape actually resolves, matching the established house idiom at cluster-census/logic.ts:314 (`"M\u2609"`, single backslash). This keeps the literal glyph out of the source text, which is why the idiom exists.
2. `\u21D2` — do not just unescape it. `⇒` is a reader-visible operator, so per CLAUDE.md it belongs inside math: `$\\Rightarrow$`.

Resulting lines:

  insight: "$P_{\\rm gas} \\propto T^1$ \u2014 linear scaling. Double $T$ $\\Rightarrow$ double $P$.",
  insight: "$P_{\\rm rad} \\propto T^4$ \u2014 explosive! Double $T$ $\\Rightarrow$ $2^4 = 16\\times P$.",
  insight: "$P_{\\rm deg} \\propto \\rho^{5/3}$ \u2014 steeper than linear. $2^{5/3} \\approx 3.17$.",

(In the file those are one backslash before `u2014` and two before `Rightarrow`.) Do not use `---`: the string reaches the DOM via `innerHTML` at main.ts:1117 with no Markdown pass, so it would render as three hyphens. `—` is an acceptable alternative to `\u2014` since the same innerHTML path decodes entities.

Two related items worth separate tickets, not folded into this one:
- main.ts:1123 `Next \u2192` uses a single backslash in a template literal, so it emits a real `→` into reader-visible text. That is the same class of Unicode-glyph question the KaTeX rule is about, and the validator misses it because the source holds an escape rather than a glyph.
- scripts/validate-math-formatting.mjs cannot see either defect: its regex scans for literal glyphs in source, and the repo has an established idiom for writing glyphs as `\uXXXX` escapes specifically to get past it. That is the architecture finding behind this bug — the validator checks source bytes, not rendered output, so both the escaped-glyph bypass and the double-escaped-garbage failure are invisible to it. Worth a P1 on its own if the gate is meant to be trusted.

Severity P2 rather than P0: physics and numbers are correct (I recomputed 2, 16, 3.1748), the page functions, and the demo is `unlisted: true` / `readiness: experimental` / `status: draft`, so it is filtered out of the catalogue by catalog.ts:26 and reachable only by direct link. This rises to P1 the moment eos-lab is listed or promoted, since it would then be visible broken copy in the pedagogical payoff line of a public activity — fix it before any promotion.
findings.note:
CONFIRMED on every technical claim, with a severity correction and a broken proposed fix. 1. Source exists as quoted. `od -c` on apps/demos/src/demos/eos-lab/logic.ts:530 shows the bytes `$ P _ { \ \ r m g a s } \ \ p r o p t o T ^ 1 $ \ \ u 2 0 1 4 l i n e a r ...` — two literal backslashes then `u2014`. Same at :543 and :556. Escape-sequence count: :530 has `\\u2014` + `\\u21D2` (2), :543 has `\\u2014` + `\\u21D2` (2), :556 has `\\u2014` (1) = 5 total, as claimed. 2. Independently recomputed the runtime value with `node -e` (my own string literal, not the finder's arithmetic): `[...tail].map(c=>c.codePointAt(0).toString(16))` over the characters following the first math span returns `5c 75 32 30 31 34 20 6c` = `\`, `u`, `2`, `0`, `1`, `4`, space, `l`. `s1.includes("—")` (real em dash, U+2014) is **false**. So the reader sees six literal characters, not a dash. The `\\` in TS collapses to one backslash and `u2014` stays plain text — correct diagnosis. 3. Render path traced line by line. main.ts:1117 `feedbackEl.innerHTML = \`${ch.insight}\``, then :1118 `renderMath(feedbackEl)`. packages/runtime/src/math.ts:27-40 calls KaTeX `renderMathInElement` with only `$$`,`$`,`\[`,`\(` delimiters; text outside them is untouched, and `\u` is not a delimiter. I counted the `$` on each line (6, 6, 4) — all pair correctly, so the escapes land in plain text nodes between typeset spans. Confirmed. 4. Live but not discoverable. The markup exists (index.html:407 `
`, :411 `#scalingChallenge`), main.ts:1147-1150 renders it lazily on accordion toggle, and the demo is built to apps/site/public/play/eos-lab/index.html. **But** apps/site/src/content/demos/eos-lab.md sets `unlisted: true`, `readiness: experimental`, `status: draft`, with unlistedReason "On hold. The equation of state is incomplete". catalog.ts:26 `demos.filter((entry) => !entry.data.unlisted)` removes it from the catalogue; catalog.ts:23 notes exhibit/station/play pages survive only so shared links work. A student browsing the site cannot find it — the finding's "A student opens eos-lab" overstates exposure. 5. Not fixed. `git log -5 -- .../eos-lab/logic.ts` top commit is 19baaf9; the broken bytes are present in the working tree now. Repo-wide `rg '\\\\u[0-9A-Fa-f]{4}'` over apps/demos/src, apps/site/src, packages/runtime/src returns only these 3 lines in production code (other hits are test files where the literal is intentional). 6. Physics is correct, so this is cosmetic, not content-wrong. Recomputed each asserted ratio myself (dimensionless pressure ratios): 2^1 = 2, 2^4 = 16, 2^(5/3) = 3.174802 → "3.17". All three insight strings state the right scaling and the right number. Nothing a student would believe is wrong; only the connective punctuation is garbage. No wrong drawing, no broken page. P0 does not apply. 7. Root cause found, and it matters for the fix. The repo's own idiom is a SINGLE-backslash escape to keep a glyph out of the source text: cluster-census/logic.ts:314 `export const MSUN_SYMBOL = "M☉";` (od confirms one backslash), and cluster-census/design-contracts.test.ts:358-359 asserts that form. eos-lab copied the idiom but doubled the backslash, matching the adjacent LaTeX `\\rm` / `\\propto` on the same line. One-character-per-site defect. 8. The proposed fix is wrong twice. (a) `--- linear scaling` goes through `innerHTML` with no Markdown processing, so it renders as three literal hyphens — garbage swapped for different garbage. (b) The claim that a literal em dash is "forbidden by the same rule" is false: scripts/validate-math-formatting.mjs:33 `FORBIDDEN_UNICODE_MATH` is `/[°☉µμ′″×−∝≈∞ (Greek) (sub/superscripts)]/u` — it contains U+2212 minus but **not** U+2014 em dash and **not** U+21D2. An em dash is punctuation, outside CLAUDE.md's "equation, symbol, unit and operator" scope; `⇒` is an operator and does belong in math.

findings.title: Five topic tokens keep dark-ground values on the paper layer, so 6 of 20 station-card titles render at 1.37-1.67:1 on white, and the paper contrast test only checks four unrelated tokens
findings.evidence: `.station-card__title { font-size: var(--cp-text-md); color: var(--topic-color, var(--cp-text)); }` with `--topic-color` set per card at line 52 from topicColor(). Layout.astro:31-33 forces `data-theme="paper"` for any path containing /stations/, and layer-paper.css redefines --cp-accent, --cp-pink, --cp-violet, --cp-accent-ice and --cp-accent-amber but not one --cp-topic-* or --cp-celestial-* token. Recomputed WCAG ratios myself against the paper card ground (.cp-card on paper = var(--cp-bg1) = #ffffff): Telescopes #8BE9FD 1.38:1, DataInference #50FA7B 1.37:1, Stars var(--cp-celestial-sun) #fbbf24 1.67:1. findings.scenario: An instructor opens /stations/ to print the station sheets for lab. Six of the twenty cards show a pale-yellow or mint title on white: 'Telescope Resolution', 'Stars on the HR Diagram', 'Cluster Census', 'EOS Lab', 'Hydrostatic Equilibrium', 'Parallax Distance' are unreadable on screen and vanish entirely on a monochrome laser printer.
findings.fix:

Same defect: eos-lab tempSlider/rhoSlider/xSlider/ySlider/compareT/compareRho/compareX/compareY (8 sliders, all min=0 max=1000), telescope-resolution #aperture and #separation, binary-orbits #separation (logSliderToValue at main.ts:1883), keplers-laws #timelineScrub (main.ts:730 divides by 1000). 14 sliders total.
findings.scenario: A blind student on /play/angular-size/ tabs to the distance slider. NVDA says 'Distance d, slider, 500'. The visible readout says 1.00e8 km. They press Right Arrow; it says '501'. The physical distance just changed by 5.7%, the angular size changed with it, and no announced number anywhere corresponds to a physical quantity. The student cannot do the assignment, and any value they report from the demo is wrong.
findings.fix:
Two defects in the proposed fix.

(1) Wrong insertion points. The finder says to set it "at main.ts:741 and the input handler at 957". The input handler at 957-971 ends with `render()`, and render() is where both the slider sync (741) and the readout write (747) live. One assignment in render(), immediately beside line 747 where distanceValue.textContent is written, covers input, presets, unit-selector changes and programmatic updates. Adding it in the handler as well is redundant and duplicates the format call (the repo's DRY rule); adding it ONLY in the handler would miss preset-driven changes, which is the more likely error.

So, in render() next to main.ts:747:
  distanceSlider.setAttribute("aria-valuetext", `${distSliderFmt.text} ${distSliderFmt.unit}`);
  diameterSlider.setAttribute("aria-valuetext", `${diamSliderFmt.text} ${diamSliderFmt.unit}`);
reusing the already-computed formatDistanceAuto/formatDiameterAuto results so the announced string cannot drift from the visible one.

(2) The test predicate "every range input whose max is 1000" is wrong in both directions. It misses real index sliders that are not max=1000 — keplers-laws #ecc (max=990), #massSlider (idx/100), cluster-census #slopeSlider (150-300), #fehSlider (-200..50), #meclSlider (200..600), conservation-laws #massSlider/#r0Slider (min=-1 max=1 log exponents) — and it would falsely demand aria-valuetext on a future slider that is genuinely linear in physical units over 0-1000. Assert instead, in apps/site/tests/accessibility.spec.ts (which already iterates every content-backed slug via demoSlugsFromContent()), that for every `input[type="range"]` inside `.cp-layer-instrument`, aria-valuetext is present and non-empty and does not equal the element's own `value`. That catches all 18 without encoding the 1000 coincidence.

(3) Add the shared helper as suggested — `setSliderValueText(el, text)` in packages/runtime next to setLiveRegionText (packages/runtime/src/liveRegion.ts:1) — and apply it to all 18: angular-size #distanceSlider/#diameterSlider, blackbody-radiation #tempSlider, eos-lab #tempSlider/#rhoSlider/#xSlider/#ySlider/#compareT/#compareRho/#compareX/#compareY, telescope-resolution #aperture/#separation, binary-orbits #separation, keplers-laws #aAu/#ecc/#massSlider/#timelineScrub.

(4) Additionally, move each readout out of the wrapping `<label>` (or point the label at the control with `for=` and bind the readout via aria-describedby). Leaving a live-updating value inside the label subtree makes the accessible NAME change as the user drags, which is its own ARIA defect and will make the aria-valuetext announcement redundant.

Since angular-size's readinessReason already names "announcing results to screen readers" as outstanding, that line should be updated in the same change once the sliders are fixed, so the public claim tracks the evidence.

findings.title: The Balmer limit is authored as 364.6 nm (air) in four places while the model computes and prints 364.70 nm (vacuum), with no site naming its medium
findings.evidence:
index.html:351: `
  • The Balmer series limit (364.6 nm) is where Balmer lines pile up and merge into the continuum.
    • `. main.ts:712: `microscopeCtx.fillText(`${SpectralLineModel.seriesName({ nLower })} limit ${limitNm.toFixed(1)} nm`, ...)` with `limitNm = SpectralLineModel.seriesLimitNm({ nLower })` (main.ts:645). I recomputed the model: spectralLineModel.ts:291-296 returns HC_EV_NM / (RYDBERG_EV / n^2) = 1239.842 / (13.598434599 / 4) = 364.701 nm, printed via toFixed(1) as "364.7 nm". 364.6 nm is the AIR value; the model is explicitly vacuum (spectralLineModel.ts:12-15). Delta = 0.1 nm. docs/reviews/spectral-lines.md lists this as SL-4, severity P2, status open; the demo's frontmatter says content_verified: true, readiness: candidate, status: beta.
findings.scenario: A student opens /play/spectral-lines/, selects the Balmer series, reads "The Balmer series limit (364.6 nm)" in the explanatory list, then looks at the series-limit microscope directly beside it and reads "Balmer limit 364.7 nm". Two different numbers for the same physical quantity on one screen. No gate or test can see it: the prose is static HTML and the other value is painted into a 2-D canvas, so neither validate-math-formatting, the design-contract string tests, nor any e2e assertion compares them.
findings.fix:
The defect is an unstated medium, not a wrong digit — so name the medium everywhere and keep the number static, which avoids both the second formatting site and the post-KaTeX injection problem. 1. `apps/demos/src/demos/spectral-lines/index.html:351` — keep it authored, add the medium and reconcile with the model's value: `
  • The Balmer series limit ($364.70\ \text{nm}$ in vacuum; the $364.6\ \text{nm}$ air value usually quoted in textbooks) is where Balmer lines pile up and merge into the continuum.
    • `. Static LaTeX, typeset by the existing `renderMath()` pass, no runtime injection, no second `toFixed`. 2. `apps/demos/src/demos/spectral-lines/main.ts:712` — make the canvas label state its medium so the two agree in kind as well as digits: `... limit ${limitNm.toFixed(1)} nm (vac)`. Canvas 2-D text is the project's ASCII exemption, so "vac" is correct there. 3. `apps/site/src/content/instructor/spectral-lines/model.md:59` — change to `$364.70\ \text{nm}$ (vacuum)`. This is the higher-impact edit: it is what an adopting instructor reads aloud while the microscope on screen shows 364.7. 4. `docs/specs/spectral-lines-spec.md:275` — make the benchmark medium-explicit and tighten it to what the model actually guarantees: "Balmer limit (n=inf->2), vacuum: lambda = 364.70 nm +/- 0.05 nm". Also fix the range at spec:100 to 364.70-656.46 nm (vacuum) so the spec stops licensing the air value for a vacuum model. 5. Gate — one assertion, not a new apparatus. Add to the demo's existing `apps/demos/src/demos/spectral-lines/design-contracts.test.ts` a single test that reads index.html as a string and asserts it contains the exact substring `SpectralLineModel.seriesLimitNm({ nLower: 2 }).toFixed(2)`, i.e. "364.70". That is the smallest decisive test: it fails the moment either the constants or the prose drift, it reuses the per-demo contract-test file the project already runs, and it needs no generic constant-differ. Do NOT build the "diff every authored constant against the model" gate from the original proposal — nothing links a prose digit to a model call, and CLAUDE.md requires a measured need before that kind of apparatus. 6. After 1-5 land, mark SL-4 closed in `docs/reviews/spectral-lines.md:14` and drop "one wavelength value" from `readinessReason` in `apps/site/src/content/demos/spectral-lines.md`. Separately worth Anna's decision, since it is the larger version of this same medium problem and is not this finding: the element catalogues in `spectralLineModel.ts` are laboratory AIR wavelengths (header, lines 14-16) while hydrogen is vacuum, so the demo already draws air and vacuum lines on one spectrum ~0.03% apart with no medium shown in the UI.
findings.note:
The core factual claim reproduces, but the P0 grade and two of the finding's supporting claims do not. VERIFIED (code read + independent recomputation): 1. `apps/demos/src/demos/spectral-lines/index.html:351` contains verbatim: `
  • The Balmer series limit (364.6 nm) is where Balmer lines pile up and merge into the continuum.
    • ` 2. `apps/demos/src/demos/spectral-lines/main.ts:712` is exactly as quoted: `microscopeCtx.fillText(\`${SpectralLineModel.seriesName({ nLower })} limit ${limitNm.toFixed(1)} nm\`, margin.left, height - 8)`, with `limitNm` from `seriesLimitNm({ nLower })` at main.ts:645. 3. I recomputed the model myself, not reusing the finder's arithmetic. `spectralLineModel.ts:291-296` returns `HC_EV_NM / (RYDBERG_EV / n^2)`; constants at spectralLineModel.ts:34 (`RYDBERG_EV = 13.598434599`) and :40 (`HC_EV_NM = 1239.842`). `node -e`: E_limit = 13.598434599/4 = 3.39960864975 eV; lambda = 1239.842/3.39960864975 = 364.7013899941616 nm, `toFixed(1)` -> "364.7". Cross-check with CODATA hc = 1239.8419843320026 eV*nm gives 364.7014 nm. Model header spectralLineModel.ts:11-16 does state Bohr-model transitions are VACUUM. 4. `SERIES_NAMES[2] = "Balmer"` (spectralLineModel.ts:53), and the microscope defaults to Balmer: `activeHydrogenSeriesForMicroscope()` (main.ts:226-232) returns `state.nLower` when `seriesFilter === "all"`, and state defaults are `nLower: 2`, `seriesFilter: "all"` (main.ts:158-161). So the canvas does print "Balmer limit 364.7 nm" on first load. 5. The gate claim holds: `packages/physics/src/spectralLineModel.test.ts:54-56` pins the model side (`expect(Math.abs(lambda - 364.7014)).toBeLessThan(TOL_NM)`), but nothing compares the authored prose string to it. `apps/demos/src/demos/spectral-lines/logic.test.ts:274` uses `minNm: 364.6` only as a bin fixture, not as a claim. REFUTED SUB-CLAIMS: A. "adjacent", "on one screen", "directly beside it" is wrong. The prose is inside `#panel-understand`, which carries `hidden` (index.html:295) and requires clicking the "Understand" stage tab (index.html:254-255). The canvas is inside `
    ` (index.html:536) with NO `open` attribute, in the drawer below the stage — the adjacent comment at index.html:534-536 says opening it adds 981px. Both values are reachable, but only after two separate deliberate disclosures, roughly 1000px apart in a scrolling page, never in one viewport. B. "364.6 nm is the AIR value; the model is explicitly vacuum... Delta = 0.1 nm" is right about provenance but the finding treats 364.6 as a defect-grade wrong number. It is not wrong. I computed the air value: 364.7014 / 1.00028 = 364.599 nm (n_air ~ 1.00028-1.00030 near 365 nm), so 364.6 nm is the correct, textbook-standard air value (3646 A). The delta is 0.027%, in the last displayed digit. C. The finding's aggravating framing from `content_verified: true` is undercut by the rest of that frontmatter: `apps/site/src/content/demos/spectral-lines.md` has `status: beta`, `readiness: candidate`, and `readinessReason: "Close to ready. Still to come: one wavelength value, the data attribution, and a remaining review item."` — "one wavelength value" is this item. The public readiness claim does not outrun the evidence, so this is not a readiness-honesty finding. OMITTED BY THE FINDING (widens scope, lowers severity): the same `364.6` literal is authored in three more places, and the project contract tolerates both values. `docs/specs/spectral-lines-spec.md:275` sets the benchmark as "Balmer limit (n=inf->2): lambda = 364.6 nm +/- 0.2 nm" — that window contains 364.7014, so no spec contract is breached. Also `docs/specs/spectral-lines-spec.md:100` ("364.6-656.3 nm") and, more consequentially, `apps/site/src/content/instructor/spectral-lines/model.md:59` ("Use the series microscope to show line pile-up toward $364.6\ \text{nm}$") — that instructs an adopting instructor to narrate 364.6 while the microscope they were just told to open prints 364.7. NOT ALREADY FIXED: `git log -3` on index.html gives e49ef06, f5bdb98, 8c87477, none touching this line; no guard exists. `docs/reviews/spectral-lines.md:14` tracks it as SL-4, P2, open (its cited `index.html:395` is stale; the line is now 351). SEVERITY: P2, not P0. Per the audit's own rubric, P0 requires a wrong number, wrong drawing, or broken page that a student would believe. 364.6 nm is a correct value in air, the demo's own spec tolerance admits both, no drawing or calculation is wrong, nothing is broken, and the gap is 0.027% behind two closed disclosures on a demo publicly labelled beta/candidate with this exact item disclosed. P2 matches the grade the project's own review already assigned. PROPOSED FIX IS PARTLY BROKEN. (i) Injecting the number at render time into `#panel-understand` creates a SECOND independent formatting site: main.ts:712 uses `toFixed(1)`, so unless the prose pins the identical precision the contradiction returns as 364.7 vs 364.70. That is a DRY violation under this repo's own single-source rule, not a fix for one. (ii) Worse, that card's math is authored LaTeX typeset by the demo's `renderMath()` pass at load; a number written into the DOM by JS after that pass lands as plain text, so a KaTeX-conventional `$364.70\ \text{nm}$` injected there renders as literal dollar signs. The finder's fix introduces a rendered-math defect while closing a 0.1 nm one. (iii) It leaves the three other authored sites, including the instructor page, still saying 364.6. (iv) Its second half — a gate that diffs "any remaining authored constant" against the model — is not implementable as stated (nothing links a prose digit to a particular model call) and is exactly the broad validation apparatus CLAUDE.md requires a measured need for.

findings.title: stars-zams-hr duplicates stellar evolution inline in main.ts: the overlaid track starts 28% below its own ZAMS and lands a 2 Msun giant 1.9 dex from where the same demo plots its population's giants
findings.evidence: main.ts:311 `function buildEvolutionTrack(massMsun: number): TrackPoint[]` takes msL from ZamsTout1996Model.luminosityLsunFromMassMetallicity, then at main.ts:333 computes `const luminosityLsun = msL * (0.72 + 0.85 * fraction);` and at :334 `const teffK = msT * (0.98 - 0.06 * fraction);`. At fraction = 0 (t = 0, the zero-age main sequence by definition) this gives L = 0.72 * L_ZAMS, i.e. 1 - 0.72 = 0.28, exactly 28% below the L the population scatter on the same axes was drawn from. The coefficients 0.72, 0.85, 0.98, 0.06 appear nowhere in packages/physics and have no cited source. CLAUDE.md and .agents/references/invariants.md both state "All physics models MUST come from @cosmic/physics — no inline equations in demo code"; I grepped scripts/validate-invariants.mjs and there is no rule of any kind for inline physics.
findings.scenario: A student picks 1 Msun in the Evolve panel and drags the time slider to t = 0. The marker appears visibly below the main-sequence band the demo just plotted for the same mass and metallicity, so the demo teaches that a zero-age star does not start on the zero-age main sequence. docs/reviews/stars-zams-hr.md records this as HR-4, open, and its own recommendation says to fix it before promoting past experimental — yet the frontmatter says content_verified: true. Nothing can catch it: validate-physics-models.mjs only checks that packages/physics/src/*Model.ts files have a sibling test and an index export, so a 118-line stellar-evolution model living in demo code is invisible to it.
findings.fix:
The finder's fix would re-create the defect: it proposes adding a NEW post-MS model to packages/physics, but one already exists — `postMainSequenceTrack` at packages/physics/src/stellarLifetimeModel.ts:348, which the population already consumes via hrInferencePopulationModel.ts:265. Adding a second would duplicate it again (DRY) and leave the 1.9 dex divergence in place.

What I would apply instead:

1. Delete the post-MS branches of buildEvolutionTrack (main.ts:339-425) and sample `postMainSequenceTrack` at the same ages, so the overlaid track and the plotted stars are the same model by construction, not by a coefficient someone keeps in sync. Note `postMainSequenceTrack` takes ageMyr and returns null on the MS and null for M >= 8 Msun past the end (neutron star / black hole), so the drawing code must branch on null rather than plot the inline 2e-5 R_sun placeholder (main.ts:410).

2. For the MS segment, the honest minimal fix is L(t) = L_ZAMS, T(t) = T_ZAMS for 0 <= t < t_MS, matching what the population does for MS stars. That makes L(t=0) = L_ZAMS by construction and introduces no new coefficient. DO NOT transplant 0.72/0.85/0.98/0.06 into packages/physics: they are unsourced, and they also misplace the present-day Sun — at 1 Msun, t = 4.6 Gyr, fraction = 0.46 gives L = 0.775 L_sun, 22% low against the 1.0 L_sun a student knows. If MS brightening is wanted pedagogically so the turnoff has a hook, that is a new closure with new coefficients: per CLAUDE.md it must be proposed with its physical motivation and approved by Anna before it lands, not chosen by an agent.

3. Test: do not assert `===` on floats as proposed. Assert L(t=0) equals ZamsTout1996Model.luminosityLsunFromMassMetallicity to within rounding tolerance, AND — the assertion that would have caught the bigger half — that for the same mass, metallicity and age the track point agrees with stageProperties/generatePopulation within tolerance, swept over all six EVOLVE_MASSES_MSUN and at least one post-MS age each. A test pinning only t = 0 lets the 1.87 dex giant-branch divergence through.

4. Gate: the proposed rule ("flag numeric-literal-bearing arithmetic on physics quantities inside main.ts") is too broad to ship — main.ts is full of legitimate literal arithmetic for pixels (margin at :487, `ctx.arc(x, y, isSelected ? 7.8 : 6, ...)` at :655, tick arrays at :511-512), so it would be mostly false positives, and CLAUDE.md forbids broad validation apparatus without a measured need. Use a unit-suffix rule instead: in scripts/validate-invariants.mjs, flag any assignment in apps/demos/src/demos/**/*.ts to an identifier ending in a physics unit (`*Lsun`, `*Rsun`, `*Msun`, `*K`, `*Gyr`, `*Myr`, `*Pc`) whose right-hand side is arithmetic rather than a call into an `@cosmic/physics` import. That fires on exactly main.ts:333-334, 360-361, 394-395, 410-411 and stays silent on the drawing code. Also extend scripts/validate-physics-models.mjs, which today only checks that packages/physics/src/*Model.ts files have a sibling test and an index export — that is why a 116-line evolution model in demo code is invisible to it.

5. Separately, the review doc docs/reviews/stars-zams-hr.md HR-4 should be corrected: it still describes stageProperties as the divergent copy, which stopped being true on 2026-09-04.
findings.note:

The function runs to :426 (116 lines). Not fixed: `git log -4` on the file shows 0f75490 (Biome) and 19baaf9 ("three shipping errors ... HR lab"), and `git show 19baaf9 -- .../main.ts` contains no change to these lines.

INDEPENDENT RECOMPUTATION (node, Tout-1996 coefficients transcribed from packages/physics/src/zamsTout1996Model.ts:40-62, Z=0.02, T_sun=5772 K). For 1 M_sun: L_ZAMS = 0.6977 L_sun, T_ZAMS = 5597 K, R_ZAMS = 0.8882 R_sun. At fraction = 0 the track gives L = 0.5024 L_sun (-28.0%, i.e. log10(0.72) = -0.14267 dex), T = 5485 K (-2.0%, -0.00877 dex), implied R = sqrt(L)(T_sun/T)^2 = 0.7848 R_sun (-11.6%). THE CONTRADICTION IS REAL AND INTERNAL. packages/physics/src/hrInferencePopulationModel.ts:257-259: `if (ageMyr < mainSequenceLifetimeMyr(massMsun)) return { stage: "ms", L: ms.L, ... }` — the population plots every MS star at exactly L_ZAMS with no age dependence, so the track's t=0 point genuinely sits 0.143 dex below the diagram's own main sequence. SEVERITY OF THE CLAIM AS TITLED IS P1, NOT P0. THEORIST_AXIS_LIMITS (logic.ts:17-22) span logLum -5..+6 = 11 dex over plotHeight = height-96 px. 0.14267/11 x 404 px = 5.2 px down (4.2 px at the 300 px canvas floor, 6.2 px at the 571 px case named in style.css:663). The T offset is 0.00877/log10(20) x 567 = 3.8 px right. The track dot is r = 5.5 px (main.ts:701), population dots r = 3.7 px (main.ts:653) — the displacement is about one marker radius. I also checked both exports (exportClaimJson main.ts:981, exportResultsPayload main.ts:1010) and the whole evolve panel (index.html:224-250): the track point's L, T and R are never printed or exported, only time, t_MS and a stage label. So no wrong NUMBER reaches a student; "visibly below" overstates ~5 px on a thin locus.

BUT THE SAME BLOCK CARRIES A GENUINE P0, WHICH IS WHY I KEEP P0 ON A RETITLED FINDING. packages/physics/src/stellarLifetimeModel.ts:348 already exports `postMainSequenceTrack`, and the population uses it (hrInferencePopulationModel.ts:265-271). So the demo draws its overlaid track and its stars from two different post-MS models on the same axes. Recomputed for 2 M_sun mid-giant-branch: inline main.ts:360-362 gives R = 1.6102*(4+95*0.5^1.15) = 75.4 R_sun, T = clamp(9082*(0.85-0.25)) = 5449 K, L = 4513 L_sun; the shared model (BGB_BRIGHTENING 2.2, tip = base*3 since 2 is not < DEGENERATE_CORE_MAX_MSUN, giantBranchBaseTemperatureK = 4700*2^-0.08) gives L = 61 L_sun, T = 3713 K, R = 18.8 R_sun. findings.title: Glossary's Parallax entry names the 2 AU baseline but omits that the parallax angle is half the total shift
findings.evidence: "Stellar parallax uses Earth's orbital diameter as a baseline to measure distances to nearby stars." The annual parallax p is defined with the Earth-Sun distance (1 AU, the orbital RADIUS) as baseline: d(pc) = 1/p(arcsec). The orbital diameter (2 AU) subtends 2p, which is the six-month total shift, not p. parallax-distance.md:36 states this correctly — "Equivalent Jan-Jul shift is derived as $2\\hat p$; it is not the direct measurement" — and parallax-distance.md:26 lists the exact misconception "Any two captures can be interpreted as a six-month (2p) measurement". The glossary asserts that misconception as the definition.
findings.scenario: A student reads the glossary entry for Parallax, takes the baseline to be 2 AU, measures a 0.1 arcsec total shift for a star, and computes d = 1/0.1 = 10 pc instead of d = 1/0.05 = 20 pc. Every distance they derive is wrong by exactly a factor of 2, and the site's own flagship demo is the thing they were using it to interpret.
findings.fix: In apps/site/src/data/glossary.ts:71, keep the orbital-diameter baseline (it matches the demo's diagram, its B_eff readout and docs/reviews/parallax-distance.md:96) and add the half-angle clause, in ASCII only, since the glossary page has no math renderer: "The apparent shift in position of an object when viewed from two different vantage points. For stellar parallax, two observations six months apart give a baseline of Earth's orbital diameter (2 AU); the parallax angle p is half that total shift -- the angle subtended by 1 AU -- so d (pc) = 1 / p (arcsec)." If the relation is to be typeset instead, that is a separate, larger change: render definitions through renderInlineMath() from apps/site/src/lib/inlineMath.ts in apps/site/src/pages/glossary.astro:68 and add apps/site/src/data to SCAN_ROOTS in scripts/validate-math-formatting.mjs:19-27 — which would also surface the pre-existing Unicode-math and SI-unit violations at glossary.ts:65 and :107.
findings.note:
Text confirmed but one line off: the definition is at apps/site/src/data/glossary.ts:71 (line 72 is `demos: ["parallax-distance"]`). The corroborating citations are also off — the `2\hat p` model note is at apps/site/src/content/demos/parallax-distance.md:33, not :36, and the misconception at :22, not :26.

The geometry recomputed independently (node, CGS: AU=1.495978707e13 cm, pc=3.0856775814913673e18 cm): 1 AU at 1 pc subtends 1.000000 arcsec, 2 AU subtends 2.000000 arcsec. So p is defined on the orbital RADIUS and the six-month total shift is 2p; the finder's arithmetic (0.1 arcsec total -> p=0.05 arcsec -> d=20.0 pc, vs the mis-step 1/0.1 = 10.0 pc, ratio 0.50) reproduces exactly.

The P0 framing is nonetheless refuted. (a) The glossary entry asserts no angle and no formula. It defines parallax as an apparent shift between two vantage points and names the observational baseline. It never states that the measured shift equals p, and there is no `Parsec` entry and no `d = 1/p` anywhere in glossary.ts (grep for `parsec|Parsec|arcsec|1/p` over all 116 lines matches only line 71, via "baseline"). The claimed failure chain needs the student to import d=1/p from somewhere else AND identify p with the total shift; the copy supplies neither step, so there is no wrong number on the page. (b) Calling the orbital diameter the baseline is standard usage and this repo already endorses it: docs/reviews/parallax-distance.md:96 reads "the full orbital diameter is 2 AU, and the parallax angle p is defined as the half-angle subtended by 1 AU. The label and the '2p (exaggerated)' angle label are consistent with the standard definition." (c) The demo's own misconception (parallax-distance.md:22, "Any two captures can be interpreted as a six-month (2p) measurement") is about capture geometry — arbitrary captures do not give the full 2 AU baseline — not about radius vs diameter, so the glossary does not "assert that misconception as the definition."

The demo and model are unaffected and correct: apps/demos/src/demos/parallax-distance/logic.ts:274 sets baselineEffAu as the projection of the capture baseline on the parallax axis, :302 computes pHatMas = deltaThetaMas / baselineEffAu, :325 dHatPc = 1000 / pHatMas. At opposite captures B_eff = 2 AU and Delta theta = 2p, so p_hat = p and a 0.1 arcsec total shift yields 20.0 pc. packages/physics/src/parallaxDistanceModel.ts:19-21 implements d(pc) = 1/p(arcsec) on the radius convention.

What survives is real but milder: a one-sentence glossary definition that names the 2 AU observational baseline and omits the clause that carries the factor of two (p is half the total shift, i.e. the angle subtended by 1 AU). Since the project's own demo is built to dispel 2p confusion, the entry should carry that clause. That is a content-precision edit on reader-visible copy with no number and no formula in it, so P2, not P0.

The proposed fix would create a new inconsistency and a rendering problem. Rewriting the baseline as 1 AU contradicts the demo's diagram and its "Effective baseline B_eff ... AU" readout (apps/demos/src/demos/parallax-distance/index.html:246-248, up to 2 AU) and the repo's own review quoted above. Separately, apps/site/src/data/ is NOT in SCAN_ROOTS of scripts/validate-math-formatting.mjs:19-27, and apps/site/src/layouts/Layout.astro:47 loads only katex.min.css with no auto-render script, while apps/site/src/pages/glossary.astro:68 renders {entry.definition} as plain text — so any `$...$` added there would display as literal dollar signs. (Noted in passing, outside this finding: the unscanned glossary already carries Unicode math and SI units at line 107, "λ_max = b / T ... 2.898 × 10⁻³ m·K", and a degree glyph at line 65.)

findings.title: Seasons orbit panel is a plan view drawn with a side-view axis: the Polaris arrow sits 53 deg off sunward at the June solstice (and 37/146 deg instead of 90 deg at the equinoxes), survives tilt = 0 at full length, and the orbit runs clockwise with no viewpoint declared; logic.test.ts:127-131 pins the chirality
findings.evidence: orbitPosition returns `y: rScaled * Math.sin(angleRad)` (logic.ts:77). SVG y points down, so increasing angle moves clockwise; I computed the successive-position cross product as +1956.7 (clockwise) and day 80 at y = +135.8 (below centre), matching STATUS.md's own measurement "day 80 at y=+134.7". logic.test.ts:127-131 asserts `pos.y).toBeCloseTo(140)` at angle pi/2 — the test pins the clockwise convention instead of catching it. Separately, polarisIndicatorEndpoints (logic.ts:428-432) returns the orbit-independent direction (sin eps, -cos eps) = (0.399, -0.917); with the June label at screen angle 165.9 deg (logic.ts:396-407), I computed the angle between the drawn axis and the Earth->Sun direction at the June solstice as 52.4 deg, and the same 52.4 deg between the axis and the away-from-Sun direction in December. It should be 0 deg in both cases.
findings.scenario: A student on the June Solstice preset looks at the orbit panel to see the north pole tilted toward the Sun — the demo's entire causal claim — and instead sees the axis pointing sideways, 52 deg off, on a planet orbiting backwards. The demo is `readiness: candidate` ("ready to assign"), so this is what a class sees. seasons.md:12 admits "Still to come: ... the direction Earth is drawn orbiting" while still claiming candidate.
findings.fix:
Fix the whole panel in one frame — plan view, Sun at centre, north up out of the screen (the alternative, redrawing the orbit as an ellipse and keeping a side-view axis, means reworking index.html:176 and both label families and is the worse trade here).

1. logic.ts:77 -> `y: -rScaled * Math.sin(angleRad)` and logic.ts:408 -> `const y = centerY - labelR * Math.sin(angle);`.
2. REQUIRED and missing from the proposed fix: main.ts:1159 -> `return Math.atan2(-local.y, local.x);`. `orbitAngleFromPointer` shares the old convention, so flipping only logic.ts inverts the Earth drag vertically (drag up, day runs backwards) — silently, since no test covers the drag.
3. Rewrite `polarisIndicatorEndpoints` (logic.ts:422-432) to the plan-view projection with a CONSTANT reference angle, never the live orbit angle: `const thJ = SeasonsModel.orbitAngleRadFromDay({ dayOfYear: 172 });` then `x2 = earthX - length*Math.sin(tiltRad)*Math.cos(thJ)`, `y2 = earthY + length*Math.sin(tiltRad)*Math.sin(thJ)` (the y sign follows the flip in step 1). Passing the current orbit angle, as proposed, would make the arrow rotate with Earth and destroy the one thing the panel teaches — that the axis is fixed in space. The `Math.sin(tiltRad)` factor is not optional: it makes the arrow vanish at tilt = 0, which the present code gets wrong at full length. Keep the label offset tied to the new endpoint (main.ts:722-723) so it does not collide with the Sun when the arrow is short.
4. Tests: replace logic.test.ts:126-131 with `y < 0` at day 80 and a chirality assertion `x80*y172 - y80*x172 < 0`; add three polaris assertions — sunward within 1 deg at day 172, anti-sunward within 1 deg at day 356, perpendicular within 1 deg at days 80 and 266, and zero length at tilt = 0. Assert the angles, not the pixel coordinates, so the next re-scaling cannot re-pin a defect.
5. index.html:173 title -> "Orbit (viewed from above the North Pole; distance exaggerated)", authored in plain words (no Unicode math glyphs).
6. Then clear the disclosure: drop "the direction Earth is drawn orbiting" from seasons.md readinessReason and close the STATUS.md:57-62 item, which already specifies items 1, 2, 3 and 5.
findings.note:
CONFIRMED on code, with two corrections (severity and the characterization of the Polaris bug). What I read and recomputed independently:

1. Quoted code exists verbatim. /Users/anna/Teaching/cosmic-playground/apps/demos/src/demos/seasons/logic.ts:77 is `y: rScaled * Math.sin(angleRad),` inside `orbitPosition` (lines 68-79). The orbit panel is a true circle with the Sun at its centre — /Users/anna/Teaching/cosmic-playground/apps/demos/src/demos/seasons/index.html:176 `<circle class="stage__orbit" cx="0" cy="0" r="140" />` plus `<circle class="stage__sun" cx="0" cy="0" r="26" />` (index.html:181) — so the panel is a plan (top-down) view, which is the frame the geometry must satisfy.

2. Chirality, recomputed myself (node, r = 140, perihelion day 3, Y = 365.2422 d): day 80 angle = 75.89 deg, y = +135.78 px (screen y-down, i.e. below the Sun); cross product of two successive positions = +196 px^2 for a +0.01 rad step, positive => clockwise on screen. Season labels run the same way (logic.ts:408 `centerY + labelR*Math.sin(angle)`): Mar lower-right, Jun left/low, Sep upper-left, Dec upper-right — self-consistent but clockwise. logic.test.ts:126-131 does assert `expect(pos.y).toBeCloseTo(140, 5)` at angle pi/2, so the test pins the convention rather than catching it. Drag uses the same convention (main.ts:1159 `Math.atan2(local.y, local.x)`).

3. Polaris arrow, recomputed myself from logic.ts:422-432 with eps = 23.44 deg: fixed screen direction (sin eps, -cos eps) = (0.3978, -0.9175). Angle between that arrow and the Earth->Sun direction at each anchor day: Jun solstice (day 172) 53.1 deg (ideal 0), Dec solstice (day 356) 125.5 deg (ideal 180), Mar equinox (day 80) 37.5 deg and Sep equinox (day 266) 145.8 deg (ideal 90 for both). My 53.1 deg vs the finder's 52.4 deg is the only numeric difference (they used the Jun label angle 165.9 deg, the live code uses the day-172 angle 166.57 deg). Stated as a phase error: the drawn axis is exactly sunward at orbital angle 113.4 deg = day 118 (28 April), so the drawing places the June solstice 54 days early. One extra check the finder missed, which clinches the diagnosis: the tilt slider goes to zero (index.html:48-54, `min="0"`), and at eps = 0 the formula still draws a full 30 px arrow (0, -30) labelled "Polaris" — a plan-view projection must vanish at eps = 0. The arrow is drawn in a side-view frame inside a plan-view panel.

4. Reachable and live. renderStage (main.ts:707-723) calls both functions every frame; the "Jun solstice" chip (index.html:40, main.ts animateToDay(172)) exposes the exact configuration. No guard or clamp intervenes.

5. Not fixed, and already triaged. Latest commit touching logic.ts is 8fcedd6 (terminator fix), seasons files are clean in the working tree, and STATUS.md:57-62 already records this exact item with a fix plan — including the `main.ts:1159 atan2(-local.y, local.x)` flip, the `-length sin(eps)(cos thJ, -sin thJ)` arrow and the index.html:173 viewpoint title. Public copy partly discloses it: seasons.md is `status: beta`, `readiness: candidate`, and readinessReason names "the direction Earth is drawn orbiting" as still to come (it does not mention the axis misalignment). index.html declares no viewpoint anywhere (I grepped for above/viewed/north pole/top-down/clockwise: only a latitude preset matched).

Where the finder overstates:
- "the Polaris axis ... returns the orbit-independent direction" is framed as the defect. Orbit-independence is required physics — the axis is fixed in space, and that fixedness is the panel's pedagogical point. The defect is which fixed direction, and the missing sin(eps) length scaling.
- "points 52.4 deg away from the Sun at both solstices" understates the correct part and overstates the wrong part: the lean sense is right (sunward in June, dot = +0.60; anti-sunward in December, dot = -0.58), so a student on the June preset still reads "tilted toward the Sun". The genuinely misleading frames are the equinoxes (37.5 deg / 145.8 deg instead of 90 deg), where the drawing implies March is near-summer and September near-winter geometry.
- No readout, declination, day length, noon altitude or globe/terminator number is affected; this is the schematic panel only, distance already labelled "exaggerated".

Severity: P1, not P0. It is a real wrong drawing in the demo's primary causal diagram and it is reachable at two of four presets, but it produces no wrong number or wrong season, the solstice lean sense is correct, the orbital sense has no declared viewpoint to contradict (undeclared, not provably inverted), and the demo ships as beta/candidate with the direction issue disclosed in public readinessReason. It is not a student-visible wrong number, which is what P0 is reserved for here.

findings.title: The onboarding wizard hardcodes a second topic taxonomy that bypasses listedDemos() and contradicts TOPIC_SEQUENCE, sending Stars to the withheld eos-lab and Data & Inference to an Orbits demo
findings.evidence: welcome.astro:17: `{ key: "Stars", label: "Stars", start: "eos-lab" }`. eos-lab.md:11-13 sets `unlisted: true` with unlistedReason "On hold. The equation of state is incomplete ... so the regime map is only trustworthy over part of the plane it draws. There is also no instructor bundle. Withheld from the catalogue until the EOS is complete and independently checked." eos-lab is also `levels: [ASTR201]` only. The wizard is the site's primary new-user entry: index.astro:64 links it as "New here? Answer two questions and we will...". `listedDemos()` filters eos-lab out of Explore, the homepage and For Instructors — but welcome.astro hardcodes the slug and bypasses that filter entirely. Of the six wizard entry points, one is unlisted, three are `experimental` (keplers-laws, telescope-resolution, and conservation-laws is mis-topiced), and none is the single `launch-ready` demo.
findings.scenario: An ASTR 101 student clicks "New here?", picks Student, picks Stars, and is handed a 201-level instrument whose regime map the project states is only trustworthy over part of the plane it draws, with no instructor notes and no station card. The unlisting that was supposed to protect them is silently defeated.
findings.fix:
Do NOT use the proposed `listedDemos()` + best-`readinessRank` sort. `readinessRank` does exist (lib/readiness.ts:70-73), but I recomputed its outcome and the proposed fix does not do what it claims: all three listed Stars demos tie at rank 2 (`experimental`), so a rank sort falls through to collection order and picks cluster-census — not "hydrostatic-equilibrium-explorer or stars-zams-hr" — and cluster-census is the demo with the known composed-domain NaN problem. The same alphabetical tiebreak also churns three entry points nobody complained about: EarthSky moon-phases -> angular-size (displacing the golden-reference demo), Orbits keplers-laws -> binary-orbits, LightSpectra unchanged only by luck. Four of six entries would move on an alphabetical accident.

Apply instead: derive the wizard from the SSOT that already encodes the editorial answer. In welcome.astro's frontmatter, delete the 6-entry `topics` array and build the chips from `TOPIC_ORDER` + `TOPIC_LABEL`, with each start slug = the first entry of `TOPIC_SEQUENCE[key]` that survives `listedDemos(await getCollection("demos"))`. Verified outcome: EarthSky->moon-phases, Orbits->keplers-laws, LightSpectra->em-spectrum, Telescopes->telescope-resolution unchanged; DataInference->parallax-distance (fixes both the mis-topic and the zero-launch-ready-entry-points problem); Stars->hydrostatic-equilibrium-explorer (eos-lab is last in its sequence and filtered as unlisted); Galaxies and Cosmology gain the chips they currently lack. Make the slug list typed/derived so an unlisted or renamed demo is a build error, not a dead recommendation.

Two things that fix does not cover, worth tracking separately: (a) the resulting Stars entry is still `levels: [ASTR201]`, because every Stars demo is ASTR201 or Both — the wizard asks role but never level, so if the Student path is meant to mean ASTR101 it needs a level filter and a documented fallback for topics with no 101 demo; (b) welcome.astro:158 labels the button "Launch demo" while linking an exhibit page — rename it "Open exhibit" so the on-hold and readiness callouts at exhibits/[slug].astro:59-74 are read as part of the arrival rather than skipped past.
findings.note: CORE CLAIM CONFIRMED, two sub-claims refuted, severity overstated. 1. Code exists, line cite is wrong. `{ key: "Stars", label: "Stars", start: "eos-lab" }` is at apps/site/src/pages/welcome.astro:14 in the working tree and :18 at HEAD (`git show HEAD:...welcome.astro | grep -n Stars`) — not :17. Line 17 at HEAD is the conservation-laws entry. The uncommitted withBase refactor (git diff) removed 4 lines, so the finder cited neither version. 2. Routing traced line by line and reachability confirmed. index.astro:64 `New here? Answer two questions`; welcome.astro:67 emits `data-start={t.start}` on every chip; welcome.astro:153 `const startSlug = chip.dataset.start;` and :158 `resultLink.href = withBase(`exhibits/${startSlug}/`)`. exhibits/[slug].astro:12-17 builds paths from an unfiltered `getCollection("demos")`, so /exhibits/eos-lab/ exists. findings.title: spectral-lines Understand card prints the air Balmer limit (364.6 nm) where the live microscope draws the vacuum value (364.7 nm), and a stale 656.1 nm readout placeholder predates the reduced-mass correction
findings.evidence: index.html:351 prints "The Balmer series limit (364.6 nm)"; index.html:346 writes the Rydberg formula with $R_\\infty = 1.097\\times10^7\\ \\text{m}^{-1}$; index.html:439 hardcodes the default readout `656.1` for the default n=3->2 state; index.html:497 says "Hydrogen wavelengths are vacuum values". The model uses RYDBERG_EV = 13.598434599 and HC_EV_NM = 1239.842 (spectralLineModel.ts:36,40). I recomputed from those constants: H-alpha vacuum = 656.462 nm (air 656.281), Balmer limit vacuum = 364.701 nm (air 364.601). And 4/R_inf = 364.507 nm while 4/R_H = 364.705 nm. So 364.6 is the AIR value on a card whose formula yields 364.51 in a demo that claims vacuum; and 656.1 matches neither air nor vacuum nor the model (off by 0.36 nm). Hydrogen requires R_H (reduced mass), not R_infinity.
findings.scenario: A student follows play_steps "move n_upper toward infinity to see line pile-up near the Balmer limit", reads 364.70 nm off the live instrument, and compares it to the 364.6 nm printed on the Understand card beside a formula that would give 364.51 — three numbers for one quantity. On first paint (or with JS blocked) the headline Wavelength readout says 656.1 nm for n=3->2, which is simply wrong.
findings.fix: Two edits, both safe (no test reads either string): 1. index.html:351 -> "The Balmer series limit (364.7 nm)". This is the only change that closes a reader-visible disagreement: main.ts:712 draws "Balmer limit 364.7 nm" and model notes at index.html:497 promise vacuum values, so the card must quote vacuum. Alternatively keep 364.6 and label it air, but then it contradicts the stated vacuum policy two cards away, so 364.7 is the cheaper fix. 2. index.html:439 -> leave the span EMPTY (``) rather than retyping 656.5. render() at main.ts:2211 populates it before first paint, so there is no visible gap, and an empty span can never drift from the model again. This is the finder's own preferred option and it is the right one; do the same sweep for the sibling placeholders at index.html:446 (`1.89` eV) and :453 (`4.57` x10^14 Hz), which are R_infinity-era fossils by the same route -- I get 1.8887 eV and 4.5675e14 Hz from the current constants, and the readouts print 4 significant figures (main.ts:1415), so `1.89` is already stale in format as well as value.
