findings.title: Presets named for cosmological objects (3C 273, high-z galaxy) drive the always-visible radial-velocity readout, with the kinematic-only model boundary one tab away instead of at the point of use
findings.evidence: main.ts:167-168 define preset 7 "Quasar 3C 273" with z = 0.158 and preset 8 "High-z galaxy" with z = 2; applyPresetById (main.ts:518) routes both through syncPhysicalFromRedshift, which calls `DopplerShiftModel.velocityFromRedshift({ z, relativistic: true })` (logic.ts:100-103) and writes the result into the prominent "Radial velocity $v_r$" readout (index.html:344). I computed the values shown: z = 0.158 -> beta = 0.14572 -> 43,689 km/s; z = 2 -> beta = 0.8 -> 239,834 km/s. The only correction, "This instrument models kinematic Doppler shift, not cosmological expansion or gravitational redshift", is at index.html:439 inside `<details class="cp-accordion">` Model notes, closed by default and never surfaced when a preset is pressed. doppler-shift.md:25 lists "Redshift always means cosmological expansion; all redshifts are the same mechanism" as a targeted misconception, and doppler-shift.md:12 admits "the redshift presets still report a velocity, which is the misconception this exhibit is meant to address."
findings.scenario: A student presses "8: High-z", the instrument announces a radial velocity of 239,834 km/s for a z=2 galaxy, and they conclude that distant galaxies move through space at 0.8c. The demo named the preset after a real cosmological object and put the disclaimer in a closed drawer, so it taught the misconception it advertises as its target.
findings.fix:
Keep the number -- it is the correct SR Doppler inversion and the SR-vs-NR contrast is the demo's point -- and fix the framing at the surface the student actually sees. 1. Add one optional field to the DopplerPreset interface (main.ts:154-160): `cosmological?: string`, set on preset 7 (main.ts:168) and preset 8 (main.ts:169) to e.g. "3C 273's redshift is cosmological. This is the kinematic-equivalent speed, not a line-of-sight velocity through space." 2. Add a visible `

` immediately after the velocity slider's `control__value` (index.html:68) -- NOT inside any `

`, and beside #velocityValue rather than the collapsed #vrValue at index.html:344, since #velocityValue (main.ts:963) is the reading the student sees. 3. In render() (main.ts:955-967), next to the existing velocityClampIndicator line (main.ts:967), toggle that element from the active preset's `cosmological` field, so it clears as soon as the student moves a slider away from the preset. 4. In applyPresetById (main.ts:525), append the same sentence to the live-region text so the announcement is `Preset 8: High-z galaxy. Non-rel approximation fails. ` -- screen-reader users currently get no caveat at all. 5. Rename the preset labels so the chip itself does not assert a kinematic reading of a cosmological redshift: "7: 3C 273 ($z=0.158$)" and "8: High-$z$ galaxy ($z=2$)" in index.html:149-151, with the kinematic qualifier carried by the caveat line. One optional field, one element, one branch -- no new abstraction, and it removes the readinessReason blocker so doppler-shift can advance past `experimental`. While editing main.ts:963, also route the display through a fixed/10^n formatter rather than formatNumber's toExponential branch, to satisfy the no-e-notation rule.
findings.note:
The underlying defect is real and reachable, but five of the finding's load-bearing claims are wrong, and they change both the severity and where the fix must land.

CONFIRMED by tracing control flow line by line:
- Presets exist, at main.ts:168 (`{ id: "7", label: "Quasar 3C 273", z: 0.158, ... }`) and main.ts:169 (`{ id: "8", label: "High-z galaxy", z: 2, ... }`). The finding cites 167-168; off by one.
- Reachable: chips `data-preset="7"/"8"` at apps/demos/src/demos/doppler-shift/index.html:142-151 inside the "Velocity presets (keys 1-8)" popover, wired at main.ts:1264-1271, plus the keyboard path at main.ts:1619.
- applyPresetById (main.ts:507) takes the `else` branch at main.ts:518 -> syncPhysicalFromRedshift (logic.ts:95-114) -> DopplerShiftModel.velocityFromRedshift({z, relativistic: true}) (packages/physics/src/dopplerShiftModel.ts:155-173).
- Not guarded upstream: z=2 is inside [REDSHIFT_SLIDER_MIN=-0.8, REDSHIFT_SLIDER_MAX=10] (logic.ts:28-29), and physicalVelocityClamp (logic.ts:75-78) caps at MAX_PHYSICAL_BETA*c = 0.999999 x 299792.458 = 299,792.16 km/s, far above the result.

RECOMPUTED INDEPENDENTLY (node, not the finder's arithmetic), beta = ((1+z)^2-1)/((1+z)^2+1), c = 299,792.458 km/s:
- z = 0.158: (1.158)^2 = 1.340964; beta = 0.340964/2.340964 = 0.145651; v_r = 43,665.10 km/s. The finding claims beta = 0.14572 -> 43,689 km/s. WRONG by ~24 km/s; the finder squared 1.158 as 1.341164.
- z = 2: (3)^2 = 9; beta = 8/10 = 0.800000; v_r = 239,833.97 km/s. This one is right.

REFUTED, claim by claim:
1. "the prominent 'Radial velocity $v_r$' readout (index.html:344)" is false. index.html:344 sits inside `<details class="cp-accordion doppler-secondary">` "Inputs and frequency view" at index.html:337, with no `open` attribute -- i.e. collapsed by default, the SAME disclosure level as the Model notes caveat it is rhetorically contrasted against. The finding's central mechanism (prominent number vs. hidden caveat) does not exist as cited. The real exposure is elsewhere: the always-visible velocity slider's `control__value` (`#velocityValue`, index.html:58 label / :68 value), written at main.ts:963 with the FULL physical velocity -- main.ts:958 clamps only the slider thumb, not the printed value.
2. "the instrument announces a radial velocity of 239,834 km/s" is false twice over. The live region (main.ts:525) emits only `Preset 8: High-z galaxy. Non-rel approximation fails.` -- no velocity at all. And running the repo's own formatter (formatSigned/formatNumber, logic.ts:57-71) on 239,833.97 with digits=2 takes the `Math.abs(value) >= 1e4` branch to `toExponential(1)`, so the screen reads `+2.4e+5 km/s`, never "239,834 km/s".
3. "the only caveat is inside a collapsed drawer" is false. A visible "Model boundary" card in the Understand tab panel (index.html:266-274) states "This demo models kinematic Doppler shift only." and "Cosmological and gravitational redshift are distinct mechanisms." That is a `role="tabpanel"`, not a `<details>` -- one tab click, not a drawer.
4. The readiness-honesty framing is inverted. apps/site/src/content/demos/doppler-shift.md:3 is `status: draft`, :10 is `readiness: experimental`, and :11 is readinessReason "Being revised: the redshift presets still report a velocity, which is the misconception this exhibit is meant to address." That reason is RENDERED PUBLICLY: apps/site/src/pages/exhibits/[slug].astro:69-73 emits the "Active development: draft / experimental" callout plus `{entry.data.readinessReason}` for any non-stable status, above the Launch button. The project already discloses this exact defect to the student before they enter. The finding quotes that disclosure as evidence against the project; it is the project behaving correctly, and it caps the severity.
5. The physics is not wrong. dopplerShiftModel.ts:167-172 implements the exact SR Doppler inversion beta = ((1+z)^2-1)/((1+z)^2+1) correctly. For the kinematic model the demo explicitly declares, 239,834 km/s is the right number. No wrong number, no wrong drawing, no broken page -- so the P0 bar ("wrong physics/wrong number/wrong drawing a student would believe, or a broken page") is not met. What survives is misleading framing: presets named after real objects whose redshift is dominantly cosmological, with the model boundary a tab away rather than at the point of use. That is "misleading copy" = P1, and self-disclosure puts it at the bottom of P1.

The proposed fix would NOT fix it: suppressing the index.html:344 readout touches a collapsed accordion and leaves `+2.4e+5 km/s` on screen at #velocityValue.

Separate issue for the parent, not this finding: main.ts:938 and :963 render large velocities as `+2.4e+5 km/s` through formatNumber's toExponential path (logic.ts:58-63), violating CLAUDE.md's "Powers of ten as $10^n$; no `e` notation in teaching-facing copy."

findings.title: Sky View's "Full Moon" reference ring is hardcoded to 0.533 deg — the Sun's mean angular diameter, not the Moon's 0.518 deg — and the label conflates phase with angular size
findings.evidence: `const FULL_MOON_DEG = 0.533;` then line 387 `const refR = (FULL_MOON_DEG / fovDeg) * VIEWPORT_R;`, drawn with the label `Full Moon` (index.html:325). Recomputed: Sun at 1 AU, theta = 2 atan(1.392e6 km / (2 x 1.495978707e8 km)) = 0.53313 deg. Moon at the demo's own preset distance, theta = 2 atan(3474 km / (2 x 384400 km)) = 0.51780 deg. The constant is the Sun's value; it is 2.93% larger than the Moon's. Full Moon at perigee is 0.560 deg and at apogee 0.490 deg, so 0.533 deg matches no lunar configuration. With the Sun preset selected: fov = 3 x 0.53313 = 1.5994 deg, objR = (0.53313/1.5994) x 140 = 46.67 px, refR = (0.533/1.5994) x 140 = 46.66 px — the Sun's disk lands on the "Full Moon" ring to within 0.01 px. With the Moon preset: objR = 46.67 px, refR = 48.04 px — the Moon is drawn inside the ring labelled "Full Moon".
findings.scenario: A student opens the demo (Sun preset is the default), sees the Sun's disk sitting exactly on the dashed ring labelled "Full Moon", and concludes the Sun and Moon are *exactly* the same apparent size. They then select "Moon (Today)" and see the Moon drawn smaller than the ring that is supposed to be the Moon. The demo's own eclipse teaching point — the Sun and Moon are *nearly* but not exactly equal, which is why both total and annular eclipses exist — is contradicted by its own drawing.
findings.fix:
The proposed fix is directionally right and does compile — both `AngularSizeModel` and `AstroConstants` are already imported at main.ts:4, and `AstroConstants` is exported from the physics barrel (packages/physics/src/index.ts:1) — but it is incomplete in three ways. What I would apply:

1. Hoist and derive, do not just substitute. The literal is declared INSIDE `renderSkyView` (main.ts:375-376), so the proposed expression would run an `atan` on every render. Move it to module scope:
   `const MOON_MEAN_DEG = AngularSizeModel.angularDiameterDeg({ diameterKm: AstroConstants.MOON.DIAMETER_KM, distanceKm: AstroConstants.MOON.DISTANCE_TODAY_KM });` // 0.51780 deg
   Then line 387 becomes `const refR = (MOON_MEAN_DEG / fovDeg) * VIEWPORT_R;` and the stale comment on main.ts:386 ("Full Moon ~0.53 deg") must go with it.

2. Fix the label, which is the deeper pedagogical error the proposed fix leaves in place. Angular size depends on distance, not phase: a full Moon spans 0.49-0.56 deg (a 14% range, which is why annular eclipses exist). A single ring labelled "Full Moon" teaches that full Moons have one size — and this demo's own orbit slider exists precisely to show they do not. Change index.html:325 to "Moon (mean)". Without this, the ring is still misleading copy even at the right radius.

3. Write the test against the constant, not the live state. The proposed assertion "the ring constant equals the Moon preset's own theta" is wrong as written: the Moon preset's live theta is mutable — the orbit slider (main.ts:222) and the recession slider (main.ts:228) rewrite `state.distanceKm` across 0.49-0.56 deg — so that test either passes vacuously at default or breaks the moment the slider moves. Assert `MOON_MEAN_DEG` against `AngularSizeModel.angularDiameterDeg({diameterKm: AstroConstants.MOON.DIAMETER_KM, distanceKm: AstroConstants.MOON.DISTANCE_TODAY_KM})` in angular-size's logic.test.ts, and add a design-contract assertion that main.ts contains no bare decimal angular-size literal (the invariant that was actually breached).

4. Correct docs/reviews/angular-size.md:81, which currently certifies `refR = (0.533 / fovDeg) * VIEWPORT_R` as correct. Left alone it will re-launder this bug at the next review.

Note on expectations: this fix will not visibly change the demo. It moves the Sun's disk from 0.011 px to 1.341 px outside the ring. It is worth doing because the constant is wrong, mislabeled, and hardcoded in demo code — not because a student can see it.
findings.note:
CONFIRMED, with one evidence correction and a severity correction.

Code exists verbatim. `apps/demos/src/demos/angular-size/main.ts:376` is `const FULL_MOON_DEG = 0.533;` (inside `renderSkyView`, which also sets `VIEWPORT_R = 140`), line 387 is `const refR = (FULL_MOON_DEG / fovDeg) * VIEWPORT_R;`, and the label is `index.html:325` (`<text id="skyRefLabel" ...>Full Moon</text>`).

Independent recomputation (node, my own arithmetic, not the finder's). theta = 2 atan(D/2d) * 180/pi:
- Sun, D = 1.392e6 km (presets.sun, main.ts via angularSizeModel.ts), d = KM_PER_AU = 149597870.7 km (astroConstants.ts:48): theta = 0.53313 deg = 31.988 arcmin. The literal 0.533 matches the Sun to 0.024%.
- Moon, D = 3474 km, d = 384400 km (DIAMETER_KM / DISTANCE_TODAY_KM, astroConstants.ts:102-104): theta = 0.51780 deg = 31.068 arcmin. The literal is 2.935% larger.
So the constant is the Sun's mean angular diameter sitting behind a "Full Moon" label. Core claim holds.

Pixel geometry recomputed. Because fov = clamp(3*theta, 0.5, 60), objR = (theta/3theta)*140 = 46.667 px for any theta in [0.167, 20] deg — the disk never changes size, so the ring is the only scale cue. Sun preset: refR = (0.533/1.59939)*140 = 46.655 px vs objR 46.667 px, gap +0.011 px. Moon at mean: refR = 48.036 px vs 46.667 px, gap -1.369 px (Moon inside its own ring). Matches the finder.

Reachable and unguarded. `sun` is the default preset (main.ts:189-191). refR = 46.66 px passes the visibility guard `refR > 5 && refR < 135` (main.ts:388), so the ring is drawn on first paint. Nothing clamps or corrects it.

Not already fixed. `git log -3` on main.ts: the most recent touch, 69094e0 "Open the Moon preset at its mean distance, not perigee", fixed a *different* Sun/Moon near-equality bug and left this one. Worse, `docs/reviews/angular-size.md:81` inspected this exact expression and certified it — "correctly scaled relative to FOV" — checking the scaling and never the value. A reviewed-and-passed defect, the repo's known "reviews encode the defect" pattern.

Internally corroborated. main.ts:280-282 and apps/site/tests/angular-size.spec.ts:163-165 both write the correct numbers in prose (Sun 0.5331, Moon mean 0.5178) and name the near-equality as the teaching point. The repo knows the right value; the ring uses the wrong one. No test pins the ring (grepped design-contracts.test.ts and the e2e specs: nothing on skyRefRing/refR).

EVIDENCE CORRECTION. The claim "0.533 deg matches no lunar configuration" is FALSE. d = 3474/(2 tan(0.533deg/2)) = 373,441 km, which sits inside the demo's own perigee/apogee span of 355,436-406,213 km (from ORBIT_MAX/MIN_ANGULAR_SIZE_DEG = 0.56/0.49, astroConstants.ts:106-107). 0.533 deg is a perfectly real lunar angular size — it is just not the mean, and it is numerically the Sun's mean.

SEVERITY CORRECTION, P0 -> P1. The claimed failure scenario does not survive the pixel count. With the *correct* constant the Sun's disk would sit 1.341 px OUTSIDE the ring instead of 0.011 px ON it — a 1.3 px change on a 140 px radius (0.96%), rendered as a 1 px dashed stroke at opacity 0.4 (style.css:77-82). No student distinguishes those two pictures, so the misconception "the Sun and Moon are exactly equal" is neither created by the bug nor cured by the fix. And every number a student actually reads is correct and model-derived: the theta readout (pinned at 0.5178 by angular-size.spec.ts:176), the station comparison rows (all built through buildStationRow from the model, main.ts:541-570), and the challenge target 0.53313 (main.ts:829). The authoritative surface is numeric and it is right. This is a mislabeled hardcoded physical constant on low-opacity reader-visible chrome, plus a violation of the "no physical constants in demo code / all physics from @cosmic/physics" invariant — exactly the architecture defect class that keeps producing P0s. P1, not a wrong number a student would believe.

findings.title: Sky View's adaptive FOV cancels angular size: the disk is frozen at 46.667 px across a 121x distance range and for 14 of 18 presets
findings.evidence: `const fovDeg = clamp(3 * thetaDegValue, 0.5, 60);` (line 379) then `const objR = clamp((thetaDegValue / fovDeg) * VIEWPORT_R, 2, VIEWPORT_R - 2);` (line 382). Whenever the clamp is inactive, objR = (theta / 3theta) x 140 = 46.667 px exactly, independent of theta. I evaluated all 18 presets: sun 46.67, moon 46.67, andromeda 46.67, pleiades 46.67, orionNebula 46.67, lmc 46.67, smc 46.67, virgoCluster 46.67, comaCluster 46.67, basketball 46.67, soccerball 46.67, quarter 46.67, thumb 46.67, airplane 46.67 — identical for 14 of 18, over angular sizes spanning 0.344 to 10.74 deg (a factor of 31). Only jupiter (3.57 px), venus (4.69), mars (2.00) and iss (4.16) differ, because theta < 0.1667 deg pins fov at 0.5. For those four, refR = 149.2 px, outside the 140-px clip circle, so the reference ring is hidden too (main.ts:388 `if (refR > 5 && refR < VIEWPORT_R - 5)`). For lmc (refR 2.3 px), smc (4.8) and virgoCluster (3.1) the ring is also hidden, so those three sky views are byte-identical renderings.
findings.scenario: The panel is titled "Sky View" and the exhibit's first learning goal is "Relate an object's apparent size to its physical size and distance." A student drags the distance slider from 1 AU to 10 AU: theta falls by a factor of 10, every readout changes, and the disk in the Sky View does not move a single pixel. Cycling LMC -> SMC -> Virgo Cluster (10.74, 5.21, 8.01 deg) produces three indistinguishable pictures. The panel teaches that apparent size is independent of distance — the exact misconception listed in the exhibit's `misconceptions` field.
findings.fix:
Keep the finder's direction — stop deriving the FOV from theta — with three amendments, because the fix as written would not hold and one part of it is not implementable.

1. Fixed eyepiece ladder, re-picked on preset change ONLY. Replace main.ts:379 with a ladder (60 deg / 5 deg / 1 deg / 5 arcmin / 30 arcsec) held in `state`. Auto-select the smallest rung containing the object when the PRESET changes, and never recompute it inside `renderSkyView`. The finder's phrase "pick the smallest that contains the object" is ambiguous and, if it fires on slider `input` (main.ts:957), reintroduces a stepped version of the same cancellation. `renderSkyView` must take the FOV as a parameter so it is structurally incapable of deriving it from theta. Expose the rung as a visible control (segmented buttons or a select) so the student can zoom deliberately.

2. The Moon ring must degrade to text, not stay drawn. "Never hide the ring" is not implementable: at a 30-arcsec field refR = (0.533*3600/30)*140 = 8960 px, 64x outside the 140-px clip circle. Keep main.ts:388's bounds check, but in the else branch replace the hidden ring with an annotation instead of `display: none` — "Full Moon = 64x this field" when refR overflows, "Full Moon = 1/60 of this field" when it underflows. That preserves the finder's real point (the object being too small to see IS the lesson) without asking for an undrawable circle.

(a) `FULL_MOON_DEG = 0.533` (main.ts:376) must come from the moon preset's own geometry (2*atan(3474/(2*384400)) = 0.5178 deg) or from a single `AstroConstants` entry — hardcoding 0.533 makes the Moon miss its own reference ring by 2.9%, and a literal duplicating physics in demo code also violates the repo's "all physics from @cosmic/physics" rule. Assert Sun at 1 AU vs 3 AU gives a ratio of 3 within rounding — today both are 46.667, which is the real frozen-plateau case (do NOT use 1 AU -> 10 AU; that pair already changes, 46.667 -> 14.928 px, and would pass against the broken code).

findings.title: Spectrum view's fixed 380-700 nm window makes every reachable Doppler shift sub-pixel (max 0.55 px vs a 3.6 px line), so the wobble the copy promises can never be seen
findings.evidence: drawSpectrum() maps a fixed 380-700 nm window onto the plot width: SPECTRUM_DOMAIN = { minNm: 380, maxNm: 700 } (main.ts:224) and wavelengthToFraction() (main.ts:480) spreads 320 nm across plotW. style.css:226 gives #spectrumCanvas aspect-ratio 16/5 inside a .rv-panel of width min(100%, 960px), so plotW = 960 - 56 - 24 = 880 px, i.e. 2.75 px/nm. I recomputed the Doppler displacement over the whole parameter space (M1=1 fixed, q in [0.001,1], a in [0.1,100] AU, i in [0,90]) at 486.1 nm: default state (q=1, a=4, i=60, K1=9.12 km/s) gives dlambda = 1.479e-2 nm = 0.041 px; the single largest amplitude anywhere (q=0.001, a=0.1 AU, i=90, K2=94.142 km/s) gives dlambda = 1.526e-1 nm = 0.42 px. Sub-pixel in every case.
findings.scenario: A student opens the Spectrum view at any settings. The lower 'Observed' strip is drawn at exactly the same pixel columns as the 'Lab' strip, the rest-to-observed arrow at main.ts:1107-1117 has zero length, and in SB2 the dashed secondary lines sit on top of the solid primary lines. The stage prompt (main.ts:512) tells them 'the observed strip wobbles with the same orbital phase' and the readout prints 'Primary Delta lambda = 0.015 nm'. The student concludes either that the demo is broken or, worse, that real stellar Doppler shifts are unobservable - the exact opposite of the lesson. The e2e test that claims to cover this (apps/site/tests/binary-orbits.spec.ts:400) only asserts that the note STRING contains '0.000', never that any pixel moved, so it passes.
findings.fix:
Keep the 380-700 nm strip as the honest orientation band and ADD a third zoomed strip below it, rather than replacing the domain (which breaks spectrumTicks and the integer tick labels).

1. In `drawSpectrum` (main.ts:1023), after the Lab/Observed strips, draw a "Zoom" strip over a window centred on the representative line: halfWidthNm = max(zoomFloorNm, Z * lambda_rest * K_edge_on/c), with K_edge_on from a `circularState({..., inclinationDeg: 90})` call (the pattern already used in `getRvChartLayout`, main.ts:743-750) so changing i still visibly shrinks the wobble instead of auto-rescaling it away. Z and zoomFloorNm are pedagogical tolerances - propose them to Anna with the derivation (Z ~ 4 puts the edge-on excursion at a quarter-strip; the floor stops a = 100 AU, q = 0.001 producing an absurd window) rather than hardcoding them.
2. Give that strip its own tick generator and formatter - `spectrumTicks` (main.ts:483-492) hardcodes a 40/50 nm step and main.ts:1141 prints `Math.round(tick)`, both of which degenerate on a sub-nm span. Label it in nm to 3-4 decimals.
3. State the magnification in reader-visible copy next to the strip, e.g. "zoom: 680x around H-alpha 656.463 nm", so the exaggeration is explicit. Canvas text stays ASCII per the CLAUDE.md canvas exemption; the HTML note uses KaTeX.
4. Draw the rest-to-observed arrow and the `Primary Delta lambda` label in the ZOOMED strip, where it has real length, and fix main.ts:1111 to take its direction from the sign of `representative.shiftedNm - representative.wavelengthNm` so a blueshift points blueward at zero pixel length.
5. In SB2, offset the secondary's dashed lines to a separate sub-row of the zoomed strip (or draw them in the lower half) so a student can see the two components moving in antiphase instead of coincident.
6. Rewrite the copy that currently promises an invisible motion: main.ts:512 ("the observed strip wobbles with the same orbital phase") and the note built at main.ts:1631 / index.html:217 should say the shift is ~0.02 nm at default - far too small to see against a 320 nm band - and point at the zoomed strip and its magnification.
7. Test it the way this repo tests canvases: publish the zoomed observed-line x position (and the magnification) as `data-` attributes on `#spectrumCanvas` - the documented pattern in CLAUDE.md for asserting on canvas state - and add an e2e case that samples phase pi/2 vs 3pi/2 and requires a difference of several pixels. A pixel-diff screenshot would be flaky here; an attribute assertion is decisive. Strengthen apps/site/tests/binary-orbits.spec.ts:400 at the same time: its `toContainText("0.000")` on a note string is not evidence that anything moved.
findings.note:
CONFIRMED on substance, severity corrected P0 -> P1. Every quoted anchor exists: `SPECTRUM_DOMAIN = { minNm: 380, maxNm: 700 }` at main.ts:224; `wavelengthToFraction` at main.ts:479-481; `drawSpectrum` at main.ts:1023 (the cited :1042 is the `shiftedPrimary` line inside it); the rest-to-observed arrow at main.ts:1101-1121 (not 1107-1117); the "wobbles" prompt verbatim at main.ts:512; `#spectrumCanvas { aspect-ratio: 16/5 }` at style.css:226-229 inside `.rv-panel { width: min(100%, 960px) }` at style.css:231-232. I read the whole of `drawSpectrum` (main.ts:1023-1154) and `DopplerShiftModel.shiftLines` (dopplerShiftModel.ts:175-205): there is no magnification, no exaggeration factor and no auto-zoom anywhere, and `grep -i "exagger|magnif|not to scale|too small to see|zoom"` over the demo and the exhibit content returns nothing.

INDEPENDENT RECOMPUTATION (my own `node -e` sweep, not the finder's arithmetic; I reimplemented `circularState` from binaryOrbitModel.ts:171-238 with P = sqrt(a^3/Mtot) yr, a1 = a*m2/Mtot, K = omega*a1*sin(i), and AU/yr -> km/s via 149597870.7/31557600 = 4.74057):
- Geometry: the finder's plotW = 880 px is wrong - it omits the panel's `padding: var(--cp-space-3)` = 12px (tokens.css:203). Canvas CSS width = 960 - 24 = 936 px, so plotW = 936 - 56 - 24 = 856 px, i.e. 2.675 px/nm (finder said 2.75). The height-driven breakpoint (style.css:604-613) caps `max-width: 860px`, so 856 px is the MAXIMUM; every other layout is worse.
- Representative line: the finder used 486.1 nm, which is wrong. `shiftedPrimary.find()` (main.ts:1096-1099) returns the FIRST in-range entry, and `SpectralLineModel.elementLines({element:"H"})` (spectralLineModel.ts:461-483) pushes Ly-alpha (out of range) then Balmer in ascending nUpper, so the representative is H-alpha = 656.463 nm vacuum (I recomputed it from the model's own Bohr constants: 1239.842/(13.598434599*(1/4-1/9))). My numbers are therefore ~1.35x LARGER than the finder's.
- Default state (q=1, slider 534 -> a = 10^(-1+0.534*3) = 3.999 AU, i=60): P = 5.656 yr, K1 = 9.120 km/s. dlambda(H-alpha) = 656.463 * 9.120/299792.458 = 1.997e-2 nm = 0.053 px. The readout prints "0.020 nm", not the "0.015 nm" the finding quotes.
- Full-space sweep (1001 separation slider steps -> a in [0.1,100] AU, q in {0.001...1}, i=90, M1 fixed at 1 Msun by DEFAULT_PRIMARY_MASS_SOLAR, logic.ts:29/226, across H/Na/Ca): max PRIMARY displacement = 0.390 px (q=1, a=0.1 AU, i=90, K1 = 66.602 km/s, dlambda = 1.458e-1 nm); max SECONDARY (dashed, SB2 only) = 0.551 px (q=0.001, a=0.1 AU, K2 = 94.142 km/s, dlambda = 2.062e-1 nm). A 1-px displacement at H-alpha needs 0.374 nm, i.e. 171 km/s - unreachable by a factor of 1.8. So the core claim holds: SUB-PIXEL AT EVERY REACHABLE SETTING, and the drawn line is 3.6 CSS px wide (1.5 + 1.0*2.1), ~7x the largest possible offset.

REACHABILITY: live and unguarded. `#viewSpectrum` is a stage chip (index.html:205), sliders are massRatio 0.001-1 (index.html:60-66), separation log 0.1-100 AU (index.html:98-105 + logic.ts:20-21), inclination 0-90 (index.html:113-118); no clamp narrows any of it. `git log -5` on main.ts shows no fix (latest touches are the post-MS track and a readout/drawer move).

NO TEST COULD CATCH IT, as claimed: the test at apps/site/tests/binary-orbits.spec.ts:400 ("face-on inclination collapses projected RV and spectrum wobble toward zero") asserts only `toContainText("0.000")` on `#spectrumProjectionNote` - a string, never a pixel. The only other spectrum tests (:579-582) assert visibility. There is no `toHaveScreenshot` on `#spectrumPanel` at all, unlike `#rvPanel` (:394).

SEVERITY CORRECTION, P0 -> P1. The physics, the readouts and the arrow's label are all CORRECT: a 9.12 km/s star really does shift H-alpha by 0.020 nm, and 0.020 nm out of a 320 nm window really is invisible. The drawing is physically faithful, no sign error, no wrong number, no broken page, and the RV view already carries the quantitative velocity-calibrated picture. What is defective is that an interactive view is structurally incapable of showing the one thing it exists to show, while main.ts:512 affirmatively tells the student "the observed strip wobbles with the same orbital phase" and main.ts:1631 reports "the line wobble is 0.866 x edge-on". That is misleading copy plus a dead affordance, which the task rubric puts squarely at P1. I would call it the top of the P1 band - fix before students are pointed at the Spectrum view. Two secondary defects I confirmed in the same block, which the finding missed: in SB2 the dashed secondary lines land on the solid primary lines at every phase, visually asserting rv1 = rv2 and contradicting the antiphase lesson the RV view just taught; and `const dir = obsX >= restX ? 1 : -1` (main.ts:1111) resolves to +1 at zero length, so the arrowhead points redward even when the readout says the star is blueshifted.

THE PROPOSED FIX WOULD BREAK TWO THINGS. Option (a), replacing the domain with lambda_rest +/- 25*(lambda_rest*K_edge-on/c), gets the pedagogy right in one respect - keying the window to the EDGE-ON amplitude rather than K(i) preserves the sin(i) lesson and avoids the silent-rescaling sin that the repo's own RV test at :380 guards against - but it breaks the axis: `spectrumTicks` (main.ts:483-492) hardcodes step 40 or 50 nm, so for a ~0.5 nm span `ceil(656.2/40)*40 = 680 > maxNm`, the loop never runs and it degenerates to a single tick; and main.ts:1141 prints `${Math.round(tick)}`, so every tick in a zoomed window would render the same integer "656". It also destroys the wide band that is the only thing making the view read as a spectrum, and with a ~0.5 nm window only one line survives the in-range filters at main.ts:1048/1081/1096. Option (b) duplicates the RV view.

findings.title: "Show peak marker" is on by default but is drawn at an unguarded x and leaves the plot frame whenever lambda_peak exits the fixed 10 nm - 1e6 nm domain (off-canvas in one click on the 1e6 K "Neutron Star" preset), while the log y axis labels the domain-edge maximum "peak"
findings.evidence: main.ts:317-336 draws the dashed marker at `x = nmToX(peakNm)` with no domain check; canvas has no clip region. Recomputed logFraction = (log10(lambda_peak)-1)/5: at T=1e6 K lambda_peak=2.898 nm -> frac=-0.1076 -> x = 62 + (-0.1076)(902) = -35.1 px (off-canvas, marker silently vanishes while the checkbox reads "Show peak marker"); at T=2.725 K lambda_peak=1.0635e6 nm -> frac=1.00535 -> x = 968.8 px while the plot border ends at mL+plotW = 964 px, so the dashed line and its "1.1 mm" label are drawn in the right margin, outside the axes. Separately, main.ts:226-227 sets `maxLog = Math.max(...logB)` over the sampled domain and main.ts:438 labels that row `"peak"`: I computed the sampled maximum lands at 10 nm for T=1e6 K and at 1e6 nm for T=2.725 K, not at lambda_peak.
findings.scenario: A student clicks "Neutron Star": the readout says lambda_peak = 3 nm, no peak marker appears anywhere on the plot, and the top gridline labeled "peak" sits above 10 nm - so the drawing asserts the peak is at 10 nm while the number asserts 3 nm. On the CMB preset the dashed "peak" line is drawn outside the plot rectangle entirely.
findings.fix:
Keep the finder's two changes, with these specifics.

(1) In `drawSpectrum()`, hoist one predicate after `peakNm` is computed (`main.ts:175`): `const peakInDomain = Number.isFinite(peakNm) && peakNm >= minNm && peakNm <= maxNm;`. Gate BOTH marker blocks on it — the dashed line at `main.ts:316-336` and the EM-band triangle at `main.ts:390-392` — so the two sites cannot drift apart.

(2) When `showPeakMarker.checked && !peakInDomain`, do not silently draw nothing. Clamp to the frame edge (`const edgeX = peakNm < minNm ? mL : mL + plotW;`) and draw an inward-pointing arrowhead at `edgeX` plus a label built from `formatWavelengthLabel(peakNm)`, e.g. `"peak 3 nm <-- off scale"` on the left and `"off scale --> peak 1.1 mm"` on the right, with `textAlign` "left"/"right" so the text stays inside the canvas. This preserves the lesson a student should take from the Neutron Star preset — the peak is blueward of the plotted window — instead of hiding it. Mirror it in `setLiveRegionText` / `status` so the screen-reader path is not worse than the visual one.

(3) At `main.ts:438`, change the log branch's top label from `"peak"` to `"0"`. The axis title at `main.ts:410` already reads "log Relative Intensity", so "0" is unambiguous as 0 dex relative to the plotted maximum, and the axis stops claiming to mark the Wien peak. Touch only the log branch: the linear branch's top label is already `"1.0"`.

(4) Add the regression test that does not exist today: assert `peakInDomain` is false at T = 1e6 K and T = 2.725 K and true at T = 5772 K. Cleanest as a pure exported helper in `logic.ts` (`isPeakInDomain(peakNm, minNm, maxNm)`), since `logic.test.ts` already covers that file and `main.ts` is DOM-bound and untested.

Alternative I considered and would NOT take alone: widening `wavelengthDomainNm()` (`logic.ts:51`) to cover every reachable peak, which needs [~1 nm, ~2e6 nm] given the 2.725-1e6 K slider. It removes the off-domain case at the source, but going from 5 to 7 decades compresses the 380-750 nm visible band from 3.4% to 2.4% of the plot width and forces `X_TICKS_NM` (`main.ts:138`) to be rebuilt — a real pedagogy cost in the one region students care most about. If the domain is widened at all, do it modestly (to 1e7 nm, fixing only the cold edge) and still ship the guard, because the hot edge needs T > 2.898e5 K coverage that no reasonable domain gives.
findings.note:
CONFIRMED on every checkable point; I reproduced all numbers independently from the repo's own constants, and corrected the severity to P1.

1. Code exists as quoted. `apps/demos/src/demos/blackbody-radiation/main.ts:316-336` is the `// --- Peak marker ---` block: `if (showPeakMarker.checked && Number.isFinite(peakNm)) { const x = nmToX(peakNm); ... ctx.moveTo(x, mT); ctx.lineTo(x, mT + plotH); ... }`. There is no domain test and no `ctx.clip()` anywhere in the demo directory (`grep -rn "clip(\|off-scale\|offScale"` over the demo dir returns nothing). `main.ts:226` is `const maxLog = Math.max(...logB);` and `main.ts:438` is `const label = i === 0 ? "peak" : `${-i}`;`. A second unguarded copy exists at `main.ts:390-392` (`const px = nmToX(peakNm)` for the EM-band triangle), as the finding says.

2. Independent recomputation (not the finder's arithmetic). Geometry from `main.ts:155` (`mL = 62, mR = 16`), `nmToX` at `main.ts:177`, and `wavelengthDomainNm()` at `logic.ts:51` returning `{10, 1e6}` nm, so frac = (log10(λ/nm) − 1)/5. Wien constant from `packages/physics/src/blackbodyRadiationModel.ts:9`, `wienDisplacementCmK: 0.2898` cm·K, so λ_peak = 2.898e6/T nm.
 - T = 1.000e6 K: λ_peak = 2.8980 nm, frac = −0.10758, x = 62 − 0.10758·plotW.
 - T = 2.725 K: λ_peak = 1.0635e6 nm, frac = +1.00535, x = 62 + 1.00535·plotW.
 Canvas CSS width is `max-width: clamp(400px, calc((100svh - 18rem)*16/9), 980px)` (`style.css:114`), so plotW runs 322-902 px. At plotW = 902 (desktop, tall viewport) the hot case gives x = −35.0 px: off-canvas, marker invisible. At plotW = 322 it gives x = +27.4 px: drawn in the left margin over the y-tick-label gutter, still outside the frame (frame starts at x = 62). The crossover where it leaves the canvas entirely is plotW > 576 px, i.e. canvas width > 654 px. Cold case: x is 2.0-4.8 px right of the frame end (62+plotW) but inside the mR = 16 margin, so on-canvas and outside the axes; the plot border is stroked at `main.ts:338-343`, i.e. AFTER the marker, so it does not cover it.
 Exact reachability thresholds I derived: λ_peak < 10 nm for T > 2.898e5 K, and λ_peak > 1e6 nm for T < 2.898 K. Slider limits are `TEMPERATURE_MIN_K = 2.725`, `TEMPERATURE_MAX_K = 1e6` (`main.ts:84-85`), so both off-domain regimes are inside the allowed input range and nothing clamps λ_peak.

3. Reachable in one click, on a default-on control. `index.html:65` is `data-temp-k="1000000"` labeled "Neutron Star"; `index.html:70` is `data-temp-k="2.725"` labeled "CMB". `index.html:47` is `<input id="showPeakMarker" type="checkbox" checked />` — the marker is on by default. So one click on "Neutron Star" yields: readout "3 nm" (I reran `formatWavelengthReadout` logic: Math.round(2.8980) = 3, unit nm) and no marker anywhere on a desktop-width canvas.

4. Sampled-maximum claim verified with my own Planck implementation using the repo's CGS constants and the exponent>700 cutoff, over `sampleLogSpace(10, 1e6, 500)`: at T = 1e6 K argmax is index 0 = 10.000 nm; at T = 2.725 K argmax is index 499 = 1.0000e6 nm; at T = 5772 K argmax is index 170 = 505.13 nm (interior, so the label is honest in the normal regime). So `maxLog` is indeed the domain-edge value, not the Wien-peak value, whenever the peak is off-domain, and labeling that row "peak" is then false.

5. Not already fixed and not pinned by a test. `git log -3` on the file (4693f76, 4c096ae, 7775c7e) touches tokens/glow reads and pedagogy copy, not the marker. `logic.test.ts` only asserts the pure helpers (domain is 10 nm to 1e6 nm at line 126-129, log fractions at 241-251); no assertion anywhere constrains the marker's x or the y-tick label, so the guard needs a new test rather than an edit to an existing one.

Two corrections to the finding. (a) Severity: P1, not P0. No computed quantity is wrong — the Planck function, the Wien peak, and the readout are all correct, and nothing is drawn at a wrong wavelength. The hot-case lie is an omission (a default-on control that draws nothing), and the demo already declares `status: draft` / `readiness: experimental` in `apps/site/src/content/demos/blackbody-radiation.md:3,10`, so it makes no launch-ready claim. The cold/CMB case is a 2-5 px overshoot into the margin and is P2 on its own. It stays high-P1 rather than P2 because it is one click away on a default-on control and the plot then contradicts the readout. (b) The evidence overstates the gridline: the row labeled "peak" is a horizontal intensity gridline spanning the full width, so it does not "sit above 10 nm" and does not assert an x position. The defensible version — which I confirmed — is that the log y axis labels the domain-edge intensity "peak", so the curve's visible maximum at the left edge reads as the peak while the readout says 3 nm.

The proposed fix is substantially right: `minNm`/`maxNm` are in scope at both marker sites (destructured at `main.ts:161`), so the guard drops in, and only the log branch at 438 needs relabeling — the linear branch already labels the top row "1.0", which is honest.

findings.title: EFF profile uses the surface-brightness gamma as a 3-D density exponent: gamma=3 lands exactly on the log-divergent mass case, so the half-number radius readout (5.2 pc vs 2.4 pc) and the rendered cluster size are set by the hard-coded truncation, and the drawn projected profile has index 2.0 not the cited 3.0
findings.evidence: Line 68: `const density = (1 + (r / scaleRadiusPc) ** 2) ** (-gamma / 2);` used directly as rho(r) in `integrand = 4 * Math.PI * r * r * density` (line 69), citing "Elson, Fall & Freeman (1987), ApJ 323, 54" at line 52. EFF's gamma is defined on the PROJECTED surface-brightness profile mu(R) ∝ (1 + R^2/a^2)^(-gamma/2); the 3-D deprojection is rho(r) ∝ (1 + r^2/a^2)^(-(gamma+1)/2). With gamma = 3 used as a 3-D exponent the mass integrand goes as 4 pi a^3 / r at large r, so M(<r) diverges logarithmically. I recomputed r_h/a numerically (200k-point trapezoid, same scheme as buildEffCdf): code's gamma=3 gives r_h/a = 4.3526 at the hard-coded rt = 15a, 6.2693 at 30a, 8.9478 at 60a (M(30a)/M(15a) = 1.287); the correct deprojection of an EFF surface gamma=3 (3-D exponent 4) gives r_h/a = 2.0372 at 15a and 2.2045 at 60a -- essentially truncation-independent. The Plummer cross-check validates my scheme: gamma=5 gives 1.2970 against the analytic 1.304766. With SCALE_RADIUS_PC = 1.2 (main.ts:245) the demo prints 5.22 pc for "EFF (young)" where the cited profile gives 2.45 pc.
findings.scenario: A student clicks "EFF (young)" (or the Young preset) and reads the "Half-number radius" readout: 5.22 pc, versus 1.57 pc for Plummer at the same scale radius. They conclude a young cluster is 3.3x more extended than a Plummer cluster of the same scale radius. The true ratio for the cited gamma = 3 EFF profile is 1.56x, and the 5.22 pc value would become 10.7 pc if EFF_TRUNCATION_SCALE_RADII (clusterProfileModel.ts:115) were changed from 15 to 60. The same wrong number goes into the clipboard export as "Half-number radius (pc)" (main.ts:1367).
findings.fix:
The finder's primary fix is the right one and I would apply it, but it is incomplete in three places I verified.

1. `packages/physics/src/clusterProfileModel.ts:68` -> `const density = (1 + (r / scaleRadiusPc) ** 2) ** (-(gamma + 1) / 2);`. This makes gamma EFF's surface-brightness index: gamma=3 gives rho exponent 2, convergent mass (2p=4>3), r_h/a = 2.0372 at the current truncation and 2.2641 asymptotically. Keep EFF_GAMMA = 3 (main.ts:243) and the "EFF (young)" label -- gamma=3 is squarely in EFF 1987's young-cluster range once the exponent is right, so the defect is the exponent, not the gamma value. Prefer this over the finder's "rename to densitySlope3d and drop the citation" alternative: the citation is already public in three reader-visible places, and renaming would keep a profile whose mass does not converge.

2. MISSED BY THE FINDER: `clusterProfileModel.ts:128` `const gamma = profile.gamma ?? 5;` must become `?? 4`, and `PLUMMER_HALF_MASS_OVER_SCALE`-adjacent comments at lines 49-52 and the `ProfileSpec` doc at line 110 ("EFF only: the 3-D density slope") must be rewritten to say gamma is the surface-brightness index with Plummer at gamma=4. Otherwise the fallback EFF profile silently becomes rho ~ (1+x^2)^-3 instead of Plummer. cluster-census always passes gamma explicitly so this is latent, not live, but it is a trap for the next consumer.

3. The two pinning tests must be rewritten, not "re-checked": clusterProfileModel.test.ts:42 moves from `effHalfMassOverScale(5)` to `effHalfMassOverScale(4)` for the Plummer degenerate case, and :55 (`> 3 * effHalfMassOverScale(5)`) must go -- it asserts the divergence artifact and would fail at the correct 2.037. Replace it with a convergence assertion that would have caught this: r_h/a must change by less than a few percent when the truncation is doubled. starClusterModel.test.ts:171-180 uses `kind: "plummer"` and is unaffected.

4. The finder's claim that the fix makes the result "essentially truncation-independent" is slightly optimistic: at rt=15a the fixed value is 2.0372 vs 2.2641 asymptotic, still 8.1% low (0.65% low at rt=240a). To genuinely stop the truncation being load-bearing, set EFF_TRUNCATION_SCALE_RADII from stated physics (a tidal radius) rather than a bare 15, or raise it and say in the model note that the quoted radius is for the truncated profile.
findings.note:
CONFIRMED on every point I could test independently.

1. Code exists as quoted. `packages/physics/src/clusterProfileModel.ts:68` is verbatim `const density = (1 + (r / scaleRadiusPc) ** 2) ** (-gamma / 2);`, consumed at line 69 as `const integrand = 4 * Math.PI * r * r * density; // dM/dr`. So the quantity written `(1+r^2/a^2)^(-gamma/2)` is used as rho(r). The comment at line 49 states that explicitly ("rho(r) proportional to (1 + r^2/a^2)^(-gamma/2)") and line 50 cites "Elson, Fall & Freeman (1987), ApJ 323, 54" (the finding said line 52; the citation is line 50, immaterial). `EFF_TRUNCATION_SCALE_RADII = 15` at line 115.

2. The convention error is real, verified by numerical Abel projection, not by recalling the literature. For rho=(1+r^2/a^2)^(-p) I integrated Sigma(R) = 2*int_R^inf rho r dr/sqrt(r^2-R^2) numerically (400k-point trapezoid, substitution r=sqrt(R^2+u^2)) and measured the log-slope of Sigma between R=0.5a and R=3a: p=1.5 gives slope -1.0000, p=2.0 gives -1.5000, p=2.5 gives -2.0000, i.e. surface index gamma_s = 2p-1 exactly. Therefore the cited EFF surface gamma=3 requires rho exponent p=2, i.e. `(1+(r/a)^2)^(-(gamma+1)/2)`; and Plummer (p=2.5) is EFF gamma=4, not the gamma=5 asserted at line 52. The code's gamma is 2p, a non-EFF convention. index.html:483 says the positions are "sampled in three dimensions and projected", so the projected profile a student actually sees at EFF_GAMMA=3 has surface index 2.00, outside EFF 1987's young-LMC range entirely.

3. Numbers recomputed independently, analytically (I did not reuse the finder's 200k trapezoid). With a=1, int_0^x 4*pi*t^2*(1+t^2)^(-p) dt has closed forms: p=1.5 -> asinh(x)-x/sqrt(1+x^2); p=2 -> 0.5*(atan x - x/(1+x^2)); p=2.5 -> x^3/(3(1+x^2)^1.5). Bisecting for half the truncated mass gives r_h/a:
  - code's reading of gamma=3 (p=1.5): 4.3526 at rt=15a, 6.2693 at 30a, 8.9478 at 60a, 18.0194 at 240a, 116.58 at 10^4 a -- unbounded, as it must be: 2p=3 is exactly the marginal case where M(<r) diverges logarithmically. M(<30a)/M(<15a) = 1.2872.
  - correct deprojection of EFF gamma=3 (p=2): 2.0372 at 15a, 2.2045 at 60a, 2.2641 asymptotic.
  - Plummer (p=2.5): 1.2970 at 15a, 1.304766 untruncated (= 1/sqrt(2^(2/3)-1)), validating the scheme.
All match the finder's figures.

4. Live path verified by transcribing `buildEffCdf` + `inverseCdf` verbatim into node and running the demo's actual constants (SCALE_RADIUS_PC = 1.2, main.ts:245; EFF_GAMMA = 3, main.ts:243; truncation 15a): inverseCdf(0.5) = 5.2232 pc for EFF vs 1.5657 pc for the Plummer path (analytic, untruncated), ratio 3.336. The correct deprojection would give 2.4448 pc, ratio 1.561. So the readout is 5.2232/2.4448 = 2.14x too large. Changing only EFF_TRUNCATION_SCALE_RADII moves the printed value 5.223 -> 7.523 -> 10.738 pc for 15a/30a/60a: the headline number is set by an internal constant, confirming the finder's central claim. My transcription reproduces the test pins exactly (effHalfMassOverScale(5) = 1.29712 vs pinned 1.2971; effHalfMassOverScale(3) = 4.35266), so the transcription is faithful.

5. Reachable by a student, nothing clamped or guarded. The "EFF (young)" chip is live at index.html:126 and the Young preset selects it (main.ts:1312, profile: "eff"). `grep -i gamma packages/physics/src/starClusterModel.ts` finds no clamp or validity guard. The readout at main.ts:926 is `formatRadiusPc(radiusEnclosingFractionPc(cluster.stars, 0.5))`, the median of the 3-D `star.radiusPc` (logic.ts:153-161), printed to 2 decimals below 10 pc (logic.ts:254-257). I Monte-Carlo'd the displayed value at the Young preset (4000 stars, 40 draws): min 5.00, median 5.25, max 5.48 pc -- so a student reads ~5.2 pc, stably. The same value goes to the clipboard as "Half-number radius (pc)" (main.ts:1367-1369) next to the export note "positions from a Plummer (1911) or truncated EFF (1987) profile" (main.ts:1377).

6. Not already fixed. `git log -- packages/physics/src/clusterProfileModel.ts` shows one commit, a7d6119, the original novascope port; nothing since. No caveat anywhere about the truncation being load-bearing; the EFF 1987 citation is reader-visible in three places (index.html:483, main.ts:1377, apps/site/src/content/demos/cluster-census.md:44).

7. Two things the finder understated, both verified. (a) The drawing is wrong too, not just the readout: `clusterPlotRadiusPc` (main.ts:448-451) frames the three.js camera on `halfNumberRadiusPc * FRAME_HALF_NUMBER_RADII` (2.6, main.ts:444), and the rendered projected profile has surface index 2.0 instead of the cited 3.0, so the on-screen EFF cluster has genuinely the wrong shape. (b) The test at clusterProfileModel.test.ts:55, `expect(effHalfMassOverScale(3)).toBeGreaterThan(3 * effHalfMassOverScale(5))`, requires r_h/a > 3.891 and therefore actively *asserts* the logarithmic-divergence artifact; the correct value, 2.037, would fail it. Its comment calls the artifact "dramatically more extended". This is the repo's known "tests encode defects" pattern, so the fix must rewrite that test, not merely re-check it.

Only mitigation: the demo is `status: draft` / `readiness: experimental` (cluster-census.md:2,10), so it makes no launch-ready claim -- but `content_verified: true` is set, it is built into apps/site/public/play/cluster-census/, and the number is shown to 3 significant figures beside a literature citation. That softens the readiness-honesty angle, not the physics.

findings.title: "Total mass" readout is unqualified initial mass: 13,481 vs 7,348 M_sun present at the Globular preset (84 percent high)
findings.evidence: main.ts:925 `totalMass.textContent = formatCount(cluster.totalMassMsun);` under the label "Total mass" with unit `$M_\odot$` (index.html:283-287). starClusterModel.ts:114 documents the quantity: "Total mass in stars and remnants [Msun]. Remnants keep their initial mass here", and line 192 sums `totalMassMsun += massMsun` before the remnant branch. No reader-visible surface says "initial". I recomputed for the shipped Globular preset (20,000 stars, 12 Gyr, Maschberger alpha=2.3 over [0.1,150]): mean initial mass 0.6741 Msun, so the readout prints 13,481 Msun. At the 12-Gyr turnoff of 0.978 Msun, 11.92 percent of stars by number hold 61.07 percent of the initial mass and are remnants. Applying the model's own IFMR (whiteDwarfMassMsun for M<8, ~1.4 for NS, ~10 for BH), surviving-star mass is 0.2624 Msun/star and remnant mass 0.1020 Msun/star, so the present mass is 7,289 Msun. The readout overstates it by 85.0 percent.
findings.scenario: A student selects the Globular preset and reads "Total mass 13,481 Msun". They use it to estimate the cluster's mass-to-light ratio or its dynamical mass and are off by a factor of 1.85, with nothing on screen or in the export ("Total mass (Msun)", main.ts:1365) warning them. The same readout is correct at age 0, so the error is invisible until the age slider is used -- exactly the control the demo is built around.
findings.fix:
Relabel only; do not add a present-mass readout in this pass.

1. apps/demos/src/demos/cluster-census/index.html:283 -- change the label from "Total mass" to "Total mass formed" (or "Initial total mass"). Either reads correctly at age 0 and at 12 Gyr. Note the strip already has a control labelled "Cluster mass $\log_{10} M_{\mathrm{ecl}}$" (index.html:90, default 10^4 M_sun, an INPUT to the derived slope); "Total mass formed" also disambiguates the readout from that input, which "Total mass" does not.

3. packages/physics/src/starClusterModel.ts:114-115 -- tighten the doc comment to name the quantity: "Total INITIAL mass of every star drawn [Msun]. No mass loss is modelled, so remnants and giants still carry their initial mass; this is the mass formed, not the cluster's present mass."
4. apps/site/src/content/demos/cluster-census.md model_notes -- add one note: the mass readout is the mass formed, because the model applies no stellar mass loss and no dynamical mass loss. While in that list, :48 ("There is no post-main-sequence evolution: a star sits at its zero-age point until its lifetime elapses") is now stale -- commit ba9cdc2 "Give cluster stars a post-main-sequence track" added postMainSequenceTrack and the demo has a live giants tally (index.html, `giantCount`) -- so that note is wrong in the opposite direction and should be corrected in the same edit.

Do NOT add a second "present mass" readout without Anna's approval, and if it is wanted, ask by popup first. It needs a neutron-star mass and a black-hole mass, neither of which exists in packages/physics, and it would still omit AGB mass loss and dynamical mass loss, so the honest options to put to her are: (a) relabel only (recommended, zero new assumptions), (b) relabel plus a present-mass readout built on an approved IFMR extension (whiteDwarfMassMsun imported into starClusterModel.ts, plus her chosen NS and BH masses) and explicitly captioned as excluding mass loss and dynamics, or (c) relabel plus drop the readout from the strip if it is not pedagogically load-bearing. Also fix the tautological test at packages/physics/src/starClusterModel.test.ts:201-206: assert the documented identity against an independently computed expectation (e.g. that totalMassMsun is unchanged by ageMyr for a fixed seed, which is the actual contract) rather than re-summing the same field.
findings.note:
CONFIRMED on the code and the arithmetic; severity corrected P0 -> P1; the proposed fix is partly wrong.

1) Code is exactly as quoted. /Users/anna/Teaching/cosmic-playground/apps/demos/src/demos/cluster-census/main.ts:925 reads `totalMass.textContent = formatCount(cluster.totalMassMsun);`. The label is `Total mass` with unit `$M_\odot$` at apps/demos/src/demos/cluster-census/index.html:283-287. The export row is main.ts:1365 `{ name: "Total mass (Msun)", value: formatCount(cluster.totalMassMsun) }`. `formatCount` is logic.ts:236-238 (`Math.round(...).toLocaleString("en-US")`), so the strip prints e.g. "13,481". packages/physics/src/starClusterModel.ts:115 documents the quantity as "Total mass in stars and remnants [Msun]. Remnants keep their initial mass here", and :192 `totalMassMsun += massMsun;` runs before the `if (isRemnant)` branch at :197. No star ever loses mass anywhere in sampleStarCluster, so the field is the sum of INITIAL masses at every age.

2) I recomputed independently, three ways, none reusing the finder's arithmetic.
 - Analytic: log-spaced Simpson integration of the Maschberger (2013) eq.5 shape (mu=0.2, beta=1.4, alpha=2.3) over [0.1,150] M_sun, normalised numerically rather than via the repo's primitive: <m_initial> = 0.674058 M_sun, so the Globular preset (main.ts:1314: starCount 20_000, ageMyr 12_000, alphaHigh 2.3; minMassMsun = CENSUS_MIN_MASS_MSUN = 0.1 at main.ts:240) prints 13,481.2 M_sun. Matches the finder's 13,481 M_sun.
 - Remnant threshold: the code's condition is `ageMyr >= totalLifetimeMyr(massMsun)` (starClusterModel.ts:190), i.e. 1.15*t_BGB (stellarLifetimeModel.ts:307-309), NOT t_MS. Retyping Hurley eqs (4)/(7) coefficients and bisecting, tTot(m)=12,000 Myr at m = 1.0277 M_sun. The finder used 0.978 M_sun, which is the t_MS=12 Gyr turnoff (I get 0.97778) and is the WRONG boundary for remnant-hood -- their 11.92% by number / 61.07% by initial mass should be 11.23% / 60.05%. Direction and conclusion unaffected.
 - Present mass, analytic, using the repo's own IFMR (whiteDwarfMassMsun, stellarLifetimeModel.ts:277-287) for M<8 and the finder's 1.4 / 10 M_sun for NS / BH: surviving stellar mass 0.26931 M_sun/star + remnant mass 0.09811 M_sun/star = 7,348.4 M_sun for 20,000 stars. Overstatement = 13,481/7,348 = 1.8346, i.e. 83.5%.
 - Monte Carlo of the actual inverse-CDF draw (my own LCG, 200 clusters of 20,000): initial total 13,478 +/- 87 M_sun, present total 7,326 +/- 17 M_sun, ratio 1.840 -> 84.0% overstatement. So the readout genuinely prints ~13.4-13.6k for any seed, and the claimed "85 percent" is right to about 1 percentage point. The claim survives.

3) Reachable. The Globular chip exists (index.html:139 `data-preset="globular"`) and is wired at main.ts:1316-1329, setting state.ageMyr = 12_000 directly. The age slider independently reaches it: AGE_MAX_MYR = 13_000 (logic.ts:34). No clamp or guard on totalMassMsun anywhere.

4) Not already fixed or handled. `grep -rn totalMassMsun` over the repo returns only the five sites above plus one test. No reader-visible surface says "initial": index.html has no caveat near the readout, and the exhibit's model_notes (apps/site/src/content/demos/cluster-census.md:43-50) never mention mass loss or the epoch of the mass readout. The one test that touches it, packages/physics/src/starClusterModel.test.ts:201-206 "totals the mass over every star including remnants", asserts `cluster.totalMassMsun` equals `stars.reduce((acc,s)=>acc+s.massMsun,0)` -- tautological, since both sides are the same initial masses. It pins the behaviour rather than checking the quantity, exactly the failure mode in the project's memory note. git log -3 on main.ts (8fcedd6, b000a14, 6ac00e6) and on starClusterModel.ts (ba9cdc2, a03be65, a7d6119) shows no related change.

5) Severity corrected P0 -> P1. The number is not arithmetically or physically wrong: 13,481 M_sun is the correct total mass FORMED. The defect is an unqualified label, which is this audit's P1 "misleading copy", and the demo is `status: draft` with `readiness: experimental` (cluster-census.md:3,10), so no public quality claim is breached and the exhibit carries the Active-development callout. It is also a passive readout: nothing directs a student to it -- predict_prompt (:24), the parameters table (:37-39), explain_prompt (:41) and the learning objectives (:16-17) are all about the IMF's shape and the stochasticity of the heaviest star, there are no challenge tasks referencing mass, and apps/site/src/content/instructor/cluster-census/ does not exist. The finder's M/L-and-dynamical-mass scenario is plausible for a curious student but is not an exercise the demo poses. A factor-1.84 unqualified number on screen at the demo's flagship old-cluster preset is still a real defect that must be fixed before classroom use -- it is simply not a wrong computation.

6) The proposed fix is half right and contains two factual errors. The relabel is correct and sufficient. The "add a present-mass readout" half is not applicable as written: (a) it claims the IFMR is "already imported" in sampleStarCluster -- it is not. starClusterModel.ts:30-36 imports only mainSequenceLifetimeMyr, postMainSequenceTrack, remnantFateFromInitialMass, spectralTypeFromTemperature and totalLifetimeMyr; `grep -rn whiteDwarfMassMsun packages/physics/src apps/demos/src` shows it reaching only stellarLifetimeModel.ts and its own test, never the cluster chain. (b) It needs two constants that do not exist anywhere in packages/physics -- there is no neutron-star or black-hole remnant mass (remnantFateFromInitialMass, stellarLifetimeModel.ts:165-169, returns only the strings "white dwarf" / "neutron star" / "black hole"). The finder's 1.4 and ~10 M_sun are its own invention. Under CLAUDE.md ("Scientific assumptions are Anna's to approve": any coefficient you would otherwise guess or recall from memory is proposed with its physical motivation and waits for approval) those are popup decisions, not agent choices. (c) Worse, a readout labelled "Present mass 7,348" would itself be wrong for a 12-Gyr globular by a comparable factor in the other direction: the model has no AGB/RGB mass loss (surviving stars keep their initial mass right through the giant branch) and no dynamics at all (cluster-census.md:49 "There are no dynamics and no mass segregation"), while a real globular has evaporated and been tidally stripped of a large fraction of its stars. That fix trades one unqualified number for a more confident-sounding one the model cannot support.

findings.title: Wave-diagram direction arrow is inverted and unlabeled: for a receding source it points toward the observer
findings.evidence: Traced line by line. Source is drawn at `cx: 118` (main.ts:804), observer at `cx: 732` (main.ts:805) — observer is to the RIGHT. The arrow is then built as `const directionSign = direction.keyword === "redshift" ? 1 : -1; const arrowStart = 118; const arrowEnd = arrowStart + 44 * directionSign;` with the head at `arrowEnd` pointing outward. So redshift (v>0, receding) gives arrowEnd = 162, i.e. an arrow from x=118 to x=162 pointing in +x, TOWARD the observer at x=732. Blueshift (v<0, approaching) gives arrowEnd = 74, pointing in -x, AWAY from the observer. Both senses are inverted. The caption `helperLabel.textContent = direction.sentence` (main.ts:866) sits at x=20,y=20 and reads "source receding -> REDSHIFT" (logic.ts:271) while the arrow 12px below it at y=32 points toward the observer. Recorded as DS-1 "open" in docs/reviews/doppler-shift.md on 2026-09-03 and still unfixed.
findings.scenario: A student sets v = +1000 km/s (preset 5). The caption says "source receding -> REDSHIFT", the lines shift red, and the arrow next to the source points at the observer. The student reads the only diagram on the page as "moving toward me = redshift" and writes exactly the inverted rule on the exam. The inverse error is taught at negative velocity.
findings.fix:
Four parts; the sign flip alone is not enough.

1. Negate the sign at apps/demos/src/demos/doppler-shift/main.ts:846 so recession points away from the observer at x=732:
   const directionSign = direction.keyword === "redshift" ? -1 : 1;
   (The arrowhead branch at main.ts:858-860 keys off directionSign > 0, so the head follows automatically. Tip x=74 is inside the 0-800 viewBox.)

2. Move the mark out of the caption band and onto the source, so it reads as a motion vector rather than as an echo of the caption's "->" glyph. Change arrowY from 32 to baseY - 28 (= 104) and start the tail just outside the source glow (r=18), e.g. arrowStart = 118 + 22 * directionSign, so the arrow does not sit on top of the circle.

3. Label it. Add an svgEl("text", { class: "wave-helper", x: ..., y: baseY - 36 }) reading "Source motion" beside the arrow, and extend the aria-label at main.ts:870-873 to name the motion sense ("source receding from the observer" / "source approaching the observer"), since a screen-reader user currently gets no mention of the arrow at all.

4. Remove the competing directional glyph from the caption so only one directional mark remains in the diagram: rewrite the sentences at logic.ts:269 and logic.ts:275 as "Source approaching: BLUESHIFT" and "Source receding: REDSHIFT" instead of "BLUESHIFT <- source approaching" and "source receding -> REDSHIFT". Those ASCII arrows are the reason the drawn arrow got its sign.

Then add the test the suites currently cannot express. Extract a pure helper into logic.ts:

export function motionArrowDirection(velocityKmS: number, sourceX: number, observerX: number): { tailX: number; tipX: number } | null

returning null at v === 0, and assert in logic.test.ts that for v > 0 Math.abs(tipX - observerX) > Math.abs(tailX - observerX) and for v < 0 the inequality reverses, with sourceX=118 and observerX=732. Assert the relation, not the literal 74/162, so the test survives a layout change. Have main.ts:846-862 consume that helper so the geometry has exactly one owner.
findings.note:
CONFIRMED, with a severity correction and an incomplete fix.

Code exists verbatim at apps/demos/src/demos/doppler-shift/main.ts:843-862 (finding cited 846). Source cx:118 (main.ts:804), observer cx:732 (main.ts:805).

No mirroring anywhere: grep for transform/scaleX/rotate in style.css returns zero hits; viewBox="0 0 800 250" with no transform attribute; the arrow is appended directly to waveDiagram, not to a translated group.

Not already fixed or guarded: git log -3 on the file shows 2150874 (typecheck sweep), 0c2e413, e803f93 -- none touches the arrow. DS-1 is still recorded "open" at docs/reviews/doppler-shift.md:24. No test constrains it: grep for arrow/directionSign in logic.test.ts, design-contracts.test.ts and apps/site/tests/doppler-shift.spec.ts returns nothing, so the suites genuinely cannot see this.

SEVERITY CORRECTION P0 -> P1. The finding overstates the spatial coupling. It says "the arrow next to the source points at the observer", but arrowY = 32 while the source circle is at baseY = 132 -- the arrow is 100 px ABOVE the source dot, sitting 12 px beneath the caption at y=20, inside the caption band, with no label of its own (the only text is helperLabel at main.ts:865-866). In that position an unlabeled arrow reads as a colored echo of the ASCII implication glyph already inside the caption string ("source receding -> REDSHIFT" / "BLUESHIFT <- source approaching", logic.ts:269,275), whose sign it matches exactly -- which is almost certainly the author's intent. The correct rule is stated in words twice in the same visual group (the caption itself and index.html:436), and the diagram's quantitative content is correct (for v>0 obsSpacing > restSpacing, so the crests do widen, and the stroke reddens via wavelengthToRgbString). So this is a genuinely ambiguous directional mark whose spatial reading teaches the inverse rule -- a misleading drawing that must be fixed before students, but not a wrong number or a wrong physical quantity presented against no competing correct information. The prior reviewer also graded it P2 (docs/reviews/doppler-shift.md:24); P1 is the right middle.

Caveat on one sub-claim I could not measure: I estimated the caption's horizontal extent (27 chars at font-size 11px, style.css:379-382, ~0.5 em average => roughly x=20 to x=170, overlapping the arrow's x=118-162) rather than reading a computed box, since this audit is read-only and no browser run is permitted. The vertical placement (arrow y=32 vs source y=132) is exact from the source and is sufficient on its own.

FIX ASSESSMENT: the proposed one-line negation does correct the spatial sense (redshift tip lands at x=74, 658 px from the observer vs tail 614 px => away), stays inside the 0-800 viewBox, needs no change to the arrowhead branch since it keys off directionSign > 0, and breaks no test. But applied alone it leaves a red arrow pointing -x twelve pixels beneath a caption reading "source receding ->", i.e. it trades one ambiguous mark for a direct contradiction with the caption. The sign flip must be accompanied by moving and labeling the mark.

findings.title: Cosmological redshifts are labeled as a kinematic "Radial velocity $v_r$": z = 2 reads +2.4e+5 km/s in the primary control panel, and the z slider does the same up to z = 10
findings.evidence: PRESETS (main.ts:159-168) include `{ id: "6", label: "Coma Cluster", velocityKmS: 6925 }`, `{ id: "7", label: "Quasar 3C 273", z: 0.158 }`, `{ id: "8", label: "High-z galaxy", z: 2 }`. applyPresetById (main.ts:506-521) routes these through syncPhysicalFromRedshift, which calls DopplerShiftModel.velocityFromRedshift with relativistic: true. I recomputed: z = 0.158 -> beta = (1.158^2-1)/(1.158^2+1) = 0.14565 -> v = +43,665 km/s; z = 2 -> beta = (9-1)/(9+1) = 0.8 -> v = +239,834 km/s. Those land in `vrValue` under the label "Radial velocity $v_r$" (index.html:349-352). The demo's own Model boundary card (index.html:270-272) states "Cosmological and gravitational redshift are distinct mechanisms", and model_notes in doppler-shift.md:47 repeats it — but that text is behind the Understand tab and a collapsed accordion, not next to the number. Recorded as DS-2 "open" on 2026-09-03 and named in readinessReason; still unfixed.
findings.scenario: A student presses key 8, reads "Radial velocity v_r = +2.4e+5 km/s" for a z = 2 galaxy, and concludes that distant galaxies move through space at 0.8c. This is the single most common cosmology misconception in intro astronomy, and the demo manufactures it with a number. For Coma the 6925 km/s is cz, not a peculiar velocity, so even the "velocity" preset is a cosmological quantity in a kinematic field.
findings.fix:
The proposed fix is right in intent but wrong in scope, and one of its two options would break the demo.

Why it does not fix it as written: (a) tagging presets 6-8 leaves the z slider — which reaches z = 10, i.e. beta = 0.98 — producing the same misconception with no preset active; (b) "blank it" is not viable, because #velocityValue is the readout of a bidirectional slider control (main.ts:959 writes the clamped state back into velocitySlider.value) and "Radial velocity (km/s)" is a named field in both ExportPayloadV1 (logic.ts:524) and the mystery-evidence text block (logic.ts:483), so blanking it silently empties Copy Results; (c) it misses preset 6 entirely, which does not take the redshift branch, and preset 5 ("Typical galaxy cluster", velocityKmS: 1000, note: "Moderate recession", main.ts:166), whose note asserts the same misconception in copy.

What I would apply instead — drive it off the value of z, not off preset identity:

1. In logic.ts, add one exported predicate next to the existing regime helpers, e.g. `export function exceedsPeculiarVelocityRegime(z: number): boolean` returning `Math.abs(z) > Z_PECULIAR_MAX`. The threshold is a scientific choice and is Anna's to approve, not mine to guess: propose Z_PECULIAR_MAX = 0.01 (3000 km/s, above any plausible peculiar velocity) with the alternative 0.003, and wait.

2. In main.ts render() (around :963), when that predicate fires, keep the number but change its frame: swap the label to "SR-equivalent $v_r$" and un-hide a sibling caveat line — the same pattern already used by #velocityClampIndicator (index.html:96) and #formulaLimitIndicator (index.html:112), so the mechanism exists and needs no new machinery. Caveat text, inline and always visible at that z: "At this $z$ the shift of a real object is cosmological, not motion through space. This is the SR-equivalent $v_r$, not a recession speed." Mirror it onto #vrValue (main.ts:938).

3. Carry the same string into the export: add a `cosmologicalCaveat` parameter row in buildDopplerExportPayload (logic.ts:522-530) and a line in the mystery-evidence block (logic.ts:483) when the predicate fires, so a copied result cannot be pasted into a lab report without the caveat.

4. Fix the two preset-copy defects found along the way: rename preset 5's note off the word "recession" (main.ts:166), and for Coma either declare it by redshift (`z: 0.0231`, the catalogued heliocentric value) so the SR inverse is not applied to a cz, or keep 6925 km/s and label it "$cz$" — the current path stores z_rel = 0.023372 against the literature 0.023099.

5. Only after 1-4: revisit doppler-shift.md:10-11 readiness, since readinessReason names this exact item.

Note for the parent: items 2-4 change reader-visible copy and a public export field, so the KaTeX-only rule applies to every string above (written as `$v_r$`, `$z$`, `$cz$`) and the new strings must pass scripts/validate-math-formatting.mjs. I did not edit anything — this audit was read-only.
findings.note:

findings.title: "Total solar eclipse" preset leaves the Moon at mean distance, so the demo answers "Annular solar"
findings.evidence: `presetTotalSolar` calls `totalSolarPreset({ sunLonDeg })` (logic.ts:437-439) which returns only `{moonLonDeg, nodeLonDeg}` and then `tweenMoonTo(p.moonLonDeg, p.nodeLonDeg, 400)` — the Earth-Moon distance is left at its default `mean` (384,400 km). I recomputed the Moon's umbral cone radius at Earth from the model's own formula (eclipseGeometryModel.ts:70): r_u = 1737.4 km - 384400 km x (696000 - 1737.4) km / 149597870.7 km = 1737.4 - 1783.9 = -46.5 km. Since r_u <= 0, `solarEclipseTypeFromBetaDeg` takes the `umbraRadiusKm > 0 ? "total-solar" : "annular-solar"` branch (eclipseGeometryModel.ts:224) and returns `annular-solar`. At perigee (363,300 km) the same formula gives r_u = +51.4 km -> total-solar. Both verified with node.
findings.scenario: A student opens "Show me an eclipse..." and clicks "Total solar eclipse". The Moon tweens to New Moon on the node, the Solar readout displays "Annular solar", and the floating reward label flashes "Annular solar!". The control the student clicked and the answer the demo gives contradict each other, teaching that a central New-Moon-on-node alignment at the mean distance is a total eclipse when the demo's own (correct) geometry says annular.
findings.fix:
The proposed fix does work mechanically — I verified the mechanism the finder did not state: `render()` re-reads `distancePreset.value` on every call and writes it into state (`main.ts:488-494`), so assigning `distancePreset.value = "perigee"` before `tweenMoonTo` takes effect on the next frame without dispatching a synthetic `change` event, and `distanceValue.textContent` updates from state at `main.ts:518`. Apply it as follows.

1. `apps/demos/src/demos/eclipse-geometry/logic.ts:470-472` — have the pure function carry the whole preset, so the preset's identity lives in one place: `return { moonLonDeg: args.sunLonDeg, nodeLonDeg: args.sunLonDeg, distancePresetKey: "perigee" as const }`.

2. `apps/demos/src/demos/eclipse-geometry/main.ts:1384-1387` — set `distancePreset.value = p.distancePresetKey` before `tweenMoonTo(...)`.

3. Add the thing the finder's fix omits: silently overwriting the student's chosen distance is itself a small teaching defect, and here the overwrite IS the physics lesson. Make it visible — either extend the button copy to "Total solar eclipse (moves Moon to perigee)" in `index.html:32`, or surface a one-line note after the tween saying the distance was set to perigee because at the mean distance the umbral cone (374,370 km) falls short of Earth's surface (378,029 km at the sub-lunar point) and the same alignment is annular. That turns the contradiction into the demo's own total-vs-annular lesson.

4. Test it through the REAL model, never the stub: the demo's stub at `logic.test.ts:59-64` returns `total-solar` for any |beta| < 0.5 with no distance term, so a preset test written against it would pass on the present bug. Assert instead that `computeDerived({...totalSolarPreset state, earthMoonDistanceKm: DISTANCE_PRESETS_KM[p.distancePresetKey]}, realModel).solarType === "total-solar"`. Also close the gap in `packages/physics/src/eclipseGeometryModel.test.ts:44-56` by adding the missing mean-distance case: `solarEclipseTypeFromBetaDeg({ betaDeg: 0, earthMoonDistanceKm: 384400 }).type === "annular-solar"`, which pins the correct physics the preset was fighting.

Do NOT "fix" this by making the model return total-solar at mean distance — that would be the real P0. Optional follow-up, separate and milder: `solarEclipseTypeFromBetaDeg` decides total-vs-annular from the cone radius at Earth's CENTRE (`eclipseGeometryModel.ts:208-224`), ignoring the 6,371 km the sub-lunar point is nearer. That biases marginally toward annular and shifts the true break-even from 374,370 km to about 380,741 km of centre distance. It changes no verdict at any of the three selectable presets (I checked all three), so it is a P2 refinement, not part of this fix.

CONFIRMED (with a severity correction and three line-number corrections).

Code exists as described. `apps/demos/src/demos/eclipse-geometry/main.ts:1381` is indeed `presetTotalSolar.addEventListener("click", () => {`, and the handler body (1382-1387) is exactly: `stopTimeActions()`, stop challenge, `const p = totalSolarPreset({ sunLonDeg: state.sunLonDeg })`, `setPhasePressed(null)`, `closePresetsPopover()`, `tweenMoonTo(p.moonLonDeg, p.nodeLonDeg, 400)`. Umbral cone length from the Moon's centre, L = R_moon * AU / (R_sun - R_moon) = 1737.4 km * 149597870.7 km / 694262.6 km = 374,370 km. Mean Earth-Moon distance 384,400 km, so the tip falls 10,030 km short of Earth's centre and still 3,659 km short of the sub-lunar SURFACE point at 378,029 km. Cross-check that I read the right formula: asin((6371 + 46.546)/384400) = 0.9566 deg, which reproduces the model's own golden assertion of 0.957 deg at `eclipseGeometryModel.test.ts:40-41`. So the MODEL's annular verdict at mean distance is physically correct (it is why annular eclipses slightly outnumber total ones); the preset's label is what is wrong.

It then reaches the student at `solarOutcome.textContent = outcomeLabel(derived.solarType)` (main.ts:525) = "Annular solar" (`logic.ts:136`), and `contextualMessage` prints "Annular solar eclipse! Moon at New Moon, 0.0 deg from nearest node." (`logic.ts:184`).

4. Not already fixed or guarded. `git log -3` on main.ts/logic.ts/eclipseGeometryModel.ts shows 7f51806, 9d35e40, 4fc1740 — none touches presets or distance. The demo's own model notes (`index.html:298-300`) say only "at perigee a central solar eclipse can be total; at apogee it can be annular" — they never claim mean is total, so nothing in the demo defends the button's promise. Readiness is `status: draft` / `readiness: experimental` (`apps/site/src/content/demos/eclipse-geometry.md:3,10`), so there is no readiness-honesty aggravation.
