findings.title: Theorist HR axis titles say log(...) while the tick labels are the un-logged values (positions are correct)
findings.evidence: main.ts:725 draws the y tick labels as `ctx.fillText(`10^${Math.round(Math.log10(tick))}`, ...)` over `yTicks.push(...logTicks(-4, 6))`, producing "10^-4" ... "10^6". main.ts:732 then titles that axis `ctx.fillText("log(L/L_sun)", 0, 0)`. The tick values ARE L/L_sun, not log(L/L_sun): the tick drawn "10^6" is at yNorm = (log10(1e6)+5)/11 = 0.9091, i.e. log L = 6, not log L = 10^6. The x axis has the identical defect: main.ts:719 labels ticks `${Math.round(tick).toLocaleString()} K` giving "3,000 K" ... "40,000 K", and main.ts:728 titles it "log(T_eff [K])". The exhibit copy repeats the claim (stars-zams-hr.md model_notes: "Theorist HR mode uses base-10 logarithmic axes: log(L/L_sun) versus log(T_eff)").
findings.scenario: A student in Theorist HR mode reads the y axis title "log(L/L_sun)" and the tick "10^0" next to the Sun's position, and concludes log(L/L_sun) = 1 for a solar-luminosity star (the true value is 0). The same student reads the x tick "40,000 K" under the title "log(T_eff [K])" and concludes log T_eff = 40,000. The exhibit's own misconception list includes "Logarithmic axes distort physics rather than reveal dynamic range", so this is the one labelling convention the demo must model correctly.
findings.fix: Make the titles agree with the ticks, in one place each, and leave the (correct) coordinate math alone. In apps/demos/src/demos/stars-zams-hr/main.ts: line 728 "log(T_eff [K])" -> "T_eff [K] (log scale)" and line 732 "log(L/L_sun)" -> "L/L_sun (log scale)". Keep the existing tick labels at 719 and 725 ("3,000 K ... 40,000 K"; "10^-4 ... 10^6"), since they already carry units and decade notation. Reword the caption at main.ts:838 to match: "Theorist HR mode: L/L_sun vs T_eff on log axes, with hotter stars to the left and optional constant-radius guides." Keep it ASCII -- the canvas is the one surface exempted from the KaTeX-only rule in CLAUDE.md, and Unicode glyphs there would be a separate violation. The finder's alternative (keep "log(...)" titles and relabel y ticks "-4 ... 6") is also internally consistent, but it would force the x ticks to lose their "K" unit and become "3.5 ... 4.6", which is a worse read for an intro course; do not mix the two. Optional consistency pass, not required for correctness: apps/demos/src/demos/stars-zams-hr/README.md:6 and apps/site/src/content/demos/stars-zams-hr.md:41 describe the axes as logarithmic, which is true -- reword only so the public copy and the on-canvas titles use the same phrasing. No test asserts these strings, so no test update is needed; add one design-contract assertion on the axis-title strings if you want the fix pinned.
findings.note: CONFIRMED as a real labelling defect, but severity is overstated. The quoted code exists verbatim: apps/demos/src/demos/stars-zams-hr/main.ts:719 draws x ticks as `${Math.round(tick).toLocaleString()} K` over xTicks = [3000, 5000, 10000, 20000, 40000] (main.ts:512); main.ts:725 draws y ticks as `10^${Math.round(Math.log10(tick))}` over yTicks = logTicks(-4, 6), and logic.ts:174-180 confirms logTicks returns 10**exp, so the tick values are 1e-4 ... 1e6 L_sun; main.ts:728 and main.ts:732 title those axes "log(T_eff [K])" and "log(L/L_sun)". I re-derived hrCoordinates (logic.ts:84-113, THEORIST_AXIS_LIMITS teffMinK 2500 K, teffMaxK 50000 K, logLumMin -5, logLumMax 6) in node independently of the finder: y tick "10^0" (1 L_sun, log10 = 0) -> yNorm = 0.4545; y tick "10^6" (1e6 L_sun, log10 = 6) -> yNorm = 1.0000 (the finder's 0.9091 is wrong arithmetic -- that is the 10^5 tick); x tick "40,000 K" (log10 T = 4.602) -> xNorm = 0.0745; the Sun (5772 K, 1 L_sun) lands at xNorm 0.7207, yNorm 0.4545, i.e. exactly log(L/L_sun) = 0. So the axes ARE correctly log-scaled and every plotted quantity -- stars (main.ts:623), evolution track (main.ts:686), constant-radius guides (main.ts:556) -- sits at its correct log position. Nothing is mis-computed and nothing is mis-drawn; the only defect is that the two axis titles name the logarithm while the tick labels name the un-logged quantity. That is misleading on-canvas copy, not a wrong number a student would read off the plot (P1), and the finder's x-axis failure scenario is not credible: the tick label carries the unit "K" ("40,000 K"), which cannot be read as log T_eff = 40,000. The y-axis misread ("10^0" under title "log(L/L_sun)") is the credible half. Reachability confirmed: Theorist mode is a one-click chip (index.html:75 #modeTheorist, handler main.ts:1192), default plotMode is "observer" (main.ts:259), and apps/site/src/content/demos/stars-zams-hr.md play_steps explicitly tells students to switch, so the path is live and unguarded. Not already fixed: git log -3 on main.ts shows 0f75490 (Biome lint), 19baaf9 (three physics fixes in spectral lines/EOS/HR lab) and 2150874 (typecheck) -- none touched the axis titles, and grep found no guard. No test pins the strings (grep over the demo folder found the wording only in main.ts:728/732/838, README.md:6 and the exhibit md:41), so the fix cannot break a test. Readiness is honest here, which further caps severity: stars-zams-hr.md has status: draft, readiness: experimental, readinessReason "launch-gate QA remain in progress". One correction to the finder's framing: apps/site/src/content/demos/stars-zams-hr.md:41 ("uses base-10 logarithmic axes: log(L/L_sun) versus log(T_eff)") is a true statement about the axes being logarithmic and is standard shorthand for an HR diagram -- it does not repeat the defect and does not need correcting, only reconciling with the new on-canvas wording.

findings.title: Guide labels are misplaced twice: hardcoded positions never derived from the model, drawn against the wrong frame
findings.evidence: GUIDE_REGIONS (logic.ts:200-241) hardcodes xNorm/yNorm per label; main.ts:758-779 places each at `left: xNorm*100%`, `top: (1-yNorm)*100%`. Inverting the axis maps myself: theorist "Main sequence" at (0.42, 0.46) lands at Teff = 14,208 K, L = 1.15 L_sun, but the Tout ZAMS at 14,208 K is M = 3.74 M_sun, L = 183.5 L_sun -> yNorm = 0.660, so the label naming the band sits 0.20 of the plot height below it while its own hint reads "Most stars lie along this diagonal band". Theorist "White dwarf region" at (0.18, 0.16) lands at Teff = 29,160 K; the model's actual white dwarfs in the default population come out at 9,581 K, 9,551 K and 13,302 K -> xNorm 0.55, i.e. the label is 0.37 of the plot WIDTH away. In the DEFAULT observer mode, "Giant branch" at (0.76, 0.78) lands at B-V = 1.804, M_V = -3.62, while the only giant in the default population is at (B-V = 1.48, M_V = +1.01) and the brightest star of any kind is near M_V = +1 -- the label is 4.6 mag (16% of the 29-mag frame) above everything drawn. Separately, .guide-overlay is `inset: 0` on .hr-plot (style.css:139-143) while the canvas reserves margins of 74/26/28/68 px (main.ts:487), so even a correct xNorm/yNorm would be mis-placed: at a 700x525 canvas, left:42% = 294 px corresponds to data xNorm (294-74)/600 = 0.367, not 0.42.
findings.scenario: Guide mode is ON by default. A first-time student in the default Observer CMD view reads the label "Giant branch -- The bright, redder giant branch sits up and to the right" placed 4.6 magnitudes above any plotted star, scans that empty region, finds nothing, and either concludes the diagram is broken or mis-identifies the brightest main-sequence turnoff stars as giants. Switching to Theorist HR, the "White dwarf region" label sits at 29,000 K while the demo's white dwarfs are at 9,500-13,300 K, so the student labels the wrong clump.
findings.fix:
Derive the positions from the rendered population and kill the dual coordinate system, rather than re-hardcoding against physical anchors.

1. In logic.ts:200-241, delete `xNorm`/`yNorm` from `GUIDE_REGIONS` and from the `GuideRegion` type (logic.ts:10-15), keeping `label` and `hint` — the copy is good, only the coordinates are wrong. Removing the fields from the type is what stops a stale position reappearing.

2. In main.ts, position each label from the points actually drawn. After `plottedPoints` is built, group the in-frame points by stage (ms; giant + supergiant; white_dwarf) and take the MEDIAN xNorm and median yNorm per group (median, not mean, so one binary-blended outlier cannot drag the label off the band). This works unchanged in both modes because the points already carry normalized coordinates for whichever space is active. Do not anchor to fixed physical values as the finding proposes: besides needing new exports from stellarLifetimeModel.ts, a fixed anchor is wrong for most of the control range the student can reach — a 12.5 Gyr cluster has no 2 M_sun giant, and a 0.05 Gyr cluster has no white dwarfs at all.

3. Skip any label whose group has fewer than ~3 in-frame members. On the default 0.7 Gyr population that drops "Giant branch" (one giant) and would drop "White dwarf region" on a young cluster. Suppressing a label for a structure the diagram does not contain is the honest outcome and is the single biggest pedagogical win here.

4. Fix the frame by removing the second coordinate system instead of patching it: draw the guide labels on the canvas inside `drawPlot`, using the same `xPx`/`yPx` closures (main.ts:504-505) that place the stars. A frame mismatch then becomes impossible by construction. These labels contain no math, so the repo's canvas-text exemption in CLAUDE.md applies cleanly; keep ASCII. If the DOM overlay must stay for styling, then publish the plot rect from `drawPlot` and position against `margin.left + xNorm*plotWidth` / `margin.top + (1-yNorm)*plotHeight`, and add `transform: translate(-50%, -50%)` to `.guide-overlay__label` (style.css:145) so the anchor is the box centre rather than its top-left corner — but the canvas route is preferable because it leaves one source of truth for the mapping.

5. Add the test that is currently missing. logic.test.ts:196-207 only checks label strings, so it would stay green through all of this. Assert instead that, for the default seed, every emitted guide label lies within ~0.08 norm of at least 3 plotted members of the stage it names, in BOTH plot modes. Confirm it RED against today's code first: the Theorist "Main sequence" label is 0.176 norm from the nearest MS star and the Observer "Giant branch" label is 0.16 norm (4.63 mag) from the only giant, so a correct test fails now.
findings.note:
CONFIRMED — I could not refute any part of it, and every number reproduced independently.

CODE EXISTS AS QUOTED. `GUIDE_REGIONS` with hardcoded `xNorm`/`yNorm` is at apps/demos/src/demos/stars-zams-hr/logic.ts:200-241. `renderGuideOverlay` at main.ts:757-778 sets `label.style.left = \`${region.xNorm * 100}%\`` and `label.style.top = \`${(1 - region.yNorm) * 100}%\`` (main.ts:766-767). `const margin = { left: 74, right: 26, top: 28, bottom: 68 }` is at main.ts:487 exactly. `.guide-overlay { position: absolute; inset: 0 }` is at style.css:139-143, on `.hr-plot` (index.html:23, 42), which has no padding (style.css:66-70).

MY OWN RECOMPUTATION (plain JS, not the finder's arithmetic). Inverting hrCoordinates (logic.ts:84-110) with THEORIST_AXIS_LIMITS (logic.ts:17-21): label (0.42,0.46) -> Teff = 14,208 K, L = 1.148 L_sun. I reimplemented Tout 1996 from packages/physics/src/zamsTout1996Model.ts (sanity: M = 1 gives L = 0.698 L_sun, Teff = 5,597 K, the correct ZAMS zero-age values) and bisected: the ZAMS at 14,208 K is M = 3.737 M_sun, L = 183.5 L_sun -> yNorm = 0.6603, so the miss is 0.2003 of plot height = 2.20 dex in L. I then rebuilt the whole seeded generator in plain JS (mulberry32/hashSeed from seededRandom.ts, Hurley t_MS, Pecaut-Mamajek colour, Torres BC_V, the post-MS track and Mestel WD cooling from stellarLifetimeModel.ts) and regenerated the exact default population (N = 320, seed "hr-lab-42", cluster 0.7 Gyr, binaryFrac 0.28, Z = 0.02, 140 pc, photErr 0.03 — DEFAULTS at main.ts:76-86). It reproduces the finder's population to the digit: 316 ms / 3 white_dwarf / 1 giant; WDs at Teff 9,581 K, 9,551 K, 13,302 K; the single giant at M = 2.46 M_sun, B-V = 1.48, M_V = +1.01; brightest star of any stage M_V = +1.01. FRAME OFFSET CONFIRMED. `.guide-overlay__label` (style.css:145-158) has NO centering transform — the `transform: translate(-50%, ...)` at style.css:173 belongs to `.plot-tooltip`, a different element — so left/top is the box's top-left corner. REACHABLE AND UNGUARDED. `plotMode: "observer"`, `guideMode: true` at main.ts:259-260, so guide mode is ON in the default Observer CMD. No clamp or guard; `git log -5` on logic.ts/main.ts/style.css shows no fix and `git status` shows no uncommitted change. The only test touching this, logic.test.ts:196-207, asserts the three label STRINGS and `hint.length > 10` and never checks a position — it pins nothing, exactly the repo's documented "tests encode defects" pattern.

CORRECTIONS THAT SHARPEN IT (none refute it):
1. Scope is narrower than "all labels point at empty diagram" AT THE INTENDED COORDINATES: 2 of 6 are roughly right. Observer "Main sequence" (0.43,0.46) has an MS star 0.013 norm away (B-V 0.81, M_V 5.79), and Observer "White dwarf region" (0.17,0.19) is within 0.03-0.08 of the real WDs. findings.title: Cluster richness is too low for a giant branch: 0-2 of 320 stars at every preset, while four places tell students to identify one
findings.evidence: generatePopulation samples sampleMassMsun over MASS_MIN_MSUN = 0.1 to MASS_MAX_MSUN = 50 with dN/dM ~ M^-2.35 and applies no magnitude limit. I reproduced the generator in node (same mulberry32/hashSeed, same Hurley/Cummings/Mestel track) and averaged over 5 seeds at N = 320: giants per population are 0.0 at 0.08 Gyr (the "Young cluster" preset), 1.0 at 0.7 Gyr (the default), 0.2 at 1 Gyr, 0.6 at 4.6 Gyr ("Solar-like reference"), 0.8 at 10 Gyr ("Old cluster") and 0.0 at 14 Gyr. The default seeded population ('hr-lab-42', 0.7 Gyr) is exactly {ms: 316, white-dwarf: 3, giant: 1}; the "Old cluster" preset gives {ms: 312, white-dwarf: 8, giant: 0}. The cause is arithmetic: at 10 Gyr the giant window is M in [1.025, 1.093] M_sun, and the Salpeter fraction of that interval is (1.0253^-1.35 - 1.0928^-1.35)/(0.1^-1.35 - 50^-1.35) = 0.0783/22.382 = 0.0035, i.e. 1.1 stars of 320. Even at the N = 1200 maximum it is only 1.8-2.4 giants.
findings.scenario: Step 1 of the Step Guide (index.html:356), the first Help bullet (main.ts:1397), and exhibit play_steps[0] all instruct: "identify the main sequence, giant-branch, and white-dwarf structures". A student presses the "Old cluster" preset -- the one whose stated purpose is an evolved population -- and gets zero giants. There is no giant branch to identify at any setting the UI offers, so the demo's opening task cannot be completed and the guide label naming the branch points at empty space.
findings.fix:
Richness, not a magnitude limit, is the dominant lever; a bright cut deletes the white-dwarf sequence (verified: WDs at M_V 12.7-17.8 vs giants at M_V ~ 1 at 10 Gyr).

1. Raise cluster richness. apps/demos/src/demos/stars-zams-hr/index.html:135 caps populationSize at 1200; lift the ceiling to ~20000 and raise the cluster-mode default. At N = 5000 and 10 Gyr I get 10.4 giants, 188 white dwarfs and ~4 Hertzsprung-gap stars: all three structures populated, the lower main sequence intact, and the gap still correctly near-empty. This is also the honest physical reason real cluster CMDs show a branch - only 6.02% of a 0.1-50 Msun Salpeter draw is above 0.8 Msun, so today's default "cluster" has 19 stars in the mass range where readable CMD structure lives, which is not a cluster CMD at all.

2. Add a limiting magnitude only as a second, separate student-facing control, since "we plot only stars brighter than M_V = x" is genuinely the measurement lesson Observer mode exists to teach - but keep it faint enough to retain the cooling sequence (M_V ~ 18 at 10 Gyr), and state it in the plot caption and in apps/site/src/content/demos/stars-zams-hr.md model_notes.

3. Cheap interim guard, worth doing either way: make the caption (main.ts:842-845, which today reports only out-of-frame culls) print the live stage census - "1 giant, 3 white dwarfs of 320" - and suppress the "Giant branch" guide label when the population contains none. getGuideRegions (logic.ts:243-245) is a static constant taking no population argument, so it needs a count parameter.

4. Separate, smaller defect found while verifying: the guide label's position is wrong even when giants exist. logic.ts:211-212 puts it at xNorm 0.76, yNorm 0.78, which on THEORIST_AXIS_LIMITS is T ~ 5130 K and L ~ 3800 Lsun, whereas the model's own branch runs 4700 K down to 3200 K up to RGB_TIP_LSUN = 2500 (stellarLifetimeModel.ts:215, :318-334), i.e. xNorm ~ 0.84-0.92. File as its own finding.

5. Also separate: buildEvolutionTrack (main.ts:311-350) is a second, inline, hand-rolled post-MS track (giantEnd = 1.12*tMs, luminosityLsun = msL*(0.72+0.85*fraction)) that never calls postMainSequenceTrack and disagrees with the population model (1.12 t_MS vs 1.15 t_BGB). That violates "all physics from @cosmic/physics" and one-source-of-truth. It is, however, the one place a student can currently see a giant branch at all, which partially mitigates the task failure above.

6. Anna's call, not the agent's: cluster richness, any IMF floor change, and any limiting magnitude are scientific assumptions under CLAUDE.md. Propose them with the counts above and wait for approval before changing a default.
findings.note:
CONFIRMED, and understated. I re-derived everything from scratch rather than reusing the finder's arithmetic.

WHAT THE CODE DOES. Stage is decided by mass and age alone. `stageProperties` (packages/physics/src/hrInferencePopulationModel.ts:247-281) returns "ms" when ageMyr < t_MS, else delegates to `postMainSequenceTrack` (packages/physics/src/stellarLifetimeModel.ts:348-409), which returns white-dwarf/null at ageMyr >= t_BGB*(1+POST_BGB_FRACTION) with POST_BGB_FRACTION = 0.15 (:209), "hertzsprung-gap" for ageMyr < t_BGB, and "giant"/"supergiant" otherwise (:388-408). So the giant window in age is exactly t_BGB(M) <= age < 1.15*t_BGB(M), a 15% window, and t_MS >= 0.95*t_BGB (:35, :60) makes the subgiant window at most 5%. Masses come from `sampleMassMsun` with dN/dM ~ M^-2.35 over MASS_MIN_MSUN = 0.1 to MASS_MAX_MSUN = 50 (:56-57, :73-80, called at :311). No magnitude limit anywhere.

MY NUMBERS (node, exact Salpeter integral over the window, p = 1-2.35 = -1.35, a = 0.1^-1.35 = 22.3872, b = 50^-1.35 = 0.005086). Expected giants at N = 320: 0.11 (young-cluster, 0.08 Gyr, window M in [5.607, 5.963] Msun), 0.29 (default/high-binary/low-Z, 0.7 Gyr, [2.398, 2.522]), 0.55 (solar-like-reference, 4.6 Gyr, [1.290, 1.345]), 0.67 (old-cluster, 10 Gyr, [1.0393, 1.0787]), 0.72 (slider max, 14 Gyr). Supergiants are 0 at every preset age (they need M >= 8 Msun on the branch, i.e. age ~ t_BGB(8) = 37.3 Myr, below the youngest preset). Subgiants are 0.01-0.27. So the MODAL outcome is zero giants at every preset, and the whole post-main-sequence region is empty.

I also replicated the seeded generator exactly (hashSeed/mulberry32, draw order 1 mass + 1 binary test [+1 q] + 4 for two gaussianUnit calls; note `stageProperties` receives `random` at :318 but never destructures or calls it, so it consumes no draws). TWO CORRECTIONS TO THE FINDER'S EVIDENCE. (1) Their 10 Gyr window [1.0253, 1.0928] is too wide; the code's window is [1.0393, 1.0787], Salpeter fraction 2.078e-3, i.e. 0.66 giants of 320, not the 1.1 they quote. Their arithmetic is 1.7x too generous, so the defect is worse than claimed. (2) "0.0 at 14 Gyr" is a 5-seed fluke; the expectation at 14 Gyr is 0.72 giants.

LINE ANCHORS ARE OFF (substance unaffected). hrInferencePopulationModel.ts:256 is a blank line inside `stageProperties`; the sampling lives at :56-57 and :311. Step 1 is index.html:353, not :356. The Help bullet is main.ts:1400, not :1397.

REACHABLE. Yes, in the default view with no interaction. The plot caption (main.ts:842-845) reports only out-of-frame culls, never a stage census, so nothing tells the student the branch is empty.

NOT ALREADY FIXED OR GUARDED. git log -3 on both model files (e61f76f, 2b3f086, ea62d4d) touches the colour relation, the white-dwarf/supergiant extension and the lifetime unification; none adds a magnitude limit or raises richness. No test pins a populated giant branch: the only post-MS count assertion is `remnants.length > 0` at hrInferencePopulationModel.test.ts:201, and it reaches for N = 5000 — above the UI's own 1200 ceiling — which is itself evidence the authors knew the evolved fractions are tiny at the sizes the UI offers and never carried that back.

SEVERITY CORRECTED P0 -> P1. No number, equation or drawing is physically wrong: the IMF, the Hurley timescales and the post-MS track all behave as designed, and a 320-star Salpeter draw down to 0.1 Msun genuinely contains well under one giant. The page is not broken. The defect is a task/sampling-design mismatch plus a static label asserting a structure the data lacks, which is the P1 band (misleading copy / architecture defect that keeps producing the same class of problem). The demo also already carries status: draft and readiness: experimental (stars-zams-hr.md:3, :10), so no public readiness claim is being broken; it would become P0 on promotion. It is top-of-P1 and blocking for launch-ready, since the default view fails the demo's own opening task.

THE PROPOSED FIX WOULD BREAK SOMETHING ELSE. But I computed where the model's own white dwarfs sit at 10 Gyr by running whiteDwarfPoint's arithmetic (Mestel cooling, the 3900 K floor, the Stefan-Boltzmann consistency recompute, then Torres BC_V): M_V = 12.69 for a 1.1 Msun progenitor and 16.5 to 17.8 for 1.3 to 7.9 Msun, against the giants at M_V ~ 1.0. An M_V < 5 cut deletes every white dwarf in the diagram, i.e. the third structure the same Step 1 sentence names. Raising MASS_MIN_MSUN has the same effect plus it removes the lower main sequence that Step 3 (mass gradient) and the OBSERVER_AXIS_LIMITS note (logic.ts:24-39) both depend on.

findings.title: Constant-radius guides clamp onto the frame edge instead of ending there — currently invisible because the 1.5px plot border is stroked over them
findings.evidence: main.ts:543-585 walks each R in RADIUS_GUIDE_VALUES_RSUN = [0.01, 0.1, 1, 10, 100, 1000] across the full Teff range and plots via hrCoordinates, whose return is clamped: `xNorm: clamp(..., 0, 1)` and `yNorm: clamp(..., 0, 1)` (logic.ts:110-111). A constant-radius line is log L = 2 log R + 4 log(T/5772), so I solved for where each crosses logLumMax = 6: R = 1000 R_sun crosses at T = 5772 K, and the axis runs to 50,000 K, so from 5772 K to 50,000 K -- log(50000/5772)/log(50000/2500) = 0.937/1.301 = 72% of the x-axis -- the line is clamped to yNorm = 1 and drawn as a horizontal dashed segment along the top border, labelled `R = 1000.00 R_sun` (main.ts:581). R = 100 R_sun crosses at T = 18,253 K and is flat over 34% of the x-axis; R = 0.01 R_sun crosses logLumMin = -5 at T = 3246 K and is flat along the bottom over 9%.
findings.scenario: Step 4 of the demo's own Start Here workflow is "Turn on radius lines". A student does so in Theorist HR mode and sees a dashed line labelled R = 1000 R_sun running horizontally at constant luminosity across three quarters of the diagram, and a second at R = 100 R_sun across a third of it. The inference the control exists to teach -- that at fixed radius L rises as T^4, so a constant-radius locus is a steep diagonal -- is contradicted by the drawing: the student reads "same radius means same luminosity".
findings.fix:
Fix it, but as a P2 latent-geometry cleanup, and do it together with the live `inFrame` bug at main.ts:630 — that is what makes the change worth making now.

1. In logic.ts:81-112, have `hrCoordinates` return `inFrame` the way `cmdCoordinates` already does (logic.ts:143): compute `xRaw`/`yRaw`, set `inFrame = xRaw >= 0 && xRaw <= 1 && yRaw >= 0 && yRaw <= 1`, and also return the unclamped values (e.g. `xRaw`/`yRaw`) so callers can draw a segment that exits the frame.

2. NOTE THE FINDER'S FIX IS INCOMPLETE: `xPx`/`yPx` at main.ts:505-506 clamp independently (`clamp(xNorm, 0, 1)`). Removing the clamp from `hrCoordinates` alone changes nothing, because the pixel mappers re-clamp. 3. In the main.ts:543-566 loop, break the path on any out-of-frame sample (`started = false` and `ctx.beginPath()`/`ctx.stroke()` per in-frame run) so each guide is drawn only over the temperature interval where it is inside the axes.

4. DO NOT relocate the labels. I verified all six already sit in-frame at labelTeff = 3800 K (yNorm 0.025-0.934), on the diagonal portion of every curve. The finder's "place each label at the midpoint of the in-frame span" is unnecessary churn and would move labels that are currently correct.

5. Same change fixes main.ts:630: once `hrCoordinates` returns `inFrame`, the `"inFrame" in norm` guard goes live in theorist mode, stars stop piling onto the HR frame edges (where, unlike the guide lines, nothing overpaints them and they are individually unselectable), and the main.ts:843-844 out-of-frame caption starts reporting in HR mode.

Why this is not P0/P1: the wrong path is masked by a coincidence of draw order and line widths (frame lineWidth 1.5 > guide lineWidth 1.2, stroked afterwards in opaque `--cp-text`). It becomes a visible wrong drawing the moment anyone thins the frame below 1.2px, changes `margin.top`, or adds an axis-zoom control — so fix it, but it is not currently teaching a student anything false.
findings.note:
CODE CONFIRMED, GEOMETRY CONFIRMED, FAILURE SCENARIO REFUTED.

1) Quoted code exists verbatim. `apps/demos/src/demos/stars-zams-hr/main.ts:543` is the `for (const radiusRsun of RADIUS_GUIDE_VALUES_RSUN)` loop; it samples 101 points across the full Teff range (main.ts:546-556) and maps each via `hrCoordinates` (main.ts:561), whose return is clamped at `apps/demos/src/demos/stars-zams-hr/logic.ts:110-111` (`xNorm: clamp(...,0,1)`, `yNorm: clamp(...,0,1)`), with no `inFrame` flag. `RADIUS_GUIDE_VALUES_RSUN = [0.01,0.1,1,10,100,1000]` at logic.ts:39. `T_SUN_K = ZamsTout1996Model.CONSTANTS.tSunK` (main.ts:88) = 5772 K (packages/physics/src/zamsTout1996Model.ts:38). Labels at main.ts:568-585.

2) Independent recomputation (my own node run, not the finder's arithmetic). L/L_sun = R^2 (T/T_sun)^4, T_sun = 5772 K, axes Teff 2500-50000 K, log L -5 to 6, xNorm = (log Tmax - log T)/(log Tmax - log Tmin):
 - R = 1000 R_sun crosses log L = 6 at T = 5772 K; clamped to yNorm = 1 from 5772 K to 50000 K = 72.1% of the x-axis (kink at xNorm = 0.721).
 - R = 100 R_sun crosses at T = 18253 K; clamped over 33.6%.
 - R = 0.01 R_sun crosses log L = -5 at T = 3246 K; clamped at yNorm = 0 over 8.7%.
 All three match the finder's numbers. The clamped path segments are real.

3) Reachable: checkbox `#showRadiusLines` (index.html:87), gate `getRadiusLinesVisible` = plotMode === "theorist" && preference (logic.ts:247-252), and Start Here step "Turn on radius lines" (index.html:388). No caller anywhere in main.ts passes `teffMinK/teffMaxK/logLumMin/logLumMax` overrides, so the geometry is fixed.

4) WHY THE P0 SCENARIO FAILS. yPx(1) = margin.top + (1-1)*plotHeight = margin.top = 28 exactly (main.ts:487, 506), so the clamped run lands precisely on the frame's top edge — and main.ts:709-711 strokes `strokeRect(margin.left, margin.top, ...)` with `strokeStyle = text` (opaque `--cp-text`) and `lineWidth = 1.5` AFTER the guides (ctx.save at 538, restore at 587; I checked 485-711 for an early return — there is none). A 1.5px opaque stroke centered on the same row fully contains the 1.2px dashed stroke. My overdraw computation of residual guide weight per device row: dpr 1 -> 15% on each of two rows; dpr 2 -> 0% on the two covered rows, 10% on the two outermost antialiased rows. The bottom clamp (R = 0.01) lands on yPx(0) = margin.top + plotHeight = the same strokeRect's bottom edge, likewise overpainted. So the student sees the curve terminate at the frame — the correct appearance — not "a dashed line at constant luminosity across three quarters of the diagram."

5) The label claim is also wrong. I computed all six labels at the fixed labelTeff = 3800 K: yNorm = 0.025, 0.207, 0.389, 0.570, 0.752, 0.934 — every one in-frame, at xNorm = 0.860, which is to the RIGHT of the R = 1000 kink at xNorm = 0.721. No label sits on a flat segment; `R = 1000.00 R_sun` is printed on the diagonal portion.

6) Not already fixed: git log -3 on main.ts (0f75490, 19baaf9, 2150874) and logic.ts (2b3f086, 19baaf9, 6eb6e6d) show no guard added; logic.test.ts:92 only asserts the array contents.

ADJACENT, HIGHER-VALUE DEFECT FOUND WHILE VERIFYING (separate from #53, worth its own entry): main.ts:630 reads `if ("inFrame" in norm && !norm.inFrame)`, but in theorist mode `norm` comes from `hrCoordinates` (main.ts:623), which returns no `inFrame` property — so the cull is dead in HR mode and population stars are still clamped onto the frame edges as filled 3.7px dots, which nothing overpaints, and the "N of M stars fall outside these axis limits" caption (main.ts:843-844) can never fire in HR mode. Only the CMD path (cmdCoordinates, logic.ts:143) is actually protected.

findings.title: Zoom divides away computeFovArcsec's `3 * separationArcsec` framing term, so 10 of 12 presets crop the binary out of the drawn field at the default zoom of 6 — nine render an almost black canvas (Hubble: brightest pixel 7/255) under a "Resolved" badge, and amateur-200mm a featureless bright wash
findings.evidence: main.ts:374-376 `const fovArcsec = computeFovArcsec(model.thetaEffArcsec, sep); const zoomedFovArcsec = zoomedFov(fovArcsec, state.zoom);` and logic.ts:103-105 `return fovArcsec / clamp(zoom, 1, 20);`. computeFovArcsec includes a `3 * separationArcsec` term precisely to keep the pair in frame, and zoomedFov then destroys that guarantee. I replicated drawPsf's exact pixel loop in node. Hubble preset (D = 2.4 m), visible band, default separation 1 arcsec, default zoom 6: theta_diff = 5.767e-2 arcsec, fov = max(0.4, max(6*0.0577, 3*1)) = 3.0000 arcsec, zoomed fov = 0.5000 arcsec, half-field = 0.2500 arcsec, stars at +/-0.5000 arcsec -> both outside the frame; brightest pixel in the whole 420x420 bitmap = 7/255. At zoom 20 it is 4/255. Keck (10 m), separation 0.1 arcsec, zoom 6: half-field 0.0333 arcsec vs star at 0.0500 arcsec, brightest pixel 36/255 (at zoom 1 the same case gives 219/255). The pair stays in frame only while fov >= zoom*sep, i.e. theta_eff >= 1 arcsec at the default zoom and separation, i.e. D <= 1.22*5.5e-5*206265 cm = 13.84 cm = 0.138 m. Of the 12 presets only `eye` (0.007 m) and `binoculars` (0.05 m) satisfy that; amateur-200mm, hubble, jwst, keck, tmt, elt, gbt, arecibo, vla and eht do not.
findings.scenario: A student opens the demo, picks "Hubble Space Telescope (2.4 m)" from the preset list — the first thing the exhibit's play_steps tell them to do — and the stage goes black while the badge reads "Resolved" and the readouts show theta_diff = 0.0577, separation = 1.0000. They conclude either that the demo is broken or that a resolved pair looks like nothing at all. Worse, the exhibit's headline learning goal is "Distinguish magnification from resolution": dragging the zoom slider makes the stars vanish instead of showing a blurred blob getting bigger, so the demo teaches the opposite of its stated lesson.
findings.note:
CONFIRMED, with one factual correction and a severity correction. I could not refute any load-bearing part of it.

1) Quoted code exists verbatim. `/Users/anna/Teaching/cosmic-playground/apps/demos/src/demos/telescope-resolution/main.ts:374-376` is exactly `const fovArcsec = computeFovArcsec(model.thetaEffArcsec, sep); const zoomedFovArcsec = zoomedFov(fovArcsec, state.zoom);` and the zoomed value is what reaches `drawPsf({... fovArcsec: zoomedFovArcsec ...})` at main.ts:386. `logic.ts:96` is `Math.max(0.4, Math.min(500, Math.max(6 * thetaEffArcsec, 3 * separationArcsec)))` and `logic.ts:103-105` is `return fovArcsec / clamp(zoom, 1, 20);`. So the `3 * separationArcsec` framing term is computed and then divided away.

2) Independent recomputation (I did NOT reuse the finder's arithmetic). I wrote my own J1 — ascending power series for x<12, Hankel asymptotic for x>=12 — and cross-checked it against published values before using it: J1(1)=0.440050586 (ref 0.4400505857), J1(12)=-0.223447110 (ref -0.2234471044), J1(100)=-0.077145352 (ref -0.0771453); max deviation 1.5e-8. That is a different algorithm from the repo's Numerical-Recipes Chebyshev fit in `packages/physics/src/telescopeResolutionModel.ts:besselJ1Approx`, so the Airy values are independent. I then replicated drawPsf's 420x420 pixel loop (canvas size confirmed at index.html:155) including the `(i1+i2)/1.4` sum, the 0.45 gamma and the 0-255 rounding.
   - Hubble (D=2.4 m = 240 cm), visible band (lambda = 5.5e-5 cm), separation 1 arcsec, zoom 6, atmosphere off: theta_diff = 1.22*(5.5e-5/240)*206264.806 = 5.7668e-2 arcsec; theta_eff = same (seeing=0 so effectiveResolutionArcsec returns the diffraction limit); base fov = max(0.4, min(500, max(0.34601, 3.0))) = 3.0000 arcsec; zoomed fov = 0.50000 arcsec; half-field 0.25000 arcsec vs stars at +/-0.50000 arcsec -> both outside the drawn field; brightest pixel in the whole bitmap = 7/255, and 0.00% of the 176400 pixels reach 8/255. At zoom 20: 4/255. The finder's 7/255 and 4/255 reproduce exactly.
   - Keck (D=10 m), visible, separation 0.1 arcsec: zoom 6 -> half-field 0.033333 arcsec vs star at 0.050000 arcsec, brightest pixel 36/255; zoom 1 -> 219/255. Both of the finder's numbers reproduce exactly.
   - Threshold: the pair is framed iff fov0/zoom >= separation, i.e. fov0 >= zoom*separation. At separation 1 arcsec and zoom 6 that needs fov0 >= 6, and since 3*sep = 3 the only route is 6*theta_eff >= 6, i.e. theta_eff >= 1 arcsec, i.e. D <= 1.22*5.5e-5*206264.806 = 13.840 cm = 0.1384 m. Confirmed. Of the 12 entries in `packages/data-telescopes/src/telescopePresets.ts` only `eye` (0.007 m) and `binoculars` (0.05 m) clear it; amateur-200mm, hubble, jwst, keck, tmt, elt, gbt, arecibo, vla and eht all push the pair out of frame.
   - Zoom sweep for the Hubble default: the pair is framed only at zoom 1, 2 and 3 (at zoom 3 the stars sit exactly on the frame edge, half-field 0.500 = star 0.500). Zoom 4 through 20 -- 17 of the slider's 20 integer stops (index.html:64, min=1 max=20 step=1 value=6) -- crop the pair out: brightest pixel 19, 9, 7, 5, 4 /255 at zoom 4, 5, 6, 10, 20.

3) ONE FACTUAL CORRECTION to the finding. "Ten of the twelve presets render an almost black canvas" is off by one. Nine render an almost black canvas (hubble 7/255, jwst 2/255, keck 1/255, tmt/elt/gbt/arecibo/vla/eht 0/255). The tenth, amateur-200mm (D=0.2 m), fails differently: theta_diff = 0.69202 arcsec so the zoomed field (0.69202 arcsec) lies entirely inside the Airy core -- brightest pixel 203/255 and 100% of pixels above threshold, i.e. a uniformly bright featureless wash with no visible pair, not a black screen. The substantive claim -- 10 of 12 presets push the pair outside the drawn field and show no pair -- holds.

4) SECOND FACTUAL CORRECTION. The failure scenario says picking Hubble from the preset list is "the first thing the exhibit's play_steps tell them to do". It is not. `apps/site/src/content/demos/telescope-resolution.md:21-24` play_steps are "Compare two apertures and note what details become distinguishable", "Try to separate a close pair...", "Compare the effect of changing magnification vs changing aperture." No step names Hubble. This does not reduce reachability -- step 1 tells the student to change aperture, and step 3 tells them to change magnification, which are the two controls that trigger it -- but the narration is wrong.

5) Reachability: live and unguarded. `presetEl.addEventListener("change", ...)` at main.ts:481-489 sets only `state.apertureM`; it does not touch zoom, separation or band, so the default zoom 6 / separation 1 arcsec / visible band survive the preset change and the broken state is one dropdown click from load. No upstream clamp exists -- `grep` for `zoomedFov|computeFovArcsec` across the demo returns only the two definitions and the two call sites. `git log -5` on logic.ts/main.ts shows the last touches were a11y aria-pressed, the cp-chip migration and the logic.ts extraction; nothing has addressed this. The built page exists at `apps/site/public/play/telescope-resolution/index.html`, and `status: draft` demos are published with a badge rather than hidden (`apps/site/src/lib/readiness.ts`), so a student can reach it.

6) Why the existing tests miss it -- reading assertions, not names. `apps/demos/src/demos/telescope-resolution/logic.test.ts:377-446` has 14 assertions across `computeFovArcsec` and `zoomedFov`. Every one tests a function in isolation on synthetic numbers (`computeFovArcsec(10, 5)` -> 60, `zoomedFov(100, 5)` -> 20). Not one composes them, and not one ties either to a real preset aperture or to the invariant that the field must contain the pair. This is the repo's documented "tests encode defects" pattern: the framing guarantee is asserted nowhere, so dividing it away is invisible to the suite.

7) SEVERITY CORRECTION: P0 -> P1. Nothing numeric or physical is wrong -- theta_diff (0.0577), theta_eff, the resolved/marginal/unresolved status (ratio = 1/0.0577 = 17.3 >= 1 -> "Resolved", correct), and the FOV label ("FOV: 0.50 arcsec (6x)", correct) are all right and mutually consistent, and the page does not break. What fails is the rendering: the primary stage goes empty under a "Resolved" badge. By the audit's own rubric that is the P1 bucket -- an architecture defect (a framing invariant established in one function and destroyed by composing a second after it, with the composed invariant untested) producing a misleading rendering -- not the P0 bucket of a wrong number or a wrong drawing a student would believe. A student reads black-plus-"Resolved" as broken, not as a fact to internalize. Two further mitigations against P0: the demo is `status: draft` / `readiness: experimental` with readinessReason "parity and launch-gate signoff are still pending" (telescope-resolution.md:3,10-12), so there is no readiness-honesty overclaim here; and the FOV readout does print 0.50 arcsec next to a separation readout of 1.0000, so the contradiction is at least visible on screen. This is a high P1, close to the boundary: the finder is right that the demo's first learning goal is "Distinguish magnification from resolution" (md:15) and its named misconception is "More magnification always shows more detail" (md:19), so the zoom slider teaching the inverse over 17 of its 20 stops is a genuine pedagogical inversion and should be fixed before students see it.

8) The proposed fix would not work as written -- it trades a black canvas for a dead control. I evaluated `clamp(max(6*thetaEff/zoom, 1.5*sep), floor, 500)` numerically. It does keep the pair framed (half-field >= 0.75*sep > sep/2 always). But for the Hubble default case 6*thetaEff = 0.34601 arcsec while 1.5*sep = 1.5 arcsec, so the max() sits on the separation branch at every zoom from 1 to 20: fov = 1.500000 arcsec identically. The rendered bitmap is byte-identical at 1x and 20x while the label reads "(20x)", and the FOV readout prints the same arcsec number at both ends of the slider. Zoom goes inert from zoom 1 for hubble, keck and elt (any D >= about 0.6 m at separation 1 arcsec), from zoom 3 for amateur-200mm and from zoom 12 for binoculars -- i.e. it dies on exactly the presets that motivated the fix, and it kills the one control whose whole purpose is the demo's headline learning goal. The finder's proposed test ("for every preset at every band the returned field satisfies fov/2 >= separation/2 at zoom 20") is trivially satisfied by the floor and would not detect the inertness. The fix also leaves `lowerFloor` undefined.

findings.title: Telescope presets' defaultWavelengthCm and apertureKind have no consumer, so picking a radio or mm instrument silently leaves the band at visible and nothing flags the unphysical pairing
findings.evidence: main.ts:482-490, the preset change handler, sets only `state.apertureM = preset.apertureM;` and never touches `state.bandId`. `defaultWavelengthCm` is declared at telescopePresets.ts:18, described in the field metadata at line 35, and populated for all 12 presets (RADIO_21CM_DEFAULT_CM = 21 for gbt/arecibo/vla, MM_1P3_DEFAULT_CM = 0.13 for eht) — and `grep -rn defaultWavelengthCm apps packages` returns hits only inside telescopePresets.ts itself. The band therefore stays at the initial `visible` (5.5e-5 cm). Recomputed: GBT, D = 100 m at 550 nm gives 1.22*5.5e-5/1e4 rad = 6.710e-9 rad = 1.384e-3 arcsec, and the readout prints "0.0014"; the correct value at 21 cm is 528.45 arcsec, a factor of 3.8e5. EHT, D = 1e7 m at 550 nm gives 1.384e-8 arcsec; at its own 1.3 mm it is 3.271e-5 arcsec, a factor of 2364. `apertureKind` (telescopePresets.ts:9) is dead in exactly the same way.
findings.scenario: A student selects "Green Bank Telescope (100 m)" to compare a radio dish with Keck, reads theta_diff = 0.0014 arcsec, and records in their Station Mode table that a radio telescope out-resolves Keck by a factor of ten. The real GBT is ~9 arcmin. Selecting "EHT (Earth diameter)" is worse: theta_diff reads 1.384e-8 arcsec (14 picoarcsec) and the canvas is pure black (brightest pixel 0/255, recomputed), so the one instrument whose entire fame is its angular resolution produces both a wrong number and an empty picture.
findings.fix:
The band-matching half of the proposed fix is sound: I verified every preset's defaultWavelengthCm is exactly equal to some wavelengthBands[i].wavelengthCm (5.5e-5 = visible, 2.2e-4 = near-ir, 21 = radio-21cm, 0.13 = mm-1p3), so the "nearest in log lambda" fallback never fires and is harmless dead code. Two corrections to the rest.

(a) Do not silently override the band. Overwriting state.bandId on every preset change destroys the "hold D fixed, sweep lambda" exploration the Wavelength fieldset exists for, and will surprise a student who set 21 cm and then switches dishes. Instead, in main.ts:482-490 set the band from preset.defaultWavelengthCm only while the student has not touched the chips (a `bandTouched` flag set in the handler at main.ts:149), and announce it in the existing statusEl live region — the same pattern render() already uses for the space-telescope/atmosphere note: "Switched to 21 cm, the band GBT observes in." That makes the change visible and reversible.

(b) Add the unphysical-pairing guard the demo actually lacks: when the selected band differs from the preset's defaultWavelengthCm by more than ~1 dex, show a one-line note next to the readout ("A 100 m dish does not observe at 550 nm — this is the diffraction limit of that aperture, not of the GBT"). This is what keeps the number from being believed, and it is needed whether or not (a) lands.

(c) The proposed dataset test is new infrastructure, not an edit: packages/data-telescopes has no test file and no test script (package.json has only typecheck, and there is no vitest dependency). Either add vitest to that package or put the cross-table assertion in the existing physics/demos test setup. Keep apertureKind only if something reads it — the readout says "Effective aperture D (m)" (main.ts:307) and never distinguishes a 36 km VLA baseline from a dish diameter, so either surface that distinction in the readout or delete the field.

(d) Separately, fix the empty canvas, which this change does not touch: in logic.ts:96-98 floor the field on theta_eff as well as separation (e.g. max(0.4, min(500, max(6*thetaEff, 3*sep))) is already there — the problem is that zoom then divides it, so clamp zoomedFov to at least a few times thetaEff), and/or integrate the Airy PSF over each pixel in main.ts:226-230 instead of point-sampling at pixel centers. Verified needed: brightest pixel is 0/255 for EHT at both 550 nm and its correct 1.3 mm, and only 7/255 for Hubble and 1/255 for Keck at their own visible band.
findings.note:
CORE CLAIM CONFIRMED, two sub-claims corrected.

(1) Code exists as quoted. apps/demos/src/demos/telescope-resolution/main.ts:482-490 is the preset `change` handler and sets only `state.apertureM = preset.apertureM;` (line 487). It never touches `state.bandId`. `state.bandId` is initialized to "visible" at main.ts:71-72/90 and is mutated in exactly one other place, the band-chip click handler at main.ts:149. Confirmed by reading, not by test names.

(3) Independently recomputed with my own node script, theta = 1.22*lambda/D * 206264.806 arcsec/rad:
- GBT, D = 100 m = 1e4 cm, lambda = 5.5e-5 cm: 1.3840e-3 arcsec. formatNumber(x,4) at logic.ts:42-48 takes the toFixed branch because |x| >= 1e-3, so the readout prints "0.0014". Correct.

- EHT, D = 1e7 m = 1e9 cm, 5.5e-5 cm: 1.3840e-8 arcsec, printed "1.384e-8" (toExponential branch, < 1e-3); at 1.3 mm: 3.2714e-5 arcsec. Ratio 2.3636e3, matching the claimed 2364.
- Keck at a shared visible band: 1.3840e-2 arcsec, so GBT does read exactly 10x "better". The finder's Keck framing is slightly off in detail: keck/jwst/tmt/elt carry defaultWavelengthCm = 2.2e-4 cm (near-IR), not visible.

(4) Reachable: yes. Both controls are live and unguarded — the preset <select> (index.html:37-40 fieldset for the band, populated at main.ts:123-137) and the band chips. The aperture slider range is 0.007 to 1e7 m (main.ts:111, 494), so every preset value is in range. No clamp or warning anywhere pairs an instrument with a plausible band.

(5) Not already fixed. git log -5 on main.ts (3a97680, 5056cde, a53da49, 071aa5c, 48c3e98) is a11y/chip/refactor/starfield work; telescopePresets.ts has one commit (f26ad26, the original migration). No guard exists.

SUB-CLAIM REFUTED — the black canvas is real but is NOT caused by this bug and would NOT be fixed by the proposed fix. I reimplemented drawPsf (main.ts:201-266) exactly, with the real besselJ1Approx, on the 420x420 canvas (index.html:155) at the default state (sep = 1 arcsec, binary on, zoom 6, no atmosphere). Brightest pixel out of 255:
- EHT at 550 nm (the bug): 0 — as claimed.
- EHT at its CORRECT 1.3 mm: also 0.
- Arecibo 305 m at 550 nm: 0. VLA at 550 nm: 0.
- Hubble 2.4 m at 550 nm (its own natural band): 7. Keck 10 m at 550 nm: 1.
Cause: computeFovArcsec (logic.ts:96-98) floors the field at 3*separation = 3 arcsec, which the default zoom 6 shrinks to 0.5 arcsec, so the star centers at +/-0.5 arcsec fall outside the +/-0.25 arcsec half-field, and the sub-pixel Airy core (1.19e-3 arcsec/px) is missed by point sampling at pixel centers. This is an independent defect that degrades every aperture above ~2 m at any band.

SEVERITY CORRECTED P0 -> P1. The physics kernel is right: telescopeResolutionModel.ts:67-81 computes 1.22*lambda/D correctly for whatever lambda is selected, so no formula or number is wrong — the pairing is unphysical, not the arithmetic. The selected wavelength is disclosed in four places: the pressed chip (setBandButtonStates, main.ts:166-174, aria-pressed), the band note text (main.ts:344), the Station Mode row (main.ts:450-452) and the Copy Results export ("Wavelength band", "Wavelength (cm)", main.ts:306-309). The band is a deliberately independent control (index.html:37-39 fieldset "Wavelength"; help copy at index.html:200 "Shorter wavelength and larger aperture improve resolution"), which is defensible for teaching theta ~ lambda/D. And apps/site/src/content/demos/telescope-resolution.md declares `status: draft`, `readiness: experimental`, readinessReason "parity and launch-gate signoff are still pending" — so it carries the readiness badge and the "Active development" callout and makes no launch-ready claim; there is no readiness-honesty finding here. What survives is exactly the project's P1 definition: two populated dataset fields with zero consumers plus an unguarded instrument/band pairing — an architecture defect that will keep producing wrong-looking states.

findings.title: AstroConstants is not the single source of truth it claims: c defined 4x, k_B (erg/K) 4x, T_sun at 5 sites in 3 modules, and sigma_SB / G_cgs / M_sun / R_sun absent entirely — a DRY defect with no student-visible error today (worst drift 0.025%)
findings.evidence: astroConstants.ts:12 declares itself "Single source of truth for definitional constants". Yet c = 2.99792458e10 appears at astroConstants.ts:67 (PHOTON) and :94 (EOS) and stellarEosModel.ts:13, and as 2.998e10 at blackbodyRadiationModel.ts:5. k_B appears at astroConstants.ts:89, hydrostaticEquilibriumModel.ts:34, stellarEosModel.ts:8, blackbodyRadiationModel.ts:7 (as 1.381e-16) and spectralLineModel.ts:42 (as 8.617333e-5 eV/K). h appears at astroConstants.ts:68 and blackbodyRadiationModel.ts:6 (as 6.626e-27). T_sun = 5772 appears at blackbodyRadiationModel.ts:16, zamsTout1996Model.ts:38, and as a bare literal at stellarLifetimeModel.ts:338, :435 and :439. sigma_SB exists only at blackbodyRadiationModel.ts:8 (5.67e-5; exact 2 pi^5 k^4 / (15 h^3 c^2) = 5.6703744e-5), and G_cgs = 6.67430e-8, M_sun = 1.98847e33 and R_sun = 6.957e10 exist only at hydrostaticEquilibriumModel.ts:33-37. The blackbody module's 4-sig-fig values are self-inconsistent too: from its own h, c, k the Wien constant is 0.289708 cm K, not the 0.2898 it declares at line 9, a 3.2e-4 relative mismatch that puts the marked Wien peak 0.2 nm off the drawn Planck curve's actual maximum at 5772 K.
findings.scenario: A reviewer corrects k_B in AstroConstants to the current CODATA value and the blackbody and spectral-line demos silently keep their old numbers, because neither imports it. Today the divergence is only in the 4th digit, but the structure guarantees that any future correction lands in one place out of five, and a student comparing the blackbody demo's peak marker to its own spectrum sees them disagree.
findings.fix:
Do the consolidation, but drop the Wien framing and sequence it behind a pinning test.

1. Add to astroConstants.ts a SUN block (massG 1.98847e33, radiusCm 6.957e10, luminosityErgPerS, effectiveTemperatureK 5772 — IAU nominal) and a THERMO block (sigmaStefanBoltzmannErgPerSCm2K4, gravitationalConstantCgs 6.67430e-8). Derive sigma from 2 pi^5 k^4 / (15 h^3 c^2) using the existing PHOTON h, c and EOS k rather than hardcoding 5.67e-5; I get 5.6703744e-5 erg s^-1 cm^-2 K^-4.

2. Do NOT add a second radiation constant: astroConstants.ts:91 already has RADIATION_CONSTANT_A_ERG_CM3_K4 = 7.5657e-15. I verified 4 sigma / c = 7.5657333e-15 erg cm^-3 K^-4, agreeing to 4.4e-6, so replace that literal with the derivation in place.

3. For the Wien constant, derive b = hc/(x_W k_B) with x_W = 4.965114231744276 from the CODATA PHOTON/EOS values, giving 0.28977720 cm K. State in the commit that this is a 7.9e-5 correction to the declared 0.2898 and a 2.4e-4 correction to what the module's rounded h, c, k currently imply — the rounded constants are the inaccuracy, not the 0.2898. The finding's premise that 0.2898 is the error is backwards.

4. Delete the private CONSTANTS blocks in blackbodyRadiationModel.ts:3-17, stellarEosModel.ts:8-13 and hydrostaticEquilibriumModel.ts:33-37, and the bare 5772 literals at stellarLifetimeModel.ts:338, :435, :439 plus zamsTout1996Model.ts:38, importing from AstroConstants instead.

5. Leave spectralLineModel.ts:42 as the one genuine exception, or better, derive it: KB_EV_PER_K = AstroConstants.EOS.K_BOLTZMANN_ERG_PER_K / AstroConstants.PHOTON.ERG_PER_EV, which I verified reproduces the declared 8.617333e-5 to 7 digits. It is not a divergent duplicate today.

6. BEFORE landing, pin the outputs. The current test (blackbodyRadiationModel.test.ts:6-8) has a +/-2 nm tolerance and will not see this change, but 5.34% of integer temperatures in 2–50000 K shift the last displayed digit of lambda_peak. Add a table test over a fixed temperature ladder (2.725, 3000, 5772, 10000, 50000 K) asserting wienPeakNm to 6 significant figures, run it red/green across the switch, and accept the new values deliberately.

7. Watch one test-independence trap: hydrostaticEquilibriumModel.test.ts:11-12 re-declares solarMassG = 1.98847e33 and solarRadiusCm = 6.957e10 as its own literals. If both sides start importing the same constant the test stops being an independent check — keep the test's literals as the oracle rather than swapping them to the shared symbol.
findings.note:
STRUCTURAL CORE CONFIRMED; HEADLINE CONSEQUENCE REFUTED; SEVERITY P1 -> P2.

Confirmed by reading the code. astroConstants.ts:4 does declare "Single source of truth for definitional constants and time scales used across demos." The duplicate literals exist exactly as cited: c = 2.99792458e10 at astroConstants.ts:67 (PHOTON) and :94 (EOS) and stellarEosModel.ts:13, and as 2.998e10 at blackbodyRadiationModel.ts:5; k_B in erg/K at astroConstants.ts:89, hydrostaticEquilibriumModel.ts:34, stellarEosModel.ts:8 and blackbodyRadiationModel.ts:7 (1.381e-16); h at astroConstants.ts:68 and blackbodyRadiationModel.ts:6 (6.626e-27); T_sun = 5772 at blackbodyRadiationModel.ts:16, zamsTout1996Model.ts:38 and bare at stellarLifetimeModel.ts:338, :435, :439. sigma_SB exists only at blackbodyRadiationModel.ts:8, and G_cgs/M_sun/R_sun only at hydrostaticEquilibriumModel.ts:33,36,37 - all genuinely absent from AstroConstants. So the DRY/one-source defect is real.

REFUTED (1): "k_B 5x" overcounts. spectralLineModel.ts is not an independent definition - lines 44-46 pull C_CM_PER_S and H_ERG_S from AstroConstants.PHOTON, and its KB_EV_PER_K = 8.617333e-5 is the exact unit conversion of AstroConstants' erg/K value. I recomputed: 1.380649e-16 erg/K / 1.602176634e-12 erg/eV = 8.6173333e-5 eV/K, identical to 7 digits, and documented "NIST CODATA 2018". AstroConstants has no eV/K Boltzmann entry, so this is a derived variant, not a divergent duplicate. The real erg/K count is 4, not 5. (I also checked HC_EV_NM: derived 1239.84198 vs declared 1239.842 - consistent.) Title's "T_sun 4x" is also off: it is 5 sites across 3 modules.

REFUTED (2) - the attribution is inverted. Solving x = 5(1 - e^-x) I get x_W = 4.965114231744277. From the module's own h=6.626e-27, c=2.998e10, k=1.381e-16: b = hc/(x_W k) = 0.28970777 cm K, so the mismatch against the declared 0.2898 is +3.184e-4 (the finder's 3.2e-4 and 0.289708 reproduce). BUT exact CODATA b = 0.28977720 cm K, so the DECLARED 0.2898 is the accurate value (+7.9e-5) and the module-derived value is the inaccurate one (-2.4e-4), driven by k_B rounded to 1.381e-16 (rel err +2.54e-4; c is +2.5e-5, h is -1.1e-5). The marked peak is ~3x closer to physical truth than the curve it is drawn on: at 5772 K the marker sits at 502.079 nm, truth is 502.039 nm, and the drawn curve's own max is 501.919 nm.

REFUTED (3) - "a student sees them disagree" is false, by three independent margins. (a) Geometry: the gap is 502.079 - 501.919 = 0.160 nm (finder said 0.2 nm, close). The x-axis is log10 over minNm=10 to maxNm=1e6 (logic.ts:52, wavelengthToLogFraction at logic.ts:121) across plotW = w - mL(62) - mR(16) (main.ts:158-159). That maps the gap to 0.014 px at w=600, 0.031 px at w=1200, 0.053 px at w=2000 - sub-device-pixel, and 70x smaller than the 2.25 px spacing of the 500-point curve sampling (main.ts:164). (b) Precision: the readout is Math.round(nm) (formatWavelengthReadout, logic.ts:134) and the export is Math.round(peakNm) (main.ts:496), so both candidate values print "502 nm". (c) Normalization: the curve is drawn as radiance[i] / maxB (main.ts:236), so the 2hc^2 prefactor cancels exactly and only the hc/(lambda k T) exponent survives, at the 2.5e-4 level.

REFUTED (4) - sigma_SB never reaches a reader. stefanBoltzmannFluxCgs is defined at blackbodyRadiationModel.ts:49 and exported at :128, but grep over apps/ and packages/ excluding tests and dist finds no caller. And luminosityRatioSameRadius is (T/T_ref)^4, so sigma cancels there. The 5.67e-5 vs 5.6703744e-5 rounding (6.6e-5 relative) is unreachable.

ALREADY TRIAGED: docs/reviews/blackbody-radiation.md:66 already records this item verbatim - "Duplicate physical constants (code hygiene, not physics)... The numerical impact is negligible (< 0.03% on any output)" - and my largest relative error anywhere is 2.54e-4 = 0.025%, which confirms that grading. The sigma/G/M_sun/R_sun inventory and the T_sun count are new, so the finding is not fully redundant. git log shows blackbodyRadiationModel.ts untouched since c7c9336 (its migration commit), so it is not already fixed.

NO CONTRACT IS VIOLATED: I grepped .agents/references/invariants.md and docs/specs/cosmic-playground-model-contract.md for constant|single source|astroConstants|DRY - zero hits in both. CLAUDE.md's physics invariant is "All physics models MUST come from @cosmic/physics - no inline equations in demo code"; these constants live inside @cosmic/physics, not in demo code. So this is not the "contract violation" that P1 requires, and it is not an "architecture defect that will keep producing P0s" - the worst drift the structure can currently produce is 0.025%, three digits below the 3-sig-fig readouts. It is a real maintainability defect worth fixing: P2.

FIX CAVEAT: the proposed fix would change displayed numbers, which the finder does not flag. I scanned integer T from 2 to 50000 K and 5.34% of them (2671/49999) shift the last displayed digit of lambda_peak once the module stops using 0.2898 (e.g. T=4 K: "725 um" -> "724 um"; T=12 K: "242 um" -> "241 um"). The existing guard will not catch it: blackbodyRadiationModel.test.ts:6-8 asserts only Math.abs(peakNm - 502) <= 2.

findings.title: The external parity gate runs only at Z = 0.02, where xi = 0 kills all 60 higher-order metallicity coefficients — 77 of 240 single-coefficient corruptions pass every test in the package
findings.evidence: `expect(metallicityZ).toBe(0.02);` and __fixtures__/stellar-startrax.json `"Z": 0.02`. zamsTout1996Model.ts:67 computes `const xi = Math.log10(metallicityZ / CONSTANTS.zSun)` with zSun = 0.02, so at the fixture's Z, xi = 0 exactly and `evaluateMetallicityCoefficient` returns `coefficients[0]` alone — every xi, xi^2, xi^3, xi^4 term vanishes. The 16 polynomials hold 80 coefficients; the fixture exercises 16. The other 64 could be transposed, sign-flipped or zeroed and all 40 parity assertions would still pass. apps/demos/src/demos/stars-zams-hr/index.html:153 gives students a live Z input over [0.0001, 0.03] — exactly the range those 64 coefficients govern. The test's own prose claims otherwise: "startrax is an independent implementation in another language, so agreeing with it to a part in a thousand means the two got there separately" and "The ends are where a transcription error in the high-order coefficients shows up" (line 101) — but "the ends" there means mass, not metallicity.
findings.scenario: A transcription error in, say, the xi^3 coefficient of RADIUS_COEFFICIENTS.omicron ships green. A student sets Z = 0.001 in stars-zams-hr and reads a radius and effective temperature that no external reference has ever checked, while the repo's documentation states the port is externally gated.
findings.fix:
Keep the finder's direction but split the loop by quantity, because the lifetime port is deliberately solar-only:

1. Regenerate `packages/physics/src/__fixtures__/stellar-startrax.json` with ZAMS rows (L, R, Teff) at Z = 1e-4, 1e-3, 4e-3, 0.02 and 0.03. Restructure as `rows: [{ Z, stars: [...] }]` and keep `t_MS` on the Z = 0.02 block ONLY.

2. In `stellarStartraxParity.test.ts`, loop the three ZAMS assertions over every metallicity block, and keep the `mainSequenceLifetimeMyr` assertion inside an `if (block.Z === 0.02)` guard with a comment pointing at `SOLAR_METALLICITY_ONLY` (stellarLifetimeModel.ts:23). Replace the `expect(metallicityZ).toBe(0.02)` guard at line 57 with an assertion that the metallicity set spans the model's full declared domain, so the gate fails if someone later narrows the fixture back to solar. This is the part that actually closes the hole: a value check at Z != 0.02 catches all 77 corruptions my sweep found, which no amount of monotonicity or round-trip checking does.

3. Fix the documentation overstatement at docs/reviews/cluster-census.md:204-208: until step 1 lands, that "Closed 2026-09-04" note must say the external gate covers solar metallicity only and that the ZAMS fit's metallicity dependence is ungated. (The test header at lines 15-19 and the fixture `_meta.note` already say "solar metallicity" and need no change.)

4. Optional but cheap, and worth it given one of the demo's stated misconceptions is that metallicity does not change bulk structure: add an internal regression that pins Teff and R at a non-solar Z to the current values (e.g. 1 Msun at Z = 1e-4 -> R = 0.8400 Rsun, Teff = 7068 K, which I computed above). That is self-referential, so label it as a change detector rather than validation, but it would have caught every one of the 77 corruptions immediately.

Do NOT simply extend the existing loop over metallicities as proposed — that fails the lifetime assertion at Z = 4e-3, 1e-3 and 1e-4 by 13x, 32x and 42x the tolerance for a reason unrelated to any transcription error, and whoever triages it is likely to "fix" it by loosening TOLERANCE, which would weaken the ZAMS gate that currently passes at 5.94e-7.
findings.note:
CONFIRMED, and stronger than claimed — but with two corrections to the evidence and a flaw in the proposed fix.

1. Quoted code exists verbatim. `expect(metallicityZ).toBe(0.02);` is at packages/physics/src/stellarStartraxParity.test.ts:57. Fixture `"Z": 0.02` confirmed. zamsTout1996Model.ts:67 is `const xi = Math.log10(metallicityZ / CONSTANTS.zSun)` with `zSun: 0.02` at line 37.

2. Recomputed independently (node, no reuse of the finder's arithmetic). `Math.log10(0.02/0.02)` returns exactly +0 (`Object.is(xi, 0) === true`), so xi, xi^2, xi^3, xi^4 are all identically 0 and evaluateMetallicityCoefficient returns coefficients[0] alone. I re-derived the table census myself: 16 polynomials (7 luminosity + 9 radius), 80 slots, 64 higher-order, of which 60 are nonzero (RADIUS_COEFFICIENTS.nu at line 57 is [0.01077422,0,0,0,0], structurally Z-free). The fixture exercises 16.

3. Decisive experiment. I re-implemented the model in plain JS with a corruption knob and re-ran every assertion in the package (30 ZAMS parity assertions, the toBeCloseTo benchmarks at test.ts:32-34 and :120-121, boundary monotonicity at test.ts:47-61, and boundary inversion at test.ts:73-93). Zeroing ALL 60 higher-order coefficients — deleting the ZAMS fit's entire metallicity dependence — passes every single assertion, with the parity worst-case relative error unmoved at 5.94e-7 (tol 1e-3). A student at Z = 1e-4 would then read Teff(1 Msun) = 5597 K instead of 7068 K (1471 K, 21% low) and R = 0.888 instead of 0.840 Rsun. Sweeping realistic single-coefficient transcription slips (sign flip, decimal-point x10 and /10, dropped row) over all 60 live slots: 77 of 240 corruptions pass EVERY existing assertion. Worst green-shipping cases: LUMINOSITY_COEFFICIENTS.beta[2] x10 shifts Teff(20 Msun, Z=1e-4) from 41,933 K to 107,009 K (+155%); RADIUS_COEFFICIENTS.theta[3] x10 drops Teff(0.3 Msun, Z=1e-4) from 4,109 K to 375 K.

4. CORRECTION to the evidence — the finder's named example is refuted. "A transcription error in, say, the xi^3 coefficient of RADIUS_COEFFICIENTS.omicron ships green" is false. Sign-flipping or zeroing omicron[3] (line 59) is caught: 1 boundary-monotonicity failure and 2 inversion failures. The finder missed that zamsTout1996Model.test.ts:47-61 and :73-93 do evaluate at CONSTANTS.metallicityMin (1e-4) and metallicityMax (0.03), giving partial — not zero — coverage of the 60 coefficients. Those are self-consistency checks (monotonic Teff, Teff->mass round trip), never value checks, which is why 77 corruptions still slip past. The title's claim (the PARITY gate is blind at Z=0.02) is exactly right; the failure scenario's "ships green" holds for 77 concrete corruptions, just not the one named.

5. Reachability confirmed. apps/demos/src/demos/stars-zams-hr/index.html:153 is `<input id="metallicityZ" type="number" min="0.0001" max="0.03" step="0.0001" value="0.02" />`, wired live to the model via main.ts:143, :1135-1142, :314-322 and :996, and exported at main.ts:1025. logic.ts:283 ships a one-click preset at metallicityZ: 0.004. starClusterModel.ts:157 also accepts Z (defaulting to 0.02). No upstream clamp to solar. The demo's own frontmatter lists the misconception "Metallicity only changes spectral lines and not bulk stellar structure" — the un-gated coefficients govern precisely the physics the demo exists to teach.

6. Not already fixed. Single commit ea62d4d ("Gate the stellar physics against startrax") for both test and fixture; no later Z work, no guard. grep found no non-solar value gate anywhere in packages/physics/src/*.test.ts.

7. No live wrong number today, which is why this stays P1 and not P0. I sanity-checked the direction of the Z dependence: at 1 Msun, Z = 1e-4 gives R = 0.840 Rsun / Teff = 7068 K versus 0.888 Rsun / 5597 K at solar — metal-poor stars come out more compact and hotter, the physically correct direction for reduced metal opacity, and ~7000 K for a 1 Msun Z=1e-4 ZAMS star is plausible. So the coefficients appear directionally sound; the defect is the missing gate, not a current error. Both consuming demos are honest about status (stars-zams-hr.md:3,10 `status: draft`, `readiness: experimental`; cluster-census.md the same), so there is no launch-ready overclaim.

8. The documentation claim checks out. docs/reviews/cluster-census.md:204-208 strikes through "Not validated against an external fixture" as "Closed 2026-09-04" and describes the gate as "10 masses from 0.1 to 100 Msun, agreeing on L, R, T_eff and t_MS to a part in a thousand against an independent implementation in another language" — with no solar-metallicity caveat. The test header and fixture _meta do say "solar metallicity", so the overstatement lives in the review doc, not the test.

9. The proposed fix would break something. I computed Hurley eq.(5)'s metallicity factor x = max(0.95, min(0.95 - 0.03*(zeta + 0.30103), 0.99)) myself. The repo hardcodes zeta = 0 (stellarLifetimeModel.ts:32) and mainSequenceLifetimeMyr(massMsun) takes no Z at all (line 58, flagged SOLAR_METALLICITY_ONLY at line 23), while the fixture generator's `times.t_ms(coefficients(Z))` is Z-dependent. x goes 0.950000 -> 0.961938 at Z=4e-3 (1.26%, 13x the 1e-3 tolerance), 0.980000 at Z=1e-3 (3.16%, 32x), 0.990000 at Z=1e-4 (4.21%, 42x) — and that is the x factor alone, before the a1..a10 Z-polynomials. So naively looping the whole parity test over metallicities would fail the lifetime assertion at 3 of the 4 proposed metallicities for a reason that is not a transcription error.

findings.title: Solar declination and the horizon hour-angle are each written twice over in @cosmic/physics; the worse copy is dead but publicly exported, and the live pair still disagrees on year length and obliquity
findings.evidence: riseSetModel.ts:28-29 computes `gamma = 2*pi*(n-80)/365` then `return SOLAR_OBLIQUITY_DEG * Math.sin(gamma)` — the small-angle form with a 365-day year and obliquity hardcoded at 23.44. seasonsModel.ts:22-24 computes the same quantity as `asin(sin(eps) * sin(L))` with L on a 365.2422-day tropical year and eps taken from the caller. The file knows: riseSetModel.ts:97-98 says "the small-angle eps*sin(lambda) is 0.23 deg high at lambda = 45" — and then uses the exact form for the Moon (line 99) while leaving the Sun on the approximation. I recomputed both over the full year: max |difference| = 0.303 deg at day 298. Feeding each into the identical `cosH0 = -tan(phi) tan(delta)` day-length formula (which is itself written three times: seasonsModel.ts:30, riseSetModel.ts:42 and riseSetModel.ts:140) gives day lengths differing by up to 2.7 minutes at 45 N and 7.4 minutes at 66 N.
findings.scenario: A second demo is wired to the exported `solarRiseSetLocalTimeHours` (index.ts:109) and reports sunset 2.7 minutes later than the seasons demo for the same date and latitude at 45 N, with no way for a student or instructor to tell which is right. Both are exported from @cosmic/physics as the solar declination.
findings.fix:
Real DRY defect, worth fixing, but as a cleanup rather than a correctness emergency. Order of work:

1. ASK ANNA FIRST (scientific assumption, per CLAUDE.md): astroConstants.ts has no obliquity constant. Adding one fixes the live 23.44 (riseSetModel.ts:3) vs 23.5 (seasons/main.ts:394) split, but the value is hers to approve — 23.44 deg (J2000 mean, 23.4393) vs the 23.5 the seasons demo shows students today. Note the seasons demo exposes axial tilt as a slider, so the constant is only the default.

2. Give the ecliptic geometry one owner. Three small exported helpers, in seasonsModel or a new eclipticGeometry.ts:
