   Then `sunDeclinationDeg` = helper 2 of helper 1, and `moonDeclinationDeg` = helper 2 of (helper 1 + elongationDeg) — this is the correct form of the finder's intent, passing the LONGITUDE across the boundary, not the declination. All three cosH0 sites (seasonsModel.ts:30, riseSetModel.ts:42, riseSetModel.ts:140) collapse to helper 3.

3. Delete `solarDeclinationDegFromDayOfYear` and `solarRiseSetLocalTimeHours` from riseSetModel.ts:26-76 and from index.ts:60-61 — verified dead in apps/demos/src, apps/site/src and packages/runtime/src. This removes the trap where a future demo author reaches for the function whose NAME reads like the obvious choice for the Sun and silently gets the worse model.

4. Repair the test file as part of the same change, not after: rewrite riseSetModel.test.ts lines 9-57 (now testing deleted functions) and re-point the Sun references at lines 106, 132 and 147 to SeasonsModel.sunDeclinationDeg plus the shared hour-angle helper. Critically, move the cross-check at line 132 off dayOfYear 172 — at the solstice the two forms agree to 0.0002 deg, so that assertion cannot fail. Put it on an asymmetric day such as 298 or 126.

5. Fix the stale documentation this leaves behind: docs/reviews/moon-phases.md:30-31 and :106 describe both deleted functions and mark them "CORRECT".

SEPARATE FINDING, LARGER THAN THIS ONE, do not fold it in: neither implementation applies the -0.833 deg refraction-plus-semidiameter horizon term, so published day lengths run short by ~10 min at 45 N and far more near the Arctic circle. Whether a teaching model should carry that term is Anna's call; if the answer is no, riseSetModel.ts:114-115 should say so in reader-visible copy rather than only in a source comment, since the seasons and moon-phases exhibits print rise and set times to the minute.
findings.note:
CONFIRMED as a code fact, with the headline numbers reproduced exactly — but the severity and the failure scenario are wrong, and the proposed fix is mathematically impossible as written.

WHAT I CONFIRMED
1. Code exists verbatim. riseSetModel.ts:27-29 is `clamp(dayOfYear,1,365)`, `gamma = 2*pi*(n-80)/365`, `return SOLAR_OBLIQUITY_DEG * Math.sin(gamma)` with SOLAR_OBLIQUITY_DEG = 23.44 hardcoded at line 3. seasonsModel.ts:19-24 is `L = 2*pi*(dayOfYear-80)/365.2422` (AstroConstants.TIME.MEAN_TROPICAL_YEAR_DAYS = 365.2422, astroConstants.ts:23) then `asin(sin(eps)*sin(L))` with eps from the caller. The self-indicting comment is real: riseSetModel.ts:97-98.
2. Three writes of the hour-angle formula confirmed by repo-wide grep: seasonsModel.ts:30, riseSetModel.ts:42, riseSetModel.ts:140. No fourth.
3. My own `node -e` recomputation (not the finder's arithmetic) reproduces all three numbers: max |delta declination| = 0.3035 deg at day 298 (riseSet -13.4492 deg vs seasons -13.1457 deg); claimed 0.303 deg at day 298. Day length through the identical cosH0: 2.66 min at 45 N (day 301, 10.0130 h vs 10.0573 h) and 7.37 min at 66 N (day 310, 6.1720 h vs 6.2948 h); claimed 2.7 and 7.4. I also split the cause: small-angle-vs-exact contributes 0.256 deg, the 365-vs-365.2422 year only 0.051 deg.

WHY THE SEVERITY IS WRONG (P1 -> P2): THE HEADLINE NUMBER IS DEAD CODE
The 0.30 deg / 7.4 min disagreement is NOT reachable by any student. Repo-wide grep for both functions returns only riseSetModel.ts itself, riseSetModel.test.ts, the index.ts barrel, and two files under docs/ — zero consumers in apps/demos/src, apps/site/src or packages/runtime/src. The finder's own fix concedes this, yet the failure scenario is written in the present tense ("A second demo IS wired to the exported solarRiseSetLocalTimeHours") and describes a hypothetical future wiring. Nothing renders a 7.4-minute discrepancy today. (Citation error too: the export is index.ts:60-61, not index.ts:109.)

THE ACTUALLY-LIVE DIVERGENCE IS 5x SMALLER
The two live paths are seasons/main.ts:300,745,840 -> SeasonsModel.sunDeclinationDeg, and moon-phases/main.ts:317 + riseSetViewModel.ts:24 -> moonRiseSetLocalTimeHours -> moonDeclinationDeg. Both already use the exact asin form; they differ only in year length. I computed that residual over all (day, elongation): max 0.0741 deg declination, 0.59 min at 45 N, 1.43 min at 66 N — and exactly 0 in moon-phases basic mode, where riseSetModel.ts:135 pins baseDay to 80.

AND THE INCONSISTENCY IS INSIDE THE MODEL'S OWN ERROR BUDGET
Both implementations use the geometric horizon (center of Sun at altitude 0) and omit the standard -0.833 deg refraction-plus-semidiameter term. I computed that omission: day length is short by 9.4-11.5 min at 45 N, 6.7-7.3 min at the equator, 16-127 min at 66 N. The equation of time, also omitted, is +/-16 min. So the 2.66 min inconsistency is roughly a quarter of an error both already carry and which riseSetModel.ts:114-115 explicitly declares ("no refraction or parallax", "local solar time"). "No way for a student or instructor to tell which is right" overstates the harm: neither matches an almanac to better than ~16 min by design.

ONE THING THE FINDER MISSED, SAME CATEGORY, AND IT IS LIVE
The obliquity itself is inconsistent across live paths: riseSetModel.ts:3 hardcodes 23.44, while the seasons demo defaults axialTiltDeg to 23.5 (seasons/main.ts:394). astroConstants.ts has no obliquity constant at all (grep found none), so there is no owner for the number.

SUPPORTING: THE CROSS-CHECK TEST IS BLIND BY CONSTRUCTION
riseSetModel.test.ts:132-135 is the one assertion that compares the two implementations — `expect(newMoon.declinationDeg).toBeCloseTo(sun.declinationDeg, 1)` — and it evaluates them at dayOfYear 172, the June solstice, where I computed the two forms agree to 0.0002 deg. Its 0.05 deg tolerance would REJECT the day-298 difference of 0.3035 deg. Exactly the "test only at symmetric points" trap CLAUDE.md warns about; the test pins the agreement instead of probing it.

WHY THE PROPOSED FIX WOULD NOT WORK
(a) "have moonDeclinationDeg call SeasonsModel.sunDeclinationDeg for the solar longitude" is impossible: sunDeclinationDeg returns a declination, not a longitude, and lambda_sun cannot be recovered from it — asin is two-to-one, so lambda and 180-lambda give the same declination and the quadrant is lost. moonDeclinationDeg needs lambda_sun itself (riseSetModel.ts:95-96) in order to add the elongation BEFORE taking the asin.
(b) Deleting the two exports breaks riseSetModel.test.ts in more places than the finder accounted for: beyond the four tests at lines 9-57, solarRiseSetLocalTimeHours is used as the Sun reference at lines 106, 132 and 147 for three moon-vs-Sun comparison tests. The fix as written leaves the test file non-compiling.

findings.title: effHalfMassOverScale hides the truncation radius that sets its answer, and its docstring sells that answer as a property of gamma alone
findings.evidence: The docstring claims it "Lets a demo quote a real half-mass radius for any gamma instead of assuming the Plummer ratio", and line 103 calls `buildEffCdf(1, gamma, 15)` with the truncation radius hardcoded at 15 scale radii (duplicating EFF_TRUNCATION_SCALE_RADII at line 115). For EFF with rho ~ (1 + r^2/a^2)^(-gamma/2), the enclosed mass diverges for gamma <= 3, so the half-mass radius is set by the truncation. I recomputed r_h/a against truncation radius: at gamma = 3 — the value line 52 names as "typical of a young cluster" — r_h/a = 3.490, 4.353, 5.072, 6.269, 8.153 at truncations of 10a, 15a, 20a, 30a, 50a. At gamma = 2.5 it runs 4.603 to 17.051. Only at gamma = 5 is it stable (1.288 to 1.306), and there my exact truncated-Plummer calculation gives 1.29700 against the function's 1.29712 — 0.009%, so the numerics are fine; the quantity is not well-defined.
findings.scenario: A demo adds an EFF gamma control and a half-mass-radius readout. At gamma = 3 the readout says 4.35 pc for a 1 pc scale radius; change the undisclosed truncation to 30a and the same cluster reads 6.27 pc. The student is being shown a property of a hidden constant as a property of the cluster. No demo calls this today, which is the only reason it is not already a P0.
findings.fix:
The proposed fix is half right and internally contradictory — do not apply it as written.

What is wrong with it: "return NaN for gamma <= 3" contradicts "take the truncation radius as an explicit required argument". Once the caller supplies r_t, the half-mass radius OF THE TRUNCATED PROFILE is well-defined, finite and correct (my closed form gives 4.35263 a at gamma=3, r_t=15a; the function returns 4.35266 a, 6e-4% off). Returning NaN would throw away a usable number at exactly the gamma this project ships (EFF_GAMMA = 3 in cluster-census/main.ts:243). NaN is the right answer only for the UNTRUNCATED half-mass radius, which this function does not compute. The fix also misses the actual DRY defect: EFF_TRUNCATION_SCALE_RADII (clusterProfileModel.ts:115) is module-private and never exported, so deleting the duplicate literal 15 without exporting the constant leaves a caller unable to pass the same truncation the sampler used — the duplication becomes an inconsistency. And it leaves test:55 pinned to the magic 15.

What I would apply, in packages/physics/src/clusterProfileModel.ts:
1. Export EFF_TRUNCATION_SCALE_RADII (line 115) and re-export it from index.ts, so the sampler and any readout share one truncation.
2. Rename to effTruncatedHalfMassOverScale(gamma, truncationScaleRadii) with truncationScaleRadii required, and delete the literal 15 at line 103 in favour of the shared constant at the call site. The name must carry "truncated"; a caller who does not read the docstring must still not be able to mistake it for a profile invariant. Update the facade at :143 and index.ts:85 — a direct rename, no alias or compat wrapper (only tests call it).
3. Rewrite the docstring to state the physics instead of hiding it: the EFF mass integral goes as r^(3-gamma) and so diverges for gamma < 3, and logarithmically at gamma = 3 (I(r) -> ln(2r) - 1), so for gamma <~ 4 the returned radius is a property of where the profile is truncated, not of gamma. Give the measured sensitivity: at gamma=3 the ratio runs 3.49 -> 8.15 over r_t = 10a -> 50a; at gamma=4, 1.94 -> 2.19; only gamma=5 is stable at 1.288 -> 1.305, approaching the analytic Plummer 1.304766. Drop "a real half-mass radius for any gamma".
4. Fix the test that encodes the defect: replace clusterProfileModel.test.ts:55 (`effHalfMassOverScale(3) > 3 * effHalfMassOverScale(5)`, which fails for any truncation below ~13a) with an assertion that is actually about the profile — e.g. monotonicity in gamma at FIXED r_t (already covered at :50), plus an explicit truncation-sensitivity test that pins the gamma=3 ratio at two different r_t and asserts they differ, so the hidden-constant dependence can never silently return.
5. Separately note, do not silently fix: makeProfileSampler (line 129-132) applies the same undisclosed 15a truncation at gamma=3 in the live cluster-census demo, so the drawn cluster's extent is also set by that constant. Whether 15a is the right truncation for a young cluster is a scientific assumption and is Anna's to approve, not an agent's to change.
findings.note:
CONFIRMED on every checkable point, and the code is worse than claimed in one respect, milder in another.

1. Code exists as quoted. clusterProfileModel.ts:102 is `export function effHalfMassOverScale(gamma: number): number {`; :103 is `const { cdf, radiiPc } = buildEffCdf(1, gamma, 15);`. The docstring at :97-101 contains "Lets a demo quote a real half-mass radius for any gamma instead of assuming the Plummer ratio". :115 is `const EFF_TRUNCATION_SCALE_RADII = 15;` — so the literal 15 is genuinely duplicated. :52 does say "gamma = 3 is typical of a young cluster".

2. Independent recomputation (I did NOT reuse the finder's method). I derived closed forms for I(r) = int_0^r s^2 (1+s^2)^(-gamma/2) ds and verified them by numerical differentiation (residuals 8e-11, 6e-13): gamma=3 -> I = asinh(r) - r/sqrt(1+r^2); gamma=5 -> I = r^3/(3(1+r^2)^(3/2)). Bisecting I(r_h) = I(r_t)/2 gives, at gamma=3, r_h/a = 3.48976, 4.35263, 5.07214, 6.26925, 8.15320 for r_t = 10a, 15a, 20a, 30a, 50a (and 11.594 at 100a, 36.846 at 1000a — still climbing). A separate 400,000-interval composite Simpson bisection reproduced the same table, plus gamma=2.5: 4.6032 -> 17.0510. Both match the finder to 4 figures. Divergence confirmed analytically, not just numerically: at gamma=3, I(r) -> ln(2r) - 1 (I(1e8) = 18.1138 vs ln(2e8)-1 = 18.1138), a log divergence; for gamma<3 it goes as r^(3-gamma). So the enclosed mass has no limit and r_h is set entirely by the truncation. Units are consistent throughout (a dimensionless pc/pc ratio).

3. The function's numerics are fine; only the definition is broken. My exact values vs the shipped 512-point trapezoid: gamma=5, r_t=15a -> 1.297000 vs 1.29712 (0.0092%); gamma=3 -> 4.352632 vs 4.35266 (6.4e-4%). The finder's "0.009%" is right, and so is their point that this is a well-posedness problem, not an accuracy one.

4. BROADER than claimed: only gamma=5 is truncation-stable (1.28749 -> 1.30477 over r_t = 10a -> infinity, 1.3%). gamma=4 moves 1.9354 -> 2.1928 (13%) and gamma=3.5 moves 2.5651 -> 3.6931 (44%) across r_t = 10a -> 50a. At r_t = 15a the profile has not reached its asymptotic value even where the mass integral formally converges, so the artifact is not confined to gamma <= 3.

5. MILDER than a P0, exactly as the finder conceded. No student can see this today. `effHalfMassOverScale` is called only from clusterProfileModel.test.ts:42,43,50,55 — no demo, app or other model calls it (repo-wide rg excluding node_modules/dist/public). It is public API: index.ts:85 plus the facade at clusterProfileModel.ts:143. cluster-census is the only EFF consumer and uses `makeProfileSampler` with a hardcoded `EFF_GAMMA = 3` (cluster-census/main.ts:243), exposes no gamma control, and has no half-mass readout — its "half radius" at main.ts:448-451 is an empirical half-NUMBER radius measured from the sample, used only to frame the view, so it is unaffected by this function.

6. Not fixed, no guard. Single commit a7d6119 ("port IMF, cluster profiles and stellar lifetimes from novascope"); the body of effHalfMassOverScale is two lines with no gamma guard.

7. NEW evidence the finder missed — the green test is pinned to the magic constant. clusterProfileModel.test.ts:55 asserts `effHalfMassOverScale(3) > 3 * effHalfMassOverScale(5)`, commented "A young-cluster slope is dramatically more extended than a Plummer sphere". I evaluated that assertion against the exact closed forms as a function of r_t: it FAILS at r_t = 8a (3.0792 vs 3.8342), 10a (3.4898 vs 3.8625) and 12a (3.8578 vs 3.8781), and passes only from about 13a up. It reads as a physics claim but is a claim about the undisclosed 15 — the repo's own documented "tests encode defects" failure mode. The comment at test:40-41 ("the gap is grid resolution plus the truncation at 15 scale radii") proves the author knew about the truncation dependence; it simply never reached the public docstring.

8. Severity P1 affirmed, as a latent public-API defect rather than a reader-visible one. It fits the rubric's "misleading copy" and "architecture defect that will keep producing P0s": a docstring in packages/physics — the project's declared single source of truth, whose model contract demands correctness and explicit units — advertises a truncation-dependent number as a property of gamma alone, which is precisely the invitation needed to produce the P0. The finder's claimed category "units" is wrong; this is model-definition/misleading-API plus DRY.

findings.title: Recession mode's constant-rate toy extrapolation runs to +/-1 Gyr, and its toy-model caveat is missing from the in-demo Model notes tab
findings.evidence: `const kmPerMyr = recessionCmPerYr * 10; return distanceTodayKm + kmPerMyr * timeMyr;` — strictly linear in time, fed by `AstroConstants.MOON.MEAN_RECESSION_CM_PER_YEAR = 3.8`, which astroConstants.ts:103 labels "Present-day mean lunar recession rate". apps/demos/src/demos/angular-size/main.ts:226 clamps the slider to [-1000, 1000] Myr. I recomputed: at t = -1000 Myr the model gives d = 346,400 km, which is inside today's perigee of 356,500 km, and an angular diameter of 0.5746 deg — above `AstroConstants.MOON.ORBIT_MAX_ANGULAR_SIZE_DEG = 0.56` (astroConstants.ts:109), the same file's declared observed maximum. Under the standard constant-Q tidal model the recession rate scales as d^(-5.5), and the present rate is anomalously high because of near-resonant ocean tides, so the present value cannot be carried over Gyr: geological rhythmite data put 36,000 km of recession at ~2.45 Gyr, which this model produces in 0.95 Gyr.
findings.scenario: A student drags the time slider to -1000 Myr and reads a mean Earth-Moon distance of 346,400 km and an angular size of 0.575 deg. Both are outside the range the repo's own constants file declares physical, and the implied past recession is ~2.5x too fast.
findings.fix:
Do NOT adopt the proposed constant-Q form and do NOT clamp to [ORBIT_MIN, ORBIT_MAX]: I verified constant-Q calibrated to 3.8 cm/yr gives a(-1 Gyr) = 328,130 km and a -> 0 at 1.56 Gyr, strictly worse than the linear model, and clamping to today's observed extremes would break the feature's whole point (the Moon looked bigger in the past).

What I would apply:

(1) DRY the caveat onto the surface students read. The string already exists at apps/demos/src/demos/angular-size/main.ts:434 and, in prose, at apps/site/src/content/demos/angular-size.md:29. Hoist one caveat constant and use it in both the export note and a new <li> in the in-demo Model notes tab (apps/demos/src/demos/angular-size/index.html:356-371), stating that recession mode is a constant-rate linear extrapolation of today's 3.8 cm/yr, valid only near the present, and that the real past rate was slower. Mechanical, no approval needed.

(2) Narrow the slider -- Anna's call, because it is a scope/regime decision. Present two options with the numbers: keep min/max at +/-1000 Myr (index.html:177-178 and the clamp at main.ts:226) and carry an explicit "~2.6x too fast over a Gyr" caveat, or narrow to +/-100 Myr with step 1, where the linear model moves the Moon 3,800 km -- small enough that a constant rate is defensible. Changing both the HTML attributes and the main.ts:226 clamp together, since they duplicate the bound (itself a small DRY defect: the range is written twice).

(3) If a non-linear form is ever wanted, it must be calibrated to the geological record (tidal rhythmite / cyclostratigraphic constraints on a(t)), NOT to today's recession rate. That is a closure with a coefficient and a regime, so it goes to Anna with its physical motivation before implementation, per the project's scientific-assumption rule.

(4) Add a test at packages/physics/src/angularSizeModel.test.ts asserting the documented validity window rather than only the unit conversion currently at :45-53 -- e.g. that the slider's extreme input stays inside whatever range the approved decision in (2) declares defensible.
findings.note:
CODE CONFIRMED, NUMBERS CONFIRMED, PROPOSED FIX REFUTED, SEVERITY CORRECTED DOWN.

1) Code exists, verbatim. /Users/anna/Teaching/cosmic-playground/packages/physics/src/angularSizeModel.ts:47-48 reads `const kmPerMyr = recessionCmPerYr * 10;` / `return distanceTodayKm + kmPerMyr * timeMyr;` inside `moonDistanceKmFromRecession` (lines 36-49). Citation drift: the finding says :45, which is the blank line; it also cites astroConstants.ts:103 and :109, actual are :100 (MEAN_RECESSION_CM_PER_YEAR: 3.8) and :107 (ORBIT_MAX_ANGULAR_SIZE_DEG: 0.56).

2) Arithmetic reproduced independently (node, not the finder's numbers). 3.8 cm/yr = 3.8e-5 km/yr x 1e6 yr/Myr = 38 km/Myr. At t = -1000 Myr: d = 384400 - 38000 = 346,400 km; theta = 2 arctan(3474/(2*346400)) = 0.5746 deg. At t = +1000 Myr: d = 422,400 km, theta = 0.4712 deg. Inverting the repo's own extremes: theta = 0.56 deg -> d = 355,436 km, theta = 0.49 deg -> d = 406,213 km. So 346,400 km is indeed inside today's perigee and 0.5746 deg exceeds 0.56 deg. Linear model reaches 36,000 km of recession in 36000/38 = 947 Myr = 0.95 Gyr. All of the finder's numbers check out.

3) Reachable by a student. Live path: apps/demos/src/demos/angular-size/index.html:151 (Recession radio), :171-183 (slider `min="-1000" max="1000" step="10"`), main.ts:226 `clamp(Number(moonRecessionTime.value), -1000, 1000)` feeding main.ts:228. Moon preset has `timeEvolution: true` (angularSizeModel.ts). No clamp or flag on the output anywhere (grepped ORBIT_MIN/MAX: used only at angularSizeModel.ts:205,209 for the orbit mode, never on the recession result). The only test, angularSizeModel.test.ts:45-53, asserts just the 1 cm/yr -> 10 km/Myr unit conversion, so nothing covers the Gyr regime.

4) PREMISE PARTLY WRONG. astroConstants.ts:105 comments ORBIT_MIN/MAX as "Angular size extremes observed from Earth (deg)" -- i.e. TODAY's orbit. A past epoch legitimately exceeding today's observed maximum is not a contradiction with the constants file; it is the pedagogical point of the recession mode. So "outside the range the repo's own constants file declares physical" is a misreading, and the proposed "clamp or flag any result that leaves [MIN, MAX]" would delete the feature and teach the wrong lesson.

5) PROPOSED FIX IS WRONG IN DIRECTION -- I computed it. Constant-Q gives da/dt proportional to a^(-11/2), so a^(13/2) is linear; calibrating C to 3.8 cm/yr at a0 = 3.844e10 cm and integrating backward: a(-0.5 Gyr) = 362,151 km, a(-1 Gyr) = 328,130 km (56,270 km of recession vs the linear model's 38,000 km), and a -> 0 at t = a0/((13/2)*3.8 cm/yr) = 3.844e10/24.7 = 1.56 Gyr. Constant-Q reaches 36,000 km of recession in 0.73 Gyr, versus linear's 0.95 Gyr -- i.e. WORSE against the ~2.45 Gyr geological datum, not better. Because the rate rises steeply as a shrinks, any model calibrated only to today's rate over-recedes into the past, and constant-Q amplifies exactly the anomaly the finder correctly identifies. This is the textbook lunar-timescale problem (Moon at Earth's surface 1.5 Gyr ago). The finder's own premise -- today's rate is anomalously high -- implies the past rate was LOWER, so the correct direction is slower past recession, the opposite of their fix. (The 36,000 km at 2.45 Gyr rhythmite datum is a literature value I could not verify from this repo; the linear-vs-constant-Q comparison above is fully verified numerically.)

6) PARTIALLY HANDLED ALREADY, which lowers severity. The toy-model caveat exists on two surfaces: main.ts:434 pushes "Toy model: linear distance change using a constant recession rate of 3.8 cm/yr" into the export payload, and apps/site/src/content/demos/angular-size.md:29 carries "a toy linear extrapolation using a constant recession rate" in model_notes (rendered at apps/site/src/pages/exhibits/[slug].astro:151). It is MISSING from the one surface a student at /play/angular-size/ would actually read: the in-demo Model notes tab, index.html:356-371, which lists the exact geometry, the small-angle form, units and "Diagram is visually scaled; numeric readouts are authoritative" -- and says nothing about recession. That is the real, verified gap.

7) No readiness overclaim: angular-size.md has `status: beta`, `readiness: candidate`, `readinessReason` already flagging unfinished work. So this is not a readiness-honesty finding.

SEVERITY: P1 -> P2. The model computes exactly what it declares (a constant-rate linear extrapolation); no number is wrong for its stated model, and the toy label is accurate and present on two of three surfaces. The genuine defects are a caveat-surface DRY gap and a slider range wider than the toy supports -- consistency/scope, not a wrong number a student would believe uncaveated across the site.

findings.title: Plot axis frames and gridlines are stroked with the panel-border token --cp-border: 1.25:1 for the frame and 1.05:1 for the gridlines against the panel background, versus the 3:1 non-text floor — and four demos share the pattern
findings.evidence: readPalette() resolves `axis: value("--cp-border", "#3a4358")` and that value feeds ctx.strokeStyle at lines 615, 639, 653 and 823. packages/theme/styles/tokens.css:9 defines `--cp-border: rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.08)` and layer-instrument.css does not override it. I recomputed WCAG relative luminance: 8% white composited over --cp-bg0 (#0f1115) gives rgb(34,36,40), L=0.01755, contrast vs background 1.216:1. The author's own fallback #3a4358 gives L=0.05618, contrast 1.911:1. WCAG non-text minimum is 3:1, so both are below floor and the token that actually renders is 57% worse. Two more fallbacks in the same block are already stale against tokens.css: --cp-accent-amber is #FFB86C but the fallback says #f2b544 (blue channel differs by 40/255), and --cp-accent-ice is #8BE9FD against fallback #7fd4e8.
findings.scenario: A student opens cluster-census, reads a mass-radius scatter plot, and cannot see the axis lines, tick marks or plot frame - they are 8%-opacity white on near-black. The plotted points float with no readable frame of reference, so no quantity can be read off the figure.
findings.fix: Treat this as one token-ownership fix, not a per-demo patch. (a) Add two purpose-made plot-ink tokens to `packages/theme/styles/tokens.css` next to `--cp-border` (line 9) — `--cp-plot-axis` for the frame and tick marks, `--cp-plot-grid` for the interpolation gridlines. The axis value must clear 3:1 against the instrument panel composite rgb(22,26,32): I measured that white needs alpha >= ~0.35 (0.35 -> 3.223:1, 0.30 -> 2.710:1), i.e. roughly `rgba(255,255,255,0.35)` or an opaque grey near #575e6e. Ask Anna to approve that value: it is a contrast-threshold choice and it will visibly change every plot in the repo. (b) Drop the `ctx.globalAlpha = 0.25` multipliers at main.ts:635 and 649 (and the 0.2 at 847) and let `--cp-plot-grid` carry the whole gridline weight, otherwise the token is silently divided by four at the point of use and no token value can be reasoned about. (c) Repoint every plot-ink consumer, not just cluster-census: main.ts:310, `stars-zams-hr/main.ts:494-495`, `spectral-lines/main.ts:707, 1354, 1371`, `binary-orbits/main.ts:245`. Leave `--cp-border` to mean "the edge of a DOM panel", which is what the instrument layer already uses it for. (d) Do NOT delete the fallback argument outright — `ctx.strokeStyle = ""` is a no-op and would leave black ink on a near-black panel. Either keep a single fallback whose value a contract test asserts equals the parsed `tokens.css` declaration (the existing `design-contracts.test.ts` already reads CSS as a string, so this is a few lines), or make `value()` throw in dev when the property resolves empty. That removes the second source of truth without introducing a silent failure, and fixes the stale `#f2b544`/`#7fd4e8` divergence as a side effect. (e) Add the non-text-contrast check to a gate: `scripts/validate-plot-contract.mjs` exists but has no colour rule, and nothing in `scripts/` computes luminance, which is why this survived four demos.
findings.note:
CONFIRMED, with three corrections. (1) The quoted code exists verbatim: `apps/demos/src/demos/cluster-census/main.ts:310` is `axis: value("--cp-border", "#3a4358"),` inside `readPalette()`, and `palette.axis` feeds `ctx.strokeStyle` at lines 615 (HR plot frame, `strokeRect`, lineWidth 1), 639 and 653 (HR gridlines) and 823 (histogram frame). `packages/theme/styles/tokens.css:9` is `--cp-border: rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.08);`. `grep -n "cp-border" packages/theme/styles/layer-instrument.css` returns nothing, so the instrument layer does not override it, and there is no `@property` registration anywhere in `packages/theme/styles/`, so `getComputedStyle(document.documentElement).getPropertyValue("--cp-border")` hands canvas the literal `rgba(255,255,255,0.08)`.
(2) I recomputed WCAG 1.4.11 relative luminance myself with `node -e` (sRGB linearization, L = 0.2126R+0.7152G+0.0722B, CR = (L1+0.05)/(L2+0.05)). The finder used the wrong background. `sizeCanvas` (main.ts:277-289) only `clearRect`s — it never fills a background — so the canvas bitmap is transparent and the stroke composites over the element's CSS background, which is `--cp-instr-panel-bg: rgba(23,27,34,0.88)` (`style.css:191`, `layer-instrument.css:26`) over `--cp-bg0 #0f1115`. That composite is rgb(22.04, 25.80, 32.44), L = 0.01008. Frame stroke = 8% white over it = rgb(40.68, 44.14, 50.24), L = 0.02509, **CR = 1.250:1** (the finder's 1.216:1 is 8% white over bare `--cp-bg0`, which I reproduce exactly but which is not what renders). Direction and verdict unchanged: the 3:1 non-text floor is missed by a factor of 2.4.
(3) The finding UNDERSTATES the gridlines, which are the worse defect. Lines 635 and 649 set `ctx.globalAlpha = 0.25` before the gridline strokes, so the effective stroke alpha is 0.08 x 0.25 = 0.02 → **CR = 1.050:1**; the histogram's expected-count line at line 847 runs at `globalAlpha = 0.2` → ~1.04:1. Those are the lines a student interpolates against, and they are mathematically indistinguishable from the panel.
(4) The finding OVERSTATES the failure scenario. "No quantity can be read off the figure" is false: tick labels are drawn in `palette.muted` = `--cp-muted` = color-mix(#ffffff 54%, bg0) = rgb(145,146,147), which I compute at **5.578:1** against the panel composite; the plotted points use `palette.amber`/`palette.accent`; and the canvas element carries a visible CSS border, `--cp-instr-panel-border: rgba(109,119,148,0.25)` (style.css:190) at 1.344:1 — faint but present. Corrected scenario: readable labelled ticks with no visible frame or gridlines between them, so a reader cannot trace a point back to an axis value or judge a turnoff position by eye; they must estimate from the label row alone.
(5) Reachability: live and unguarded. The path is the normal draw path of both plot canvases; no flag, no clamp. `apps/site/src/content/demos/cluster-census.md` is `status: draft`, `readiness: experimental` — so this is NOT a readiness-honesty finding, but the demo still ships at `/play/cluster-census/`. `git log -5` on main.ts (8fcedd6, b000a14, 6ac00e6, a03be65) shows no contrast work; `grep -rn "cp-plot-axis\|cp-plot-grid"` finds nothing, and there is no contrast gate in `scripts/` (`grep -rln "contrast\|luminance" scripts/` is empty), so nothing catches it.
(6) The high-contrast escape hatch does not rescue it: `high-contrast.css:6,15` raises `--cp-border` to `rgba(255,255,255,0.25)` → I compute **2.268:1**, still under 3:1. Nor does the paper layer: `layer-paper.css:13` `rgba(17,20,37,0.12)` on `#fafaff` → 1.283:1.
(7) The one claim I do refute is the implied locality. This is not a cluster-census bug; `--cp-border` is the plot-ink token across the repo: `apps/demos/src/demos/stars-zams-hr/main.ts:494` (`majorGrid`, used at 518, 529), `apps/demos/src/demos/spectral-lines/main.ts:707, 1354, 1371`, and `apps/demos/src/demos/binary-orbits/main.ts:245`. A cluster-census-only fix leaves three demos broken and the next demo reintroduces it.
(8) The stale-fallback sub-claims are true but belong at a lower severity: `--cp-accent-amber` is `#FFB86C` (tokens.css:123) vs fallback `#f2b544`; `--cp-accent-ice` is `#8BE9FD` (tokens.css:125) vs `#7fd4e8`; `--cp-text` and `--cp-muted` are `color-mix()` (tokens.css:13, 31) computing to rgb(226,226,227) and rgb(145,146,147) vs fallbacks `#e8edf7` and `#93a0b8`. All five diverge, but the `||` branch only fires when the stylesheet is absent, so that is P2 hygiene, not the P1.
(9) The proposed fix is directionally right but would break something as written. "Delete all five hardcoded hex fallbacks" leaves `value()` returning `""`; `ctx.strokeStyle = ""` is a silent no-op in Canvas 2D, so the previous `strokeStyle` persists — default `#000` on first use, i.e. black axes on a near-black panel. That is worse than the current state, not better. Also note the author's own intended fallback `#3a4358` only reaches 1.767:1 on the panel composite (1.911:1 on bg0), so "restore the intended colour" is not a fix either — a genuinely new value is needed, which is why this is Anna's call.

findings.title: The no-color-literals invariant is CSS-scoped by design (CLAUDE.md:223, invariants.md:47), leaving 147 static color literals in canvas-drawing demo .ts outside any gate — including 4 duplicated wavelength/temperature-to-RGB ramps
findings.evidence: Line 104: `const colorLiteralExts = new Set([".astro", ".css", ".html"]);`. The literal regex at line 115 is only applied when path.extname is in that set (guards at lines 154 and 315). .ts is absent. Counting with the same regex over apps/demos/src/demos/*/*.ts excluding tests: 147 matches. Representative hits: blackbody-radiation/main.ts:252-271 hardcodes an 11-stop rgba() visible-spectrum gradient; cluster-census/main.ts:310-314 hardcodes #3a4358, #e8edf7, #93a0b8, #7fd4e8, #f2b544 as fallbacks for five design tokens; cluster-census/main.ts:506 and 1046 hardcode rgba() panel fills; doppler-shift/logic.ts:255 hardcodes rgb(120, 80, 200). Line 160 additionally exempts the whole of DemoIllustration.astro by filename, which carries 13 hex literals.
findings.scenario: A maintainer retones the instrument palette in tokens.css. Every .astro and .css surface follows; every canvas-drawn pixel in 20 demos keeps the old colors, and `corepack pnpm build` reports success. CLAUDE.md states the build enforces this invariant automatically, so nobody looks.
findings.fix:
Treat this as DRY/maintainability, not a broken gate. Do not ship the fix as written.

(a) Fix the sound half now: replace the file-wide `filePath.endsWith("DemoIllustration.astro")` exemption at scripts/validate-invariants.mjs:157-158 with a per-line `/* cp-allow-color-literal: spectral data */` opt-out. That removes a blanket bypass on a scanned .astro file without touching scope.

(b) De-duplicate the color ramps — the real finding. Collapse the two byte-identical `wavelengthToRgbString` copies (doppler-shift/logic.ts:221, spectral-lines/logic.ts:182) into one exported helper, and reconcile temperature-to-RGB (cluster-census/logic.ts:172 vs packages/physics/src/blackbodyRadiationModel.ts:63) onto the physics one. Wavelength-to-RGB is physical data, so packages/physics is the right owner; add a test pinning a few anchors (486.1 nm -> rgb(0, 235, 255), 656.3 nm -> rgb(255, 0, 0)) so a future edit to one call site cannot silently change one demo's spectrum and not the other's.

(c) Convert genuine UI chrome to token reads, which needs no validator change: eos-lab/main.ts:415-419 hardcodes Tailwind-palette chart series colors (#34d399/#f472b6/#a78bfa/#fbbf24) while the same demo already has `resolveCss` at mechanismViz.ts:74 — route them through it. Same for doppler-shift/main.ts panel and grid fills (:566,570,605,639,669,694,718,725,737) and cluster-census/main.ts:506,1046.

(d) Only if Anna decides to widen the contract (her call — it is a design-system contract change): add ".ts" to colorLiteralExts AND first narrow the regex, or the gate lands false positives. Skip hex matches in selector context (`querySelector`/`getElementById`/`must<...>("#...")`) and skip `rgb(`/`rgba(`/`hsl(` immediately followed by `${` inside a template literal. Verify against conservation-laws/main.ts:77 and keplers-laws/main.ts:32, which must stay clean.

(e) Either way, amend CLAUDE.md:223 and .agents/references/invariants.md:47 to state the scope explicitly ("demo CSS, .astro and .html; canvas-drawn colors in .ts are not gated — see <owner>") so the next auditor does not re-file this as an enforcement hole.
findings.note:
CORE CLAIMS CONFIRMED, FRAMING AND SEVERITY WRONG.

1) Code exists verbatim. scripts/validate-invariants.mjs:104 is exactly `const colorLiteralExts = new Set([".astro", ".css", ".html"]);`. Regex at :115 `/#[0-9a-fA-F]{3,8}\b|\brgba?\(|\bhsla?\(/gi`. Guards at :154 (site) and :315 (demos) — both the lines the finder named. `textExts` at :99-110 DOES include ".ts", so demo .ts files are read and checked for BASE_URL/root-absolute links, then skipped for color literals. DemoIllustration exemption is at :157-158 (`filePath.endsWith("DemoIllustration.astro")`), not :160 — 3 lines off. That file carries exactly 13 hex literals, 0 rgb()/hsl() — the finder's "13" is exact.

2) I reproduced 147 independently, and the derivation matters. My own walk of apps/demos/src/demos for non-test .ts (49 files) gives 157 raw regex matches. Subtracting 2 DOM id selectors and 8 dynamic template constructions leaves exactly 147 static literals. Spot hits all verified at the named lines: cluster-census/main.ts:310-314 holds exactly #3a4358, #e8edf7, #93a0b8, #7fd4e8, #f2b544; main.ts:506 `rgba(10, 14, 24, 0.65)`; main.ts:1046 `rgba(150, 158, 176, 0.7)`; doppler-shift/logic.ts:255 `rgb(120, 80, 200)`; blackbody-radiation/main.ts:252-271 is a 10-entry specStops array plus UV and IR bracket stops (12 stops, not 11 — trivial).

3) The failure scenario's premise is FALSE. CLAUDE.md:223 reads "forbids hardcoded `rgba()` or hex values in demo CSS" and .agents/references/invariants.md:47 reads "no color literals in demo CSS". Every per-demo contract test scopes it the same way (angular-size/design-contracts.test.ts:127, blackbody-radiation:115, em-spectrum:76, binary-orbits:86, eos-lab:44 — all assert it of CSS only). The validator does exactly what the docs claim; it even exceeds them by covering .astro/.html. So there is no silently-unenforced invariant and no doc/implementation mismatch. The finding is arguing the contract's SCOPE should be wider — a design-system decision for Anna — not that a stated gate has a hole. "CLAUDE.md states the build enforces this invariant automatically, so nobody looks" misreads the documented scope.

4) "Every canvas-drawn pixel in 20 demos" is overstated ~2.5x. Only 8 of 20 demo slugs contain real static literals: eos-lab 48, galaxy-rotation 22, em-spectrum 20, spectral-lines 20, doppler-shift 14, blackbody-radiation 13, cluster-census 7, telescope-resolution 3. Worse for the finding, 6 of those 8 already read tokens live via getComputedStyle/resolveCss (eos-lab/mechanismViz.ts:74-80, eos-lab/uplotHelpers.ts:14-18, plus blackbody-radiation, spectral-lines, cluster-census main.ts), so a tokens.css retone DOES propagate to their canvas chrome. The cluster-census five at :310-314 sit behind `style.getPropertyValue(name).trim() || fallback` — they fire only if the token is undefined. The finder cited them as proof of the retone scenario while its own wording ("fallbacks for five design tokens") contradicts it.

5) Student reachability is nil for launch-ready surfaces. None of the 8 affected demos claims readiness: eos-lab, doppler-shift, blackbody-radiation, cluster-census, telescope-resolution are status: draft / readiness: experimental; galaxy-rotation, em-spectrum, spectral-lines are status: beta / readiness: candidate. No `launch-ready`/`stable` demo is affected. Wrong canvas tint is cosmetic — it cannot produce a wrong number or wrong geometry, so this will not "keep producing P0s."

6) The proposed fix is partly wrong. Adding ".ts" alone makes the hex regex fire on DOM id selectors — `must<HTMLSpanElement>("#ecc")` at conservation-laws/main.ts:77 and `querySelector<HTMLInputElement>("#ecc")` at keplers-laws/main.ts:32 — because `#[0-9a-fA-F]{3,8}\b` cannot distinguish the id `#ecc` from a color. It would also flag 8 dynamic `rgb(${...})`/`hsl(${...})` constructions (blackbody-radiation/main.ts:381,476; cluster-census/logic.ts:193-194; doppler-shift/logic.ts:259; spectral-lines/logic.ts:214, main.ts:661; stars-zams-hr/logic.ts:197) that compute color from physical data and are exactly what you want. Net effect: two demos with zero real violations acquire false ones. Also, "route physical-color data through a helper in packages/physics or packages/runtime" relocates literals into directories the validator deliberately does not scan (comment at :112-113), satisfying the lint by moving the code.

7) The stronger defect hiding inside this one, which the finder missed: wavelength/temperature-to-RGB is implemented four times — doppler-shift/logic.ts:221 and spectral-lines/logic.ts:182 both export `wavelengthToRgbString`, and temperature-to-RGB exists at cluster-census/logic.ts:172 and packages/physics/src/blackbodyRadiationModel.ts:63. I read both wavelength copies: identical branch boundaries (380/440/490/510/580/645/750), identical tapering, identical UV/IR fallbacks. I evaluated the shared ramp: 486.1 nm -> rgb(0, 235, 255), 656.3 nm -> rgb(255, 0, 0), 370 nm -> rgb(120, 80, 200). They agree today, so there is no correctness divergence — but it is a textbook single-source-of-truth violation that will drift, and it is the part of this finding actually worth a tracker entry.

findings.title: 52 inline trig expressions across 11 demos' main.ts compute drawn coordinates that no unit test can import, and the one demo that does extract them tests only symmetric phases
findings.evidence: Measured across all 20 demos: main.ts totals 26,736 lines against 8,511 lines of logic.ts (3.1:1 overall; angular-size is 1040 vs 140 = 7.4:1; binary-orbits 2353 lines; spectral-lines 2223). `ls */main.test.ts` returns no matches. Test-file census: 20 logic.test.ts, 20 design-contracts.test.ts, and exactly one main-level test in the whole repo (parallax-distance/main.integration.test.ts). Counting `^function draw|^function render|^function update` in main.ts gives 151 functions (binary-orbits 19, keplers-laws 15, moon-phases 12, retrograde-motion 11). The invariants file states "Pure UI logic goes in each demo's logic.ts (tested); main.ts is thin DOM wiring" - a 2,353-line main.ts is not thin wiring, and the project's own CLAUDE.md records that SVG y-down sign errors and a waxing/waning swap are the recurring defect class, both of which live in these functions.
findings.scenario: A geometry edit flips a sign in one of the 151 untested render functions - say cy + r*sin(theta) where SVG y-down needs cy - r*sin(theta). Unit tests all pass because none of them can import main.ts. The only coverage is Playwright, which asserts on readout text, not on drawn coordinates, so a mirrored orbit ships and a class learns a retrograde planet as prograde.
findings.fix:
Do not start with the 20-demo refactor the finding proposes; it is priced off a 151-function count that includes 9 demos with zero trig in main.ts and a precedent (riseSetViewModel) that returns text, not coordinates.

1. Cheapest decisive step first — add asymmetric probes to geometry that is ALREADY extracted and already tested, where a sign flip is currently invisible. In apps/demos/src/demos/binary-orbits/logic.test.ts:426, add a phase = pi/2 case: `bodyPositions(200,200,50,30,Math.PI/2)` must give y1 = 150, y2 = 230 px; a y-sign flip gives 250 and 170 px. This is a RED-capable test today and costs one edit.

2. Scope extraction to the 11 demos that actually hold view trig in main.ts, highest first: spectral-lines (12 lines), eclipse-geometry (9), keplers-laws (8), retrograde-motion (7), parallax-distance (6). Extract each as a coordinate-returning function in that demo's logic.ts and unit-test it at an asymmetric angle (not 0, 90, 180, 270). keplers-laws is the best first target: its logic.ts has no coordinate export at all, so main.ts:315-316 and :402-408 are the whole gap.

3. Only AFTER step 2 shows the same converter repeated should a shared module go into packages/runtime — and it must NOT be the single north-up `cy - r*sin` converter the finding proposes. CLAUDE.md records that seasons and eclipse-geometry are deliberately clockwise; a north-up-only helper would silently mirror both. The shared signature needs an explicit handedness argument (e.g. `polarToSvg({cx, cy, r, thetaRad, handedness: "ccw" | "cw"})`) with unit tests for both senses at an asymmetric angle, or it will manufacture the exact defect class it is meant to prevent.

4. Correct the record in the tracker: coordinate-level Playwright coverage already exists for seasons (20 attribute reads), conservation-laws (8), parallax-distance (4), keplers-laws (equal-area from path `d`), eclipse-geometry, moon-phases and cluster-census. Those demos are lower priority than the ones with neither unit nor coordinate-level e2e coverage: spectral-lines, retrograde-motion, planetary-conjunctions, galaxy-rotation and hydrostatic-equilibrium-explorer.
findings.note:
CONFIRMED (every number recomputed independently, not reused): `wc -l` over the 20 main.ts files gives 26,736 lines; over the 20 logic.ts files 8,511; my own sum/divide gives 3.141:1, angular-size 1040/140 = 7.43:1, binary-orbits 2,353, spectral-lines 2,223. `grep -cE '^function (draw|render|update)'` per demo gives 19/15/12/11/9/9/8/8/7/7/7/6/6/5/5/5/4/3/3/2, which I summed to exactly 151. `find apps/demos/src/demos -name '*.test.ts'` returns 20 logic.test.ts, 20 design-contracts.test.ts, four extra moon-phases module tests (animation, exportPayload, riseSetUiState, riseSetViewModel) and exactly one main-level test, apps/demos/src/demos/parallax-distance/main.integration.test.ts. No main.test.ts exists. The quote is verbatim at /Users/anna/Teaching/cosmic-playground/.agents/references/invariants.md:45. No shared SVG-geometry module exists in packages/runtime/src (its math.ts only re-exports @cosmic/math numerics plus KaTeX helpers; the only Math.sin/cos in the package are in starfield.ts).

THREE CLAIMS INSIDE THE FINDING ARE WRONG:

(1) The anchor file is the worst possible example of its own mechanism. `grep -cE 'Math\.(sin|cos|atan2)' apps/demos/src/demos/binary-orbits/main.ts` returns 0. Its orbital geometry lives in apps/demos/src/demos/binary-orbits/logic.ts:583 `bodyPositions` (and :549 `computeOrbitScreenRadii`) — inside the test boundary, imported at logic.test.ts:7. The claimed failure ("cy + r*sin(theta) in one of the 151 render functions") cannot occur in binary-orbits/main.ts at all. angular-size, the 7.4:1 demo, is also 0.

(2) "The only coverage is Playwright, which asserts on readout text, not on drawn coordinates" is false. Nine of 28 specs read drawn coordinates: apps/site/tests/seasons.spec.ts has 20 such reads (terminator `cx` at equinox vs solstice :308-318, axis `rotate(...)` :333, perihelion vs aphelion `cx`/`cy` :440-448), conservation-laws.spec.ts 8, parallax-distance.spec.ts 4, eclipse-geometry.spec.ts 2, moon-phases.spec.ts 1, cluster-census.spec.ts 1, and apps/site/tests/keplers-laws.spec.ts:620 computes wedge area from the path `d` string for the equal-areas check.

(3) The fix's cited precedent is misdescribed. apps/demos/src/demos/moon-phases/riseSetViewModel.ts:3-8 returns `{riseText, setText, statusText, isPolar}` — text and a flag, no coordinates. It is not "the coordinate-returning pattern moon-phases already uses."

WHAT SURVIVES, AND IS REAL: `grep -cE 'Math\.(sin|cos|atan2)'` across main.ts gives 52 lines in 11 demos — spectral-lines 12, eclipse-geometry 9, keplers-laws 8, retrograde-motion 7, parallax-distance 6, planetary-conjunctions 3, galaxy-rotation 2, hydrostatic-equilibrium-explorer 2, seasons/moon-phases/doppler-shift 1 each — and 9 demos have 0. keplers-laws/main.ts:315-316 computes `px = cx + rAu*cos*scale; py = cy - rAu*sin*scale` on canvas; keplers-laws/logic.ts exports no coordinate function at all (only formatters, readouts, drift, export payload), so that line is reachable by no unit test. The sign there is correct north-up: I recomputed at theta = +30 deg, cx=cy=200 px, r=50 px — correct gives y = 175.00 px (above center), flipped gives 225.00 px. So there is absent coverage, not a live wrong drawing.

A STRONGER DEFECT THE FINDING INVERTED: binary-orbits/logic.test.ts:426-442 probes `bodyPositions` only at phase 0 and phase pi. I recomputed both the shipped form and a y-sign-flipped form at 200,200,50,30: phase 0 gives 150.00, 200.00, 230.00, 200.00 for BOTH; phase pi gives 250.00, 200.00, 170.00, 200.00 for BOTH. sin = 0 at both probes, so a y-sign flip is invisible. Only at phase pi/2 do they diverge (y1 = 150.00 vs 250.00 px). This is the exact trap CLAUDE.md records ("Test physics at asymmetric points, not only symmetric ones") and it is in code the finding counts as safely inside the test boundary.

SEVERITY: corrected P1 -> P2. invariants.md:45 ("main.ts is thin DOM wiring") is literally violated, which argues for P1, but no live defect was demonstrated, 9 demos already keep geometry in tested logic.ts, and coordinate-level e2e coverage exists for 9 demos. This is refactor-and-coverage debt, not something a student currently sees wrong. The true scope is 52 trig lines in 11 demos, not 151 functions in 20.

git log -3 on binary-orbits/main.ts (2b3f086, ff714a3, 0f75490) shows no work addressing this.

findings.title: All 84 museum pages load and execute a 275 kB KaTeX chunk; hasMath is a no-op for both bundle and behavior
findings.evidence: KatexAutoRender.astro:2-3 contains a bundled `<script>` doing `import katex from "katex"` and `import renderMathInElement from "katex/contrib/auto-render"`. Layout.astro:131 renders it behind a runtime conditional, `{hasMath ? <KatexAutoRender /> : null}`, which Astro resolves after it has already hoisted the script into the page bundle. Traced in dist: apps/site/dist/index.html loads _astro/hoisted.f6KNXGkz.js (577 bytes), whose first statements are `import"./hoisted.CIKfj6fN.js";import"./HeroOrbit...js";import"./hoisted.DGZXIX3A.js"` - and hoisted.DGZXIX3A.js is 274,704 bytes containing 2,127 LaTeX macro strings. index.astro:42 explicitly passes hasMath={false}. I counted the built museum pages: 84 total, 69 referencing the chunk directly in HTML plus 15 reaching it through a hoisted entry = 84 of 84. CLAUDE.md's hard constraint reads "minimal client JS on museum pages", and the repo already owns a build-time renderer (apps/site/src/lib/inlineMath.ts).
findings.scenario: A student on a lecture-hall phone opens the homepage on shared wifi. Before any content is interactive the browser downloads and parses 275 KB of KaTeX that the page author explicitly declared it does not need, and that typesets nothing because hasMath={false} removed the only consumer.
findings.fix:
Remove the client KaTeX pass entirely rather than trying to make the conditional work — the chunk is shared with MobileNav's script, so gating the render is useless while the static import at Layout.astro:4 exists.

Order matters, because deleting first would put literal `$M_2/M_1$` on 20 public exhibit pages:

1. Migrate every non-Markdown surface that prints frontmatter text to build-time KaTeX, using the existing `renderInlineMath()` from apps/site/src/lib/inlineMath.ts (the pattern already in DemoCard.astro:112,115 and index.astro:122): `exhibits/[slug].astro:101` and `:115`, plus the `$...$` occurrences in `stations/[slug].astro` and `instructor/[slug].astro`, plus Explore's excerpts. Audit by grepping the 17 demo content files whose frontmatter carries `$` against every page that prints those fields — do not assume predict_prompt/explain_prompt are the only two.
2. Verify no reader-visible surface needs display math outside Markdown. Today none does (the only `$$` in any .astro is inside KatexAutoRender itself), but `renderInlineMath` is inline-only, so add a `renderDisplayMath()` wrapper over `katex.renderToString(..., {displayMode: true})` if step 1 turns one up.
3. Delete apps/site/src/components/KatexAutoRender.astro, its import at Layout.astro:4, the `hasMath?: boolean` type at Layout.astro:12, the default at :22, the conditional at :110, and the eight `hasMath={...}` call sites.
4. Keep the WCAG 2.1.1 keyboard-reachability pass as a small `<script>` with no katex import — it only needs `scrollWidth > clientWidth` on `.katex-display`, and that now applies to build-time output. Verify after the rebuild that this script does not land in a chunk with anything heavy.
5. Update CLAUDE.md:128's surrounding math-authoring table: the row claiming ".astro pages still use client auto-render, where `$$` is display" becomes false.

Verification that does not depend on a test name: rebuild, then re-run the import-graph closure over apps/site/dist and assert that no `.html` reaches a chunk containing KaTeX, and that dist/index.html's total JS drops from 295,893 B to roughly 21,000 B. Confirm by eye that an exhibit page still renders its predict prompt as typeset math in markup with JS disabled.
findings.note:
CONFIRMED, and the defect is worse than claimed. I verified every load-bearing fact independently.

(1) Code exists, with citation drift. `apps/site/src/components/KatexAutoRender.astro:1-3` is a bundled (non-`is:inline`) `<script>` doing `import katex from "katex"` and `import renderMathInElement from "katex/contrib/auto-render"`. The conditional is at `apps/site/src/layouts/Layout.astro:110`, not :131 — `{hasMath ? <KatexAutoRender /> : null}` — with the static import at Layout.astro:4 and the prop defaulted at Layout.astro:22. `apps/site/src/pages/index.astro:43` (not :42) passes `hasMath={false}`. The finder's line numbers are from before the uncommitted `noindex`/nav-extraction edits in the working tree; the mechanism is unchanged.

(2) Recomputed the bundle myself, not reusing the finder's arithmetic. `node -e` on `apps/site/dist/_astro/hoisted.DGZXIX3A.js`: 274,704 bytes = 268.3 KiB raw; gzip -9 = 80,400 B = 78.5 KiB; brotli = 66,740 B = 65.2 KiB. For scale, `node_modules/.pnpm/katex@0.16.28/.../katex.min.js` is 276,705 B, so the chunk is essentially all KaTeX. I confirmed chunk identity two ways rather than by name: it contains the component's own string `"Scrollable equation"` (grep -l shows it in that chunk and no other) and 1,029 unique `\macro` tokens.

(3) Recomputed the page count with my own import-graph resolver over `apps/site/dist` (104 HTML files, transitive closure of `_astro/*.js` imports): **direct 69, indirect 15, reachable-but-neither 0, no-JS 20**. Identical to the claim: 84 of 84 museum pages pull the chunk; the 20 misses are all `/play/<slug>/index.html`, the Vite-built demos that do not use Layout. `dist/index.html` has exactly one script tag, `_astro/hoisted.f6KNXGkz.js` (577 B), whose first statements are `import"./hoisted.CIKfj6fN.js";import"./HeroOrbit...js";import"./hoisted.DGZXIX3A.js"`.

(4) The `hasMath` prop is a complete no-op — stronger than the finding says, and this refutes the finding's own failure scenario. The compiled auto-render call sits at **top level** of the imported chunk (offset 265,384 of 271,868): `const st=document.querySelector("main");if(st){Tn(st,{delimiters:...})...}`. Importing the chunk executes it. So on the homepage, with `hasMath={false}`, KaTeX is downloaded, parsed, *and* the auto-render pass still walks `main`. The claimed "typesets nothing because hasMath={false} removed the only consumer" is wrong; nothing was removed. Three pages author the opt-out and get zero benefit: index.astro:43, explore/index.astro:176, stations/index.astro:23.

(5) Root cause is sharper than "Astro resolves the conditional too late." The chunk also contains MobileNav's compiled script (`document.getElementById("mobile-nav")` immediately follows the KaTeX pass), so it is Layout's shared hoisted chunk. Making the conditional work would not help — MobileNav renders unconditionally and Vite has merged it with KaTeX. The static `import` at Layout.astro:4 must go.

(6) Reachable and live, not already fixed. `git log -3` on both files shows the last touches are `3964c95` (header nav) and `0719a09` (Markdown math moved to rehype-katex) — the latter is what left this pass with only non-Markdown math to do, and it did not remove the import. No guard exists; `grep -rn hasMath` finds only the eight call sites. `dist/` is stale (Sep 11) but I confirmed the current source still has the identical structure, so a rebuild reproduces it.

(7) Contract text confirmed: `CLAUDE.md:128` reads "Prefer static + fast pages; minimal client JS on museum pages." Homepage JS is 295,893 B raw across four chunks, of which KaTeX is 93%.

Severity: P1 stands. Not P0 — no wrong number, wrong drawing, or broken page. Not P2 — it violates a documented hard constraint on 84/84 museum pages, and a prop that silently does nothing is a false affordance that will keep misleading page authors (it already has, three times). One correction to the magnitude rhetoric: GitHub Pages serves gzip, so the wire cost is 78.5 KiB, not 275 KB — a 3.5x overstatement in the failure scenario. The 275 kB parse/compile cost on a low-end phone is real and is the better argument.

Fix correction: the proposed fix works but is under-scoped and has one latent gap. `apps/site/src/pages/exhibits/[slug].astro:101` and `:115` print `{entry.data.predict_prompt}` / `{entry.data.explain_prompt}` as raw text, and 17 of the demo content files carry `$...$` in frontmatter (binary-orbits.md:24, galaxy-rotation.md:23 among them), so deleting the component without migrating those first puts literal `$M_2/M_1$` on 20 public exhibit pages. `stations/[slug].astro` and `instructor/[slug].astro` also pass `hasMath={true}` and each carry one `$...$` occurrence of their own. Also, `renderInlineMath` (apps/site/src/lib/inlineMath.ts) splits on `(\$[^$]+\$)` with `displayMode: false`, so it cannot render display math; CLAUDE.md asserts ".astro pages still use client auto-render, where `$$` is display", but I grepped every `.astro` under apps/site/src and the only `$$` is inside KatexAutoRender.astro itself — so that gap is latent, not live, and the CLAUDE.md sentence becomes stale once this lands.

findings.title: The 36 KB minified theme chain is flattened into all 20 demo CSS bundles — 82% of per-demo CSS is a duplicated design system, and 5 contract tests pin the pattern
findings.evidence: stub-demo.css lines 1-16 @import tokens.css, animations.css, layer-instrument.css, demo-shell.css and 12 component files; every demo's style.css line 1 imports stub-demo.css, so Vite inlines the whole chain into each demo's CSS entry. The chain concatenates to 62,977 bytes of source. In the deployed tree, all 20 of apps/site/public/play/assets/*.css contain the tokens.css marker --cp-celestial-sun-core and the demo-shell.css marker cp-demo__shelf; total deployed demo CSS is 916,720 bytes (895 KB), with individual bundles at 60,415 (hydrostatic-equilibrium-explorer), 54,869 (eos-lab) and 48,599 (binary-orbits) bytes. Each bundle has its own content hash, so no byte is shared.
findings.scenario: A lab section works through a playlist of four demos. Each navigation re-downloads the full design system - roughly 50 KB of identical tokens, shell and component CSS under a new hashed filename - because nothing is shared between /play/<slug>/ bundles. On a classroom connection that is four render-blocking stylesheet fetches that should have been one cache hit.
findings.fix:
Drop the `manualChunks` half of the proposed fix — it cannot work. Each demo's CSS is reached through `<link rel="stylesheet" href="./style.css">` in its entry index.html (apps/demos/src/demos/moon-phases/index.html:7), and the `@import` chain is resolved and flattened by Vite's CSS pipeline (postcss-import) *before* rollup chunking. `build.rollupOptions.output.manualChunks` governs JS chunk boundaries and has no power to split an already-flattened CSS entry.

The `<link>` half is correct, and the repo already proves the mechanism: every source index.html separately links `../../assets/katex/katex.min.css` (moon-phases/index.html:8), and Vite emitted exactly ONE shared hashed chunk for it (`stellarLifetimeModel-D2lIc1rk.css`) that all 20 built pages reference at the same URL. So:

1. Stop importing the chain from each demo's style.css. Reduce every `apps/demos/src/demos/<slug>/style.css` to demo-local rules only.
2. Add one `apps/demos/src/shared/cosmic-theme.css` holding the 16 `@import`s plus stub-demo.css's own rules, and link it from each demo's index.html *above* `./style.css`, exactly as katex.min.css is linked today. Vite will hash-and-share it once across all 20 entries, matching the katex precedent.
3. Keep the cascade order: the theme link must precede the demo-local link, since demo rules currently rely on being emitted after the chain (the measured 36,281-byte prefix is followed by demo-local CSS in every bundle).
4. Update the five design-contracts tests that assert the `@import` (e.g. apps/demos/src/demos/cluster-census/design-contracts.test.ts:166, `expect(css.trimStart()).toMatch(/^@import "\.\.\/\.\.\/shared\/stub-demo\.css";/)`) to assert the index.html `<link>` to the shared theme instead. Do not delete the assertion — it is the only thing stopping a demo from silently shipping without the token system.

Expected gain, by my own measurement: per-demo CSS drops from 887,881 B to ~198,000 B raw, eliminating 673 KiB of duplication, and a 4-demo playlist saves ~21 KiB gzipped. Fix it for the single-source-of-truth and build-hygiene win, not for the bandwidth — on a gzipping CDN the wire saving is ~6.9 KiB per navigation.
findings.note:
CORE CLAIM CONFIRMED, BUT THE CACHING CLAIM, THE MAGNITUDE AND THE CATEGORY ARE ALL WRONG.

Confirmed by reading the code:
- apps/demos/src/shared/stub-demo.css:1-16 @imports tokens.css, animations.css, layer-instrument.css, demo-shell.css and 12 component files, exactly as quoted.
- apps/demos/src/demos/moon-phases/style.css:1 is `@import "../../shared/stub-demo.css";`, and moon-phases/index.html:7 links it as `<link rel="stylesheet" href="./style.css" />` — so Vite's CSS pipeline (postcss-import) flattens the chain into each entry's CSS before rollup chunking.
- I did NOT reuse the finder's arithmetic. Source chain by my own `wc -c`: 63,737 B (finder said 62,977 — off by 760 B). Total deployed demo CSS: 916,720 B = 895.2 KiB (exact match). Individual bundles 60,415 / 54,869 / 48,599 B (exact match). All 20 demo bundles contain both `--cp-celestial-sun-core` and `cp-demo__shelf`.
- I proved the duplication independently with a common-prefix computation in `node -e`: moon-phases vs seasons = 36,281 B identical prefix; moon vs telescope-resolution = 36,282 B; seasons vs telescope = 36,281 B. That prefix ends exactly at stub-demo.css's final rule (`.cp-drawer ul{margin:8px 0 0;padding-left:18px;color:var(--cp-muted)}`) and contains the tokens, shelf, starfield, playbar, chip, toggle, reduced-motion and cp-slide-up markers. So the duplicated region is precisely the whole shared chain: 35.4 KiB minified, repeated in all 20 bundles. 19 redundant copies = 689,339 B = 673 KiB, i.e. 82% of the 867.1 KiB of per-demo CSS is duplicated theme. The DRY defect is real.

REFUTED sub-claims:
1. "Each bundle has its own content hash, so no byte is shared" / "nothing is shared between /play/<slug>/ bundles" is FALSE. Every built page links TWO stylesheets, e.g. apps/site/public/play/moon-phases/index.html: `../assets/stellarLifetimeModel-D2lIc1rk.css` AND `../assets/moon-phases-CP0VWBc5.css`. The first is 28,839 B, is linked by all 20 demos at the identical URL (`grep -l … | wc -l` = 20), and so IS a cross-demo cache hit. Its content is the KaTeX stylesheet (`@font-face{…font-family:KaTeX_AMS…}`, misnamed by Vite's chunk naming); it contains none of the theme markers. The finder's own 916,720 B total includes this shared chunk, inflating the "per-demo" figure — per-demo bundles alone are 887,881 B.
2. The failure scenario's "roughly 50 KB of identical tokens, shell and component CSS" per navigation is overstated. Measured duplicate is 35.4 KiB raw, and the deploy target is GitHub Pages (.github/workflows/deploy.yml uses upload-pages-artifact@v3 / deploy-pages@v4), whose CDN gzips CSS. I measured the prefix gzipped: 7,092 B = 6.9 KiB. A 4-demo playlist therefore wastes 3 x 6.9 KiB = 20.8 KiB on the wire, not ~150-200 KB.
3. "four render-blocking stylesheet fetches that should have been one cache hit" is wrong on both halves: each page makes two stylesheet fetches, and one of them already is a cache hit.
4. The measured tree is a gitignored stale local build, not a deployed committed artifact: `git ls-files apps/site/public/play` returns 0 files and `git check-ignore -v` resolves to `.gitignore:12:apps/site/public/play/`. Timestamps are Sep 11 19:45 while stub-demo.css has changed since (7dd9b81). The mechanism is a property of the build config so it still holds, but the exact bytes are from a six-week-old build.

Severity correction P1 -> P2, and category "performance" -> architecture/DRY. 6.9 KiB gzipped per extra navigation is not a classroom-bandwidth problem, and no student sees a wrong number, wrong drawing or broken page. What gives the finding real weight is the single-source-of-truth angle the user asked about: 82% of every demo's CSS bytes are a duplicated copy of the design system, and five design-contracts tests (`grep -rln 'stub-demo.css' apps/demos/src/demos/*/design-contracts.test.ts` = 5) pin the inlining pattern in place, so it is self-perpetuating.

findings.title: KaTeX is fanned into three trees: the whole /play/assets/katex/ copy (1.05 MiB) deploys dead and unreferenced, and woff/ttf in the two live sets add 1.56 MiB no browser fetches (2.607 MiB total)
findings.evidence: main() at lines 74-80 copies the KaTeX bundle into apps/site/public/assets/katex, apps/demos/public/assets/katex, and apps/demos/src/assets/katex. Measured on disk: apps/site/dist/assets/katex is 1.2 MB / 61 files and apps/site/dist/play/assets/katex is 1.2 MB / 61 files - two complete copies in the Pages artifact at different URLs, so a visitor who moves from a museum page to a demo re-downloads every font. Breaking down one copy's fonts/ directory: 20 woff2 files = 296 K, 20 woff = 336 K, 20 ttf = 540 K. All 20 demo index.html files link ../../assets/katex/katex.min.css.
findings.scenario: A student opens an exhibit page (fonts fetched from /assets/katex/fonts/) then clicks Play (same fonts re-fetched from /play/assets/katex/fonts/ with no cache hit). Each fetch set also offers woff and ttf variants that no browser capable of running these demos will ever request, so the deployed artifact carries 1.75 MB of font payload that can never be used.
findings.fix:
1. Delete `await copyKatexIntoPublic(demosDir);` at scripts/copy-katex-assets.mjs:75. That single line removes the entire dead play/assets/katex/ tree (1,100,304 B = 1074.5 KiB) from the Pages artifact. Nothing references it - verified by grep over all of apps/site/dist, which yields only /cosmic-playground/assets/katex/katex.min.css. KEEP copyKatexIntoSourceAssets(demosDir) at :77: Vite resolves ../../assets/katex/katex.min.css through it, which is why commit 4369ffd added it.

2. Harden scripts/build.mjs:58-60. Instead of treating every directory in apps/demos/dist as a demo slug, intersect the directory list with the real content-collection slugs that scripts/validate-play-dirs.mjs already derives from apps/site/src/content/demos/*.md. Copying dist/assets as a slug is the root cause of the dead tree, and it will recreate one for any future apps/demos/public subdirectory. Fixing this makes step 1 robust rather than incidental.

3. Only if the remaining 1.56 MiB of woff/ttf is worth removing (it costs students zero bytes - it is artifact size alone): do NOT merely filter the copy to fonts/*.woff2, which breaks the Vite build on unresolvable url() references. Instead, in copyKatexBundle, read katex.min.css and strip the woff/truetype src entries (regex over `,url\([^)]*\.(woff|ttf)\) format\("(woff|truetype)"\)`) before writing it, then copy only fonts/*.woff2. Doing it inside the one script keeps site and demos in sync - the single-source-of-truth property the audit is after. Verify with one `pnpm build` at an agreed batch boundary (not now, other agents are running) and re-measure dist.

4. Do NOT pursue the museum/demo font URL dedup as proposed. It is the one change with real breakage risk and the smallest payoff (tens of KiB of woff2 on one navigation). If it is ever worth closing, the lever is a single shared URL injected at build time from import.meta.env.BASE_URL plus far-future Cache-Control headers, never a relative ../../../ guess or a hardcoded /cosmic-playground/ prefix.

Net effect of steps 1-2 alone: -1.05 MiB artifact, no behavior change, no build risk, and the accidental-slug bug closed.
findings.note:
Core structural claim VERIFIED, causal mechanism and all numbers REFUTED, severity corrected P1 -> P2.

VERIFIED: scripts/copy-katex-assets.mjs main() spans lines 70-78 and fans the bundle into three trees - copyKatexIntoPublic(siteDir) at :74, copyKatexIntoPublic(demosDir) at :75, copyKatexIntoSourceAssets(demosDir) at :77 (finding said "74-80"; minor). du -sk confirms apps/site/dist/assets/katex = 1196 KB/61 files and apps/site/dist/play/assets/katex = 1196 KB/61 files. All 20 apps/demos/src/demos/*/index.html link ../../assets/katex/katex.min.css at line 8. @font-face src order in katex.min.css is url(...woff2) format("woff2"), url(...woff) format("woff"), url(...ttf) format("truetype") across all 20 rules, so woff/ttf are never fetched by any browser that can run these ES-module/WebGL demos.

REFUTED - the mechanism. Vite BUNDLES that stylesheet link; it does not survive as a reference to /play/assets/katex/. The built demo head (apps/site/dist/play/moon-phases/index.html) has NO katex href; KaTeX lands in apps/site/dist/play/assets/stellarLifetimeModel-D2lIc1rk.css, whose font URLs are Vite-hashed siblings: url(./KaTeX_AMS-Regular-BQhdFMY1.woff2). `grep -rho "[^\"' (]*assets/katex/[^\"' )]*" apps/site/dist` returns exactly ONE string: /cosmic-playground/assets/katex/katex.min.css (the site copy). So play/assets/katex/ is referenced by nothing - it is not a second serving copy, it is entirely dead weight. There are THREE font sets in the artifact, not two: (1) dist/assets/katex/fonts, live for museum pages; (2) dist/play/assets/KaTeX_*-<hash>.*, live for demos; (3) dist/play/assets/katex/, dead.

REFUTED - the arithmetic (finder used du block-allocated sizes, inflated ~40 KiB per set by 4-KiB rounding over 20 files). Recomputed with node from apparent byte sizes: woff2 20 files 259792 B = 253.7 KiB (claimed 296 K); woff 20 files 303116 B = 296.0 KiB (claimed 336 K); ttf 20 files 513664 B = 501.6 KiB (claimed 540 K). woff+ttf = 816780 B = 797.6 KiB, not 876 KB. True never-fetchable payload: (a) site copy woff+ttf 816780 B + (b) play/assets/katex/ entire tree 1100304 B (1074.5 KiB, 60 fonts + 23732 B css) + (c) hashed woff+ttf 816780 B = 2733864 B = 2.607 MiB, i.e. 1.56x the claimed 1.75 MB - the finder UNDERCOUNTED by missing the hashed third set and by not realizing the whole play/assets/katex tree is dead.

REFUTED - "re-downloads every font". Browsers fetch only the families whose glyphs actually render (KaTeX_Main-Regular, KaTeX_Math-Italic, a Size*, sometimes AMS), typically 3-6 of 20, so the museum->demo transition costs tens of KiB of woff2, not 253.7 KiB. The cache miss itself is real but incidental: museum fetches /cosmic-playground/assets/katex/fonts/*.woff2, demos fetch /cosmic-playground/play/assets/KaTeX_*-<hash>.woff2 - different URLs, separate cache entries. Right conclusion, wrong route.

Reachability/provenance: the dead tree is genuinely build-produced, not stale. scripts/build.mjs:58-60 reads apps/demos/dist with withFileTypes and treats EVERY directory as a demo slug; Vite copies publicDir (apps/demos/public) verbatim, so dist/assets exists and is copied to apps/site/public/play/assets. Confirmed: both apps/demos/dist and apps/site/public/play list an "assets" entry alongside the 20 slugs. All of it is generated and gitignored (.gitignore:6,7,12,16,17,18; `git ls-files` on those paths returns 0), so this is deploy-artifact weight only, zero repo bloat.

Severity P1 -> P2. Nothing is broken: every page renders, all math displays, no wrong number or drawing reaches a student. Not a contract violation, not an a11y blocker, not misleading copy, not an architecture defect that will keep producing P0s. Real impact is ~2.6 MiB of bytes GitHub Pages stores but nobody fetches, plus a modest woff2 re-fetch on one navigation. The legitimate angle is DRY/single-source-of-truth - a script fanning one bundle into three trees, one of which silently becomes dead deployed weight because build.mjs mistakes dist/assets for a demo slug - which is P2 "polish/consistency/DRY".

Proposed fix is backwards on its key point. git show 4369ffd ("fix KaTeX build warning") ADDED copyKatexIntoSourceAssets exactly so Vite could resolve ../../assets/katex/katex.min.css from src/demos/<slug>/index.html; it is NOT a "dev-server-only convenience" and dropping it reintroduces that warning. The droppable copy is apps/demos/public/assets/katex. Also "restrict copyKatexBundle to fonts/*.woff2 only" would break the build: the bundled katex.min.css still carries url(fonts/*.woff) and url(fonts/*.ttf), and Vite 5.4 cannot resolve the absent files. And routing demo HTML to the site-root copy is fragile: apps/demos/vite.config base is "./" while apps/site/astro.config base is /<repoName>/, so any path from /play/<slug>/ to site root either hardcodes the base path (breaking the CP_BASE_PATH-unset E2E case and the CLAUDE.md import.meta.env.BASE_URL rule) or breaks the standalone dev server.

findings.title: 11 demos snapshot prefers-reduced-motion at module scope, and their rAF loops never consult it, so a mid-session preference change does not stop an animation already playing
findings.evidence: Fourteen demos compute a module-scope constant and never update it: binary-orbits/main.ts:227-230, blackbody-radiation:84, conservation-laws:150, doppler-shift:151, eclipse-geometry:246, galaxy-rotation:200, keplers-laws:173, moon-phases:270, parallax-distance:119, planetary-conjunctions:256, retrograde-motion:59, seasons:415-418, spectral-lines:151-154, plus eos-lab/mechanismViz.ts:56. Only parallax-distance/main.ts:1387-1400 constructs a live MediaQueryList and attaches a change handler (it also handles the legacy addListener path). seasons/main.ts:420-422 shows the consequence directly - the reduced-motion note is written once at load and never revised. By contrast apps/site/src/components/DemoCanvasThumbnail.astro attaches media.addEventListener("change", ...) and redraws statically, so the museum layer already has the correct pattern. CLAUDE.md Motion Contract: "All animations respect prefers-reduced-motion."
findings.scenario: A student with motion sensitivity opens keplers-laws, finds the orbit animation uncomfortable, and turns on Reduce Motion in system settings. The demo keeps animating, because the preference was read once before the page finished loading, and nothing short of a reload will stop it.
findings.fix:
The proposed fix would not fix the stated failure, and over-reaches on three files.

Why it does not fix it: swapping the 11 module-scope constants for a live getter changes nothing for a loop already in flight, because the loops never read the preference at all — they check only their own playing flag (galaxy-rotation `tick` :424-427 tests `sweepFrame === 0`; keplers-laws `step` :697 tests `state.playing`). A live `get matches()` is only consulted where the old constant was consulted, which in every case is at play-request time, not per frame.

What I would apply instead:
1. Add `watchReducedMotion(onChange: (reduced: boolean) => void): { matches: boolean; dispose(): void }` to packages/runtime/src/polish.ts, next to the existing private `prefersReducedMotion()` at :11 so a 4th variant of the snippet is not created, and export it from packages/runtime/src/index.ts:38 beside `initDemoPolish`. Implement with `addEventListener("change", ...)` plus the `addListener` fallback that parallax-distance/main.ts:1393-1397 already carries.
2. In each of the 11 demos, the onChange callback must call that demo's existing stop function, not merely re-read a flag: `stopRadiusSweep()` (galaxy-rotation:408), `stopAnimation()` (keplers-laws:712), `setPlaying(false, false)` (parallax-distance:1391), and the equivalents in the other eight, then re-run the demo's `render()`/`update()` and its `syncPlaybarState()`-style button sync. parallax-distance:1387-1400 is the correct reference precisely because it does this — it clears `state.blinkMode`, calls `setPlaying(false, false)`, then `updateBlinkTimer()` and `render()`.
3. Also add the preference check to the two confirmed in-flight loops that live-read elsewhere but not per frame (keplers-laws `step` :696-707, galaxy-rotation `tick` :424-440), or rely on step 2 calling their stop functions — step 2 is sufficient and cheaper.
4. Do NOT migrate eos-lab/mechanismViz.ts:55: it already holds a live MediaQueryList and reads `.matches` live at all twelve call sites. Converting it risks regressing working code. keplers-laws:169 and parallax-distance:116 need only step 2 (the stop-on-change wiring), not a constant migration — they have no constant to migrate.
5. Guard against a secondary regression: several demos disable the Play button when the preference is set (galaxy-rotation:401, moon-phases:656, eclipse-geometry:1043-1045). The onChange handler must re-enable those buttons when the preference is turned OFF mid-session, otherwise the fix introduces a permanently dead Play button — a defect the current snapshot code does not have.
findings.note:
The headline claim is real at the named file:line, but the count, three of the fourteen citations, the contract quote and the failure scenario are all wrong, and the severity is one level too high.

CONFIRMED. apps/demos/src/demos/binary-orbits/main.ts:227-230 is exactly a module-scope boolean snapshot in the form quoted (`const prefersReducedMotion = typeof window !== "undefined" && typeof window.matchMedia !== "undefined" && window.matchMedia("(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)").matches;`), read later at :435, :463, :567, :2064 and never recomputed. I read each cited file directly and confirmed 11 such snapshots: binary-orbits:227, blackbody-radiation:81, conservation-laws:149, doppler-shift:148, eclipse-geometry:243, galaxy-rotation:197, moon-phases:268, planetary-conjunctions:253, retrograde-motion:57, seasons:415, spectral-lines:151. parallax-distance/main.ts:1387-1400 does construct a live MediaQueryList with both addEventListener and the addListener fallback, and apps/site/src/components/DemoCanvasThumbnail.astro:113 does the same, so both reference patterns cited exist.

COUNT CORRECTION: 11, not 14. Three cited lines are misidentified as snapshots. (a) keplers-laws/main.ts:173 is the body of `function prefersReducedMotionEnabled()` declared at :169, invoked live at :689 (startAnimation), :911 (space key) and :1131 — not a constant. (b) parallax-distance/main.ts:119 is likewise the body of a function declared at :116, invoked live at :132, :847, :1024; the finding lists this file as a broken snapshot AND as the one correct implementation, which is self-contradictory. (c) eos-lab/mechanismViz.ts:55-56 binds a MediaQueryList *object*, not a boolean, and every one of its twelve uses (:137, :147, :160, :162, :319, :329, :339, :340, :456, :462, :470, :471) reads `reducedMotion.matches`, which is live per CSSOM View. Not a snapshot at all.

FAILURE SCENARIO REFUTED AS WRITTEN. It names keplers-laws, which live-reads: a student who enables Reduce Motion and then presses Play gets no animation (:689 returns early, :911 returns early). The real keplers-laws gap is much narrower — an *already-running* loop does not stop, because `step` at :697 checks only `state.playing`. I confirmed the identical narrow gap in galaxy-rotation's `tick` (:424-427, checks only `sweepFrame === 0`).
