So the defect that actually bites is "an in-flight rAF loop never consults the preference," which is a different and smaller defect than "the preference is snapshotted."

CONTRACT QUOTE TRUNCATED. CLAUDE.md:226 invariant 8 reads in full: "All animations respect `prefers-reduced-motion` via the global override in `animations.css`." The finding dropped the clause naming the mechanism. packages/theme/styles/animations.css:80-89 is a live CSS media query forcing `animation-duration: 0.01ms !important`, `animation-iteration-count: 1 !important` and `transition-duration: 0.01ms !important` on `*`, `*::before`, `*::after`, which takes effect the instant the preference flips with no reload. The invariant as literally written is therefore satisfied, live, in all 11 demos. The uncovered surface is JS-driven rAF stepping, which invariant 8 does not name — so this is not a contract violation.

REACHABILITY. The preference is honored correctly on the common path: OS motion settings are set once, before browsing, and module-scope evaluation runs at page load, so all 11 demos correctly disable autoplay and the Play button (galaxy-rotation:401, :1494; moon-phases:656; retrograde-motion:385; spectral-lines:1599; doppler-shift:452; eclipse-geometry:1043-1045). The defect requires flipping the OS setting while the page sits open, and even then every affected demo exposes a Pause button, plus reload. Not an a11y blocker.

FIX PREMISE PARTLY RIGHT: packages/runtime/src/polish.ts:11 already holds a private `prefersReducedMotion()`, and packages/runtime/src/index.ts:38 exports only `initDemoPolish` and `initScrollAffordance`, so there is indeed no exported helper today.

findings.title: formatNumber is copy-pasted into 14 demos with six divergent behaviours, and its exponential path emits the e-notation CLAUDE.md forbids
findings.evidence: I dumped all 14 implementations. Thresholds for switching to exponential differ: stars-zams-hr/logic.ts:72 switches at abs >= 1e5, doppler-shift/logic.ts:59 at 1e4, angular-size/logic.ts:27, blackbody-radiation:39, planetary-conjunctions:184, spectral-lines:142 and telescope-resolution:42 at 1e6, while binary-orbits/logic.ts:46, galaxy-rotation:33, parallax-distance:50, seasons:12, retrograde-motion:16 and eclipse-geometry:16 never switch at all. conservation-laws/logic.ts:44 uses a third strategy (widening toFixed decimals). Non-finite sentinels diverge too: stars-zams-hr returns "-" where all 13 others return the em dash. Every exponential path calls value.toExponential(...), which produces strings such as 1.234e+7. CLAUDE.md and .agents/references/invariants.md both state: "Powers of ten as $10^n$; no `e` notation in teaching-facing copy."
findings.scenario: A student computes a stellar luminosity of 2.5e5 Lsun in stars-zams-hr (rendered 2.50e+5) and the same magnitude in galaxy-rotation (rendered 250000.000). They copy both into a lab report and cannot tell whether the quantities agree, and the e-notation form is the one the course has told them not to write.
findings.fix:
The direction is right — one shared formatter, no e-notation, one sentinel — but the fix as proposed would break more than it repairs, because a single LaTeX-returning function cannot serve this repo's three incompatible output sinks. I counted them: 98 `textContent = ...formatNumber(...)` assignments, 10 `ctx.fillText(...formatNumber(...))` canvas sites, and 5 `setLiveRegionText(...formatNumber(...))` ARIA sites. Returning `$1.23 \times 10^{5}$` renders literally as dollar signs and backslashes in all 98 textContent sites, prints as raw LaTeX source in the canvas sites (which CLAUDE.md explicitly exempts from KaTeX and requires ASCII), and makes a screen reader speak the backslashes in the 5 live-region sites. It would also poison the CSV/JSON exports that flow through `toCsv` / `formatExport`: a spreadsheet cell holding `$3.58 \times 10^{5}$` is strictly worse than the `3.58e+5` it replaced.

What I would apply instead:

1. Add `formatQuantity(value, { sigFigs, style })` to packages/runtime beside `renderInlineKatex`, with three styles, never e-notation, and one `"—"` sentinel:
   - `style: "katex"` -> returns the rendered HTML for `$3.58 \times 10^{5}$`; migrate the 98 DOM sites from `.textContent =` to `.innerHTML =` (or have the helper take the element), since LaTeX in textContent renders literally.
   - `style: "ascii"` -> `3.58 x 10^5`, for the 10 canvas `fillText` sites (CLAUDE.md's documented KaTeX exemption) and for every export path through `toCsv` / `formatExport`.
   - `style: "spoken"` -> "3.58 times ten to the fifth", for the 5 `setLiveRegionText` sites.

2. Fold in the sibling duplicates in the same pass or they re-diverge immediately: `formatWithUnit` (stars-zams-hr/logic.ts:80), `formatSigned` (doppler-shift/logic.ts:67 and galaxy-rotation/logic.ts:38), `formatSignedBeta` (eclipse-geometry/logic.ts:27), `formatSignedPercent` (keplers-laws/logic.ts:57). Delete all 14 local `formatNumber` copies, including stars-zams-hr's `"-"` sentinel.

3. Add the build guard that makes it stick, which the finding omits and which is why 14 copies accumulated unnoticed: extend `scripts/validate-math-formatting.mjs` (its `SCAN_ROOTS` at line 19 already covers `apps/demos/src/demos`) to fail on `toExponential(` and on a locally declared `function formatNumber` anywhere under that root. Without this, nothing prevents the 15th copy — the existing validator at line 33 only screens Unicode glyph literals.

4. Two questions for Anna, both pedagogical and hers to decide, and the second is more urgent than the finding suggests: (a) the single switching threshold at which a readout goes to powers-of-ten notation; (b) significant figures versus fixed decimals. The current `toFixed(4)` prints L = "92321.6838" — nine significant figures from a polynomial fit good to perhaps two or three. Moving to sig-figs is a precision claim about the physics, so it needs her approval rather than an engineering default.
findings.note:
NOT REFUTED — confirmed by reading all 14 files and independently recomputing the output.

1. Quoted code exists verbatim. `apps/demos/src/demos/stars-zams-hr/logic.ts:72-77`: `if (!Number.isFinite(value)) return "-";` then `if (abs >= 1e5 || abs < 1e-3) return value.toExponential(Math.max(0, digits - 1));`.

2. All 14 copies and every claimed threshold confirmed by dumping each body: stars-zams-hr:72 (1e5), doppler-shift:59 (1e4), angular-size:27 / blackbody-radiation:39 / planetary-conjunctions:184 / spectral-lines:142 / telescope-resolution:42 (1e6), binary-orbits:46 / galaxy-rotation:33 / parallax-distance:50 / seasons:12 / retrograde-motion:16 / eclipse-geometry:16 (plain toFixed, never switch), conservation-laws:44 (widening decimals on the small side only). The "six distinct behaviours" count is exactly right — angular-size:31 is its own sixth variant, calling `value.toExponential(digits - 1)` with no `Math.max(0, ...)` guard unlike the other four 1e6 demos. Sentinel divergence confirmed: stars-zams-hr returns `"-"`, the other 13 return `"—"` (retrograde-motion via `EM_DASH` at logic.ts:10).

3. Invariant text confirmed verbatim: `CLAUDE.md:170` "Powers of ten as `$10^n$`; no `e` notation in teaching-facing copy." and `.agents/references/invariants.md:27` "never `e` notation in teaching copy."

4. Independently recomputed, NOT reusing the finder's arithmetic. I re-implemented the Tout+1996 luminosity fit from the coefficient table at `packages/physics/src/zamsTout1996Model.ts:40-48` in plain node and evaluated L(M, Z=0.02) = (alpha*M^5.5 + beta*M^11)/(gamma + M^3 + delta*M^5 + epsilon*M^7 + zeta*M^8 + eta*M^9.5):
   - L(28 Msun) = 1.008e5 Lsun -> readout prints "1.008e+5"
   - L(50 Msun) = 3.58398e5 Lsun -> readout prints "3.58e+5"
   - crossover: e-notation begins at M = 27.91 Msun (L = 1.00000e5 Lsun)
   Also `COMPACT_REMNANT` (`hrInferencePopulationModel.ts:292`) has Teff = 2.2e5 K, and `main.ts:797/893` call `formatNumber(star.Teff, 0)`, which yields `toExponential(0)` = "2e+5" K — forbidden notation at one significant figure.

5. Reachable by a student. Population mass range is `MASS_MIN_MSUN = 0.1` to `MASS_MAX_MSUN = 50` (`hrInferencePopulationModel.ts:56-57`), sampled at line 311, so stars above 27.9 Msun are drawn. Live reader-visible sinks, not dead code: `stars-zams-hr/main.ts:796` (`${formatNumber(star.L, 3)} L/L_sun`), `main.ts:892` (`selectedLuminosity.textContent = formatNumber(star.L, 4)`), `main.ts:1031` and `1438` (exports).

6. Not already fixed or guarded. `git log -3` on the file ends at 2b3f086 with no formatter change. `packages/runtime/src/index.ts` exports only `formatExportText` and `formatExport` — there is no shared numeric formatter to migrate to. `rg toExponential scripts/` returns nothing, and `scripts/validate-math-formatting.mjs:33` only screens Unicode glyph literals, so nothing catches a runtime-generated "3.58e+5".

CORRECTION TO THE FINDING — one leg of the failure scenario is fabricated. galaxy-rotation cannot render "250000.000" for a luminosity: it has no luminosity readout at all, and every mass it formats is pre-divided by 1e10 (`mTotal10`, `mVisible10`, `mDark10` at `galaxy-rotation/main.ts:950-952`), so its values are O(0.1-100) kpc, km/s and ratios and its missing exponential branch is never exercised. The cross-demo collision as written does not occur. The real and sharper scenario is inside stars-zams-hr alone: two neighbouring stars in the same cluster plot, 27 and 28 Msun, print "92321.6838" and "1.008e+5" — 9 percent apart in L, shown in two different notations with two different apparent precisions, on the same axes.

SEVERITY P1 CONFIRMED, not downgraded. No number is wrong, so it is not P0; but it is a breach of an explicitly written repo invariant in reader-visible output, plus a 14-way duplication with six divergent behaviours — exactly the "architecture defect that will keep producing" class.

Also noted, not a separate finding: angular-size:31's missing `Math.max(0, ...)` guard would throw `RangeError: toExponential() argument must be between 0 and 100` if `digits = 0` were ever passed. I grepped `angular-size/main.ts` and no call site passes 0, so it is latent and unreachable today — but it is one copy-paste away from a thrown exception.

findings.title: A student inside /play/<slug>/ has no link back to Explore or the homepage
findings.evidence: Every one of the 20 demos has exactly three escape links, all inside a popover behind a three-dot icon button labelled "Navigation" / "More links": `grep -c cp-popover-link apps/demos/src/demos/*/index.html` returns 3 for 19 demos (7 for eclipse-geometry, of which 3 carry hrefs). Enumerating every href gives exactly `../../exhibits/<slug>/`, `../../stations/<slug>/`, `../../instructor/<slug>/` × 20 and nothing else. `grep -rln '\.\./\.\./explore' apps/demos/src/demos/` returns 0 files, and `grep -rn "explore/" packages/runtime/src apps/demos/src/shared` returns nothing, so no shared runtime injects one either. Two of the three available links (Station card, Instructor notes) are instructor artefacts.
findings.scenario: An instructor pastes https://astrobytes-edu.github.io/cosmic-playground/play/moon-phases/ into a course page — the natural deep link, since it is the demo itself. The student finishes the activity and wants another demo. There is no header, no breadcrumb, and the only menu offers the exhibit page, a printable station card, and instructor notes. They hit the back button into the LMS instead of browsing the catalogue.
findings.fix: Add a "Back to all demos" link (`../../explore/`) as the first item of the nav popover in all 20 `apps/demos/src/demos/*/index.html` files — or, better, stop hand-writing the popover per demo and emit it from one helper in packages/runtime/src (the markup is already byte-identical across 19 of them), which also fixes the per-demo drift in the toolbar button ids noted separately.

findings.title: The "In N playlists" link is dead: playlists/index.astro reads searchParams at build time on a static site
findings.evidence: `const demoFilterSlug = Astro.url.searchParams.get("demo")?.trim() ?? ""` (playlists/index.astro:15) feeds `filteredPlaylists` (:16-20), `demoFilterTitle` (:25-27) and the "Showing playlists containing X" status region (:57-64). `apps/site/astro.config.mjs:11` sets `output: "static"`, so frontmatter runs once at build with an empty query string: `demoFilterSlug` is always `""`, `filteredPlaylists === playlists`, and the status region never renders. `grep -c "<script" apps/site/src/pages/playlists/index.astro` returns 0, so nothing re-applies it in the browser. The links that target it are built at explore/index.astro:255 and :323 as `${withBase("playlists/")}?demo=${encodeURIComponent(d.slug)}` and rendered by DemoCard.astro:145-147 as "In N playlists". This is the same defect catalog.ts:6-15 and explore/index.astro:32-37 document as already fixed elsewhere.
findings.scenario: A student on /explore/ clicks "In 2 playlists" under Moon Phases and lands on the full, unfiltered playlists index with four use-case groups and no indication of which two contain Moon Phases, and no "Clear filter" affordance to explain what happened.
findings.fix: Delete the build-time read at playlists/index.astro:15-27 and move it to a small client script that reads `location.search`, hides non-matching `.playlist-card` elements and unhides the filter note — the pattern already proven in apps/site/src/lib/exploreFilter.ts. Extract the shared "read a narrowing param from the URL after hydration" helper into lib/ so the third page that needs it does not reinvent it.

findings.title: Homepage "Start here" sequence is two experimental drafts, and excludes the only launch-ready demo
findings.evidence:
index.astro:88-93 renders `

Start here

` with the lede "These three demos introduce the core orbital mechanics concepts. Work through them in order for the best experience." The three are `featured: true` in frontmatter and ordered by `featuredOrder = ["keplers-laws", "retrograde-motion", "binary-orbits"]` (index.astro:26). Reading the frontmatter of all 20 demos: keplers-laws is `readiness: experimental` / `status: draft`; retrograde-motion is `experimental` / `draft`; binary-orbits is `candidate` / `beta`. The one `launch-ready` / `stable` demo in the whole catalogue is parallax-distance, which is not featured. Tallying all 20: 11 experimental/draft, 8 candidate/beta, 1 launch-ready. `readiness.ts:39-55` means each of keplers-laws and retrograde-motion carries a "experimental -- usable, still being revised" badge on its own card inside the "work through them in order" sequence. The same three are re-presented at explore/index.astro:231-235 as "Featured sequence / Begin with the core orbit ideas before branching out."
findings.scenario: An instructor evaluating the site for a Spring course follows the homepage's own recommendation, clicks card 1 of 3, and the exhibit page immediately shows "Active development: draft / experimental" plus a "Legacy content (unverified)" callout. The site's loudest recommendation and its own readiness data disagree.
findings.fix: Derive the featured set from readiness rather than hand-curation: in apps/site/src/pages/index.astro replace the `featured` filter with the top three by `readinessRank` (lib/readiness.ts:70), or keep curation but gate it — refuse to feature anything below `candidate` and say so in the lede. Move `featuredOrder` out of index.astro:26 and explore/index.astro:48 (verbatim duplicates) into lib/catalog.ts so there is one answer.

findings.title: /about/ claims "3 modes per demo" and "each demo ships with Challenge Mode"; 9 of 20 have no Challenge control
findings.evidence: about.astro:19-24 hardcodes `{ value: "3", unit: "modes per demo", label: "Station / Challenge / Export" }` and :89-93 states "Each demo ships with Station Mode ..., Challenge Mode ..., and Export". I enumerated the controls in all 20 `apps/demos/src/demos/*/index.html`: Export (`id="copyResults"`) is present in 20/20; a station control is MISSING in em-spectrum and planetary-conjunctions (2 of 20); a challenge control is MISSING in blackbody-radiation, cluster-census, conservation-laws, em-spectrum, keplers-laws, parallax-distance, planetary-conjunctions, spectral-lines and stars-zams-hr (9 of 20, including the homepage's featured card 1 and the only launch-ready demo). The surviving controls also carry seven different ids for the same job (btn-challenges, challengeMode, challengeModeBtn, challengeCard, rvChallengePanel, scalingChallenge, copyChallengeEvidence), i.e. a per-demo fork of shared behaviour. The same false claim is embedded in a code comment at explore/index.astro ("every demo ships a Station-mode lab, so 'Labs' narrows 19 to 19"). The stat bar's own comment at about.astro:16 brags "Derived, not hardcoded: this read '14' while 19 demos shipped" — about the adjacent number only.
findings.scenario: An instructor reads "3 modes per demo" on /about/, builds a lab around Challenge Mode for Kepler's Laws, and finds no challenge control in that instrument at all. Nine of twenty assigned demos cannot deliver the self-assessment the site advertises.
findings.fix: Derive both numbers in apps/site/src/pages/about.astro:19-24 from the demos collection instead of hardcoding them, which requires adding `modes: ("station"|"challenge"|"export")[]` to the demos schema in apps/site/src/content/config.ts and populating it per demo; then reword :89-93 to say what the catalogue actually offers ("every demo exports its data; most add Station Mode; N add Challenge Mode"). Add a datasets/contract test asserting the frontmatter `modes` list matches the controls present in that demo's index.html.

findings.title: The /welcome/ onboarding quiz hand-lists 6 of 8 topics and routes "Data & Inference" to a demo outside that topic
findings.evidence: welcome.astro:11-18 hardcodes `const topics = [...]` with six entries and hardcoded `start` slugs, importing nothing from lib/topics.ts. Galaxies and Cosmology are absent. The start slugs disagree with `TOPIC_SEQUENCE` (topics.ts:82-111) in two places: DataInference -> `conservation-laws` here vs `parallax-distance` in the sequence, and Stars -> `eos-lab` here vs `hydrostatic-equilibrium-explorer` in the sequence. conservation-laws.md:6 reads `topics: [Orbits]` — it is not a DataInference demo at all, so welcome.astro:157 sends the student to `exhibits/conservation-laws/` while :160 offers "See all Data & Inference exhibits" at `topics/datainference/`, a page that lists parallax-distance, doppler-shift, cluster-census and galaxy-rotation and does NOT contain conservation-laws. eos-lab.md is `readiness: experimental`, is last in `TOPIC_SEQUENCE.Stars` ("the microphysics"), and per CLAUDE.md has a first-visit tour that blocks interaction. This is verbatim the drift topics.ts:5-8 was written to end ("`TopicStrip` shipped six of the eight topics").
findings.scenario: A student clicks the homepage's "Answer two questions" link, picks Student, picks "Data & Inference", and is told "We recommend starting with this exhibit" above a link to Conservation Laws — a demo the site's own taxonomy files under Orbits. Picking "Stars" lands them on the hardest, least-ready instrument in the catalogue. Students interested in Galaxies or Cosmology cannot choose them at all.
findings.fix: In apps/site/src/pages/welcome.astro delete the local `topics` array and build it from `TOPIC_ORDER`, `TOPIC_LABEL` and `TOPIC_SEQUENCE[key][0]` in apps/site/src/lib/topics.ts, filtering to topics that have at least one listed demo (the same derivation topics/index.astro:16-21 already uses). Add a unit test asserting every `TOPIC_SEQUENCE[k][0]` resolves to a listed demo whose `topics` include `k`.

findings.title: /welcome/ is JS-only and is the homepage's only onboarding entry point
findings.evidence: Steps 2 and 3 ship with `class="welcome-step is-hidden"` / `welcome-result is-hidden` (welcome.astro:57, 77) and `.welcome-step.is-hidden { display: none }` / `.welcome-result.is-hidden { display: none }` (:181, :299). The only thing that removes those classes is the inline `<script define:vars={{base}}>` at :96-162 (`revealStep` -> `el.classList.remove("is-hidden")`). The role controls are `<button type="button" data-role=...>` inside no form, so with JS unavailable they are inert, the two further steps stay `display: none`, and the page is a heading plus two dead buttons. The result card's static fallback text is "Loading recommendation..." (:84), which never resolves. index.astro:63-66 is this page's single inbound link ("New here? Answer two questions and we will point you at the right starting place"), and the page appears in neither the header nav (Layout.astro:94-125) nor the footer nav (:135-143) nor MobileNav.astro:18-24.
findings.scenario: A student on a locked-down campus machine, a slow connection that drops the module, or a browser extension that blocks inline scripts follows the homepage's "New here?" link and reaches a page reading "Who are you?" with two buttons that do nothing and the text "Loading recommendation..." below the fold. The site's entire onboarding path is a dead end.
findings.fix: Render all three steps unconditionally in apps/site/src/pages/welcome.astro and let the script collapse the later ones progressively (add `is-hidden` from JS rather than removing it), so the no-JS page degrades to a plain list of role and topic links. Replace the `<button>` role/topic controls with real `<a>` links to the destinations they already compute, which makes the whole page work without the script and removes the need for `define:vars`.

findings.title: Glossary renders Wien's law in SI units as Unicode glyphs with a literal underscore subscript
findings.evidence:
glossary.ts:105-108 stores `definition: "The peak wavelength of a blackbody spectrum is inversely proportional to the temperature: λ_max = b / T, where b ≈ 2.898 × 10⁻³ m·K."` and glossary.astro:72 renders it as `

{entry.definition}

` — plain text, no `renderInlineMath()`. So a reader sees literally: `λ_max = b / T, where b ≈ 2.898 × 10⁻³ m·K`. Three separate invariant breaks: (1) SI units — CLAUDE.md says "NEVER use SI units (meters, kg, Joules) — use CGS (cm, g, erg)"; in CGS Wien's constant is b = 0.2898 cm K (I converted: 2.8977719e-3 m K x 100 cm/m = 0.28977719 cm K). (2) Unicode math (λ, ≈, ×, superscript −3, ·) where the repo mandates LaTeX. (3) `λ_max` renders with a visible underscore instead of a subscript, because nothing typesets the string. glossary.ts:65 has the same pattern: `(~23.4°)`. apps/site/src/data is NOT in `SCAN_ROOTS` at scripts/validate-math-formatting.mjs:19-27, so the build gate never looks at this file.
findings.scenario: A student in an ASTR 101 section whose lab sheets are all in CGS looks up "Wien's displacement law" in the site glossary and copies b = 2.898 x 10^-3 m K into a calculation they are doing in cm and erg, off by a factor of 100. They also see `λ_max` with a literal underscore and `10⁻³` as a glyph the surrounding CSS can restyle at will.
findings.fix: Rewrite both definitions in apps/site/src/data/glossary.ts as LaTeX in CGS ($\\lambda_{\\max} = b/T$ with $b \\approx 0.2898\\ \\mathrm{cm\\,K}$; $\\approx 23.4^{\\circ}$), render them through `renderInlineMath()` from apps/site/src/lib/inlineMath.ts at apps/site/src/pages/glossary.astro:72, and add `path.join(repoRoot, "apps", "site", "src", "data")` to `SCAN_ROOTS` in scripts/validate-math-formatting.mjs:19 so the gate covers this surface.

findings.title: The math gate misses ≤, →, · and every \uXXXX escape, so banned glyphs ship green
findings.evidence: `FORBIDDEN_UNICODE_MATH = /[°☉µμ′″×−∝≈∞ + Greek + sub/superscript digits]/u` (validate-math-formatting.mjs:33). It contains no `≤ ≥ ≠ ± · ÷ √ ∑ ∫ → ←`. Grepping the already-scanned roots for those characters finds live violations the gate passes: FilterBar.astro:62 `<option value="lt10" data-label="≤10 min">≤10 min</option>` (twice on one line), for-instructors/index.astro:44 `Predict → Play → Explain` (twice), and `·` at explore/index.astro:212, topics/[slug].astro:186, for-instructors/index.astro:63, CitationCard.astro:32. Separately, the regex is run against raw file text, so `\uXXXX` escapes are invisible to it — which .agents/references/invariants.md explicitly forbids ("and no `\uXXXX` escapes that produce them (the validator cannot see escapes)"). DemoCard.astro:73 does exactly that: `timeMinutes <= 10 ? "≤10 min" : ...`, i.e. a reader-visible `≤10 min` time pill on every card on every catalogue surface.
findings.scenario: `corepack pnpm build` passes, so a reviewer concludes the KaTeX-only rule holds. Meanwhile every demo card on /explore/, /topics/*/ and the homepage shows a `≤` glyph that inherits whatever the surrounding CSS does to it — the precise failure mode CLAUDE.md records for 2026-09-05, when an inherited `text-transform` turned frequency ν into "N".
findings.fix: Extend the character class at scripts/validate-math-formatting.mjs:33 with `≤≥≠±·÷√∑∫→←↔⊙∂∇`, and add a second pass that decodes `\\u[0-9A-Fa-f]{4}` and `&#x...;` escapes before testing, so escape evasion fails the gate. Then fix the three call sites it will light up: DemoCard.astro:73 (render the time pill through `renderInlineMath` as `$\\leq$10 min`), FilterBar.astro:62, and for-instructors/index.astro:44.

findings.title: Explore's topic dropdown and filter chips print raw enum keys, bypassing TOPIC_LABEL
findings.evidence: explore/index.astro:38 builds `const topics = Array.from(new Set(demos.flatMap(d => d.data.topics))).sort()` — the raw schema enum keys from content/config.ts:12-21 — and passes them to FilterBar. FilterBar.astro:50-54 renders `<option value={t} data-label={t}>{t}</option>`; FilterBar.astro imports only `Icon` and defines `READINESS_LABEL` and `LEVEL_LABEL` but never imports `TOPIC_LABEL`. So the dropdown reads "DataInference", "EarthSky", "LightSpectra" where topics.ts:32-41 defines them as "Data & Inference", "Earth & Sky", "Light & Spectra". The active-filter chip repeats it: explore/index.astro's `CHIP_LABEL` sets `topic: (v) => \`Topic: ${v}\``, so the chip reads "Topic: LightSpectra". The `.sort()` also replaces `TOPIC_ORDER` ("roughly the order an intro course meets these ideas") with alphabetical order on the internal key, putting Data & Inference first and Earth & Sky second. Every other surface — TopicStrip, DemoCard, exhibit header, topics/index, topic sections on the same Explore page (explore/index.astro:301 uses `TOPIC_SUMMARY[section.key]` and :299 the label) — uses the human label.
findings.scenario: A student on /explore/ opens "Choose a topic" and sees "LightSpectra (4)" in a list sorted alphabetically by an internal identifier, while the section heading twenty pixels below the same control reads "Light & Spectra". Selecting it produces a chip reading "Topic: LightSpectra".
findings.fix: Pass `TOPIC_ORDER`-filtered keys from apps/site/src/pages/explore/index.astro:38 (drop the `.sort()`), and in apps/site/src/components/FilterBar.astro import `TOPIC_LABEL`/`isTopicKey` from ../lib/topics and emit `<option value={t} data-label={label}>{label}</option>`. Change `CHIP_LABEL.topic` in explore/index.astro to look the label up the same way, so the client script and the server markup share one vocabulary.

findings.title: Three hand-listed navigation sources with three different link sets; /instructor/ and /welcome/ are in none
findings.evidence: Three independent hand-written lists: the desktop nav as five inline `<a>` elements at Layout.astro:94-125 (Explore, Topics, Playlists, For Instructors, About); the footer nav as seven inline `<a>` elements at Layout.astro:135-143 (adds Station cards and Glossary); and `const links = [...]` at MobileNav.astro:18-24 (five, matching the desktop set). Nothing derives from a shared constant, and `grep -rn "const withBase" apps/site/src` plus the route inventory shows /instructor/ and /welcome/ appear in none of the three — /welcome/ has exactly one inbound link anywhere on the site (index.astro:64, a line of body copy) and /instructor/ two (index.astro:201 and for-instructors/index.astro:111). MobileNav.astro:2-4 also claims it is "Enhanced with a small script for Escape key + ARIA handling" and is "Visible only below 768px (--cp-bp-md)", but the script at :45-61 does no ARIA work at all (`aria-label="Open navigation menu"` on the summary at :28 never changes when the panel opens) and the breakpoint is 899px (:71).
findings.scenario: A route added to the desktop nav is silently missing from the mobile nav and the footer, exactly as /instructor/ and /glossary/ already are from one list or another. A screen-reader user on a phone opens the menu and the toggle still announces "Open navigation menu" while it is open.
findings.fix: Add `export const PRIMARY_NAV` and `export const FOOTER_NAV` to a new apps/site/src/lib/nav.ts (or to lib/catalog.ts), each an array of `{href,label}`, and consume them in Layout.astro:94-125, Layout.astro:135-143 and MobileNav.astro:18-24. While there, bind the summary's accessible name to the open state in MobileNav.astro and correct the stale comment at :2-7.

findings.title: /explore/ renders 29 demo cards for 20 demos, and with JS off shows all of them under a count that reads 20
findings.evidence: `topicSections` (explore/index.astro:105-109) renders one card per demo-topic pair. I recomputed from the 20 frontmatter `topics` arrays: 26 topic-section cards (galaxy-rotation alone appears 3 times, under Galaxies, Cosmology and DataInference), plus 3 in the featured strip = 29 `DemoCard` instances. The result count at :272 prints `{sorted.length}` = 20. Deduplication and the hiding of the featured demos' topic-section copies happen only in the client script ("if (!filtering) { if (card.dataset.featured === 'yes') card.hidden = true }"), so with JS unavailable the page shows keplers-laws, retrograde-motion and binary-orbits twice each and galaxy-rotation three times, above the text "20 interactive exhibits". Each `DemoCard` is 7-10 tab stops (illustration link, title link, 1-3 topic pills, Play, Station card, Instructor notes, Open exhibit, optional playlist chip); summing per-card stops x cards gives at least 196 tab stops inside `.results` alone, before the header, filter bar, quick chips and topic jump nav.
findings.scenario: A keyboard-only student presses Tab from the filter bar and needs roughly 200 presses to traverse the catalogue, with "Station card" and "Instructor notes" — two instructor artefacts — in the path on every single card. With JS blocked they also see six duplicate cards under a count claiming twenty.
findings.fix: Render one card per demo in a single results grid in apps/site/src/pages/explore/index.astro and make the topic headings pure in-page anchors over that one grid, rather than re-rendering cards per topic; move the featured three out of the grid entirely or mark their topic-section copies `hidden` in the markup so no-JS is correct by default. Reduce DemoCard.astro's actions to Play plus "Open exhibit" and move Station card / Instructor notes behind the exhibit page (where they already are), cutting roughly 60 tab stops.

findings.title: binary-orbits is featured as step 3 of 3 while its 320px reflow failure is documented and excluded from the gate
findings.evidence: reflow.spec.ts:49-55 states: "Play routes are added one demo at a time, for demos at `candidate` readiness or above whose `/play/` page has been separately verified not to scroll sideways at 320px. `binary-orbits` is candidate but currently DOES scroll sideways at 320px (its drawer accordions take their minimum from unbreakable KaTeX display equations), so it stays out until that is fixed." `PLAY_ROUTES = ["play/conservation-laws/"]` (:56) — 1 of 20 play routes is gated. binary-orbits.md is `readiness: candidate` ("ready to assign, pending final review", readiness.ts:53) and `featured: true`, and index.astro:88-93 presents it as step 3 of a sequence to "work through in order". `apps/site/tests/accessibility.spec.ts` covers only `/play/` instrument internals (root aria-label, status region, starfield aria-hidden, toolbar role, readout unit spans) — it has no assertion about the site's header, nav, skip link, breadcrumbs or focus visibility, so none of the chrome a11y defects in this audit has any gate at all.
findings.scenario: A student on a phone, or a sighted user at 400% browser zoom, opens the homepage's featured card 3 of 3 and has to scroll sideways to reach the controls — a WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.10 failure the repo knows about, on a demo the site labels "ready to assign, pending final review".
findings.fix: Either demote binary-orbits from `featured: true` and `candidate` in apps/site/src/content/demos/binary-orbits.md until the reflow failure is fixed, or fix it (`min-width: 0` on the accordion grid tracks and `overflow-x: auto` on the KaTeX display blocks) and add `play/binary-orbits/` to `PLAY_ROUTES` in apps/site/tests/reflow.spec.ts:56. Independently, add an apps/site/tests/site-chrome-a11y.spec.ts covering the skip link, nav current-state and keyboard order on the museum routes.

findings.title: apps:no-color-literals skips .ts, so 142 colour literals and every canvas drawing surface sit outside the token system
findings.evidence: `const colorLiteralExts = new Set([".astro", ".css", ".html"]);` gates the only use of rxColorLiteral (line 115). Counted with rg over apps/demos/src/**/*.ts excluding tests: 142 literal colour values in 13 files -- galaxy-rotation/main.ts 22, spectral-lines/main.ts 14, blackbody-radiation/main.ts 13, eos-lab/mechanismViz.ts 12, doppler-shift/main.ts 12, eos-lab/main.ts 7, eos-lab/regimeMap.ts 6, plus 21 in packages/runtime/src/starfield.ts. These are not only spectral data: galaxy-rotation/main.ts:628-629 paints its legend card with `fillStyle = "rgba(8, 12, 22, 0.78)"` and `strokeStyle = "rgba(212, 224, 248, 0.22)"`, :660 its labels with `rgba(226, 234, 248, 0.9)`, :696 gridlines with `rgba(217, 226, 243, 0.2)`. I recomputed the gridline against its own ground: 1.65:1, below the 3:1 WCAG 1.4.11 floor for a graphical object a student reads values off. CLAUDE.md invariant 5 states the rule without the .ts caveat.
findings.scenario: The theme changes --cp-bg1 or --cp-accent for legibility. Every CSS surface follows; the eight canvas/uPlot demos keep their hand-mixed panel, label and gridline colours and drift out of the system, and no gate reports it. Today a student reading galaxy-rotation's rotation curve has gridlines at 1.65:1 that the design system has never seen.
findings.fix: Two parts. (a) In scripts/validate-invariants.mjs add ".ts" to colorLiteralExts for apps/demos/src, with an explicit allowlist keyed to physically-motivated palettes (spectral-lines/logic.ts wavelength-to-RGB, blackbody Planck gradient, starfield spectral classes) rather than a blanket exemption. (b) Give packages/runtime a cssVar()-backed chart-chrome helper that reads --cp-bg2 / --cp-muted / --cp-border / --cp-chart-* once per resize, and convert the demo canvases to it so axis, label, legend and gridline colours come from tokens.

findings.title: Nothing measures the ground the instrument panels are actually painted on: readout labels fall to 3.88:1 over a bright star, orbit-shell glass text to 1.55:1
findings.evidence: `--cp-instr-panel-bg: rgba(23, 27, 34, 0.88)` and `--cp-instr-glass-bg: color-mix(in srgb, var(--cp-bg1) 62%, transparent)` (line 32) are painted over the starfield canvas, which draws its brightest class with `ctx.fillStyle = "#ffffff"` (packages/runtime/src/starfield.ts:175) at baseOpacity 0.90 +/- 0.08 (starfield.ts:90). tokenContrast.test.ts's glass block composites only over --cp-tint-violet and its own comment scopes that to "Phase 1"; no test composites over a star at all, and no test uses --cp-instr-panel-bg as a ground. I recomputed, compositing a 0.98-alpha white star over ink, then the panel over it: on the 0.88 panel (ground rgb(51,54,61)) --cp-muted = 3.88:1 and --cp-energy-potential = 4.45:1, both below 4.5; on the 62% glass (ground rgb(111,114,118)) --cp-muted = 1.55:1, --cp-accent-amber = 2.84:1, --cp-accent-ice = 3.49:1, --cp-text = 3.73:1, --cp-energy-potential = 1.78:1. The same tokens over ink read 5.76 / 10.53 / 12.97 / 13.86 / 6.60, which is the only question the suite asks.
findings.scenario: In conservation-laws (the one demo with data-shell="orbit", index.html) a brilliant star lands behind the energy panel. The amber energy value a student is asked to read sits at 2.84:1 and its --cp-muted label at 1.55:1 -- the exact 'the suite only ever asked the easy question' failure the 2026-09-09 note in tokens.css was written about, one layer up.
findings.fix: Keep the starfield out from under text: in packages/theme/styles/layer-instrument.css give `.cp-panel` and `[data-shell="orbit"] .cp-panel` a two-stop background that is opaque behind the body (`linear-gradient` over `var(--cp-bg1)`), or paint a 0.9-alpha scrim layer under the glass. Then add a ground to tokenContrast.test.ts that composites each panel token over `#ffffff` (the star core) and assert the same 4.5:1 / 3:1 thresholds, so the real worst case is in the suite.

findings.title: The reduced-motion override resets duration but never delay, so entry stagger still blanks and pops the shell for up to 200 ms
findings.evidence: The global block sets only `animation-duration: 0.01ms !important; animation-iteration-count: 1 !important; transition-duration: 0.01ms !important` -- no `animation-delay`, no `transition-delay`, no `animation: none`. Demo stylesheets contain 28 `animation-delay` declarations across 8 files, every one paired with `animation: cp-slide-up ... both` or `cp-fade-in ... both`; `both` means the element holds the keyframe's `from` state (`opacity: 0; transform: translateY(10px)`) for the whole delay. moon-phases/style.css:361-382 stages four sections at `calc(var(--cp-stagger) * 1..4)` = 50/100/150/200 ms. I traced every local `@media (prefers-reduced-motion)` block: moon-phases/style.css:403 covers only `.timeline-phase, .cp-button, .cp-readout`; keplers-laws/style.css:333 covers only `#orbitPath, #planet, #equalAreasWedge, [data-focus-group], #periodScalingHint` while its own stagger is on the shell sections at lines 308-320. No demo's block names a staggered element, and angular-size, conservation-laws and planetary-conjunctions stagger with no local block at all.
findings.scenario: A student with vestibular sensitivity sets prefers-reduced-motion. Opening moon-phases they see an empty frame, then the sidebar, stage, readouts and shelf flash in one after another over 200 ms -- a sequential pop, which is the stimulus the setting exists to suppress, while tokens.test.ts's 'includes reduced-motion override' assertion stays green because it only greps for the string 'prefers-reduced-motion'.
findings.fix: In packages/theme/styles/animations.css add `animation-delay: 0s !important; transition-delay: 0s !important; animation-name: none !important` to the existing `*, *::before, *::after` block (keeping duration at 0.01ms so animationend still fires for JS listeners), then delete the 11 per-demo reduced-motion blocks that were trying to patch around it. Replace the tokens.test.ts string check with an assertion that the block contains all five longhands.

findings.title: vars.ts is a hand-kept mirror of 58 of 187 tokens with no test tying it to tokens.css, and BREAKPOINTS re-hardcodes the breakpoint values
findings.evidence: Parsed both files: tokens.css defines 187 `--cp-*` tokens; CSS_VARS names 58 (31%). Every one of the 58 exists in the CSS, but 129 do not appear in the mirror -- the whole spacing scale, the whole type scale, every motion token, every readout size/weight, every status and topic token. No generator header, no codegen script in scripts/, and `rg` over packages/theme/src/*.test.ts finds no test that reads vars.ts. BREAKPOINTS (vars.ts:112-117) hardcodes "640px"/"768px"/"1024px"/"1280px", duplicating --cp-bp-sm..xl (tokens.css:216-219); they agree today, so the duplication is latent, not yet broken. Only two files import anything from it (moon-phases/main.ts, retrograde-motion/main.ts) and neither does so through the package name -- `rg 'from "@cosmic/theme"'` returns zero hits repo-wide.
findings.scenario: Someone renames --cp-accent2 out of tokens.css as CLAUDE.md invariant 7 (token purity) requires. vars.ts keeps exporting `accent2: "--cp-accent2"`, typecheck passes, the two demos reading it through cssVar() get an empty string, and whatever property it fed falls back to its initial value -- black, for an SVG fill, which is the failure theme:undefined-token was added to catch and which this path routes around.
findings.fix: Generate packages/theme/src/vars.ts from packages/theme/styles/tokens.css in a build step (a ~30-line script that emits the key/name pairs plus the four value groups), have BREAKPOINTS read `var(--cp-bp-*)` instead of literals, and add a vitest that regenerates and diffs so a drifted mirror fails. If generation is not wanted, the honest alternative is to delete vars.ts and have the two demos read `--cp-*` names directly, since nothing imports the package.

findings.title: The panel-translucency contract test passes after both declarations are deleted from the block it names, and 15 of 20 demos have no such test at all
findings.evidence: `expect(css).toMatch(/\.viz-panel[\s\S]*?background:\s*var\(--cp-instr-panel-bg\)/)` and line 110 `toMatch(/\.viz-panel[\s\S]*?backdrop-filter/)`. The lazy `[\s\S]*?` spans the whole 409-line file, so the assertion only requires the two substrings to appear in that order anywhere. I verified the false pass by mutating the file in memory: after stripping `background: var(--cp-instr-panel-bg)`, `backdrop-filter` and `-webkit-backdrop-filter` out of the `.viz-panel` block and appending `.totally-unrelated { background: var(--cp-instr-panel-bg); backdrop-filter: blur(8px); }`, both regexes still return true. This is the golden reference CLAUDE.md tells every migration to copy. Coverage of the same invariant elsewhere: 15 of 20 design-contracts.test.ts files never mention backdrop-filter (binary-orbits, blackbody-radiation, conservation-laws, doppler-shift, eclipse-geometry, em-spectrum, eos-lab, galaxy-rotation, hydrostatic-equilibrium-explorer, keplers-laws, parallax-distance, planetary-conjunctions, seasons, stars-zams-hr, telescope-resolution); 2 never mention cp-starfield; 2 never mention cp-readout__unit. The file also contains 12 assertions on specific element ids, which is markup inventory rather than an invariant.
findings.scenario: A migration copies moon-phases/design-contracts.test.ts as instructed, writes an opaque demo panel, and the 'Panel translucency' test is green. There is no central check, so invariant 4 has no enforcement at all for three quarters of the catalogue -- and 12 opaque `background: var(--cp-bg0..3)` declarations already sit in 5 demo stylesheets today.
findings.fix: Replace the per-demo regex with one shared test in apps/demos/src/shared that, for every demo directory, parses style.css into selector/body pairs and asserts that any rule whose selector matches /panel|card|dock|shelf/ uses var(--cp-instr-panel-bg) or var(--cp-instr-glass-bg) plus backdrop-filter, with an explicit per-demo opt-out list. Keep the per-demo files for genuinely demo-specific markup only.

findings.title: contrast.test.ts asserts arithmetic on stale constants: its --cp-muted is the retired 46% value and its paper block checks three colours the theme no longer uses
findings.evidence: `const MUTED = "#7d7e81"; // --cp-muted  (46%)`. tokens.css:29 now reads `--cp-muted: color-mix(in srgb, #ffffff 54%, var(--cp-bg0))`; I resolved it: 255*0.54 + 15*0.46 = 144.6 -> #919293. #7d7e81 is exactly the 46% mix the comment block at tokens.css:14-27 documents as retired. Lines 65-79 assert `contrastRatio("#047857", "#fafaff") >= 4.5` and two siblings -- fg and bg are both local consts, so the assertion is a constant-folding exercise that cannot fail for any theme change. tokenContrast.test.ts:5-8 already states this in prose and the file was left in place, so both run and the stale one contributes 14 green assertions.
findings.scenario: --cp-muted is lowered again for aesthetics. contrast.test.ts keeps measuring #7d7e81 and reports AA pass on four grounds; tokenContrast.test.ts catches it only on the three grounds it happens to list. A reader counting green tests sees contrast covered twice.
findings.fix: Delete packages/theme/src/contrast.test.ts. Every assertion it makes that is worth keeping (accent-green and accent-rose on --cp-bg0, the --cp-faint floor) should be moved into tokenContrast.test.ts, which resolves from the CSS, and the --cp-faint case should be re-decided against 4.5:1 rather than its current 2.5:1 licence.

findings.title: Every instrument surface token restates another token's hex as decimal rgb(), and the panel border uses the museum violet inside the layer that replaces it
findings.evidence: Verified each conversion by hand: `--cp-instr-panel-bg: rgba(23, 27, 34, 0.88)` -- rgb(23,27,34) is exactly #171b22 = --cp-bg1; `--cp-instr-panel-bg-muted: rgba(23, 27, 34, 0.75)` likewise; `.cp-layer-instrument .cp-readout { background: rgba(33, 34, 43, 0.7) }` (line 81-85) -- rgb(33,34,43) = #21222b = --cp-bg2; `--cp-glow-teal/-pink/-violet` and `--cp-tint-teal/-pink/-violet` (lines 36-44) restate rgb(45,212,191)=#2dd4bf, rgb(244,114,182)=#f472b6, rgb(167,139,250)=#a78bfa, the three accents this same block defines eight lines above. Worst case: `--cp-instr-panel-border: rgba(109, 119, 148, 0.25)` is rgb(109,119,148) = #6d7794 = the MUSEUM --cp-violet, while line 20 of the same selector sets `--cp-violet: #a78bfa`. The theme's own literal check (components.test.ts:16) never reads layer files, and validate-invariants.mjs deliberately exempts packages/theme.
findings.scenario: --cp-bg1 is darkened for contrast. Every CSS surface that says var(--cp-bg1) follows; the instrument panel background, muted panel background and readout background keep the old slate, so panels now sit lighter than the page they float on, and the border is a violet that exists nowhere else in the instrument layer.
findings.fix: Rewrite these in packages/theme/styles/layer-instrument.css as color-mix over the token they are copies of: `--cp-instr-panel-bg: color-mix(in srgb, var(--cp-bg1) 88%, transparent)`, `-bg-muted` at 75%, the readout background as `color-mix(in srgb, var(--cp-bg2) 70%, transparent)`, `--cp-instr-panel-border: color-mix(in srgb, var(--cp-violet) 25%, transparent)` (which also fixes the wrong hue), and the glows/tints as color-mix over var(--cp-accent) / var(--cp-pink) / var(--cp-violet). Then extend components.test.ts's assertNoColorLiterals to the layer files.

findings.title: Demos load no @font-face, so every /play/ page renders in system-ui while --cp-font-display promises Outfit
findings.evidence: `rg 'font-face|rel="preload"|\.woff2|googleapis' apps/demos/` returns nothing; moon-phases/index.html's head loads only ./style.css and ../../assets/katex/katex.min.css. The real @font-face rules are inline in apps/site/src/layouts/Layout.astro:48-74 (Outfit, SourceSans3, SourceSans3-Italic, Inter) and that layout wraps site pages only. packages/theme/styles/fonts.css, which declares the faces, is imported by nothing -- `rg 'fonts.css' --glob '!packages/theme/styles/**'` returns zero hits -- and it declares Inter, Lexend and Source Sans 3 but not Outfit, which is what --cp-font-display names (tokens.css:155). It also writes `src: url("/fonts/Inter.woff2")`, a root-absolute URL that would break under the GitHub Pages base path, in a directory validate-invariants.mjs does not scan.
findings.scenario: A student opens /play/moon-phases/. Headings fall through "Outfit" to ui-sans-serif and body text through "Source Sans 3" and "Inter" to system-ui, so the instrument renders in San Francisco or Segoe UI with different metrics and x-height than the exhibit page they came from; readout values fall through "SF Mono"/"Fira Code" to a generic monospace off macOS, breaking the tabular-nums alignment the readouts rely on. tokens.test.ts's 'defines display font for headings (Outfit)' is green because it only greps tokens.css for the string.
findings.fix: Fix packages/theme/styles/fonts.css to declare the four faces the tokens actually name (Outfit, Source Sans 3 roman + italic, Inter) with relative `url("../fonts/...")` or a Vite-resolved import, import it from apps/demos/src/shared/stub-demo.css ahead of tokens.css, copy the woff2 files into the demo build in scripts/build.mjs, and have Layout.astro import the same file instead of restating the faces inline.

findings.title: packages/theme/README.md advertises prefers-contrast support that cannot work, because high-contrast.css is imported nowhere
findings.evidence: `rg 'high-contrast.css' --glob '!packages/theme/styles/**' --glob '!docs/**'` returns no import. apps/demos/src/shared/stub-demo.css imports 16 theme files and this is not one; apps/site/src/styles/global.css imports 8 and this is not one. README.md:70 states 'High contrast mode: `data-contrast="high"` or `prefers-contrast: more`' and :69 states 'All colors meet WCAG AA contrast (4.5:1)'. Both are false: the file never loads, and I measured --cp-faint as --cp-input-placeholder at 2.62:1 and --cp-border at 1.22:1. Separately, if it were loaded, line 24 `[data-contrast="high"] { --cp-focus: color-mix(in srgb, var(--cp-accent) 90%, transparent) }` would make the focus ring *less* visible than the base theme -- tokens.css:143-146 deliberately made --cp-focus fully opaque because a 55% mix composited to 2.25:1; a 90% mix composites to 4.06:1 versus the opaque accent's 4.73:1 on --cp-bg0, so high-contrast mode lowers the one indicator it should raise. No test loads this file either: tokenContrast.test.ts reads only tokens.css, layer-instrument.css and layer-paper.css.
findings.scenario: A student with low vision turns on Windows high-contrast or macOS Increase Contrast. Nothing changes anywhere on the site, because the stylesheet implementing it is not in either import chain -- while the package README tells an instructor evaluating the site for accessibility that it is supported.
findings.fix: Decide one way and make the docs match. Either import packages/theme/styles/high-contrast.css from both apps/site/src/styles/global.css and apps/demos/src/shared/stub-demo.css, change line 24's --cp-focus override to a brighter opaque value, and add a `hc` layer to tokenContrast.test.ts; or delete the file and remove lines 69-70 of packages/theme/README.md.

findings.title: 28 cp-namespaced classes are defined only inside individual demo stylesheets, and two of them already mean different things in different demos
findings.evidence: Diffed every `.cp-*` selector defined in a demo style.css against every one defined in packages/theme/styles (plus apps/demos/src/shared/stub-demo.css): 28 are absent from the theme. Two are defined independently in two demos and have diverged: `.cp-button-row` is `display: grid; grid-template-columns: repeat(auto-fit, minmax(120px, 1fr)); gap: var(--cp-space-2); margin-bottom: var(--cp-space-3)` at keplers-laws/style.css:68 and `display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; gap: var(--cp-space-1)` at conservation-laws/style.css:384; `.cp-context-message` differs in colour, font-size and grid-area between eclipse-geometry/style.css:18 and seasons/style.css:587. The rest are a de-facto component set with no home: binary-orbits alone owns `.cp-live-insight` + three children, `.cp-scaling-cue`, `.cp-predict-panel`, `.cp-readout--focus`, `.cp-prediction-outcome`; a checkbox component is split as `.cp-check--prominent` (keplers-laws) and `.cp-check--inline` (parallax-distance); five `.cp-readout--*` / `.cp-readout__*` modifiers are scattered across eclipse-geometry, eos-lab, moon-phases and parallax-distance.
findings.scenario: A new demo author greps the theme for `.cp-button-row`, finds nothing, and invents a third layout. Or any future attempt to hoist these into packages/theme silently changes conservation-laws from a flex row to a 120px grid, because the two definitions share a name and nothing flags the collision.
findings.fix: Enforce the namespace: add a rule to scripts/validate-invariants.mjs that fails when a selector matching /^\.cp-[a-z0-9-]+/ is defined in apps/demos/src/demos/*/style.css and not in packages/theme/styles. Then promote the genuinely shared ones (cp-button-row, cp-context-message, cp-check, cp-readout modifiers, cp-live-insight) into packages/theme/styles/components/, resolving the two divergences explicitly, and rename the demo-private ones to the demo's own prefix.

findings.title: validate-math-formatting.mjs enforces a narrower rule than CLAUDE.md states: five reader-visible Unicode-math violations are live, and \uXXXX escapes are invisible by construction
findings.evidence: FORBIDDEN_UNICODE_MATH covers degree, sun, mu, primes, times, minus, propto, approx, infinity, Greek, sub/superscript digits -- and omits plus-minus, <=, >=, !=, radical, sigma-sum, integral, partial, arrows, middle dot, divide. EXTENSIONS (line 29) omits .css, so `content:` strings are never scanned. Live violations found by rg over the scanned roots with the missing glyph set: apps/site/src/components/FilterBar.astro:62 ships `<option value="lt10" data-label="<=10 min">` with a real U+2264 in both the label and the option text, visible on /explore/; apps/demos/src/demos/seasons/index.html:455 'uncertainty of about +/-2 days' with a real U+00B1; apps/demos/src/demos/galaxy-rotation/index.html:241 `<summary>Dark matter != dark energy</summary>` with U+2260; apps/demos/src/demos/spectral-lines/index.html:496 `$hc = 1239.8\ \text{eV·nm}$`, a middle dot inside \text{} so KaTeX renders the raw glyph; apps/demos/src/demos/spectral-lines/logic.ts:460 `return `n = ${nUpper} → n = ${nLower}`` -- a validator-invisible escape, which .agents/references/invariants.md explicitly forbids ('no \uXXXX escapes that produce them (the validator cannot see escapes)'). The same escape pattern at eos-lab/main.ts:1123 is what produced the P0 above.
findings.scenario: The gate is green while five reader-visible surfaces carry Unicode math. The spectral-lines transition label 'n = 3 -> n = 2' is plain DOM text, not a KaTeX node, so the `.katex { text-transform: none }` guard at layer-instrument.css:118 does not protect it: any ancestor uppercase rule turns the principal quantum number n into N, which is the exact silent-wrong-symbol failure that rule was written for.
findings.fix: Extend FORBIDDEN_UNICODE_MATH in scripts/validate-math-formatting.mjs with the missing operator set, add ".css" to EXTENSIONS, and add a second pattern for `\\u[0-9a-fA-F]{4}` escapes in the scanned roots that resolves the code point and flags it if it is in the forbidden set. Then fix the five sites: FilterBar's option needs prose ('10 min or less') since <option> cannot hold KaTeX, and spectral-lines/logic.ts:460 should return `$n = ${nUpper} \\to n = ${nLower}$`.

findings.title: Five demos never announce a parameter change; the only live-region calls are the copy path
findings.evidence: Every setLiveRegionText call in angular-size/main.ts is at lines 1006, 1016, 1019 and they are 'Copying...', 'Copied results to clipboard.' and the copy-failure message. blackbody-radiation/main.ts: 640, 644, 647 (copy) + 652 (reduced-motion notice). em-spectrum/main.ts: 315, 317 (copy only). telescope-resolution/main.ts: 399 (one seeing note), 540, 544, 546 (copy). seasons/main.ts: 1250, 1254, 1257 (copy) + 1415 ('Year scrub tip shown.'). None of these demos writes the computed readouts to #status on an input or preset change, and none sets aria-valuetext (see finding 1). So the #status region that accessibility.spec.ts verifies exists is, in these demos, wired to nothing pedagogical.
findings.scenario: On /play/telescope-resolution/ a student moves the aperture slider. The diffraction limit, the resolved/unresolved verdict and the PSF all change. A screen reader announces only the raw slider index. Nothing reaches #status, so the student has no way to learn the result of the interaction the demo exists to teach.
findings.fix: In each of the five demos, call setLiveRegionText(status, <one-sentence summary of the primary readouts>) from the input/change and preset-click handlers only (never from render()). angular-size: after state.distanceKm/diameterKm update in the handlers at main.ts:957+. Add a cross-demo assertion to accessibility.spec.ts: move a range input and require #status textContent to change.

findings.title: seasons writes an aria-live region from render(), which runs on every animation frame
findings.evidence:
index.html:418 is

. main.ts:807 does contextMessage.textContent = msg, inside render() (declared at main.ts:736). render() is called from tick() at main.ts:532, and tick re-arms itself with window.requestAnimationFrame(tick) at main.ts:533 for the whole year animation. So the live region is reassigned up to 60 times a second for the animation's duration. The assignment is a raw textContent write that bypasses setLiveRegionText entirely, so the helper's same-text guard does not apply either - the text node is replaced every frame.
findings.scenario: A student presses 'Animate year' with a screen reader running. The polite queue is fed a new contextMessage every frame; the queue never drains, so the reader is stuck speaking stale pedagogical hints and the student can no longer hear the readouts, the controls they tab to, or anything else on the page until the animation ends.
findings.fix: Move the contextMessage write out of render(). Compute msg in render but commit it through setLiveRegionText only when it actually differs from the last committed string and no more than once every ~500 ms (the throttle keplers-laws/main.ts:160-166 already implements). Better: lift that throttle into packages/runtime/src/liveRegion.ts as announceThrottled(el, text, minIntervalMs) and use it in both demos.

findings.title: keplers-laws has aria-hidden="true" on a focusable, unnamed sr-only text input
findings.evidence: <input id="meanAnomalyDeg" class="sr-only" type="text" aria-hidden="true" value="0" />. .sr-only (packages/theme/styles/demo-shell.css:27-37 and keplers-laws/style.css:295-305) is position:absolute; width:1px; height:1px; clip:rect(0,0,0,0) - visually hidden but NOT removed from the tab order (no display:none, no tabindex=-1, no disabled). The element is write-only output: main.ts:629 sets .value and nothing reads it; its only consumers are smoke.spec.ts:434 and keplers-laws.spec.ts:601. So a test hook was implemented as a focusable form control and then masked from AT.
findings.scenario: A keyboard-only or screen-reader student tabbing through the Kepler controls lands, after the timeline scrubber, on an invisible stop. Sighted keyboard users see the focus ring vanish with no visible target; screen-reader users get silence because aria-hidden suppresses the node while focus is on it (axe rule aria-hidden-focus). Typing there changes nothing, so the stop is pure dead weight in the tab order.
findings.fix: Replace the input with a non-focusable element: plus a data-* attribute, and change main.ts:629 to set textContent/dataset. Update the two Playwright reads (smoke.spec.ts:434, keplers-laws.spec.ts:601) to read the attribute. If it must stay an input, add tabindex="-1" and drop aria-hidden.

findings.title: The focused skip link is painted underneath the sticky site header
findings.evidence: .skip-link is position:absolute; left:12px; top:-999px with no z-index (global.css:29-37) and .skip-link:focus only sets top: var(--cp-space-3) = 12px (global.css:39-41). .site-header, which follows it in the DOM (Layout.astro:80 then :81), is position:sticky; z-index:var(--cp-z-sticky)=200 with background color-mix(in srgb, var(--cp-bg0) 72%, transparent) and backdrop-filter: blur(12px) (global.css:43-51, tokens.css:211). A positioned element with z-index:200 paints after one with z-index:auto, so the header covers the skip link. Header height: .site-header__inner padding 16px top/bottom (--cp-space-4) around .brand, a two-row column (brand__home ~24px + 2px gap + brand__cadence ~24px, global.css:68-118) => ~82px. The focused link occupies y = 12 to ~54px, entirely inside that box, behind a blur plus a 72%-opaque layer. grep confirms no z-index is set on .skip-link anywhere in apps/site/src or packages/theme/styles.
findings.scenario: A keyboard user presses Tab on any museum page. The first stop is the skip link; it moves to top:12px but renders as a blurred smudge behind the translucent header, so the user cannot tell they have a skip target and has to tab through the whole header on every page.
findings.fix: Add z-index: calc(var(--cp-z-sticky) + 1) to .skip-link in apps/site/src/styles/global.css:29 and give it an opaque background (background: var(--cp-bg0)) so it is legible wherever it lands. Add a site-header.spec.ts case: focus the skip link and assert its bounding box is the topmost element at its own centre via document.elementFromPoint.

findings.title: seasons' Earth drag handle is role="button" with a continuous value and no announced value
findings.evidence: <circle id="earthOrbitDot" ... role="button" aria-label="Earth marker. Drag along orbit to set day of year." tabindex="0" /> (index.html:184-193). Arrow keys do work - the document keydown handler at main.ts:1322-1360 moves dayOfYear by 1 (left/right) or 30 (up/down) - so 2.1.1 is met. But grep for earthOrbitDot in seasons/main.ts shows only cx/cy writes (709-710), class toggles and pointer wiring (1231-1240): aria-valuenow, aria-valuemin, aria-valuemax and aria-valuetext are never set on it, and seasons' #status only ever receives copy-to-clipboard text (finding 2). Contrast keplers-laws/index.html:138-147, which uses role="slider" with the full aria-value* set plus aria-valuetext at main.ts:805 - the correct pattern exists in the repo but is not shared, because packages/runtime has no draggable-value-handle primitive.
findings.scenario: A screen-reader student focuses the Earth marker and hears 'Earth marker. Drag along orbit to set day of year., button' - an instruction they cannot follow. They press Right Arrow anyway: the day of year, solar declination, daylight hours and both hemispheres' seasons all change, and nothing is announced. The control reports itself as a button that does nothing.
findings.fix: Change role to "slider" on seasons/index.html:190, add aria-valuemin="1" aria-valuemax="365", reword the label to 'Day of year' (drop the mouse-only instruction), and in seasons/main.ts render() set aria-valuenow and aria-valuetext (e.g. 'day 80, 21 March, declination 0.0 deg') next to the cx/cy writes at 709-710. Then extract the pattern into a runtime helper so moon-phases, eclipse-geometry and keplers-laws share one implementation.

findings.title: Controls with no accessible name, including two sliders in the only launch-ready demo
findings.evidence: I parsed all 20 index.html files with html.parser, tracking both for= and ancestor <label> (implicit) association. Unnamed controls: parallax-distance #distancePcRange (line 96) and #orbitPhaseScrub (line 112), both inside <div class="cp-field"> whose visible text is a <span class="cp-label"> - a span, so no association; and retrograde-motion #preset (74), #speed-select (103), #observer (140), #target (151), #plotStepDay (181), all the same div+span pattern. The repo has three competing patterns: <label class="cp-field"> wrapping the control (parallax-distance:78-81, correct), <label class="cp-label" for="speedSelect"> (keplers-laws/index.html:308, correct), and <div class="cp-field"> + <span class="cp-label"> (broken). apps/site/src/content/demos/parallax-distance.md declares readiness: launch-ready and status: stable.
findings.scenario: A screen-reader student on /play/parallax-distance/ reaches the distance scrubber and hears only 'slider, 10' with no indication of what it controls or its units; on /play/retrograde-motion/ all five dropdowns announce as 'combo box, Earth -> Mars' with no field name, so observer and target are indistinguishable. Voice-control users cannot say 'click Preset' because no control has that name.
findings.fix: Convert each div.cp-field that contains a single control into <label class="cp-field">, or give the span an id and add aria-labelledby to the control. Then gate it: extend apps/site/tests/accessibility.spec.ts to walk every input/select/textarea under #cp-demo and assert a non-empty accessible name - that single check would have caught all seven. Until it is fixed, parallax-distance should not carry launch-ready / stable.

findings.title: Reflow at 320px is unverified on 19 of 20 /play/ routes, and one known failure is left unfixed
findings.evidence: const PLAY_ROUTES = ["play/conservation-laws/"]; - one route. The comment immediately above (lines 50-55) states: 'binary-orbits is candidate but currently DOES scroll sideways at 320px (its drawer accordions take their minimum from unbreakable KaTeX display equations), so it stays out until that is fixed.' binary-orbits is readiness: candidate / status: beta in apps/site/src/content/demos/binary-orbits.md, i.e. publicly offered to students. The remaining 18 /play/ routes have never been measured at 320px by any gate.
findings.scenario: A student opens /play/binary-orbits/ on a phone, or at 400% browser zoom as WCAG 1.4.10 contemplates. The page scrolls in two dimensions, so reading the mass-ratio readout means scrolling right and then back left for every slider move. This is a documented AA failure on a demo the site presents as near-ready, and no gate will ever report it because the route is excluded from the only spec that looks at 320px.
findings.fix: Fix the binary-orbits accordion minimum first: wrap its .katex-display in the keyboard-reachable scroll region the site already uses (KatexAutoRender.astro:26-32 pattern, applied via packages/runtime - see finding 9) and add min-width: 0 to the drawer's grid track. Then add all 20 slugs to PLAY_ROUTES as map(s => `play/${s}/`) so the gate fails on the next regression rather than documenting it in a comment.

findings.title: Demo equations scroll horizontally but are not keyboard-reachable; initMath omits the fix the site has
findings.evidence: initMath/renderMath (math.ts:27-54) call renderMathInElement and stop - they never add tabindex, role or a label. The site's equivalent, KatexAutoRender.astro:26-32, does exactly that for .katex-display ('A scrollable region must be reachable by keyboard: browsers do not make an overflow container focusable on their own (WCAG 2.1.1)'), and rehypeScrollableTables.mjs:38-43 does it for tables. Demos load initMath, not KatexAutoRender. Six demo containers declare overflow-x: auto: conservation-laws/style.css:170 (.instrument__equation, holding $U_{\rm eff}(r) = -\mu/r + h^2/(2r^2)$ at index.html:137) and :397, doppler-shift/style.css:306, binary-orbits/style.css:132, eos-lab/style.css:569, galaxy-rotation/style.css:156. None of those elements carries tabindex in the HTML.
findings.scenario: On /play/conservation-laws/ at 320px the effective-potential equation is wider than its box. A mouse user drags it; a keyboard-only user cannot focus the container, so the right-hand terms of the equation are unreachable - and the same holds for the readout tables in binary-orbits, eos-lab, doppler-shift and galaxy-rotation.
findings.fix: Add the tabindex/role=region/aria-label pass to packages/runtime/src/math.ts inside initMath, after renderMath, applying it to .katex-display and to any element matching a shared .cp-scroll-x class; re-run it on a debounced resize (see finding 17). That makes one implementation serve both the site and the demos instead of two.

findings.title: --cp-faint fails 1.4.3 as body text: 2.87:1 on dark, 3.69:1 on paper
findings.evidence: .mini-card__date { color: var(--cp-faint); font-family: var(--cp-font-mono); font-size: 0.7rem; }. tokens.css:32 defines --cp-faint: color-mix(in srgb, #ffffff 32%, var(--cp-bg0)) with --cp-bg0: #0f1115, i.e. rgb(92,93,96). I computed the WCAG relative-luminance ratios in node: 2.87:1 on bg0, 2.62:1 on bg1 (#171b22), 2.40:1 on bg2 (#21222b). layer-paper.css:20 sets --cp-faint: #7d8599, which gives 3.55:1 on #fafaff, 3.69:1 on #ffffff and 3.10:1 on #e8ebf5. AA needs 4.5:1 (the text is 0.7rem = 11.2px, far below the 18.66px large-text threshold). The sibling token --cp-muted was deliberately re-derived against its real grounds (tokens.css:14-30) and clears 4.5:1 everywhere; --cp-faint was never given the same treatment.
findings.scenario: A student with low vision browsing Explore or a topic hub cannot read the 'updated' date on any mini card - on dark theme it is at 2.87:1, under two-thirds of the required ratio - and the same token sets the global input placeholder (tokens.css:152), so placeholder text in the Explore search box is equally unreadable.
findings.fix: Either stop using --cp-faint for text - change MiniCard.astro:161 to var(--cp-muted) (6.06:1 on bg0) - or raise the token. Raising needs approval: color-mix(in srgb, #ffffff 45%, var(--cp-bg0)) measures 4.52:1 on bg2, the worst ground, but narrows the faint/muted gap. Then extend packages/theme/src/tokens.test.ts to assert every token used as a color: in a text rule clears 4.5:1 against bg0, bg1, bg2 and the instrument panel - the test that caught --cp-muted only checked bg0.

findings.title: Two information-bearing canvases have neither a text alternative nor aria-hidden
findings.evidence: <canvas id="orbitCanvas" width="520" height="520"></canvas> - the main two-body orbit view, with no role, no aria-label and no aria-hidden. apps/demos/src/demos/em-spectrum/index.html:94: <canvas id="spectrumWaveCanvas" class="spectrum__wave"></canvas>, same. Both demos are readiness: candidate. The repo's own convention is applied everywhere else: blackbody-radiation, cluster-census (x3), doppler-shift, eos-lab (x4), galaxy-rotation, spectral-lines (x2) and stars-zams-hr all use role="img" plus a descriptive aria-label, and cluster-census' overlay is explicitly aria-hidden="true". A further inconsistency: binary-orbits' three secondary canvases (rvCanvas:?, spectrumCanvas, energyCanvas) carry aria-label but no role="img", and canvas has no implicit role, so the name may not be exposed at all.
findings.scenario: A screen-reader student on /play/binary-orbits/ reaches the orbit view and the reader announces nothing - no name, no role, no indication that the central visualisation exists. accessibility.spec.ts checks only that canvas.cp-starfield is aria-hidden, so it reports the demo as clean.
findings.fix: Add role="img" plus an aria-label describing what is plotted to binary-orbits/index.html:209 and em-spectrum/index.html:94, and add role="img" to binary-orbits' rvCanvas/spectrumCanvas/energyCanvas which already have labels. Then add a cross-demo assertion in accessibility.spec.ts: every <canvas> that is not .cp-starfield must have either aria-hidden="true" or role="img" with a non-empty accessible name.

findings.title: No automated WCAG engine exists; the only a11y gate checks seven attributes and catches none of these findings
findings.evidence: The cross-demo suite asserts exactly: #cp-demo has an aria-label longer than 3 chars (44-48), #status has role=status and aria-live=polite (50-55), canvas.cp-starfield is aria-hidden (57-60), .cp-utility-toolbar has role=toolbar (62-65), .cp-utility-btn elements all have aria-label (67-76), and at least one .cp-readout__unit span exists (78-82). Plus play-button-disabled-under-reduced-motion for 5 named demos (90-110) and one challenge-feedback check (117-126). grep for 'axe' across package.json, apps/site/package.json, apps/demos/package.json, packages/*/package.json and apps/site/tests/ returns one hit, a prose use of the word 'axes' in explore.spec.ts:10 - axe-core and @axe-core/playwright are not dependencies anywhere. So nothing checks accessible names on inputs, aria-hidden-focus, canvas alternatives, colour contrast, heading order, duplicate landmarks or ARIA attribute validity.
findings.scenario: An instructor or an institutional accessibility review asks whether the site meets WCAG 2.2 AA. CI is green, so the answer looks like yes - while 11 of the findings in this report are live in production, including a launch-ready demo with unnamed sliders. For a public university resource this is the defect that keeps producing the others.
findings.fix: Add @axe-core/playwright and a spec that runs axe with the wcag2a, wcag2aa, wcag21aa and wcag22aa tags over every museum route, every /play/<slug>/ route and both themes, failing on violations with a short, explicit allowlist. Then add the three targeted assertions named in findings 7, 11 and 2 (accessible name on every control, text alternative on every non-starfield canvas, #status changes on an input event), which axe cannot infer.

findings.title: popover.ts pulls focus back to the trigger when the user clicks elsewhere on the page
findings.evidence: onOutsideClick (99-107) is bound to document (line 111) and calls closePopover on any click outside trigger or popover; closePopover (47-51) unconditionally calls returnFocusToTrigger(trigger) -> trigger.focus() (17-19). A click first focuses whatever was clicked (on mousedown), then the click event bubbles to document and focus is yanked to the popover trigger. popover.test.ts:78-94 ('closes on outside click') asserts only popover.hidden, never where focus ended up, so the behaviour is untested. initPopovers runs on every demo via shared/stub-demo.ts:58 and explicitly in blackbody-radiation, doppler-shift, eclipse-geometry and retrograde-motion main.ts.
findings.scenario: A student opens the nav popover on /play/parallax-distance/, then clicks the distance slider to carry on working. The slider takes focus, then the document click handler closes the popover and moves focus to the popover trigger, so the student's subsequent arrow keys do nothing to the slider. Focus has silently jumped to an unrelated control.
findings.fix: Make focus return conditional: in closePopover, only call trigger.focus() when document.activeElement is inside the popover (or when closing via Escape / the trigger itself). Pass a reason flag from the three call sites. Add a popover.test.ts case asserting that after an outside click on a focusable element, document.activeElement is that element.

findings.title: Unicode math operators reach readers, and the validator's forbidden set omits them and HTML entities
findings.evidence: <option value="lt10" data-label="≤ 10 min">≤ 10 min</option> (the glyph is U+2264). Also apps/demos/src/demos/galaxy-rotation/index.html:241 <summary>Dark matter ≠ dark energy</summary> and apps/demos/src/demos/seasons/index.html:455 'uncertainty of about ±2 days'. scripts/validate-math-formatting.mjs:33 defines FORBIDDEN_UNICODE_MATH as a character class containing degree, sun, mu, primes, multiplication, minus, proportional, approx, infinity, the Greek alphabet and sub/superscript digits - it does not contain U+2264, U+2265, U+2260, U+00B1, U+2213, U+2261, radical, integral, sum, partial or nabla. apps/site/src/components is in SCAN_ROOTS (line 23) and packages/runtime/src is too (line 26), so these files are scanned and pass. The entity form evades it as well: packages/runtime/src/demoModes.ts:362 emits aria-label="Close" with × as the visible glyph, exactly the escape class CLAUDE.md warns the validator cannot see.
findings.scenario: A student using NVDA at default punctuation level opens galaxy-rotation's 'Dark matter ≠ dark energy' drawer; U+2260 is not in NVDA's English symbol dictionary, so the heading can be spoken as 'Dark matter dark energy' - the negation that is the entire point of the drawer is dropped, and the student hears the opposite of the intended claim. The same risk applies to '±2 days' in seasons and '≤ 10 min' in the Explore time filter.
findings.fix: Fix the three sources: $\leq 10$ min, $\neq$, $\pm 2$ days (rendered via renderInlineMath in FilterBar, renderMath in the demos), and replace × in demoModes.ts:362 with an inline SVG or a CSS-drawn glyph. Then close the gate: extend FORBIDDEN_UNICODE_MATH in scripts/validate-math-formatting.mjs:33 with the operators listed above and add a second pass that decodes HTML entities and numeric/\\u escapes before matching.

findings.title: validate-plot-contract is a gate that cannot fail: it guards a Plotly/mountPlot architecture that does not exist in the repo
findings.evidence: The validator's only three checks are RX_IMPORT_PLOTLY / RX_REQUIRE_PLOTLY / RX_DIRECT_PLOTLY_CALL and, gated on `/\bmountPlot\s*\(/`, PlotSpec axes-label and id metadata. I searched the whole repo: `ls packages/runtime/src/plots` -> "No such file or directory"; the strings `plotly` and `mountPlot` occur in exactly one file, apps/demos/src/demos/eos-lab/design-contracts.test.ts:152-153, as `expect(mainTs).not.toContain("plotly")`. The actual plotting stack is uPlot (apps/demos/src/demos/eos-lab/uplotHelpers.ts) and three.js (cluster-census/clusterScene.ts). 121 LOC of validator plus 74 LOC of its own test run inside both `pnpm lint` and scripts/build.mjs on every build and can never produce a violation.
findings.scenario: A developer reads package.json's lint chain and scripts/build.mjs and concludes that plot axis labels are contract-checked. They add a uPlot chart in a new demo with no axis label, or with a Unicode 'λ' in a tick label (which the canvas exemption forbids — ASCII only). Lint passes, build passes, the chart ships with an unlabelled or wrongly-cased axis. The gate's existence is worse than its absence because it makes the hole look covered.
findings.fix: Delete scripts/validate-plot-contract.mjs and scripts/validate-plot-contract.test.mjs and remove them from the `lint` script in package.json and from scripts/build.mjs. Replace with a uPlot/canvas contract that asserts what this project actually needs: every uPlot axis config carries a `label` containing a unit, and every string reaching ctx.fillText or a uPlot label is ASCII-only.

findings.title: The KaTeX-only invariant is defeated by \uXXXX escapes, and two tests assert the Unicode output
findings.evidence: DemoCard.astro:73: `const timeLabel = timeMinutes <= 10 ? "≤10 min" : timeMinutes <= 20 ? "10–20 min" : "20+ min";` rendered at :128 as `<TagPill label={timeLabel} .../>`. angular-size/logic.ts:77: `return `${mantissa} × 10${toSuperscript(expNum)}`;` whose result reaches the DOM at angular-size/main.ts:757 `thetaDisplay.textContent = display.text;` — a reader-visible readout, not a canvas. invariants.md says plainly "no \uXXXX escapes that produce them (the validator cannot see escapes)", and validate-math-formatting.mjs matches raw glyphs only. Separately, the FORBIDDEN_UNICODE_MATH class at validate-math-formatting.mjs:45 omits plus-minus, less-or-equal, greater-or-equal, not-equal, radical, Angstrom, U+2299 and the partial/nabla/sum/integral family, and three raw violations are live in scanned roots right now: FilterBar.astro:62 (less-or-equal, twice), seasons/index.html:455 (plus-minus), galaxy-rotation/index.html:241 (not-equal, inside a <summary> whose point is "dark matter is not dark energy"). Two tests PIN the violation: smoke.spec.ts:151 `expect(text).toMatch(/(≤|–|\+)/)` and angular-size/logic.test.ts:161 `expect(formatSci(1.5e8, 3)).toBe("1.50 × 10⁸")`.
