findings.scenario: A developer fixes DemoCard.astro:73 to render LaTeX via renderInlineMath() as the contract requires. smoke.spec.ts:151 immediately fails, because it asserts the Unicode glyph is present in the badge. The suite therefore rewards the violation and punishes the fix — the exact pattern the project's own memory records as "five green tests that pinned the bug instead of catching it". Meanwhile the angular-size theta readout renders a raw multiplication sign and superscript digits that inherit whatever text-transform the surrounding CSS applies, which is the 2026-09-05 defect class that math-rendering.spec.ts exists to stop — and it cannot see these, because they are plain text nodes, not .katex nodes.
findings.fix: In scripts/validate-math-formatting.mjs: (a) decode \uXXXX and \xXX escapes before testing each line, so escapes are no longer an escape hatch; (b) widen FORBIDDEN_UNICODE_MATH to the full operator set (plus-minus, the comparison family, radical, Angstrom, both solar-circle codepoints, partial/nabla/sum/integral, all superscript and subscript letters); (c) add packages/data-astr101/src, packages/data-spectra/src, packages/data-telescopes/src and packages/theme/src to SCAN_ROOTS, since dataset titles and field labels are reader-visible. Then fix the four live sites and rewrite smoke.spec.ts:151 and angular-size/logic.test.ts:161,181 to assert the LaTeX/KaTeX output instead of the glyph.

findings.title: content_verified: true on 19 of 20 demos is gated only by a review file existing, and the review files are stale in both directions
findings.evidence: The gate is `if (!/^content_verified:\s*true\s*$/m.test(front)) continue; const reviewPath = path.join(repoRoot, "docs", "reviews", `${slug}.md`); if (await pathExists(reviewPath)) continue;` — existence only; the file's contents are never read. I tabulated the frontmatter: 19 of 20 demos carry content_verified: true (only planetary-conjunctions says false). Counting open rows in the per-demo reviews: galaxy-rotation 4, stars-zams-hr 4, hydrostatic-equilibrium-explorer 3, spectral-lines 3, eos-lab 2. Stale in the other direction too: docs/reviews/galaxy-rotation.md:22 still marks GR-1 "**open**" ("the band still reaches 22.1 km/s (13.2%) at R = 7 kpc" with the halo at zero), but I read the code and galaxyRotationModel.ts:403-412 documents the fix and galaxyRotationModel.test.ts:223-245 is a real regression test asserting vVisible toBeCloseTo vTotal to 10 places across 0.25-30 kpc with haloMass10 === 0. So the artifact backing the strongest public quality claim on the site is simply not maintained.
findings.scenario: An instructor filters Explore for verified content and assigns spectral-lines to a class. Its exhibit page says its content has been verified; its own review file says its line strengths are ad hoc while captioned as NIST data (SL-5, open) and that two divergent strength sets drive the drawn line widths. The build is green throughout, because the gate only asked whether a file with that name exists.
findings.fix: In scripts/validate-play-dirs.mjs, parse the review's findings table and fail when a demo claiming content_verified: true has any row whose severity is P0 or P1 and whose status is not fixed/closed; also require a `reviewed_commit:` or `reviewed_at:` field in the demo frontmatter that names the commit the review covered, and fail when the demo's own sources have changed since it. Then sweep the five review files so their status columns match the code.

findings.title: Physical constants are duplicated across four modules and AstroConstants.EOS has zero consumers
findings.evidence: astroConstants.ts:88-95 declares an EOS block whose comment says "same values used in stellarEosModel.ts" — and stellarEosModel.ts:6-13 does indeed hold its own private `CGS_CONSTANTS` with the identical six values. I searched for consumers of the canonical block: `rg 'AstroConstants\.EOS'` across apps and packages returns nothing. hydrostaticEquilibriumModel.ts:32-38 keeps a fourth copy, `HYDROSTATIC_CONSTANTS`, including gravitationalConstantCgs 6.67430e-8, protonMassG 1.67262192369e-24, solarMassG 1.98847e33 and solarRadiusCm 6.957e10 — four quantities AstroConstants does not define at all. moonPhasesModel.ts:1 is a fifth case: `const SYNODIC_MONTH_DAYS = 29.53;` against the canonical AstroConstants.TIME.MEAN_SYNODIC_MONTH_DAYS = 29.530588 (a 50.8 s difference), and moonPhasesModel.test.ts:26 asserts `toBeCloseTo(29.53 / 2, 3)`, pinning the private literal. No gate or test asserts that any pair of these copies agrees; astroConstants.test.ts has three tests total, two of which compute their expected value from the same constants under test.
findings.scenario: Someone corrects the radiation constant a from 7.5657e-15 to the exact 7.565733e-15 in astroConstants.ts, where "single source of truth" is written at the top of the file. stellarEosModel keeps computing radiation pressure from its private 7.5657e-15, so eos-lab and any future consumer of AstroConstants.EOS now disagree about P_rad at the same (rho, T), and every test stays green because each module tests only itself. This is the composition failure the project already recorded for cluster-census: two individually correct models, silently inconsistent.
findings.fix: Delete the AstroConstants.EOS block or make it the only definition: have stellarEosModel.ts and hydrostaticEquilibriumModel.ts import from AstroConstants, and move G_CGS, PROTON_MASS_G, SOLAR_MASS_G and SOLAR_RADIUS_CM into it. Have moonPhasesModel.ts import MEAN_SYNODIC_MONTH_DAYS and update moonPhasesModel.test.ts:26 to assert against the canonical constant. Then extend scripts/validate-physics-models.mjs with a duplicate-constant check: flag any numeric literal in packages/physics/src/*.ts that matches a value already defined in astroConstants.ts.

findings.title: 34 e2e tests are skipped and 5 more live in a Playwright project that neither test:e2e nor any CI workflow runs
findings.evidence: The desktop project carries `grepInvert: /@visual/` and the mobile project `testMatch: /reflow\.spec\.ts/`, so the only project that can run a @visual test is `visual` (grep: /@visual/). apps/site/package.json defines `test:e2e` as `playwright test --project=desktop --project=mobile`, which both deploy.yml and nightly-e2e.yml invoke — so the 5 @visual tests in binary-orbits.spec.ts (lines 381, 416, 854, 861, 871) never execute anywhere automated. I counted 34 `test.skip("screenshot: ...")` declarations across 12 per-demo specs (keplers-laws 3, blackbody-radiation 4, telescope-resolution 3, planetary-conjunctions 2, conservation-laws 3, eclipse-geometry 3, em-spectrum 3, seasons 2, retrograde-motion 4, moon-phases 3, angular-size 4). apps/site/tests/binary-orbits.spec.ts-snapshots holds 2.6 MB of committed PNGs, and half of them (the five dated March 2026, without the `-visual-` project infix) are orphans from before the project rename — no test can ever match them. The surviving tolerances are maxDiffPixelRatio 0.05, which at 1280x720 permits 46,080 differing pixels.
findings.scenario: Someone changes the RV panel's axis autoscaling so the curve silently rescales instead of flattening when inclination drops — exactly the regression binary-orbits.spec.ts:381 was written to catch. The suite reports 771 passing tests and says nothing, because that test is tagged into a project no command runs. Worse, 2.6 MB of binary baselines in git imply visual coverage that does not exist.
findings.fix: Either restore the coverage or remove the claim. Restore: regenerate the baselines on Linux (the mcr.microsoft.com/playwright container) and add `--project=visual` to the nightly-e2e.yml run. Remove: delete the orphaned non-`-visual-` PNGs, and convert the 34 skipped screenshot tests into either real assertions or deletions — a test.skip with no linked issue is dead weight that inflates the suite count.

findings.title: The 320px reflow gate covers 1 of 20 /play/ routes, so 19 instruments have no mobile accessibility check
findings.evidence: `const PLAY_ROUTES = ["play/conservation-laws/"];` — one route, with a comment noting binary-orbits is excluded because it currently does scroll sideways at 320px (its drawer accordions take their minimum from unbreakable KaTeX display equations). The museum routes are fully covered (9 site pages plus exhibits/stations/instructor for all 20 slugs), and reflow.spec.ts is the only spec in the `mobile` project (playwright.config.ts:40 `testMatch: /reflow\.spec\.ts/`), so accessibility.spec.ts and layout-budget.spec.ts never run below 1280px either. layout-budget.spec.ts samples 1440x900 only, and its own comments record two separate cases (binary-orbits, stars-zams-hr) where media queries gated on min-height switched the stage bounds OFF at 1280x720 and pushed every readout below the fold — invisible to a single-width sample.
findings.scenario: A student opens any instrument but conservation-laws on a phone, or at 400% zoom on a laptop as WCAG 1.4.10 describes. Content sits outside the viewport and they cannot reach a control or a readout. Nothing fails: the mobile project only matches reflow.spec.ts, and reflow.spec.ts only visits one play route. For binary-orbits this is not hypothetical — the spec's own comment states it scrolls sideways today.
findings.fix: Turn PLAY_ROUTES into the full slug list with an explicit, dated allowlist of known failures (the same ratchet shape layout-budget.spec.ts already uses), so each demo must either pass or be named. Fix binary-orbits first by letting its KaTeX display blocks wrap or scroll inside their accordion. Separately, add layout-budget.spec.ts to the mobile project, or widen it to sample 1280x720 and 1366x768 as well as 1440x900.

findings.title: 1,636 LOC of challenge grading and Station Mode have no unit test, and the engine's default numeric path marks correct answers wrong
findings.evidence: packages/runtime/src has test files for bottomSheet, popover, starfield and tabs only. challengeEngine.ts (874 LOC) and demoModes.ts (762 LOC) — the two largest modules, and the ones that grade students and drive Station Mode — have none; neither do clipboard.ts, polish.ts, domStyle.ts, math.ts or liveRegion.ts. Tracing evaluateAnswer: the final fallback at :549-550 is `const ok = userAnswer === (challenge as any).answer; return { correct: ok, ... }` — strict equality on the raw input, with the challenge's tolerance discarded entirely. And normalizeChallenge at :304 is `const tolerance = (raw as any).tolerance ?? DEFAULT_TOLERANCES[type ?? ""] ?? 0;` where DEFAULT_TOLERANCES (:96-101) covers only angle 15, phase 0.1, position 20, boolean 0 — so any numeric challenge type gets tolerance 0. I confirmed all four current call sites (hydrostatic-equilibrium-explorer/main.ts:1779, galaxy-rotation/main.ts:1096, doppler-shift/main.ts:1196, spectral-lines/main.ts:540) use type: "custom" or an object payload, so the defect is latent, not live.
findings.scenario: The next demo adds the obvious thing — a numeric challenge, `{ type: "value", answer: 0.53, tolerance: 0.01 }`. type "value" is not handled, so control falls to :549: the student types 0.53 into a text input, userAnswer is the string "0.53", and "0.53" === 0.53 is false. The student is told their correct answer is "Incorrect." Even with type handled, a challenge that omits tolerance gets 0, so only an exact float match passes. Nothing catches either: there is no test file for this module, and e2e only ever exercises the custom path.
findings.fix: Add packages/runtime/src/challengeEngine.test.ts covering each branch of evaluateAnswer: string-vs-number coercion on the fallback path, tolerance defaulting, the angle wrap at the 180-degree boundary, the phase wrap at 0/1, and the close-but-wrong band. Then make the fallback explicit — parse numerically via the existing parseNumberAnswer and compare within tolerance, and throw at normalizeChallenge time on an unrecognised type rather than silently reaching a strict-equality fallback. Add demoModes.test.ts for Station Mode state transitions.

findings.title: apps/site/src has zero unit tests and the three data packages have no test script, so 644 lines of teaching-facing physical data are unverified
findings.evidence: The root `test` script runs packages/math, physics, theme, runtime and apps/demos, then five script validators. It never touches apps/site/src or packages/data-*. `find apps/site/src -name '*.test.ts'` returns nothing, so exploreFilter.ts (298 LOC, the browser-side filter that must work because the site is output: "static" and query params never reach a server), topics.ts (121), readiness.ts (73, which CLAUDE.md names as the thing that controls a public quality badge), inlineMath.ts and catalog.ts are untested. packages/data-astr101, data-spectra and data-telescopes each declare only `{"typecheck": ...}` in package.json — no test script and no test file — across 644 lines of data: 10 stellar parallaxes, 106 lines of atomic lines, 144 lines of telescope/instrument entries, wavelength bands and seeing conditions. scripts/validate-datasets.mjs validates manifest SHAPE only: every violations.push is about a missing manifest key, a missing export, a missing provenance field or a unit-name suffix. It never imports a dataset or looks at a single value.
findings.scenario: A wavelength, parallax or aperture in packages/data-spectra or data-telescopes is mistyped by a factor of ten, or an air wavelength is entered where the model expects vacuum (the exact SL-3 defect the spectral-lines review found). The number flows into a preset dropdown and a readout a student records as a measurement. Lint passes (manifest shape is intact), the unit gate never runs these packages, and no e2e assertion knows what the right number is. Separately, a regression in exploreFilter.ts silently breaks catalogue filtering with no unit test to catch it.
findings.fix: Add a test script and a values test to each packages/data-* package and add them to the root `test` chain: assert each entry against its cited source value with a stated tolerance, and assert required invariants (parallax > 0, wavelength within the band it is filed under, `medium` present on every spectral line). Add apps/site/src/lib/exploreFilter.test.ts, topics.test.ts and readiness.test.ts and run them from the root test script.

findings.title: hydrostatic-equilibrium-explorer has 2,582 LOC, a 155-line logic test and no e2e spec, while listed on Explore as verified
findings.evidence: I tabulated every demo. hydrostatic-equilibrium-explorer: main.ts 1,868 lines, logic.ts 714, logic.test.ts 155, design-contracts.test.ts 138 — and it is the only slug of 20 with no apps/site/tests/<slug>.spec.ts. Its frontmatter says content_verified: true, readiness: experimental; docs/reviews/hydrostatic-equilibrium-explorer.md carries 3 open rows. It is not hidden: smoke.spec.ts:44-48 asserts its heading renders on Explore and smoke.spec.ts:100-102 asserts its thumbnail scene is "stellar-core". Its 1,868-line main.ts is covered by nothing but the generic cross-demo sweeps (accessibility, math-rendering, layout-budget). galaxy-rotation is the next worst ratio: 1,510 + 234 LOC against a 157-line logic test, at readiness: candidate. More broadly, every demo's main.ts runs 410-2,353 lines against invariants.md's "main.ts is thin DOM wiring", and no main.ts in the repo is unit-tested at all.
findings.scenario: A regression in hydrostatic-equilibrium-explorer's shell-balance rendering, guided-steps sequencing or checkpoint grading ships to a class. The three cross-demo sweeps confirm its root has an aria-label, its KaTeX is not re-cased and its readouts are above the fold — none of them touch a single slider or check a single number. The demo is on Explore, claims verified content, and is interactively untested.
findings.fix: Write apps/site/tests/hydrostatic-equilibrium-explorer.spec.ts covering the pressure/radius scaling the demo teaches (central pressure rises as R shrinks at fixed mass), the shell force balance readouts, and the checkpoint flow, following the eclipse-geometry spec as the pattern. Add a per-demo floor to the gate: validate-play-dirs.mjs should fail when a slug has no apps/site/tests/<slug>.spec.ts, the same way it already fails on a missing content entry.

findings.title: The 8 design-system invariants are enforced by 20 divergent copies of a template; translucency is tested in 5 demos and celestial tokens in 9
findings.evidence: I measured every design-contracts.test.ts for mentions of each invariant's marker. Starfield (invariant 2): zero mentions of cp-starfield in parallax-distance and stars-zams-hr. Panel translucency (invariant 4): backdrop-filter appears in only 5 of 20 — angular-size, cluster-census, moon-phases, retrograde-motion, spectral-lines. Readout unit spans (invariant 3): zero mentions of cp-readout__unit in hydrostatic-equilibrium-explorer and stars-zams-hr. Celestial tokens (invariant 1): zero mentions of cp-celestial in 11 of 20. Test counts range from 10 (hydrostatic) to 59 (cluster-census). CLAUDE.md says to copy moon-phases/design-contracts.test.ts and adapt it; the adaptation dropped whole invariants, and no meta-test asserts that each demo covers all eight. The checks themselves are also string-presence assertions on the demo's own source — `expect(html).toContain('id="focus-moon-btn"')` is true by construction once the HTML is written, and asserting that a token NAME appears in a gradient says nothing about whether that token resolves or what the gradient looks like.
findings.scenario: A new demo (or a refactor of parallax-distance or stars-zams-hr) ships an opaque sidebar over the starfield, or drops the starfield canvas entirely. Its own design-contracts.test.ts has no assertion for either, the theme's tokens.test.ts only checks that token names exist in tokens.css, and no cross-demo test covers it — so invariants 2 and 4 are simply unenforced for those demos while the suite reports every design contract green.
findings.fix: Replace the 20 bespoke files with one shared cross-demo contract — apps/demos/src/designContracts.test.ts — that iterates the demo directories and asserts all eight invariants for every slug, keeping per-demo files only for genuinely demo-specific SVG structure. Pair it with a runtime check in the e2e suite that reads computed styles (panel background alpha, starfield canvas present and painting, celestial fills non-black), since the string checks cannot see whether a token resolves.

findings.title: The glow-opacity test's regex is written around the three tokens that violate the 30-50% rule
findings.evidence: tokens.test.ts:203: `const glowPattern = /--cp-glow-(?:sun|moon|planet|star|accent-teal|accent-rose|accent-violet):.*?rgba\([^)]*,\s*([\d.]+)\)/g;` then asserts each captured alpha is within [0.3, 0.5]. The family it names is exactly the compliant set. tokens.css:80-82 defines three more glow tokens that it skips by name: `--cp-glow-teal: 0 0 20px rgba(45, 212, 191, 0.28)`, `--cp-glow-pink: ... 0.24`, `--cp-glow-violet: ... 0.24` — all below the 30% floor CLAUDE.md states as invariant 6 ("Glow opacity Contract: celestial glow tokens use 30-50% opacity. If a glow looks invisible, it's wrong"). The test also reads only tokens.css (loaded at :6-7), while layer-instrument.css:39-41 and layer-paper.css redefine glow tokens per layer, so an instrument-layer glow at any opacity is unexamined. The guard `expect(opacities.length).toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(4)` is satisfied by the 7 named tokens regardless.
findings.scenario: Someone sets --cp-glow-moon to rgba(200,200,220,0.05) inside layer-instrument.css. The moon's glow becomes invisible in every instrument-layer demo, which is precisely the symptom invariant 6 was written to describe, and the test passes: it never opens layer-instrument.css. Conversely the three sub-threshold tokens in tokens.css are live violations that the test is shaped to miss, so the invariant is documented, apparently tested, and false.
findings.fix: Change the regex to the whole family, `--cp-glow-[a-z0-9-]+`, skip `var(...)` aliases as validate-invariants.mjs already does, scan tokens.css plus layer-instrument.css and layer-paper.css, and assert a non-zero count per file. Then either raise --cp-glow-teal/pink/violet to the 0.30 floor or amend invariant 6 in CLAUDE.md to state the real rule for non-celestial accents — one or the other, not both.

findings.title: The missing gates: no authored-constant-versus-model diff, no rendered-DOM Unicode scan, no inline-physics rule
findings.evidence: Walking the historical defects in docs/reviews/ against the five gates in scripts/gates.mjs: (1) An authored number contradicting the model that computes it — spectral-lines' 364.6 vs 364.7 nm Balmer limit (SL-4, open), and the review's note that index.html:395 and main.ts:712 disagreed. No gate reads prose numbers. (2) Unicode math reaching rendered text — the 2026-09-05 case of 94 KaTeX nodes uppercased, the 2026-09-10 multiplication sign in a filter chip, and the four live violations I found today, two of them hidden behind \uXXXX escapes in DemoCard.astro:73 and angular-size/logic.ts:77. validate-math-formatting.mjs scans SOURCE text only and cannot see escapes; math-rendering.spec.ts inspects the rendered DOM but looks only at .katex nodes and TeX leakage, never at Unicode glyphs in ordinary text. (3) Inline physics in demo code — stars-zams-hr HR-4 (main.ts:333), and the review notes a divergent second copy of the post-main-sequence model. validate-physics-models.mjs checks only that packages/physics/src/*Model.ts files have a sibling test and an index export; it never looks at demo code at all, and it ignores non-*Model.ts files such as keplerSolver.ts, twoBodyAnalytic.ts and units.ts.
findings.scenario: Each of these three classes has already shipped at least once with every gate green, and two of them are shipping right now. Nothing in the current gate set changes that: the same defect reintroduced tomorrow passes lint, typecheck, unit, build and e2e exactly as it does today.
findings.fix: Add three checks. (a) A constants-consistency test in apps/site/tests/ that extracts every number-plus-unit from each demo's index.html prose and compares it against the matching @cosmic/physics call, failing on disagreement beyond the printed precision — start with the series limits, the Balmer/Lyman wavelengths and the synodic month. (b) Extend math-rendering.spec.ts with a rendered-DOM Unicode sweep: walk every text node under main that is not inside .katex, canvas or [aria-hidden], and fail on any character in the forbidden math class — this catches escapes, concatenation and anything the source scanner cannot see. (c) Add an apps:inline-physics rule to validate-invariants.mjs that flags arithmetic on named physics quantities with numeric literal coefficients inside apps/demos/src/demos/**/*.ts, with an explicit per-site exemption comment, and widen validate-physics-models.mjs from *Model.ts to every non-test file in packages/physics/src.

findings.title: Instructor answer keys are indexable: the noindex meta is emitted inside <body>, and there is no robots.txt
findings.evidence: `<head><meta name="robots" content="noindex" /></head>` sits inside the `<Layout>` slot (line 56-60), and Layout.astro accepts only `title` and `hasMath` — nothing hoists it. I checked the built artifact: in dist/instructor/moon-phases/index.html the string `robots` appears at byte offset 7630, inside `<main id="content">`, while `</head>` closes at offset 2368. A robots directive outside `<head>` is ignored by crawlers. No robots.txt exists anywhere in the repo (`find . -name robots.txt` returns nothing). The pages being exposed contain answer keys: instructor/moon-phases/assessment.md prints "**Correct:** C.", "**Correct:** B.", and "**Answer key:** $\\cos 60^\\circ = 0.5$, so $f = 0.75$ (75%)". CLAUDE.md states instructor pages are "optionally `noindex`", so the intent is explicit.
findings.scenario: A student searches the exact text of a clicker prompt from lecture and Google returns /instructor/<slug>/ with every correct answer and the exit-ticket key. All 20 instructor pages and all 19 assessment banks are affected.
findings.fix: Add a `noindex?: boolean` prop to Layout.astro and render the meta inside Layout's real `<head>`; pass `noindex` from instructor/[slug].astro. Add a public/robots.txt disallowing /instructor/ as defence in depth, and assert in the smoke test that the meta appears before </head>.

findings.title: The "NIST Atomic Spectra Database" attribution is false for the line intensities and contradicted on air-vs-vacuum within the same demo
findings.evidence: The catalog header reads "Multi-element empirical data (NIST ASD)" (line 107) and readers are told "Multi-element line data from the NIST Atomic Spectra Database (strongest lines only)" (spectral-lines/index.html:497, logic.ts:560, spectral-lines.md:40). But every `relativeIntensity` in ELEMENT_CATALOG is a multiple of 0.05 and normalised to 1.00 per element (He: 0.45/0.35/0.25/0.40/1.00/0.55/0.30; Na: 0.30/0.20/1.00/0.95; Ca: 1.00/0.90/0.55/0.25/0.20) — hand-assigned illustrative weights, not ASD relative intensities, and no ASD version, retrieval date or DOI is given. The wavelengths are air values rounded to 0.1 nm (Na D2 589.0, Na D1 589.6, Ca II K 393.4, He I D3 587.6 are the standard AIR values; the vacuum values are ~0.16-0.18 nm higher), which doppler-shift/logic.ts:554 concedes ("Element catalogs use air wavelengths") while doppler-shift/index.html:439 says "Vacuum wavelengths are used throughout" and doppler-shift.md:45 says "vacuum wavelengths, NIST teaching subset". STATUS.md confirms: "other lines are air values rounded to 0.1 nm, strengths are illustrative -- say so."
findings.scenario: A student in the Mystery Spectrum round reasons from relative line strengths they were told came from NIST and draws a conclusion the data cannot support. Separately, the air/vacuum mixture injects a 0.18 nm offset at H-alpha — 27% of the 0.66 nm shift the doppler predict_prompt asks them to estimate for 300 km/s — so a lab measurement comparing a computed vacuum hydrogen line against an air metal line is systematically biased.
findings.fix: In spectralLineModel.ts, rename `relativeIntensity` to `illustrativeStrength` and state in the comment and in every reader-facing note that strengths are illustrative, not ASD intensities; label the catalog wavelengths "laboratory air" everywhere; fix doppler-shift/index.html:439 and doppler-shift.md:45, which currently claim vacuum throughout; and add the ASD citation with version and retrieval date for the wavelengths that genuinely come from it.

findings.title: STATUS claims "Research-grade" demos "used in ASTR 101/201" against the project's own contrary evidence
findings.evidence: STATUS.md:10 (Current focus): "Research-grade interactive demos (physics unit-tested), deployed live, used in ASTR 101/201. Cottrell EdTech instrument." Contradicted inside the same repo: STATUS.md:30 "(no empirical learning data yet — assessment plan via CRMSE)"; cluster-census.md:12 "the demo is new and has not been used in a classroom yet"; conservation-laws.md:12 "awaiting classroom use before stable"; CLAUDE.md states the LEGACY demos at ~/Teaching/astr101-sp26/demos/ "are actively used for teaching this semester"; and STATUS.md:57-96 lists unfixed reader-visible physics defects (seasons orbit backwards, galaxy-rotation MOND curve +9% and a wrong M_dark formula, spectral-lines wrong wavelengths and uncited data, a Balmer proxy reading 0.000 on 33% of its slider). MEMORY.md records the 2026-09-03 audit grading the project C/59 after an earlier self-assessed A+.
findings.scenario: The line is pulled verbatim into a Cottrell report, a CV, or a federated portfolio dashboard (federate.py reads this file), asserting classroom use and research-grade validation that the repo's own frontmatter and backlog deny. This is the same self-assessment failure the 2026-09-03 audit already caught.
findings.fix: Rewrite STATUS.md:10 to what is true: "Interactive astronomy instruments with unit-tested physics models, deployed live; 1 of 20 exhibits is launch-ready, none has classroom or pre/post assessment evidence yet. Cottrell EdTech instrument." Drop "Research-grade" until an external validation exists to cite.

findings.title: About page claims "3 modes per demo" and "Every demo includes a Station Mode"; Station Mode is 18/20 and Challenge Mode is 8/20
findings.evidence: about.astro:21 StatBar: `{ value: "3", unit: "modes per demo", label: "Station / Challenge / Export" }`; :98-100 "Each demo ships with **Station Mode** ..., **Challenge Mode** ..., and **Export**"; :193 "**Every demo** includes a Station Mode". Counted directly: `createDemoModes` appears in 18 of 20 demo main.ts files — em-spectrum and planetary-conjunctions have none (em-spectrum.md:12 concedes "Still to come: ... Station and Challenge modes"). `challenges` is passed in only 8: angular-size, doppler-shift, eclipse-geometry, galaxy-rotation, moon-phases, retrograde-motion, seasons, spectral-lines. parallax-distance — the single launch-ready demo — has createDemoModes but challenges=0, so the flagship has no Challenge Mode. Also at :165 "Decorative elements are minimized — every visual element encodes data", while Design System Invariant 2 (CLAUDE.md) *mandates* a purely decorative `<canvas class="cp-starfield" aria-hidden="true">` on every instrument-layer demo.
findings.scenario: An instructor adopts the suite on the strength of "Challenge Mode (self-assessment)" on every demo, builds a lab around self-check, and finds it on 8 of 20 — not including the one demo the site calls launch-ready. The stat bar is the first thing on the About page and reads as a measured count.
findings.fix: Derive the stat from the catalogue the way `demoCount` already is (about.astro:17 carries the comment "Derived, not hardcoded: this read 14 while 19 demos shipped" — apply the same lesson): add booleans for station/challenge support to the demos schema or compute them at build time, render "Station Mode on 18 of 20, Challenge Mode on 8 of 20", and change "Every demo includes" to "Most demos include". Drop or qualify the "every visual element encodes data" claim given the mandated starfield.

findings.title: parallax-distance is marked launch-ready/stable although the parity audit it cites recommends promotion only to beta
findings.evidence: parallax-distance.md declares `status: stable`, `readiness: launch-ready`, and readinessReason "Physics and page checked in the September 2026 audits with nothing open". Its own `parityAuditPath`, docs/audits/migrations/parallax-distance-parity.md, section 6 says: "Recommendation should remain **conservative** (hold at **experimental**) if instructor-backlog P0 items are still open" and "Promote to **beta** after instructor-backlog P0 items are closed." The document never recommends stable or launch-ready — beta is its ceiling. This is the only demo in the project whose `status: stable` suppresses the "Active development" callout (exhibits/[slug].astro:73) and whose `launch-ready` suppresses the card badge (readiness.ts:58), so it is the one exhibit that presents with no caveat at all.
findings.scenario: An instructor filtering Explore by readiness picks the only uncaveated exhibit, assigns it unexamined, and is relying on a promotion two levels beyond what the cited evidence document supports. Worse, the glossary entry a student will consult for that very demo contains a factor-of-2 parallax error (see the glossary finding), which is exactly the class of "instructor-facing blocker" the audit warned about.
findings.fix: Either set `status: beta` / `readiness: candidate` to match the parity audit, or append a dated closure section to docs/audits/migrations/parallax-distance-parity.md that explicitly recommends stable/launch-ready and lists the instructor-backlog P0 items it closed. Do not leave frontmatter asserting more than the file it points to.

findings.title: The exhibit page defeats predict-before-play: the live demo renders above the Predict prompt and the teaching content is collapsed
findings.evidence: Source order is: launch buttons (:80-87), then `<IframeStage src={demoHref} />` with the comment "Iframe embed — visible early, before scrolling through text" (:89-90), then `<PPEBlock phase="predict">` (:103). So the interactive instrument is above the prediction prompt. README.md describes "exhibit pages (predict→play→explain)" and about.astro:139-147 grounds the whole scaffold in White & Gunstone (1992) and Crouch et al. (2004) — "students who predicted the outcome first showed significantly greater understanding". Separately, Learning goals (:124), Misconceptions targeted (:136) and Model notes (:149) are each wrapped in `<details class="collapsible">` with no `open` attribute, so all three are closed by default; only Evidence Base on the About page uses `open`. The frontmatter misconception list — the only place the shadow/distance/parallax misconceptions are named to a student — is therefore hidden by default on every exhibit.
findings.scenario: A student lands on /exhibits/seasons/, the iframe is already live, they drag the tilt slider for a minute, and only then scroll past it to "Predict: If Earth's axis were not tilted, what would happen to seasons?" — a prediction after the observation, which is the condition Crouch et al. found produced no measurable gain. They never open Misconceptions, so the distance myth is never confronted in text.
findings.fix: Move IframeStage below the Predict block in exhibits/[slug].astro, or render it collapsed behind a "Start the demo" control that the Predict block unlocks. Add `open` to the Misconceptions and Model notes `<details>` so the two sections that carry the conceptual-change work are visible by default.

findings.title: ASCII math, e-notation and reused symbols in demo frontmatter render straight onto exhibit pages; the validator cannot see any of it
findings.evidence: The validator only tests FORBIDDEN_UNICODE_MATH (validate-math-formatting.mjs:33), so ASCII-instead-of-LaTeX passes. Rendered verbatim by exhibits/[slug].astro:155: eos-lab.md:40-43 "P_gas = rho k_B T/(mu m_u)", "P_deg,e = max(P_e,FD - n_e k_B T, 0)", :22 "aT^4/3", :24 "T/T_F"; stars-zams-hr.md:44 "0.1 <= M/Msun <= 100 and **1e-4** <= Z <= 0.03" — e-notation, which CLAUDE.md bans outright in teaching copy ("Powers of ten as $10^n$; no `e` notation") — plus :45 "log(L/L_sun) versus log(T_eff)", :46 "M_V versus (B-V)"; doppler-shift.md:41-42 "lambda_obs = lambda_0 (1 + v/c)" and "sqrt((1+beta)/(1-beta))"; hydrostatic station_params "1 M_sun", "Mean molecular weight mu", "order 10^7 K". The same lists mix LaTeX and ASCII for the same symbols. Two symbol collisions also reach readers: keplers-laws.md uses $M$ for the central mass (":35 $P^2=a^3/M$", "vary the central mass $M$") and for mean anomaly in the same list (":37 "advances mean anomaly $M$ uniformly"); binary-orbits.md uses $K$ for kinetic energy (:21 "energies ($K$, $U$, $E$)") and for RV semi-amplitude ($K_1$, $K_2$) on adjacent lines.
findings.scenario: An ASTR 201 student reads the eos-lab Model notes and sees "P_deg,e = max(P_e,FD - n_e k_B T, 0)" as unparsed ASCII while the neighbouring blackbody exhibit renders $F = \\sigma T^4$ in KaTeX — and "1e-4" for a metallicity, the exact notation the project bans. In keplers-laws a student reads "$P^2 = a^3/M$" and then "mean anomaly $M$" and cannot tell which $M$ the time slider moves.
findings.fix: Rewrite the ASCII-math frontmatter in eos-lab.md, stars-zams-hr.md, doppler-shift.md and hydrostatic-equilibrium-explorer.md as LaTeX ($10^{-4}$ for 1e-4), rename the colliding symbols ($\\mathcal{M}$ or $M_{\\rm anom}$ for mean anomaly; $E_K$ for kinetic energy), and extend validate-math-formatting.mjs with a frontmatter rule that flags bare `_`/`^`/`sqrt(`/`\\d+e-?\\d+` outside `$...$` in the reader-visible fields (model_notes, play_steps, station_params, predict_prompt, explain_prompt, learning_goals, misconceptions).

findings.title: Two reader-visible source directories are outside the math validator's scan, and \\uXXXX escapes evade it even inside them — Wien's law ships in SI
findings.evidence: SCAN_ROOTS (validate-math-formatting.mjs:19-27) covers apps/demos/src/demos, apps/site/src/{content,pages,components,layouts,lib} and packages/runtime/src — not apps/site/src/data and not packages/physics/src. glossary.ts:110 reads `"\\u03BB_max = b / T, where b \\u2248 2.898 \\u00D7 10\\u207B\\u00B3 m\\u00B7K"`, which I decoded: "λ_max = b / T, where b ≈ 2.898 × 10⁻³ m·K". That is λ, ≈, ×, ⁻ and ³ — five characters in the validator's own FORBIDDEN_UNICODE_MATH — plus SI units (m·K) against CLAUDE.md's "NEVER use SI units ... use CGS"; the CGS value is 0.28978 cm·K. glossary.astro:72 renders `{entry.definition}` as plain text with no KaTeX, so it displays as raw Unicode. Because they are written as `\\uXXXX` escapes, adding `data` to SCAN_ROOTS would still not catch them — CLAUDE.md names this exact evasion ("no `\\uXXXX` escapes that produce them (the validator cannot see escapes)"). In packages/physics/src, spectralLineModel.ts:124,132,133 hold the UI strings "He I D₃ 587.6", "Na D₂ 589.0", "Na D₁ 589.6" with Unicode subscripts, and they are drawn to screen by `ctx.fillText(line.label, ...)` (spectral-lines/main.ts:1305, doppler-shift/main.ts:671) — the canvas exemption permits ASCII and explicitly says "never Unicode". A scan of the two unscanned roots found 69 lines matching the validator's own forbidden set.
findings.scenario: The glossary shows a 100-level student Wien's law in metre-kelvin with a Unicode λ that inherits whatever text-transform the surrounding CSS applies — the precise failure CLAUDE.md documents (94 KaTeX nodes uppercased on 2026-09-05, turning ν into N). A student converting cm to m silently mixes conventions with every other page on the site, which is CGS.
findings.fix: Add apps/site/src/data and packages/physics/src to SCAN_ROOTS; add a rule rejecting `\\u[0-9a-fA-F]{4}` escapes in reader-visible string literals under those roots; rewrite the glossary definitions as LaTeX rendered through `renderInlineMath()` from apps/site/src/lib/inlineMath.ts, with $b \\approx 0.290\\ \\mathrm{cm\\,K}$; and rename the three catalog labels to ASCII ("He I D3 587.6", "Na D2 589.0", "Na D1 589.6").

findings.title: The hubs collection is never rendered by any page, and its three substantive files point at a capstone and an activity that do not exist
findings.evidence: `grep -rn getCollection` across apps/site/src/{pages,components,lib,layouts} returns demos, stations, instructor and playlists — never "hubs" — and there is no pages/hubs route (find pages -name '*.astro' lists 15 files, none for hubs). So all four hub files are authored but unreachable, including the only document that sequences the four core demos into a teaching throughline. Inside them: all three substantive hubs link `[Rotation + synthesis](capstone.qmd)` and repeat "Rotation + synthesis lab: `capstone.qmd`" (cosmic-playground.md:8,34; distance-and-measurement.md:9,33; light-and-telescopes.md:8,33) — no capstone.qmd exists in the repo, and .qmd is Quarto, not this Astro site. distance-and-measurement.md:9 lists "Cosmic Distance Builder (coming soon)" and then its connection map (:22) and Recommended sequencing (:28) both build on it as though it existed. All three also show link text "[/demos/_instructor/]" for a URL that is actually ../../instructor/. hubs/meta.md says in full: "This entry exists to keep the `hubs` collection non-empty during early migration."
findings.scenario: The instructor guidance Anna wrote — the throughline, the sequencing, the MW-lecture-moment plan — reaches nobody, so For Instructors offers 19 station cards and 19 note bundles with no document saying how they compose into a unit. If a hubs route were added tomorrow, every hub would ship three dead links and a Friday-lab plan built on a capstone and an activity that were never written.
findings.fix: Decide and act: either add apps/site/src/pages/hubs/[slug].astro and link hubs from for-instructors (deleting the capstone.qmd links, the "coming soon" activity references in the connection map and sequencing, the placeholder meta.md, and fixing the link text), or delete the hubs collection from content/config.ts and move the throughline prose into the instructor bundles where it will actually be read.

findings.title: For Instructors promises "everything you need" while 3 demos have no instructor bundle, 2 have no station card, and 15 of 20 station cards have no parameter table
findings.evidence: for-instructors/index.astro:32-34 "Everything you need to run Cosmic Playground in your classroom: printable station cards, detailed instructor notes, and curated playlists"; :73-74 "Station Cards — One-page printable cards with controls, **parameters**, and the PPE flow for each demo"; and it links all 19 listed demos in both grids. On disk: content/instructor/ has bundles for 17 slugs — cluster-census, eos-lab and stars-zams-hr have none, so those pages render the "Instructor notes not written yet ... This page is a scaffold" callout. content/stations/ has 18 demo files — planetary-conjunctions and stars-zams-hr have none. `station_params` is present in only 5 of 20 demo files (cluster-census, binary-orbits, eos-lab, hydrostatic-equilibrium-explorer, stars-zams-hr), so 15 station cards have no parameter table. The Instructor Notes cards label each destination with `{d.data.misconceptions.length} misconceptions targeted` (:113) — a count of frontmatter strings, which is 1 for 10 of the demos and is shown even for slugs whose destination is an empty scaffold.
findings.scenario: An instructor reads "everything you need", clicks "Cluster Census — 3 misconceptions targeted" expecting activities, timing and assessment, and lands on a scaffold notice. stars-zams-hr is the worst case: an ASTR 201 instrument with neither instructor notes nor a station card, advertised in both grids. There is no way to answer "what do students submit, and what is the answer" for those three demos.
findings.fix: Gate the two grids on actual content: build a Set of instructor `bundle` values and station `demo_slug` values and either omit those cards or mark them "notes not written yet" on the card itself, so the promise matches the destination. Qualify "with controls, parameters" to reflect that only 5 cards carry a parameter table, and replace the misconception count with a content-completeness label.

findings.title: hydrostatic-equilibrium-explorer's reader-visible model notes are written as unmet specifications, with content_verified: true
findings.evidence: Four of the six model_notes are in the subjunctive, describing what the demo ought to do rather than what it does: ":40 'The model **should show** hydrostatic equilibrium as $\\frac{dP}{dr} = -\\frac{GM(r)\\rho(r)}{r^2}$, not as a statement that pressure vanishes'; :41 'Pressure scale height **should be interpreted** as $H_P = ...$'; :43 'A one-zone core-temperature estimate **should be presented as** a scaling relation ...'; :44 'the core-temperature number **should be labeled** as an inference'." These render verbatim under "Model notes" on the exhibit page (exhibits/[slug].astro:149-158). The file nonetheless sets `content_verified: true`. The physics in the notes is correct — I verified $H_P = -(d\\ln P/dr)^{-1} = P/(\\rho g)$ follows from $dP/dr = -\\rho g$, that $T = (\\mu m_u/k_B) g H_P$ follows from the ideal gas law, and that $T_c \\sim (\\mu m_u/k_B)(GM/R)$ gives 1.40e7 K for $\\mu = 0.61$, $M_\\odot$, $R_\\odot$, matching the station card's "order 10^7 K" — so the notes are a usable spec, just not a description.
findings.scenario: A 201 student opens Model notes to learn what the instrument assumes and reads a developer to-do list that says the model "should" show the HSE equation — leaving them unable to tell whether it does, and unable to decide how far to trust the core-temperature readout they were told to reason from. `content_verified: true` asserts that this copy was checked.
findings.fix: Rewrite the six notes in the indicative to state what the demo computes ("Gravity is evaluated as $g = GM(r)/r^2$; the required gradient is $dP/dr = -\\rho g$; the core temperature is a one-zone scaling $T_c \\sim (\\mu m_u/k_B)(GM/R)$ times an order-unity structure factor, not a stellar-structure solution"), or set `content_verified: false` until they are. Grep the other 19 demo files for "should" in model_notes.

findings.title: galaxy-rotation tells readers the MOND curve is the deep-MOND asymptote; its own exhibit page says full interpolation
findings.evidence: index.html:374: "The MOND curve shows the deep-MOND asymptotic limit ($a \\ll a_0$) where $V^4 \\approx G\\,M\\,a_0$. The full MOND interpolating function transitions smoothly from Newtonian at small $R$ to this flat regime." The two sentences describe different curves. galaxy-rotation.md:38 says the opposite of the first: "MOND is shown as an optional comparison curve via **full interpolation**, not as a full parameter-fitting workflow." STATUS.md (GR-3) confirms the demo note is the wrong one: "index.html:374 'deep-MOND limit' is wrong (the curve is the simple interpolating function)", and adds that galaxyRotationModel.ts:454 feeds MOND a spherical $g_N$ instead of $g_{\\rm bar} = V_{\\rm bar}^2/R$, shifting the plotted curve by +9% at 8 kpc. The formula itself is right — the deep-MOND asymptote is $V_\\infty^4 = GMa_0$ — but it is not what is drawn. galaxy-rotation is `readiness: candidate`.
findings.scenario: A student following play_step "Turn on MOND and compare it to the dark-halo model at galaxy scales" is told the curve they see is the $a \\ll a_0$ asymptote, so they expect it flat at $(GMa_0)^{1/4}$ everywhere and read the rising inner portion as a contradiction — or conclude MOND predicts Keplerian behaviour at small R as a matter of principle rather than as interpolation. The explain_prompt asks them to say what breaks the tie between models, on a curve that is mislabelled and 9% off.
findings.fix: Rewrite index.html:374 to one claim matching the code: "The MOND curve uses the simple interpolating function, which approaches Newtonian behaviour at small $R$ and the asymptote $V^4 = G M a_0$ where $a \\ll a_0$." Fix galaxyRotationModel.ts:454 to pass $g_{\\rm bar} = V_{\\rm bar}^2/R$ (a physics change — propose it to Anna with the +9% magnitude before changing it), and cite the constants at ts:254-261.

findings.title: Geometry diagram's 6-px disk floor makes the viewing cone miss the object's limbs for the default Sun view
findings.evidence: `objectCircle.setAttribute("r", String(Math.max(6, radius)));` where `radius = Math.tan(halfRad) * (objectX - observerX)` with span 520 - 90 = 430 SVG units (line 305). `rayTop`/`rayBottom` end at centerY +/- radius and `sizeLine` spans the same (lines 338-355), i.e. the true cone, unfloored. Recomputed radius = tan(theta/2) x 430: sun 2.00 px vs disk 6.00; moon 1.94 vs 6.00; jupiter 0.05 vs 6.00; venus 0.06; mars 0.03; orionNebula 4.18; basketball 5.14; soccerball 2.36; airplane 1.29; iss 0.06 — 10 of 18 presets have the disk drawn larger than the cone that is supposed to subtend it. radius exceeds 6 px only for theta > 1.599 deg.
findings.scenario: Default load (Sun preset): the student sees a 12-px disk with two rays that stop 2 px either side of its centre, an amber arc at the observer measuring that 4-px opening, and a dashed line labelled `D ~ 1.39 x 10^6 km` drawn entirely inside the disk. The one thing the diagram exists to show — that theta is the angle between the lines of sight to the object's two edges — is visibly false in the demo's own opening state, and the drawn angle looks about 3x the true one.
findings.fix: In renderStage, floor the *geometry* rather than the disk: when `radius < MIN_VISIBLE` (6), keep the disk at `radius` and instead draw a labelled magnifier/inset, or move the object nearer in SVG space (reduce `objectX`) so the exact cone reaches 6 px, and state the applied visual magnification in the drawing. Whatever is chosen, `objectCircle` r, the ray endpoints and `sizeLine` must always be the same number.

findings.title: Distance slider is dead on the Moon preset and teleports its own thumb mid-drag
findings.evidence: `render()` begins with `applyMoonControlsToDistance()` (line 729), which for the Moon preset reads `Number(moonOrbitAngle.value)` (line 220) and *overwrites* `state.distanceKm` that the slider handler just set (lines 952-957). `orbitAngleDegFromMoonDistance` clamps w to [0,1], so any distance outside [perigee, apogee] saturates. Traced with the real constants (perigee 355436 km, apogee 406213 km): slider 100 -> user asked 2.512e-2 km -> angle 0 -> rendered 355436 km, theta 0.5600 deg; slider 300 -> asked 1.585e3 km -> same 355436 km; slider 507 -> asked 1.472e8 km -> angle 180 -> rendered 406213 km, theta 0.4900 deg; slider 900 -> asked 3.981e17 km -> same 406213 km. render() then writes the slider back via `valueToLogSlider(355436, ...)` = index 398, so the thumb jumps away from the pointer. Recession mode fails the same way: `moonRecessionTime.value` is clamped by the input's min/max of +/-1000, pinning distance to 384400 +/- 38000 km.
findings.scenario: A student on "Moon (Today)" nudges the distance slider slightly left to see the Moon get bigger. The Moon jumps to extreme perigee (0.5600 deg, now larger than the Sun), the distance readout reads 355,436 km regardless of where they dropped the thumb, and the thumb snaps to a different position than the one they are dragging. The slider has two reachable states out of 1001 and contradicts its own label.
findings.fix: Make state the single source of truth: `applyMoonControlsToDistance` should read `state.moonOrbitAngleDeg` / `state.moonRecessionTimeMyr`, not the DOM, and should run only from the moon-control handlers — not from `render()`. Then either (a) disable the distance slider while the Moon preset owns the distance, with a one-line note saying the orbit control drives it, or (b) let the distance slider drop the preset to "Custom" (the `AngularSizeDemoState` type already has a `"Custom"` member that nothing ever assigns) and hide the moon controls.

findings.title: Challenge 1 is passable at exactly one of 1001 slider positions, and its hint points at a control that fires no event
findings.evidence: initialState sets `presetKey: "sun", distanceKm: 2 * AngularSizeModel.presets.sun.distance`; check requires `presetKey === "sun"` and `|theta - 0.53313| <= 0.02`. The distance slider is log-mapped over 24 decades in 1001 steps, so one step multiplies d by 10^(24/1000) = 1.0568. Recomputed the neighbourhood: s=506 -> d=1.3932e8 km, theta=0.57248, err 0.03935 FAIL; s=507 -> 1.4723e8, theta=0.54170, err 0.00857 PASS; s=508 -> 1.5560e8, theta=0.51258, err 0.02055 FAIL. Exactly one passing position. The hint says "Try changing the distance back toward 1 AU (Sun preset)", but `render()` line 744 sets `preset.value = state.presetId` = "sun", so the select already displays "Sun" and re-choosing that option fires no `change` event — the preset route cannot restore 1 AU.
findings.scenario: A student starts challenge 1, follows the hint, clicks "Sun" in the preset dropdown, and nothing happens. They then hunt the slider, where 1000 of 1001 positions are rejected and the one that passes reports "Nice: theta ~ 0.542 deg" for a challenge that asked for 0.53 deg. The first of three challenges is effectively unsolvable.
findings.fix: Either widen the tolerance to about one slider step in theta (tol ~ 0.04 deg, i.e. +/- 6% in d, so 2-3 positions pass) or add a non-log fine-adjust for distance. Separately, make the preset select restorable: add a `change`-independent path (e.g. a "Reset to preset" button, or set `preset.value = ""` on a mismatch so re-selecting "Sun" fires) and fix the hint to name the control that actually works. Add an e2e test that drives each challenge to a pass through the real UI.

findings.title: Eight Unicode math glyphs reach the reader through \u escapes and HTML entities the math validator cannot see
findings.evidence: logic.ts:43 `"⁰¹²³⁴⁵⁶⁷⁸⁹"` and line 77 `` return `${mantissa} × 10${toSuperscript(expNum)}` `` — rendered by `thetaDeg.textContent = formatSci(thetaDegValue, 4)` (main.ts:761) and every distance/diameter readout, so Andromeda's distance prints `778 kpc` but its diameter prints `4.083 x 10^1` style output with a literal MULTIPLICATION SIGN and SUPERSCRIPT digits. main.ts:400-404 emit `°`, `′`, `″` into `#skyFov`, which is an HTML `<span>` (index.html:293) that KaTeX could render. main.ts:423 has a literal `↔`. index.html:73 `≈ 2°`, index.html:148 `↔`, index.html:273 and :277 `θ` as the readout labels. scripts/validate-math-formatting.mjs:33 tests `FORBIDDEN_UNICODE_MATH` against the raw file text, so escapes and entities pass unseen; `↔` (U+2194) is not even in the character class, so the literal on main.ts:423 and in angular-size.md:29 passes too.
findings.scenario: The CLAUDE.md rationale is that a Unicode glyph inherits whatever the surrounding CSS does to it — on 2026-09-05 an inherited `text-transform` turned 94 KaTeX nodes' `\nu` into "N". Every readout in this demo carries bare Unicode superscripts and a multiplication sign that no test and no build gate can see; a single `text-transform` or font-fallback change silently corrupts the exponents of every number on the page, and the build stays green.
findings.fix: Replace `formatSci`'s Unicode output with KaTeX: emit `$1.50 \times 10^{8}$` and render it with `renderMath()` from `@cosmic/runtime` (already imported as `initMath`), deleting `toSuperscript` and `SUPERSCRIPT_DIGITS`. Convert index.html:73, :148, :273, :277 to `$\approx$`, `$^{\circ}$`, `$\leftrightarrow$`, `$\theta$`; convert main.ts:400-404 to LaTeX in the span; change main.ts:423 and angular-size.md:29 to `$\leftrightarrow$`. Then close the gate: have validate-math-formatting.mjs decode `\uXXXX` escapes and `&#x...;`/`&#...;` entities before testing, and add U+2194 to the character class.

findings.title: No announcement path for screen readers: log sliders expose raw 0-1000 values and nothing announces theta
findings.evidence: `#distanceSlider` and `#diameterSlider` are `type="range" min="0" max="1000" step="1"` with no `aria-valuetext`, and nothing in main.ts ever sets one (grep for aria-valuetext in this folder returns nothing). The only live region is `#status` (index.html:187), and `setLiveRegionText` is called from exactly one place — the copy-results handler (main.ts:1000-1015). The readout strip is a plain `<div class="cp-readout-strip" aria-label="Readouts">` with no role, so the aria-label is dropped by most AT and the values are not announced on change. The house pattern exists elsewhere: moon-phases/index.html:317 and cluster-census/main.ts:975-982 set aria-valuetext, and cluster-census/design-contracts.test.ts:255 is a contract test titled "sets aria-valuetext on every slider whose raw value is not its meaning".
findings.scenario: A screen-reader user arrives at the distance slider and hears "Distance d, slider, 507". They press Right Arrow and hear "508". Nothing tells them the distance is 1.47e8 km, nothing tells them theta changed from 0.5417 to 0.5126 deg, and the number they hear has no physical meaning at all. The demo is unusable without sight, while its sibling demos solved this.
findings.fix: In `render()`, set `distanceSlider.setAttribute("aria-valuetext", `${distSliderFmt.text} ${distSliderFmt.unit}`)` and the same for `diameterSlider`, `moonOrbitAngle` and `moonRecessionTime`. Add a debounced (not per-frame) live announcement of theta on control release — or give the readout strip `role="group"` plus a separate `aria-live="polite"` summary node updated outside the render path. Copy cluster-census's design-contracts assertion into this demo's test file so it cannot regress.

findings.title: Demo CSS has no media queries, so the two-panel stage never stacks at phone width
findings.evidence: `.viz-layout { display: grid; grid-template-columns: minmax(0, 1.4fr) minmax(0, 1fr); gap: var(--cp-space-4); }` with zero `@media` blocks anywhere in the file (`grep -c "@media"` returns 0). Siblings: moon-phases 3, parallax-distance 5, seasons 4, eclipse-geometry 1. At a 320-px viewport the two panels plus padding leave roughly 130 px for the 640-unit-wide geometry SVG, scaling its 12-px `.stage__metricLabel` text to about 2.4 px. `.unit-selectors` (line 20) also uses bare `1fr 1fr`, which CLAUDE.md flags as the overflow pattern (a `1fr` track grows to its widest item). `/play/angular-size/` is not in `PLAY_ROUTES` in apps/site/tests/reflow.spec.ts:55, so no test covers this.
findings.scenario: A student opens the demo on a phone, as the exhibit's readinessReason claims works ("the page works on a phone"). The geometry diagram and the Sky View sit side by side at roughly 130 px each; the `D ~ ...` and `d ~ ...` labels render at about 2-3 px and are unreadable, and the unit-selector row can push the sidebar wider than the viewport.
findings.fix: Add a breakpoint matching the house pattern: `@media (max-width: 760px) { .viz-layout { grid-template-columns: minmax(0, 1fr); } .unit-selectors { grid-template-columns: minmax(0, 1fr); } }`, and change `.unit-selectors` to `minmax(0, 1fr) minmax(0, 1fr)` at wide widths. Then add `play/angular-size/` to `PLAY_ROUTES` in reflow.spec.ts and verify with the scroll probe (`scrollTo(2000,0)` then `scrollX > 0`), not `scrollWidth`.

findings.title: content_verified and lastVerifiedAt predate the Sky View panel, and the cited parity audit recommends "experimental"
findings.evidence: Frontmatter: `readiness: candidate`, `content_verified: true`, `parityAuditPath: "docs/audits/migrations/angular-size-parity.md"`, `lastVerifiedAt: "2026-02-02"`, `last_updated: "2026-02-02"`. Git dates for this demo: `be9f85d 2026-02-06 feat(angular-size): Phase C layout redesign + Sky View panel`, `03a8314 2026-02-06 feat(angular-size): add scientific notation, deep-sky presets, and unit selectors`, `8581a93 2026-02-06 refactor(angular-size): move readouts into geometry panel`, `69094e0 2026-09-10 Open the Moon preset at its mean distance, not perigee`. Every feature carrying the P0s above (the Sky View ring, the adaptive FOV, the Unicode scientific notation, the deep-sky presets) landed *after* the claimed verification date. The cited parity audit is a stub: all five sections read "Pending detailed parity review" and section 6 reads "Current recommendation: experimental until parity review is completed."
findings.scenario: An instructor filtering the Explore page by readiness sees a `candidate` demo marked content-verified and assigns it as a lab. The verification covers a build four days older than the panel that draws the Sun's angular size as the Moon's, and the audit the frontmatter points to as evidence recommends the opposite readiness level.
findings.fix: Set `readiness: experimental` (matching the parity audit's own recommendation) until the two P0 drawing bugs are fixed, set `content_verified: false`, and update `readinessReason` to name the Sky View defects rather than only the screen-reader gap. After the fixes, re-verify, bump `lastVerifiedAt`/`last_updated` to that date, and fill in docs/audits/migrations/angular-size-parity.md — or drop `parityAuditPath` rather than cite a stub as evidence.

findings.title: Energy chart draws its five bar labels 404 px below the canvas, so K1/K2/K/U/E are unidentifiable
findings.evidence: drawEnergyView() places each bar's identity label with energyCtx.fillText(bar.label, x + barW/2, yFromEnergy(-maxMagnitude) + plotH + 20). yFromEnergy(v) = margin.top + ((maxMagnitude - v)/(2*maxMagnitude))*plotH (main.ts:968), so yFromEnergy(-maxMagnitude) = margin.top + plotH already. The label y is therefore margin.top + 2*plotH + 20. With the real CSS geometry (style.css:221-224, aspect-ratio 3/1.55 at width <= 960 px -> 960x496 px canvas; margin.top 24, margin.bottom 44 -> plotH = 428) that is 24 + 428 + 428 + 20 = 900 px on a 496 px canvas: 404 px below the bottom edge. Algebraically it is off-canvas for any height above 92 px, so no viewport saves it. The numeric value labels at main.ts:1005 are placed correctly, so the bars show numbers with no names.
findings.scenario: A student switches to the Energy view and sees five bars with values like '0.85', '0.85', '1.69', '-1.69', '-0.85' and no indication of which is K1, K2, K, U or E. There is no visual snapshot test for the energy view (apps/site/tests/binary-orbits.spec.ts-snapshots/ contains only default, mobile, q0p2, rv-inclination-30 and rv-sb1), so nothing caught it.
findings.fix: Change the y argument at main.ts:1004 to yFromEnergy(-maxMagnitude) + 20 (i.e. margin.top + plotH + 20, inside the bottom margin). Delete the unused locals y (main.ts:995) and baselineY (main.ts:958) while in there, and add an @visual snapshot test for the energy panel so the chart is covered at all.

findings.title: Orbit view's observer arrow points the opposite way from the RV sign convention, inverting redshift and blueshift
findings.evidence: drawOrbit() draws the sightline as a horizontal dashed line and puts the arrowhead at the RIGHT end: moveTo(sightlineEndX, sightlineY); lineTo(sightlineEndX - 12, ...) (main.ts:673-678), labelled 'observer line of sight' (main.ts:682). So the observer is at screen +x. Body 1 is drawn at x1 = cx - r1px*cos(phase) (logic.ts:593), so dx1/dphase = +r1*sin(phase): with phase increasing, body 1 moves toward +x, i.e. TOWARD the drawn observer, whenever sin(phase) > 0. The model gives rv1 = k1AuPerYr * sin(phaseRad) (binaryOrbitModel.ts:135), positive for the same sin(phase) > 0, and the RV chart labels the positive half-plane 'receding' (main.ts:829, with yFromVelocity mapping positive velocity upward). Body 2 is consistent with body 1 (x2 = cx + r2px*cos, rv2 = -k2*sin), so both curves carry the same inverted sense. The Doppler chain agrees with the chart and not the drawing: shiftedWavelengthNm uses factor = 1 + beta (dopplerShiftModel.ts:101), so positive rv redshifts.
findings.scenario: A student is asked (Station Mode step 3, and learning goal 3 'connect barycentric motion to spectroscopic observables') to say whether the primary is red- or blue-shifted when it is on the left of the barycenter moving right. From the orbit view's arrow they correctly read 'moving toward the observer', then switch to RV or Spectrum and the demo reports a positive radial velocity in the half-plane labelled 'receding' and a redshift. They learn the sign convention backwards.
findings.fix: Pick one convention and make the drawing carry it. Smallest fix: in drawOrbit() move the arrowhead to sightlineStartX pointing left (observer at screen -x) and label it 'to observer', which makes +x motion recession and matches rv1 = +K1 sin(phase). Then add a unit test that is NOT at a symmetric phase - e.g. assert that at phase pi/2 bodyPositions puts body 1 at smaller x than at phase -pi/2 while BinaryOrbitModel.radialVelocityAtPhase returns rv1 > 0 - so the pairing is pinned.

findings.title: Inclination never changes the drawing; the orbit view always depicts the edge-on (i=90) geometry
findings.evidence: I read drawOrbit() in full (main.ts:546-690). model.inclinationDeg appears only inside fillText at main.ts:683 ('i = N deg') and main.ts:686 (the face-on note), and model.sinInclination only inside projectionFactorLabel (main.ts:499). The orbits are drawn as true circles, arc(cx, cy, r1px, 0, 2*PI) (main.ts:583-587), and the sightline is always the same horizontal line at sightlineY = cy + min(h*0.24, 110) (main.ts:661). A sightline lying in the plane of a face-on-drawn orbit IS the i=90 configuration, so the picture asserts sin i = 1 at every setting while the readouts apply sin i. There is no second reference line for the drawn 'i = 60 deg' label to subtend an angle against.
findings.scenario: A student drags inclination from 90 to 0 deg. Nothing in the picture moves: the circles stay circles, the sightline stays in the orbital plane. The readouts say K1 and K2 collapse to 0.000 km/s and the canvas prints 'Face-on view: RV signal collapses toward zero' over a diagram that still shows the stars sweeping straight along the line of sight. The student has to choose between the picture and the number, and the picture is more persuasive. 'Changing inclination leaves the orbit geometry alone' (index.html:375) is true in 3-D but, read against this drawing, teaches that inclination is a free fudge factor.
findings.fix: Make the drawing show the projection. Either (a) draw the apparent (projected) orbit as an ellipse with semi-minor axis r*cos(i) while keeping the sightline horizontal, so i=0 collapses to a circle seen face-on and i=90 collapses to a line, and label it 'apparent orbit'; or (b) add a small side-view inset in which the sightline tilts by i against the orbital-plane normal, so the 'i = N deg' label actually subtends the angle it names. Option (a) is cheaper and reuses the existing canvas.

findings.title: 'Show angular frequency' checkbox is a no-op: syncReadoutsToView overwrites its decision every frame
findings.evidence: renderAtPhase() calls updateReadouts(targetModel) at main.ts:1735 and updateViewControls() at main.ts:1744. updateReadouts ends with omegaReadout.hidden = !state.showOmega (main.ts:1622). updateViewControls then calls syncReadoutsToView() (main.ts:1692), which loops over every .cp-readout[data-views] and sets readout.hidden = views.length > 0 && !views.includes(state.view) (logic in main.ts:1706-1710). #omegaReadout carries class="cp-readout" hidden data-views="orbit energy" (index.html:246), so it matches that selector and is unconditionally un-hidden in the orbit and energy views and unconditionally hidden in the rv and spectrum views. The later write wins on every frame, including the frame triggered by the checkbox's own change handler (main.ts:1895-1898).
findings.scenario: On first load, with the checkbox unchecked, the 'Angular frequency omega' readout and the 'v1 = omega a1, v2 = omega a2' note are already visible - the control contradicts its own state. A student (or instructor following play_steps item 5, 'Toggle angular frequency view and verify v1 = omega a1') clicks the checkbox and nothing changes; in the RV view, checking it also does nothing. No test covers showOmega at all - I grepped both logic.test.ts and apps/site/tests/binary-orbits.spec.ts and found no reference.
findings.fix: Give the omega readout one owner. Add 'omega' as a condition inside syncReadoutsToView (e.g. honour a data-requires="showOmega" attribute) or drop the hidden write from updateReadouts and instead fold state.showOmega into the data-views decision, then delete whichever write is no longer the owner. Add a test asserting #omegaReadout is hidden in the orbit view when the box is unchecked.

findings.title: aria-live insight region is rewritten with innerHTML and re-typeset by KaTeX 60 times per second
findings.evidence: The animation loop is unconditional: frame() calls renderAtPhase(...) then requestAnimationFrame(frame) (main.ts:2081-2087). renderAtPhase calls updateMassRatioInsight(targetModel) (main.ts:1736), which assigns massRatioInsightTitle.innerHTML, assigns massRatioInsightBody.innerHTML with three paragraphs of LaTeX, and then calls initMath() on both elements (main.ts:1201-1208). The container is <div id="massRatioInsight" class="cp-live-insight" aria-live="polite"> (index.html:118-120). So an assertive-adjacent live region has its entire subtree destroyed and rebuilt, and four KaTeX expressions re-parsed and re-rendered, every frame. updateProjectionMessaging (main.ts:1627-1632) likewise rewrites three note strings per frame, and updateScalingCue writes the two aria-live="polite" cue paragraphs (index.html:180-181) per frame.
findings.scenario: A screen-reader user opens the demo and the polite queue is fed a fresh copy of the insight text roughly 60 times a second; the reader either talks continuously or never finishes a sentence, and the rest of the page becomes unusable. Separately, every visitor pays four KaTeX renders plus two full innerHTML teardowns per frame - the single most expensive thing in the frame - which on a classroom laptop competes directly with the canvas draw. This is the pattern CLAUDE.md names explicitly: live-region announcements on change, never inside a render loop.
findings.fix: Hoist all non-canvas DOM updates out of the rAF loop. Keep renderAtPhase doing only the canvas draw plus the phase-dependent marker, and call the readout/insight/prompt/cue updaters from the control handlers (handleLiveControlChange, the view and preset handlers) instead. If updateMassRatioInsight must stay reachable from the loop, guard it with a memo on (massRatio, separation, inclinationDeg) so innerHTML and initMath only run when one of those actually changes.

findings.title: The RV inversion challenge - the demo's graded activity - is reachable only with a mouse
findings.evidence: Measurement happens exclusively through rvCanvas.addEventListener("click", (event) => captureRvAmplitudeFromCanvasClick(event)) (main.ts:2055-2057), and that handler reads event.clientX/clientY to derive the phase and velocity (main.ts:1459-1472). I grepped every addEventListener in main.ts: the only keydown listener is the one bindButtonRadioGroup attaches to chip buttons (main.ts:1552). <canvas id="rvCanvas" width="520" height="260" aria-label="Radial velocity versus phase"> (index.html:214) has no tabindex, so it cannot even receive focus. #orbitCanvas (index.html:209) has no aria-label at all, unlike the other three canvases.
findings.scenario: A keyboard-only or screen-reader student follows play_steps item 8 ('Start the RV inversion challenge, click both RV curves to measure amplitudes, infer q, then reveal and compare error'). They can press 'Start challenge' and 'Check / reveal', but reveal refuses with 'Measure both RV amplitudes before reveal' (main.ts:1817) and there is no way to ever satisfy it. The activity that carries learning goal 5 is unreachable, and the e2e a11y coverage stops at 'tab navigation reaches mass ratio slider' (spec.ts:537).
findings.fix: Add a keyboard path to sampling: give #rvCanvas tabindex="0" plus a visible focus ring, and a keydown handler where Left/Right step a phase cursor, Up/Down step the velocity cursor, Tab or a key toggles the primary/secondary target, and Enter commits the sample through the same captureRvAmplitude code path (refactor it to take {phaseCycle, velocityKmPerS} so both the mouse and keyboard call one function). Announce each committed sample once through #status. Also add aria-label to #orbitCanvas.

findings.title: Under prefers-reduced-motion the phase is frozen at 0 forever, the one phase where both radial velocities are exactly zero
findings.evidence: state is initialised with phaseRad: 0 (main.ts:385), and the only writer is renderAtPhase's state.phaseRad = phaseRad (main.ts:1731). Under reduced motion the branch at main.ts:2064-2078 calls renderStatic() - which is renderAtPhase(state.phaseRad, ...) (main.ts:1760) - and never starts a rAF loop, so the phase stays 0 for the whole session. There is no phase slider, scrub control or play/pause anywhere in index.html. At phase 0, rv1 = k1 * sin(0) = 0 and rv2 = -k2 * sin(0) = 0 (binaryOrbitModel.ts:135-136), so the RV phase markers (main.ts:879-889) both sit on the zero line and the spectrum's rvSample is 0, giving Delta lambda = 0.000 nm exactly.
findings.scenario: A motion-sensitive student (or any student on a machine with reduce-motion set, which includes many lab images) opens the RV view and sees two curves with both phase dots pinned to v_r = 0, then opens the Spectrum view and sees Delta lambda = 0.000 nm with identical strips. They have no control that can move the system off that phase, so two of the four views convey nothing. Note the phase is also not persisted or restorable, so this is not recoverable by reloading.
findings.fix: Add an explicit phase control that works in every motion mode: a range input bound to state.phaseRad (0 to 2 pi, labelled 'Orbital phase' in deg or in cycles) plus a play/pause button, and under reduced motion start it at a non-degenerate phase such as pi/2 rather than 0. This also gives sighted students the ability to hold a phase and read the orbit position against the RV sign, which is the correspondence the demo exists to teach.

findings.title: Fixed 3-decimal formatting prints 0.000 and -0.000 for real physics in the shipped Planet-limit preset
findings.evidence: formatNumber returns value.toFixed(digits) with no scale awareness (logic.ts:46-49), and every readout passes 2-4 digits (main.ts:1588-1620). presetPlanet sets the mass ratio to 0.001 (main.ts:2015-2017) and the 'planet' anchor button does the same (index.html:71). I recomputed that state: at q=0.001, a=4 AU, i=60, f(m) = P*k1^3/(2 pi G) = 6.482e-10 Msun, printed as '0.000'; kinetic energy of M1 = 4.6e-6 Msun AU^2/yr^2, printed as '0.000'. At q=0.001 with the separation slider at 100 AU the whole energy view degenerates: U = -(4 pi^2 * 1 * 0.001)/100 = -3.948e-4, printed as '-0.000'; E = -1.974e-4, printed as '-0.000'; both kinetic terms print '0.000'. The virial residual prints '0.000' at every setting, so that readout can never say anything.
findings.scenario: A student clicks the 'Planet limit' preset - a one-click path the demo advertises - opens the Energy view and reads 'Potential energy U = -0.000', 'Total orbital energy E = -0.000', 'Mass function f(m) = 0.000 Msun'. They conclude a planet-mass companion has zero binding energy and that the mass function is zero, when it is 6.5e-10 Msun. '-0.000' is also a nonsense readout on its face. Nothing tests this: the e2e checks only that the parsed value is not NaN (spec.ts:227, 566).
findings.fix: Make formatNumber scale-aware for small magnitudes. Since the project bans e-notation in teaching copy, render small values as a KaTeX power of ten (e.g. $6.5 \\times 10^{-10}$) through renderMath, or switch the affected readouts to a unit that keeps them O(1) - M_Jup for the secondary mass and mass function, and a stated 10^n prefix for the energies. At minimum, never emit a signed zero: clamp |value| < 0.5*10^-digits to exact '0'. Add a test over the preset grid asserting no readout prints '0.000' or '-0.000' for a non-zero quantity.

findings.title: Exhibit copy promises prediction gating of snapshots and Copy Results that the code does not implement and the tests assert is absent
findings.evidence: The exhibit's play_steps say 'Prediction gating is enforced for snapshots and Copy Results while a reveal is pending.' The gate does not exist: copyResults' handler guards only on isRvChallengeLocked (main.ts:2331-2335) and the station snapshot guard is the same RV-challenge check (main.ts:2155). logic.ts exports isPredictionLocked (logic.ts:232) and selectDisplayModel (logic.ts:236) for exactly that purpose; I grepped apps and packages for both names and they appear nowhere outside logic.ts - not even in logic.test.ts - so they are dead code. The shipped e2e tests assert the opposite behaviour: 'copy results stays available during prediction compare workflow' (spec.ts:469) and 'station snapshot remains available during prediction compare workflow' (spec.ts:624), and 'prediction compare uses a captured baseline while the live demo keeps updating' (spec.ts:636).
findings.scenario: An instructor reads the exhibit page to design a lab, relies on the demo withholding Copy Results until a student commits to a prediction, and builds the worksheet around it. In class, students copy the answers out before predicting; the stated pedagogical control does not exist. The same stale claim appears in docs/audits/migrations/binary-orbits-parity.md ('readouts freeze until reveal', 'export and station snapshot now respect prediction-lock state').
findings.fix: The current live-while-comparing behaviour is the better design, so correct the copy rather than the code: delete that play_steps line from apps/site/src/content/demos/binary-orbits.md and replace it with what the demo actually does (the baseline is captured and compared against while the readouts stay live). Then delete isPredictionLocked and selectDisplayModel from logic.ts, and fix the two stale bullets in the parity audit.

findings.title: readiness: candidate and content_verified: true outrun the parity audit the exhibit cites, which itself says 'stay experimental'
findings.evidence: The frontmatter claims status: beta, content_verified: true, readiness: candidate, lastVerifiedAt: 2026-02-25, featured: true, and names docs/audits/migrations/binary-orbits-parity.md as its evidence. apps/site/src/lib/readiness.ts:50-54 renders 'candidate' as the badge 'near-ready' with ariaLabel 'Readiness: candidate -- ready to assign, pending final review'. The cited audit's own section 7 reads: 'Current recommendation: stay experimental until full app/site gates pass with this upgrade (build, site e2e), and manual pedagogy QA confirms prediction-gate pacing in class use.' The audit is also stale against the code in three checkable ways: it says the mass-ratio lower bound was expanded 'from 0.1 to 0.01' (actual MASS_RATIO_MIN = 0.001, logic.ts:18), it says the prediction gate freezes readouts until reveal (removed - see the dead isPredictionLocked), and it says the energy view draws '|U| and marker for E' (drawEnergyView draws signed U and a signed E bar, main.ts:964-965).
findings.scenario: An instructor filtering Explore by readiness sees 'near-ready / ready to assign, pending final review' on a featured card and assigns the demo. Their class then meets a Spectrum view that shows nothing, an Energy view with five unlabelled bars, a dead 'Show angular frequency' checkbox, and readouts printing -0.000 on a one-click preset. The badge, not the demo, is what failed them.
findings.fix: Set readiness: experimental and content_verified: false in apps/site/src/content/demos/binary-orbits.md until the P0/P1 items here are closed, and rewrite readinessReason to name the real blockers (spectrum view shows no visible shift; energy bar labels off-canvas; omega toggle inert) instead of only the phone-width issue. Refresh docs/audits/migrations/binary-orbits-parity.md to the current code and re-date it. Promote to candidate only once the spectrum view, the energy labels, the omega control and the sightline sign are fixed and covered by tests.

findings.title: bodyPositions tests only sample phase 0 and pi, where sin(phase)=0, leaving the orbit sense untested
findings.evidence: The whole bodyPositions suite is two cases: 'at phase=0, bodies are on the x-axis' expects x1=150, y1=200, x2=230, y2=200 (logic.test.ts:427-433) and 'at phase=pi, bodies swap sides' expects x1=250, y1=200, x2=170, y2=200 (logic.test.ts:435-441). Both have sin(phase)=0, so both y assertions reduce to y = cy and the sin terms in logic.ts:594-596 are multiplied by zero. Flipping y1 to cy + r1px*sin and y2 to cy - r2px*sin - which reverses the drawn orbit from clockwise to counter-clockwise and therefore inverts the position-to-RV-phase relationship the demo teaches - leaves both tests green. No test anywhere ties a drawn position to a radial-velocity sign. This is the exact failure mode CLAUDE.md records ('a waxing/waning swap passed because tests checked only full and new moon').
