findings.scenario: Any future edit to the canvas y convention - the kind of edit the repo has already been bitten by - silently reverses the orbit direction and the redshift/blueshift mapping with a fully green suite, because the only two sample points are the two where the sign cannot be observed.
findings.fix: Add asymmetric cases to the bodyPositions suite: at phase = pi/2 assert y1 < cy and y2 > cy (and the reverse at 3pi/2), and assert x1 and x2 straddle cx at phase = pi/4. Then add the cross-check that currently has no test at all: for phase = pi/2, assert sign(bodyPositions(...).x1 - cx increasing) agrees with sign(BinaryOrbitModel.radialVelocityAtPhase({...}).rv1KmPerS) under whichever observer convention the fixed drawing adopts.

findings.title: Plot domain 10 nm-1e6 nm excludes the CMB peak the code comment claims it includes; 86% of the x-axis is blank on that preset
findings.evidence: logic.ts:49-52 `/** Wide enough to show peaks for both CMB (2.725 K) and hot stars. */ return { minNm: 10, maxNm: 1e6 };`. Recomputed lambda_peak(2.725 K) = 0.2898/2.725 cm = 1.0635e6 nm, 6.3% beyond maxNm. The repo's own test hard-codes that number: logic.test.ts:269 `formatWavelengthReadout(1063486)`. With the hard-coded 6-decade log window (main.ts:227 `minLog = maxLog - 6`) I counted the visible curve points: 72/500 for the CMB (14% of the x-range, spanning 1.94e5-1.00e6 nm, hugging the right edge) and 159/500 for T=1e6 K (32%, hugging the left edge), against 260/500 for every stellar preset. docs/reviews/blackbody-radiation.md:64 logged this on 2026-02-07, called it "cosmetic", and concluded "The current trade-off is reasonable" - and its claim that the marker "is not rendered" is wrong (see the marker finding: it is drawn in the margin).
findings.scenario: An instructor demonstrating that the CMB is a 2.725 K blackbody clicks the CMB preset and gets a short rising stub in the rightmost seventh of an otherwise empty plot, with the peak itself off the chart and a dashed peak line outside the axes - the one preset that makes the Planck curve a cosmology result is the one that cannot show its peak.
findings.fix: In apps/demos/src/demos/blackbody-radiation/logic.ts, make the domain a function of temperature instead of a constant: `wavelengthDomainNm(temperatureK)` returning about [lambda_peak/30, lambda_peak*30] snapped to decade bounds, which keeps the peak centred for every preset from 2.725 K to 1e6 K and keeps the 6-decade window populated. Pass `state.temperatureK` at main.ts:163 and update the X_TICKS_NM list (main.ts:142) to be derived from the returned domain rather than fixed.

findings.title: Stellar spectral class and colour name are assigned to non-stellar presets: the Earth and the CMB read "L+", the 1e6 K neutron star reads "O - Blue"
findings.evidence: blackbodyRadiationModel.ts:110-123 `spectralClassLetter` is a pure temperature ladder with no domain gate: `if (temperatureK >= 30000) return "O"` ... `return "L+"`. index.html:218 renders it unconditionally as ` - `. Traced for the shipped presets (index.html:64-70): 1000000 K -> "O" (an O star is 30000-50000 K) with colorName "Blue"; 288 K (Earth) -> "L+"; 310 K (Human) -> "L+"; 2.725 K (CMB) -> "L+". Neither function has any test (blackbodyRadiationModel.test.ts has 5 tests, none touching colorName or spectralClassLetter).
findings.scenario: A student clicks "Earth" and the readout under the spectrum says "L+ - Infrared (invisible)", then clicks "CMB" and gets the same spectral class for the cosmic microwave background, then clicks "Neutron Star" and reads "O - Blue" for a 10^6 K object. They leave believing the MK spectral sequence is a thermometer that applies to planets and to the CMB.
findings.fix: Add a `kind` field to the preset buttons in index.html (`data-kind="star"` vs `"thermal"`) and in main.ts:474-475 render the spectral class only for `kind="star"` within 2400-50000 K, showing an em-dash with the label "not a stellar spectrum" otherwise. Alternatively gate inside blackbodyRadiationModel.ts:110 by returning `null` outside 2400-50000 K and have main.ts render the em-dash; either way add value tests for both functions at the class boundaries and at 288 K, 2.725 K and 1e6 K.

findings.title: Star colour swatch is non-monotonic in temperature: the green channel drops 250 -> 180 at exactly 4000 K, so heating the star through 4000 K makes it look redder
findings.evidence: blackbodyRadiationModel.ts:76-82: the `temperatureK < 4000` branch gives `g = (T-1000)/12` (so g=250 at 3999 K) and the `< 6500` branch gives `g = 180 + (T-4000)/35` (so g=180 at 4000 K). Recomputed swatch RGB: 3000 K ->(255,167,0); 3500 K ->(255,208,0); 3900 K ->(255,242,0); 3999 K ->(255,250,0); 4000 K ->(255,180,0); 5772 K ->(255,231,222). So a 3900 K star renders essentially pure yellow, hotter than it, 4000 K renders orange, and the function is discontinuous by 70/255 in green. colorName (line 97) meanwhile calls 3000-3500 K "Deep Red" while the swatch there is amber (255,167,0) - swatch and label disagree.
findings.scenario: A student drags the temperature slider slowly upward to test "hotter means bluer". Between 3900 K and 4000 K the swatch visibly jumps from yellow back to orange, and a 3900 K star appears more yellow than the 5772 K Sun. The exhibit .md lists "Red stars are hotter than blue stars" as the misconception to break; the swatch supplies a counter-example in the student's own hands.
findings.fix: Replace the piecewise RGB ladder in packages/physics/src/blackbodyRadiationModel.ts:63-96 with a monotonic chromaticity mapping (integrate the Planck curve against CIE 1931 x-bar/y-bar/z-bar, convert to sRGB, normalise to constant luminance) or, if that is too heavy for the teaching layer, with a monotone interpolation over a fixed table of published blackbody sRGB values at 500 K steps from 1000-40000 K. Either way the coefficients and the table are a scientific choice that needs Anna's approval before it lands. Add a test asserting the hue angle decreases monotonically in T across 2000-20000 K and that colorName agrees with the swatch at each boundary.

findings.title: Temperature readout prints "1e+6 K" for the Neutron Star preset and "3 K" for the 2.725 K CMB
findings.evidence: logic.ts:40-45 `formatNumber`: `if (abs >= 1e6 || abs < 1e-3) return value.toExponential(Math.max(0, digits - 1))`, else `value.toFixed(digits)`. main.ts:462 calls `formatNumber(tempK, 0)`. Recomputed: formatNumber(1e6, 0) = "1e+6" -> tempValue renders "1e+6 K"; formatNumber(2.725, 0) = "3" -> "3 K". The same string also goes into `aria-valuenow` (main.ts:460), the export "Temperature T (K)" (main.ts:492) and the Station Mode snapshot row (main.ts:601). CLAUDE.md: "Powers of ten as $10^n$; no `e` notation in teaching-facing copy." apps/site/tests/blackbody-radiation.spec.ts:126-128 pins the defect: "// Display rounds to 0 decimal places: 2.725 -> \"3 K\"" then `expect(text).toContain("3")`. The L/L_sun readout has the same route: formatNumber(9.01e8, 3) = "9.01e+8".
findings.scenario: A student clicks the CMB preset and records "3 K" in a Station Mode row and in the copied CSV, losing the three significant figures that make 2.725 K the measured CMB temperature; another clicks Neutron Star and sees a temperature written in forbidden e-notation as "1e+6 K".
findings.fix: In apps/demos/src/demos/blackbody-radiation/logic.ts, add a dedicated `formatTemperatureK(T)` that returns significant-figure-aware fixed-point below 1e5 K (so 2.725 -> "2.725") and a KaTeX power-of-ten string above it (so 1e6 -> `$10^{6}$`, rendered by renderMath from @cosmic/runtime), and use it at main.ts:462/492/601 instead of formatNumber(tempK, 0). Then rewrite the e2e assertion at apps/site/tests/blackbody-radiation.spec.ts:124-132 to expect "2.725" rather than documenting the rounding.

findings.title: Unicode mu reaches the readout DOM and the canvas labels via a \u escape that the math validator cannot see
findings.evidence: logic.ts:112, 113, 132, 133 all emit `μm`, e.g. line 132 `return { value: (nm / 1e3).toFixed(0), unit: "μm" };`. main.ts:470-472 writes that string straight into `peakUnitEl.textContent`, i.e. into the reader-visible `.cp-readout__unit` span - not a canvas exemption. scripts/validate-math-formatting.mjs:33 forbids exactly this glyph (`FORBIDDEN_UNICODE_MATH = /[...µμ...]/u`) and line 29 does include `.ts`, but it matches against the raw source text, so the escape passes. CLAUDE.md states this trap explicitly: "and no `\uXXXX` escapes that produce them (the validator cannot see escapes)". Traced trigger: lambda_peak >= 1000 nm whenever T <= 2898 K, so the Human (310 K), Earth (288 K) and Brown Dwarf (250 K) presets all render a Unicode mu. logic.test.ts:227, 231, 265 assert the escape, so the tests lock the violation in.
findings.scenario: A student clicks "Earth": the peak-wavelength readout renders "10" + a raw Unicode mu glyph, which inherits whatever text-transform the surrounding CSS applies - the exact failure mode CLAUDE.md records for 2026-09-05, when an inherited uppercase turned mean molecular weight mu into "M" across 14 demos with every test green.
findings.fix: In apps/demos/src/demos/blackbody-radiation/logic.ts, return the unit as LaTeX (`"$\\mu$m"`) from formatWavelengthReadout and render it through renderMath() from @cosmic/runtime at main.ts:472; keep formatWavelengthLabel (canvas-only, main.ts:334/360) but switch it to the ASCII form "um" per the canvas exemption. Update logic.test.ts:227/231/265 to assert the new strings, and add a check to scripts/validate-math-formatting.mjs that flags `\\u03bc`-style escapes in source as well as literal glyphs.

findings.title: Temperature slider announces its 0-1000 track position, not a temperature: aria-valuenow conflicts with the native value and no aria-valuetext is set
findings.evidence: index.html:23-32 declares `<input id="tempSlider" type="range" min="0" max="1000" step="1" value="500">`, so the native value is a track index (logSliderToValue(500, 2.725, 1e6) = 1650 K, i.e. the attribute value does not even correspond to the 5778 K initial state at main.ts:93). main.ts:458-460 then sets `aria-valuemin="2.725"`, `aria-valuemax="1000000"` and `aria-valuenow` to the temperature - values that contradict the host-language min/max/value, which take precedence in HTML-AAM, and no `aria-valuetext` is set anywhere in this demo. The repo's own pattern is the opposite: moon-phases/main.ts:458, em-spectrum/main.ts:250 and cluster-census/main.ts:975-982 all use `setAttribute("aria-valuetext", ...)`, and cluster-census/design-contracts.test.ts:255 enforces it ("sets aria-valuetext on every slider whose raw value is not its meaning").
findings.scenario: A screen-reader user arrows the temperature slider and hears "501, 502" (or a percentage) instead of "5850 kelvin" - the demo's single primary control conveys no physical quantity at all, and the conflicting aria-valuemin/max/now make the announced range nondeterministic across AT.
findings.fix: In apps/demos/src/demos/blackbody-radiation/main.ts, delete the three setAttribute calls at lines 458-460 and replace them with `tempSlider.setAttribute("aria-valuetext", "" + formatTemperatureK(tempK) + " kelvin")`, matching moon-phases and em-spectrum. Fix index.html:29 to omit the misleading `value="500"` (render() sets the position) and extend the cluster-census aria-valuetext contract test to this demo's design-contracts.test.ts.

findings.title: No readout change is ever announced and the spectrum canvas has a static aria-label, so a screen-reader user gets no data from the demo
findings.evidence: main.ts:471-476 writes peak wavelength, luminosity ratio, spectral class, colour name and swatch colour straight to `textContent` on elements inside `<div class="cp-readout-strip cp-demo__readouts" aria-label="Readouts">` (index.html:214) - that container has no `role="status"`, no `aria-live` and no `aria-atomic`. The only live region in the demo, `#status` (index.html:113), is written by exactly two code paths: the clipboard handler (main.ts:640-648) and the reduced-motion notice (main.ts:652). The canvas label (index.html:130) is the fixed string "Blackbody spectrum curve showing relative intensity versus wavelength" and is never updated with T or lambda_peak. apps/site/tests/accessibility.spec.ts:49-54 only asserts that `#status` carries role/aria-live - never that anything is announced on change.
findings.scenario: A blind student moves the temperature slider from the Sun to an M dwarf. Nothing is announced: the readout spans change silently, the canvas label still says the same sentence it said at load, and the only live region stays empty. The entire quantitative content of the instrument is unavailable to them.
findings.fix: In apps/demos/src/demos/blackbody-radiation/main.ts render() (after line 476), call `setLiveRegionText(status, ...)` with a debounced one-line summary ("5772 kelvin, peak 502 nanometres, class G") - debounced outside the draw path, never once per frame - and update the canvas `aria-label` with the same summary so the role=img element describes the current state. Add an e2e assertion in apps/site/tests/blackbody-radiation.spec.ts that #status text changes after a slider input.

findings.title: Preset buttons' aria-pressed is hardcoded "false" and never updated; the design contract blesses the stale attribute
findings.evidence: index.html:55-70 gives all 13 preset buttons `aria-pressed="false"`. main.ts:534-542 is the complete preset handler - it reads `data-temp-k`, sets `state.temperatureK` and calls `render()`, and render() (main.ts:451-479) touches no preset attribute. Compare main.ts:510-514, which does maintain aria-pressed for the Log/Linear chips. So every preset permanently reports "not pressed". design-contracts.test.ts:229-236 asserts only that each cp-chip button `.includes("aria-pressed")` in the static HTML, which is true by construction, and the e2e spec tests aria-pressed only for #scaleLog/#scaleLinear (blackbody-radiation.spec.ts:136-146).
findings.scenario: A screen-reader user tabs the preset row after clicking "Sun": every button including Sun is announced "not pressed", so there is no way to tell which preset is active, and sighted users get no selected state either (no class is toggled). The demo offers 13 presets and no indication of which one you are looking at.
findings.fix: In apps/demos/src/demos/blackbody-radiation/main.ts, add a `syncPresets()` that sets `aria-pressed` to `String(Math.abs(Number(btn.dataset.tempK) - state.temperatureK) < 1e-6)` plus a `cp-chip--active` class, and call it from render() so slider moves also clear the pressed preset. Then strengthen design-contracts.test.ts:229-236 to require a `setAttribute("aria-pressed"` call in main.ts for preset buttons, not just the attribute's presence in HTML.

findings.title: No test constrains the value of the Planck function - a wrong exponent, a dropped factor of 2 or a missing -1 would all stay green
findings.evidence: blackbodyRadiationModel.test.ts has 5 tests. The only two that touch `planckSpectralRadianceCgs` are line 20-21 (`wavelengthCm: -1` and `temperatureK: -1` both expect 0) and line 25-29 (`wavelengthCm: 1e-12` expects 0 via the exponent>700 clip). There is no assertion on any finite return value, and no test that the sampled maximum of the Planck curve coincides with `wienPeakNm` - the single cheapest cross-check available. I verified by independent recomputation that the implementation is in fact correct (1.20999e14 vs 1.20753e14 erg/s/cm^2/sr/cm at 300 nm, 5772 K, a 0.2% constants-only difference), so the test suite is not catching a live bug - it simply cannot catch one.
findings.scenario: Someone refactors blackbodyRadiationModel.ts:40 from `Math.pow(wavelengthCm, 5)` to `, 4)` (a plausible slip, since the Rayleigh-Jeans tail in the Understand tab is written with lambda^4). Every test stays green, the curve shape changes, the plotted peak moves by a factor of 1.25 in lambda, and the readout - which comes from Wien, not from Planck - still agrees with the textbook, so nothing flags it.
findings.fix: Add value tests to packages/physics/src/blackbodyRadiationModel.test.ts at asymmetric points computed from exact constants, with a 0.5% tolerance that covers the model's 4-sig-fig constants: B_lambda(300 nm, 5772 K) = 1.208e14, B_lambda(1200 nm, 3000 K) = 8.961e12, B_lambda(0.05 cm, 2.725 K) = 9.886e-4 (erg s^-1 cm^-2 sr^-1 cm^-1). Add a test that argmax over a dense log grid of planckSpectralRadianceCgs agrees with wienPeakNm to within one grid spacing, and a Rayleigh-Jeans limit test that B_lambda -> 2ckT/lambda^4 within 1% at hc/(lambda k T) < 0.01.

findings.title: The colour test asserts only the bounds clampByte already guarantees, and colorName / spectralClassLetter have no tests at all
findings.evidence: blackbodyRadiationModel.test.ts:31-39 is the entire colour coverage: it calls `temperatureToRgbApprox({temperatureK: 5778})` and asserts each channel is `>= 0` and `<= 255`. Those bounds are produced unconditionally by `clampByte` (blackbodyRadiationModel.ts:19-21), so the assertion holds for literally any mapping - including the 4000 K green discontinuity I measured (250 -> 180). Grepping the file for `colorName` and `spectralClassLetter` returns nothing: the two functions that print "O - Blue" for a neutron star and "L+" for the CMB are untested. The e2e colour test (blackbody-radiation.spec.ts:100-114) only asserts that two different slider positions give two different colours.
findings.scenario: The reviewer or a future agent reads "produces bounded RGB values for reasonable temperatures" as colour-mapping coverage and ships the non-monotonic swatch and the unlabelled-domain spectral class - which is exactly what happened. This is the repo's documented failure mode (memory: five green tests pinned a bug instead of catching it).
findings.fix: Replace the bounds test in packages/physics/src/blackbodyRadiationModel.test.ts:31-39 with behavioural assertions: continuity (|rgb(T+1) - rgb(T)| <= 3 per channel across 1000-40000 K in 1 K steps near each branch boundary), monotonic blue/red ratio in T, and agreement between the swatch hue and colorName at every colorName boundary. Add boundary tests for spectralClassLetter at 2400/3700/5200/6000/7500/10000/30000 K and assert the non-stellar gate (288 K, 2.725 K, 1e6 K) once that gate exists.

findings.title: Learning goal 2 has no supporting readout: the Stefan-Boltzmann flux function is exported but never called by any demo
findings.evidence: apps/site/src/content/demos/blackbody-radiation.md:16 states the goal "Use Stefan-Boltzmann scaling to separate surface flux from total emitted power trends." Grepping the repo for `stefanBoltzmannFluxCgs` returns exactly three hits: its definition (blackbodyRadiationModel.ts:49), its export (line 128), and its own negative-input guard test (blackbodyRadiationModel.test.ts:22). No demo, site page or runtime module calls it. The demo exposes no flux readout at all (index.html:222-234 has exactly two readouts: peak wavelength and the mislabeled luminosity ratio), so the only T^4 surface a student can see is the number that is itself mislabeled.
findings.scenario: An instructor assigns the exhibit expecting students to distinguish surface flux F = sigma T^4 from total power L = 4 pi R^2 sigma T^4. The demo never shows F, so the assignment cannot be completed from the instrument; the student's only T^4 number is labeled L/L_sun, which teaches the opposite of the stated goal.
findings.fix: Add a third readout to apps/demos/src/demos/blackbody-radiation/index.html driven by `BlackbodyRadiationModel.stefanBoltzmannFluxCgs`, labeled `Surface flux $F$` with the unit span `erg s$^{-1}$ cm$^{-2}$`, wired in main.ts render() beside the existing two - which also makes the flux-versus-luminosity distinction in the Understand tab (index.html:176-187) demonstrable rather than merely asserted. Either that, or remove learning goal 2 from blackbody-radiation.md:16.

findings.title: content_verified: true and a 2026-02-02 lastVerifiedAt overclaim, given a mislabeled headline readout and a peak marker drawn outside the axes
findings.evidence: blackbody-radiation.md:4 `content_verified: true` and line 13 `lastVerifiedAt: "2026-02-02"`, while line 10-11 carry `readiness: experimental` and `readinessReason: "Thermal-spectrum core is stable ... full launch-gate and parity signoff remain pending."` The verification date precedes both the 2026-02-07 physics review (docs/reviews/blackbody-radiation.md) and the 2026-09-10 UI changes (git mtimes on index.html, main.ts, style.css). Against that claim stand the mislabeled L/L_sun readout (off by up to 9 orders of magnitude on a shipped preset), the off-axes peak marker, and stellar spectral classes printed for the Earth and the CMB. The readiness pair itself is defensible: apps/site/src/lib/readiness.ts:44-48 defines experimental as "usable, still being revised" and the parity audit (docs/audits/migrations/blackbody-radiation-parity.md:25) independently recommends staying there.
findings.scenario: An instructor filtering the Explore page trusts `content_verified: true` to mean the reader-visible numbers and labels have been checked, assigns the demo for a thermal-radiation lab, and their students record a White Dwarf at 352 L_sun.
findings.fix: Set `content_verified: false` in apps/site/src/content/demos/blackbody-radiation.md:4 and clear `lastVerifiedAt` until the L/L_sun label, the peak-marker domain guard and the spectral-class gate are fixed; keep `readiness: experimental` and `status: draft` as they are. Recommended level on current evidence: experimental. It is a defensible candidate once the two P0s plus the spectral-class gate, the colour monotonicity and the aria-valuetext fix land.

findings.title: Public exhibit copy and the clipboard export both say there is no post-main-sequence evolution, while the demo draws and tallies a giant branch
findings.evidence: cluster-census.md:48 model_notes: "There is no post-main-sequence evolution: a star sits at its zero-age point until its lifetime elapses, then becomes a remnant. The turnoff is therefore an edge, not the hook a real cluster shows." The identical claim is in the exported payload at main.ts:1381. But starClusterModel.ts:247 calls `postMainSequenceTrack`, main.ts:676-688 draws giants with a halo, index.html:303-306 shows a live `giantCount` tally, and index.html:412-417 says the opposite: "The giant branch is schematic. Two of its three timescales are real". docs/reviews/cluster-census.md:135 dates the giant branch to 2026-09-04 and the .md's own `lastVerifiedAt` is "2026-09-04" with `content_verified: true`. Line 47 of the same file is stale the other way: "Below 0.1 Msun ... Those stars appear in the cluster and the histogram but carry no HR point" -- main.ts:240 sets CENSUS_MIN_MASS_MSUN = 0.1, so no such star is ever drawn and `outsideModelCount` is structurally always 0.
findings.scenario: An instructor reads the exhibit page before class, tells students the diagram shows only the zero-age main sequence with a hard edge at the turnoff, then opens the demo at 1 Gyr and a giant branch is on screen. A student who copies results to the clipboard gets a note asserting the giant branch they are looking at does not exist.
findings.fix: Replace cluster-census.md:48 with the index.html:412-417 wording (real Hurley timescales, textbook shape, positions good to a factor of a few), correct line 47 to say the draw starts at the 0.1 Msun ZAMS floor, apply the same correction to main.ts:1380-1381, and set `content_verified: false` with a fresh `lastVerifiedAt` until the two notes are re-checked.

findings.title: Giant-branch tip luminosity jumps 1.38 dex across M = 2.000 Msun, splitting the drawn branch into two clumps
findings.evidence: Lines 390-393: `massMsun < DEGENERATE_CORE_MAX_MSUN ? Math.max(RGB_TIP_LSUN, baseLuminosityLsun) : baseLuminosityLsun * 3` with RGB_TIP_LSUN = 2500 and DEGENERATE_CORE_MAX_MSUN = 2. I evaluated the Tout Z=0.02 polynomials across the boundary: L_zams(1.999) = 15.858 Lsun so L_base = 34.89 and L_tip = 2500.00 (log 3.398); L_zams(2.000) = 15.891 so L_base = 34.96 and L_tip = 104.88 (log 2.021). A 0.001 Msun change moves the tip by a factor of 23.8. From the Hurley fits the post-MS mass window at a given age is {M : t_MS(M) <= age < 1.15 t_BGB(M)}; at 1250 Myr that is M in [1.95, 2.05], which straddles 2.000 (t_MS(2.0) = 1164 Myr, t_tot(2.0) = 1350 Myr, t_tot(2.1) = 1172 Myr). So for ages 1.16-1.35 Gyr the post-MS population sits on both sides of the discontinuity. The Understand tab (index.html:416) promises "positions are good to a factor of a few"; a factor of 24 is not that.
findings.scenario: At 20,000 stars and an age near 1.25 Gyr, roughly 20 giants are drawn and they separate into two clumps 1.4 dex apart in luminosity with no stars between them. A student reads this as real structure -- a horizontal branch, or two populations -- when it is a branch in the code. Nothing on screen distinguishes it from the real RGB-tip feature the copy asks them to notice.
findings.fix: In packages/physics/src/stellarLifetimeModel.ts make the tip luminosity continuous in mass: blend between the degenerate-core tip (max(RGB_TIP_LSUN, L_base)) and the non-degenerate 3*L_base over a transition band (e.g. 1.8-2.2 Msun) instead of switching at a point. This is a scientific-assumption change (the band width and blend form) and needs approval, so propose it rather than pick one.

findings.title: A preset click while "Derive alpha from the environment" is pressed overrides the derived slope, making the demo assert false physics about the shown environment
findings.evidence: The preset handler (main.ts:1318-1330) sets `state.alphaHigh = preset.alphaHigh` (line 1323, all three presets carry 2.3) but never touches `state.deriveSlope` and never calls `applyDerivedSlope()`. Tracing `update()` afterwards: `syncChips()` (965-966) keeps `deriveToggle aria-pressed="true"` and `derivePanel.hidden = false`; `renderReadouts()` (939-947) writes `slopeValue` = `"2.30 - " + slopeVerdict(2.3, 2.3)` which is "Canonical slope: this environment is nothing special." (logic.ts:448), and pushes the slider to 230; `fehValue` and `meclValue` still display the untouched environment. With the sliders at their extremes ([Fe/H] = -2.00, log M_ecl = 6.00) `highMassSlopeFromEnvironment` returns x = 0.4961, alpha3 = 1.7366 -- I recomputed it -- so the correct statement is "Top-heavy". `reset` (1333-1337) does restore deriveSlope via DEFAULTS; the presets do not.
findings.scenario: A student opens the derive panel, drags to a metal-poor 10^6 Msun environment, watches the slope fall to 1.74 and the histogram's tail fatten -- the demo's headline pedagogical payoff -- then clicks "Globular" to see it in a real cluster. The panel still shows [Fe/H] = -2.00 and 1,000,000 solar masses, the toggle still reads pressed, and the slope readout now says the environment is nothing special at alpha = 2.30. The student concludes the environment effect was an artifact.
findings.fix: In apps/demos/src/demos/cluster-census/main.ts, in the preset click handler, either set `state.deriveSlope = false` before assigning `state.alphaHigh` (presets specify a slope, so they own it), or call `applyDerivedSlope()` after the assignment so the environment keeps precedence. The first is more honest about what a preset is; pick it and state the choice. Add an e2e case: click deriveToggle, set fehSlider to -200 and meclSlider to 600, click the globular preset, assert #slopeValue still contains /top-heavy/i.

findings.title: "About 80 percent of any cluster sits below 1 Msun" is stated twice; the demo's own laws give 88.4 and 89.0 percent
findings.evidence: index.html:374 "Around 80 percent of a cluster sits below $1\,M_\odot$" and index.html:460 "about 80 percent of any cluster sits below $1\,M_\odot$". Both are presented as what the histogram shows. Over the demo's actual sampling range [CENSUS_MIN_MASS_MSUN, IMF_MAX_MSUN] = [0.1, 150] at the default alpha = 2.3 I computed the number fraction below 1 Msun two independent ways: numeric integration of the Maschberger Eq. 5 pdf gives 0.88400, and the repo's own `maschbergerMassFraction` primitive gives 0.88400. The Kroupa law over the same range gives 0.89007. Over the full physical range [0.08, 150] they are 0.89715 and 0.90287. There is no setting in the demo at which 80 percent is the answer unless the user flattens the slope (alpha = 1.5 gives 0.564).
findings.scenario: The "What to notice" accordion is open by default. A student is told to notice that about 80 percent of the cluster is below 1 Msun, counts the bars (or reads the tally), and gets roughly 88 percent -- an 8-point discrepancy on a number the exercise asks them to verify against the picture. The misconceptions list in the exhibit .md already flags 'a histogram and the law should match exactly', so a student who finds the mismatch may blame sampling noise rather than the copy.
findings.fix: In apps/demos/src/demos/cluster-census/index.html change both occurrences (lines 374 and 460) to "roughly nine stars in ten" or "about 88 percent (0.1-1 Msun, canonical slope)". Keeping it qualitative is safest because the exact number moves with the slope slider.

findings.title: The 3-D scale bar measures distance from the origin, not to the camera target, so panning mis-scales the panel's only size reference
findings.evidence: clusterScene.ts:393-395: `const distance = perspective.position.length(); const visibleHeight = 2 * distance * Math.tan(...); return visibleHeight / height;` -- the comment one line above claims "At the cluster centre, which is what the scale bar is measuring." But `controls.screenSpacePanning = true` (line 176) and OrbitControls panning translates `object.position` AND `controls.target` by the same vector, so |position| changes while |position - target| does not. The correct expression is used 80 lines earlier for the shader depth cue: line 314, `perspective.position.distanceTo(controls.target)`. The resulting value is published as `data-pc-per-pixel` (main.ts:481) and drives `niceScaleLength` and the "N pc" label (main.ts:483-509). With the default framing distance = 3.2 * plotRadiusPc, a pan of one plot radius changes |position| by up to one plot radius, a +/-31 percent error in the bar.
findings.scenario: A student switches to 3D, drags with the right button to bring the cluster core to one side, and reads the scale bar as "2 pc". The bar is then up to 31 percent wrong, and it changes label as they pan without the zoom changing. They use it to estimate the cluster's physical size. The e2e test at cluster-census.spec.ts:401 exercises zoom and reset but never pans, so nothing catches it.
findings.fix: In apps/demos/src/demos/cluster-census/clusterScene.ts:393 replace `perspective.position.length()` with `perspective.position.distanceTo(controls.target)`. Add an e2e case that pans in 3D (right-button drag) and asserts data-pc-per-pixel is unchanged to within a percent.

findings.title: The design-system contract test certifying "all physics from @cosmic/physics" never inspects main.ts, where the inline mass-temperature relation lives
findings.evidence: Lines 285-290: `it("takes all physics from @cosmic/physics rather than inlining it", () => { expect(mainTs).toContain('from "@cosmic/physics"'); expect(mainTs).toContain("sampleStarCluster"); expect(logicTs).not.toMatch(/maschbergerPrimitive|HURLEY_A|zamsLuminosity/); });` -- the only negative assertion is against logic.ts and names three identifiers that were never going to appear there. main.ts:908-910 holds `function massToApproxTemperatureK(massMsun: number): number { return 5772 * massMsun ** 0.55; }`, an inline mass-Teff relation used to tint every histogram bar. The same file-grep pattern weakens the neighbouring tests: line 36 asserts the string "perspective.position.distanceTo(controls.target)" is present in clusterScene.ts and passes while line 393 of that same file uses the wrong expression (see the scale-bar finding). Lines 199-207 forbid colour literals in style.css only, while main.ts:506 and 1046 hold `rgba(...)` literals.
findings.scenario: A reviewer runs the demo contract suite, sees 'takes all physics from @cosmic/physics' green, and ships an inline fitted relation plus hardcoded colours. The suite's green state is evidence about three identifier strings, not about the invariant it names, so every future inline equation in main.ts passes too.
findings.fix: In apps/demos/src/demos/cluster-census/design-contracts.test.ts:285 add a negative assertion against mainTs for fitted-relation shapes (e.g. a numeric literal raised to a fractional power, or the specific constants 5772 and 0.55 outside a comment), and extend the colour-literal assertions at lines 199-207 to mainTs and logicTs. The durable fix is to widen `colorLiteralExts` in scripts/validate-invariants.mjs:104 to include ".ts" so the gate, not a per-demo test, owns it.

findings.title: The derived-slope verdict is a full sentence in a white-space: nowrap grid cell, overflowing a 360px sidebar
findings.evidence: main.ts:939-941 writes into #slopeValue: `${state.alphaHigh.toFixed(2)} - ${slopeVerdict(...)}`, i.e. "1.74 - Top-heavy: markedly more massive stars than a canonical cluster." (70 characters) or "2.30 - Canonical slope: this environment is nothing special." (59 characters). index.html:53 puts #slopeValue as the sole child of `<span class="control__value">`. Tracing the cascade: packages/theme/styles/components/control.css:36-37 sets `grid-template-columns: minmax(0, 1fr) auto` and lines 48-55 set `.control__value { justify-self: end; white-space: nowrap; }`. A nowrap inline in an auto track has min-content width equal to its full rendered width, so the track cannot shrink; the label track is minmax(0,1fr) and collapses to 0. The sidebar is `clamp(280px, 25vw, 360px)` (demo-shell.css:44) less panel padding, so about 310-330px usable, and `.cp-demo__controls .cp-panel-body` is `overflow: auto` (demo-shell.css:145-149). At the demo's 0.9rem control font a 70-character proportional sentence is roughly 500-560px, so the panel body gains a horizontal scrollbar roughly 200px wide.
findings.scenario: A student opens the derive panel. Every slider in the controls panel is now laid out at the width of that one sentence, so the right half of the N, slope, age, [Fe/H] and M_ecl sliders is off-screen and reachable only by scrolling the sidebar sideways. The layout-budget e2e cases (cluster-census.spec.ts:513-520) measure `body.scrollHeight - body.clientHeight`, which is vertical only, and cluster-census is not in reflow.spec.ts's PLAY_ROUTES (line 55 lists only conservation-laws), so neither the desktop nor the 320px WCAG 1.4.10 check sees it.
findings.fix: Move the verdict out of the value cell: in apps/demos/src/demos/cluster-census/index.html give the slope control a sibling `.control__hint` (control.css:67-73 already gives those full width and `white-space: normal`) and in main.ts:939-941 write only `state.alphaHigh.toFixed(2)` into #slopeValue and the verdict sentence into the hint. Then add play/cluster-census/ to PLAY_ROUTES in apps/site/tests/reflow.spec.ts with the derive panel open.

findings.title: Speed is printed in km/s beside a label that defines K = v^2/2 in AU^2/yr^2, so the stated relation fails by 22.47x
findings.evidence:
index.html:165-168 renders `
Speed $v$
` with `km/s`, and main.ts:548 sets it from `TwoBodyAnalytic.speedKmPerSFromAuPerYr(vAuYr)`. index.html:121 labels the kinetic readout `Kinetic ${K = v^2/2}$` with unit AU$^2$/yr$^2$. I recomputed the default state (M=1, r0=1, f=1): v = 6.28319 AU/yr = 29.785 km/s, K = v^2/2 = 19.7392 AU^2/yr^2. A student who squares the printed speed gets 29.785^2/2 = 443.6, which is 22.47x the printed K - exactly (4.7405 km/s per AU/yr)^2. Same at the Elliptical preset: v = 22.339 km/s, (22.339)^2/2 = 249.5 vs K = 11.1033 printed.
findings.scenario: A student on the default circular orbit reads v = 29.785 km/s and K = 19.7392 AU^2/yr^2, applies the relation the label states, gets 443.6, and concludes the demo (or their own arithmetic) is broken. The one quantity the instrument asks them to square is the only one not in the demo's own AU/yr/Msun system.
findings.fix: In index.html:165-172 show $v$ in AU/yr as the primary readout (unit span `AU/yr`, value from `vAuYr` directly in main.ts:548) and add km/s as a secondary line or a parenthetical second readout. The project convention (CLAUDE.md units section, .agents/references/invariants.md) already names AU/yr/Msun for orbital mechanics.

findings.title: Eccentric orbits are drawn passing through the central-mass glyph, and periapsis inside R_sun is never flagged
findings.evidence: index.html:47 is `<circle id="centralMass" class="orbit__mass" cx="300" cy="300" r="10">` - a fixed 10 user-unit radius in a 600x600 viewBox, with `filter: drop-shadow(var(--cp-glow-sun))` (style.css:102-105) making it visually larger still. logic.ts:177-193 fixes the scale: for M=1, r0=1, f=0.3 the view radius is 1.50 AU so scale = 250/1.5 = 166.67 px/AU, and the glyph's 10 px radius is 0.0600 AU = 12.9 R_sun. I recomputed r_p = p/(1+e) with p = f^2 r0: f=0.3 -> r_p = 0.047120 AU = 7.85 px < 10 px; f=0.2 -> 3.40 px; f=0.1 -> 0.84 px. Separately, bisecting r_p(f) = R_sun = 0.004650 AU gives f = 0.09622, so every slider setting from 0.01 to 0.09 (speed slider min=0, step=0.01, index.html:244-252) puts periapsis physically inside the Sun while #orbitType still reads "elliptical" and #rpAu reads e.g. "0.0050251" with no comparison.
findings.scenario: A student drags the speed factor to 0.3 and presses Play. The body sweeps through the middle of the Sun disc and out the other side. The honest reading is a collision; the physics is a point-mass orbit with r_p = 0.047 AU. At f <= 0.09 the orbit really is unphysical (periapsis inside the photosphere) and the demo says nothing.
findings.fix: Two parts, both small. (1) Draw the central mass to the orbit's own scale with a stated floor, e.g. r = max(4, R_sun_AU * anim.scalePxPerAu), and say in the stage caption or Model notes that the star is drawn at a minimum size, not to scale. (2) In recomputeOrbit (main.ts:461-472) add a callout when o.rpAu < AstroConstants solar radius in AU - 'periapsis is inside the star; the point-mass model no longer applies' - beside the existing apoCaption.

findings.title: No upper bound on on-screen orbit duration: v/v_circ = 1.41, the value the copy sends students to, takes 38.5 minutes per lap with the body visible for 8.2 s
findings.evidence: logic.ts:238 `MIN_ON_SCREEN_ORBIT_SEC = 1.5` and logic.ts:245-248 `animationTimeScaleYrPerSec = Math.min(DEFAULT_SIM_YEARS_PER_SEC, characteristicYr / MIN_ON_SCREEN_ORBIT_SEC)` - a one-sided clamp that only ever slows fast orbits down; there is no cap on the slow side. I recomputed for M=1, r0=1: f=1.40 -> e=0.96, a=25 AU, T=125.0 yr, view radius 6 AU, scale stays 1/3 yr/s so one lap = 375 s and the fraction of the period inside 6 AU (from M = E - e sin E at r=6) is 1.12%, i.e. 8.45 s visible. f=1.41 -> e=0.98810, a=84.03 AU, T=770.3 yr, lap = 2311 s = 38.5 min, 8.16 s visible. The caption still reads 'Time: 1 s on screen = 4 months' (formatTimeScale(1/3)) and #timeScaleSlowed stays hidden. conservation-laws.md:25 (play_steps) says 'Drag $v/v_{\rm circ}$ from 1.41 to 1.42' and index.html:289 repeats it.
findings.scenario: A student follows play_steps step 3, drags the slider to 1.41, presses Play, watches the body leave the view after ~8 s, and then waits. Nothing happens for 38 minutes. There is no 'left the view' message for bound orbits (main.ts:447-458 only sets nuMax for e>=1), so the demo looks frozen at the exact setting the exhibit copy names.
findings.fix: Add a MAX_ON_SCREEN_ORBIT_SEC companion in logic.ts:236-248 (e.g. 30 s) so animationTimeScaleYrPerSec also returns max(characteristicYr / MAX_ON_SCREEN_ORBIT_SEC, ...) and surface it with the existing #timeScaleSlowed span (add a '(sped up so the whole orbit fits)' variant). Separately, in main.ts:420-472, when Number.isFinite(o.raAu) && o.raAu > rMaxAu, show the fraction of the period spent off view in #apoCaption, which already fires for this case.

findings.title: Both effective-potential drawings ship with no axis labels, no units and no key; the four lines are told apart by colour alone
findings.evidence: index.html:138-152 is the whole instrument plot: an `<svg id="ueffPlot" role="img" aria-label="Effective potential against distance.">` holding #ueffAllowed, #ueffZero, #ueffCurve, #ueffEps, #ueffDrop and #ueffDot, followed by two absolutely-positioned spans `$r_p$` and `$r_a$` that are both `aria-hidden="true"`. There is no x-axis title, no 'AU', no y-axis title, no 'AU$^2$/yr$^2$', no tick values and no legend. The four graphical layers are separated only by style.css:320-343: #ueffZero `var(--cp-faint)` dashed, #ueffCurve `var(--cp-energy-potential)`, #ueffEps `var(--cp-energy-total)`, #ueffDrop `var(--cp-energy-kinetic)`. index.html:63-78 (the Potential stage view) is the same, plus a `$\varepsilon$` label and minus the turning-point text in its aria-label. The readout labels right above use the project's own 3px colour swatch pattern to avoid colour-only encoding (style.css:203-221), so the plots are the outlier.
findings.scenario: A colour-blind student, or any student reading in daylight, sees a curve and three horizontal lines and cannot tell which is the total energy, which is zero and which is the radial kinetic energy - the one the exhibit's play_steps step 2 and index.html:287 ask them to watch shrink to zero. A screen-reader user gets 'Effective potential against distance' plus one sentence of turning points and no numbers at all, because the only ticks are aria-hidden.
findings.fix: In index.html:138-152 and 63-78 add an x-axis caption ('distance $r$, AU') and a y-axis caption ('energy per unit mass, AU$^2$/yr$^2$'), label the zero line '$0$' and the energy line '$\varepsilon$' in the instrument plot as the Potential view already does, and add a small inline key tying each colour to a name (reuse the .cp-readout[data-energy] swatch rule). Give #potentialSvg the same turningPointsText-bearing aria-label that main.ts:576-581 already builds for #ueffPlot.

findings.title: Two incompatible definitions of the relativistic regime: markers solve 5% divergence, regime() switches on |beta| = 0.1
findings.evidence: `regime()` classifies on absBeta alone: `if (absBeta < 0.02) non-relativistic; if (absBeta < 0.1) mildly-relativistic; else relativistic` (dopplerShiftModel.ts:238-243). But computeRegimeThresholdMarkers (logic.ts:401-430) numerically solves divergence = 5%, and formulaAppliedMode (main.ts:288) gates the silent override on `regime(...).label === "relativistic"`. I solved both boundaries: 5% divergence is crossed at beta = +0.095436 (v = +28,611 km/s, z = +0.100459) and beta = -0.105590 (v = -31,655 km/s, z = -0.100562). Recomputed divergence at the regime switch: beta = +0.1 -> 5.2506%, beta = -0.1 -> 4.7494%. So two reachable bands disagree. Red: v in (+28,611, +29,979) km/s gives divergence 5.00-5.25% while regime() still says "mildly-relativistic", so NR is kept and formulaLimitIndicator stays hidden even though the student is past the marker the caption calls the boundary. Blue: v in (-31,655, -29,979) km/s gives divergence 4.75-5.00% while regime() says "relativistic", so main.ts:288 overrides the student's NR choice and index.html:112 asserts "Non-relativistic approximation exceeds 5% here" when it is 4.75-5.00%.
findings.scenario: A student follows play_steps step 4 ("use the regime markers and divergence readout to identify where non-relativistic error exceeds 5%"), drags to z = -0.098 (v = -31,000 km/s), and reads "Non-relativistic approximation exceeds 5% here; relativistic prediction is applied" while the NR divergence readout right beside it says 4.902. The instrument contradicts itself on the exact quantity the step asks them to measure. Symmetrically, at v = +29,500 km/s they sit past the red marker with divergence 5.163% and the demo quietly keeps feeding them the NR number.
findings.fix: Make divergence the single source of truth. In packages/physics/src/dopplerShiftModel.ts:226-247 take a `thresholdPercent` (default REGIME_DIVERGENCE_THRESHOLD_PERCENT) and classify on `formulaDivergencePercent` against it rather than on hardcoded beta cuts, so regime(), the markers and the copy all derive from one number. Add a test asserting regime() flips exactly at the solved boundary velocities on both signs.

findings.title: Reader-visible copy still claims vacuum wavelengths while the catalogues are air values; DS-3 was recorded as fixed
findings.evidence: packages/physics/src/spectralLineModel.ts:12-15 is explicit: "Bohr-model transitions ... are VACUUM wavelengths. The element catalogues (elementLines) are laboratory AIR wavelengths, which differ by ~0.03% in the optical -- do not mix them without converting." Three strings describe this and they disagree. index.html:272 is correct ("empirical rest wavelengths measured in air ... hydrogen lines computed from the Bohr model are vacuum"); logic.ts:554 is correct ("Element catalogs use air wavelengths ... Bohr-model hydrogen lines are vacuum"); but index.html:438, in the Model notes accordion of the same page, says flatly "Vacuum wavelengths are used throughout." and apps/site/src/content/demos/doppler-shift.md:45 says "multi-element catalogs are empirical line lists (vacuum wavelengths, NIST teaching subset)". docs/reviews/doppler-shift.md records DS-3 as "fixed" with "Both now state air" — two of four strings were fixed, the other two were missed, and the review was closed.
findings.scenario: A student selects Na, reads lambda_0 = 589.0 nm, and is told by the Model notes that it is a vacuum wavelength. They look it up, find the vacuum value is 589.16 nm, and either lose trust in the instrument or carry a 0.16 nm systematic into any comparison with a real spectrum. At v = -110 km/s (preset 3, Barnard's Star) the true shift is 0.216 nm, so the air/vacuum confusion is comparable to the physics being measured.
findings.fix: Change index.html:438 to the sentence already used at index.html:272, and change doppler-shift.md:45 to "multi-element catalogs are empirical air wavelengths (NIST teaching subset); Bohr-model hydrogen lines are vacuum wavelengths". Then add an assertion to logic.test.ts's export-payload test that pins the air/vacuum note text, so the string cannot drift again.

findings.title: Velocity readout and slider label emit 2-significant-figure e-notation, violating the no-e-notation rule
findings.evidence: formatNumber (logic.ts:59-65) switches to `value.toExponential(digits - 1)` whenever |value| >= 1e4, and formatSigned (logic.ts:67-73) wraps it. The velocity readout and the slider's own label both call `formatSigned(state.velocityKmS, 2)` (main.ts:936, main.ts:962), i.e. digits = 2 -> toExponential(1). I ran the real functions: formatSigned(100000, 2) = "+1.0e+5", formatSigned(239833.9664, 2) = "+2.4e+5", formatSigned(43665, 2) = "+4.4e+4", but formatSigned(9990, 2) = "+9990.00". CLAUDE.md and .agents/references/invariants.md both state: "Powers of ten as $10^n$; no `e` notation in teaching-facing copy."
findings.scenario: A student drags the velocity slider upward. At 9,990 km/s the label reads "+9990.00 km/s"; one 10 km/s step later it reads "+1.0e+4 km/s" — the format flips mid-drag and precision collapses from 6 digits to 2. At the slider's end stop they cannot read their own setting ("+1.0e+5") and cannot distinguish 95,000 from 104,000 km/s. Preset 8 reports "+2.4e+5 km/s", so the station-mode row they copy for a worksheet carries 2 significant figures of a 6-digit quantity.
findings.fix: In apps/demos/src/demos/doppler-shift/logic.ts:59-65, raise the exponential threshold above the velocity range (or take an explicit `allowExponential` flag) and group thousands with a separator for the velocity readout, so 100000 renders "+100,000". Add logic.test.ts cases pinning formatSigned(100000, 2) and formatSigned(239834, 2) — neither function has any test today.

findings.title: Unicode Greek and subscript glyphs reach the Representative line readout and canvas labels, invisible to the math validator
findings.evidence: elementLines for the DEFAULT element H builds labels `["Hα", "Hβ", "Hγ", "Hδ", "Hε", "H8"]` plus "Lyα" (spectralLineModel.ts:471-473); the catalogues add "He I D₃ 587.6" (:123), "Na D₂ 589.0" (:134) and "Na D₁ 589.6" (:135). Traced the path: lineCatalog() -> selectRepresentativeLine(preferVisible) picks Halpha (656.46 nm, intensity 1.0, the strongest line inside 380-750) -> `lineLabelValue.textContent = readouts.representativeLineLabel` (main.ts:934), and `ctx.fillText(line.label, ...)` (main.ts:664). scripts/validate-math-formatting.mjs:33 forbids exactly these characters, but SCAN_ROOTS (:19-27) covers apps/demos, apps/site and packages/runtime — NOT packages/physics, so the build passes. index.html:317 hardcodes the ASCII placeholder "H-alpha 656.3", which render() overwrites on first paint, so the static file the design-contract test reads is clean while the live page is not. The canvas exemption in CLAUDE.md is explicitly ASCII-only ("use ASCII (lambda, deg, M_sun), never Unicode"), so the canvas labels violate it too.
findings.scenario: On first load the Representative line readout shows a Unicode alpha, and selecting Na shows a Unicode subscript 2. Any inherited text-transform, font-fallback or export encoding mangles them — the exact failure the project logged on 2026-09-05, when 94 KaTeX nodes were uppercased and nu became N. A real glyph can be checked by the validator; one hidden behind a static ASCII placeholder cannot.
findings.fix: Store ASCII labels in packages/physics/src/spectralLineModel.ts ("H-alpha", "Na D2", "He I D3", "Ly-alpha") since that is the data layer feeding both HTML and canvas, and render the pretty form in HTML via renderInlineMath/renderMath at the readout. Independently, add packages/physics/src to SCAN_ROOTS in scripts/validate-math-formatting.mjs:19 so these strings are gated.

findings.title: The exhibit's predict_prompt states H-alpha = 656.3 nm; the demo computes 656.463 nm from the Bohr model
findings.evidence: predict_prompt reads "Hydrogen H-alpha sits at 656.3 nm. If a source is approaching at 300 km/s, does the line move to longer or shorter wavelength, and by about how much?" But the H catalogue is generated from the Bohr model (spectralLineModel.ts:465-482) with R_H = 13.598434599 eV. I recomputed: lambda(3->2) = 1239.842 / (13.598434599 * (1/4 - 1/9)) = 656.4625 nm. The air value is 656.279 nm; the prompt's 656.3 is the air value, the demo shows the vacuum value, a 0.1835 nm offset. index.html:317 and :355 also hardcode the air-based placeholders 656.3 nm and 456.8 THz, where the live values are 656.463 nm and 456.679 THz.
findings.scenario: A student answers the predict prompt from 656.3 nm, computes Delta lambda = -0.657 nm at -300 km/s, then opens the demo and sees lambda_0 = 656.463 and Delta lambda = -0.657 against a different baseline. The 0.1835 nm disagreement in the rest wavelength is 28% of the 0.659 nm shift they were asked to estimate, so the check they were told to perform does not close.
findings.fix: Either state the vacuum value in apps/site/src/content/demos/doppler-shift.md:23 ("H-alpha sits at 656.46 nm in vacuum") and update the index.html:317/:355 placeholders to 656.463 and 456.679, or convert the Bohr output to air in the catalogue so the demo agrees with the 656.3 nm value every line list prints. Pick one and say which in the model notes.

findings.title: The "NR divergence" readout is a relative error in z only, and collapses toward zero on the blueshift side while lambda_obs is off by tens of percent
findings.evidence: formulaDivergencePercent (dopplerShiftModel.ts:205-218) returns |z_rel - z_nonrel| / |z_rel| * 100. Because z >= -1 by construction while z_nonrel = beta is unbounded below, this is non-monotonic in beta < 0. I computed, all reachable on the z slider (min -0.8 -> beta = -0.923): beta = -0.5, div(z) = 18.30%, lambda_NR = 328.15 vs lambda_rel = 378.92 nm (13.4% off); beta = -0.9, div(z) = 16.79%, lambda_NR = 65.63 vs 150.57 nm (56.4% off); beta = -0.923 (slider end stop), div(z) = 15.39%, lambda_NR = 50.54 vs 131.33 nm (61.5% off). So the divergence number FALLS from its peak while the error in the drawn and labelled quantity keeps rising. The readout is labelled only "NR divergence" with unit "%" (index.html:331-334) and never says divergence in what.
findings.scenario: A student answers explain_prompt ("At what velocity scale does the non-relativistic Doppler formula become meaningfully wrong (>5% error)?") by sweeping the z slider to its blue end. They read "NR divergence 15.4%" and conclude the approximation is 85% right, while the non-relativistic lambda_obs the demo would draw is 50.5 nm against a true 131.3 nm — a factor of 2.6. The metric they were pointed at understates the error by a factor of four in exactly the regime the prompt is about.
findings.fix: Label the readout "NR error in $z$ (%)" in index.html:331 and the export row in logic.ts:522, and add a second row for the relative error in lambda_obs, |lambda_NR - lambda_rel| / lambda_rel, which is monotonic in |beta| and is the quantity the drawings and the prompt are actually about. Keep the z-based number for the slider markers.

findings.title: Selecting "Non-relativistic" is silently overridden above |beta| = 0.1 while the chip still reads as checked
findings.evidence: `function formulaAppliedMode(requestedMode, velocityKmS) { if (requestedMode === "non-relativistic" && DopplerShiftModel.regime(velocityKmS).label === "relativistic") return "relativistic"; return requestedMode; }` (main.ts:288-293). Every reader-visible quantity then uses the applied mode: lambdaObsNm, deltaLambdaNm, nuObsTHz, deltaNuTHz (main.ts:303-312), the spectrum lines (main.ts:614-618), the representative-line arrow (main.ts:683-687) and the wave spacing (main.ts:765-774). Meanwhile render() leaves `formulaNonRel` with aria-checked="true" (main.ts:966) — the control reports a selection the instrument is not honouring. The only signal is a muted paragraph at index.html:111-113. doppler-shift.md:5 lists learning_goal "Decide when non-relativistic Doppler is acceptable and when relativistic Doppler is required", and explain_prompt:32 asks where the NR formula becomes wrong.
findings.scenario: A student is asked to find where the non-relativistic formula fails. They select Non-relativistic, drag to v = +50,000 km/s, and read lambda_obs = 772.3 nm — the relativistic answer. Every number, every line position and the crest spacing are the exact values they were sent to find the error in. The instrument makes the assigned discovery impossible while telling them, via aria-checked, that their chosen formula is in force.
findings.fix: Stop substituting. In main.ts:288 keep the requested mode for all primary readouts and drawings, and instead force `comparisonReadouts` visible (it already shows lambda_obs non-rel vs relativistic, main.ts:994) with a warning badge on the Non-relativistic chip. If the override must stay, set aria-checked on formulaRel so the control state matches the physics being shown.

findings.title: Live region is written on every slider input event, flooding screen readers during a drag
findings.evidence: `velocitySlider.addEventListener("input", () => { ...; setPhysicalVelocity(Number(velocitySlider.value)); })` (main.ts:1225-1229) and the same for redshiftSlider (main.ts:1231-1235). setPhysicalVelocity defaults announce = true (main.ts:434-440) and calls announceShift, which writes a full sentence ("Observed wavelength 672.147 nm, shift 15.684 nm toward red. Crests are farther apart.") into #status, declared aria-live="polite" aria-atomic="true" (index.html:214). setLiveRegionText (packages/runtime/src/liveRegion.ts:1-18) has no debounce or throttle — it writes immediately on every call. The velocity slider has step="10" over a 200,000 km/s range (index.html:62-70) = 20,000 steps, and `input` fires continuously during a pointer drag and on every arrow-key repeat. CLAUDE.md's own a11y rule for this project: live-region announcements on change, "never inside a render loop".
findings.scenario: A screen-reader user presses and holds the Right arrow on the velocity slider. Each repeat writes a new 90-character sentence to a polite live region; the queue never drains, so they hear a continuous unbroken stream and cannot reach the value they want or hear the final state. A sighted mouse user drags and generates hundreds of queued utterances for anyone else on the page.
findings.fix: Debounce the announcement, not the render: in apps/demos/src/demos/doppler-shift/main.ts wrap announceShift in a ~400 ms trailing debounce for the two slider input handlers (keep it immediate for presets, keyboard steps and chip changes), or announce on the `change` event and render on `input`. The same pattern belongs in packages/runtime as a shared helper since every slider demo has it.

findings.title: A +/-5 deg syzygy gate reports eclipses when the Moon is 5 deg from the Sun on the sky
findings.evidence: `SYZYGY_TOLERANCE_DEG = 5` (logic.ts:262); `computeDerived` gates on `angularSeparationDeg(phaseAngle, 0) <= 5` and then classifies from `betaDeg` ALONE (logic.ts:287-298). The eclipse-limit formulae are latitude-at-conjunction limits, so the longitude offset must also enter the impact parameter. I recomputed lambda_M = 5 deg, lambda_sun = 0, Omega = 0, i = 5.145 deg, d = 384,400 km: beta = -asin(sin 5.145 x sin 5) = 0.4478 deg, and the demo returns `annular-solar`. The true angular separation from the shadow axis is acos(cos beta cos Delta) = 5.020 deg, giving an impact parameter d sin(5.020 deg) = 33,640 km against a partial limit of only R_E + r_penumbra = 6371 + 3530 = 9,901 km. No eclipse of any kind — the Moon is about 9.4 solar diameters from the Sun.
findings.scenario: A student nudges the Moon-position slider from 0 to 5 deg (five arrow-key presses). The Solar readout keeps saying "Annular solar" and the context line keeps saying "Annular solar eclipse! Moon at New Moon, 5.0 deg from nearest node" across eleven slider positions, teaching that the alignment tolerance in longitude is +/-5 deg when the real window is under ~1.5 deg.
findings.fix: Replace the two-part gate with one impact parameter in packages/physics/src/eclipseGeometryModel.ts: add `shadowAxisSeparationDeg({betaDeg, deltaFromSyzygyDeg}) = radToDeg(acos(cos(beta) cos(delta)))` and feed that into `solarEclipseTypeFromBetaDeg`/`lunarEclipseTypeFromBetaDeg` in place of `betaDeg`; then `SYZYGY_TOLERANCE_DEG` can be deleted from logic.ts:262 because the geometry self-limits. If the pedagogical snapshot framing is kept instead, tighten the tolerance to ~0.5 deg and show it on the readout strip, not only in the export notes.

findings.title: Ten reader-visible Unicode math glyphs, written as \u escapes and ° entities so the validator cannot see them
findings.evidence: logic.ts:29 `const sign = betaDeg > 0 ? "+" : "−";` (Unicode minus in the beta readout); logic.ts:184, 187, 195 x3, 198 x3, 204 use `°` and `β` inside the context message set via `contextMessage.textContent` (main.ts:512); main.ts:375-376 `asc. node ${...}°` / `desc. node ${...}°` in SVG text; index.html:284-285 `tilted ~5° from the ecliptic` and `Try setting tilt to 0°`. scripts/validate-math-formatting.mjs:33 matches literal characters only — `FORBIDDEN_UNICODE_MATH = /[deg-sign ... beta ... minus ...]/u` tested against the raw file text (line 114) — so an escape sequence and an HTML entity both pass. CLAUDE.md warns of exactly this: "no \uXXXX escapes that produce them (the validator cannot see escapes)".
findings.scenario: The inherited `text-transform` incident of 2026-09-05 repeats: `|β|` in "Almost! |B| = 1.60 deg" uppercases to a different physical quantity, and the degree signs render in the body font rather than KaTeX. Every one of the ten sites is green under `pnpm build`.
findings.fix: Rewrite the strings as LaTeX and render them: in apps/demos/src/demos/eclipse-geometry/logic.ts return `$|\\beta|$`, `$^{\\circ}$`, `$-$` and in main.ts:512 set `contextMessage.innerHTML = renderMath(ctxMsg)` using `renderMath` from @cosmic/runtime (already imported at main.ts:2). For main.ts:375-376 the labels are SVG `<text>`, where KaTeX cannot render, so use the ASCII canvas exemption (`asc. node 210 deg`). Replace `°` in index.html:284-285 with `$5^{\\circ}$` / `$0^{\\circ}$`. Extend the validator regex to also flag `\\u00b0|\\u03b2|\\u2212` and `°|×|−`.

findings.title: The status live region is rewritten every animation frame, and its clear-then-set path forces a re-announcement at 60 Hz
findings.evidence: `render()` ends with `setLiveRegionText(status, "Thresholds (mean-distance example): solar partial ~ ...")` (main.ts:546-550), and `render()` is called from inside the rAF loop on every frame (main.ts:1197 animate-month, 1210 animate-year, 1244 simulate) and from every tween frame (main.ts:1348). `#status` is `role="status" aria-live="polite" aria-atomic="true"` (index.html:135). The message depends only on `earthMoonDistanceKm`, so while the Moon animates the text is UNCHANGED, which drives the worst branch of packages/runtime/src/liveRegion.ts:10-17: `el.textContent = ""` followed by a rAF that re-sets it — a deliberate re-announcement trigger, fired once per frame. The text also claims "mean-distance example" while interpolating `thresholds` computed from the currently selected preset (main.ts:504-506), so at perigee it announces 1.55 deg and still says "mean".
findings.scenario: A screen-reader user clicks "Animate month". The polite queue receives a cleared-then-restored threshold string roughly sixty times a second for the whole animation, so the announcement never finishes and the one genuinely useful change — the Solar/Lunar outcome flipping to "Total lunar" — is never heard.
findings.fix: Move the threshold announcement out of `render()` in apps/demos/src/demos/eclipse-geometry/main.ts: call `setLiveRegionText` only from the `distancePreset` change handler (main.ts:1533) and the `tilt` input handler, and announce the eclipse outcome on transition inside the existing `prevSolarType`/`prevLunarType` block (main.ts:531-543). Drop the words "mean-distance example" and name the selected distance instead.

findings.title: Node longitude Omega has no labelled control — it is reachable only by dragging an 8 px SVG dot typed as a button
findings.evidence: `<circle id="ascNodeDot" class="stage__node" cx="140" cy="0" r="8" tabindex="0" role="button" aria-label="Ascending node" />` (index.html:182-183). The keyboard handler at main.ts:1682-1696 moves `state.nodeLonDeg` by 1 deg (10 with Shift) on arrow keys, but the element advertises `role="button"` with no `aria-valuenow`, `aria-valuetext` or `aria-orientation`, and nothing is announced after the change — `render()` does not touch the node's ARIA. There is no node slider in the sidebar; main.ts:487 still carries the stale comment `// Node longitude comes from state (no slider -- will be draggable nodes in Task 3)`. Three of the five challenges ask the student to "adjust node longitude Omega" (main.ts:744, 806, 919) and the hint for one says "try Omega near 90 deg" — a target the UI never displays numerically except inside the moving SVG label.
findings.scenario: A screen-reader user tabs to the stage, hears "Ascending node, button", presses Enter and Space (nothing happens), and never discovers that arrow keys are the only way to set Omega. With r=8 in a 920-unit viewBox the dot renders about 10 px across on a phone, so a touch user cannot reliably grab it either. Challenge 1 ("Achieve a solar eclipse") is then unsolvable for both users.
findings.fix: Add a `Node longitude Omega (deg)` range input to the sidebar in apps/demos/src/demos/eclipse-geometry/index.html next to the tilt control and bind it in main.ts the way `tilt` is bound, making the SVG dots a convenience rather than the only path. On the dots, change `role="button"` to `role="slider"` with `aria-valuemin="0" aria-valuemax="360"` and update `aria-valuenow`/`aria-valuetext` inside `renderStage`. Enlarge the hit area with a transparent `r="22"` circle behind each dot.

findings.title: prefers-reduced-motion disables the whole simulation, making the eclipse-statistics challenge unreachable
findings.evidence: main.ts:248-254: `if (prefersReducedMotion) { animateMonth.disabled = true; animateYear.disabled = true; runSimulation.disabled = true; stopSimulation.disabled = true; ... }`, and `runSimulation` re-enables only as `prefersReducedMotion` allows (main.ts:1043, 1264). The fifth challenge's check is `if (!lastCompletedSim) return { correct: false, close: false, message: "Run a simulation first ..." }` (main.ts:948-950), and `lastCompletedSim` is only ever assigned in the simulate branch (main.ts:1259). `runSimulation.addEventListener` also bails first thing: `if (prefersReducedMotion) return;` (main.ts:1452). The simulation is a numerical integration whose only output is a table of counts — it has no requirement to animate.
findings.scenario: A student with reduced motion enabled in the OS opens the demo, sees "Animation and simulation disabled due to reduced-motion preference", enters Challenge mode, reaches challenge 5 of 5, and is told to "Run a simulation first" using a button that is permanently greyed out. One fifth of the assessed content is closed to them.
findings.fix: In apps/demos/src/demos/eclipse-geometry/main.ts:248-254 keep the two `animate*` buttons disabled but leave `runSimulation` enabled, and in the simulate branch of `tick` (main.ts:1222-1270) skip the per-frame `render()` when `prefersReducedMotion` so the stage does not animate — run the integration to completion and render the result table once. Update the `motionNote` copy accordingly.

findings.title: The demo's unit tests validate computeDerived against a fabricated stub physics whose solar classification ignores distance
findings.evidence: logic.test.ts:48-73 injects `stubModel` with `eclipticLatitudeDeg: ({tiltDeg, moonLonDeg, nodeLonDeg}) => tiltDeg * Math.sin(...)` (small-angle, not the model's arcsin form) and `solarEclipseType: ({betaDeg}) => { if (abs < 0.5) return "total-solar"; if (abs < 1.0) return "annular-solar"; if (abs < 1.5) return "partial-solar"; return "none"; }` — the `earthMoonDistanceKm` argument is destructured away and never used, so total-vs-annular is decided by |beta| alone, which is physically meaningless. Consequently `it("detects solar eclipse at New Moon near node")` asserts `expect(result.solarType).toBe("total-solar")` at 384,400 km (logic.test.ts:337-351) while the REAL model returns `annular-solar` there (recomputed above: umbra radius -46.5 km). No test in the repo composes `computeDerived` with the real `EclipseGeometryModel`.
findings.scenario: The P0 preset/label contradiction above lives in exactly the seam these tests cover, and all of logic.test.ts stays green. Any future change to the real classifier — or a swap of the total and annular branches — is invisible to this 40 KB suite.
findings.fix: Add an integration describe block to apps/demos/src/demos/eclipse-geometry/logic.test.ts that imports the real `EclipseGeometryModel` from @cosmic/physics, builds the same `EclipseModelCallbacks` object main.ts:258-265 builds, and asserts the distance-dependent outcomes at asymmetric points: (lambda_M, lambda_sun, Omega, i, d) = (0,0,0,5.145,384400) -> annular-solar; the same at 363300 -> total-solar; (187,0,190,5.145,405500) -> none. Keep the stub only for the pure formatters.

findings.title: The physics model test pins ecliptic latitude only where it is identically zero, so the sign of beta is unconstrained
findings.evidence: The only `eclipticLatitudeDeg` assertion is `it("returns 0 deg ecliptic latitude at the node longitude")` with `moonLonDeg: nodeLonDeg` -> `toBeCloseTo(0, 12)` (eclipseGeometryModel.test.ts:14-23). Every candidate formula of the form +/-asin(k sin(lambda_M - Omega)) returns 0 there, so a global sign flip passes. The 59-line file has six tests total and contains no call to `lunarEclipseTypeFromBetaDeg`, `nearestNodeDistanceDeg`, `phaseAngleDeg`, `betaFromDeltaLambdaDeg` or `deltaLambdaFromBetaDeg`. I verified the sign is currently correct by recomputation — beta(i=5.145 deg, Delta lambda = +30 deg) = +asin(sin 5.145 x sin 30) = +2.5697 deg, i.e. north of the ecliptic just after the ascending node — but nothing in the suite holds it there.
findings.scenario: A sign flip in `eclipticLatitudeDeg` (eclipseGeometryModel.ts:33) leaves all six physics tests green while inverting the beta-panel sinusoid, the signed beta readout, the beta indicator line in the top view, and the meaning of the "asc. node" and "desc. node" labels — the exact waxing/waning-swap failure mode CLAUDE.md records.
findings.fix: Add asymmetric assertions to packages/physics/src/eclipseGeometryModel.test.ts: beta(i=5.145, Delta lambda=+30) is close to +2.5697 and beta(i=5.145, Delta lambda=-30) is close to -2.5697 (sign pinned, 4 decimals); a round trip `deltaLambdaFromBetaDeg(betaFromDeltaLambdaDeg(...))`; and the three lunar tiers at 384,400 km against recomputed limits (total |beta| <= 0.4265 deg, umbral <= 0.9445 deg, penumbral <= 1.4777 deg).

findings.title: Exhibit learning goal "Distinguish umbra vs penumbra" is not supported — the demo never draws a shadow cone
findings.evidence: eclipse-geometry.md:16 lists the learning goal `"Distinguish umbra vs penumbra in a qualitative way."` and the `tags` at line 9 include `"umbra", "penumbra"`. The stage contains exactly two panels (index.html:160-243): a top-view orbit circle with node dots and threshold arcs, and a beta-vs-orbital-position plot. Neither draws Earth's or the Moon's shadow; `grep` for umbra across index.html returns nothing, and the words never reach the screen — the umbral and penumbral radii exist only as intermediate numbers inside `eclipseThresholdsDeg`. Worse, `thresholds.lunarTotalDeg` is computed (eclipseGeometryModel.ts:117) and never rendered: `renderBands` draws only solar-partial, solar-central and lunar-penumbral (main.ts:470-472) and `renderArcs` draws solar-partial, solar-central, lunar-penumbral and lunar-umbral (main.ts:422-431), so "Total lunar" is a reported outcome with no threshold shown anywhere.
findings.scenario: An instructor assigns this exhibit to meet the umbra/penumbra objective on the syllabus. The student plays the demo for twelve minutes (the stated `time_minutes`), never sees a shadow cone, and cannot answer the umbra-versus-penumbra question on the follow-up assessment.
findings.fix: Either add a third stage panel drawing the Moon's and Earth's cones to scale from `EclipseGeometryModel.shadowRadiiKmAtDistance` (the numbers are already computed), or delete the umbra/penumbra learning goal and tags from apps/site/src/content/demos/eclipse-geometry.md:16 and 9 and reword the Model notes tab (index.html:291-293), which currently claims "We model eclipse geometry using similar triangles for the umbra/penumbra" without showing either. Also render a `lunar-total` band and arc so every reported outcome has a visible threshold.

findings.title: Eight threshold arcs and three shaded bands carry no legend or units anywhere on the stage
findings.evidence: index.html:170-177 declares eight arc paths (`arc-solar-any-asc` ... `arc-lunar-central-desc`) styled only by colour and width: `.stage__arc--solar { stroke: var(--cp-accent-rose) }`, `.stage__arc--lunar { stroke: var(--cp-accent) }`, `.stage__arc--central { stroke-width: 12; opacity: 0.4 }` (style.css:180-191). The only text explaining any of them is the pair `solar zone` / `lunar zone` in the beta panel (index.html:216-217). The beta panel's vertical axis has no numeric scale at all — index.html:203-205 label it with a bare `+`, `-` and `height`, while the quantitative content sits at `BETA_Y_SCALE = 20` px per degree (main.ts:388), so the solar band occupies only +/-29.5 px of a +/-140 px axis. The orbit panel's "height above the ecliptic" indicator (main.ts:380-386) is drawn as a vertical screen offset inside a view whose screen plane IS the orbit plane, mixing two incompatible projections with no caption.
findings.scenario: A student sees two pink and two teal bands around each node dot and two pink/teal stripes in the right panel, with no key saying which is solar and which lunar, which is the central tier, or what degree value any edge represents. Asked "how many degrees from the node can a solar eclipse happen?" (the answer is 16.7 deg at i = 5.145 deg, which the arcs encode exactly) they cannot read it off, and the readout strip does not report it either.
findings.fix: Add a small legend group to the stage SVG in apps/demos/src/demos/eclipse-geometry/index.html — four swatches reading `solar: partial / central` and `lunar: penumbral / umbral` — and tick the beta axis in degrees at +/-1, +/-2, +/-5 using the same `BETA_Y_SCALE`. Add a `Node window` readout to the strip showing `eclipseArcExtentDeg` in deg, so the quantity the arcs draw is also a number. Label the orbit panel's beta indicator "(out of plane, schematic)".

findings.title: The demo's own physics review claims "no issues found" and content_verified is true, over a stub parity audit
findings.evidence: docs/reviews/eclipse-geometry.md:9: "Verdict: **all physics equations, coordinate conventions, and inverse mappings are correct; no issues found.**", and its Issues section reads "None -- all chains verified clean." Its coordinate audit item 1 inspects the clockwise mapping and concludes "**Consistent** -- ... No inversion bug" — it checked the forward/inverse round trip and never asked whether the drawn orbit sense matches the panel title, which is the P0 above. docs/reviews/2026-02-07-seasons-eclipse-physics-review.md:322 repeats the same reasoning verbatim. Meanwhile `parityAuditPath: "docs/audits/migrations/eclipse-geometry-parity.md"` (eclipse-geometry.md:12) points at a file whose six sections all read "Pending detailed parity review." Yet the exhibit frontmatter asserts `content_verified: true` with `lastVerifiedAt: "2026-02-02"` — before main.ts was last changed on 2026-09-10.
findings.scenario: The next agent or instructor reads "all chains verified clean" and promotes the demo, or skips re-auditing the drawing. The three P0s in this report all sit inside chains the review marked OK.
findings.fix: In docs/reviews/eclipse-geometry.md replace the verdict with the findings in this report and record the specific thing the review did not test (orbit handedness against the stated viewpoint; the real model composed with computeDerived). Set `content_verified: false` in apps/site/src/content/demos/eclipse-geometry.md:4 until the parity audit at docs/audits/migrations/eclipse-geometry-parity.md is written. `readiness: experimental` and `status: draft` are the right labels and should stay.

findings.title: The on-bar wavelength label is clipped away by overflow:hidden and never renders
findings.evidence: style.css:73-82 gives `.spectrum__bar { position: relative; height: 80px; overflow: hidden; }` -- it is the marker's containing block and the only rule for that class (grepped apps/demos/src, apps/site/src and packages/theme/src: no override). style.css:103-109 puts `.spectrum__marker` at `top: -6px; height: 92px`, and style.css:111-115 puts `.spectrum__markerLabel` at `top: -22px` inside the marker. The label's box therefore spans y = -6 - 22 = -28 px to about -4 px in the bar's coordinate space (label height ~24 px from 0.82rem text + 2px padding + 1px border), entirely above the clip rectangle y = 0..80. main.ts:205-210 still computes and writes its text every update (`markerLabel.textContent = ...`), and the marker's own top 6 px and bottom 12 px are clipped as well.
findings.scenario: A student drags the slider. The marker is a bare 2 px line with no number on it, and the "520 nm" pill the code writes on every frame is painted outside the clip and discarded. Reading the current wavelength requires looking away from the bar to the readouts aside, which is precisely the cross-reference the misaligned ticks then corrupt.
findings.fix: Remove `overflow: hidden` from `.spectrum__bar` (style.css:78) and instead put `overflow: hidden; border-radius: 12px` on an inner gradient layer, or move `#marker`/`#markerLabel` out of `.spectrum__bar` into a sibling overlay positioned over it. Add an e2e assertion that `#markerLabel` has a non-zero bounding box and lies within the viewport.

findings.title: Energy and frequency readouts emit raw JavaScript exponential notation over most of the slider range
findings.evidence: logic.ts:176 falls back to `{ value: energyErg.toPrecision(3), unit: "erg" }` whenever E < 1e-3 eV. I computed the crossover: E = 1e-3 eV corresponds to lambda = hc/E = 1.9864e-16/1.602e-15 = 0.124 cm, which is position 38.4% on the axis, so the entire left 38% of the slider shows erg. toPrecision(3) returns exponential form once the exponent exceeds the precision, so the actual rendered strings are (recomputed with node): lambda = 10 km -> "1.99e-22 erg"; radio centre 3.16 m -> "6.28e-19 erg"; 21 cm HI -> "9.46e-18 erg". The same defect hits frequency at logic.ts:152: the gamma band centre renders "3.00e+3 EHz" and the axis right edge "3.00e+4 EHz". CLAUDE.md and .agents/references/invariants.md both state: "Powers of ten as $10^{n}$; no `e` notation in teaching-facing copy." There is also a hard discontinuity at the boundary -- 1.60e-15 erg becomes 0.00100 eV for a one-step slider move.
findings.scenario: A student parks on the 21 cm hydrogen line, the single most-taught radio wavelength in ASTR 101, and the photon-energy readout says "9.46e-18 erg" -- a notation the course has not taught, in a unit the public model notes promise will not appear, next to a frequency of 1.43 GHz. At the other end the frequency reads "3.00e+4 EHz" instead of 3e22 Hz.
findings.fix: Add meV and ueV branches below eV in formatEnergyFromErg (logic.ts:168-177) so the radio end reads e.g. "5.90 ueV" instead of erg, add GeV and TeV above MeV, and extend formatFrequency (logic.ts:150-158) past EHz (or render the mantissa/exponent through renderMath from @cosmic/runtime). Add a logic.ts test asserting that no formatter output matches /e[+-]\d/ for any lambda sampled across the full axis.

findings.title: readiness: candidate contradicts the parity audit's written recommendation, and none of its P0/P1 items has landed
findings.evidence: docs/audits/migrations/em-spectrum-parity.md section 8 states: "Keep `readiness: experimental` until P0 + P1 items are addressed and this parity audit is updated with verification notes + screenshots." The frontmatter instead declares `readiness: candidate` (em-spectrum.md:10), which apps/site/src/lib/readiness.ts:49-52 renders as "near-ready" with ariaLabel "ready to assign, pending final review".
