I verified every blocking item is still open: no listener on `.spectrum__bar` in main.ts (only `spectrumBarEl.style.background` at main.ts:157-159), so click-to-jump is absent; no ArrowLeft/ArrowRight wavelength handler (the only keydown handler is the tab roving one at main.ts:382-390); telescope/object entries are plain `li.textContent` with no interactivity (main.ts:259-270); Convert still has fixed nm/Hz/eV with no unit selects (index.html:155-170); `grep -rn "Arecibo|Event Horizon" packages/data-spectra/src/` returns nothing; and apps/site/src/content/instructor/em-spectrum/model.md:17-18 still cites the legacy `demos/_assets/em-spectrum-model.js` and `demos/em-spectrum/em-spectrum.js`, the audit's other P0. On top of that `lastVerifiedAt: "2026-02-02"` (em-spectrum.md:13) predates both the audit (2026-02-11) and the gradient fix in commit 8fcedd6 (2026-09-09), and `content_verified: true` (em-spectrum.md:4) is asserted over the Microwave band error above.
findings.scenario: An instructor filters Explore by readiness, sees "near-ready / ready to assign", and assigns em-spectrum as homework. Students read an axis mislabelled by up to 72x and a Microwave band card whose four examples all live in the demo's Radio band, with no live-region announcement for screen-reader users.
findings.fix: Set `readiness: experimental` in em-spectrum.md:10 and rewrite readinessReason to name the open defects (axis labels, microwave band definition, clipped marker label) rather than only the missing modes; clear `content_verified` to false until the band table is corrected; and bump `lastVerifiedAt` only when a re-verification actually happens.

findings.title: The standing physics review records "Issues Found: None" while describing and excusing the gradient bug that was later fixed
findings.evidence: docs/reviews/em-spectrum.md closes with "## Issues Found\n\nNone. All physics equations, constants, unit conversions, band boundaries, and rendering chains are correct." Its "Spectral gradient" section computes 550 nm at 57% itself, notes "The gradient places green at 44%", and dismisses the 13-point disagreement as "an artistic approximation of spectral colors, not a physically precise colorimetric mapping." `git log` dates the review at 2026-02-07 (commit 144ae01) and the actual fix at 2026-09-09 (commit 8fcedd6, "Fix the seasons terminator and the em-spectrum gradient"); the in-code comment now at logic.ts:216-224 records the same defect as a real bug that "left the real visible band (56.4%-57.9%) painted flat violet." The review also asserts "Microwave | 1e-2 (0.1 mm) | 1e-1 (1 mm) | Conventional: 0.1-1 mm | CORRECT" (the convention is 1 mm to 1 m) and "A mutex lock (`convertLock`) prevents circular updates", which is false (see the convertLock finding). The review has never been revised and is still this demo's physics-review record of file.
findings.scenario: A reviewer or instructor consults docs/reviews/em-spectrum.md to decide whether the demo's physics has been checked, reads "Issues Found: None", and skips the re-derivation -- which is how the microwave band definition and the axis-label misalignment have survived two review cycles.
findings.fix: Replace docs/reviews/em-spectrum.md with a dated re-review that records the axis-label geometry, the microwave band definition and the erg/e-notation formatting as open findings, and strike the two false CORRECT rows (microwave convention, convertLock mutex). Going forward a review that computes a disagreement should file it, not excuse it as artistic.

findings.title: The gamma band stops at 124 MeV and MeV is the largest energy unit, excluding the GeV-TeV photons its own examples name
findings.evidence: The axis floor is 1e-12 cm (logic.ts:97). I computed E = hc/lambda at that floor: 1.9864e-16/1e-12 = 1.9864e-4 erg = 124 MeV; bandCenterCm("gamma") = sqrt(1e-13*1e-9) = 1e-11 cm = 12.4 MeV. formatEnergyFromErg (logic.ts:168-177) has no branch above MeV, so the hardest reachable photon reads "124 MeV". Meanwhile logic.ts:87-89 lists gamma examples "Gamma-ray bursts, nuclear reactions, pulsars" and detectors "Space detectors (Fermi) and ground Cherenkov telescopes (VERITAS)": Fermi-LAT covers 20 MeV to 300 GeV (lambda 6.20e-12 to 4.13e-16 cm, computed) and VERITAS 85 GeV to 30 TeV (lambda 1.46e-15 to 4.13e-18 cm), both largely or wholly off the left-hand side of the axis. GRB prompt emission peaks in the 0.1-1 MeV range and the Fermi/VERITAS science the card advertises is GeV-TeV.
findings.scenario: A student clicks Gamma to see what Fermi and VERITAS detect. They get 100 fm / 12.4 MeV, a nuclear-decay photon, with no way to reach the GeV or TeV photons the same card attributes to those instruments, and no GeV/TeV unit even if the axis were extended.
findings.fix: Extend LAMBDA_MIN_LOG (logic.ts:96) to -17 or -18 so TeV photons are reachable, and add GeV and TeV branches above MeV in formatEnergyFromErg. If the axis range is kept for layout reasons, say so in the band card copy and drop VERITAS from the gamma detection string, since the demo cannot represent its band.

findings.title: Contextual hint tells students stronger degeneracy restores dynamical stability -- the inverse of the Chandrasekhar-limit physics
findings.evidence: `return "The effective adiabatic index is near or below 4/3 ... Try increasing density to push into stronger degeneracy and restore stability."` fires whenever gammaEff < 4/3 + 0.05. But adiabaticIndex (logic.ts:696-698) sets gammaDeg = 5/3 - t/3 with t = clamp((x_F - 0.3)/0.7, 0, 1), so pushing to stronger (more relativistic) degeneracy drives gammaDeg DOWN to 4/3 and raises the degeneracy weight, driving Gamma_eff toward 4/3 exactly. Traced at my asymmetric point C (T = 6.1e8 K, rho = 7.3e7 g cm^-3, X=0.11/Y=0.86/Z=0.03): x_F = 3.465 so t = 1 and gammaDeg = 4/3 already; P_gas = 3.258e24, P_deg,e = 1.417e25, Gamma_eff = 1.396, so the hint fires -- and raising rho increases P_deg/P_tot, monotonically lowering Gamma_eff toward 1.3333. The advice is only right in the radiation-dominated case (where raising rho raises P_gas), and the string does not distinguish them.
findings.scenario: A student at a dense, relativistically degenerate state sees Gamma_eff = 1.396 with the hint "try increasing density to push into stronger degeneracy and restore stability", drags density up, watches Gamma_eff fall toward 4/3, and learns that relativistic electron degeneracy stabilises a star -- precisely backwards from the Chandrasekhar mass limit this demo exists to motivate.
findings.fix: Split rule 1 in getContextualSuggestion (logic.ts:801-807) on which channel is depressing Gamma. When radiationToGas is large, keep the raise-density advice. When x_F > 0.3 (relativistic degeneracy is the cause), say the opposite: that raising density pushes x_F up, drives the degeneracy exponent from 5/3 toward 4/3, and is what sets the Chandrasekhar limit -- and suggest lowering density or raising T to recover Gamma > 4/3. The input type already carries chiDegeneracy; add xF to ContextualSuggestionInput (logic.ts:785-793) and pass model.fermiRelativityX from main.ts:862.

findings.title: The Gamma_eff instability warning can never fire: Gamma_eff is bounded below by 4/3 by construction
findings.evidence: adiabaticIndex returns (pGas*5/3 + pRad*4/3 + pDeg*gammaDeg)/pTotal with gammaDeg = 5/3 - t*(1/3), t in [0,1], so every per-channel exponent lies in [4/3, 5/3]; with no additionalPressureTerms ever supplied (evaluateStateCgs is called with no `additionalPressureTerms` at main.ts:220, logic.ts:261 and logic.ts:466) the three weights sum to exactly 1, so Gamma_eff is in [4/3, 5/3]. I swept the whole slider domain (log T 3..9, log rho -10..10 at 0.1 dex): min Gamma_eff = 1.333333 at (9.0, -10.0), never below. The branch at main.ts:841-843, `if (gammaEff < GAMMA_CRIT - 0.01) { ... "Below 4/3 - dynamically unstable" }`, is therefore unreachable, as is data-stability="unstable". index.html:471 promises it anyway: title="... Values below 4/3 indicate dynamical instability." The unit tests at logic.test.ts:484-488 and :498-502 only assert the implemented formula reproduces 4/3 in its own limits, so nothing catches this.
findings.scenario: An instructor builds a lesson around "drive Gamma_eff below 4/3 and see the instability warning" from the tooltip at index.html:471. No reachable state in the demo produces it; the readout stops at "approx 4/3 - marginal stability" and the red unstable state never appears, so the lesson silently has no payoff and the student concludes stellar matter is unconditionally stable.
findings.fix: Either delete the unreachable branch and the tooltip clause, or -- better, and it fixes the next finding too -- replace the pressure-weighted mean with Chandrasekhar's Gamma_1 for a gas+radiation mixture, Gamma_1 = beta + (4-3beta)^2 (gamma-1)/(beta + 12(gamma-1)(1-beta)) with gamma = 5/3 and beta = P_gas/(P_gas+P_rad), blended with the degeneracy exponent. That form genuinely approaches 4/3 from above and makes the marginal band meaningful; keep the strict floor documented so the copy does not promise a sub-4/3 reading the model cannot produce.

findings.title: Gamma_eff is a pressure-weighted mean mislabelled "the standard stellar structure approximation"; 5.3% off Chandrasekhar's Gamma_1 at a shipped preset
findings.evidence: logic.ts:681 docstring: "Uses the standard stellar structure approximation: Gamma_eff = (P_gas * 5/3 + P_rad * 4/3 + P_deg * gamma_deg) / P_total". The standard result for an ideal-gas + radiation mixture is Chandrasekhar's Gamma_1 = beta + (4-3beta)^2(gamma-1)/(beta+12(gamma-1)(1-beta)). At the Massive-star core preset (main.ts:219-221: T = 4e7 K, rho = 10 g cm^-3, X=0.35/Y=0.63/Z=0.02) I computed mu = 0.84567, P_gas = 3.93274e16, P_rad = 6.45606e15 dyne cm^-2, P_deg,e = 0 (chi = T/T_F = 37.1 > 8), beta = P_gas/(P_gas+P_rad) = 0.8590. The demo displays Gamma_eff = 0.8590*(5/3) + 0.1410*(4/3) = 1.620; Chandrasekhar's Gamma_1 = 1.538. Error +5.3%, in the direction of overstating stability. At beta = 0.5 the naive mean gives 1.500 vs 1.426 (+5.2%). This is EOS-5 in docs/reviews/eos-lab-2026-09-03.md, still open and filed P3 there -- but the number is displayed to 3 decimals with a stability verdict attached, which is not a P3 consequence.
findings.scenario: A student selects "Massive-star core", reads Gamma_eff = 1.620, and reports that a radiation-supported massive-star core sits comfortably above 4/3. The physically correct Gamma_1 is 1.538 -- still stable, but the margin above 4/3 is 24% smaller than displayed, and the error grows as beta falls, exactly where the instability lesson lives.
findings.fix: Replace the body of adiabaticIndex (logic.ts:686-698) with Chandrasekhar's Gamma_1 on beta = pGas/(pGas+pRad), then blend the degeneracy channel in by its pressure weight with the existing x_F-dependent exponent, and correct the docstring to name the formula and its source rather than calling the mean "standard". Replace the implementation-mirroring test at logic.test.ts:505-510 with a case pinned to the analytic Gamma_1 at a stated beta.

findings.title: Thirty-plus forbidden Unicode math glyphs reach the reader as \uXXXX escapes that the build validator cannot see
findings.evidence: scripts/validate-math-formatting.mjs:33 forbids `×`, `ρ`, `μ`, `≈` and the superscript digits, and scripts apps/demos/src/demos (SCAN_ROOTS line 20) -- but it tests the RAW SOURCE TEXT (`FORBIDDEN_UNICODE_MATH.test(raw)` at line 114), so a `ρ` written as an escape is six ASCII characters and passes. eos-lab writes exactly those escapes: tallying `\u[0-9A-Fa-f]{4}` across logic.ts, main.ts and regimeMap.ts gives 6x ρ (rho), 1x μ (mu), 4x × (times), 6x ⁻ + 6x ³ + 2x ² + 3x ⁴ (superscript minus/2/3/4), 1x ≈, plus the whole ⁰..⁹ superscript map in `superscript()` at logic.ts:30-38. These are rendered output, not comments: logic.ts:85 returns `${mantissa}×10${superscript(exp)}` from formatScientific, which feeds #pGasValue, #pRadValue, #pDegValue, #pTotalValue, #tempValue, #rhoValue (main.ts:731 appends " g cm⁻³"), #xFValue, #chiDegValue and the station-mode table; main.ts:842 writes "⚠ Below 4/3"; logic.ts:816/821/836/841 put raw rho, mu_e, times and T-superscript-4 into #trySuggestion's text node. CLAUDE.md records the exact consequence: on 2026-09-05, 94 math nodes across 14 demos were silently uppercased by an inherited text-transform, turning nu into N and mu into M.
findings.scenario: A `text-transform: uppercase` anywhere in the cascade above #trySuggestion turns the hint "switching from He-rich to H-rich changes mu_e" into "...changes M_e" -- a different physical quantity -- and the build gate reports green, because the glyph never appears literally in the source it scans. The same mechanism silently restyles every `×10^n` in every pressure readout.
findings.fix: Delete `superscript()` (logic.ts:30-38) and have formatScientific return LaTeX (`${mantissa} \\times 10^{${exp}}`) rendered through renderMath/setMathText, keeping the ASCII-only variant solely for the uPlot tick callback and the regime-map canvas labels, which are the documented exemption. Rewrite the eight getContextualSuggestion strings and main.ts:731/842/926-930 in LaTeX. Then close the hole in the gate: in scripts/validate-math-formatting.mjs, also test `raw` after replacing /\\u[0-9A-Fa-f]{4}/ escapes with their characters, so this class of evasion fails the build.

findings.title: Scaling-quiz feedback shows students the literal text "—" and "⇒"
findings.evidence: All three SCALING_CHALLENGES insights use a DOUBLE backslash: logic.ts:530 `insight: "$P_{\\rm gas} \\propto T^1$ \\u2014 linear scaling. Double $T$ \\u21D2 double $P$."` (also :543, :556). In TS source `\\u2014` is an escaped backslash followed by u2014, so the runtime string literally contains the six characters — -- I confirmed this with JSON.stringify, which returns "...$ \\u2014 linear scaling...". main.ts:1115 writes that string into `feedbackEl.innerHTML` and calls renderMath, whose auto-render (packages/runtime/src/math.ts:29-35) only typesets the `$...$` spans; — and ⇒ sit OUTSIDE the delimiters, so they stay as plain text in the DOM. (The single-backslash escapes elsewhere in the file do produce real glyphs -- that is the separate invariant finding above.)
findings.scenario: A student answers the radiation scaling question correctly and the reward text reads: "P_rad — explosive! Double T ⇒ 2^4 = 16x P." -- raw escape sequences in the one place the demo congratulates them, in a quiz with no other feedback channel.
findings.fix: In logic.ts:530, 543 and 556 replace `\\u2014` with ` -- ` (or an em dash authored as text outside the math spans per the project's LaTeX rule) and `\\u21D2` with `$\\Rightarrow$` so it is typeset by KaTeX, and add a unit test asserting that no SCALING_CHALLENGES string matches /\\u[0-9A-Fa-f]{4}/.

findings.title: Preset identity is never cleared when a slider moves, so exports and station-mode rows mislabel custom states as named presets
findings.evidence: `state.selectedPresetId` is assigned at main.ts:387 (initial), :517 (applyPreset) and set to null only at main.ts:1366, inside the regime-map click handler. The six slider handlers -- tempSlider (:1289), rhoSlider (:1299), xSlider (:1309), ySlider (:1317) and the two Tab-2 mirrors (:1012, :1022) -- mutate state.temperatureK / densityGPerCm3 / composition and never touch selectedPresetId. So after dragging temperature away from the Solar core preset: renderPresetState (:532-535) keeps the chip's aria-pressed="true" and is-active class, presetNote still prints "Expected: Gas with meaningful radiation fraction" (:541), exportResults emits `{ name: "Preset", value: "Solar core" }` (:665), and station mode's getSnapshotRow records `case: "Solar core"` (:1216) for a state that is not the solar core. The "Custom" fallback in both places is dead for slider-driven states.
findings.scenario: A student following station step 1 ("Record at least three presets") clicks Solar core, then drags temperature to 10^9 K to see radiation take over, then clicks "Add row (snapshot)". The table row is labelled "Solar core" with T = 1.00x10^9 K. The submitted lab table, and the copy-results export, both attribute a fabricated state to a named stellar environment, and the preset chip on screen still reads as selected.
findings.fix: Add `state.selectedPresetId = null;` to each of the six slider input handlers in main.ts (:1289, :1299, :1309, :1317, :1012, :1022) -- or factor the three state mutations through a single setState helper that clears it -- and make renderPresetState hide #presetNote when selectedPresetId is null. Add an E2E assertion in apps/site/tests/eos-lab.spec.ts that after choosing a preset and filling #tempSlider, no .preset chip has aria-pressed="true".

findings.title: Hard 1e5 floor on the pressure axis puts the current state off-chart for two of the six presets
findings.evidence: `const logPressureRange = (_u, mn, mx) => [Math.max(mn, 1e5), mx];` is wired to the y scale at main.ts:478, and the double-click reset at :506 hardcodes the same `{ min: 1e5, max: 1e25 }`. Two shipped presets sit below that floor. Solar envelope (main.ts:211-212: T = 5800 K, rho = 1e-7, X=0.74/Y=0.24/Z=0.02, mu = 0.5988): P_gas = 8.0534e4, P_rad = 2.854, P_tot = 8.054e4 dyne cm^-2. Red giant envelope (main.ts:228-229: T = 4000 K, rho = 1e-9, mu = 0.6173): P_gas = 5.3878e2, P_rad = 0.6456, P_tot = 5.394e2 dyne cm^-2. Both are below 1e5. Worse, currentStatePlugin (main.ts:432-460) computes cy = u.valToPos(pTotal,"y",true) and only guards `Number.isFinite(cy)` -- there is no clip to u.bbox and no ctx.rect/clip before the fill -- so the amber state diamond is painted at a y coordinate outside the plot rectangle, over the axis area.
findings.scenario: A student clicks "Red giant envelope", looks at the Pressure Curves panel, and finds the curves clipped off the bottom of the axis at the density they are standing at, with the amber "you are here" diamond drawn down among the x-axis tick labels. The panel caption still says the curves show how pressure varies at the current temperature, so the student concludes the demo is broken or that envelope pressure is unrepresentable.
findings.fix: Replace the fixed 1e5 floor in main.ts:172 with a data-driven one, e.g. `[Math.max(mn, Math.min(1e5, 10 ** (Math.floor(Math.log10(pTotalAtState)) - 1))), mx]`, or simply drop the floor and let uPlot pick from the data; update the double-click reset at :506 to match. Independently, wrap the currentStatePlugin draw in ctx.save/ctx.rect(u.bbox)/ctx.clip so the marker can never paint outside the plot area, and show a short note when the state falls outside the visible range.

findings.title: LTE closure chip raises a spurious caution at the Massive-star core preset, and that warning hijacks the exploration hint
findings.evidence: `const likelyLte = rho >= 1e-7 && temperatureK <= 3e7;` -- once rho clears 1e-7 the verdict is decided by temperature alone. The Massive-star core preset (main.ts:219-220: T = 4e7 K, rho = 10 g cm^-3) fails only the T test, so assessRadiationClosure returns tag "caution" with the note "Low-density/high-temperature states may violate isotropic LTE assumptions" -- at rho = 10 g cm^-3, which is not low density. Checking the actual criterion: with electron-scattering opacity kappa_es = 0.2(1+X) = 0.27 cm^2 g^-1 at X = 0.35, the photon mean free path is 1/(kappa rho) = 0.37 cm against a temperature scale height of ~10^10 cm, so LTE is excellent by ~10 orders of magnitude. Then getContextualSuggestion rule 2 (logic.ts:808-812) fires because lteTag !== "lte-like" and the dominant channel is gas (beta = 0.859), replacing any radiation-related hint with "The LTE closure chip shows a warning -- radiation pressure may be unreliable here."
findings.scenario: A student selects "Massive-star core" -- the preset whose note reads "Higher core temperatures increase radiation support strongly via T^4 scaling" -- and is simultaneously told that radiation pressure may be unreliable there and advised to leave the regime. They learn to distrust P_rad = aT^4/3 in exactly the stellar interior where it is most reliable and most important.
findings.fix: Make the heuristic a density-temperature criterion rather than a temperature cut: estimate the electron-scattering mean free path l = 1/(kappa_es rho) with kappa_es = 0.2(1+X) cm^2 g^-1 and flag caution only when l is not small compared with a stated reference length (the physical choice of that reference length is a scientific assumption and should be approved before it is coded). Keep the existing eta_rad != 1 proxy branches unchanged, and add a test asserting the Massive-star core preset returns tag "lte-like".

findings.title: None of the six range sliders has aria-valuetext, so screen readers announce 0-1000 slider units instead of T, rho, X or Y
findings.evidence: #tempSlider (index.html:83), #rhoSlider (:100), #xSlider (:115), #ySlider (:130) and the Tab-2 mirrors #compareT (:322) and #compareRho (:328) are all `type="range" min="0" max="1000" step="1"`, mapped to physical values only in JS by logSliderToValue (logic.ts:44). grep for aria-valuetext across the whole demo returns nothing, and packages/runtime/src contains no aria-valuetext helper either. The physical value is written to a sibling span (#tempValue, main.ts:730) which is not referenced by aria-describedby, so it is never part of the slider's announcement. The e2e spec's only a11y assertion checks that #status has role=status (apps/site/tests/eos-lab.spec.ts:139-143).
findings.scenario: A screen-reader user arrows the temperature slider and hears "slider, 501 of 1000" while the demo moves from 1.57x10^7 K to 1.66x10^7 K. The entire quantitative content of the instrument -- which is a lab about reading numbers off controls -- is inaccessible, and nothing announces that density has units of g cm^-3 at all.
findings.fix: In main.ts's render(), set aria-valuetext on each slider next to where the visible span is written (:730-731 and the composition block at :744-746): e.g. tempSlider.setAttribute("aria-valuetext", `${temperatureK.toExponential(2)} kelvin`), using a spoken-units string rather than LaTeX or Unicode. Do the same for #compareT/#compareRho in syncCompareSliders (:916-921). Add an e2e assertion that #tempSlider's aria-valuetext changes when the slider is filled.

findings.title: Three aria-live regions are written from inside the render loop, firing on every slider sample
findings.evidence: index.html:374, :388 and :402 declare #compareGasFlash, #compareRadFlash and #compareDegFlash as `aria-live="polite"`. render() calls renderCompareView whenever Tab 2 is visible (main.ts:884-886), and renderCompareView calls showDeltaFlash on all three (main.ts:988-997), which writes el.textContent (:923-936) -- an em-dash or an up/down arrow with a ratio. render() itself is called from every `input` event on every slider (:1289, :1299, :1309, :1317, :1012, :1022). CLAUDE.md's a11y rule for this project is explicit: live-region announcements on change, never inside a render loop. The one correctly-placed live region is #status, written only on discrete actions (preset click :1283, map click :1368, copy :1397).
findings.scenario: With Tab 2 open, a screen-reader user drags the temperature slider. Each pointer sample writes three polite live regions, so the assistive technology queues dozens of "up times 1.2" announcements and the user cannot hear the readouts they are trying to change. Keyboard arrowing produces one triple-announcement per keypress.
findings.fix: Remove aria-live from the three .compare-column__flash divs in index.html (they are decorative delta badges with aria-hidden-worthy content) and instead announce the change once per settled interaction: add a `change`-event handler that writes a single summary to #status, mirroring the pattern already used for preset selection at main.ts:1283.

findings.title: Solar-model overlay mislabels the base of the convection zone, and the two zone labels are effectively swapped
findings.evidence: solarProfileData (logic.ts:850, docstring "Standard Solar Model profile (Bahcall et al. 2005, approximate)") labels `[5.9, -2.5, "Base of CZ"]` at line 863 and `[6.35, -0.8, "Radiative zone"]` at line 861. The standard solar convection-zone base is at r = 0.713 R_sun, T = 2.18e6 K (log T = 6.34), rho = 0.19 g cm^-3 (log rho = -0.72). So the point the file calls "Radiative zone" (6.35, -0.8) IS the CZ base to within 0.01 dex in T and 0.08 dex in rho, while the point labelled "Base of CZ" (5.9, -2.5) is T = 7.9e5 K, rho = 3e-3 g cm^-3 -- a factor 2.8 too cool and 60x too rarefied, well up inside the convective envelope. The Core (7.196, 2.176 -> 1.57e7 K, 150 g cm^-3) and Photosphere (3.76, -7.0 -> 5750 K, 1e-7) anchors are correct. logic.test.ts:595-599 only asserts that the labels "Core" and "Photosphere" exist, so nothing checks these two.
findings.scenario: A student ticks "Show solar model profile", reads the dot labelled "Base of CZ", and takes away T ~ 8x10^5 K and rho ~ 3x10^-3 g cm^-3 for the bottom of the Sun's convection zone -- a number they may reuse in a homework estimate of the convective flux or the tachocline, where it is wrong by a factor of 60 in density.
findings.fix: In logic.ts:856-868, move the "Base of CZ" label to the (6.35, -0.8) entry (whose values already match the standard model) and either relabel (5.9, -2.5) as a plain unlabelled envelope point or drop the label, and move "Radiative zone" to a point interior to the CZ base such as (6.75, 0.5). Replace the Bahcall attribution with the specific table and column the numbers came from, or soften it to "schematic". Extend logic.test.ts:595-599 to assert the labelled CZ-base point lies within 0.1 dex of log T = 6.34 and log rho = -0.72.

findings.title: The test suites pin three of the defects above instead of catching them
findings.evidence: Three assertions lock in behaviour this audit found wrong. (1) stellarEosModel.test.ts:509 `expectRelativeClose(state.electronDegeneracyPressureDynePerCm2, 5.808123130210272e15, 5e-4)` under the name "matches the solar-core EOS checkpoint reference values" -- the 18-digit literal is the previous output of the 192-interval quadrature, and my independent refinement gives 4.654806e15, so the test pins a +24.8% error to 0.05% tolerance and will fail when the quadrature is fixed. (2) apps/demos/src/demos/eos-lab/design-contracts.test.ts:45 `expect(css).not.toMatch(/#[0-9a-fA-F]{3,8}\b/)` reads only style.css, and style.css is indeed clean -- while main.ts:420-424 declares five hex channel colours (with the comment "keeps hex out of CSS"), main.ts:452/495 add "#000"/"#fbbf24", and regimeMap.ts:146-156 adds eight more plus rgba() literals at :152, :153, :422, :444. (3) apps/demos/src/demos/eos-lab/logic.test.ts:82 `expect(result).toContain("×")` positively requires the forbidden Unicode multiplication sign. The e2e spec is uniformly existence-and-change-only: every numeric test is of the form `expect(after).not.toBe(before)` (eos-lab.spec.ts:31-41, :57-61), so no assertion anywhere constrains a value.
findings.scenario: An engineer fixes the quadrature, the checkpoint test goes red, and -- reading a test named "matches the EOS checkpoint reference values" with an 18-digit literal -- reverts the fix or re-pins the literal, keeping the 25% error. Meanwhile apps:no-color-literals stays green while the colour literals accumulate in TypeScript, and the Unicode assertion makes the KaTeX invariant fix look like a regression.
findings.fix: Re-derive the two solar-core literals at stellarEosModel.test.ts:509 and :511 from the converged integral and add a comment naming the independent method used, plus a convergence test (doubling intervals must change P_deg,e by <0.1%). Widen design-contracts.test.ts:44-52 to scan main.ts, regimeMap.ts, mechanismViz.ts and uplotHelpers.ts for hex and rgba literals. Replace logic.test.ts:77-85 with an assertion that formatScientific emits `\\times 10^{...}` and contains no character matching the validator's FORBIDDEN_UNICODE_MATH class.

findings.title: docs/reviews/eos-lab.md declares the demo "Student-ready. All gates green" with "Accessibility (WCAG): Full"
findings.evidence: Line 6: "**Status:** Student-ready. All gates green." Line 14 claims "Three independent review agents verified scientific correctness (22 checks, all correct), coordinate conventions (8 rendering chains, zero sign bugs)", and the capability table claims "Accessibility (WCAG) | Full". Against this audit: the default state's P_deg,e is 24.8% wrong, the regime map prints GAS nine decades of density inside the degeneracy region, six sliders have no aria-valuetext, and three aria-live regions are written from the render loop. The exhibit frontmatter is honest by contrast -- apps/site/src/content/demos/eos-lab.md has status: draft, readiness: experimental, unlisted: true with a specific unlistedReason -- so the repo carries two contradictory readiness claims for the same demo, and the later re-review (docs/reviews/eos-lab-2026-09-03.md) leaves EOS-4 and EOS-5 open without amending the "all gates green" header.
findings.scenario: An instructor or a future agent searching docs/reviews/ for the state of eos-lab reads "Student-ready. All gates green" and "WCAG Full", skips the frontmatter, and assigns the demo to a class -- shipping the 25% P_deg,e error and the mislabelled regime map to students, and telling a screen-reader user the instrument is accessible.
findings.fix: Amend docs/reviews/eos-lab.md line 6 to point at the frontmatter as the single source of readiness truth (status: draft / readiness: experimental / unlisted) and replace the "all gates green" and "WCAG Full" claims with the open-finding list, as docs/reviews/eos-lab-2026-09-03.md already does for EOS-4 and EOS-5. The frontmatter pair itself is correctly set and should stay at status: draft + readiness: experimental until at least the two P0s and the Gamma_eff findings are closed; `content_verified: true` and `plotParityAudit: "pass"` should be revisited at the same time, since the verified content includes the GAS label and the P_deg,e checkpoint.

findings.title: The plotted MOND curve is the full simple-mu interpolation while the Understand card and Model notes tell the student it is the deep-MOND limit (GMa_0)^(1/4)
findings.evidence: index.html:236 shows `$$V_{\rm MOND}\approx\left(G\,M_{\rm vis}\,a_0\right)^{1/4}$$` and index.html:374 says "The MOND curve shows the deep-MOND asymptotic limit ($a \ll a_0$) where $V^4 \approx G\,M\,a_0$" — then contradicts itself in the same sentence with "The full MOND interpolating function transitions smoothly...". main.ts:766-771 plots `row.vMondKmS`, which is galaxyRotationModel.ts:447-459, the simple-mu inverse a = 0.5*a_N*(1+sqrt(1+4a_0/a_N)). I recomputed both for the MW preset: R = 3 kpc plotted 194.50 vs deep-limit 134.25 km/s (equation 31.0% low); R = 10 kpc 196.88 vs 164.60 (16.4% low); R = 30 kpc 179.81 vs 168.68 (6.2%); R = 50 kpc 175.35 vs 168.74 (3.8%). `vMondDeepKmS` (galaxyRotationModel.ts:436) is called only from its own test file. Prior finding GR-3 (docs/reviews/galaxy-rotation.md:24) is still open.
findings.scenario: A student on the Understand tab computes (G*M_vis*a_0)^(1/4) by hand for the MW preset at R = 10 kpc, gets 165 km/s, reads 197 km/s off the pink MOND curve, and cannot reconcile them. The error is largest exactly where students check arithmetic (small R), and the misconceptions list already warns about over-reading MOND fits.
findings.fix: Pick one and make the code and copy agree. Recommended: keep the full interpolation on the plot (it is the physically honest curve) and rewrite index.html:236 as the interpolation relation with the deep limit named as the large-R asymptote, and delete the self-contradicting half of index.html:374. Then either wire `vMondDeepKmS` to an optional dashed asymptote so the equation has a line on the plot, or delete it as dead code.

findings.title: The MOND curve's Newtonian acceleration is spherical GM_vis/R^2, the exact shortcut the model's own comment documents as a removed defect
findings.evidence: galaxyRotationModel.ts:454 `const aN = (this.G_GALAXY * masses.visible) / (radiusKpc * radiusKpc);` uses the spherically-enclosed visible mass, while vVisibleKmS (line 401) now uses `Math.hypot(vBulge, vDisk)` with the exact Freeman disk, after the comment at lines 379-397 recorded that "It previously used a spherical sqrt(G*M_visible(<R)/R), which is not the rotation curve of a disk." The baryonic a_N for a disk is v_visible^2/R. I recomputed both routes: milky-way-like R = 3 kpc 194.50 vs 200.39 km/s (-2.9%); R = 7 kpc 200.18 vs 218.99 (-8.6%, 18.8 km/s); R = 13 kpc 192.74 vs 204.89 (-5.9%); R = 30 kpc 179.81 vs 181.55 (-1.0%). no-dark-matter shows the same shape, -20.3 km/s at R = 7 kpc.
findings.scenario: With the no-dark-matter preset and MOND on, a student compares the pink MOND curve to the amber total curve at R = 7 kpc to judge whether MOND can replace the halo. The MOND curve is 20 km/s too low there purely because the same panel models the disk two different ways, so MOND looks worse at the radius where the comparison is most interesting.
findings.fix: In packages/physics/src/galaxyRotationModel.ts:454, build a_N from the baryonic rotation curve the demo already computes: `const vVis = this.vVisibleKmS({ radiusKpc, params }); const aN = vVis * vVis / radiusKpc;`. Add a test asserting V_MOND -> V_visible as a_0 -> 0 and that a_N agrees with v_visible^2/R for the MW preset at R = 3, 7, 13 kpc.

findings.title: A face-on galaxy schematic carries a blueshift/redshift slit, which for face-on geometry has zero line-of-sight velocity
findings.evidence: main.ts:548-565 draws a horizontal slit with a cyan half labelled `"Blueshift"` (line 562) and a red half labelled `"Redshift"` (line 566), and main.ts:569 captions the same drawing `"Schematic face-on view. V(R) is intrinsic inclination-corrected velocity."`; index.html:347 repeats "Face-on pedagogical view." For a face-on disk the rotation velocity is perpendicular to the line of sight, so the rotational Doppler shift is identically zero and no such slit exists. The drawing is also internally inconsistent about inclination: the disk and halo are drawn as circles (main.ts:491, 500) while the spiral arms are drawn with x*0.9, y*0.58 (main.ts:525-526), an ~50 deg inclined ellipse. Prior finding GR-4 (docs/reviews/galaxy-rotation.md:25) is still open, and readinessReason names it ("an honest caption for the galaxy view").
findings.scenario: The exhibit's own misconceptions list includes "A face-on schematic means real observations are made face-on too" — and the schematic then teaches exactly that, by showing measurable blueshift and redshift on a disk it labels face-on. A student asked where the 21-cm shift readout comes from points at a geometry that produces none.
findings.fix: Draw the disk inclined to match the arms (apply the same 0.9/0.58 ellipse to the disk circle at main.ts:500 and to the halo at main.ts:491), put the slit along the resulting major axis, and change the caption at main.ts:569 and index.html:347 from "face-on" to an inclination-stated view, e.g. "Inclined disk (i ~ 55 deg); the slit samples the line-of-sight component, and V(R) is the inclination-corrected intrinsic speed."

findings.title: All six model sliders are disabled on first load, with no on-screen explanation of how to enable them
findings.evidence: main.ts:894-901: `const lockedPreset = state.presetId !== "custom"; const modelControlsLocked = lockedPreset && !state.challenge.active;` then `haloMassSlider.disabled = modelControlsLocked;` and the same for haloScale, diskMass, diskScale, bulgeMass, bulgeScale. The initial state is `presetId: "milky-way-like"` (main.ts:160), so on load all six are disabled; only the radius marker is live. Nothing in index.html says so — there is no hint text next to the sliders, and the only way to unlock them is to discover the "Custom" option in #presetSelect (index.html:66). The e2e spec encodes the workaround: apps/site/tests/galaxy-rotation.spec.ts:46 must `selectOption("custom")` before it can fill #haloMassSlider. readinessReason already names this ("sliders that show when they are locked") and main.ts:905-907 contains a dead loop that only ever sets `row.hidden = false`.
findings.scenario: A student opens the demo and does play_steps[2], "Increase halo mass and watch the outer curve flatten while M_dark/M_vis rises." The halo-mass slider does not move. Six of the seven sliders are grey. Nothing on the page says to switch the preset dropdown to Custom first, so the central exercise of the demo is unreachable without the instructor.
findings.fix: In apps/demos/src/demos/galaxy-rotation/main.ts, stop disabling the sliders: on any slider input `setCustomFromSliderChange()` (already wired at main.ts:1118-1158) switches the preset to Custom, so locking is unnecessary. If the lock must stay, render a visible hint inside each locked `.control` row ("Preset locked — choose Custom to edit") and set aria-describedby on the inputs, and delete the dead `row.hidden = false` loop at main.ts:905-907.

findings.title: The schematic draws the dark halo on a radial scale 4.6x different from its own radius marker, and clamps it so a zero-mass halo still renders
findings.evidence: main.ts:487 `const haloRadius = clamp((derived.rVirKpc / 260) * 255, 110, 280);` gives 0.981 px/kpc, while the radius marker at main.ts:545 maps 50 kpc onto (slitRight - cx) = (600-72) - 300 = 228 px, i.e. 4.561 px/kpc — a factor 4.65 mismatch inside one 600x600 drawing. I recomputed each preset: milky-way-like r_vir = 218.4 kpc -> drawn 214.2 px, which reads as 47.0 kpc on the slit scale; massive-spiral 242.2 kpc -> 237.5 px = 52.1 kpc; dwarf-galaxy 77.9 kpc -> raw 76.4 px clamped up to 110 px = 24.1 kpc; no-dark-matter r_vir = 0 -> raw 0 px clamped up to 110 px = 24.1 kpc. The lower clamp binds for every haloMass10 below 14.9e10 Msun (I inverted r_vir(M) at 112.2 kpc), so the whole bottom of the slider, zero included, draws one identical halo. The disk circle is a hardcoded r = 158 px = 34.6 kpc on the slit scale. There is no scale bar.
findings.scenario: A student switches between "Dwarf galaxy" and "No dark matter" to see what removing the halo does to the picture, and the halo graphic is pixel-identical in both — including a halo glow around the galaxy that has no halo. A student who instead compares the Milky Way halo to the 50 kpc radius marker reads the 218 kpc virial radius as ending at 47 kpc, just inside the measurement slit, understating the halo by a factor of 4.6.
findings.fix: Give the schematic one radial scale. In main.ts:487 choose px/kpc from the view extent (e.g. `const pxPerKpc = 228 / 50;`), draw the halo at `min(r_vir * pxPerKpc, 290)` with an explicit "halo extends beyond this view" marker when it clips, drop the 110 px floor so haloMass10 = 0 draws nothing, derive the disk radius from a few disk scale lengths instead of the constant 158, and add a labelled scale bar in kpc.

findings.title: Public exhibit copy, the Understand card and the Station column still call the visible-matter curve V_Kep after the model was renamed because it is not Keplerian
findings.evidence: galaxyRotationModel.ts:395-396 records the rename: "(Named vKeplerianKmS until 2026-09-04. A true Keplerian falloff is the point-mass limit sqrt(G*M/R), which this is not and never was at small R.)" The name survives in four reader-visible places: galaxy-rotation.md:26 play_steps "compare $V_{\rm total}$ with $V_{\rm Kep}$ at the same radii" and md:16 learning_goals "Compare visible-matter-only Keplerian predictions" (both rendered by apps/site/src/pages/exhibits/[slug].astro:107 and :125); index.html:232 `$$V_{\rm Kep}(R)\propto R^{-1/2} \quad (R\gg R_d)$$`; and main.ts:1371 Station column `label: "V_Kep (km/s)"`, which is exported into student data tables. The curve is hypot(v_bulge, v_disk_Freeman): I computed v_visible for the MW preset at R = 3 kpc = 160.3 km/s, where a point-mass Keplerian sqrt(G*M_vis(<3)/R) would give 185.2 km/s — 15.5% apart, so the label is wrong precisely where students look first. index.html:356 already states the correct physics ("Closer in the disk is not a point mass, so the curve is not Keplerian there"), contradicting index.html:232 on the same page.
findings.scenario: A student is told in the play steps to compare V_total with "V_Kep", reads on the Understand tab that V_Kep goes as R^(-1/2), measures the blue dashed curve rising from 0 to a 164 km/s peak at R = 7 kpc, and concludes either that the demo is broken or that R^(-1/2) can rise. The same wrong name lands in their exported Station table.
findings.fix: Replace $V_{\rm Kep}$ with $V_{\rm vis}$ (or $V_{\rm bar}$) in apps/site/src/content/demos/galaxy-rotation.md:16,26, apps/demos/src/demos/galaxy-rotation/index.html:232, and the Station column label at main.ts:1371; rewrite the index.html:232 card as the large-R asymptote of the visible curve rather than a definition. Rename `state.show.keplerian` (main.ts:164) to `visible` in the same pass so the internal name stops reseeding the wrong word.

findings.title: The Station prompt compares f_b at 50 kpc to the cosmic 0.157, which for the massive-spiral preset gives 0.21 — above the cosmic value
findings.evidence: main.ts:1365 Station step: "Compare baryon fraction at 50 kpc with the cosmic value (0.157)." and main.ts:1430 synthesisPrompt repeats "how does $f_b(50\,{\rm kpc})$ compare to the cosmic value $0.157$?". I recomputed f_b = M_vis/(M_vis+M_halo) at 50 kpc and at each preset's own r_vir: massive-spiral 0.2125 at 50 kpc vs 0.0740 at r_vir = 242.2 kpc; milky-way-like 0.1215 vs 0.0443 at r_vir = 218.4 kpc; dwarf-galaxy 0.0729 vs 0.0566 at r_vir = 77.9 kpc. The cosmic baryon fraction is a ratio within a virialized halo, and 50 kpc is only 0.21-0.23 r_vir for the two spiral presets, where the baryons are concentrated and the halo is not yet counted.
findings.scenario: A student runs the station on "Massive spiral", reads f_b = 0.213 at 50 kpc, compares it to 0.157, and writes that the galaxy holds more baryons than the universe's share — the opposite of the missing-baryon result. On "Milky Way-like" they get 0.122 and conclude the galaxy is roughly cosmically complete, when within r_vir it retains 0.044, about 28% of cosmic.
findings.fix: In apps/demos/src/demos/galaxy-rotation/main.ts:1365 and :1430, move the comparison to the virial radius, which the demo already computes and displays (#rVirValue): "Compare f_b inside R_vir with the cosmic value 0.157." That needs the readout evaluated at r_vir rather than at the 50 kpc slider cap — either extend the radius slider to r_vir or add an `f_b(<R_vir)` readout from GalaxyRotationModel.baryonFraction at derived.rVirKpc.

findings.title: During a hidden challenge the model sliders stay live while the answer key stays frozen on the original preset, so "Correct" can be reported for a curve no longer on screen
findings.evidence: startChallenge (main.ts:1062-1065) sets `state.presetId = "custom"` and copies the target's params, which makes `lockedPreset` false at main.ts:894 so the six model sliders are enabled for the whole hidden round. checkChallengeAnswer (main.ts:1094-1100) then compares the guess against `state.challenge.target.presetId`, which was fixed at pick time and is never re-derived from `state.params`. The e2e spec cements it: apps/site/tests/galaxy-rotation.spec.ts:92-94 asserts `#haloMassSlider` is enabled during the challenge, fills it to "200", and then clicks #checkChallenge and asserts only that the copy buttons unlock. Nothing re-checks that the displayed curve still is the target.
findings.scenario: A student starts a mystery round on the dwarf-galaxy target, drags halo mass to 200e10 Msun (allowed, readouts are blanked so they cannot see what they did), now sees a steeply flat high-velocity curve, guesses "Massive spiral / flat", and is told "Not yet — target was Dwarf galaxy" for a curve that genuinely looked like a massive spiral. The converse also happens: reshape the curve beyond recognition and still be told "Correct". Either way the feedback is about a curve the student is not looking at.
findings.fix: In apps/demos/src/demos/galaxy-rotation/main.ts, lock the six model sliders while `state.challenge.active && !state.challenge.revealed` (add the condition at main.ts:894) with a visible "locked while the target is hidden" hint, or re-derive the target from the live params at check time so the key always matches the drawn curve. Update apps/site/tests/galaxy-rotation.spec.ts:92-94, which currently asserts the defective behavior.

findings.title: The velocity axis is floored at 240 km/s, squashing the dwarf-galaxy preset into the bottom third of the plot
findings.evidence: main.ts:682-691 `const velocityYMax = state.plotMode === "velocity" ? Math.max(240, ...curve.map(row => row.vTotalKmS), ...) : ...`. I computed the dwarf-galaxy preset's peak over the 260-point grid: V_total,max = 76.80 km/s, so the entire curve occupies 32.0% of the plot height and the top two thirds are empty grid. The dwarf is one of the four mystery-challenge targets (main.ts:152-157), and during a hidden round every numeric readout is blanked to an em dash (main.ts:940-950), so the plot is the only evidence available — while the hint asks the student to judge whether V_total "stays nearly constant or declines like R^(-1/2) between 30 and 50 kpc" (main.ts:1007). The true dwarf ratio is v50/v30 = 59.49/64.73 = 0.919, which must be distinguished from the Keplerian 0.775 inside 32% of the axis.
findings.scenario: A student gets the dwarf target in a mystery round, sees a nearly flat line hugging the bottom of a 240 km/s axis, cannot resolve a 5 km/s drop over 20 kpc at that scale, and guesses the slope class by coin flip on an exercise designed to be read off the plot.
findings.fix: In apps/demos/src/demos/galaxy-rotation/main.ts:682-691, replace the fixed 240 floor with a data-driven axis — a nice-number ceiling about 20% above the largest plotted series (e.g. 100 km/s for the dwarf) — and add numeric y tick labels at the existing five gridlines (currently only one axis title is drawn, main.ts:820-823). Keep the axis stable across a slider drag by rounding to a step so the curve does not jitter.

findings.title: docs/reviews/galaxy-rotation.md still lists the fixed GR-1 as open and as the blocker on promotion past candidate
findings.evidence: docs/reviews/galaxy-rotation.md:22 marks GR-1 as `**P1** | **open**` with the fix "build the benchmark as hypot(v_bulge, v_disk) and add a test asserting V_total === V_visible when haloMass10 = 0", and line 30 concludes "GR-1 should be fixed before this demo is promoted past `candidate`." Both halves of that fix have landed: galaxyRotationModel.ts:405-410 is `return Math.hypot(vBulge, vDisk);` and galaxyRotationModel.test.ts:238-245 sweeps R = 0.25..30 kpc asserting `expect(vVisible).toBeCloseTo(vTotal, 10)` for the zero-halo preset. Meanwhile GR-2 (line 23), GR-3 (24), GR-4 (25) and GR-5 (26) are all still genuinely open — I verified each against the current code — and the doc's line numbers are stale too (it cites galaxyRotationModel.ts:401-404 and main.ts:714-733 for code now at 399-410 and 752-771).
findings.scenario: An instructor or reviewer opens the demo's own review doc to decide whether to assign this demo, reads that the headline P1 is open and that the demo must not be promoted, and either blocks work that is already done or re-fixes an already-fixed model. The same doc hides that GR-2, the one defect that actually reaches a student as a wrong number, is still live and was downgraded to P2.
findings.fix: Update docs/reviews/galaxy-rotation.md: mark GR-1 `fixed 2026-09-04` with the commit and the regression test path, re-rate GR-2 as P0 with the recomputed no-dark-matter numbers (0.000 readout vs 1.421e10 Msun equation at R = 10 kpc), refresh the cited line numbers, and rewrite the Recommendation to name GR-2 as the promotion blocker.

findings.title: content_verified: true and readinessReason omit the open equation defect, so the public readiness claim understates what is wrong
findings.evidence: galaxy-rotation.md:4 `content_verified: true`, md:10 `readiness: candidate`, md:3 `status: beta`, md:11 `readinessReason: "Close to ready. Still to come: clearer wording about the MOND limit, an honest caption for the galaxy view, and sliders that show when they are locked."`, md:12 `lastVerifiedAt: "2026-09-03"`. The three named items are GR-3, GR-4 and the slider lock. GR-2 — the only open finding that puts a wrong number in front of a student (the Understand card's M_dark equation, which I recomputed as 0.000 readout vs 1.421e10 Msun equation for the no-dark-matter preset at R = 10 kpc) — is absent from readinessReason, which is public copy per CLAUDE.md. Separately, index.html and main.ts were last modified 2026-09-10, a week after the 2026-09-03 lastVerifiedAt, so `content_verified: true` certifies a version that no longer exists.
findings.scenario: An instructor browsing the catalog reads the readiness badge and reason, sees three cosmetic-sounding items (wording, a caption, a slider affordance), and assigns the demo for homework — unaware that the equation on the Understand tab contradicts the readout beside it by 42% on the Milky Way preset and manufactures dark matter on the no-dark-matter preset.
findings.fix: In apps/site/src/content/demos/galaxy-rotation.md, add the equation defect to readinessReason as the first item, set `content_verified: false` until a re-verification pass is run against the current files, and bump `lastVerifiedAt` only when that pass happens. Hold `readiness: candidate` / `status: beta` — the evidence supports candidate, not launch-ready, and does not support dropping to a lower tier since the component physics is verified.

findings.title: Readout labelled "Exact central pressure" with no toy qualifier is 174x below the real solar value
findings.evidence:
`
Exact central pressure dyne cm^-2
`. For the default sun-like uniform preset the value is 3GM^2/(8 pi R^4) = 1.3447e15 dyne cm^-2. The accepted solar central pressure is about 2.34e17 dyne cm^-2, so the card shows 5.7e-3 of the real value. The word 'Exact' is literally true only of the uniform-sphere toy, and the readout strip carries no toy-model badge (the badges are on the hero card, a separate scroll region).
findings.scenario: A student copies 'Exact central pressure 1.34x10^15 dyne cm^-2' into a homework answer or station worksheet for a 1 Msun, 1 Rsun star and is wrong by a factor of 174. Nothing adjacent to the number says it is a toy value.
findings.fix: Rename the label in index.html to 'Toy-model central pressure' (and the export row in main.ts exportResults to match), and add the already-written disclaimer as the card's secondary line, e.g. 'uniform-sphere toy; the Sun is ~2x10^17'.

findings.title: Published exhibit copy promises a pressure-scale-height readout the demo never computes
findings.evidence: play_steps[0]: "identify the readouts for gravity, pressure support, pressure scale height, and core temperature"; play_steps[2]: "compare the pressure scale height against the radius"; learning_goals 2 and 3 and model_notes 3 and 4 all build on H_P = P/(rho g); the body text says "pressure scale height tells you how sharply that balance must change"; docs/audits/migrations/hydrostatic-equilibrium-explorer-parity.md names it step 3 of the intended physics chain. `grep -rni "scaleheight|scale height|H_P"` over the demo folder and packages/physics/src/hydrostaticEquilibriumModel.ts returns zero hits. There is no scale-height function, readout, plot tab, or label anywhere.
findings.scenario: A student opens the exhibit page, reads play step 1, opens the demo, and cannot find the pressure-scale-height readout because it does not exist. Two of the four stated learning goals cannot be met with the instrument as built, and the instructor's station sheet asks for a number the demo cannot produce.
findings.fix: Add `pressureScaleHeightCm({ pressureDynePerCm2, densityGPerCm3, gravityCmPerS2 })` = P/(rho g) to packages/physics/src/hydrostaticEquilibriumModel.ts, surface it as a sixth profile tab plus a readout card (units cm and R), and have Anna approve the near-centre behaviour (g -> 0 so H_P -> infinity) before it ships. Until that lands, delete the scale-height language from the exhibit frontmatter and body rather than leaving instructions a student cannot follow.

findings.title: Station-mode CSV and clipboard export emit raw LaTeX in every numeric column
findings.evidence: getSnapshotRow returns `gravity: formatScientificLatex(scenario.shellPoint.gravityCmPerS2, 3)`, `gradient: formatScientificLatex(...)`, `pressureScale: formatScientificLatex(...)`. formatScientificLatex (logic.ts:517) returns `${mantissa} \\times 10^{${exponent}}`. packages/runtime/src/demoModes.ts:304 toCsv just csvEscapes those strings; packages/runtime/src/index.ts:130 formatExportText interpolates them into plain text lines. For the default sun-like shell I recomputed g = G*M*0.55/R^2 = 1.5081e4 cm s^-2 and dP/dr = -2.1262e4 dyne cm^-3, so the CSV cell under the header "g (cm s^-2)" literally reads `1.51 \times 10^{4}` and the clipboard line reads `- Local gravity: 1.51 \times 10^{4} cm s^-2`.
findings.scenario: A lab group runs the station activity, adds four rows, clicks copy CSV, and pastes into Sheets. Every number column is text like `1.51 \times 10^{4}`; no plot or mean can be computed and the whole data-collection activity has to be hand-retyped.
findings.fix: Add a plain-text sibling of formatScientificLatex in logic.ts (e.g. formatScientificAscii -> "1.51e4" or "1.51 x 10^4") and use it in getSnapshotRow and exportResults. Keep formatScientificLatex for KaTeX surfaces only, and add a unit test asserting no backslash appears in any getSnapshotRow value.

findings.title: Exhibit claims has_math_mode: true but the demo runtime is created with hasMathMode: false
findings.evidence: Content file: `has_math_mode: true`. main.ts:1018 `createInstrumentRuntime({ hasMathMode: false, ... })`, and packages/runtime/src/index.ts:106 `if (!args.hasMathMode && candidate === "math") return "concept";` — the math mode is forced off. This is the only demo in the catalog with the flag true (all 20+ others are false), and the flag drives a public 'math mode' TagPill on DemoCard.astro:136 and exhibits/[slug].astro:55 plus the explore filter facet DemoCard.astro:90 `data-math={hasMathMode ? "yes" : "no"}`.
findings.scenario: A student filters Explore by 'math mode', gets exactly this one card, opens /play/hydrostatic-equilibrium-explorer/ and finds no math-mode control; ?mode=math silently resolves to concept. The site's only math-mode promise is the one demo that cannot honour it.
findings.fix: Set has_math_mode: false in the content file (the demo's KaTeX-heavy copy is not the same thing as the runtime math mode), or pass hasMathMode: true in main.ts and add the math-mode surface the flag advertises. Pick one and add a datasets/content test asserting the frontmatter flag matches the value passed to createInstrumentRuntime.

findings.title: The whole Understand panel, and the "Show derivation hints" toggle, are unreachable in student mode
findings.evidence: render(): `stageTabs.hidden = state.explorerMode === "student";` then `if (state.explorerMode === "student") { ... panelUnderstand.hidden = true; }`. state.explorerMode defaults to "student" (main.ts:1030). #panel-understand (index.html 392-594) holds #reasoningLadder, all four equation cards (g = GM(r)/r^2, dP/dr = -rho g, P_c ~ GM^2/R^4, T_c ~ mu G M m_p/(k_B R)), their #gravityNotice/#hydroNotice/#pressureScaleNotice/#temperatureNotice targets, all six misconception cards, and all four `.derivation-toggle` <details> (index.html 455, 476, 497, 519 — the only matches in the folder). derivationToggles (main.ts:932) therefore only ever contains elements inside that hidden panel, and main.ts:1605 `for (const details of derivationToggles) details.hidden = !state.showDerivations;` has no visible effect in student mode.
findings.scenario: A student reaches guided step 6, where the sidebar unlocks the 'Show derivation hints' checkbox, ticks it, and nothing appears anywhere on screen — a dead control. Across the entire seven-step student flow they never see the reasoning ladder, the four equation cards with their live notices, or any of the six misconception cards; render() computes all of that text on every tick and writes it into a permanently hidden subtree.
findings.fix: Either keep .stage-tabs visible in student mode (remove the `stageTabs.hidden = ...` line and let initTabs own panel switching, with the guided step only setting the initially selected tab), or move the four equation cards and the reasoning ladder into #panel-explore and gate them per guided step the way thermalBridgeCard already is. Then make the derivation toggle's target set non-empty in student mode, or hide the toggle until the Understand surface is reachable.

findings.title: Design-system invariant 7 violated: ten --cp-warning / --cp-accent2 legacy aliases in demo CSS
findings.evidence: CLAUDE.md invariant 7: "Token Purity: Zero legacy aliases (--cp-warning, --cp-accent2) in demo code. Use semantic names." grep finds --cp-accent2 at style.css:232, 338, 842, 863, 885, 1195 and --cp-warning at 299, 300, 720, 721. Example line 299-300: `border-color: color-mix(in srgb, var(--cp-warning) 56%, var(--cp-border)); background: color-mix(in srgb, var(--cp-warning) 10%, transparent);`. design-contracts.test.ts:112-116 ('keeps token-first styling') asserts only that the file contains 'stub-demo.css', contains 'var(--cp-', and matches no hex literal — it never checks token purity, so this ships green.
findings.scenario: A theme change that retires --cp-warning or --cp-accent2 (the stated direction of the design system) silently blanks the preset-active border, the challenge-feedback panel and the imbalance state banner in this demo, and no test fails.
findings.fix: Replace --cp-warning with --cp-accent-amber (the demo already uses it for the gravity/imbalance family) and --cp-accent2 with the semantic accent the surface actually means (--cp-accent-ice for selection chrome, --cp-accent-rose for the perturbed state), then add `expect(css).not.toMatch(/--cp-(warning|accent2)\b/)` to design-contracts.test.ts so invariant 7 is enforced rather than assumed.

findings.title: Design-system invariant 1 violated: the star is drawn with no --cp-celestial-* token
findings.evidence: CLAUDE.md invariant 1: "Every SVG celestial object MUST use --cp-celestial-* tokens." `grep -n "cp-celestial" style.css main.ts` returns nothing. The star body instead uses demo-local `--hydro-star-core: color-mix(in srgb, var(--cp-accent) 30%, var(--cp-bg0) 70%)` (style.css:11) and `--hydro-star-outer` (style.css:12), consumed by the hydroStarFill radialGradient in main.ts renderHeroSvg, and the shell marker uses --hydro-shell built from --cp-accent-amber (style.css:13). design-contracts.test.ts asserts nothing about celestial tokens.
findings.scenario: The star in this demo is a different hue from the star in every migrated demo (moon-phases, seasons, eclipse-geometry all key off --cp-celestial-*), so a student moving between exhibits in one class session sees the same object in two colours, and a future change to --cp-celestial-star leaves this demo behind.
findings.fix: Redefine --hydro-star-core/--hydro-star-outer in terms of var(--cp-celestial-star) (or --cp-celestial-sun for a self-luminous body) in style.css:11-12, keeping the per-demo alias names so the SVG does not change, and add `expect(css).toContain("--cp-celestial-")` to design-contracts.test.ts.

findings.title: "Show units" toggle strips units from all six readouts, leaving bare numbers
findings.evidence: All six readout values are built with showUnits hardcoded false: formatMassLatex(..., false), formatRadiusLatex(..., false), scientificQuantityLatex(..., "{\\rm g\\,cm^{-3}}", false), scientificQuantityLatex(..., "{\\rm cm\\,s^{-2}}", false), scientificQuantityLatex(..., "{\\rm dyne\\,cm^{-2}}", false), formatTemperatureLatex(scenario.coreTemperatureScaleK, false) (main.ts:1537-1600). The only unit text is the label span, and main.ts:1532 `readoutUnitLabels.forEach((unit) => { unit.hidden = !state.showUnits; })` hides it. With the checkbox cleared the strip reads "Exact central pressure: 1.34 x 10^15" and "Core-temperature scale: 1.43 x 10^7" with no unit anywhere. Separately, formatTemperatureLatex(..., false) never reaches the MK branch, so the readout says 1.43 x 10^7 while temperatureNotice on the same screen says 14.3 MK, and buildProfileInterpretation (main.ts:341) hardcodes showUnits true while profileCurrentValue honours the toggle, so the big value loses its unit and the sentence below it keeps it.
findings.scenario: A student unchecks 'Show units' (unlocked at the thermal-bridge step), reads 1.43 x 10^7 off the core-temperature card and writes it down with no unit, or assumes MK because that is the format the paragraph beside it uses. CLAUDE.md requires units on every reader-visible number.
findings.fix: Delete the toggleUnits control and the hydro-readout-unit hiding (main.ts:1532, index.html 160-180 toggle-stack) so units are always shown; or, if the toggle must stay, pass state.showUnits through to all six value builders and to buildProfileInterpretation so value and prose agree. Either way make formatTemperatureLatex use the MK form consistently with temperatureNotice.

findings.title: ARIA radiogroups have no arrow-key handling and the profile tablist contains no tabs
findings.evidence: index.html:325 `<div id="profileTabGroup" class="cp-chip-group profile-tabs" role="tablist" aria-label="Profile quantity">` whose five children are `<button class="cp-chip" type="button" data-profile-key="..." aria-pressed="...">` — no role="tab", no aria-selected, no aria-controls. packages/runtime/src/tabs.ts:55-57 `const tabs = tablist.querySelectorAll('[role="tab"]'); if (tabs.length === 0) continue;` so initTabs skips it entirely: no arrow keys, no Home/End, no roving tabindex. The four role="radiogroup" groups (index.html:74 View mode, 112 Local shell state, 143 Density model, 223 Prediction prompt) hold role="radio" buttons; main.ts setSelectionButtons (1136-1158) only writes aria-checked and there is no keydown listener anywhere in main.ts for these groups.
findings.scenario: A screen-reader user hears "Profile quantity, tab list" with zero tabs, and hears "Density model, radio group, Uniform-density toy, radio button, 1 of 2" and presses Right Arrow as the ARIA pattern dictates. Nothing happens. They must discover that Tab + Enter is the only way through, and in the radiogroups every option is a separate tab stop, so reaching the stage past the sidebar takes ~20 extra tabs.
findings.fix: Either give #profileTabGroup role="tab" children with aria-selected/aria-controls so the shared initTabs owns it, or drop role="tablist" and keep it an honest toolbar of aria-pressed toggles. For the chip groups, add a shared arrow-key + roving-tabindex helper to packages/runtime (one copy, reused by every demo's cp-chip-group) rather than a per-demo handler, and call it from main.ts beside initTabs.

findings.title: No e2e spec: /play/hydrostatic-equilibrium-explorer/ is never loaded by any Playwright test
findings.evidence: `ls apps/site/tests/` lists a dedicated spec for 20 demos (angular-size, binary-orbits, blackbody-radiation, cluster-census, conservation-laws, doppler-shift, eclipse-geometry, em-spectrum, eos-lab, galaxy-rotation, keplers-laws, moon-phases, parallax-distance, planetary-conjunctions, retrograde-motion, seasons, spectral-lines, stars-zams-hr, telescope-resolution) and none for this one. The only two hits for "hydrostatic" are smoke.spec.ts:44 (its heading appears on /explore/) and smoke.spec.ts:102 (its thumbnail exists); accessibility.spec.ts:25 only asserts the slug is in a list. reflow.spec.ts:55 `const PLAY_ROUTES = ["play/conservation-laws/"];` so the 320px reflow check never visits it either, and style.css has no breakpoint below 720px while the instructor-mode grid is `clamp(292px, 24vw, 338px) minmax(0, 1fr)` (style.css:16).
findings.scenario: main.ts resolves 60+ elements through `q<T>(selector)` which THROWS on a miss, at module scope. Renaming or deleting any one id in index.html takes the entire demo page down to a blank instrument with a console error, and every gate stays green because no test ever navigates to the page. Likewise a horizontal-scroll regression at 320px is invisible.
findings.fix: Add apps/site/tests/hydrostatic-equilibrium-explorer.spec.ts modelled on moon-phases.spec.ts: load /play/hydrostatic-equilibrium-explorer/, assert zero pageerror/console-error, walk the seven guided steps, switch density model and support mode and assert the hero SVG markup changes, and assert the readout values carry units. Add "play/hydrostatic-equilibrium-explorer/" to PLAY_ROUTES in reflow.spec.ts once the 320px case passes.

findings.title: localShellPatchBalance, the function behind every force arrow, has zero tests
findings.evidence: The whole test file (130 lines, 6 `it` blocks) never calls localShellPatchBalance; I read every assertion. Nothing asserts netForceDyne === 0 at supportFactor 1, nothing asserts netForceDyne < 0 for 0.78 and > 0 for 1.22, nothing asserts pressureInnerDynePerCm2 > pressureOuterDynePerCm2, and nothing asserts pressureForceDifferenceDyne equals gravitationalForceDyne in the balanced case. I verified those four properties by hand (balanced net = 0.000e0 exactly; under net = -1.953e13 dyne; over net = +1.953e13 dyne at r/R = 0.55, M = 1 Msun, R = 1 Rsun, thickness 0.06R, area 1 cm^2) — the code is right, but nothing holds it there.
findings.scenario: Flipping the sign on `pressureDifferenceDynePerCm2 = -pressureGradientApplied * shellThicknessCm` (hydrostaticEquilibriumModel.ts:369) would reverse both pressure arrows and the net arrow in the hero drawing — gravity and pressure would both point inward — and the entire physics suite would stay green, because the only consumer of that value is SVG geometry and no test reads it.
findings.fix: Add a describe block to packages/physics/src/hydrostaticEquilibriumModel.test.ts asserting, for both density models at an ASYMMETRIC radius (r/R = 0.37, not 0 or R): netForceDyne within 1e-9 of 0 at supportFactor 1; netForceDyne/gravitationalForceDyne close to -0.22 at 0.78 and +0.22 at 1.22; pressureInner > pressureOuter; and pressureForceDifferenceDyne equal to densityGPerCm3*gravityCmPerS2*shellThicknessCm*patchAreaCm2 at supportFactor 1.

findings.title: content_verified: true while three frontmatter claims contradict the demo
findings.evidence: `content_verified: true`, `lastVerifiedAt: "2026-09-03"`. Contradictions I confirmed against the code: (1) station_params line 39 `value: "0.61"` for mean molecular weight mu, while every preset in logic.ts:116-171 and the muSlider default (index.html:162) use 0.62 — I computed T_c for both (1.4098e7 K vs 1.4329e7 K), so a student following the station card cannot reproduce the demo's number; (2) predict_prompt line 24 asks about "gravity gets stronger while the star's size stays the same", but the in-app prediction (logic.ts:291, index.html:218) asks about "the same mass squeezed into a smaller radius" with choices up/down/same — different question, different variable held fixed; (3) the pressure-scale-height readout named in play_steps does not exist. docs/audits/migrations/hydrostatic-equilibrium-explorer-parity.md lists "Confirm the UI surfaces the support chain in the same order used here" as still-required verification; that check has not been done.
findings.scenario: An instructor trusts content_verified: true, prints the station card with mu = 0.61 and the gravity-at-fixed-size prediction prompt, and the class finds the demo defaults to mu = 0.62 and asks a different question. The prediction a student wrote on paper cannot be checked against the in-app prediction gate.
findings.fix: Set content_verified: false until the three mismatches are closed, then fix the content: change station_params mu to 0.62, rewrite predict_prompt to match the in-app wording verbatim (single source of truth would be better — export the prompt string from logic.ts and have the station page read it), and remove the scale-height references or ship the readout. Refresh lastVerifiedAt only after that pass.

findings.title: The whole readouts panel is permanently dimmed to 55% opacity; labels fall to 2.59:1 and 1.63:1 contrast with no way to undo it
findings.evidence: index.html:410 `<aside class="cp-demo__readouts cp-panel" ... data-focus-group="readouts-primary">`. style.css:283-287 dims `[data-focus-group]:not([data-focus-group~="<focus>"]):not([data-focus-group~="focus-selector"])` to `opacity: 0.55` for all three values of data-concept-focus, and "readouts-primary" matches none of law2/energy/law3. grep shows exactly one `opacity: 0.55` rule and no reset anywhere in the file, and opacity composites the whole subtree, so the per-card rule at style.css:289-291 (which only adds a drop-shadow) cannot restore it. The inner cards carry their own focus tokens (index.html:446 period = "readouts-primary law3", 441 accel = "readouts-primary energy"), so in the default law2 focus they are dimmed twice: 0.55 x 0.55 = 0.3025. --cp-readout-label-color is --cp-muted (tokens.css:294) = color-mix(#fff 54%, #0f1115) = rgb(145,146,147). Composited over --cp-bg1 #171b22 I computed WCAG contrast 5.54:1 at full opacity, 2.59:1 at 0.55, and 1.63:1 at 0.3025 (AA needs 4.5:1, and 3:1 even for large text).
findings.scenario: Any student loading /play/keplers-laws/ sees the Distance, Speed, Acceleration and Period cards — the instrument's entire numeric output — washed out, and the 'Period P' and 'Acceleration' labels at 1.63:1 are effectively unreadable on a projector or a laptop in a lit classroom. The concept-focus selector has no 'show everything' option, so there is no way to turn it off. The e2e test at keplers-laws.spec.ts:315 reads textContent and passes regardless of opacity, so nothing catches it.
findings.fix: In index.html remove `data-focus-group="readouts-primary"` from the aside at line 410 (the panel is never the thing being de-emphasised) and drop the redundant "readouts-primary" token from the four card elements so each card carries only its concept token. Then in style.css replace `opacity: 0.55` with a de-emphasis that does not touch text contrast — e.g. `border-color` plus a lower-contrast surface — or raise it to a value you have measured at >= 4.5:1 for --cp-muted. Add a design-contract test asserting no ancestor of .cp-readout__label carries an opacity rule, and an e2e check on the computed opacity of .cp-demo__readouts in each concept focus.

findings.title: The 'v' and 'F' arrow labels never move; they sit at their hardcoded markup positions while the arrows travel the orbit
findings.evidence: index.html:121 `<text id="velocityLabel" x="410" y="145" ...>v</text>` and index.html:135 `<text id="forceLabel" x="360" y="190" ...>F</text>`. Neither id appears anywhere in main.ts: `grep -n "velocityLabel\|forceLabel" main.ts` returns nothing, and they are absent from the `elements` map (main.ts:23-109), so no code ever sets their x/y. updateVectors (main.ts:381-409) moves only #velocityLine and #forceLine. The hardcoded (410,145) and (360,190) correspond to the markup's placeholder arrow at planet (400,200); the planet actually starts at perihelion, which orbitalToSvg puts at x = 300 - 0.983*150 = 152.6.
findings.scenario: Student ticks Vectors in Newton mode. At the default perihelion state the arrows are drawn around x=153 on the left of the star while the letters 'v' and 'F' sit at x=410 and x=360 on the right of it, next to nothing — and 'F' lands right on top of the dashed r line and the 'r = ... AU' text. As the planet moves the letters stay put, so the student cannot tell which arrow is which, and at aphelion the velocity arrow passes under the stationary 'F'.
findings.fix: Add velocityLabel and forceLabel to the elements map in main.ts and set their x/y in updateVectors from the arrow endpoints (e.g. a few px beyond x2,y2 along each arrow's direction), guarded so they stay inside the 600x400 viewBox. Add an e2e assertion that the distance from #velocityLabel to the #velocityLine endpoint stays under ~20 px at three different mean anomalies.

findings.title: aria-valuenow on the planet slider is set from true anomaly in (-180, 180], outside its own declared range of 0-360
findings.evidence: index.html:138-147 declares `role="slider" aria-valuemin="0" aria-valuemax="360" aria-valuenow="0" tabindex="0"`. main.ts:804 sets `aria-valuenow` to `Math.round(AstroUnits.radToDeg(state.thetaRad))`, and state.thetaRad comes from stateAtMeanAnomalyRad -> meanToTrueAnomalyRad, whose last step is `Math.atan2(sinT, cosT)` (twoBodyAnalytic.ts:80), so the range is (-pi, pi] -> (-180, 180]. Traced: for the default Earth preset at M = 270 deg, I computed theta = -90.98 deg, so the element announces aria-valuenow="-91" with aria-valuemin="0".
findings.scenario: A screen-reader user tabs to the planet and presses ArrowLeft from perihelion. The slider's value goes to -3, then -6, ... -91, while the widget claims a minimum of 0. NVDA/JAWS compute slider percentage from (now - min)/(max - min), so the announced position is negative or nonsensical for the entire second half of the orbit, and the user is told they are below the minimum of a control they can still move.
findings.fix: In main.ts:804 normalise before publishing: `const deg = ((AstroUnits.radToDeg(state.thetaRad) % 360) + 360) % 360;` and set aria-valuenow from that (aria-valuetext already carries the human-readable string). Add an e2e assertion that Number(aria-valuenow) stays within [0, 360] at several mean anomalies including M > 180 deg.

findings.title: A focusable, aria-hidden, sr-only text input leaves keyboard users a tab stop that does nothing
findings.evidence: index.html:298: `<input id="meanAnomalyDeg" class="sr-only" type="text" aria-hidden="true" value="0" />`. It has no tabindex="-1" and no disabled attribute, so it is in the natural tab order; .sr-only (style.css:295) clips it to a 1x1 px box, and aria-hidden="true" removes it from the accessibility tree — the two attributes contradict each other. main.ts only ever writes to it (line 629) and binds no listener: `grep -n meanAnomalyDeg main.ts` shows lines 39, 629, 995, 1053, 1072, 1102 and no addEventListener, so typing in it changes nothing and the next update() overwrites it. Its only consumer is the e2e wedge test (keplers-laws.spec.ts:600, 619).
findings.scenario: A keyboard-only student tabbing through the controls lands between the mean-anomaly slider and the Play button on an invisible text field. The focus ring is on a 1x1 px clipped element so nothing visible is highlighted, a screen reader announces nothing because the element is aria-hidden, and typing a value has no effect. WCAG 2.1 SC 4.1.2 / the ARIA rule that aria-hidden content must not be focusable are both violated.
findings.fix: Stop using a form control as a test hook. Either add `tabindex="-1"` and `readonly` to index.html:298, or better, drop the input entirely and publish the value as `data-mean-anomaly-deg` on #cp-demo in main.ts:629, updating the two reads in apps/site/tests/keplers-laws.spec.ts (lines ~600 and ~619) to read the attribute.

findings.title: Newton mode's 'Conservation drift' readout can only ever display 0.000%, and the e2e test pins that
findings.evidence: Both modes compute the same analytic state (main.ts:609 calls KeplersLawsModel.stateAtMeanAnomalyRad unconditionally; there is no integrator anywhere in the demo). For that state specificEnergyAu2Yr2 = 0.5*v^2 - mu/r with v from vis-viva, which I reduced analytically to exactly -mu/(2a), and specificAngularMomentumAu2Yr = sqrt(mu*a*(1-e^2)) (keplersLawsModel.ts:138-152) — both independent of M. So the only way either can differ from the baseline is if a, e or M* changed, and captureDriftBaseline() is called on every one of those changes (main.ts:831, 840, 848, 646, 684). logic.ts:108-117 therefore computes computeRelativeDriftPercent(x, x) = 0, and formatSignedPercent(0, ...) returns "0.000%" (no plus sign, since the test is `valuePercent > 0`). index.html:453 labels the panel 'Conservation drift (relative to reset)'. keplers-laws.spec.ts:353-361 asserts only `expect(driftText).toContain("%")`, which "0.000%" satisfies, so the test certifies the dead readout.
findings.scenario: An instructor switches to Newton mode to show that the simulation conserves energy, plays a full orbit at 10x, and reads delta-eps = 0.000%, delta-h = 0.000%. They tell the class 'this is the integrator conserving energy to within a thousandth of a percent'. There is no integrator: the number is 0 by algebra, and it would read 0.000% even if the drawing, the velocity components and the force law were all wrong. A readout labelled as a numerical check that cannot fail is worse than no readout.
findings.fix: Either (a) relabel honestly — make Newton mode show 'eps = -mu/2a, h = sqrt(mu a(1-e^2)): constants of the analytic orbit' with the values and no percentage, mirroring the Kepler-mode '~0 (analytic)' text in logic.ts:98-99; or (b) if the pedagogical goal is to show drift, add a real leapfrog/RK4 integrator for Newton mode in packages/physics and compute the drift against the analytic constants. (a) is the honest small fix. Either way replace the `toContain("%")` assertion in keplers-laws.spec.ts:361 with one that distinguishes a measured drift from a structural zero.

findings.title: The keyboard shortcuts panel advertises Space, Home/End and arrows as global; they only work while the planet glyph has focus
findings.evidence: index.html:205-211 lists Space (Play/Pause), Home/End (Perihelion/Aphelion) and Left/Right (Move along orbit) in a 'Keyboard shortcuts' disclosure in the controls panel, and createDemoModes repeats Space and Home/End in the help overlay (main.ts:1023-1024). But those four keys are handled only in the listener attached to `elements.planetGroup` (main.ts:891-932). The document-level listener (main.ts:934-973) handles k/n/1-6 only and returns early for any target inside `input, select, textarea, button, a, summary, [contenteditable], [role=button]`. Traced: with focus on <body> or on the page after a click outside, ArrowRight and Home reach no handler at all, and Space reaches none either (it just scrolls the page).
findings.scenario: Student reads the shortcuts list, clicks on the stage background, and presses Space expecting Play/Pause. The page scrolls and the orbit does not move. They press Home expecting to jump to perihelion; nothing happens. Nothing in the list says 'first Tab to the planet', and the discoverable affordance (the list) is the misleading one. Conversely, 1-6 and k/n do work globally but are the only ones not reachable from the planet's own documented key set.
findings.fix: Move the Space/Home/End/arrow cases into the document-level handler in main.ts:934 (keeping the input/button guard, and keeping the planetGroup handler so the role=slider stays independently operable), or scope the copy honestly: change index.html:205-211 to 'With the planet focused (Tab to it): ...' and split the globally-bound keys into their own list. Add e2e coverage pressing Home, End, ArrowRight and Space with focus on body and asserting the mean anomaly actually changed — there is no keyboard test today.
