findings.title: The Kepler-3 period-scaling hint reads 'x 1.00' for every slider move because it compares against the previous frame, not the previous orbit
findings.evidence: main.ts:572-585: `const previous = state.pendingPeriodComparison ? state.periodReferenceYr : period;` then at line 583-584 `state.periodReferenceYr = period; state.pendingPeriodComparison = false;`. The slider's input handler sets pendingPeriodComparison = true and calls update() on every single input event (main.ts:828-832), so periodReferenceYr is overwritten on each event and 'previous' is always the period from one slider step earlier. Traced numerically: the a slider is 1000 steps over 0.3-40 AU (index.html:218-227), so one step multiplies a by 10^(2.1249/1000) = 1.00490 and P by 1.00735 — buildPeriodScalingHint (logic.ts:69-80) renders `\times 1.01` at best, and the is-active highlight needs |ratio-1| > 0.03 (main.ts:582), which one step never reaches. Dragging from a=1 to a=4 shows x1.00/x1.01 the whole way instead of the x8.00 the helper is built to show. Presets work (one big jump, main.ts:672).
findings.scenario: Student doing play_steps 3 drags the semi-major axis slider from 1 AU to 4 AU to watch Kepler 3. The hint under the slider reads '$P \propto a^{3/2}$ (for fixed M). $\Delta P$: x 1.00 vs previous.' at every position and never lights up, so the headline scaffold for the third law silently contradicts the law. The e2e test at keplers-laws.spec.ts:449-455 uses fill() (a single jump) and asserts only toContainText("x"), which x1.00 also satisfies, so it passes either way.
findings.fix: Anchor the comparison to a user-meaningful reference rather than the last frame: keep `state.periodReferenceYr` fixed at the value in force when the student last pressed a preset or Reset, and update it only there (plus an explicit 'set reference' affordance), so the hint reads 'x 8.00 vs Earth'. Move the ratio logic's reference handling into logic.ts and unit-test a multi-step drag (ten successive small updates) asserting the reported ratio equals the end-to-end ratio, not 1.00.

findings.title: Screen-reader position announcements are driven from inside the requestAnimationFrame render loop
findings.evidence: update() ends with `maybeAnnouncePosition();` (main.ts:630), and update() is called from the rAF step function on every frame while playing (main.ts:704). maybeAnnouncePosition (main.ts:162-167) throttles to one announcement per 500 ms, then announcePosition (main.ts:783-806) writes a new string into #orbitStatus, which is `role="status" aria-live="polite" aria-atomic="true"` (index.html:406). Because the string always contains a changing distance and velocity, setLiveRegionText (packages/runtime/src/liveRegion.ts:2-6) takes the 'changed' branch and the live region updates twice a second for as long as the animation runs. CLAUDE.md states live-region announcements must never be inside a render loop.
findings.scenario: A screen-reader student presses Play. Every 500 ms the polite live region replaces its content with 'orbit, distance 1.02 AU, velocity 29.4 km/s, 53% through orbit'. aria-atomic="true" means the whole string is re-read each time, so the user hears an endless stream of interrupted half-sentences and cannot reach or hear any other control until they find Pause — which they cannot hear themselves tab to.
findings.fix: Remove the maybeAnnouncePosition() call from update() in main.ts:630 and keep announcements on discrete user actions only (the existing maybeAnnouncePosition(true) calls after slider input, presets, toggles, keydown and timeline scrub already cover those). While playing, announce once on start ('playing, one orbit every N seconds') and once on stop with the final state. Add an e2e test that counts #orbitStatus mutations over 3 s of playback and asserts <= 2.

findings.title: The orbit is drawn with reversed handedness (clockwise), contradicting the repo's own documented north-up convention
findings.evidence: main.ts:181-189 orbitalToSvg: `xOrb = -rAu * Math.cos(thetaRad)`, `yOrb = rAu * Math.sin(thetaRad)`, screen x = cx + xOrb*scale, screen y = cy - yOrb*scale — i.e. screen_x = cx - r cos(theta), screen_y = cy - r sin(theta). That is a reflection about the vertical axis, which reverses chirality. Traced the screen path as theta increases from 0: theta=0 -> (cx - r, cy) at 9 o'clock; theta=90 deg -> (cx, cy - r) at 12 o'clock; theta=180 deg -> (cx + r, cy) at 3 o'clock; theta=270 deg -> (cx, cy + r) at 6 o'clock. 9 -> 12 -> 3 -> 6 is clockwise on screen. The physics model is counter-clockwise (keplersLawsModel.ts:115-116, x = r cos(theta), y = r sin(theta), with v_theta = (mu/h)(1 + e cos(theta)) > 0 always, so motion is in +theta). CLAUDE.md states 'a north-up (counter-clockwise) orbit needs cy - r*sin(theta)' and lists which demos are still clockwise; keplers-laws is not among them, and no UI copy says the view is from the south.
findings.scenario: Student compares the demo to the standard solar-system figure in their textbook (planets counter-clockwise viewed from the north ecliptic pole) and sees the planet going the other way. Worse for instruction: this demo is the Kepler-3 companion to retrograde-motion and planetary-conjunctions, so a student reasoning about which way a planet overtakes another gets the opposite sense here than in a correctly oriented demo. The mirror is self-consistent (the drag inverse, apsides, foci and velocity arrow all follow it), so no test or readout reveals it.
findings.fix: Flip the mapping to the project convention in main.ts:183-188: `xOrb = rAu*Math.cos(thetaRad)` (drop the negation), which puts perihelion on the right and makes the motion counter-clockwise. Then change the three places that encode the mirror: updateOrbitPath's ellipse offset to `SVG_CENTER.x - c` (main.ts:266), updateFociMarkers' second focus to `SVG_CENTER.x - 2*c` (main.ts:335), updateApsidesMarkers' peri/aph x to `cx + (rx - c)` / `cx - (rx + c)` (main.ts:346, 355), and updateVectors' `vx = -stateAtM.vxAuPerYr` to `+` (main.ts:390), plus getAngleFromEvent to `atan2(cy - svgY, svgX - cx)` (main.ts:749). This also removes the need for the canvas mirror in the next finding. Extract the whole mapping into logic.ts first so the change is covered by unit tests.

findings.title: All of the demo's geometry and screen mapping lives in main.ts, so none of the drawing math has a unit test
findings.evidence: The invariants file states 'Pure UI logic goes in each demo's logic.ts (tested); main.ts is thin DOM wiring.' main.ts is 1154 lines / 42 KB and holds every coordinate decision: orbitalToSvg (181-189), updateOrbitPath's ellipse geometry rx/ry/c (261-270), drawOrbitCanvas's independent and differently-oriented mapping (278-322), apsides placement (341-365), the velocity/force arrow scaling (381-409), and the 30-point wedge construction (411-491). logic.ts holds only formatting, slider mapping and time<->anomaly helpers; not one of the functions above is exported or tested. The design-contract test that claims to cover this (design-contracts.test.ts:150-158) only asserts `mainTs.not.toMatch(/function\s+orbitalPeriod/i)` and `/function\s+stateAtMean/i` — it would pass with every geometry bug in this report still present.
findings.scenario: The three drawing defects in this audit (constant-length arrows, a-independent scale, mirrored canvas) all live in untestable code, which is why the prior physics review verified every equation in packages/physics and still missed all three. The next person who changes the scale, the mirror or the arrow lengths has no test that can fail, so the defect class keeps reproducing — the same pattern MEMORY.md records for the eclipse sign bugs.
findings.fix: Extract the pure geometry from main.ts into logic.ts as data-in/data-out functions — `orbitalToSvg({rAu, thetaRad, aAu, center, scalePx})`, `ellipseGeometry({aAu, e, scalePx})`, `apsidesPixels(...)`, `arrowScale({speedAuPerYr, refSpeedAuPerYr})` — leaving main.ts to set attributes from their return values. Then unit-test the round trip (orbitalToSvg followed by the drag inverse returns theta), the handedness (theta = 90 deg is above centre, theta = 0 and 180 deg are on opposite sides), and that rx differs for a = 1 vs a = 5 at a fixed scale. Replace the two grep assertions in design-contracts.test.ts:150-158 with a check that main.ts contains no Math.cos/Math.sin/Math.sqrt calls.

findings.title: No unit test asserts a single converted physical number; the CGS conversions are untested and 'kinetic + potential = total' is true by construction
findings.evidence: Every buildReadouts test asserts only unit STRINGS (logic.test.ts:104-114, 136-147) or structure (116-122, 149-165). The two numeric ones, 'kinetic + potential = total energy' (124-134), compare `kinetic + potential` against `total` — but logic.ts:141 defines `potentialAu2Yr2 = args.specificEnergyAu2Yr2 - kineticAu2Yr2`, so the sum is the total identically, for any conversion factor including a wrong one. The CGS converters au2PerYr2ToCm2PerS2 (logic.ts:32-36) and au2PerYrToCm2PerS (logic.ts:38-42) are never given a value and checked against one: I recomputed h = 6.2832 AU^2/yr = 6.2832 x (1.495978707e13 cm)^2 / 3.15576e7 s = 4.4558e19 cm^2/s, and no test asserts that number or anything like it. If the yr->s factor were applied squared in au2PerYrToCm2PerS (a one-character error), every test in the file would still pass.
findings.scenario: A refactor of the AU/yr -> CGS conversions ships a factor-of-3.16e7 error in the 201 (CGS) unit system. All 30 logic tests stay green, the design-contract tests stay green, and the e2e suite stays green because keplers-laws.spec.ts:109-121 only checks that the unit label contains 'cm'. An ASTR201 student doing the CGS exercise copies an angular momentum wrong by seven orders of magnitude. This is exactly the failure mode MEMORY.md records as 'tests encode defects'.
findings.fix: Add numeric assertions to logic.test.ts with independently computed expected values and explicit units: for speedAuPerYr = 2*pi, velocity.value in 101 must be 29.785 km/s and in 201 must be 2.9785e6 cm/s; for specificAngularMomentumAu2Yr = 2*pi, conservation.h.value in 201 must be 4.4558e19 cm^2/s (tolerance 1e-4 relative); for accelAuPerYr2 = 4*pi^2, acceleration.value in 101 must be 5.931 mm/s^2. Also compute potential independently as -mu/r rather than total minus kinetic so the sum test stops being an identity.

findings.title: Nothing tests the demo's central claim that the planet is faster at perihelion than at aphelion
findings.evidence: The exhibit's stated misconception is 'Planets move at the same speed all along their orbits' (keplers-laws.md) and its first learning goal is 'Describe how orbital speed changes along an ellipse'. The only test touching the speed readout is 'all four primary readouts display non-empty values' (keplers-laws.spec.ts:315-330), which asserts `parseFloat(velocity) > 0`. No test anywhere compares two orbital positions: grep for Home/End/ArrowRight/#velocityValue across the spec finds no before/after comparison, and logic.test.ts never exercises stateAtMeanAnomalyRad at two anomalies. The one genuine physics test, the wedge-area check (keplers-laws.spec.ts:578-644), runs only on the default Earth preset at e = 0.017 — I computed that the perihelion/aphelion radius ratio there is just 1.035, so a geometrically wrong wedge would spread far less than the test's 1.05x tolerance at that eccentricity.
findings.scenario: A sign flip in the perifocal velocity rotation, or an r(theta) with (1 - e cos theta) instead of (1 + e cos theta), would swap fast and slow ends of the orbit — the orbital analogue of the waxing/waning swap this repo's verification notes warn about — and the entire test suite would stay green, because every speed assertion is 'greater than zero' and the one area assertion runs on a near-circle where both versions look the same.
findings.fix: Add an e2e test that reads #distanceValue and #velocityValue at the High-e preset (a = 5, e = 0.9) with the timeline at M = 0 and at M = 500/1000, and asserts r_peri < r_aph while v_peri > v_aph, with the ratio checked against the computed value (v_peri/v_aph = (1+e)/(1-e) = 19.0 for e = 0.9). Add the wedge-area test a second parameterisation at the High-e preset. In logic.test.ts, assert the model's own speeds at M = 0 vs M = pi for e = 0.9 against independently computed numbers.

findings.title: No reader-visible equation or symbol in the sidebar or readout strip is KaTeX; HTML numeric entities slip past the validator
findings.evidence: index.html:536 renders the demo's central equation as plain text: `f = (1 + cos α)/2 = 1.000`. Also :74, :85, :86, :100 (`α`) and :101 (`0° = Full, 180° = New`). scripts/validate-math-formatting.mjs:33 matches literal characters only -- `/[°☉µμ′″×−∝≈∞αβγ...]/u` -- so `α` (nine ASCII characters) and `°` are invisible to it; `grep -P` for literal glyphs in index.html returns NONE while the page renders α and °. The demo already calls initMath(document) (main.ts:1093) and uses real KaTeX in the shelf tabs (index.html:562, `$f = \\frac{1 + \\cos\\alpha}{2}$`), so this is a lapse, not a capability gap. packages/theme/styles/layer-instrument.css:110 guards only `.cp-layer-instrument .katex { text-transform: none; }` -- an entity is not inside .katex and inherits whatever an ancestor does. I checked and no ancestor of these five spans is currently uppercased, so this is not a live rendering bug today; it is the contract violation that made the 2026-09-05 bug possible, sitting in the demo CLAUDE.md names as the golden reference every other demo copies.
findings.scenario: Someone adds `text-transform: uppercase` to .cp-label or .cp-readout__value--equation for visual consistency -- the kind of change the theme already makes on .cp-readout__label -- and the readout silently reads "F = (1 + COS Α)/2". Α is capital Alpha, a different symbol; the DOM text stays correct so screen readers and every test still pass, exactly as in the 94-node incident. Separately, two tests now PIN the violation: design-contracts.test.ts:100 asserts `html` contains the literal "f = (1 + cos", and moon-phases.spec.ts:49-50 assert the rendered page contains "α = Sun–Moon–Earth angle" and "0° = Full, 180° = New", so authoring the equation correctly turns three tests red.
findings.fix: Replace all six sites in index.html with KaTeX: `$\\alpha$`, `$0^{\\circ}$`, `$180^{\\circ}$`, and `$f = \\frac{1 + \\cos\\alpha}{2} =$` with the numeric span outside the math. Then teach the validator about entities: in scripts/validate-math-formatting.mjs add a second pattern for `&#x0?3[9a-c][0-9a-f];|&#9[0-9]{2};|°|×|−|α|θ|π` so the escape hatch closes for every demo, not just this one. Update design-contracts.test.ts:100 to assert on `id="illumination-equation-value"` plus a `.katex` node, and moon-phases.spec.ts:49-55 to match the rendered KaTeX text.

findings.title: Nothing anywhere tests which limb the lit crescent is drawn on; inverting isWaxing leaves every test green
findings.evidence: The only assertions on computePhaseViewPath's physics-bearing output are `expect(path).not.toBe("")` and `expect(path).toContain("A")` for 225 (line 384-388) and 45 (390-394), and `not.toBe("")` plus `toContain("M 0")` for 270 (376-382) -- where the real expectation is left in a comment, `// isWaxing = true (270 > 180), squeeze >= 0 -> flag 0 0 1`, asserting nothing. I traced the effect of flipping logic.ts:187 from `normalized > 180` to `normalized < 180`: a=0 takes the illum>0.99 full-circle branch (unchanged, passes); a=180 returns "" (unchanged, passes); a=270 yields `M 0 -60 A 60 60 0 0 0 0 60 A 1.1e-14 60 0 0 1 0 -60`, which still contains "M 0" and is non-empty (passes); 225 and 45 are still non-empty and still contain "A" (pass). The e2e spec is no better: apps/site/tests/moon-phases.spec.ts:437-442 asserts only that `#lit-portion`'s `d` attribute is truthy. So a complete east-west mirror of every phase ships green.
findings.scenario: A refactor of the four arc-flag branches mirrors the terminator. Every waxing phase draws its crescent on the east limb and every waning phase on the west, the full/new/quarter cases look unchanged, 59 unit tests and 40 e2e tests pass, and a class spends a lab period reading waxing moons as waning ones -- the same failure mode the project's gotchas file records from the last swap.
findings.fix: Add a geometric assertion in apps/demos/src/demos/moon-phases/logic.test.ts that does not inspect the path string: parse the two arcs with the W3C endpoint parameterization (or sample the path in a jsdom SVGGeometryElement) and assert sign(centroid_x) > 0 for alpha in {200, 225, 270, 315, 340} and < 0 for {20, 45, 90, 135, 160}, plus enclosed_area/(pi*r^2) === (1+cos alpha)/2 within 1e-3 at the same ten angles. I ran exactly that check and it currently passes at every one of them, so the test can be added green and will then hold the limb side.

findings.title: The waxing/waning test checks only alpha = 0 and 180, the symmetric pair that already hid this bug once
findings.evidence: `test("waxing/waning flips after full", ...)` asserts exactly two points: waxingWaningFromPhaseAngleDeg(180) === "Waxing" and (0) === "Waning". I substituted the classic sign error -- daysSinceNew computed as ((180 - alpha + 360) % 360)/360 * P instead of ((alpha - 180 + 360) % 360)/360 * P -- and recomputed: the flipped model still gives Waxing at 180 and Waning at 0, so the test still passes, while at alpha=225 it returns "Waning" (correct: Waxing) and at alpha=45 "Waxing" (correct: Waning). CLAUDE.md's verification gotchas say in as many words: "Test physics at asymmetric points, not only symmetric ones: a waxing/waning swap passed because tests checked only full and new moon." The sibling test "phase names follow legacy bins" (line 12) likewise omits 225 and 315, the only two bins whose names encode waxing.
findings.scenario: Any future edit to daysSinceNewFromPhaseAngleDeg that flips the elongation sign passes CI. The timeline header reads "WANING" while the Moon fills toward Full, the Waxing/Waning badge and the Station Mode 'trend' column are inverted for every intermediate phase, and the rise/set line is 12 hours out for everything except the quarters -- the identical regression riseSetModel.ts's header comment says was shipped and later measured.
findings.fix: In packages/physics/src/moonPhasesModel.test.ts extend the waxing/waning test to the four asymmetric anchors -- 225 and 315 must be "Waxing", 45 and 135 must be "Waning" -- and assert daysSinceNewFromPhaseAngleDeg(270) = 7.3825 and (90) = 22.1475 so the direction of time is pinned numerically. Add phaseNameFromPhaseAngleDeg(225) === "Waxing Crescent" and (315) === "Waxing Gibbous" to the bin test.

findings.title: logic.test.ts reimplements the whole physics model as a mock, so the demo-side tests never exercise @cosmic/physics
findings.evidence: `function mockCallbacks(...)` (lines 29-59), under the comment "Mock callbacks (avoid importing @cosmic/physics)", re-derives the illumination formula `(1 + Math.cos(rad)) / 2`, the full eight-bin phase-name ladder, `((normalized - 180 + 360) % 360)/360 * 29.53`, the waxing/waning rule and the 29.53 d synodic month. That is the fourth copy of this physics: packages/physics/src/moonPhasesModel.ts, this mock, the duplicate normalizeAngle in exportPayload.ts:12, and computeApproxRiseSet in logic.ts:81. normalizeAngle alone is defined four times in the repo (moonPhasesModel.ts:15, logic.ts:38, exportPayload.ts:12, eclipse-geometry/logic.test.ts:39) while @cosmic/math exports no angle helper at all. The synodic month is also duplicated: moonPhasesModel.ts:1 hardcodes 29.53 while packages/physics/src/astroConstants.ts:27 already defines MEAN_SYNODIC_MONTH_DAYS = 29.530588, which nothing imports.
findings.scenario: MoonPhasesModel.illuminationFractionFromPhaseAngleDeg is changed to (1 - cos a)/2, or the phase bins are rotated by one slot. Every test in logic.test.ts -- which the design-contracts suite and the migration checklist treat as this demo's physics coverage -- still passes, because they test the mock. The only file that would notice is moonPhasesModel.test.ts, whose own gaps are the previous two findings.
findings.fix: Delete mockCallbacks from apps/demos/src/demos/moon-phases/logic.test.ts and import MoonPhasesModel from @cosmic/physics (exportPayload.ts already does, so the dependency is present); keep injection only where a test deliberately stubs an edge case, as the illum=0.005 case at line 397 does. Delete the duplicate normalizeAngle in exportPayload.ts:12 and import it from ./logic, and have moonPhasesModel.ts import MEAN_SYNODIC_MONTH_DAYS from ./astroConstants instead of its own 29.53 literal (updating the one test that asserts 29.53/2 to the constant).

findings.title: A physics review still in the repo certifies "Issues Found: None" for a rise/set formula later measured 3.7 hours wrong
findings.evidence: Line 33 of the review table: "| Moon rise shift = (alpha - 180) / 360 * 24 hours | `shiftHours = ((phaseAngleDeg - 180) / 360) * 24` | ... | CORRECT |", and line 112: "None. All physics equations, phase conventions, terminator geometry, rise/set calculations, and rendering chains are correct." That review is dated 2026-02-07 (git 144ae01). packages/physics/src/riseSetModel.ts then documents, from 2026-09-10 (commits 4351045 and 5a57f5b), that this approach "borrowed the Sun's declination for the Moon" and "Measured 2026-09-10 at 45 N on the June solstice, it read 'Rises ~4 PM, Sets ~8 AM' against a correct ~7:43 PM to ~4:17 AM" -- a 3.7 h error at rise. I independently reproduce the corrected figures (dec -23.44 deg, 8.57 h above the horizon, 19:43-04:17). The review also states "Snap to cardinal phases ... within 5 degrees" while logic.ts:9 sets SNAP_DEGREES = 2, and describes a `shiftHours` variable that no longer exists in main.ts. Nothing in the file marks it superseded.
findings.scenario: The next reviewer or promotion gate opens docs/reviews/moon-phases.md, reads "Issues Found: None" with a table of ticked equations, and treats the demo's physics as audited. The audit it is trusting certified the specific defect that was later found by hand, so the document actively lowers the chance of catching the next one -- and it is the template the other 13 demo reviews were generated from in the same commit.
findings.fix: Add a dated superseded banner at the top of docs/reviews/moon-phases.md stating that the 2026-02-07 verdict is retracted for the rise/set section, strike the line-33 row, and replace lines 110-112 with the actual history: the shift-by-phase model was wrong by the full seasonal swing and was replaced on 2026-09-10 by moonDeclinationDeg + moonRiseSetLocalTimeHours. Correct the SNAP_DEGREES value. Then check whether the other 13 reviews from commit 144ae01 carry the same unfalsifiable "Issues Found: None" ending.

findings.title: The demo re-derives rise/set physics in logic.ts, and that copy is the one the UI uses whenever Advanced is off
findings.evidence: logic.ts opens with the comment "pure UI logic (no DOM, no @cosmic/physics)" and then at line 81 defines `computeApproxRiseSet(phaseAngleDeg)` returning `riseHour = (18 + phaseAngleDeg / 15) % 24`. main.ts:338 calls it on the else branch of `if (advancedEnabled)`, so with the Advanced toggle off -- the default -- the on-screen rise/set line comes from demo code, not from @cosmic/physics, while the export (exportPayload.ts -> riseSetViewModel.ts) always goes through moonRiseSetLocalTimeHours. The invariants are explicit: "Physics lives in packages/physics. Demo code calls models; it never re-derives equations." I verified the two paths currently agree exactly -- at alpha = 0, 37, 90, 180, 225, 270, 294, 315 both give 18:00/06:00, 20:28/08:28, 00:00/12:00, 06:00/18:00, 09:00/21:00, 12:00/00:00, 13:36/01:36, 15:00/03:00 -- because moonRiseSetLocalTimeHours with useAdvanced:false sets phi = 0, where every object is above the horizon for 12 h. The agreement is a coincidence of the equator case, not a shared derivation.
findings.scenario: The next correction to the rise/set physics -- refraction, parallax, the 5.1 deg inclination, or a different reference day than 80 -- is made in packages/physics, lands green, and the default view of the demo keeps showing the old numbers while the exported CSV shows the new ones. That is precisely the shape of the September regression: one of the two paths was fixed and the discrepancy was only found by hand at 45 N.
findings.fix: Delete computeApproxRiseSet from apps/demos/src/demos/moon-phases/logic.ts and collapse main.ts:311-342 to a single call to moonRiseSetLocalTimeHours({ phaseAngleDeg, latitudeDeg, dayOfYear, useAdvanced: advancedEnabled }), which already implements the equator/equinox fallback internally. Move its four spot-check assertions from logic.test.ts:234-258 into packages/physics/src/riseSetModel.test.ts against the real model. Then correct logic.ts's header comment, which will finally be true.

findings.title: A screen-reader user driving the main phase slider is never told the phase, illumination, or day
findings.evidence: The readout strip (index.html:516) is `<div class="cp-readout-strip cp-demo__readouts" aria-label="Readouts">` with no aria-live and no aria-atomic; #phase-name, #illumination, #days-since-new and #illumination-equation-value are updated by main.ts:450-454 with bare textContent. The #angle range input (index.html:90-99) has no aria-valuetext and no aria-describedby. The only textual announcement of the physics is aria-valuetext on #moon-group (main.ts:458), which a screen reader voices only when focus is on that SVG group. #status (index.html:204) is a correct role=status/aria-live=polite region, but setLiveRegionText is called only for the shadow toggle, the Focus Moon button and Copy results -- never for a phase change. I traced every write path in update() (main.ts:482-489) and confirmed no live region is touched.
findings.scenario: A blind student tabs to "Phase angle alpha (deg)" -- the control the demo's own play_steps tell them to move -- presses ArrowRight, and hears "91". They hear no phase name, no illuminated percentage and no day number, so the demo conveys nothing. The workaround (find the Focus Moon button, move focus into an SVG group, then use different arrow-key step sizes) is undiscoverable from the slider and is not mentioned beside it.
findings.fix: In apps/demos/src/demos/moon-phases/main.ts, set `angleInputEl.setAttribute("aria-valuetext", data.ariaValueText)` alongside the existing #moon-group write at line 458 -- computeReadoutData already builds the string. Keep it out of the rAF path: guard the write so it is skipped while isAnimating, matching the project's rule about announcements inside a render loop (which the current 60 Hz aria-valuetext update on #moon-group also breaks). Add an e2e assertion in apps/site/tests/moon-phases.spec.ts that #angle's aria-valuetext contains the phase name after a slider change.

findings.title: Station Mode's synthesis text misdefines the illuminated fraction, and is wrong by 10 percentage points at the gibbous phases
findings.evidence: synthesisPrompt: "The Sun always lights half the Moon. The phase is the fraction of that lit half we can see from Earth." The first sentence is right; the second is not. f = (1 + cos a)/2 is the illuminated fraction of the apparent disc AREA. The fraction of the lit hemisphere that is visible is a different quantity: the near side and the lit side are hemispheres whose poles are separated by a, their intersection is a lune of dihedral angle (180 - a), and a lune of angle theta has area 2*theta*R^2 against a hemisphere's 2*pi*R^2, giving 1 - a/180. At a = 45 the demo reports f = 0.8536 while the fraction of the lit half that is visible is 0.7500 -- a 10.4 point gap, 12% relative. The two agree only at a = 0, 90 and 180, which is why the error survives every cardinal-phase check. The same page's learning_goals (moon-phases.md:18) name this exact distinction as an objective: "Distinguish illuminated fraction from how much of the Moon you can see."
findings.scenario: A class works through Station Mode, records f for eight phases, and is then asked to 'Explain' using a sentence that defines f incorrectly. They write down that a gibbous Moon shows 85% of the lit half, when it shows 75% of the lit half and 85% of the disc. The demo fails the one learning goal it lists for itself, and the station card is the artifact the instructor collects.
findings.fix: Rewrite the synthesisPrompt in apps/demos/src/demos/moon-phases/main.ts:1038-1041 to define f as what it is: "The Sun always lights half the Moon. $f$ is the fraction of the Moon's visible DISC that is lit -- the projected area, not a fraction of the lit hemisphere." Then add the contrast the learning goal asks for, with the number: "At $\\alpha = 45^{\\circ}$, $f = 0.85$ of the disc looks lit, while only $1 - \\alpha/180^{\\circ} = 0.75$ of the Sun-lit half faces Earth." Relabel the "Illuminated (%)" readout and export row to "Disc illuminated (%)".

findings.title: The timeline crescent icons draw the lit sliver detached from the limb, which is geometrically impossible
findings.evidence: `.phase-icon.waxing-crescent::after { left: 50%; width: 25%; border-radius: 0 50% 50% 0; }` and `.phase-icon.waning-crescent::after { left: 25%; width: 25%; border-radius: 50% 0 0 50%; }`, on a 24 px `.phase-icon` (style.css:314-321) that is `border-radius: 50%; overflow: hidden` with a dark `--cp-bg3` background and a light `--cp-text2` lit band. The waxing band therefore occupies x = 12-18 px of 24, leaving x = 18-24 -- the entire west limb -- dark; the waning band occupies x = 6-12, leaving x = 0-6, the east limb, dark. A crescent's lit region must touch the limb, because the limb is the edge of the sphere farthest from the terminator. The sibling icons are consistent (first-quarter left:50%, third-quarter left:0, gibbous widths 75% touching their limbs), and the main phase SVG draws the crescents correctly -- I measured its lit region spanning x = 0 to +60 at alpha = 225, i.e. hard against the west limb -- so the icon strip contradicts the drawing directly above it.
findings.scenario: A student uses the eight-icon timeline as the phase legend -- it is the primary navigation affordance and at widths under 700 px style.css:393 hides the text labels, leaving only the icons. They see the crescent drawn as a bright band floating in the middle of a dark disc with a dark rim on the outside, and read the dark outer rim as the lit limb being eclipsed or as the terminator being on the wrong side. Moving the main slider to the same phase shows something different.
findings.fix: In apps/demos/src/demos/moon-phases/style.css, move both crescents out to their limbs and put the curvature on the terminator side: `.waxing-crescent::after { left: 62%; width: 38%; border-radius: 50% 0 0 50% / 50%; }` and the mirror `.waning-crescent::after { left: 0; width: 38%; border-radius: 0 50% 50% 0 / 50%; }`, keeping the parent's circular overflow clip to form the outer limb. Add a design-contract assertion that each crescent rule's `left + width` reaches 100% (waxing) or `left` is 0 (waning), so a future edit cannot detach them again.

findings.title: Exhibit copy claims content verified 2026-02-02 and calls the demo a pilot, seven months and two physics corrections later
findings.evidence: Frontmatter: `content_verified: true` (line 4), `lastVerifiedAt: "2026-02-02"` (13), `last_updated: "2026-02-02"` (32). The rise/set physics was found wrong and rewritten on 2026-09-10 (git 4351045 "Give the Moon its own declination instead of the Sun's", 5a57f5b "Stop the Moon's rise and set swapping waxing and waning"), and index.html, main.ts and logic.ts all have mtime 2026-09-10. The last content-verification commit touching this file is 092ed99, dated 2026-02-01. model_notes are staler still: line 27 "This pilot visualization is a simplified 2D aid; it is not a full 3D rendering" and line 28 "Angle here is a proxy for Sun–Moon–Earth geometry; details will be refined in the full version" -- while the demo now ships Station Mode, five challenges, latitude/day-of-year rise/set and a documented declination model, and CLAUDE.md calls it the fully migrated golden reference. Line 17's "Sun–Earth–Moon geometry" also disagrees with line 28's "Sun–Moon–Earth".
findings.scenario: An instructor picking demos for a unit reads content_verified: true with a February date, assumes the copy matches what students will see, and assigns it. The model_notes then tell the class the angle is only "a proxy" whose "details will be refined", which undersells a model that is now derivation-backed, while saying nothing about the assumptions that do bite: zero ecliptic latitude, no lunar orbital tilt, local solar time, no refraction or parallax. Nothing in the public copy records the two corrections.
findings.fix: In apps/site/src/content/demos/moon-phases.md set lastVerifiedAt and last_updated to the date of the actual re-verification, and replace lines 27-28 with the assumptions the physics now states: "Circular orbits, zero ecliptic latitude (the Moon's 5.1 deg orbital tilt is dropped), local solar time, no refraction or parallax" and "$\\alpha$ is the Moon's synodic position angle measured from Full; the elongation is $(\\alpha - 180)\\bmod 360$." Make line 17 say Sun-Moon-Earth to match. Keep readiness: candidate -- it is the level the evidence supports, and after the three P0s above are fixed and a limb-side test exists, candidate is still the right call until a 320 px reflow check and an axe pass exist.

findings.title: Orbit panel draws the target star 1.07 AU from the Sun — an 86 degree parallax angle — with no not-to-scale label anywhere
findings.evidence: STAR_RADIUS_PX = 148 against ORBIT_RADIUS_PX = 138 (main.ts:91-92), i.e. the star is drawn at 148/138 = 1.07 orbital radii = 1.07 AU. Recomputed the angle the rays actually subtend at the star for captures at phase 0 and 180 with the authored star position (280,72): v1 = (138,148), v2 = (-138,148), cos = (-138*138 + 148*148)/(138^2 + 148^2) = 2860/40948 = 0.0698 -> 86.0 deg, so the drawn 2p is 86 deg and the implied distance is ~1.3 AU = 6e-6 pc. The orbit SVG contains no exaggeration or schematic note (index.html:166-199); the only such wording is on the detector control, "Detector exaggeration (visual only)" (index.html:141), which governs a different panel. The prior review records that the earlier version did carry an explicit "2p (exaggerated)" angle label and a clampNote (docs/reviews/parallax-distance.md:62-63).
findings.scenario: A student compares the orbit panel with the readout saying d_true = 10 pc and sees a triangle whose apex angle is tens of degrees, with the star essentially touching Earth's orbit. Nothing on the panel says the geometry is exaggerated, so the student takes the picture as roughly proportional and leaves with the belief that parallax angles are large and nearby stars are a few AU away — the exact scale intuition the demo exists to build.
findings.fix: In apps/demos/src/demos/parallax-distance/main.ts, add an SVG note in the orbit panel (alongside #geometryCue) reading that the target direction is schematic and the star is thousands of times farther than drawn, and draw the target direction as a direction marker at the frame edge with a break symbol rather than a star dot at 148 px — or render the star at the viewBox edge and label the line "to target star (not to scale)".

findings.title: Neither distance number input — the control labelled "primary input" — can accept a multi-digit value
findings.evidence: `distancePcInput.addEventListener("input", () => { ... setDistancePc(Number(distancePcInput.value)); })` (main.ts:1253-1256) -> setDistancePc (943) -> render() (948) -> renderControls -> syncDistanceControls, which writes back `distancePcInput.value = formatNumber(state.distancePc, 2)` (540) and `distanceLyInput.value = formatNumber(distanceLy, 2)` (541) on the field the user is typing in. Traced: type "2" -> state 2 -> field rewritten to "2.00", caret to end -> type "5" -> "2.005" -> ~2 pc. The ly field is worse because it also round-trips through the pc clamp (DISTANCE_PC_MIN = 1, main.ts:79): type "1" -> 1/3.26156 = 0.307 pc -> clamped to 1 pc -> field rewritten to "3.26", so the field can never leave the neighbourhood of its minimum. index.html:85 labels this block "Distance $d$ (primary input)".
findings.scenario: Student is told to set the star to 25 pc. They click the pc box, type "2", "5", and the readout shows 2.0 pc; the field shows "2.01". They try the ly box for 100 ly and it snaps to "3.26". Each keystroke also runs clearCaptures(false) (main.ts:947) and fires a live-region announcement (951), so the captures they already took are silently destroyed while they fight the field. The only working path to a chosen distance is the 50,000-step slider.
findings.fix: In apps/demos/src/demos/parallax-distance/main.ts, stop echoing into the field being edited: give syncDistanceControls a parameter naming the element to skip (or skip any element equal to document.activeElement when it is one of the two number inputs), and commit the typed value on `change`/blur rather than `input`. Keep the slider and the #distancePcValue readout updating live.

findings.title: The window Space handler preventDefaults unconditionally, so Space activates no button in the demo — including inside the station and help dialogs
findings.evidence: main.ts:1345-1355: `window.addEventListener("keydown", (event) => { ... const inEditable = !!target?.closest("input, select, textarea"); if (inEditable) return; if (event.key === " ") { event.preventDefault(); setPlaying(!state.isPlaying); return; } ... })`. A focused `<button>` does not match that selector, so preventDefault runs, and suppressing the default on a Space keydown over a button suppresses its activation. Nine buttons are affected: #playPauseOrbit, #captureEpochA, #captureEpochB, #swapCaptures, #clearCaptures, #detectorModeOverlay, #detectorModeDifference, #stationMode, #help, #copyResults. The dialog does not shield them either — packages/runtime/src/demoModes.ts:404-431 handles only Escape and Tab on the backdrop and never calls stopPropagation, so Space still reaches window from inside the station dialog. The e2e spec only ever presses Space with focus on the body (apps/site/tests/parallax-distance.spec.ts:150), so nothing catches this.
findings.scenario: A keyboard-only student Tabs to "Capture A" and presses Space, the standard button activation key. No capture is taken; instead the orbit starts or stops behind them, and the live region says "Orbit playing". They repeat on "Capture B", "Clear captures" and "Copy results" with the same result. In station mode, Space on "Add row (snapshot)" and "Copy CSV" also does nothing. The whole instrument is operable only with Enter, with no indication why.
findings.fix: In apps/demos/src/demos/parallax-distance/main.ts:1348, widen the opt-out to interactive controls that own the key: `const inEditable = !!target?.closest("input, select, textarea, button, [role=\"button\"], a[href], [contenteditable]")`. Then add an e2e assertion that focuses #captureEpochA, presses Space, and expects #status to contain "Captured A" rather than an orbit announcement.

findings.title: The uncertainty visualization is invisible: error circles are 3.00-3.60 px radius inside 7 px marker dots across almost the whole sigma range
findings.evidence: errorRadiusPx = clamp(|sigma * exaggeration * pxPerMas|, 3, 46) (logic.ts:204-213) with DETECTOR_PX_PER_MAS = 0.012 (main.ts:97) and the markers drawn at r="7" (index.html:219-222). Recomputed radii: at the default 15x exaggeration, sigma = 0.1, 1, 5, 20 mas give 3.00, 3.00, 3.00, 3.60 px; at 1x all four give 3.00 px; at the maximum 40x they give 3.00, 3.00, 3.00, 9.60 px. So across a 200-fold sigma range the circle is pinned at the 3 px minimum except at sigma = 20, and it only exceeds the 7 px marker dot at sigma = 20 with exaggeration >= ~30. The integration test asserts only `expect(largeErrorRadius).toBeGreaterThan(smallErrorRadius)` (main.integration.test.ts:232), which 3.60 > 3.00 satisfies.
findings.scenario: Student follows play_steps 5, "Increase sigma and observe how p_hat/sigma_p_hat and sigma_d_hat change", and drags sigma from 0.1 to 20 mas. The SNR number falls as it should, but the two error circles and both scatter clouds never visibly change — they are hidden behind the 7 px A and B dots the whole way. The student concludes the uncertainty control has no effect on the measurement picture, which is the opposite of the lesson.
findings.fix: In apps/demos/src/demos/parallax-distance/main.ts, scale the detector to the current signal instead of using a fixed DETECTOR_PX_PER_MAS: set pxPerMas each render from the true p so a 1 AU offset is a fixed fraction of DETECTOR_RANGE_PX, and shrink the marker radius (7 -> 3.5) so the error circle can be seen around it. Then replace the `toBeGreaterThan` assertion in main.integration.test.ts:232 with one that requires the radius to grow by a stated factor over a stated sigma ratio.

findings.title: Detector has no resolvable shift beyond ~30 pc, yet the distance slider runs to 5000 pc, and it clamps silently below ~2.5 pc
findings.evidence: DETECTOR_PX_PER_MAS = 0.012 (main.ts:97), DETECTOR_RANGE_PX = 182 (main.ts:98), silently clamped in detectorToScreen (main.ts:493-497), against DISTANCE_PC_MAX = 5000 (main.ts:80). Recomputed A-to-B separation for captures at 0/180 deg at the maximum 40x exaggeration: 10 pc -> 96.0 px; 33 pc -> 29.1 px; 100 pc -> 9.6 px (less than the 14 px diameter of either dot); 1000 pc -> 0.96 px; 5000 pc -> 0.19 px. At the other end, d <= 2.5 pc saturates: p = 400 mas gives 400*40*0.012 = 192 px, clamped to 182, with no on-screen note, so both markers sit pinned at the axis ends while the readout keeps reporting the true 800 mas shift. Only roughly 1 pc to 30 pc of a 1-5000 pc slider produces a usable picture.
findings.scenario: Student picks a distance from the middle of the slider — say 1200 pc — captures A at 0 and B at 180, and the two detector markers land 0.8 px apart, i.e. one dot. The readouts still show a shift and an inferred distance, so the student cannot connect the number to the picture and has no way to know the panel has run out of scale. Going the other way to 1.5 pc, the markers pin at the axis ends and stop responding to the exaggeration slider while the readout keeps changing.
findings.fix: In apps/demos/src/demos/parallax-distance/main.ts, derive pxPerMas per render from the current true parallax (e.g. so |offset| at 1 AU maps to ~0.35 * DETECTOR_RANGE_PX) and keep the exaggeration slider as a multiplier on top; show the resulting plate scale in mas/px in the panel. Where the clamp does engage, write a note into #degenerateWarningLabel saying the markers are pinned at the field edge, instead of clamping silently.

findings.evidence:

Add an e2e assertion that every `input.cp-range` has a non-empty accessible name.

findings.title: Distance slider is linear over 1-5000 pc at step 0.1, so keyboard traversal takes ~50,000 presses and the teaching range is 2% of the track
findings.evidence: `<input id="distancePcRange" type="range" min="1" max="5000" value="10" step="0.1">` (index.html:96) = (5000-1)/0.1 = 49,990 steps, each arrow press moving 0.1 pc. The nearby-star presets that populate the dropdown span 1.30-7.68 pc (packages/data-astr101/src/starsNearby.ts:30-40, parallax 768.5 to 130.2 mas), i.e. the entire preset set and the whole range where the detector is legible (<= ~30 pc, see the detector-scale finding) occupy under 0.6% of the track. A single pixel of a ~300 px track is ~17 pc.
findings.scenario: Keyboard student focuses the distance slider and presses the right arrow to move from 10 pc to 100 pc: 900 presses. A mouse student trying to set 25 pc finds one pixel of travel jumps past it, and since the number inputs do not accept typed multi-digit values either (see that finding) there is no working way to land on a chosen distance.
findings.fix: In apps/demos/src/demos/parallax-distance/index.html, make the slider logarithmic in distance: keep the input on a 0-100 unitless track and map it in main.ts as d = 10^(linear interpolation between log10(1) and log10(5000)), with the pc value shown in #distancePcValue as now. Or, if the linear scale is wanted, cut max to 200 pc (where the detector still resolves) and raise step so arrow keys move a useful amount.

findings.title: logic.ts re-derives the parsec relation instead of calling @cosmic/physics, so the demo has two sources of truth for d(p)
findings.evidence: logic.ts:325 `const dHatPc = 1000 / pHatMas;` and logic.ts:342 `equivalentSixMonthShiftMas: 2 * pHatMas`, in a file with zero imports, duplicating `ParallaxDistanceModel.distanceParsecFromParallaxMas` (packages/physics/src/parallaxDistanceModel.ts:25-28). logic.ts also keeps its own `MAS_PER_ARCSEC = 1000` (logic.ts:7) and `parallaxArcsecFromMas` (logic.ts:51), which main.ts imports for the arcsec readout (main.ts:600, 628) rather than taking from the model. The invariant is explicit: ".agents/references/invariants.md — Physics lives in packages/physics (@cosmic/physics). Demo code calls models; it never re-derives equations." The design-contract test that claims to enforce this asserts only that the string `from "@cosmic/physics"` appears in main.ts (design-contracts.test.ts:185), which it does, so the duplicate passes. Note also that the physics model returns Infinity for non-positive p while logic.ts:325 would return Infinity only via a divide-by-zero that the `pHatMas > 0` guard at 313 already excludes — the two paths have different domain contracts.
findings.scenario: A later correction to the parsec relation or its domain handling — say switching the mas branch to 1/(p/1000) for float symmetry, or changing the non-positive-p return — lands in packages/physics and its 11 tests go green, while every inferred distance a student reads still comes from the untouched `1000 / pHatMas` in the demo. The two numbers in the readout strip (d_true from the model, d_hat from logic.ts) then come from different code.
findings.fix: In apps/demos/src/demos/parallax-distance/logic.ts, import the model and call it: replace line 325 with `ParallaxDistanceModel.distanceParsecFromParallaxMas(pHatMas)` and drop the local MAS_PER_ARCSEC/parallaxArcsecFromMas in favour of a `parallaxArcsecFromMas` added to packages/physics/src/parallaxDistanceModel.ts. Then make the design-contract assertion real: assert that logic.ts contains no bare `1000 /` or `/ 1000` arithmetic on a parallax quantity.

findings.title: The geometry test constrains no sign, and its own hand-fed data uses the opposite sign from the implementation it is testing
findings.evidence: logic.test.ts:56-70, "keeps detector true offset on the measurement axis", asserts only `at0.y ~ 0`, `at90.x ~ 0`, `at90.y ~ 0`, `at180.y ~ 0`, `at0.x ~ -at180.x` — four zero-components and one antisymmetry, no sign relative to the Earth's position, so it passes identically whether logic.ts:127 reads `+pMas *` or `-pMas *`. Then logic.test.ts:101-120 feeds `earthPosAuA: {x:1,y:0}` with `detectorMeasMasA: {x:-50,y:0}` and `earthPosAuB: {x:-1,y:0}` with `detectorMeasMasB: {x:50,y:0}` — the physically correct anti-parallel sign — while `detectorTrueOffsetMasFromPosition(50, {x:1,y:0}, {x:-1,y:0})` actually returns `{x:+50,y:0}` (recomputed: dot = -1, scalar = -50, scaleVec2((-1,0), -50) = (+50,0)). The test passes anyway because computeCaptureInference only uses |deltaTheta| (logic.ts:300). The design-contract file is the same kind of evidence throughout: 203 lines of `expect(html).toContain('id="..."')` that assert no celestial token, no panel translucency, no reduced-motion rule and no numeric behaviour.
findings.scenario: The P0 sign error above has been in the repo through a physics review and a readiness promotion with a green suite, because the two tests that touch the sign either ignore it or silently disagree with the code. The same tests will go green again after any future sign regression, and the design-contract file will keep certifying "token-first" and "imports physics, not hardcoded formulas" from string matches alone.
findings.fix: In apps/demos/src/demos/parallax-distance/logic.test.ts, add an assertion at an asymmetric phase that pins the physics: at phase 37 deg with p = 100 mas and axisHat = (-1,0), `dotVec2(detectorTrueOffsetMasFromPhase(100, 37, axis), axis)` must be `+79.864` mas (i.e. opposite in sign to `dotVec2(earthPosAuFromPhaseDeg(37), axis) * 100`). Then make the inference test build its detectorMeasMas inputs by calling detectorTrueOffsetMasFromPosition rather than hand-typing them, so the two functions can no longer disagree.

findings.title: The uncertainty propagation — the demo's headline new pedagogy — has no test at all
findings.evidence: computeCaptureInference returns sigmaShiftMas, sigmaPHatMas, sigmaDHatPc and snrPHat (logic.ts:326-329, 338-346). Grepping logic.test.ts for those four names returns nothing: the "recovers parallax" test (101-125) asserts computable, reason, deltaThetaMas, baselineEffAu, pHatMas, dHatPc and equivalentSixMonthShiftMas and stops. main.integration.test.ts:225-234 asserts only `lowSnr < highSnr` and that the quality string is one of four values. I verified the formulas by hand (p = 100 mas, B_eff = 2 AU, sigma_meas = 1 mas -> sigma_shift = 1.414214, sigma_p = 0.707107, sigma_d = 1000*0.707107/100^2 = 0.07071068 pc, matching the analytic d^2 sigma_p/1000 = 0.07071068 pc at d = 10 pc) — they are correct today, and nothing holds them there.
findings.scenario: A refactor drops the sqrt(2) from sigma_shift (logic.ts:326) or writes sigma_d as 1000*sigma_p/p instead of /p^2 (logic.ts:328). Every test in the repo stays green, `lowSnr < highSnr` still holds, and the readout strip reports an uncertainty wrong by a factor of sqrt(2) or by a factor of p — which is the number students are asked to reason about in play_steps 5 and in the station-mode synthesis prompt.
findings.fix: Add a case to apps/demos/src/demos/parallax-distance/logic.test.ts asserting the three propagated values at the worked point above (sigma_shift 1.414214, sigma_p 0.707107, sigma_d 0.07071068 pc for p_hat = 100 mas, B_eff = 2 AU, sigma_meas = 1 mas), plus a second asymmetric case with B_eff = 1.5973 AU to pin the 1/B_eff dependence, and one asserting sigma_d scales as d^2 between 10 pc and 20 pc.

findings.title: docs/reviews/parallax-distance.md audits a version of the demo that no longer exists and certifies "no sign bugs"
findings.evidence: The review concludes (line 102) "No physics errors, sign bugs, unit mismatches, or rendering convention issues were found." Its subject does not exist: it describes a "1..1000 mas" parallax slider, `currentInputs()`, `diagramHalfAngle(parallaxMas, exaggeration=6000)`, `diagramStarY(baselineY=420, baselineLen=320, halfAngle)`, a `clampNote`, an `angleArc` and an HTML label "Baseline (Jan - Jul): 2 AU (schematic)" (lines 55-73, 92). None of those identifiers appear anywhere in the current demo, whose primary input is distance in pc (index.html:85-98) and whose geometry is the two-panel orbit/detector pair. It also claims `describeMeasurability` is dead code (line 79) when it is called at main.ts:915, and claims there is no distance-uncertainty readout (line 81) when #distancePcPm exists (index.html:262). It asserts "27 logic tests" against the 12 now in logic.test.ts. It predates commit 4da8a9b, "fix(parallax): tighten uncertainty semantics and capture-first pedagogy".
findings.scenario: The next reviewer, or the readiness auditor, opens the one review file on record for this demo, reads "no sign bugs ... rendering convention issues" and a per-equation CORRECT table, and skips the two P0s above — which is apparently what already happened, since the demo carries readiness: launch-ready. The file is load-bearing false assurance.
findings.fix: Replace docs/reviews/parallax-distance.md with a review of the current two-panel demo, or add a dated header at the top stating that it reviews the pre-capture-workflow version (before commit 4da8a9b) and that its conclusions do not apply. Add the file's subject commit SHA to the review template so staleness is detectable.

findings.title: readiness: launch-ready / status: stable / content_verified: true are unsupported, and readinessReason contradicts lastVerifiedAt
findings.evidence: Frontmatter: `status: stable` (line 3), `content_verified: true` (4), `readiness: launch-ready` (10), `readinessReason: "Physics and page checked in the September 2026 audits with nothing open: it works on a phone, announces changes to screen readers..."` (11), `lastVerifiedAt: "2026-02-09"` (13). The reason cites September 2026 audits while the verified date is February, seven months earlier, and `readinessReason` is public copy per CLAUDE.md. "Works on a phone" has no evidence: apps/site/tests/reflow.spec.ts:55 is `const PLAY_ROUTES = ["play/conservation-laws/"]`, so no /play/ route for this demo is tested at 320px. "Announces changes to screen readers" is contradicted by the two unnamed sliders (index.html:96, 112). Per CLAUDE.md only `launch-ready` removes the card badge and only `status: stable` removes the exhibit's "Active development" callout, so both claims are currently shown to students. Two copy errors in the same file: play_steps says "Increase $\sigma_p$" (line 28) when the control is $\sigma_{\rm meas}$ and $\sigma_p$ is a derived output, and predict_prompt writes "deltaTheta" in ASCII (line 22) where the KaTeX-only rule requires $\Delta\theta$.
findings.scenario: An instructor filters the explore page for launch-ready demos to pick what to run in a 50-minute class, gets parallax-distance with no caveat badge and no "Active development" callout, assigns it, and 30 students meet a flipped star, a backwards shift direction, and a distance box that will not accept "25".
findings.fix: In apps/site/src/content/demos/parallax-distance.md set `readiness: needs-work` and `status: in-development`, set `content_verified: false`, and rewrite readinessReason to name what is open (drawing orientation, shift sign, distance input, keyboard Space) with no audit-date claim; correct line 28 to $\sigma_{\rm meas}$ and line 22 to $\Delta\theta$. Restore launch-ready only after the two P0s are fixed and `play/parallax-distance/` is added to PLAY_ROUTES in apps/site/tests/reflow.spec.ts and passes at 320px.

findings.title: No pause, step or time scrub anywhere; reduced-motion users get a frozen t=0 diagram with no way to advance time
findings.evidence: The only time-related controls in index.html are a speed range (line 38) and a single Reset button (lines 42-44) -- there is no play, pause, step or scrub control in the file. main.ts:272-281: `function startAnimation(): void { if (prefersReducedMotion) { setLiveRegionText(status, "Reduced motion is enabled; animation is disabled."); render(); return; } ... }`. With reduced motion on, elapsedDays stays 0 forever, so the speed slider and Reset are both no-ops and no alignment is ever reachable. By contrast the sibling retrograde-motion demo (same physics family, same element table) ships the shared component: index.html:85-99 has #btn-play, #btn-pause, #btn-step-back, #btn-step-forward, #btn-reset, and index.html:293-304 a `cp-playbar` region with a `#scrubSlider` (min 0, max 720, step 0.25, aria-label "Model day scrub") plus a "Day 0 of 720" readout and a Space shortcut. `grep -rln cp-playbar apps/demos/src/demos/` lists moon-phases, doppler-shift, spectral-lines and retrograde-motion; planetary-conjunctions is absent.
findings.scenario: A student with prefers-reduced-motion set (or anyone on a locked-down lab machine profile) opens the demo, sees Earth and Mars both parked at longitude 0, moves the speed slider and clicks Reset with no effect, and can never observe an opposition. A sighted student without reduced motion can see events but cannot pause to read the six readouts at the moment of alignment, and cannot jump to day 780 to check the synodic period -- they must sit through it in real time.
findings.fix: Adopt the shared cp-playbar in apps/demos/src/demos/planetary-conjunctions/index.html exactly as retrograde-motion/index.html:85-99 and :293-304 do -- play/pause/step/reset buttons plus a day scrub bound to elapsedDays -- and in main.ts drive elapsedDays from the scrub value so time advances under reduced motion by explicit user action instead of by animation. That one change makes the reduced-motion path functional, gives everyone a pause, and removes the per-demo fork of the control row.

findings.title: "What to notice" gives a false reason for Mars having the longest synodic period
findings.evidence: index.html:149: "Mars has the longest synodic period (~780 days) among naked-eye planets because its sidereal period is closest to Earth's." I computed the sidereal periods from the same JPL a-values the demo uses: Earth 365.251 d, Venus 224.698 d, Mars 686.980 d. |P - P_Earth| is 140.6 d for Venus and 321.7 d for Mars, so Venus's sidereal period is more than twice as close to Earth's as Mars's is -- the stated reason is false as written. What is actually closest is the mean motion: |1/P - 1/P_Earth| is 1.2822e-3 /d for Mars against 1.7126e-3 /d for Venus, which is why Mars wins. Bullet 1 on line 148 compounds it by calling Venus's 584 d "frequent" when Jupiter (398.9 d) and Saturn (378.1 d) are both more frequent.
findings.scenario: Student reads "longest synodic period because its sidereal period is closest to Earth's", applies the rule to the planet list on screen, and predicts Venus (224.7 d, closest to 365.25 d of the two inner/outer options they can select) should have the longest synodic period. They then select Venus, read 583.9 d against Mars's 779.9 d, and conclude either that the demo is broken or that they misunderstood synodic periods.
findings.fix: Rewrite index.html:148-149 in terms of angular rate: Mars has the longest synodic period of the four because its mean motion is closest to Earth's (P_syn = 1/|1/P_E - 1/P_t| blows up as the rates converge), and drop or requalify the "frequently" claim for Venus, whose 584 d is the second-longest of the four on offer, not the shortest.

findings.title: The J2000 mean longitudes are discarded, so the lambda readouts are not the quantity they are labelled and t=0 is a spurious alignment
findings.evidence: main.ts:182-183 propagates from zero phase: `const earthAngle = planetAngleRad(elapsedDays, earthPeriodDays); const targetAngle = planetAngleRad(elapsedDays, targetPeriodDays);` and logic.ts:93-101 defines planetAngleRad as 2*pi*t/P with no epoch term. The callbacks at main.ts:91-102 read only `.aAu` from `RetrogradeMotionModel.planetElements(name)`, although that same table (retrogradeMotionModel.ts:36-42) carries L0Deg for all five bodies. Meanwhile index.html:125 and :129 label the readouts with the standard symbols for heliocentric ecliptic longitude, and index.html:164 claims "Sidereal periods come from JPL J2000 approximate elements". I computed the consequences: at t=0 the demo shows Earth longitude 0.0 deg where J2000 L0 is 100.46 deg, and the true t=0 heliocentric separations are Venus 81.5 deg, Mars 105.0 deg, Jupiter 66.1 deg, Saturn 50.5 deg -- never the 0.0 deg the demo draws and reports.
findings.scenario: Student reads "Earth longitude = 0.0 deg, Mars longitude = 0.0 deg, Angular separation = 0.0 deg" at load, sees the two dots on one ray, and records that Earth and Mars start at opposition at the J2000 epoch the model notes cite. They are off by 105 deg. A student who cross-checks the Earth longitude against any ephemeris for J2000.0 finds 100.46 deg and concludes the demo's angles are meaningless.
findings.fix: In apps/demos/src/demos/planetary-conjunctions/main.ts, pass each body's L0Deg from RetrogradeMotionModel.planetElements() into the phase, and give logic.ts's planetAngleRad an epoch-longitude argument so angle = L0 + 2*pi*t/P. That costs nothing, makes both readouts the quantity their labels name, and removes the artificial alignment at t=0. If the zero-phase start is kept deliberately, relabel the readouts as relative longitude from the start of the run and strike the J2000 claim from index.html:164.

findings.title: role="radio" planet selector has no arrow-key, Home/End or roving-tabindex support, unlike its sibling demos
findings.evidence: index.html:28-33 declares the full radiogroup pattern: `<div class="cp-chip-group--grid planet-selector__row" role="radiogroup" aria-label="Target planet">` with four `<button ... role="radio" aria-checked="...">`. main.ts attaches only click handlers (lines 338-343) and sets aria-checked (line 313); `grep -n "keydown|keyup|KeyboardEvent|tabindex|tabIndex" main.ts` returns nothing, so arrow keys do nothing and all four radios remain in the tab order. Sibling demos implement the pattern properly -- binary-orbits/main.ts:1528-1539 handles ArrowRight/ArrowDown/ArrowLeft/ArrowUp/Home over its radio buttons, and moon-phases, seasons, galaxy-rotation and six others have ArrowRight handlers.
findings.scenario: Screen-reader user hears "Target planet, radio group, Mars, radio button, 2 of 4" and presses the arrow keys that every radio group responds to. Nothing happens and nothing is announced. Tab then moves them through all four radios one at a time instead of out of the group, so the group behaves like neither a radio group nor a button row and they cannot tell whether selection failed or the control is dead.
findings.fix: Add the same keydown handler binary-orbits/main.ts:1520-1545 uses to apps/demos/src/demos/planetary-conjunctions/main.ts: Arrow keys move and select, Home/End jump to the ends, and selectPlanet sets tabindex 0 on the checked chip and -1 on the rest so the group is one tab stop. Better still, lift that handler into packages/runtime as a shared chip-radiogroup helper -- six demos now reimplement it.

findings.title: Exhibit copy promises a from-Earth sky view and a time-advance control the demo does not have
findings.evidence: The .md play_steps are: line 22 "Advance time to find a conjunction and an opposition"; line 23 "Compare where the planet is in space to how close it appears to the Sun in the sky"; line 24 "Measure the time between two conjunctions". learning_goals line 15 is "Define conjunction and opposition as seen from Earth" and predict_prompt line 20 asks whether the planet "stay[s] near the Sun in our sky". The demo has no time-advance control (index.html offers only a speed range and Reset), no sky or geocentric view of any kind, and no Earth-to-target line of sight -- the SVG (index.html:76-106) is purely heliocentric. It also detects one alignment type per target by construction: its own model note at index.html:168 says "Only the same-longitude alignment is detected. The complementary alignment 180 degrees away ... is not flagged", so "find a conjunction and an opposition" is impossible for any single target. The listed misconception (line 19, that a conjunction means the planets are physically close) has no corresponding readout or feature.
findings.scenario: Instructor assigns the exhibit's play_steps as the lab worksheet. A student with Mars selected is told to find both a conjunction and an opposition; the counter only ever says "Oppositions observed", so they hunt for a conjunction that the code will never flag. Step 2 asks them to compare the space geometry to the planet's apparent distance from the Sun in the sky, and there is no sky view to compare against, so the step cannot be completed and the stated learning goal is never exercised.
findings.fix: Either rewrite the play_steps, learning_goals, predict_prompt and misconceptions in apps/site/src/content/demos/planetary-conjunctions.md to the heliocentric relative-motion story the demo actually tells, or add the missing capability to the demo: a second small sky panel showing the target's elongation from the Sun as seen from Earth, and detection of the complementary alignment so both event types occur for every target. Do not leave the copy describing one demo and the code implementing another.

findings.title: The demo re-implements its physics in logic.ts instead of calling a @cosmic/physics model, by design
findings.evidence: logic.ts:1-5 states the intent: "Pure UI logic ... Extracted from main.ts so that formatting, coordinate helpers, and conjunction detection can be unit-tested without DOM or physics imports." What lives there is physics, not UI: logic.ts:93-101 propagates heliocentric longitude (2*pi*t/P), :107-112 computes angular separation, :121-124 is the alignment criterion, :150-161 classifies inferior conjunction vs opposition from the two semi-major axes, and :66-68 re-derives the model year as 31557600/86400. `grep -ril "conjunction|synodic" packages/physics/src/` returns moonPhasesModel, twoBodyAnalytic, astroConstants and eclipseGeometryModel -- there is no planetary-conjunctions model in packages/physics at all. The invariants file is explicit: "Physics lives in packages/physics (@cosmic/physics). Demo code calls models; it never re-derives equations."
findings.scenario: The alignment criterion and the longitude propagation are unreachable from any other demo and untested against the package's own conventions, so the leading-edge counting defect above lives in a file no physics reviewer reads and no physics test imports. Retrograde-motion, which needs the same relative-longitude geometry, cannot reuse any of it; the next demo that needs conjunctions writes a third copy, and a fix to one does not reach the others.
findings.fix: Add packages/physics/src/planetaryAlignmentModel.ts owning the heliocentric longitude propagation (with epoch longitude), the signed and absolute separation, the alignment-epoch solver that returns the day of minimum separation, and the inferior-conjunction/opposition classification, with its own tests in the physics package. Reduce apps/demos/src/demos/planetary-conjunctions/logic.ts to formatting and SVG mapping, and delete the dependency-injection callback interface at logic.ts:20-27, which exists only to let the demo test physics it should not own.

findings.title: Earth's semi-major axis and the model year are hardcoded in the demo while the same values are available from the model
findings.evidence: Three copies of Earth's a coexist. logic.ts:53: `const aEarthAu = 1.00000261; // from PLANET_ELEMENTS`. main.ts:146: `const earthAu = 1.00000261;` -- used for every orbit radius via getMaxAu() at main.ts:155-158. main.ts:121 reads the authoritative value: `const EARTH_SEMI_MAJOR_AXIS_AU = RetrogradeMotionModel.planetElements("Earth").aAu;` -- and that one is used only for the alignment classification. logic.test.ts:383 adds a fourth copy: `const EARTH_AU = 1.00000261;`. Separately logic.ts:66-68 `return 31557600 / 86400;` duplicates RetrogradeMotionModel.modelYearDays(), which returns AstroConstants.TIME.YEAR_S / DAY_S = 31557600/86400 (astroConstants.ts:15,19). logic.ts:41-43 also makes a dead call whose result is thrown away: `const aAu = name === "Earth" ? cb.planetSemiMajorAxisAu("Venus") // will be overridden below`.
findings.scenario: A later correction to the JPL element table -- or a switch from the Standish 1800-2050 set to a different epoch -- updates retrogradeMotionModel.ts. Earth's period and the alignment classification then follow the new value while the drawn orbit radii (main.ts:146) and the Earth period inside logic.ts (:53) keep the old one. Nothing fails: the orbits are silently drawn at the wrong relative scale and Earth's sidereal period disagrees with the table the model notes cite, with every test still green because the tests hold a fourth hardcoded copy.
findings.fix: Delete the literals. In apps/demos/src/demos/planetary-conjunctions/main.ts use EARTH_SEMI_MAJOR_AXIS_AU (already defined at line 121) wherever earthAu is used; add Earth to the ConjunctionCallbacks lookup so logic.ts:49-56 needs no constant and the dead Venus call at :42 can go; and have the demo call RetrogradeMotionModel.modelYearDays() instead of logic.ts's yearDays(). Change logic.test.ts to import the value it asserts against rather than restating it.

findings.title: Planet labels are drawn at a fixed 12 px offset, so with Jupiter or Saturn selected the "Earth" label lands inside the Sun
findings.evidence: main.ts:191-197 offsets both labels by a constant in screen y regardless of orbit radius or position angle: `earthLabel.setAttribute("y", (earthPos.y - 12).toFixed(1));` and the same for the target. Orbit radii are linear in a/a_max with MAX_ORBIT_PX = 240 (main.ts:109, logic.ts:239-247), so I computed Earth's ring: Venus selected 240.0 px, Mars 157.5 px, Jupiter 46.1 px, Saturn 25.2 px. The Sun is drawn as a glow disc of r = 14 plus a core of r = 8 at the centre with a drop-shadow (index.html:93-94, style.css:100-103). With Earth near the top of its orbit the label baseline sits at radius 46.1 - 12 = 34.1 px for Jupiter and 25.2 - 12 = 13.2 px for Saturn -- inside the 14 px Sun disc. Earth's own dot (r = 7) spans 18.2-32.2 px for Saturn, clearing the Sun's edge by 4.2 px.
findings.scenario: Student selects Saturn to watch Saturn oppositions. Earth's orbit is a 25 px ring around a 14 px Sun, Earth's dot nearly touches the Sun's glow, and twice per Earth year the word "Earth" is drawn on top of the Sun. The student reads the diagram as Earth sitting on or inside the Sun, and cannot see the Earth-side geometry that defines the opposition they were sent to observe.
findings.fix: In apps/demos/src/demos/planetary-conjunctions/main.ts, place each label radially outward from the Sun rather than always up: offset along the body's own position angle (label point at radius r + 14 using the same orbitToSvg call) and set text-anchor from the angle's sign. Separately, give the inner system a floor -- either a minimum drawn radius for Earth's ring or a square-root/log radial map for the Jupiter and Saturn scales -- and say in the model notes which mapping is in use.

findings.title: The e2e reduced-motion test asserts the frozen state is correct, pinning the defect
findings.evidence: spec:309-319 is the whole reduced-motion contract: after emulating reduced motion and waiting 500 ms it asserts `expect(days).toBe("0")` and `expect(statusText).toContain("Reduced motion")`. That makes "time can never advance for a reduced-motion user" the specified behaviour, so any future fix that lets them scrub or step time will fail this test and look like a regression. The same file's "days elapsed increments over time" test (spec:107-113) does `const days = parseFloat(daysText || "0"); expect(days).toBeGreaterThan(0)` -- I checked that parseFloat("4.1 yr") returns 4.1, so this test passes while the readout displays "4.1 yr days". And "days elapsed readout has days unit" (spec:142-146) asserts only that the static span says "days", which is exactly the half of the pair that is never wrong.
findings.scenario: An engineer adopts the shared playbar so reduced-motion users can step time. The suite goes red on "respects prefers-reduced-motion" and the fix is reverted as a regression. Meanwhile the "yr days" unit bug ships indefinitely because the two tests nominally covering that readout are both satisfied by the broken output.
findings.fix: Rewrite the reduced-motion test in apps/site/tests/planetary-conjunctions.spec.ts to assert what the user needs -- that no animation runs unprompted AND that an explicit time control still advances the day readout. Change the elapsed-day assertions to match the full rendered text of the readout row (value plus unit span) against a regex that rejects a year value next to a "days" unit, so the pairing itself is constrained.

findings.title: Authored KaTeX in the state-formula strip is overwritten with ASCII on every render
findings.evidence: index.html:260-262 authors the strip correctly as `Direct: $d\tilde{\lambda}/dt > 0$ | Stationary: $|d\tilde{\lambda}/dt| \le \epsilon$ | Retrograde: ...`. main.ts:528-530 then does `stateFormula.textContent = "Direct: d(lambda~)/dt > 0 | Stationary: |d(lambda~)/dt| <= eps | Retrograde: d(lambda~)/dt < 0"`. Traced boot order: main.ts:1740 `recomputeSeries()` -> setCursorDay -> render -> renderReadouts -> line 528 fires, and only then does main.ts:1741 call `initMath(document)`. The ASCII string contains no `$` delimiters, so KaTeX finds nothing to typeset, and every later render re-sets it. The rendered math is never visible.
findings.scenario: On first paint and forever after, the strip beneath the plot title reads `d(lambda~)/dt > 0 ... |d(lambda~)/dt| <= eps`, with `lambda~` standing in for lambda-tilde and a bare `eps` whose value (0.005-0.01 deg/day) is never stated. The one place the demo defines its own retrograde criterion is the one place it does not render math.
findings.fix: In main.ts:528-530 write the two branches as LaTeX source and hand them to `renderMath()` from @cosmic/runtime (set `innerHTML` from the rendered result, not `textContent`), or leave the index.html markup alone and only toggle a class for the undefined-pair case. Then fix apps/site/tests/retrograde-motion.spec.ts:355, which currently asserts `toContainText("eps")` and would fail on the corrected copy.

findings.title: Unicode math glyphs reach the page as \uXXXX escapes, which the build validator cannot see
findings.evidence: main.ts:1036 `arcLabel.textContent = "λ_app"` puts a literal lambda into SVG text; logic.ts:361, 364 and 367 put `≈` (the approximately-equal sign) into the three stationary-nav button labels. I checked both glyphs against the build gate's own regex: `FORBIDDEN_UNICODE_MATH` in scripts/validate-math-formatting.mjs:33 matches lambda -> true and approx -> true, and apps/demos/src/demos IS in SCAN_ROOTS (:20) with .ts in EXTENSIONS (:29). The gate passes only because it reads the raw file (:108, :114) and the source text is a six-character escape, not the glyph - precisely what CLAUDE.md forbids: "no \uXXXX escapes that produce them (the validator cannot see escapes)". The demo's own guard, design-contracts.test.ts:157, lists only \\u00B0 \\u00B1 \\u2264 \\u2265 \\u2248 \\u2190 \\u2192 and checks only `html` and `main` - so it misses lambda entirely and never opens logic.ts.
findings.scenario: The rendered SVG text node contains a raw lambda that inherits whatever the surrounding CSS does to it - the exact 2026-09-05 failure where 94 KaTeX nodes were uppercased by an inherited text-transform and nu became N. This demo's own stylesheet already ships `text-transform: uppercase` (style.css:184). Meanwhile the nav buttons read "Prev stationary ~ Day 123.5" with an unrenderable operator, and apps/site/tests/retrograde-motion.spec.ts:588 asserts the lambda glyph is present, so the correct fix fails the suite.
findings.fix: Replace main.ts:1036 with a `renderMath()`-produced `$\lambda_{\mathrm{app}}$` inside an SVG `<foreignObject>` (or move the label out of the SVG into an HTML overlay, as the WebGL convention in CLAUDE.md already prescribes for text), and replace the `≈` in logic.ts:361/364/367 with the ASCII word "about" or a rendered `$\approx$` in the button's innerHTML. Then widen design-contracts.test.ts:155-161 to scan logic.ts too and to test for the GLYPHS (via the same regex the validator uses, applied to `JSON.parse`-unescaped source) rather than a hand-picked list of escape spellings, and update spec.ts:585/588.

findings.title: Station mode asks students to explain a trend the demo's own numbers contradict
findings.evidence: main.ts:1684 (station step 5) says "Use your data to explain why inner planets have shorter retrograde arcs" and main.ts:1726 says "Inner-planet retrogrades are shorter because the relative angular velocity at conjunction is larger." I recomputed the arcs from the model's own elements: Earth->Venus 16.35 deg, Earth->Mars 13.90 deg, Earth->Jupiter 10.05 deg, Earth->Saturn 6.93 deg. The inner planet has the LARGEST arc; arcs decrease outward. Durations are what order inward: 42.0 d (Venus), 59-69 d (Mars), 117-123 d (Jupiter), 133.5 d (Saturn). The stated mechanism also fails against the demo's own readout: `relativeAngularSpeedProxyDegPerDay` gives -0.6165 deg/day for Venus, +0.4616 for Mars, +0.9026 for Jupiter, +0.9522 for Saturn - the largest magnitude belongs to Saturn, which has the longest retrograde, so a larger Delta-n does not imply a shorter retrograde.
findings.scenario: A student completes the station worksheet, records Venus 42 d and Mars 69 d, is told the explanation is "larger relative angular velocity at conjunction", then opens the Delta-n readout in Advanced, sees Saturn at 0.952 deg/day with a 133 d retrograde, and finds the stated rule inverted. If they instead measure the arc (which the plot's y axis invites), they find Venus's arc is larger than Mars's - the opposite of what step 5 asserts.
findings.fix: In main.ts:1684 and :1726, say "shorter retrograde DURATIONS" (never "arcs") and replace the mechanism with the correct one: retrograde lasts as long as the observer's transverse velocity relative to the target exceeds the target's own apparent drift, which for a distant superior planet asymptotes to roughly half the observer's year, so durations grow outward. Either drop the Delta-n proxy readout or relabel it as the synodic mean-motion difference with its sign explained - it is not a predictor of duration.

findings.title: No test pins lambda_app to a value, so a 180 deg error passes the entire suite
findings.evidence: The only assertions on the observer-to-target chain are existence checks: retrogradeMotionModel.test.ts:119-120 `expect(series.stationaryDays.length).toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(2)` and `expect(series.retrogradeIntervals.length).toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(1)`. I reran my independent model with the subtraction reversed (observer minus target instead of target minus observer, retrogradeMotionModel.ts:244-246) and compared: lambda(t=0) moves from 327.974 deg to 147.974 deg (exactly -180.000), while stationaryDays count stays 2, retrogradeIntervals stays 1, and dLambda/dt(0) is bit-identical at 0.7755841768 deg/day. Every e2e readout test only asserts `expect(parseFloat(value)).not.toBeNaN()` (spec.ts:99, 122, 147, 285, 301, 312) and the state tests only `toMatch(/Direct|Retrograde|Stationary/)` (spec.ts:263, 322). The logic.test.ts `computeDisplayState` block (:279-370) feeds a hand-built fake series, so `expect(state.retroDuration).toBe("80.0")` (:337) re-asserts its own fixture.
findings.scenario: Any future edit that flips a sign, swaps observer/target, or shifts the reference axis by 180 deg ships green. The lambda readout, the Sky View dot position and the zodiac constellation under the planet would all be wrong by six signs, and no gate would notice.
findings.fix: Add value assertions to packages/physics/src/retrogradeMotionModel.test.ts: pin lambda_app for Earth->Mars at three asymmetric days against numbers derived independently (I get t=137.00 -> lambda 69.5635 deg, dLambda/dt +0.691884 deg/day; Earth->Venus t=503.75 -> 14.3086 deg, +0.755887; Earth->Jupiter t=911.50 -> 112.9040 deg, +0.220239), and pin the first retrograde duration per preset against the published planetary values (Venus ~42 d, Mars ~60-70 d, Jupiter ~120 d, Saturn ~134 d). Add one e2e assertion that the lambda readout matches the model for a fixed scrub day.

findings.title: Orbit view and Sky View have no accessible name; their text nodes leak unlabeled
