findings.evidence: index.html:280 is `<svg id="orbitSvg" class="retro__svg" viewBox="0 0 420 420"></svg>` and :284 is `<svg id="skySvg" class="retro__sky-svg" viewBox="0 0 400 60"></svg>` - no `role="img"`, no aria-label, no `<title>`, and the `.panel-title` divs at :279 and :283 are plain divs with no programmatic association. Both SVGs are then filled with `<text>` nodes at runtime: planet names (main.ts:1062, 1071), "0 deg" (main.ts:877), twelve zodiac abbreviations (main.ts:891) and the Sky View degree label (main.ts:1147). main.ts:745 sets `marker.setAttribute("aria-label", ...)` on a bare SVG `<circle>` with no role, which assistive technology ignores. Only the plot has a name, and it is on the wrapping div (index.html:268), not the SVG.
findings.scenario: A screen-reader student tabs to the stage and reaches two unnamed graphics regions, then hears a bare stream of "Earth Mars 0 deg Ari Tau Gem ... 327 deg" with no indication of which panel it came from or what it depicts. Two of the three synchronized views that the demo's pedagogy is built on convey nothing.
findings.fix: Add `role="img"` plus an aria-label to both SVGs in index.html:280 and :284, mark the decorative children `aria-hidden="true"`, and render a short live text summary of the geometry (observer, target, lambda, state, elongation) next to each panel so the drawing has a real text alternative. Replace the no-op aria-label at main.ts:745 with either a `<title>` child of the circle or an entry in that summary.

findings.title: Nothing announces the Direct-to-Retrograde transition, the demo's central observable
findings.evidence: `renderReadouts` (main.ts:483-537) computes the new state, writes `readoutState.textContent` (:505) and swaps the badge class (:511-527), and never calls `setLiveRegionText`. Grepping every call site of `setLiveRegionText` in main.ts gives :273 (pair change), :391 (reduced motion), :1371 (midpoint jump), :1410/:1413/:1416 (copy results) and :1461 (onboarding reopen) - none on the state path. `#readoutState` (index.html:339) and `#stateBadge` (index.html:255) carry no aria-live, and the only polite region is `#status` (index.html:228). Correctly, no announcement is made from inside the rAF loop; the problem is that none is made at all.
findings.scenario: A screen-reader student plays the animation or presses Right arrow through a stationary point. The badge changes to RETROGRADE and the pink band appears - silently. The single event the whole exhibit exists to teach is never announced, so the demo is operable but not perceivable.
findings.fix: In main.ts:492-499 compare the newly computed `currentMotionState` against its previous value and, only on a change, call `setLiveRegionText(statusEl, ...)` with the new state and the day (e.g. "Retrograde begins, day 123.5"). Guard it with the existing transition detection so it fires once per transition rather than per frame.

findings.title: observer === target yields a degenerate series with one stationary point per grid sample
findings.evidence: With observer === target, `lambdaAppWrappedDegAtModelDay` (retrogradeMotionModel.ts:244-247) gets dx = dy = 0 and `Math.atan2(0, 0)` returns 0 (confirmed in node), so lambda is exactly 0 at every sample, the unwrapped series is constant, and `centralDifferenceDegPerDay` returns exactly 0 everywhere. The detector at :352 then takes the `if (d0 === 0)` branch at every index and pushes one stationary day per sample. I computed the counts: at the default 24-month window n = 2881, giving 2880 stationary days; at the 72-month maximum n = 8641, giving 8640 stationary days and 8640 interval segments, each calling `dLambdaDtAt` (:379) for 2 more full Kepler solves - about 17,280 extra solves on top of the 17,282 already done for the series.
findings.scenario: A student opens Advanced and sets Target to Earth while Observer is Earth (both selects list Earth, and nothing prevents it). The model silently returns 8,640 'stationary points' for a geometry where lambda is undefined, the compute takes a visible stall, and `findPrevNextStationary` (logic.ts:102-110) then walks that 8,640-element array on every single render frame thereafter. The UI happens to hide the output behind `isUndefinedPair()` guards, so the nonsense never surfaces as a number - it surfaces as a hang.
findings.fix: In retrogradeMotionModel.ts:244-247, detect the degenerate separation explicitly (`if (dx === 0 && dy === 0) return Number.NaN`) so the series is NaN rather than a constant, and make the `d0 === 0` branch at :352 require a genuine sign change on either side rather than firing on a flat series. Keep the UI guards as presentation, not as the only line of defence.

findings.title: Sky View cannot resolve a retrograde loop and has no axis at all
findings.evidence: `projectToSkyView` (logic.ts:230-236) maps the full 360 deg across the 400-unit strip, i.e. 1.111 units per degree. The Mars retrograde arc I measured from the model is 13.90 deg, so the dot traverses 13.90 x 1.111 = 15.4 units of a 400-unit strip - 3.9% of the width - over the entire 69-day event. `buildSkyLayers` (main.ts:1082-1116) draws only a background rect and eleven decorative circles at hardcoded x positions [20, 55, 88, ... 370] with `cy = 12 + (sx*37) % 30` (:1110): no tick marks, no longitude axis, no east/west labels, no zodiac ruler. The only numeric is a label under the dot (:1147).
findings.scenario: The "What to notice" tab (index.html:366) promises the planet "appears to reverse its motion against the background stars", and the panel titled Sky View is where a student looks for that. The dot shifts by about 15 px over 69 days against stars that are at arbitrary decorative positions, so there is nothing to measure the reversal against and no axis to read. The panel that is supposed to connect model to observation shows the least of the three.
findings.fix: Zoom the strip to a window around the current lambda (e.g. +/- 20 deg) instead of the full circle, add labelled longitude ticks and an explicit increasing-lambda direction marker, and plot the target's recent lambda track as a trail so the reversal is visible as a loop. Place the decorative stars at the actual zodiac longitudes used by `zodiacLabelPositions` (after fixing finding 15) so "against the background stars" means something, and label the panel with what its axis is.

findings.title: Demo code re-derives physics that @cosmic/physics already owns, with a duplicated year constant
findings.evidence: logic.ts:382-383 computes `modelYearDays * Math.pow(aAu, 1.5)` - Kepler's third law, re-implemented in demo code, with `args.modelYearDays ?? 365.25` hardcoded at :377 as a fallback for `AstroConstants.TIME.YEAR_S / DAY_S` (= 31557600/86400 = 365.25). logic.ts:189-191 re-derives the conic `r = a(1-e*e)/(1 + e*cos(nu))` and the periapsis rotation `theta = nu + varpiRad`, duplicating the geometry already in `orbitStateAtModelDay` (retrogradeMotionModel.ts:146-157). main.ts:52-55 defines a third `wrap360` duplicating the model's private `wrap0To360Deg` (retrogradeMotionModel.ts:16-20). The stationary tolerances are defined twice with the same values: logic.ts:11-12 (`DEFAULT_EPS_LO_DEG_PER_DAY = 0.005`, `_HI = 0.01`) and main.ts:209-210 (`STATIONARY_EPS_LO/HI` = the same two numbers). CLAUDE.md: "All physics models MUST come from @cosmic/physics - no inline equations in demo code."
findings.scenario: If AstroConstants.TIME.YEAR_S is ever changed (for instance to the tropical year, which is already in that file as MEAN_TROPICAL_YEAR_DAYS = 365.2422), the orbit ellipses and the Delta-n readout keep using 365.25 from logic.ts while the plotted series uses the new value - the drawn orbits and the computed longitudes silently disagree. Changing one epsilon without the other makes the badge and the classifier disagree about what counts as stationary.
findings.fix: Export `orbitalPeriodDaysFromAu` and a conic-point helper from packages/physics (both already exist internally as `TwoBodyAnalytic.orbitalPeriodYrFromAuSolar` and the geometry in `orbitStateAtModelDay`) and have logic.ts call them instead of re-deriving; drop the 365.25 fallback so an unavailable constant fails loudly. Export `wrap0To360Deg` from the model and delete main.ts:52-55. Keep one copy of the two epsilons - export them from logic.ts and have main.ts import them.

findings.title: The demo's review of record claims student-ready, zero sign bugs and full WCAG, against a stub parity audit
findings.evidence: docs/reviews/retrograde-motion.md:6 states "**Status:** Student-ready. All gates green."; :14 "Zero critical issues remain"; :181 "**Zero sign bugs found.**" (contradicted by the P0 arc bug above, which that review's own coordinate audit lists as item 5 "Zodiac ring labels: Correct" without ever examining the arc); :197 and :222 "Accessibility | Full (aria-labels, keyboard nav, reduced motion)" and "Full WCAG keyboard navigation, screen reader support" (contradicted by two unnamed SVGs and no state announcement); :49 "Accessibility (WCAG) | Full" in a comparison table against five named external tools. Meanwhile docs/audits/migrations/retrograde-motion-parity.md - which the exhibit frontmatter cites as `parityAuditPath` - says "Pending detailed parity review." in all four sections and "Current recommendation: experimental until parity review is completed." The review is also stale: its station-mode column list (:128-133) names four columns where the code has seven (main.ts:1686-1694), and its Known Limitation 3 (:209) says "SVG rebuilds every frame", which the static/dynamic layer split fixed.
findings.scenario: The review doc is the artifact an instructor or a grant reviewer reads to decide whether to put this in front of a class, and it is also quoted under a "Grant-Relevant Metrics" heading (:217-227) claiming "155 automated tests verify scientific correctness" and "three independent review agents found zero critical issues". Someone acts on "Student-ready, all gates green" and ships a demo with a wrong drawing, two inaccessible panels and a false station-mode claim.
findings.fix: Rewrite docs/reviews/retrograde-motion.md as a dated review that states the actual status (experimental, parity audit pending), remove the "Zero sign bugs found", "Student-ready" and "Accessibility: Full" claims, correct the stale station-mode column list and the fixed per-frame-rebuild limitation, and replace the test-count totals with what the files contain. Leave the exhibit frontmatter as it is - `readiness: experimental` / `status: draft` is the defensible pair and the evidence supports keeping it there. Reconsider `featured: true` (apps/site/src/content/demos/retrograde-motion.md:14), which puts an experimental demo in the homepage featured grid as one of three entry points (apps/site/src/pages/index.astro:26).

findings.title: Design-system contract tests are largely vacuous and exempt an invariant they claim to enforce
findings.evidence: Line 30 `expect(main).toContain("initStarfield")` is satisfied by the import statement at main.ts:7 alone, so the Starfield contract passes even if `initStarfield()` is never called. Line 167 "SVG backgrounds use translucent treatment" asserts `expect(css).toMatch(/color-mix|radial-gradient|--cp-instr-panel-bg/)` - a match anywhere in a 574-line file, which style.css satisfies 20 times over for unrelated reasons. Line 172 "controls or readouts use backdrop-filter or translucent bg" asserts only `expect(css).not.toMatch(/background:\s*(#|rgb|hsl)/)`, an absence check an empty file would pass, and it never checks that any panel actually uses `--cp-instr-panel-bg` + blur. Lines 62-66 title themselves "main.ts has no legacy tokens" but assert only `not.toContain("--cp-accent3")`, with a comment explicitly permitting `--cp-warning` - which design invariant 7 (Token Purity) names as forbidden in demo code. Nothing tests glow opacity (invariant 6) or the reduced-motion override (invariant 8).
findings.scenario: The per-demo contract suite is the gate that is supposed to make the eight design invariants non-negotiable, and it reports green on a demo that smuggles Unicode math past the validator, paints an opaque `fill: var(--cp-bg0)` rect inside a translucent panel (main.ts:1102), and would still report green if the starfield were never initialised. The badge of compliance is cheaper than compliance.
findings.fix: Make each assertion name the thing it guards: assert a call shape (`/initStarfield\s*\(/`) not a substring; assert that `.viz-panel` specifically declares both `--cp-instr-panel-bg` and `backdrop-filter`; scan main.ts for opaque SVG `fill` values pointing at `--cp-bg*`; drop the `--cp-warning` exemption so the test matches invariant 7; and add the missing glow-opacity and reduced-motion assertions. Since moon-phases/design-contracts.test.ts is the golden reference these were copied from, check whether the same vacuous assertions were propagated to the other twelve demos.

findings.title: "Sep equinox" anchor is 3.4 days off the model's own equinox and reports a non-zero declination
findings.evidence: The four anchors are days 80, 172, 266, 356 (main.ts:1191-1194, station rows at main.ts:336-340, scrub ticks at index.html:339-342). The model's declination is delta = asin(sin eps * sin(2*PI*(d-80)/365.2422)) (seasonsModel.ts:22-24), so its stationary points are fixed at 80, 171.31, 262.62 and 353.93. I recomputed each anchor at eps = 23.5: day 80 -> delta = 0.000 deg, 12.000 h at 40 N; day 172 -> +23.498 deg; day 266 -> delta = -1.327 deg, 11.851 h at 40 N, noon altitude 48.67 deg; day 356 -> -23.484 deg. The model's own September equinox (delta = 0.0004 deg) is day 262.62. The uniform-L model cannot put the September equinox at day 266 because it forces the two equinoxes exactly half a tropical year apart; the real 186 d / 179 d asymmetry comes from eccentricity, which this model omits.
findings.scenario: Student clicks "Mar equinox" and records delta = 0.0 deg, day length 12h 00m. They click "Sep equinox" expecting the same and get delta = -1.3 deg, 11h 51m, noon altitude 48.7 deg instead of 50.0 deg. In Station Mode the "Sep equinox" row is written into their data table as delta = -1.3, so the lab worksheet now contains an equinox with unequal day and night, contradicting the demo's own contextual message "nearly equal day and night worldwide" and learning goal 1.
findings.fix: Either (a) derive the anchor days from the model instead of hardcoding calendar dates — expose the stationary points from seasonsModel (80, 80+T/4, 80+T/2, 80+3T/4) and label the buttons "Sep equinox (model)", or (b) keep the calendar days and add the equation of centre to sunDeclinationDeg so the model's equinoxes land on the real dates. (b) is the scientifically honest fix and needs Anna's approval because it changes the model's identity; (a) is the smallest correct fix. Either way the station-mode anchor rows (main.ts:336-340) and the scrub ticks (index.html:339-342) must read from the same source.

findings.title: Polar day/night badge hardcodes 66.5 deg instead of 90 - epsilon, so it is wrong whenever the tilt slider moves
findings.evidence: `polarLatitudeBadge.hidden = Math.abs(latitudeDeg) < 66.5;` (main.ts:794). The polar-day condition from the demo's own dayLengthHours is |lat| >= 90 - delta_max = 90 - epsilon. I recomputed at day 172: tilt=40, lat=55 -> delta=40.00, day length 24.000 h (polar day) with badgeShown=false; tilt=40, lat=50.1 -> 24.000 h, badge hidden; tilt=60, lat=35 -> 24.000 h, badge hidden; tilt=10, lat=70 -> 15.863 h (no polar day) with badgeShown=true; tilt=10, lat=75 -> 17.486 h, badge still shown. The adjacent line has a second threshold inconsistency: `noSeasonsBadge.hidden = axialTiltDeg >= 0.5` (main.ts:793) while contextualMessage fires its no-seasons text at `axialTiltDeg < 1` (logic.ts:470), so at tilt = 0.7 the context line says "no seasons" and the badge is hidden.
findings.scenario: Student drags tilt to 40 deg (a standard "what if Earth were tilted more?" exercise), sets latitude 55 N, clicks "Jun solstice". The readout shows "24h 00m" and the globe correctly shows the 50 deg arctic circle wholly lit, but no badge explains the 24 h value, so the student reports it as a bug or a glitch. Conversely at tilt 10 deg and latitude 70 N the badge claims polar day/night is possible when the model gives 15h 52m and never reaches 24 h at any day.
findings.fix: Replace the literal with the model: `polarLatitudeBadge.hidden = Math.abs(latitudeDeg) < 90 - clamp(axialTiltDeg, 0, 90);` in main.ts:794, and align main.ts:793 with logic.ts:470 by exporting one NO_SEASONS_TILT_DEG threshold from logic.ts and using it in both places. Add a unit test over a grid of (tilt, lat) asserting the badge is shown exactly when SeasonsModel.dayLengthHours hits 24 or 0 at some day of the year.

findings.title: Earth revolves clockwise on screen while a "Polaris" arrow asserts a north-pole view, and no viewpoint is stated
findings.evidence: orbitPosition returns `y: rScaled * Math.sin(angleRad)` (logic.ts:77) and SVG y points down, so increasing day sweeps clockwise on screen. orbitSeasonLabelPositions (logic.ts:396-412) places Mar at +75.9 deg, Jun at 165.9, Sep at 255.9, Dec at 345.9 in the same y-down frame, i.e. Mar lower-right, Jun lower-left, Sep upper-left, Dec upper-right — the drawn sequence Mar -> Jun -> Sep -> Dec is clockwise. Viewed from the north ecliptic pole Earth's revolution is counter-clockwise. The panel is only self-consistent as a south-pole view, but index.html:201-204 draws an in-plane arrow from Earth labelled "Polaris" (the north celestial pole), and I traced its orientation as physically correct for a north-up reading: at the Jun label the axis direction (sin 23.5, -cos 23.5) dotted with the outward radial gives -0.611 (pointing toward the Sun) and at Dec it gives +0.611 (away). The orbit title (index.html:173) says only "Orbit (exaggerated distance)" — no viewing direction anywhere on the page. Separately, polarisIndicatorEndpoints (logic.ts:422-433) draws a 23.5 deg tilt from screen-vertical inside a face-on view (the orbit is a perfect circle, r=140), where screen-vertical is an in-plane direction, so the out-of-plane obliquity is drawn in the wrong plane at full length instead of projecting to length ~L*sin(eps).
findings.scenario: Student reads the orbit panel as the standard textbook top-down (north-up) figure — which the Polaris arrow invites — and concludes Earth orbits clockwise as seen from above the north pole. They then carry that handedness into retrograde-motion, keplers-laws and any sky-motion question. Nothing on the page contradicts them; the caveat lives only in seasons.md frontmatter, which students never see.
findings.fix: Pick one convention and make the drawing state it. Smallest correct fix: negate the y term in orbitPosition (logic.ts:77) and in orbitSeasonLabelPositions (logic.ts:408) so the motion is counter-clockwise, flip the drag handler's `Math.atan2(local.y, local.x)` (main.ts:1148) to match, change the orbit title to "Orbit, viewed from above the north ecliptic pole (distance exaggerated)", and redraw the Polaris indicator as a fixed short arrow of length L*sin(eps) rather than a full-length 23.5 deg screen tilt. Add an e2e assertion that cy at day 94 is negative (above the Sun) with the north-pole caption in place.

findings.title: Unicode math glyphs reach reader-visible text through \uXXXX escapes the validator cannot see, plus a literal ± in the HTML
findings.evidence: Reader-visible strings built from escapes: `causalTiltChip.textContent = `ε ${...}`` (main.ts:789, epsilon), `causalDeclinationChip.textContent = `δ ${...}`` (main.ts:790, delta), formatDegreeValue returns `${...}°` (main.ts:656,658, degree sign), export note `±${...} days` (main.ts:893), help rows `"← / →"` and `"Step ±1 day"` (main.ts:253-254), formatLatitude returns `"0° (Equator)"` and `${absText}°${dir}` (logic.ts:349,354), contextualMessage returns `"...stays near 0° all year"` (logic.ts:471). scripts/validate-math-formatting.mjs:33 tests the raw file text against FORBIDDEN_UNICODE_MATH, so it sees the seven ASCII characters `°` and passes — exactly the blind spot CLAUDE.md names ("no \uXXXX escapes that produce them (the validator cannot see escapes)"). Separately index.html:455 contains a literal `±2 days`; U+00B1 is absent from the regex at line 33, so that passes too. Within one screen the same quantity is shown two ways: the readout strip uses `deg` (index.html:400,404) while the causal-ladder chips and the latitude value render the ° glyph.
findings.scenario: Any inherited text-transform or font fallback on .seasons-value-chip or .control__value mutates these glyphs with every test green — the documented 2026-09-05 incident where an inherited uppercase turned nu into N and mu into M. Concretely, a student at tilt 23.5 sees the chip "ε 23.5°" rendered from a raw codepoint that no KaTeX node guards; under text-transform: uppercase it becomes "Ε 23.5°", a different symbol.
findings.fix: Replace every escape with KaTeX: render the causal chips with renderMath() from @cosmic/runtime using `$\varepsilon = 23.5^{\circ}$` and `$\delta = -1.3^{\circ}$`, change formatDegreeValue and formatLatitude to emit `^{\circ}` LaTeX (or plain ASCII "deg" to match the readout strip), replace main.ts:893 and index.html:455 with `$\pm$`, and use `$\leftarrow$ / $\rightarrow$` and `$\pm 1$` in the help rows. Then close the hole: add `\\u00B0`, `\\u03B4`, `\\u03B5` and the other escape forms to scripts/validate-math-formatting.mjs:33 as a second pattern, and add U+00B1 to FORBIDDEN_UNICODE_MATH.

findings.title: The draggable Earth marker is a focusable role=button with no key handler, inside a role=img subtree
findings.evidence: #seasonStage carries `role="img"` (index.html:151) and #earthOrbitDot inside it carries `role="button"`, `tabindex="0"` and aria-label "Earth marker. Drag along orbit to set day of year." (index.html:185-192). role=img prunes the whole subtree from the accessibility tree, so the marker has no accessible name or role for assistive tech while still being in the tab order. main.ts:1231-1241 registers only pointerdown/pointermove/pointerup/pointercancel/lostpointercapture on it — there is no keydown listener anywhere for this element (the only keydown is the document-level handler at main.ts:1320). Pressing Enter does nothing; pressing Space falls through to the document handler and starts the year animation instead of activating the "button". apps/site/tests/seasons.spec.ts:24-33 asserts `role="img"`, pinning the defect.
findings.scenario: Keyboard-only student tabs onto the Earth marker, sees a focus ring on a control announced as nothing (pruned by role=img), presses Enter — nothing happens — then presses Space expecting activation and instead launches a 10-second year animation that moves every readout. A screen-reader user never reaches the control's description at all.
findings.fix: Change #seasonStage to `role="group"` (or drop role and keep aria-labelledby on a <title>) so the subtree is exposed, then give #earthOrbitDot real keyboard semantics: role="slider" with aria-valuemin=1, aria-valuemax=365, aria-valuenow and aria-valuetext set from formatDateFromDayOfYear in render(), plus a keydown handler on the element handling ArrowLeft/Right (+/-1 day), ArrowUp/Down (+/-30), Home/End, and calling stopPropagation so Space never reaches the document handler. Update apps/site/tests/seasons.spec.ts:24-33 to assert the new role and add a keyboard test.

findings.title: aria-live context message is rewritten on every frame of the 10-second year animation
findings.evidence: #contextMessage has `aria-live="polite"` (index.html:418, asserted by design-contracts.test.ts:247-250) and `contextMessage.textContent = msg;` sits inside render() (main.ts:807). render() is called from tick() on every requestAnimationFrame (main.ts:531) for YEAR_ANIM_DURATION_MS = 10_000 (main.ts:496), so at 60 fps that is ~600 textContent assignments; each assignment replaces the text node and mutates the live region even when the string is unchanged. The same render() also writes six readout spans and the two causal chips, none of which are in a live region, so the derived values (declination, day length, noon altitude) are never announced when a slider changes.
findings.scenario: Screen-reader user presses Space to play the year. The polite queue receives ~600 mutations in 10 s; the reader either floods with repeated "June solstice: longest day in the North..." or falls silent under coalescing. Meanwhile a student who drags the latitude slider hears only the raw slider number and is never told the day length or noon altitude changed, which is the entire point of the control.
findings.fix: Hoist the live-region write out of render(): keep the last announced string in a module variable and only call setLiveRegionText (already imported from @cosmic/runtime) when the string actually changes AND isAnimating is false; render the visible paragraph without aria-live and mirror it into #status instead. Then add a debounced announcement (~400 ms after the last input) that reads "Day 172, Jun 21: declination 23.5 deg, day length 14h 51m, noon altitude 73.5 deg" so slider changes are announced once.

findings.title: Orbit drag is unusable on touch: no touch-action, and the handle is about 7.5 px across at 320 px
findings.evidence: startOrbitDrag uses pointerdown + setPointerCapture (main.ts:1172-1184) but `grep -rn touch-action` returns nothing in apps/demos/src/demos/seasons/style.css or ../../shared/*.css, so the element keeps the default touch-action: auto and the browser hands the gesture to page panning once it is recognised as a scroll. Size: #earthOrbitDot has r="12" in a 920x420 viewBox (index.html:189) and .stage__svg is `width: 100%` with `height: auto` (style.css:111-113); at 1024 px and below the shell stacks to one column (style.css:16-26), so on a 320 px viewport the stage is about 288 px wide -> scale 288/920 = 0.313 -> the dot renders 24*0.313 = 7.5 px across, against the 44 px minimum. .stage__earth sets `cursor: grab` and a :hover filter (style.css:152-165), both mouse-only affordances.
findings.scenario: Student on a phone sees a 7.5 px Earth dot with no visible affordance, touches it and drags; the page scrolls instead of the Earth moving. They conclude the orbit is decoration. /play/ routes are not covered by reflow.spec.ts (per CLAUDE.md), so nothing fails.
findings.fix: Add `touch-action: none;` to .stage__earth in style.css:152 and give the marker an invisible larger hit area (a concentric `<circle r="26" fill="transparent" pointer-events="all">` in the same group, or `stroke: transparent; stroke-width: 28px; paint-order: stroke`). Make the drag affordance non-hover (a dashed ring or a small grab glyph rendered at all times). Add a 320 px Playwright case for /play/seasons/ that drags the marker and asserts #dayOfYear changed.

findings.title: ArrowRight cannot wrap past day 365 — the keyboard dead-ends at Dec 31
findings.evidence: ArrowRight sets `state.dayOfYear = ((state.dayOfYear - 1 + 1) % 365.25) + 1` (main.ts:1331) and render() then does `const day = clamp(Math.round(state.dayOfYear), 1, 365); state.dayOfYear = day;` (main.ts:770-775). I traced day 365: ((365-1+1) % 365.25) + 1 = (365 % 365.25) + 1 = 366, which render clamps to 365 and writes back — the state is unchanged, so every further ArrowRight is a no-op. ArrowLeft from day 1 gives ((1-1-1+365.25) % 365.25) + 1 = 365.25 -> rounds to 365 and wraps correctly. The wrap modulus is 365.25 in five places (main.ts:513, 530, 1132, 1331-1358) while the slider max is 365 (index.html:28) and formatDateFromDayOfYear assumes a 365-day year (logic.ts:16-34), which is what opens the 1.25-day dead zone.
findings.scenario: Student scrubs the year with the right arrow key (the documented interaction — help row "Step +/-1 day", main.ts:253). At Dec 31 the readouts freeze; pressing ArrowRight twenty more times changes nothing and the student cannot get back to January without reaching for the mouse. The e2e spec only tests ArrowRight from day 80 (seasons.spec.ts:216-223), so this passes.
findings.fix: Wrap on the same 365-day grid the rest of the demo uses: in main.ts:1331-1358 replace the 365.25 modulus with 365 (`state.dayOfYear = ((state.dayOfYear - 1 + step + 365) % 365) + 1`), and do the same at main.ts:513, 530 and 1132 so the animation and preset transitions share one year length. Add e2e cases stepping right from 365 and left from 1.

findings.title: Both prior physics reviews audit a UI that no longer exists and declare "no physics bugs were found"
findings.evidence: docs/reviews/seasons.md (committed 2026-02-07, 144ae01) describes `rScaled = 140 * clamp(distanceAu, 0.95, 1.05)` — the current orbitPosition is `orbitR * (1 + distExaggeration * (distanceAu - 1))` (logic.ts:75) — and audits a "Tilt/sunlight panel" with a disk, subsolar dot, observer dot and a sunlight arrow at x1=-220, none of which exist in index.html today. Its SVG coordinate check concludes the orbit "progresses clockwise visually" and then rules "This matches the apparent direction of Earth's orbit as seen from the ecliptic north pole... PASS", which is backwards. docs/reviews/2026-02-07-seasons-eclipse-physics-review.md:122 blesses globeAxisEndpoints leaning the north pole right because "the sun is to the right of the globe"; the shipped demo puts the Sun on the LEFT (index.html:262-272 rays at x=-262..-158, main.ts:567) and uses globeAxisScreen, which leans it left. Line 388 of that file blesses the shifting-circle terminator that logic.ts:131-148 records as geometrically impossible and removed. Line 390 says the title reads "Orbit (toy distance)" with 8x exaggeration; it reads "Orbit (exaggerated distance)" (index.html:173) at 2x (main.ts:708). Both files close with "Issues Found: None" / "No physics bugs were found". The demo was rewritten 2026-09-09 (8fcedd6).
findings.scenario: The next promotion review (or /cp-promote seasons) reads "No physics bugs were found" for seasons, treats the physics as cleared, and launch-ready is granted over the P0 day-arc defect and the Sep-equinox anchor error — the documented failure mode where a green artifact pins a defect instead of catching it.
findings.fix: Mark both files stale at the top ("AUDITS THE PRE-2026-09-09 SIDE-VIEW PANEL; superseded") and write a dated replacement review of the current globe projection, orbit panel and anchor days, recording the clockwise-orbit question as open rather than PASS. Add the stale-review check to the readiness gate: a review whose newest commit predates the demo's newest source commit does not count as evidence.

findings.title: A dead parallel projection stack survives with 25+ green tests pinning the opposite convention
findings.evidence: axisEndpoint (logic.ts:85), diskMarkerY (logic.ts:97), latitudeToGlobeY (logic.ts:263), latitudeBandEllipse (logic.ts:277) and globeAxisEndpoints (logic.ts:308) are exported but `grep -rn` across apps and packages (excluding tests and logic.ts itself) finds zero importers; main.ts imports none of them (verified by grep count 0 each). Only latitudeBandEllipse is still reachable, via the defective dayLengthArcGeometry. Their tests are live and green: logic.test.ts:348-420 asserts latitudeBandEllipse's `ry = 0` collapse at zero tilt and globeAxisEndpoints' "north end tilts right" (line 402: `expect(axis.x2).toBeGreaterThan(200)`) — the exact opposite of the shipped globeAxisScreen, which the same file tests at line 270 as leaning the north pole LEFT toward the Sun. logic.test.ts:131-134 also pins `default distExaggeration is 8` while main.ts:708 passes 2.
findings.scenario: A reviewer runs the demo suite, sees ~40 green geometry tests, and concludes the globe geometry is covered. Half of those tests certify a side-view convention with the Sun on the right that the demo abandoned, and one certifies the opposite axis lean. The next person who needs a latitude ellipse reaches for latitudeBandEllipse because it is tested, reintroducing the P0.
findings.fix: Delete axisEndpoint, diskMarkerY, latitudeToGlobeY and globeAxisEndpoints from logic.ts along with their describe blocks in logic.test.ts (lines 153-181, 319-420), and delete latitudeBandEllipse once dayLengthArcGeometry is rebuilt on projectLatitudeCircle. Change the orbitPosition default to 2 so logic.test.ts:131-134 tests the value the demo actually uses, or drop the default and make the argument required.

findings.title: "Cel. Equator" overlay draws the terrestrial equator and "Ecliptic" draws a line the projection contradicts
findings.evidence: The chip labelled "Cel. Equator" (index.html:518-524) targets #globe-equator, which main.ts:595 fills with `setBand(globeEquator, 0)` — the same projectLatitudeCircle(0, dec, 20, R) call used for #equator-band at main.ts:590. The two elements therefore draw identical ellipses; turning on "Cel. Equator" overdraws the terrestrial equator and labels it as a great circle on the sky. The "Ecliptic" chip (index.html:525-531) targets #globe-ecliptic, a static `<line x1="-160" y1="0" x2="160" y2="0">` (index.html:295) that never changes with declination; under the panel's own 20 deg view elevation the ecliptic great circle through the globe centre would project to an ellipse of ry = R*sin(20 deg) = 155*0.342 = 53 px, not a horizontal line. Both chip tooltips read "Reference circles used in sky geometry" (index.html:522,529), which says nothing. The e2e spec blesses both by name (seasons.spec.ts: "clicking Cel. Equator overlay chip shows the celestial equator", "clicking Ecliptic overlay chip shows the ecliptic line").
findings.scenario: Student opens Overlays to find the celestial equator and the ecliptic — the two circles whose 23.5 deg inclination IS the cause of seasons — and gets a duplicate of the terrestrial equator plus a horizontal line that does not move when they drag through the year. They leave believing the celestial equator is a line on the Earth's surface and that the ecliptic is fixed relative to the globe.
findings.fix: Remove #globe-equator and its chip (it duplicates #equator-band), and either delete the ecliptic overlay or make it real: draw the great circle of the ecliptic plane under the same Rx(view)*Rz(dec) map as the bands, which is an ellipse with rx = R, ry = R*sin(view) rotated with the declination, and retitle the chips with what they show ("Equator", "Ecliptic plane through Earth's centre"). Update seasons.spec.ts so the test names stop certifying the mislabel.

findings.title: "Day arc" tooltip promises the Sun's path across the sky; the drawing is the lit part of a latitude circle
findings.evidence: The chip's title attribute reads "Path of the Sun across the sky for your latitude." (index.html:495). The element it toggles is #dayArc / #nightArc (main.ts: overlayTargets "day-arc": [dayArc, nightArc]), filled by dayLengthArcGeometry (logic.ts:513-567), which returns the lit and unlit portions of the observer's circle of latitude ON THE GLOBE — a terrestrial curve traced by the observer as Earth rotates, clipped by `url(#globe-clip)` inside the globe group (index.html:289-291). It is not an altitude-azimuth sky path; the demo has no sky dome.
findings.scenario: Student toggles "Day arc" looking for the Sun's daily arc across the sky (rising in the east, culminating at the noon altitude the readout gives, setting in the west) and is shown a curve on the Earth's surface instead. They map the amber curve's highest point onto the "Noon altitude 73.5 deg" readout, which is a different quantity in a different frame, and build a wrong mental model of what noon altitude means.
findings.fix: Retitle the chip "Your latitude circle, day side and night side" and relabel the two paths in the legend, or add a separate small sky-dome panel that actually plots altitude vs hour angle from the model and move the "Path of the Sun across the sky" wording there. The retitle is the smallest honest fix.

findings.title: Hour grid draws straight vertical lines and calls them meridians
findings.evidence: initHourGrid (main.ts:637-651) appends five `<line>` elements at x = -100, -50, 0, 50, 100 running y = -155 to +155, inside the group commented "Hour grid (meridian lines) [S8]" (index.html:298-299), with the chip tooltip "Reference hour lines for reading daylight span" (index.html:506). Meridians are great circles through the poles; under the panel's own Rx(20 deg)*Rz(dec) map each projects to a half-ellipse, and all of them must rotate with the declination exactly as the latitude bands and axis do. These lines are built once at init and never touched by renderGlobe, so they do not move with the day, do not converge at the poles, and are not equally spaced in longitude (equal screen spacing corresponds to arcsin spacing in longitude, so the outer "hours" span far more than one hour).
findings.scenario: Student toggles the hour grid on to count daylight hours against the day arc. The lines do not meet at the poles, do not tilt with the axis, and the spacing is not uniform in longitude, so counting grid cells between the day arc's endpoints gives a wrong hour count — and at latitude 60 N the error is large because screen-x spacing compresses near the limb.
findings.fix: Either delete the overlay and its chip (index.html:498-511, main.ts:637-651, overlayTargets entry), or render it correctly from renderGlobe: for each of 12 longitudes, project the meridian semicircle with the same m-matrix used by projectLatitudeCircle and emit a rotated elliptical arc, rebuilt whenever the declination changes. Deletion is the smaller correct fix until someone needs it.

findings.title: Five different year lengths and three copies of the equinox/perihelion epochs outside the physics model
findings.evidence: seasonsModel.ts owns the constants (TROPICAL_YEAR_DAYS = AstroConstants.TIME.MEAN_TROPICAL_YEAR_DAYS = 365.2422 at seasonsModel.ts:4, dayOfMarchEquinox default 80 at line 20, perihelionDay default 3 at lines 49 and 61). They are re-declared outside it: logic.ts:42-43 (`yearDays = 365.2422`, `dayOfMarchEquinox = 80` inside seasonFromPhaseNorth), logic.ts:364 (`yearLength = 365.25`), logic.ts:396 (`MAR_ANGLE = (77 / 365.25) * 2 * PI`), main.ts:408-409 (ORBIT_YEAR_DAYS = 365.2422, ORBIT_PERIHELION_DAY = 3), main.ts:513, 530, 1132, 1331-1358 (bare 365.25), and logic.ts:16-34 where formatDateFromDayOfYear sums the months to exactly 365. So the state advances on a 365.25-day year, seasons are classified on a 365.2422-day year, labels are placed on a 365.25-day year and dates are formatted on a 365-day year. design-contracts.test.ts:122-126 is supposed to guard this and only asserts `not.toMatch(/function\s+sunDeclination/)`, a negative that any renamed reimplementation passes.
findings.scenario: The year-length mismatch is already producing the ArrowRight dead-end at day 365 (365.25 modulus vs 365 clamp). Any future change to the equinox epoch in seasonsModel.ts silently desynchronises the season labels, the orbit-angle mapping, the drag handler and the scrub ticks, because four of them read their own copy — the architecture defect that will keep producing P0s.
findings.fix: Export one DAYS_IN_MODEL_YEAR and the MARCH_EQUINOX_DAY / PERIHELION_DAY epochs from seasonsModel.ts, import them in logic.ts and main.ts, and delete every literal 365, 365.25 and 365.2422 from the demo (including the month table's implicit 365 — derive it or state the non-leap assumption in one place). Replace the design-contracts assertion with a positive one: scan logic.ts and main.ts for numeric literals matching /36[45](\.\d+)?/ and fail on any hit.

findings.title: No test anywhere constrains a declination or day-length value at an asymmetric date
findings.evidence: Every value assertion in seasonsModel.test.ts is at a symmetric or limiting point: delta = 0 at the anchor day (line 6, named "(given formula)" — it re-asserts the implementation's own epoch), |delta - eps| <= 0.5 at day 172 (line 30), |delta + eps| <= 0.5 at day 356 (line 44), 12 h at the equator (line 48), 24 h / 0 h at the pole (lines 74, 80), N/S symmetry at the equinox where both sides are exactly 12 (line 87), 90 deg noon altitude at lat = dec (line 98), perihelion/aphelion ordering (lines 104-106). There is no (lat, dec) pair where the answer is an ordinary number: nothing pins delta = +16.19 deg on day 125, 13.43 h at 32.7 N, or delta = -13.83 deg on day 300. The e2e spec is weaker still — "tilt slider updates declination readout" only asserts the text changed (seasons.spec.ts:64-73) and the one numeric check is `> 80` at tilt 90 (last test). sunNoonAltitudeDeg has no test at a general (phi, delta) pair and none for its negative (polar-night) branch. Four shipped functions have zero tests: dayLengthArcGeometry, contextualMessage, orbitSeasonLabelPositions and polarisIndicatorEndpoints (grep count 0 each in logic.test.ts) — which is why the P0 day-arc defect went unnoticed. seasons.spec.ts:24-33 asserts role="img", pinning the a11y defect.
findings.scenario: A wrong phase epoch, a swapped sin/cos in L, or a reintroduced sign error anywhere off the solstices and equinoxes ships green. The demo's whole mid-season range — where students actually read values, and where the Sep-equinox anchor error already lives — is unconstrained, which is the documented repeat failure ("a waxing/waning swap passed because tests checked only full and new moon").
findings.fix: Add a golden table to seasonsModel.test.ts with at least four asymmetric rows computed independently and checked against ephemeris, e.g. day 125 / eps 23.5 -> delta = 16.19 deg (+/-0.01) with day length 13.432 h at 32.7 N, day 300 -> -13.83 deg with 14.724 h at 54.8 S, day 45 -> -13.05 deg with 6.826 h at 69.7 N, and a noon-altitude row that goes negative at 80 N on day 356. Add logic.test.ts coverage for dayLengthArcGeometry (endpoints on x = 0 for several asymmetric lat/dec), contextualMessage (each branch, including the day-266 band) and orbitSeasonLabelPositions (the sense of revolution).

findings.title: Understand tab teaches the Rydberg formula with R_infinity in SI units, contradicting the instrument's own readout
findings.evidence: `$$\frac{1}{\lambda} = R_\infty \left(\frac{1}{n_{\text{lower}}^2} - \frac{1}{n_{\text{upper}}^2}\right), \quad R_\infty = 1.097 \times 10^7\ \text{m}^{-1}$$`. Two defects. (1) Units: m^-1 is SI, which CLAUDE.md and .agents/references/invariants.md forbid in reader-visible copy ('NEVER use SI units'); the repo convention is CGS, so this should be cm^-1. (2) Constant: the hydrogen series needs R_H = 1.0967758e7 m^-1, not the infinite-nuclear-mass R_infinity = 1.0973732e7 m^-1. I computed the card's own prediction: with the printed 1.097e7, lambda(3->2) = 656.34 nm; with the exact R_infinity, 656.11 nm. The instrument's readout, computed from R_H in `spectralLineModel.ts:36`, says 656.5 nm. Using R_infinity for hydrogen is precisely the 0.054% error that prior review finding SL-1 removed from the code on 2026-09-03 — it survives in the teaching copy beside the corrected number.
findings.scenario: Student reads the Rydberg card, computes 1/lambda = 1.097e7 x (1/4 - 1/9) by hand, gets 656.3 nm, compares it with the demo's 656.5 nm readout, and cannot tell which is wrong — or trusts the card and carries R_infinity into every later hydrogen calculation.
findings.fix: In index.html:346 write the formula with R_H, give its value in cm^-1 (`R_H = 1.0967758 \times 10^5\ \text{cm}^{-1}`), and add one bullet saying R_infinity assumes an infinitely heavy nucleus while R_H carries the reduced-mass factor m_p/(m_p+m_e) = 0.9994566 — the distinction is worth 0.35 nm at H-alpha and is exactly what the instrument computes. Source the number from `SpectralLineModel.BOHR.RYDBERG_EV` rather than retyping it.

findings.title: Three live reader-visible strings overwrite rendered KaTeX with ASCII and Unicode pseudo-math
findings.evidence: `initMath(document)` runs exactly once, after the first `render()` (main.ts:2215-2216), and nothing re-typesets afterwards. Three strings are then written as raw text into elements that started as LaTeX: (1) main.ts:721 `scalingInsight.textContent = "Delta E ~ 27.2 eV / n^3 (large n). At n=20, adjacent spacing ~ 0.0034 eV."` replaces the KaTeX-rendered `$\Delta E \approx \frac{27.2\ \text{eV}}{n^3}$` authored at index.html:556; (2) main.ts:261 `inverseResult.textContent = \`Inferred ${transitionLabel(...)} (...), Delta E=1.889 eV, residual=0.46 nm (exact).\`` emits both ASCII 'Delta E' and the Unicode arrow from `logic.ts:460` (`\`n = ${nUpper} → n = ${nLower}\``); (3) main.ts:1409 `readoutTransition.textContent = context.transitionText` overwrites the authored `$n = 3 \to n = 2$` at index.html:435 with that same Unicode arrow. The invariant is explicit: 'TS that emits reader-visible math: renderInlineMath() (site) or renderMath() (@cosmic/runtime)'. The project has a recorded incident (2026-09-05, 94 KaTeX nodes uppercased by an inherited text-transform) whose whole lesson is that real math nodes can be checked and stray glyphs in strings cannot.
findings.scenario: Student opens Advanced Hydrogen Tools. The neatly typeset Delta-E scaling line is replaced in place by 'Delta E ~ 27.2 eV / n^3'. Solving an inverse transition prints 'Inferred n = 3 → n = 2 (Balmer), Delta E=1.889 eV' in a panel where every other equation is typeset, and the main Transition readout permanently shows a raw arrow glyph that inherits whatever the surrounding CSS does to it.
findings.fix: Build these three strings as LaTeX and set them with `renderMath()` from @cosmic/runtime instead of `textContent` (or call `initMath` on the three containers after each write). Then add a design-contract test that greps main.ts for `textContent =` assignments containing 'Delta', 'lambda' or a non-ASCII codepoint.

findings.title: Forbidden Unicode math reaches the DOM through \u escapes the validator cannot see
findings.evidence: `photon.textContent = "γ"` (main.ts:992), `photonLabel.textContent = "γ"` (main.ts:1145), `ionRight.textContent = "∞"` (main.ts:1057), and the Station Mode row labels `"Hα"`, `"Hβ"`, `"Hγ"`, `"Hδ"` (main.ts:2146-2149), which also go into the copied CSV. Every one of those codepoints — gamma U+03B3, infinity U+221E, alpha/beta/delta — is in the validator's own blocklist `FORBIDDEN_UNICODE_MATH` (scripts/validate-math-formatting.mjs:33), and `apps/demos/src/demos` is in its SCAN_ROOTS (line 20). The check is `FORBIDDEN_UNICODE_MATH.test(raw)` against the file bytes (line 114), so the escaped form never matches while the browser renders the exact banned glyph. The invariants file names this hole verbatim: 'no \uXXXX escapes that produce them (the validator cannot see escapes)'.
findings.scenario: The build and `pnpm lint` pass clean, while the Bohr atom and the energy ladder both label the photon with a bare Unicode gamma and the ionization limit with a bare infinity sign — glyphs that inherit the surrounding CSS and are not checkable, the exact failure mode that turned nu into 'N' across 14 demos in September.
findings.fix: Render the photon and infinity labels as KaTeX (an SVG `foreignObject` carrying `renderMath("$\\gamma$")`, or a `<text>` whose content is set via renderMath) and write the Station Mode labels as `H-alpha`/`H-beta` ASCII, since a CSV is not a KaTeX surface. Separately, close the validator hole: add a second pattern that flags `\\u(03b3|221e|03b1|...)` escapes in the scanned extensions.

findings.title: Mystery Spectrum shows the answer in the Wavelength readout and announces it to screen readers
findings.evidence: `currentReadoutContext()` hides only the label: `transitionText: hideRepresentativeLabel ? "Hidden during mystery challenge" : elementContext.representativeLineLabel` (main.ts:299) while `wavelengthNm`, `energyEv`, `frequencyHz` and `band` pass through unchanged (main.ts:300-304), and `updateReadouts` writes all of them (main.ts:1411-1424). The representative line is the catalogue's strongest, chosen by `selectRepresentativeElementLine` (logic.ts:382-394): He 587.6, Na D2 589.0, Ca II K 393.4, Fe I 532.8, H Ly-alpha 121.6 (ties at intensity 1.0 break to the shorter wavelength). Each of the five mystery targets therefore has a unique, uniquely identifying number on screen. `announceCurrentTransition` (main.ts:342-347) pushes the same number into the live region: 'Mystery spectrum updated, representative wavelength 589.0 nm.' Meanwhile `syncCopyLockState` disables Copy Results and shows a lock hint (main.ts:333-338, index.html:241), and the e2e spec tests that lock in detail (apps/site/tests/spectral-lines.spec.ts, 'copy results is locked during unrevealed mystery') without ever checking `#readoutWavelength`.
findings.scenario: Student clicks Mystery Spectrum, ignores the unresolvable spectrum entirely, reads 'Wavelength lambda 589.0 nm' off the readout panel, selects Na, and is told 'Correct'. The evidence-commitment gate and the Copy Results lock are both defeated without looking at the drawing.
findings.fix: In `currentReadoutContext` (main.ts:296-308), mask wavelength, energy, frequency and band with an em-dash while `state.mystery.active && !state.mystery.revealed`, and strip the wavelength from the live-region message in `announceCurrentTransition` (main.ts:343-345). Add an e2e assertion that `#readoutWavelength` does not contain a digit during an unrevealed mystery.

findings.title: Bohr orbit selection targets a sub-pixel dashed stroke, unusable by pointer or touch
findings.evidence: Each orbit is a `<circle>` with `fill: "none"`, `"stroke-width": isActive ? 1.8 : 0.8` and `"stroke-dasharray": isActive ? "none" : "4 4"`, carrying `role: "button"`, `tabindex: 0` and click/mouseenter handlers (main.ts:845-889). With SVG's default `pointer-events: visiblePainted` and no fill, the hit region is only the painted stroke: 0.8 user units in a 400-unit viewBox. The Bohr SVG renders at roughly 330 px (`svgRenderScale` is documented around 0.82 at main.ts:786), so an inactive orbit's hit band is about 0.66 px wide — and the dash pattern means half of that ring is not painted and therefore not hittable at all. The WCAG 2.5.8 minimum is 24x24 px (2.5.5 asks 44x44). The focus indicator is also weak: `.orbit-selectable:focus-visible { outline: none; stroke: var(--cp-accent-ice); stroke-width: 2.4; }` (style.css:458-463) replaces the outline with a roughly 2 px stroke change on one of eight concentric rings. The e2e test only ever does `firstOrbit.focus()` then `press("Enter")` (apps/site/tests/spectral-lines.spec.ts, 'orbit selection is keyboard operable'), so the pointer path has no coverage.
findings.scenario: On a museum-station tablet or any touch device a student taps an orbit to pick n=4 and nothing happens, repeatedly, because the target is 0.66 px of dashed line; the tooltip that explains each level's energy also never appears, since it is bound to the same hit region. Keyboard users are fine, which is why this has stayed invisible.
findings.fix: Add a transparent hit ring per orbit — a second `<circle>` with `fill: "none"`, `stroke: "transparent"`, `"stroke-width": 18`, `"pointer-events": "stroke"` carrying the handlers, with the visible ring left `pointer-events: none` — and restore a real focus indicator (`outline: 2px solid var(--cp-accent-ice); outline-offset: 2px` or an explicit focus halo circle). Add a Playwright test that clicks the n=4 orbit by coordinate.

findings.title: The demo keeps two private copies of the Rydberg constant, one of them the value SL-1 removed
findings.evidence: `const rydbergEv = args.rydbergEv ?? 13.605693;` — that default is R_infinity, the exact constant prior review finding SL-1 deleted from `spectralLineModel.ts` on 2026-09-03 for making every hydrogen wavelength 0.054% short. A second copy sits at logic.ts:261: `const eMin = -13.606;` inside `energyLevelY`, while the level energies it maps come from `SpectralLineModel.hydrogenEnergyEv` with R_H = 13.598434599 — so the ladder's own floor is 0.0076 eV below its n=1 line. The function also duplicates `SpectralLineModel.largeNAdjacentSpacingEv` (spectralLineModel.ts:432-436), which already computes 2R/n^3 from the model's constant. Today the only caller passes the right value (`main.ts:720` supplies `SpectralLineModel.BOHR.RYDBERG_EV`), so the wrong default is latent, not live — and the test cannot see it: `logic.test.ts:283-287` asserts only `d20 < d10` and `d10/d20 > 7`, a pure 1/n^3 ratio check that passes identically for either constant (I computed the two: 2R_H/n^3 and 2R_infinity/n^3 differ by 0.0534% at every n, and both give a ratio of exactly 8).
findings.scenario: A future caller writes `computeLargeNSpacingApproximation({ nUpper: 20 })` without the second argument and silently reintroduces the September defect; the unit test stays green because it only checks the n^-3 slope, never the coefficient. This is the architecture defect that keeps producing P0s.
findings.fix: Delete `computeLargeNSpacingApproximation` from logic.ts and call `SpectralLineModel.largeNAdjacentSpacingEv` directly; replace the `eMin = -13.606` literal with `SpectralLineModel.hydrogenEnergyEv({ n: 1 })`. If a parameterised version must stay, make `rydbergEv` required and add a test asserting the returned value equals 2*R_H/n^3 to 1e-9, not just the ratio.

findings.title: Hydrogen has two different invented line-strength sets, both captioned as NIST data
findings.evidence: The Hydrogen tab computes `intensity: 1 / (transition.nUpper - transition.nLower + 1)` (main.ts:1212), which drives both `ctx.lineWidth = Math.max(1.4, line.intensity * 3)` and `ctx.globalAlpha` (main.ts:1264-1266). That gives H-alpha:H-beta:H-gamma:H-delta = 0.50:0.33:0.25:0.20 against Case-B recombination's 1.00:0.35:0.16:0.09, and makes Ly-alpha (1/2) exactly equal to H-alpha, when Ly-alpha is about an order of magnitude stronger in photon number. The Elements tab, for the same element, uses a different invented set: `const balmerIntensities = [1.0, 0.75, 0.55, 0.40, 0.30, 0.22]` (spectralLineModel.ts:474). Both are drawn beneath 'Multi-element line data from the NIST Atomic Spectra Database (strongest lines only)' (index.html:497, repeated in the export notes at logic.ts:567 and asserted by the e2e test 'copy results includes required ... fields'). Prior review finding SL-5 recorded this and is still open.
findings.scenario: Student compares hydrogen on the Hydrogen tab with hydrogen on the Elements tab and sees two different relative line strengths for the same element, both credited to NIST. A student asked to rank Balmer line strengths reads 0.50/0.33/0.25/0.20 — a 1/(Delta n + 1) artefact with no physical content — and concludes H-delta is a fifth as strong as H-alpha rather than a tenth.
findings.fix: Pick one source of truth: put Case-B relative intensities (or real NIST transition probabilities) in `ELEMENT_CATALOG.H` / the generated hydrogen catalogue in `spectralLineModel.ts`, have `drawSpectrum` read them from the model instead of computing `1/(Delta n + 1)`, and state the source in the model note. If no sourced intensities are used, remove the NIST attribution from index.html:497 and the export notes and label line widths as indicative only. Anna owns the choice of intensity set.

findings.title: The Balmer limit is 364.6 nm in the teaching copy and 364.7 nm on the canvas beside it
findings.evidence: index.html:351 states 'The Balmer series limit (364.6 nm) is where Balmer lines pile up and merge into the continuum.' The Series Limit Microscope computes the same quantity from the model and prints it: `microscopeCtx.fillText(\`${SpectralLineModel.seriesName({nLower})} limit ${limitNm.toFixed(1)} nm\`, ...)` (main.ts:712). I recomputed `seriesLimitNm({nLower: 2}) = HC_EV_NM / (R_H/4) = 1239.842 / 3.39960865 = 364.7014 nm`, so the canvas prints 'Balmer limit 364.7 nm'. 364.6 nm is the laboratory AIR value, inconsistent with the demo's own stated convention three bullets away ('Hydrogen wavelengths are vacuum values', index.html:498) and with the model test that pins 364.7014 (spectralLineModel.test.ts:54). Prior review finding SL-4 recorded this and is still open.
findings.scenario: Student reads 364.6 nm on the Understand tab, opens Advanced Hydrogen Tools, and the microscope labels the same limit 364.7 nm. Asked on an exam for the Balmer limit, the student has two numbers from one instrument and no stated reason for the difference.
findings.fix: Change index.html:351 to 364.7 nm (vacuum) and add the half-sentence that the familiar 364.6 nm is the air value, which is the one teaching point the discrepancy is good for. Better still, render the number from `SpectralLineModel.seriesLimitNm({nLower: 2})` rather than typing it, and add a design-contract test that no hard-coded wavelength literal in index.html disagrees with the model by more than 0.05 nm.

findings.title: readiness: candidate and content_verified: true outrun the evidence
findings.evidence: Frontmatter: `status: beta`, `content_verified: true`, `readiness: candidate`, `lastVerifiedAt: "2026-09-03"`, with `readinessReason: "Close to ready. Still to come: one wavelength value, the data attribution, and a remaining review item."` Per apps/site/src/lib/readiness.ts:52, `candidate` renders the public badge 'near-ready' with the accessible name 'ready to assign, pending final review'. The readinessReason honestly names the three open prior-review items (SL-4, SL-5, SL-6) but describes them as cosmetic leftovers, and `content_verified: true` asserts the content was checked. Against that: the absorption arrow is drawn backwards (main.ts:949), the Elements tab and the Mystery challenge are visually unresolvable (main.ts:1174), 'Neutral-H proxy' is inverted at the cool end (spectralLineModel.ts:420), and the Understand tab teaches R_infinity in SI (index.html:346). `play_steps` also instructs 'enable H Balmer comparison to contrast fingerprints against sodium or iron' and 'Use Mystery Spectrum ... then check your answer' — two steps that cannot be completed as written.
findings.scenario: Instructor filters Explore by readiness, sees the 'near-ready' badge and content_verified, and assigns the demo. Students follow play_steps 8 and 9 into the Elements tab, cannot distinguish any fingerprint, and the ones who switch to Absorption get a Bohr picture that contradicts the energy ladder next to it.
findings.fix: Drop to `readiness: experimental` and `content_verified: false` until the three P0s are fixed, and rewrite `readinessReason` to name the real blockers (absorption arrow direction, elements-tab wavelength axis, neutral-H proxy labelling) instead of 'one wavelength value'. Re-promote to candidate only once the arrow has a direction test, the elements axis has a resolution test, and SL-4/SL-5/SL-6 are closed in docs/reviews/spectral-lines.md.

findings.title: No test in the demo or the e2e spec asserts a single wavelength value, and the contract suite is sixty presence checks
findings.evidence: `design-contracts.test.ts` is essentially `expect(html).toContain('id="bohrAtom"')` sixty times over (lines 122-308); not one assertion reads a number, a geometry or a behaviour, so every finding above leaves it green. The e2e spec is no better on physics: `apps/site/tests/spectral-lines.spec.ts` never touches `#readoutWavelength`, and its single inverse test asserts only `toContainText("n = 3")` / `toContainText("n = 2")` plus `#readoutSeries` text — it would pass with R_infinity, with hc wrong by a percent, or with the whole wavelength readout blank. In logic.test.ts the formatter cases feed literals (`formatWavelengthReadout(656.3)` at line 86, 'returns 656.3 nm' in the announcement test at line 310) so they assert nothing about the physics; `logic.test.ts:201-203` ('mode behavior is independent of tab') actively pins the dead `viewTab` parameter that `shouldRenderEmission` discards with `void args.viewTab` (logic.ts:366). Uncovered entirely: the Bohr arrow direction and the marker mapping, the spectrum-strip wavelength-to-x mapping, line resolvability on the elements domain, the mystery wavelength leak, and the orbit pointer hit area (tested only via `.focus()`).
findings.scenario: Any of the P0s above is introduced or reintroduced, `pnpm -C apps/demos test` and the Playwright suite both pass, and the demo ships. The repo already has this scar: SL-1 shipped green because the tolerance was 3x the error.
findings.fix: Add three behavioural tests. (1) A DOM test (jsdom or Playwright) asserting that `#bohrAtom line` has y1 > y2 in absorption and y1 < y2 in emission. (2) An e2e assertion that `#readoutWavelength` reads 656.5 for n=3->2 and 121.6 for n=2->1 — the two numbers a wrong constant would move. (3) A logic test asserting that on the elements domain two lines 0.6 nm apart differ in fraction by more than one line width. Then delete the `shouldRenderEmission` viewTab parameter and its test.

findings.title: Element-tab photon energy and frequency are re-derived inline in main.ts, twice, bypassing PhotonModel
findings.evidence: `activeElementLineContext` computes `energyEv = SpectralLineModel.BOHR.HC_EV_NM / wavelengthNm` (main.ts:275) and `frequencyHz = SpectralLineModel.BOHR.C_CM_PER_S / (wavelengthNm * 1e-7)` (main.ts:278); the Station Mode element rowset repeats the first at main.ts:2174. Both equations already have an owner in the physics package: `PhotonModel.photonEnergyEvFromWavelengthNm` (packages/physics/src/photonModel.ts:75) and `PhotonModel.frequencyHzFromWavelengthNm` (line 58), the latter going through `AstroUnits.nmToCm` rather than a bare `1e-7` literal. CLAUDE.md is explicit: 'All physics models MUST come from @cosmic/physics — no inline equations in demo code.' The inline form also applies the vacuum relation hc/lambda to the catalogue's laboratory AIR wavelengths, which the model header at spectralLineModel.ts:14-17 warns against: for Na D2 it yields 1239.842/589.0 = 2.1050 eV where the vacuum wavelength 589.158 nm gives 2.1044 eV, so the fourth decimal of a four-decimal readout (main.ts:1416, `formatNumber(context.energyEv, 4)`) is wrong.
findings.scenario: A future change to hc or to the nm-to-cm conversion in the physics package leaves the Elements tab reading the old value, because the Elements tab does not use the package. Today a student reading 'Energy E_gamma 2.1050 eV' for Na D2 and checking it against a vacuum line list gets 2.1044.
findings.fix: Replace both inline expressions with `PhotonModel.photonEnergyEvFromWavelengthNm` and `PhotonModel.frequencyHzFromWavelengthNm` (import PhotonModel from @cosmic/physics). Separately decide with Anna whether to convert the catalogue's air wavelengths to vacuum before the photon-energy conversion or to drop the readout to 3 decimals and label it 'from air wavelength'.

findings.title: No reader-visible math is KaTeX: ASCII M_sun and a full Stefan-Boltzmann equation in HTML, plus Unicode arrows
findings.evidence:
index.html contains zero `$` characters (grep -c '$' returns 0) yet main.ts:1465 calls `initMath(document)`, so the KaTeX pass has nothing to render. Reader-visible math is ASCII throughout: index.html:48-49 `0.1 M_sun` / `50 M_sun`, :227 `Mass (M_sun)`, :319 and :323 `L/L_sun` and `R/R_sun`, and :369 the whole relation as plain text, `
  • Radius guides follow L/L_sun = (R/R_sun)^2 (T/T_sun)^4.
    • `. index.html:33-36 use the Unicode glyphs in "Brighter ↑", "Fainter ↓", "Hotter ←", "Cooler →". The golden reference does it correctly: moon-phases/index.html:555 and :562 use `$\alpha$` and `$f = \frac{1 + \cos\alpha}{2}$`. scripts/validate-math-formatting.mjs:33 only tests FORBIDDEN_UNICODE_MATH, which contains Greek letters, degree, times and sub/superscripts but no arrows, so none of this fails the build.
findings.scenario: The exhibit page renders its Stefan-Boltzmann note as typeset KaTeX (stars-zams-hr.md model_notes uses \frac and \odot) while the demo the student opens from it shows the same relation as "L/L_sun = (R/R_sun)^2 (T/T_sun)^4" in body text. Per CLAUDE.md the hazard is concrete: a bare ASCII or Unicode glyph inherits surrounding CSS, which is how 94 KaTeX nodes were silently uppercased on 2026-09-05 and turned nu into N.
findings.fix: In apps/demos/src/demos/stars-zams-hr/index.html, author every reader-visible symbol as LaTeX so the existing initMath(document) pass renders it: `$M_\odot$`, `$L/L_\odot$`, `$R/R_\odot$`, and `$$\frac{L}{L_\odot} = \left(\frac{R}{R_\odot}\right)^2\left(\frac{T_{\rm eff}}{T_\odot}\right)^4$$` at line 369; replace the four arrow badges at :33-36 with `$\uparrow$`, `$\downarrow$`, `$\leftarrow$`, `$\rightarrow$`. Then add the arrow glyphs to FORBIDDEN_UNICODE_MATH in scripts/validate-math-formatting.mjs so the gate catches the next one.

findings.title: buildEvolutionTrack is a second, divergent physics model inlined in the demo (review finding HR-4, still open)
findings.evidence: main.ts:311-422 computes an evolutionary track from hardcoded coefficients -- `luminosityLsun = msL * (0.72 + 0.85 * fraction)`, `teffK = msT * (0.98 - 0.06 * fraction)`, `radiusRsun = msR * (4 + 95 * fraction ** 1.15)` -- while the population plotted in the same axes goes through HrInferencePopulationModel -> postMainSequenceTrack (stellarLifetimeModel.ts:348). I evaluated both: at t = 0 the inline track gives 0.72 x L_ZAMS at every mass, i.e. 0.143 dex (28%) below the ZAMS the population sits on. At the end of the inline main sequence a 1 M_sun star is at L = 1.095 L_sun, and the very next sample is L = 12.28 L_sun -- a 1.05 dex jump in one segment, drawn as a single straight chord, so there is no Hertzsprung gap. The inline RGB tip for 1 M_sun is 730 L_sun at 3200 K against the shared model's 2500 L_sun (stellarLifetimeModel.ts:213 RGB_TIP_LSUN, documented as the degenerate-core tip that makes the RGB a standard candle) -- a factor of 3.4. CLAUDE.md: "All physics models MUST come from @cosmic/physics -- no inline equations in demo code." The 2026-09-03 review logged this as HR-4/open and recommended fixing it before promotion.
findings.scenario: exhibit play_steps[2] asks the student to "compare track shape and timescale for 0.8 and 20 M_sun stars". In an old-cluster population the model's own giants climb to 2500 L_sun while the evolve track for the same mass tops out at 730 L_sun, 0.53 dex lower, in the same frame -- so the track visibly misses the branch it is supposed to explain, and its subgiant phase is a straight diagonal where the population shows the horizontal-then-vertical shape.
findings.fix: Delete buildEvolutionTrack from apps/demos/src/demos/stars-zams-hr/main.ts:311-422 and build the track by sampling the shared model: for each time step call ZamsTout1996Model for the ZAMS values and StellarLifetimeModel.postMainSequenceTrack({massMsun, ageMyr, zamsLuminosityLsun, zamsTemperatureK}), treating a null return before t_MS as the ZAMS point and a null return after totalLifetimeMyr as the compact remnant. That makes the track exactly the locus the population is drawn from, removes the t = 0 offset and the 1.05 dex jump, and satisfies the no-inline-physics rule.

findings.title: evolveTime slider step is fixed at 0.001 Gyr, giving 10 positions at 20 M_sun and 31,821 at 0.8 M_sun (HR-5, still open)
findings.evidence: index.html:235-243 fixes `step="0.001"` (Gyr) on #evolveTime, while main.ts:927 updates only the max: `evolveTime.max = String(maxTime)` with `maxTime = 1.2 * tMs`. I computed the Hurley t_MS for each option in the EVOLVE_MASSES_MSUN select: 0.8 -> 26.518 Gyr, 1 -> 11.003, 2 -> 1.164, 5 -> 0.104, 10 -> 0.0243, 20 -> 0.008675 Gyr. The resulting reachable positions at a 0.001 Gyr step are 31,821 / 13,203 / 1,396 / 124 / 29 / 10. For 20 M_sun the whole track is 11 slider stops, of which only the last two are post-main-sequence; for 0.8 M_sun one arrow-key press advances 1 Myr, so traversing the track takes 31,821 presses.
findings.scenario: A keyboard-only student follows the README's own manual-verification step 10 ("Run the evolve tool for 0.8 and 20 M_sun"). At 0.8 M_sun each arrow press moves the marker 1/31,821 of the track -- no perceptible change, and reaching the giant branch is impossible. At 20 M_sun the slider has 11 stops total, so the supergiant and remnant phases are a single pixel-wide jump with nothing in between to read.
findings.fix: Make the slider dimensionless and map it to time. In apps/demos/src/demos/stars-zams-hr/index.html:235-243 set `min="0" max="1000" step="1"`, and in main.ts:924-929 convert: `state.evolveTimeGyr = (Number(evolveTime.value) / 1000) * 1.2 * tMs`, with evolveTime.value = Math.round(1000 * state.evolveTimeGyr / maxTime). Every mass then gets 1001 uniform stops regardless of lifetime, and add aria-valuetext so the announced value carries Gyr and the stage.

findings.title: Main-sequence lifetime is solar-metallicity only, so changing Z moves the ZAMS but never the turnoff
findings.evidence: stellarLifetimeModel.ts:23-33 sets `SOLAR_METALLICITY_ONLY = 0.02` and `HURLEY_ZETA = 0`, and mainSequenceLifetimeMyr (line 58) takes only massMsun -- there is no Z argument anywhere in the chain. Meanwhile the demo exposes Metallicity Z over 1e-4 to 0.03 (index.html:152-156) and ships a "Low metallicity" preset at Z = 0.004 (logic.ts HR_LAB_PRESETS). I evaluated both halves: Tout gives L(1 M_sun) = 0.6977 L_sun at Z = 0.02, 1.165 at Z = 0.004 and 1.586 at Z = 0.0001 (Teff 5597 / 6245 / 7068 K), while t_MS(1 M_sun) = 11.003 Gyr is bit-identical at all three and the turnoff mass at 10 Gyr is 1.0253 M_sun at both Z = 0.02 and Z = 0.0001. Since t_MS ~ M/L, a Z = 0.0001 star 2.27x brighter should live ~2.3x less long: about 4.8 Gyr, not 11.0. Nothing in index.html's Model Notes or stars-zams-hr.md discloses the limitation.
findings.scenario: A student presses "Low metallicity" (Z = 0.004) to test the exhibit's own listed misconception "Metallicity only changes spectral lines and not bulk stellar structure". The main sequence shifts blue and up, correctly -- but the turnoff stays at exactly the same mass and the same number of evolved stars appear, so the student concludes metallicity changes a star's appearance but not its lifetime. At Z = 0.0001 and a 5 Gyr cluster age the demo still shows a 1 M_sun star on the main sequence when a real metal-poor star of that mass would already have left it.
findings.fix: Either make the clock Z-dependent or state the limit where the reader sees it. The cheap, honest fix: add a line to the Model Notes list in apps/demos/src/demos/stars-zams-hr/index.html (near :366-370) and to model_notes in apps/site/src/content/demos/stars-zams-hr.md saying the lifetime and turnoff use the Hurley relation evaluated at Z = 0.02, so changing Z moves the zero-age sequence but not the turnoff age. The full fix is to evaluate Hurley's zeta polynomials for the selected Z in packages/physics/src/stellarLifetimeModel.ts -- a scientific scope decision that needs Anna's approval, since it changes every demo that consumes mainSequenceLifetimeMyr.

findings.title: Theorist mode has no out-of-frame reporting, so 220,000 K compact remnants are drawn clamped at an apparent 50,000 K
findings.evidence: main.ts:630 guards the cull with `if ("inFrame" in norm && !norm.inFrame)`. cmdCoordinates returns inFrame (logic.ts:141) but hrCoordinates returns only {xNorm, yNorm} (logic.ts:109-112), so in Theorist HR mode the key is absent, the branch never fires, and starsOutsideFrame stays structurally 0 -- which makes the caption at main.ts:843 ("N of M stars fall outside these axis limits and are not drawn") dead code in half the demo. hrCoordinates clamps instead: COMPACT_REMNANT (hrInferencePopulationModel.ts:292) is Teff = 2.2e5 K, R = 2.0e-5 R_sun, L = 8.44e-4 L_sun; log10(2.2e5) = 5.342 exceeds xLogMax = log10(50000) = 4.699, so xNorm clamps to 0 and the remnant is painted on the left frame edge at log L = -3.07. Running the generator over 5 seeds, compact remnants appear in 0.4 of every 320-star population and 2.4 of every 1200-star population -- reachable, not theoretical. The same clamp applies to whiteDwarfPoint at its 0.1 Myr cooling-age floor (stellarLifetimeModel.ts:424), which I evaluated at 181,565-208,804 K and 158.5 L_sun.
findings.scenario: A student in Theorist HR mode at N = 1200 clicks a point sitting exactly on the left edge of the frame, under the 40,000 K tick, and the readout says Stage: Compact remnant, Effective temperature: 220000 K. The plotted position says 50,000 K; the readout says 220,000 K; the caption says nothing was dropped. The physics model's own comment calls the remnant "parked off the visible diagram", but the clamp puts it on the diagram.
findings.fix: Give hrCoordinates the same contract cmdCoordinates already has: in apps/demos/src/demos/stars-zams-hr/logic.ts:85-112 compute the raw normalized values, return `inFrame: xRaw >= 0 && xRaw <= 1 && yRaw >= 0 && yRaw <= 1` alongside the clamped pair, and add the mirror of the existing logic.test.ts out-of-frame test. The guard at main.ts:630 then fires in both modes and the caption reports the count. Separately, consider excluding neutron stars and black holes from a diagram of photospheres rather than parking them at a placeholder temperature.

findings.title: massColorHex inverts the astronomical colour convention: low-mass stars blue, high-mass stars orange-red
findings.evidence: logic.ts:190-197: `const t = clamp((log10(max(massMsun, 0.1)) - log10(0.1)) / (log10(50) - log10(0.1)), 0, 1); const hue = 220 - 200 * t;` so 0.1 M_sun -> hue 220 (blue) and 50 M_sun -> hue 20 (orange-red), with the ramp passing through cyan, green and yellow. main.ts:92-94 builds the legend from the same function and index.html:48-49 labels its ends "0.1 M_sun" (blue) and "50 M_sun" (red). In the default Observer CMD mode the x axis IS colour: B-V runs from -0.4 (blue, hot, massive) on the left to 2.5 (red, cool, low-mass) on the right, so the mass overlay paints the left-hand massive end red and the right-hand low-mass end blue. No comment in logic.ts justifies the direction, and the ramp is also a raw hsl() literal emitted from demo TypeScript rather than a --cp-* token.
findings.scenario: The staged reveal is the demo's headline inference step (learning_goal 3: "Infer hidden mass ordering along the main sequence"; predict_prompt: "predict where high-mass and low-mass stars should lie"). A student predicts correctly that the hot blue upper-left end is the massive end, ticks "Reveal mass colors", and sees that end painted orange-red with the legend confirming red = 50 M_sun -- so the reveal appears to refute the correct prediction and reinforces the colour confusion the CMD axis is teaching against.
findings.fix: Reverse the ramp in apps/demos/src/demos/stars-zams-hr/logic.ts:194 to `const hue = 20 + 200 * t;` so mass increases toward blue, matching the B-V axis and the O-through-M sequence, and update the legend end labels in index.html:48-49 accordingly. Better: build the ramp from the design system's own stellar tokens (--cp-celestial-star, --cp-accent-ice, --cp-accent-rose) read via cssVar() instead of emitting a literal hsl() string, which also closes the Token Purity invariant. Strengthen the test (see the test-integrity finding) to assert the hue direction, not just the "hsl(" prefix.

findings.title: Four tests would still pass with the physics or the contract wrong, including one that pins the Unicode arrows
findings.evidence: (1) logic.test.ts:43-58 "supports SB forward/inverse consistency" calls luminosityLsunFromRadiusTemperature({radiusRsun: 2, teffK: 5772, tSunK: 5772}) and asserts 4. Since teffK === tSunK the temperature ratio is exactly 1, so `tempRatio ** 4` contributes 1 whatever the exponent is: replacing ** 4 with ** 2, ** 5 or ** 1 in logic.ts:158 still returns 4 and the test still passes. The T^4 law -- the one relation the entire demo teaches -- has no test, at exactly the symmetric point CLAUDE.md's verification gotchas warn about. (2) logic.test.ts:95-98 "maps mass to an hsl color" asserts only `c.startsWith("hsl(")`, so the inverted hue direction above is unconstrained. (3) design-contracts.test.ts:46-47 asserts `expect(html).toContain("Brighter ↑")` and `toContain("Hotter ←")`, so the KaTeX contract cannot be satisfied without breaking the design-contract test. (4) hrInferencePopulationModel.test.ts:202-210 "high-mass old-cluster populations include finite compact-remnant endpoints" asserts only that Teff is finite and > 0 for a value of 2.2e5 K, which is 4.4x the plotted axis maximum. Nothing anywhere tests that the evolve track starts on the ZAMS, that the radius guides stay in frame, or that the guide-region positions match the model.
findings.scenario: A future edit swaps the Stefan-Boltzmann exponent or reverses the mass colour ramp, the suite stays green, and the defect ships. Conversely, the correct fix -- replacing the Unicode arrows with KaTeX -- turns design-contracts.test.ts red, so the contract test actively blocks compliance with the contract it exists to defend.
findings.fix: In apps/demos/src/demos/stars-zams-hr/logic.test.ts, re-point the SB test at an asymmetric case: luminosityLsunFromRadiusTemperature({radiusRsun: 3, teffK: 8000, tSunK: 5772}) must be 9 * (8000/5772)^4 = 34.50, and the inverse must return 3. Assert the mass-colour hue direction by parsing the hue out of massColorHex(0.1) and massColorHex(50). In design-contracts.test.ts:46-47 assert the rendered KaTeX arrow nodes (or the LaTeX source) instead of the glyphs. In packages/physics/src/hrInferencePopulationModel.test.ts, bound the remnant temperature rather than only its sign. Add a test asserting buildEvolutionTrack(or its replacement) at t = 0 equals the Tout ZAMS values for that mass and metallicity.

findings.title: The plot is role="img" with keyboard selection, and the only announcement is an opaque star id
findings.evidence: index.html:24-30 gives #hrCanvas `role="img"` together with `tabindex="0"` and an arrow-key/Home/End handler (main.ts:1315-1352). role="img" declares a static image, so assistive technology does not expose it as operable and does not surface the selection model. The live announcement carries no physics: main.ts:969 `setLiveRegionText(status, \`Selected ${star.id}: ${stageLabels[star.stage]}.\`)` emits "Selected star-57: Main sequence." -- the id is an array index with no meaning, and the temperature, luminosity, radius and mass the demo exists to compare are not announced. Separately, main.ts:1350 calls `event.preventDefault()` only after the early return at :1349 (`if (!nextId || nextId === state.selectedStarId) return;`), so pressing ArrowDown on the lowest star, or End when already at the boundary, scrolls the page instead.
findings.scenario: A screen-reader student tabs to the plot, hears it announced as an image named "Stellar population plot", and gets no indication the arrow keys do anything. If they try anyway, each press announces "Selected star-212: Main sequence" with no values, and at the edge of the population the key scrolls the page away from the plot instead. Every learning goal in stars-zams-hr.md requires comparing L, Teff and inferred R between stars, so the demo is not completable without sight.
findings.fix: In apps/demos/src/demos/stars-zams-hr/index.html:24-30, drop role="img" in favour of a focusable group whose operability is exposed (role="application" with the existing aria-describedby, or an off-screen listbox of stars mirroring plottedPoints). In main.ts:969 announce the physics, not the id: temperature in K, L/L_sun, inferred R/R_sun, stage, and mass when revealed. Move `event.preventDefault()` in main.ts:1315-1352 above the no-move early return so arrow and Home/End keys never scroll the page while the plot has focus.
