findings.title: content_verified: true and parityAuditPath both outrun the evidence; the README documents a superseded lifetime law
findings.evidence: The frontmatter sets `content_verified: true` and `lastVerifiedAt: "2026-09-03"` -- the same date as docs/reviews/stars-zams-hr.md, which closed HR-1/2/3 but left HR-4, HR-5, HR-6 and HR-7 open and ends "HR-4 and HR-5 should be fixed before this demo is promoted past experimental". I confirmed all four are still open in the current tree (main.ts:311 inline track; index.html:239 step="0.001"; stellarLifetimeModel.ts:58 lifetime unchanged by Z; logic.ts sampleMassMsun floor). `parityAuditPath: "docs/audits/migrations/stars-zams-hr-parity.md"` points at a document describing a different instrument: it claims "explicit override presets for non-ZAMS objects", "Disables metallicity control in override mode", a "(`M`, `Z` -> `L`, `R`, `Teff`)" single-star control, and an export annotating "`ZAMS inferred` vs `Override`" -- grepping the demo folder for "Override" and "ZAMS inferred" returns nothing, there is no mass control, and exportResultsPayload (main.ts:1010-1056) has no such field. The demo README's "Physical assumptions (explicit)" still states `t_MS ~ 10 Gyr * (M/M_sun)^(-2.5)`, which the code replaced with Hurley: at 0.8 M_sun the README gives 17.47 Gyr against the code's 26.52, at 20 M_sun 0.00559 against 0.008675. Also: model_notes claims the fits are used "over 0.1 <= M/Msun <= 100" while MASS_MAX_MSUN = 50, and station_params lists a "Mass M" parameter at "1 Msun" that no control in the demo sets.
findings.scenario: An instructor reads content_verified: true with a September verification date, follows parityAuditPath to confirm scope, and is told the demo has an override mode and a mass/metallicity single-star control. They build a lab around controls that do not exist, and around a main-sequence lifetime law the demo stopped using (so a student's hand-calculated 20 M_sun lifetime disagrees with the readout by 55%).
findings.fix: Set `content_verified: false` in apps/site/src/content/demos/stars-zams-hr.md and bump lastVerifiedAt only when the P0s above are closed; keep readiness: experimental and status: draft, which are the defensible values today. Rewrite docs/audits/migrations/stars-zams-hr-parity.md to describe the instrument that exists, or remove the parityAuditPath pointer until it does. Update the "Physical assumptions" block in apps/demos/src/demos/stars-zams-hr/README.md to the Hurley relation and the Pecaut & Mamajek colour sequence, correct the mass range in model_notes to 0.1-50, and delete or re-point the "Mass M" station_param.

findings.title: The 0.4 arcsec field-of-view floor makes the Airy pattern unframeable at its own scale for every aperture above ~2 m — the exact instruments the demo exists to teach
findings.evidence: logic.ts:96-98 `return Math.max(0.4, Math.min(500, Math.max(6 * thetaEffArcsec, 3 * separationArcsec)));`. The `6 * thetaEff` term — the one that frames the diffraction pattern — is overridden by the hard 0.4 arcsec floor whenever theta_eff < 0.0667 arcsec. Solving 1.22*5.5e-5/D * 206265 = 0.0667 gives D = 207 cm = 2.07 m. Recomputed consequences: Hubble theta_eff = 0.0577 arcsec -> 6*theta = 0.346 < 0.4, floor wins; Keck at visible theta_eff = 0.0138 -> 0.083 < 0.4, floor wins; EHT at its correct 1.3 mm theta_eff = 3.271e-5 -> field is 12,200x the first-null radius, and the brightest pixel at the minimum selectable separation (1e-3 arcsec) is 2/255. The floor and the zoom divide then fight each other: zoom is the only way to reach the diffraction scale, and zoom is what ejects the pair (finding 1).
findings.scenario: A student picks any modern telescope and tries to see the Airy rings the Model notes promise ($I(x)=[2J_1(x)/x]^2$). At zoom 1 the pattern is a sub-pixel point inside a 0.4 arcsec field; at zoom 20 the rings would be resolvable but the pair is gone. There is no zoom setting at which an 8 m telescope's diffraction pattern and its binary pair are both on screen, so the demo's central visual claim is unreachable for its central use case.
findings.fix: Derive the floor from the physics instead of hardcoding it: in logic.ts:96-98 drop the 0.4 constant and let the lower bound be set by the rendering resolution (e.g. `max(6*thetaEff, 1.5*separation, 3*W_px^-1-equivalent)`), and fold this into the single computeFovArcsec rewrite from finding 1 so the field is always min(what frames the PSF, what frames the pair) rather than a magic number. Replace the logic.test.ts 'clamps to minimum 0.4 arcsec' test, which currently pins the floor as a contract.

findings.title: Interferometer baselines are labeled as the diameter $D$ and fed the filled-aperture 1.22 coefficient, violating the project's D/d symbol rule and overstating VLBI resolution by 22%
findings.evidence: index.html:24 labels the control `Effective aperture $D$ (m)` unconditionally, and telescopePresets.ts:61-62 supply `vla` (36,000 m) and `eht` (1e7 m) with `apertureKind: "baseline"`. CLAUDE.md and .agents/references/invariants.md both state: "`D` = physical diameter, `d` = distance. Never reuse either for anything else." A 36 km VLA baseline is $B$, not a diameter. The physics compounds it: telescopeResolutionModel.ts:5 `RAYLEIGH_COEFFICIENT = 1.22` is the first zero of $J_1$ for a *filled circular aperture*; a two-element interferometer has fringe resolution ~$\lambda/B$ with no 1.22. Recomputed for the EHT at 1.3 mm: 1.22*0.13/1e9 rad = 1.586e-10 rad = 3.271e-5 arcsec = 32.7 microarcsec, versus lambda/B = 26.8 microarcsec — a 22% overestimate, against a published EHT resolution of ~20-25 microarcsec. `apertureKind` exists to make exactly this distinction and is read nowhere.
findings.scenario: A student selects "VLA (36 km baseline)", sees the control labeled "Effective aperture D", and learns that an interferometer is equivalent to a 36 km mirror obeying the same 1.22 law. They then write 1.22*lambda/B on an exam for an interferometer and get the wrong coefficient, and they carry away that $D$ can mean a baseline.
findings.fix: Read `apertureKind` in main.ts: when it is "baseline", relabel the control as `Baseline $B$ (m)` and the readout label accordingly, and call a new `TelescopeResolutionModel.fringeResolutionArcsecFromBaseline()` that uses coefficient 1.0 with its own named constant. Add one sentence to the Model notes in index.html explaining why the 1.22 belongs to a filled aperture. The coefficient choice for baselines is a scientific assumption — propose 1.0 vs keeping 1.22 for pedagogical uniformity and get it approved before coding.

findings.title: Aperture and separation sliders have no aria-valuetext, so a screen reader announces the raw 0-1000 log position instead of metres and arcsec
findings.evidence: index.html:25-33 (`#aperture`, min=0 max=1000) and index.html:44-55 (`#separation`, min=0 max=1000) are log-mapped sliders whose raw value carries no physical meaning: logic.ts:17-23 maps 0-1000 onto 0.007 m to 1e7 m and 1e-3 to 1e3 arcsec. Neither main.ts nor index.html ever sets `aria-valuetext` — `grep -rn aria-valuetext apps/demos/src/demos/telescope-resolution` returns nothing. The project already treats this as a contract elsewhere: cluster-census/design-contracts.test.ts:255 'sets aria-valuetext on every slider whose raw value is not its meaning', conservation-laws/design-contracts.test.ts:245 'every slider carries aria-valuetext with its physical value', with eight demos implementing it.
findings.scenario: A screen-reader user tabs to the aperture slider with Hubble selected and hears "Effective aperture D m, slider, 400". Pressing Right announces "401". The actual aperture (2.4 m) and the step size (a 2.1% multiplicative change per press) are never spoken, so the control is unusable: the student cannot set a 10 m aperture, and cannot tell the separation slider reads 1 arcsec rather than 500 of something.
findings.fix: In main.ts's render(), add `apertureEl.setAttribute("aria-valuetext", `${apertureFmt.text} ${apertureFmt.unit}`)` and `separationEl.setAttribute("aria-valuetext", `${formatNumber(sep, 3)} arcsec`)` next to the existing textContent writes at lines 346-351, and copy the cluster-census design-contract assertion into this demo's design-contracts.test.ts so it cannot regress.

findings.title: The resolved/marginal/unresolved verdict is never announced, and the PSF canvas has no state-describing alternative, so the demo's only output is invisible to assistive tech
findings.evidence: main.ts:363-372 writes the verdict into `statusReadoutEl` and `statusBadgeEl` with plain `textContent`; index.html:151 `<span class="cp-badge" id="statusBadge">` and index.html:175 `<span id="statusReadout">` carry no aria-live, and neither sits inside the `#status` region (index.html:143) that does. The only `setLiveRegionText` calls in the file are main.ts:399 (the space-telescope note) and main.ts:540/544/546 (copy feedback) — none on a physics change. index.html:155 gives the canvas a static `aria-label="Point-spread function view"` and no `role="img"`; nothing ever updates it with the current state.
findings.scenario: A screen-reader user drags the separation slider across the Rayleigh threshold — the single interaction the demo is built around — and hears nothing change. The badge flips Unresolved -> Marginal -> Resolved silently and the canvas keeps saying "Point-spread function view". The demo's entire output is unreachable, so the exhibit's learning goals cannot be met without sighted assistance.
findings.fix: In main.ts render(), after computing `model.status`, call `setLiveRegionText(statusEl, ...)` with a composed sentence ("Resolved: separation 1.00 arcsec is 17 times the 0.058 arcsec limit") guarded by a module-scope `lastAnnouncedStatus` so it fires only on an actual status change, never on every input event. Separately set `canvasEl.setAttribute("role", "img")` and update its aria-label each render with the same sentence.

findings.title: The space-telescope seeing warning is written from inside render(), re-announced on every slider tick, and never cleared when the condition stops holding
findings.evidence: main.ts:397-400: `if (preset && preset.platform === "space" && state.includeAtmosphere) { setLiveRegionText(statusEl, "Note: space telescopes have no atmospheric seeing."); }` — inside render(), which main.ts:492-537 calls from every `input` and `change` handler. There is no `else` branch, so nothing ever resets `#status`. packages/runtime/src/liveRegion.ts:1-18 shows setLiveRegionText deliberately clears and re-sets on a rAF when the text repeats, specifically to force re-announcement — so a repeated call is not a no-op, it is a fresh announcement. CLAUDE.md's own a11y guidance names this: "live-region announcements on change (never inside a render loop)".
findings.scenario: Select Hubble, tick "Include atmosphere", then drag the seeing slider: `input` fires at ~60 Hz, render() runs each time, and the screen reader is handed the same note over and over. Then untick atmosphere, or switch the preset to Keck: the paragraph still reads "Note: space telescopes have no atmospheric seeing" for the rest of the session, contradicting the now-ground-based configuration, and it is the only text in the region so a later "Copied results" is the only thing that can displace it.
findings.fix: Move the note out of render() into the `presetEl` and `includeAtmosphereEl` change handlers (main.ts:482-490 and 514-518), compute the message once, and give it an explicit empty-string else branch so the region clears when the condition lapses. If the status announcement from the previous finding is added, give the note its own non-live element instead so the two do not overwrite each other.

findings.title: Reader-visible readouts print e-notation ("1.384e-8"), which the project's math convention forbids — and a unit test pins the behavior
findings.evidence: logic.ts:46 `if (abs >= 1e6 || abs < 1e-3) return value.toExponential(Math.max(0, digits - 1));` feeds main.ts:359-360, which write straight into the `#thetaDiff` and `#thetaEff` readouts. CLAUDE.md and invariants.md both state: "Powers of ten as `$10^n$`; no `e` notation in teaching-facing copy." Reachable with the shipped presets: I recomputed theta_diff for EHT at 1.3 mm = 3.271e-5 arcsec -> readout "3.271e-5"; EHT at the band it actually gets (visible) = 1.384e-8 -> "1.384e-8"; and GBT at 21 cm = 528.45 arcsec, so the other end is reachable too (any value >= 1e6 prints "2.50e+8", with a literal plus sign). logic.test.ts:148-150 asserts `expect(formatNumber(0.00007, 3)).toBe("7.00e-5")`, so the invariant violation is locked in by a green test.
findings.scenario: A student on the EHT preset sees the diffraction limit as "1.384e-8 arcsec" in a demo whose own documentation bans e-notation, pastes it into a lab writeup, and has no cue that the site's convention is $1.384\times10^{-8}$. Any later attempt to fix formatNumber breaks logic.test.ts, so the defect is self-defending.
findings.fix: Have formatNumber return a structured `{mantissa, exponent}` (or a LaTeX string) for out-of-range magnitudes and render it through `renderMath()` from @cosmic/runtime into the readout spans, as the project requires for TS-emitted math; or switch the readouts to milliarcsec/arcmin so values stay in fixed-point range. Then rewrite logic.test.ts:144-158 to assert the LaTeX form instead of the e-notation form.

findings.title: No test anywhere constrains a computed number: the only numeric physics test accepts a 2x-wide window, and all 25 e2e assertions are "something changed"
findings.evidence: telescopeResolutionModel.test.ts:7-16 is the sole numeric check on the headline formula: `expect(thetaArcsec).toBeGreaterThan(0.04); expect(thetaArcsec).toBeLessThan(0.08);` for Hubble at 550 nm. The true value is 0.057668 arcsec. I recomputed the window: coefficient 1.0 gives 0.047269 (passes), 1.5 gives 0.070903 (passes) — so replacing RAYLEIGH_COEFFICIENT 1.22 with the slit value 1.0, or with 1.5, leaves the suite green. The remaining physics tests (lines 18-42) assert only monotonicity in D and lambda, which any theta proportional to lambda/D satisfies with any coefficient. Nothing asserts that the Airy PSF's first null coincides with the reported Rayleigh limit (the coupling between the drawing and the readout; I had to compute I(theta_diff) = 4.7e-8 myself). besselJ1Approx has no accuracy test at all. In apps/site/tests/telescope-resolution.spec.ts every behavioral test is of the form `expect(after).not.toBe(before)` (lines 58-74, 101-107) or a presence check — e.g. 'telescope preset selector changes aperture readout' passes if Hubble loads the wrong aperture entirely, which is precisely why finding 2 survived. logic.test.ts's 100+ cases test only clamp and string formatting.
findings.scenario: Any future edit to the coefficient, the preset-to-aperture mapping, the arcsec conversion chain or the band wiring ships green. Concretely: the live preset-wavelength bug (finding 2) and the off-frame rendering bug (finding 1) both pass the full existing suite today, as does a 1.22 -> 1.0 swap that would change every number a student records.
findings.fix: Add to telescopeResolutionModel.test.ts a table test asserting exact values to 4 significant figures for at least three asymmetric cases (Hubble 2.4 m at 550 nm = 0.05767 arcsec; Keck 10 m at 2.2 um = 0.05536 arcsec; GBT 100 m at 21 cm = 528.4 arcsec), plus `expect(airyIntensityNormalizedFromThetaRad({thetaRad: diffractionLimitRad(...)})).toBeLessThan(1e-6)` to pin the PSF-to-Rayleigh coupling, plus a J1 accuracy test against tabulated values at x = 1.8412, 3.8317, 5.3314. In the e2e spec, replace the `not.toBe(before)` assertions with exact expected readout text after selecting a named preset.

findings.title: The AO Strehl ratio of 0.6 is hardcoded, appears in no reader-visible surface, and is omitted from the export — so an exported theta_eff cannot be reproduced from the exported parameters
findings.evidence: telescopeResolutionModel.ts:6 `const AO_STREHL_DEFAULT = 0.6;` is applied at lines 95-100 as `correctedSeeing = seeing*(1-strehl)` then combined in quadrature. main.ts:186-190 never passes `aoStrehl`, so 0.6 always governs. The export at main.ts:318-324 records only `Adaptive optics (AO): On` — no Strehl — while the readouts at main.ts:331-332 export theta_eff. index.html:219 says only "with AO we reduce seeing and combine in quadrature"; telescope-resolution.md:28 says only "AO reduces the seeing contribution in the demo". Recomputed: seeing 1.0 arcsec, theta_diff 0.0577 -> theta_eff = sqrt(0.0577^2 + 0.4^2) = 0.4041 arcsec. From the exported parameters alone (theta_diff, seeing, "AO: On") that 0.4041 is unreproducible; it would be 0.5025 at S = 0.5 and 0.3041 at S = 0.7. The redundant `Math.max(diffractionLimitArcsec, combined)` at line 101 is also dead, since the quadrature sum is always >= theta_diff.
findings.scenario: A student turns on AO, copies results into a lab report, and is asked to show how theta_eff follows from theta_diff and the seeing. The export gives them no path to 0.4041 arcsec. A second student with a different (future) Strehl default produces a different number from an identically-labeled export, and neither report can be checked.
findings.fix: Surface the assumption: add `{ name: "AO Strehl ratio", value: formatNumber(strehl, 2) }` to the export parameters in main.ts:318-324 whenever AO is on, state it in the Model notes in index.html:219 and in model_notes in apps/site/src/content/demos/telescope-resolution.md, and delete the dead Math.max at telescopeResolutionModel.ts:101. Whether 0.6 is the right teaching default (and whether it should become a slider) is a scientific assumption for Anna to approve before it is re-stated publicly.

findings.title: Solar total/annular boundary evaluates the umbra at Earth's centre, misclassifying a 6,371 km window as annular
findings.evidence: `return { type: umbraRadiusKm > 0 ? "total-solar" : "annular-solar" };` where `umbraRadiusKm` comes from `shadowRadiiKmAtDistance({ ..., distanceFromBodyKm: dEarthMoonKm })` (line 213) — the Moon-to-Earth-centre distance. So the type flips on whether the umbra reaches Earth's centre, not its surface. I recomputed the umbra tip length as R_moon * d_sun / (R_sun - R_moon) = 1737.4 x 1.495979e8 / 694262.6 = 374,370 km, so the model's boundary is 374,370 km while the geometric condition for a total eclipse at the sub-lunar point is 374,370 + 6,371 = 380,741 km. For d in (374,370, 380,741) km the model returns annular where a total eclipse is possible: at 378,000 km it gives umbra = -16.8 km and reports "annular-solar". The test at eclipseGeometryModel.test.ts:45 probes only 363,300 and 405,500 km — perigee and apogee, the symmetric points CLAUDE.md's verification note warns about — so the boundary is untested. `distanceToSunKm` is also pinned at 1 AU, so the demo cannot show the July/January total-vs-annular asymmetry.
findings.scenario: A continuous Earth-Moon distance control is added (today only three presets exist, and all three classify correctly). At 378,000 km — a value real eclipses occur at — the demo labels a central eclipse annular when it is total, and the 6,371 km misclassified window is 13% of the perigee-apogee range.
findings.fix: In eclipseGeometryModel.ts, evaluate the umbra at the sub-lunar point by passing `distanceFromBodyKm: dEarthMoonKm - earthRadiusKm` for the total/annular decision in `solarEclipseTypeFromBetaDeg` and `eclipseThresholdsDeg`, and add a test case at 378,000 km asserting "total-solar". Separately, let `distanceToSunKm` vary so the seasonal asymmetry is reachable.

findings.title: AstroConstants is declared `as const` then mutated through casts, so eleven derived constants carry the TypeScript literal type 0
findings.evidence: The object literal ends `} as const;` (line 115), which makes every numeric property deeply readonly with a literal type — so `MEAN_TROPICAL_YEAR_S: 0` (line 36) has type `0`. Lines 118-130 then re-cast `AstroConstants.TIME` to a mutable `{...: number}` shape purely to strip that readonly, and line 132 onward writes real values into it: MEAN_TROPICAL_YEAR_S, MEAN_SIDEREAL_MONTH_S, MEAN_SYNODIC_MONTH_S, MEAN_NODE_REGRESSION_S, MEAN_NODE_REGRESSION_DAYS, MEAN_DRACONIC_MONTH_DAYS, MEAN_DRACONIC_MONTH_S, M_PER_AU, CM_PER_AU, EV_PER_ERG, NM_PER_CM. Their declared type stays `0` while their runtime value is not; the cast is what launders the contradiction past the compiler. I verified the derived arithmetic is correct (DRACONIC = 1/(1/27.321661 + 1/6797.3025) = 27.2124 d against the accepted 27.212221 d; KM_PER_LY = c x Julian year = 9.4607304725808e12 km; KM_PER_PC = 1 AU / tan(1 arcsec) = 3.0856775814914e13 km).
findings.scenario: A guard written as `if (AstroConstants.LENGTH.CM_PER_AU > 0)` is narrowed by TypeScript against the literal 0 rather than checked, and a future module that imports AstroConstants into a cycle reads 0 before the bottom-of-file side effects run — a silent divide-by-zero in every AU conversion, with the declared type agreeing that it is 0.
findings.fix: Compute the derived values inline in the literal (MEAN_TROPICAL_YEAR_S: 365.2422 * 86400, and so on, or via small local consts declared above the object) and delete the three cast blocks and eleven assignments at astroConstants.ts:118-173. The object then really is `as const` and the types match the values.

findings.title: moonPhasesModel hardcodes the synodic month at 29.53 days beside AstroConstants' 29.530588
findings.evidence: `const SYNODIC_MONTH_DAYS = 29.53;` with no import, while astroConstants.ts:29 holds `MEAN_SYNODIC_MONTH_DAYS: 29.530588` and eclipseGeometryModel.ts:4 correctly reads it from there. The module also exports its own value as `synodicMonthDays` (line 48), so a consumer importing from @cosmic/physics can get either number depending on which model it asks. The numeric gap is 0.000588 d = 50.8 s in `daysSinceNewFromPhaseAngleDeg`, and the `waxingWaningFromPhaseAngleDeg` threshold at line 45 sits at 14.765 d rather than 14.765294 d — too small to see, but the two values are definitionally the same quantity.
findings.scenario: The eclipse demo and the moon-phases demo are placed side by side and quote the synodic month as 29.53 and 29.530588 days. More practically, a correction to the mean synodic month in AstroConstants reaches eclipse-geometry and not moon-phases.
findings.fix: In moonPhasesModel.ts, replace line 1 with `import { AstroConstants } from "./astroConstants";` and `const SYNODIC_MONTH_DAYS = AstroConstants.TIME.MEAN_SYNODIC_MONTH_DAYS;`, matching eclipseGeometryModel.ts:4.

findings.title: parallaxDistanceModel hardcodes pc-to-ly in the one demo claiming launch-ready, instead of deriving it from AstroConstants
findings.evidence: `const PC_TO_LY = 3.26156;` with no import. astroConstants.ts:48-52 already holds KM_PER_PC = 3.0856775814914e13 and KM_PER_LY = 9.4607304725808e12, whose ratio I computed as 3.2615637769 — so the literal is a 6-digit truncation of a value the package can derive exactly. This is the model behind apps/site/src/content/demos/parallax-distance.md, the only demo in the repo claiming `readiness: launch-ready` and `status: stable`, so it is the one place where an undocumented magic constant is most at odds with the public claim. The numeric error is 1.2e-6 relative (0.012 ly at 10,000 ly), harmless on its own.
findings.scenario: A student converts 100 pc to light-years in the parallax demo and gets 326.156 ly, then converts via the AU/parsec constants elsewhere in the same package and gets 326.15638 ly. The demo that carries the repo's only quality guarantee is the one with an unsourced literal.
findings.fix: In parallaxDistanceModel.ts, import AstroConstants and set `const PC_TO_LY = AstroConstants.LENGTH.KM_PER_PC / AstroConstants.LENGTH.KM_PER_LY;`.

findings.title: Spectroscopic mass function and minimum masses are circular-orbit-only but exported under the general names
findings.evidence: `massFunctionSolar` returns `(periodYr * k1AuPerYr^3) / (2 * pi * G)` — correct for e = 0, but the general spectroscopic mass function carries a factor (1 - e^2)^(3/2): f(m) = P K1^3 (1-e^2)^(3/2) / (2 pi G). `minimumMassesSolar` (line 282) has the same omission. The model is circular throughout — the only state builder is `circularState` (line 171) and BinaryOrbitInputs has no eccentricity field — but nothing in the exported names (index.ts, model object lines 363-364), the parameter types (`BinaryMassFunctionInput`) or the function docstrings says so. I verified the circular case is internally exact: the model's virial residual 2K + U is identically zero because K = 0.5 G m1 m2 / a and U = -G m1 m2 / a for a circular binary.
findings.scenario: An instructor or a future demo feeds real catalogue values for a spectroscopic binary — say P and K1 for an e = 0.5 system — into `massFunctionSolar` and gets a mass function too large by (1 - 0.25)^(-3/2) = 1.54, a 54% overestimate of the companion mass, with nothing in the API to warn them.
findings.fix: Either rename to `massFunctionSolarCircular` / `minimumMassesSolarCircular` and state "circular orbits only (e = 0); the general form carries (1 - e^2)^(3/2)" in each docstring, or add an optional `eccentricity` to the input types and multiply by (1 - e*e)**1.5, defaulting to 0.

findings.title: DopplerShiftModel exports the speed of light in SI metres per second, which the project's units convention forbids
findings.evidence: `const C_M_S = 299_792_458;` is exported on the model object at line 66 as `C_M_S`. CLAUDE.md states "NEVER use SI units (meters, kg, Joules) — use CGS (cm, g, erg)" and .agents/references/invariants.md requires "CGS for astrophysics". The value is also the third independent definition of c in the package (after astroConstants.ts:67/:94 and blackbodyRadiationModel.ts:5) and the second in km/s (galaxyRotationModel.ts:258 also carries `C_KM_S: 299_792.458`). I confirmed `C_M_S` appears in no file under apps/demos/src, apps/site/src or packages/runtime/src — it is dead, and a dead invariant violation on the public API surface.
findings.scenario: A demo author reaches for the nearest speed-of-light export, finds `DopplerShiftModel.C_M_S`, and silently introduces SI into a readout or export — the exact leak the units convention exists to prevent, sanctioned by the physics package itself.
findings.fix: Delete `C_M_S` from dopplerShiftModel.ts (both the const at line 42 and the export at line 66) and derive `C_KM_S` from AstroConstants: `const C_KM_S = AstroConstants.PHOTON.C_CM_PER_S / AstroConstants.LENGTH.CM_PER_KM;`. Do the same for galaxyRotationModel.ts:258.

findings.title: eclipseThresholdsDeg returns a `_debug` field as part of its public contract
findings.evidence: The declared return type includes `_debug: { earthShadowAtMoon: {...}; moonShadowAtEarth: {...} }`, populated at lines 155-158 and consumed by the demo at apps/demos/src/demos/eclipse-geometry/main.ts (five call sites: 419, 451, 504, 587, 775). The underscore-prefixed name says the field is internal, but it is in the type signature, so it is API: a consumer cannot tell whether it is safe to read, and the two shadow geometries it carries are legitimately useful quantities being smuggled out under a name that disclaims support. I verified the underlying numbers are right — Earth's umbra radius at the mean lunar distance comes out 4,599.0 km against the accepted ~4,600 km.
findings.scenario: A demo starts drawing the umbra and penumbra from `_debug.earthShadowAtMoon`, and a later refactor removes the field as internal because its name says it is, breaking the drawing with no type error at the model boundary.
findings.fix: Rename the field to `shadowGeometry` (or return `earthShadowAtMoon` and `moonShadowAtEarth` as top-level members) in eclipseGeometryModel.ts, document the units as km, and update the five call sites in apps/demos/src/demos/eclipse-geometry/main.ts.

findings.title: Eccentricity is silently clamped to 0.99 on a stated numerical-stiffness ground the solver does not actually have
findings.evidence: `/** ... We avoid e->1 because the Kepler solver becomes numerically stiff. */ clampEccentricity(e) { ... return clamp(e, 0, 0.99); }`, applied without signalling inside `orbitExtremaAu` (line 61) and `stateAtMeanAnomalyRad` (line 86). I measured the solver it is protecting: over e in {0, 0.1, 0.3, 0.5, 0.8, 0.81, 0.9, 0.95, 0.99, 0.995, 0.999, 0.9999} x 2000 mean anomalies, max |E - E_ref| = 2.2e-12 rad, every call converged on the Newton path inside 15 iterations, and the bisection fallback was never reached. The premise is false at least to e = 0.9999. The clamp is currently unreachable from the UI — apps/demos/src/demos/keplers-laws/index.html:247 caps the slider at 990, i.e. e = 0.990 — so no student sees the silent substitution today.
findings.scenario: A demo or an instructor passes e = 0.995 (a long-period comet) to `stateAtMeanAnomalyRad`. The returned perihelion, aphelion, speed and energy are all for e = 0.990 with no flag, so the readouts are self-consistent and quietly describe a different orbit. The perihelion is 0.010a instead of 0.005a — a factor of 2.
findings.fix: Either raise the bound in keplersLawsModel.ts:55 to the solver's measured domain (e <= 0.9999) and note the measurement in the comment, or return NaN rather than a clamped value so a caller finds out, and correct the docstring's claim about solver stiffness.

findings.title: packages/theme's entire TypeScript surface is dead, and the token mirror CLAUDE.md names as a layer covers 58 of 187 tokens with no parity test
findings.evidence: Zero consumers for every export: grepping apps and packages (excluding the defining files) for CSS_VARS, Z_INDEX, BREAKPOINTS, CHART_COLORS, MOTION, setCosmicLayer, getCosmicLayer, setTheme and CosmicLayer each returns nothing, and `from "@cosmic/theme"` (the TS entry, as opposed to @cosmic/theme/styles/*) has no hits anywhere. CLAUDE.md's token hierarchy lists vars.ts as "TypeScript mirror of CSS tokens" and tokens.test.ts as the contract test, but tokens.test.ts imports only fs and path and reads the CSS - it never imports CSS_VARS, so nothing checks either direction. Counting declarations: tokens.css defines 187 distinct --cp-* custom properties; vars.ts names 58 (31%). vars.ts also still publishes the legacy aliases --cp-accent2/3/4 that CLAUDE.md Invariant 7 forbids. BREAKPOINTS duplicates --cp-bp-sm/md/lg/xl (tokens.css:216-219) as hardcoded strings; `var(--cp-bp` has zero usages anywhere, and the CSS actually uses 26 distinct ad-hoc media-query widths (1025, 1024, 980, 900, 880, 860, 720, 700, 1080 px and others), none of them 768 or 1280.
findings.scenario: A maintainer adds a token to tokens.css, consults CLAUDE.md, dutifully mirrors it into vars.ts, and nothing consumes or verifies it - so the mirror keeps drifting while the documentation keeps asserting it is a source of truth. Meanwhile responsive behaviour is governed by 26 undocumented pixel values while four named breakpoint tokens sit unused.
findings.fix: Delete packages/theme/src/vars.ts, layer.ts and index.ts, and drop the `.` export from packages/theme/package.json so the package exports only ./styles/*. If a TS surface is wanted later, generate it from tokens.css at build time rather than hand-mirroring. Separately, consolidate the 26 media-query widths onto a small documented set and delete the unused --cp-bp-* tokens, or adopt them via a PostCSS custom-media step.

findings.title: Four dead modules totalling ~590 lines, one of which still ships its CSS into all 20 demo bundles
findings.evidence: bottomSheet.ts exports initBottomSheet (line 65) but is not re-exported from packages/runtime/src/index.ts and has zero importers; its test is 5,292 bytes; packages/theme/styles/components/bottom-sheet.css (67 lines) is nevertheless imported unconditionally at apps/demos/src/shared/stub-demo.css:11, and grepping for the cp-bottom-sheet class across apps/demos/src and the theme styles finds it only in that stylesheet - no markup uses it, yet 20 of 20 deployed demo CSS bundles contain it. apps/demos/src/shared/stub-demo.ts (initStubDemo) and stub-modes.ts (initStubPedagogyModes) have zero importers across all .ts, .html, .css, .mjs and .astro files - about 220 lines. packages/ui/src/index.ts is two lines exporting only a PACKAGE_NAME string with zero dependents. @cosmic/runtime also re-exports eight @cosmic/math symbols (EPS, findRootBisection, findRootNewton, integrateSimpson, integrateTrapz, interp1, linspace, logspace) that no demo or site file imports from runtime, creating a second import route for the same functions. The 2026-09-03 adversarial audit (docs/audits/2026-09-03-comprehensive-adversarial-audit.md:389) already reported this set; it is still present.
findings.scenario: A maintainer reads packages/ui and shared/stub-demo.ts as live architecture and extends them, or copies initStubPedagogyModes with its window.prompt()-based challenge answers into a real demo. Meanwhile every student loading any demo downloads bottom-sheet.css for a component that does not exist in any page.
findings.fix: Delete packages/runtime/src/bottomSheet.ts and bottomSheet.test.ts, packages/theme/styles/components/bottom-sheet.css and its @import at apps/demos/src/shared/stub-demo.css:11, apps/demos/src/shared/stub-demo.ts and stub-modes.ts, and the whole packages/ui directory (removing it from pnpm-workspace coverage is automatic). Narrow packages/runtime/src/index.ts to re-export only clamp from @cosmic/math and have anything else import @cosmic/math directly. Rename shared/stub-demo.css to shared/demo-theme.css, since it is now the canonical theme entry rather than a stub artifact.

findings.title: three.js is inlined into the cluster-census entry chunk (561 KB), not code-split as CLAUDE.md claims
findings.evidence: main.ts:22 imports createClusterScene statically (`import { createClusterScene } from "./clusterScene";`), and clusterScene.ts imports three at module scope. In the deployed assets directory there is no three-* or OrbitControls-* chunk at all, while cluster-census-CBv7sFvP.js is 561,175 bytes and contains six occurrences of WebGLRenderer - three.js is inside the demo's entry chunk. The next largest demo entry is eos-lab at 121,137 bytes. CLAUDE.md states "Vite code-splits it, so only demos that import it pay the ~130 KB gzipped" - the outcome (only cluster-census pays) is right but the stated mechanism is not, so the entry is 4.6x the next heaviest and must be fully parsed before anything renders.
findings.scenario: A student opens cluster-census on a classroom Chromebook. 561 KB of JavaScript must download and parse before the first star appears, because the renderer is in the entry chunk rather than a parallel-loadable vendor chunk - and any edit to the demo's own code invalidates the cached three.js along with it.
findings.fix: Make the three.js dependency a dynamic import: change apps/demos/src/demos/cluster-census/main.ts:22 to `const { createClusterScene } = await import("./clusterScene")` (clusterScene.ts already returns null when the renderer cannot be created, so the no-WebGL path is unchanged), or add a manualChunks entry for three in apps/demos/vite.config.ts. Then render the 2-D panels first and attach the GPU scene when its chunk resolves.

findings.title: withBase is defined 14 times and parseIsoDate is reimplemented in a file that already imports it
findings.evidence: Fourteen withBase definitions across apps/site/src: Layout.astro:15, about.astro:9, exhibits/[slug].astro:21, for-instructors/index.astro:13, glossary.astro:9, instructor/index.astro:13, stations/index.astro:13, topics/[slug].astro:34, topics/index.astro:11 and welcome.astro:6 each inline the same four-line normalizedBase body; explore/index.astro:29, playlists/[slug].astro:18 and playlists/index.astro:13 correctly delegate to normalizeBasePathPath from lib/catalog.ts:17; welcome.astro:98 adds a fourteenth, untyped copy inside a client script. index.astro uses a fourth idiom entirely, interpolating `${base}` directly (lines 56, 59, 64). Separately, index.astro:20 declares `function parseIsoDate(iso: string)` while line 3 already imports from ../lib/catalog, which exports an identical parseIsoDate at catalog.ts:40. .agents/references/invariants.md actively instructs "copy withBase() from apps/site/src/layouts/Layout.astro", so the duplication is doctrine.
findings.scenario: The Pages base path changes, or a bug is found in base-path joining (a double slash, a missing trailing slash). Eleven hand-written copies must be found and fixed identically; one is missed and that page's internal links 404 on the deployed site while working in local dev where the base is empty.
findings.fix: Move withBase into apps/site/src/lib/basePath.ts as `export const withBase = (path: string) => normalizeBasePathPath(path, import.meta.env.BASE_URL)`, import it in all 13 .astro files, delete every local definition, and replace welcome.astro:98's client-script copy by passing the computed href into the script via a data- attribute. Delete index.astro:20-23 and use catalog.ts's parseIsoDate. Then change .agents/references/invariants.md to say import it, not copy it.

findings.title: Three parallel per-slug art registries; the SVG fallback covers 14 of 20 demos and emits duplicate element ids on every listing page
findings.evidence: Three registries that must be kept in step by hand: DemoCanvasThumbnail.astro:9-30 maps all 20 slugs to a scene name; the same file's inline painter branches on those scene names at lines 208-558; and DemoIllustration.astro has 14 `{slug === "..."}` branches (lines 53, 66, 81, 97, 115, 132, 156, 174, 197, 214, 231, 250, 267, 288) with no fallback branch - so cluster-census, doppler-shift, galaxy-rotation, hydrostatic-equilibrium-explorer, spectral-lines and stars-zams-hr render only the shared star dots. DemoIllustration is instantiated once per card via DemoCanvasThumbnail.astro:39, and its defs block hardcodes id="sun-glow", id="earth-glow" and id="soft-glow" (lines 25, 30, 34), so /explore/ with 19 listed demos emits 57 duplicate element ids and every url(#sun-glow) resolves to the first instance in document order. DemoCanvasThumbnail.astro is 643 lines holding the map, the painter, the styles and the driver script.
findings.scenario: With JavaScript disabled or before the thumbnail canvas paints, six demo cards - including the newest ones - show an empty star field with no illustration, so they read as broken next to fourteen illustrated siblings. And the first card's gradients silently govern all nineteen, so any future per-demo gradient tweak has no effect beyond card one.
findings.fix: Move each demo's fallback SVG into its own file under apps/site/src/components/illustrations/<slug>.astro, add a generic default for unmatched slugs, and derive the id suffixes per instance (id={`sun-glow-${slug}`}) so they are unique. Split the canvas painter out of DemoCanvasThumbnail.astro into apps/site/src/lib/thumbnailScenes.ts with one exported scene registry, and add a test asserting every slug in content/demos has both a scene and a fallback.

findings.title: The topic taxonomy is restated in six places and welcome.astro ships six of the eight topics - the exact drift topics.ts claims to have ended
findings.evidence: welcome.astro:12-18 declares its own topic list with inline labels and covers six topics - Galaxies and Cosmology are absent. topics.ts:1-12 documents that this is the historical failure ("TopicStrip shipped six of the eight topics") and claims "TopicKey is derived from TOPIC_ORDER, so adding a topic to the content schema without adding it here is a type error" - but content/config.ts:12-21 declares the eight keys as an independent zod enum with no type relationship to TOPIC_ORDER, so that claim does not hold. Six restatements in total: config.ts:12-21 (zod enum), topics.ts:15-24 plus TOPIC_LABEL:32-41, topicColors.ts:2-11 (TOPIC_CSS_VAR, typed Record<string,string> so a typo is not caught), TopicIcon.astro:14-23 (topicIcons, also Record<string, any>), welcome.astro:12-18 (keys plus labels plus a start slug), and tokens.css:320-327 (--cp-topic-* values).
findings.scenario: A student picks Galaxies as their interest on the welcome page and finds it is not offered, so the two-question onboarding cannot route them to galaxy-rotation. A ninth topic added to the schema compiles, gets a topic page with an undefined label, and never appears in the icon map or the welcome flow.
findings.fix: Make TOPIC_ORDER in apps/site/src/lib/topics.ts the only list: derive the zod enum in content/config.ts from it (z.enum(TOPIC_ORDER)), type TOPIC_CSS_VAR and topicIcons as Record<TopicKey, ...> so an omission is a compile error, and have welcome.astro map over TOPIC_ORDER with TOPIC_LABEL plus a TOPIC_START_SLUG record added alongside TOPIC_SEQUENCE. Delete the local lists in welcome.astro:12-18 and fix the inaccurate claim in the topics.ts:9-11 docstring.

findings.title: Three demos declare instructor bundles and two declare station cards that have no content, and the frontmatter paths are root-absolute
findings.evidence: Comparing content/demos (20 files) against content/instructor (17 bundles) and content/stations (18 cards): no instructor bundle exists for cluster-census, eos-lab or stars-zams-hr, and no station card exists for planetary-conjunctions or stars-zams-hr - yet every one of those files declares a required path, e.g. instructor_path: "/instructor/stars-zams-hr/" and station_path: "/stations/stars-zams-hr/". explore/index.astro:252-253 and 320-321 render these unconditionally as stationHref and instructorHref, and DemoCard.astro:138-142 turns them into "Station card" and "Instructor notes" buttons. The routes do not 404 (instructor/[slug].astro:5-10 generates from the demos collection and degrades to a no-content state - cluster-census builds to 12,998 bytes against moon-phases' 73,754), so the result is a button leading to an empty page. Separately, every path value begins with "/", the form .agents/references/invariants.md forbids; it survives only because explore passes it through normalizeBasePathPath, so any consumer that uses the raw value as an href breaks on GitHub Pages.
findings.scenario: An instructor planning a lecture clicks "Instructor notes" on the stars-zams-hr card, lands on a page with the title and navigation but no activities, assessment or model notes, and has no way to tell whether the notes are missing or the page is broken.
findings.fix: Either write the five missing bundles or hide the affordance: pass stationHref/instructorHref only when the corresponding collection entry exists (compute the sets once in apps/site/src/lib/catalog.ts and use them in explore/index.astro:252-253 and 320-321). Store the paths as bare slugs rather than root-absolute strings in content/config.ts:56-57 and build the hrefs from withBase, and add a check to scripts/validate-play-dirs.mjs that every declared station_path and instructor_path resolves to real content.

findings.title: withBase is hand-reimplemented 12 times beside the lib helper written to replace it
findings.evidence: `normalizeBasePathPath(path, base)` exists at catalog.ts:17-21 and is imported by exactly three pages (explore/index.astro:20, playlists/index.astro:7, playlists/[slug].astro:6). The identical four-line body is retyped as a local `const withBase` in Layout.astro:15, about.astro:9, exhibits/[slug].astro:21, for-instructors/index.astro:13, glossary.astro:9, instructor/index.astro:13, stations/index.astro:13, topics/[slug].astro:34, topics/index.astro:11 and welcome.astro:6 — and a twelfth time, in plain JS, inside welcome.astro's client script at :98. `Breadcrumb.astro:21` and `MobileNav.astro:12` then take `withBase` as a prop, so the function is also threaded through the component API rather than imported.
findings.scenario: A base-path change (for example moving off GitHub Pages, or adding a trailing-slash rule) has to be made correctly in twelve places. One miss produces a 404 only on the deployed sub-path site, where local `astro dev` at base `/` cannot reproduce it — the class of bug site-links.spec.ts was written for.
findings.fix: Export `withBase(path: string)` from apps/site/src/lib/catalog.ts (reading `import.meta.env.BASE_URL` itself), import it in all eleven pages and Layout.astro, and drop the `withBase` props from Breadcrumb.astro:21 and MobileNav.astro:12. For welcome.astro's client script, pass the single prebuilt URL strings via `define:vars` instead of re-deriving them in the browser.

findings.title: /for-instructors/ duplicates the stations and instructor indexes while dropping their authored-vs-scaffold honesty
findings.evidence: for-instructors/index.astro:78-95 lists all 20 demos as "Station Cards" and :108-122 lists all 20 as "Instructor Notes", in both cases from `sortedDemos` with no check that content exists. But 2 demos have no station card (planetary-conjunctions, stars-zams-hr — `apps/site/src/content/stations/` holds 18 demo cards plus meta.md) and 3 have no instructor bundle (cluster-census, eos-lab, stars-zams-hr — `apps/site/src/content/instructor/` has 17 bundle directories). The two dedicated indexes are honest about this: stations/index.astro:24,38-40 prints "18 of 20 exhibits have a dedicated card; the rest render a generic observation template", and instructor/index.astro:56-62 shows "scaffold template" when the section count is 0. So three pages render the same two lists at three different honesty levels, and the hub — the one in the header nav — is the least honest. The hub is also the only one of the three in the primary nav, while /instructor/ and /stations/ sit in no nav list.
findings.scenario: An instructor plans a five-station lab from /for-instructors/, prints the Stars (ZAMS/HR) station card expecting a dedicated scaffold, and gets a generic observation template — with no warning anywhere on the page they planned from.
findings.fix: Delete the two re-listings from apps/site/src/pages/for-instructors/index.astro:69-133 and replace each with a single card linking to /stations/ and /instructor/, which already own those lists and their honesty. If the hub must keep inline lists, import the same `authoredStationSlugs` / section-count derivations (stations/index.astro:22 and instructor/index.astro:20-24) rather than reimplementing the list without them.

findings.title: explore/index.astro at 1004 lines duplicates five pieces of page logic and copy with index.astro and others
findings.evidence: Verbatim duplicates between explore/index.astro and its siblings: (1) `featuredOrder` + the `featured` filter/sort — explore:48-55 and index.astro:26-33, identical. (2) `excerptFromBody` — explore:57-64 and topics/[slug].astro:62-70, identical. (3) `parseIsoDate` — exported from catalog.ts:40-43, imported by explore:21, yet redefined locally at index.astro:20-23 in the same file that already imports `listedDemos` from catalog. (4) the `.site-state-note` CSS rule block — identical in index.astro:255-262, explore:772-780 and topics/index.astro:76-84, with four different wordings of the beta notice across index.astro:53, explore:195, topics/index.astro:37 and topics/[slug].astro:115. (5) the identity copy "An interactive museum of astronomy reasoning instruments." and "Explore observables, models, and inferences—like doing experiments on ideas." appear word for word at explore:189,191 and playlists/index.astro:47,49, and the tagline "Play with the universe. Learn the physics." at index.astro:51 and explore:193. index.astro also inlines `d.data.short_key_idea ?? d.data.learning_goals[0]` at :100 and :151 instead of calling `demoKeyIdea` from catalog.ts:35-38.
findings.scenario: The site's own one-line description of what it is exists in two files and its beta disclosure in four, so a copy edit lands on some pages and not others — already visible, since the four beta notices say four different things about what a readiness badge means.
findings.fix: Move `featuredDemos()`, `excerptFromBody()` and the site copy constants (SITE_IDENTITY, SITE_TAGLINE, BETA_NOTICE) into apps/site/src/lib/catalog.ts and a new lib/copy.ts; delete index.astro:20-33, explore/index.astro:48-64 and topics/[slug].astro:62-70; promote `.site-state-note` to a `SiteStateNote.astro` component (or a rule in apps/site/src/styles/global.css) and use it on all four pages; replace the inline key-idea expressions at index.astro:100,151 with `demoKeyIdea(d)`.

findings.title: Dead routes and dead code: the hubs collection has no page, JourneyStep.astro has no importer, ?theme=paper never fires
findings.evidence: Three verified orphans. (1) `hubs` is a full collection — schema at content/config.ts:84-92, registered at :120, four content files (hubs/cosmic-playground.md, hubs/meta.md, hubs/light-and-telescopes.md, hubs/distance-and-measurement.md) — and grepping `hubs` across apps/site/src/**/*.astro and **/*.ts returns only those two config.ts lines: no page calls `getCollection("hubs")`, so none of that content is reachable. (2) `apps/site/src/components/JourneyStep.astro` is 165 lines and `grep -rn "JourneyStep" apps/site/src` returns no import. (3) Layout.astro:30-34 computes `const themeParam = Astro.url.searchParams.get("theme")` and keys `isLightTheme` partly on `themeParam === "paper"`; astro.config.mjs:11 is `output: "static"`, so that read is always null at build time and the `?theme=paper` branch can never be taken — the same build-time-searchParams class of dead code that catalog.ts:6-15 documents having already removed once.
findings.scenario: A maintainer edits apps/site/src/content/hubs/light-and-telescopes.md expecting it to appear somewhere, or links a colleague to a URL with `?theme=paper` to get the printable light theme, and in both cases nothing happens with no error anywhere.
findings.fix: Decide and act in one pass: either add a route that renders `hubs` or delete the four files and the schema at apps/site/src/content/config.ts:84-92,120; delete apps/site/src/components/JourneyStep.astro; and either remove the `themeParam` branch at apps/site/src/layouts/Layout.astro:30-34 or implement it as a client-side `data-theme` toggle that can actually run. Add a `getCollection` coverage assertion to the datasets contract test so a future unrendered collection fails a gate.

findings.title: tokenContrast.test.ts's resolver ignores selector and @media context, so its whole paper suite measures the print palette instead of the screen theme
findings.evidence: `parseTokens` matches `/(--cp-[a-z0-9-]+)\s*:\s*([^;]+);/g` over the entire file and keeps the last occurrence ('later wins'). layer-paper.css ends at lines 119-127 with `@media print { .cp-layer-paper, [data-theme="paper"] { --cp-bg0: #fff; --cp-bg1: #fff; --cp-text: #000; --cp-muted: #333; } }`, so the `paper` map (line 109) resolves --cp-bg0 to #fff, --cp-text to #000 and --cp-muted to #333. The paper describe block then asserts --cp-text and --cp-muted 'on --cp-bg0' while measuring #000 on #fff (21.00:1) and #333 on #fff (12.63:1). I recomputed the screen values the test believes it is checking: --cp-text #111425 on #fafaff = 17.54:1, --cp-muted #4b556b on #fafaff = 7.18:1. Both still pass, so nothing is broken today -- the mechanism is.
findings.scenario: Someone darkens the paper screen background or lightens --cp-muted for a lighter look. The paper block keeps reporting the @media print palette, which the change never touched, and the screen regression ships green -- in the one file written specifically because 'those tests cannot fail when a token drifts'.
findings.fix: In packages/theme/src/tokenContrast.test.ts make parseTokens selector-aware: strip `@media` blocks (or accept a predicate so a print layer can be tested deliberately) and collect declarations per selector, keeping only the block that matches the layer under test. The print palette then deserves its own describe block instead of silently shadowing the screen one.

findings.title: The design system has no panel or readout component: their base styles live in an app file with raw px, and the documented import chain lists 6 of 16 imports
findings.evidence: packages/theme/styles/components/ holds 17 files but none for panel or readout. `.cp-readout`, `.cp-readout__label`, `.cp-readout__value` and `.cp-panel-body` are defined only at apps/demos/src/shared/stub-demo.css:18, 49, 57, 62 -- app layer, with raw literals (`margin-top: 12px; padding: 10px; border-radius: 10px`) rather than --cp-space-* / --cp-r-1 -- while their themed form lives at packages/theme/styles/layer-instrument.css:81-146 behind a `.cp-layer-instrument` descendant selector. `.cp-panel` itself has no base rule anywhere (only print.css:33 and the layer-scoped version), and `.cp-readout__unit` exists only inside the layer, so CLAUDE.md's Readout Typography Contract has no implementation on the museum or paper layer at all. CLAUDE.md's 'CSS Import Chain (demo entry point)' documents tokens -> animations -> layer-instrument -> demo-shell -> button -> form; stub-demo.css actually imports 16 files, adding control, popover, tabs, playbar, bottom-sheet, utility-toolbar, readout-strip, scroll-shadow, chip and toggle. CLAUDE.md also claims '30 tests' in tokens.test.ts; it has 47 it()/it.each cases.
findings.scenario: A new demo cannot be built without new CSS, because the two structures every demo needs most -- a panel and a readout -- are half-defined in a file inside apps/demos and half in a layer file, with the unit span existing in only one layer. That is the mechanism behind the 10,252 lines of demo CSS and the 28 orphan cp-* classes.
findings.fix: Create packages/theme/styles/components/panel.css and components/readout.css holding the layer-agnostic structure (grid, spacing from --cp-space-*, radius from --cp-r-*, the label/value/unit typography from the --cp-readout-* tokens), leaving layer-instrument.css to override only colour and translucency; delete the duplicate rules from apps/demos/src/shared/stub-demo.css; and update the import-chain and test-count lines in CLAUDE.md to match the files.

findings.title: 10,252 lines of demo CSS restate the shared layer: 26 declaration bodies repeated verbatim in 3+ demos, the motion contract copy-pasted 8 times
findings.evidence: Parsed all 20 style.css files into 1,354 top-level rules. Declaration bodies of 40+ characters repeated verbatim across three or more demos: 26. The top four are all the entry-stagger pattern -- `animation: cp-slide-up var(--cp-duration-enter) var(--cp-ease-out) both; animation-delay: calc(var(--cp-stagger) * 2)` appears identically in 8 demos, the *3 variant in 6, the bare slide-up in 6, the stage fade-in in 4 -- i.e. CLAUDE.md invariant 8 is implemented by copy-paste rather than by demo-shell.css. `.cp-chip:focus-visible, .cp-button:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--cp-focus); outline-offset: 2px; }` is restated in 5 demos, duplicating the global `:focus-visible` rule at tokens.css:396. 230 of the 1,354 rules (17%) target a `.cp-*` shared class; binary-orbits alone restyles 42 of them across 126 declaration lines, 11 of those rules reaching into `.cp-demo__readouts .cp-readout*` to re-specify the readout typography the theme already owns. Raw px spacing/radius declarations where a token exists: 38 in stars-zams-hr, 18 in hydrostatic-equilibrium-explorer, 15 in binary-orbits (e.g. `.viz-panel { border-radius: 12px }` in moon-phases rather than var(--cp-r-2)).
findings.scenario: Changing the stagger timing, the focus-ring offset or the readout rhythm requires editing 5 to 8 demo stylesheets, and missing one leaves a demo visibly out of step with the rest -- which is how hydrostatic-equilibrium-explorer reached 1,303 lines for one instrument.
findings.fix: Move the entry-animation stagger into packages/theme/styles/demo-shell.css as `.cp-demo > :where(.cp-demo__sidebar, .cp-demo__stage, .cp-demo__controls, .cp-demo__readouts, .cp-demo__shelf)` with an nth-child-driven delay, delete the 29 copies, and delete the 5 focus-ring restatements (tokens.css already covers them). Then extend the invariant script to reject raw px in padding/margin/gap/border-radius inside apps/demos/src/demos/*/style.css, which is the same class of rule as no-color-literals and would retire ~90 declarations.

findings.title: --cp-input-placeholder resolves to --cp-faint at 2.62:1, and a test explicitly licenses it at 2.5:1
findings.evidence: `--cp-input-placeholder: var(--cp-faint)` and --cp-faint is `color-mix(in srgb, #ffffff 32%, var(--cp-bg0))` = #5c5d60. form.css:28-31 applies it as `.cp-input::placeholder`. I resolved and recomputed against the ground it is painted on, --cp-input-bg = --cp-bg1 #171b22: 2.62:1. On the paper layer --cp-faint #7d8599 on #fafaff = 3.69:1. WCAG 1.4.3 covers placeholder text at 4.5:1. contrast.test.ts:138-140 asserts `--cp-faint on --cp-bg0 >= 2.5:1 (decorative / placeholder only)` -- the test encodes the defect rather than catching it, and it measures the easier --cp-bg0 ground, not the input. Live placeholders using .cp-input: apps/site/src/components/FilterBar.astro:42 ('Search demos') and apps/site/src/pages/glossary.astro:59 ('Filter terms'). Three <textarea> placeholders in hydrostatic-equilibrium-explorer/index.html:387-395 and an <input> in stars-zams-hr/index.html:408 carry no .cp-textarea / .cp-input class, so they fall through to the UA default instead.
findings.scenario: A student on a classroom projector looks for the search box on /explore/. The only cue that it is a search field is 'Search demos' at 2.62:1, which washes out entirely under room light -- and the field's border is the 1.22:1 --cp-border, so neither the affordance nor its label is visible.
findings.fix: In packages/theme/styles/tokens.css point --cp-input-placeholder at a new mix that clears 4.5:1 on --cp-bg1 (about 48% white) instead of aliasing --cp-faint, keeping --cp-faint for genuinely decorative use; add the pair ('--cp-input-placeholder' on '--cp-input-bg', 4.5) to tokenContrast.test.ts for all three layers; and add .cp-textarea / .cp-input to the four unclassed fields in hydrostatic-equilibrium-explorer and stars-zams-hr.

findings.title: --cp-border is 1.22:1, so the only boundary on inputs, cards and panels fails the 3:1 UI-component minimum and no test measures it
findings.evidence: `--cp-border: rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.08)`. Composited over --cp-bg0 #0f1115 that is #222428; I recomputed the ratio against --cp-bg0: 1.22:1 (--cp-border-subtle at 0.06 is 1.15:1). It is the sole visible boundary of `.cp-input` / `.cp-select` / `.cp-demo select` (form.css:14 via --cp-input-border), `.cp-card` (layer-museum.css:30), `.cp-badge` and `.cp-chip`. WCAG 1.4.11 requires 3:1 for the visual information needed to identify a UI component. Neither contrast.test.ts nor tokenContrast.test.ts includes --cp-border or --cp-border-subtle in any pair. Even the unreachable high-contrast.css raises it only to 0.25 alpha, which I computed as 2.23:1 -- still short of 3:1.
findings.scenario: On a projector or any screen with sRGB clipping in the shadows, the Explore filter inputs, the demo select menus and the exhibit cards have no perceptible edge; a student cannot tell where a text field begins, and the 2.62:1 placeholder is the only remaining hint.
findings.fix: Raise --cp-input-border (not --cp-border, which is also used for hairline dividers where 1.22:1 is acceptable) to a value clearing 3:1 on --cp-bg1 -- about rgba(255,255,255,0.34) -- and give `.cp-card` / `.cp-panel` an explicit border token at the same level. Add ('--cp-input-border' on '--cp-input-bg', 3.0) and ('--cp-card-border' on its ground, 3.0) to tokenContrast.test.ts, and correct the 0.25 value in high-contrast.css once that file is wired up or deleted.

findings.title: initBottomSheet, its stylesheet and its 11 tests are unreachable dead code, and its handle is pointer-only
findings.evidence: grep for initBottomSheet across apps/demos/src, apps/site/src and packages returns only bottomSheet.ts:65 (the definition) and bottomSheet.test.ts (2, 29, 159). It is not re-exported from packages/runtime/src/index.ts, which exports initPopovers, initStarfield and initTabs but not this. .cp-bottom-sheet markup exists in no index.html - only in bottomSheet.ts/.test.ts, packages/theme/styles/components/bottom-sheet.css and packages/theme/src/components.test.ts. If it were wired up it would be mouse-only: the handle gets pointerdown/pointermove/pointerup listeners (142-144) and nothing else, and a keyboard activation of a <button> fires click, not pointerdown - so Enter/Space could not open it. bottomSheet.test.ts has no Enter/Space case (its 11 its cover tap, drag, Escape, outside click and the live region). Escape (135-140) collapses the sheet without moving focus out of it.
findings.scenario: Nothing fails for a student today, because no demo has a bottom sheet. The cost is that 11 green tests and a design-system contract test vouch for a mobile controls drawer that does not exist, so /play/ routes have no mobile control affordance at all (see finding 8), and whoever adopts this module next ships a mouse-only drawer with tests that pass.
findings.fix: Decide and act in one direction. If mobile drawers are wanted, add a click listener alongside the pointer ones (or key handling for Enter/Space), move focus to the first control in the sheet on expand and back to the handle on Escape-collapse, export it from index.ts, and adopt it in one demo. Otherwise delete bottomSheet.ts, bottomSheet.test.ts, packages/theme/styles/components/bottom-sheet.css and its assertions in packages/theme/src/components.test.ts.

findings.title: Demo pages skip from h1 straight to h3, in 8 of 20 demos
findings.evidence: angular-size has one h1 (line 14, sr-only) and one h3 (line 139, 'Moon time mode') with no h2 between. Counted across all 20 index.html files: angular-size h1=1 h2=0 h3=1; blackbody-radiation h1=1 h2=0 h3=5 (first at line 136); cluster-census h1=1 h2=0 h3=5; doppler-shift h1=1 h2=0 h3=7 h4=2; galaxy-rotation h1=1 h2=0 h3=7; spectral-lines h1=1 h2=0 h3=12; binary-orbits h1=1 h2=1 h3=7 (one h2 for seven h3s); retrograde-motion h1=1 h2=0 h3=0. Only eos-lab, hydrostatic-equilibrium-explorer and stars-zams-hr have a contiguous h1-h2-h3 chain.
findings.scenario: A screen-reader student navigating /play/spectral-lines/ by heading level (a primary navigation strategy) jumps from the h1 to twelve h3s with no h2, so the reader reports a structure with a missing level and the student cannot tell which sections are siblings and which are nested - the drawer groupings the sighted layout conveys are lost.
findings.fix: Demote the orphaned h3s to h2 where they are top-level sections of the demo, or add the missing h2 section heading. Mechanical, no copy decisions. Then add to accessibility.spec.ts a per-demo check that the sorted sequence of heading levels under #cp-demo increases by at most 1.

findings.title: KatexAutoRender decides equation focusability once at load, so zooming to 400% leaves new overflow unreachable
findings.evidence: for (const node of root.querySelectorAll('.katex-display')) { if (node.scrollWidth > node.clientWidth) { node.tabIndex = 0; node.setAttribute('role','region'); node.setAttribute('aria-label','Scrollable equation'); } } - a single pass with no resize or matchMedia listener. The comparison is evaluated at whatever width the page loaded at. (I checked the related trap: .katex-mathml in apps/demos/src/assets/katex/katex.min.css is position:absolute with width:1px;height:1px;overflow:hidden, so it cannot inflate scrollWidth here - the defect is purely the one-shot timing.)
findings.scenario: A low-vision student loads an exhibit page at 1280px, where a display equation fits, then zooms to 400% as WCAG 1.4.10 contemplates. The equation now overflows its .katex-display box, but tabIndex was never assigned, so the overflowing right-hand side of the equation cannot be scrolled into view by keyboard - exactly the condition the code was written to handle.
findings.fix: Extract the pass into a function and re-run it from a debounced ResizeObserver on <main> (and on matchMedia resolution changes), setting tabIndex/role/aria-label when a node overflows and removing them when it no longer does. Share the same function with packages/runtime/src/math.ts (finding 9) so the site and the demos have one implementation.

findings.title: Exhibit pages embed each demo in a fixed 16:10 iframe, and the reflow gate cannot see inside it
findings.evidence: .iframe-stage__frame { width: 100%; aspect-ratio: 16 / 10; overflow: clip; } with iframe { width: 100%; height: 100% } (lines 31-45). At the 320px viewport reflow.spec.ts tests, minus .site-main padding of 2 x var(--cp-space-5) = 48px and .iframe-stage padding of 2 x var(--cp-space-4) = 32px, the frame is about 240 x 150 CSS px - and the demo inside is a full instrument shell with a sidebar, a stage and a readout strip. reflow.spec.ts measures with page.evaluate (lines 70-105), which runs only in the top frame, so the embedded document's layout is never inspected; overflow: clip then hides the evidence from the outer measurement too. Every exhibits/<slug>/ route is in CONTENT_ROUTES and passes.
findings.scenario: A student follows a link to /exhibits/moon-phases/ on a phone. The demo is squeezed into a roughly 240x150 box that scrolls in both directions inside the page, so neither the controls nor the readouts are usable, while the reflow gate reports the route as compliant.
findings.fix: Below about 700px, replace the iframe with the 'open the demo fullscreen' link that already exists at IframeStage.astro:15-19 (or let the frame grow to a tall portrait aspect ratio with a minimum height). Separately, add a reflow case that navigates directly to each play/<slug>/ route at 320px (finding 8) so the embedded document is measured as a page in its own right.

findings.title: The no-color-literals invariant is unenforced in TypeScript, where the canvas drawing code lives
findings.evidence: validate-invariants.mjs:101 `const colorLiteralExts = new Set([".astro", ".css", ".html"]);` gates the apps:no-color-literals rule, so `.ts` is never checked even though the rule's own message says "Hardcoded color literal in apps". I counted the hole: 18 non-test TypeScript files under apps/demos/src/demos contain roughly 175 hex/rgba/hsla literals — galaxy-rotation/main.ts 22, eos-lab/mechanismViz.ts 21, em-spectrum/logic.ts 20, spectral-lines/main.ts 18, blackbody-radiation/main.ts 15, and so on. Some are defensible physical spectral data (em-spectrum/logic.ts:243-257 maps wavelength to colour, the same case DemoIllustration.astro is explicitly exempted for at :167) and some are token fallbacks (cluster-census/main.ts:310-314 `value("--cp-border", "#3a4358")`), but galaxy-rotation/main.ts:813 `ctx.fillStyle = "#fff2cf";` is a bare UI colour. Biome does not cover it either: biome.jsonc's includes are *.ts and *.mjs only, so *.astro is deliberately unlinted, and there is no colour rule.
findings.scenario: A demo's canvas rendering keeps hardcoded fills while the theme's tokens change — for a high-contrast pass (packages/theme/styles/high-contrast.css exists) or a light museum layer. Every token-based surface follows; the canvas does not, so plot ink stays at its old value and can drop below contrast threshold or vanish against a changed panel ground. Invariant 5 says the build forbids this; the build has never looked at a .ts file.
findings.fix: Add ".ts" to colorLiteralExts in scripts/validate-invariants.mjs, then triage the 175 hits into three buckets: delete the bare UI colours in favour of cssVar(); keep token fallbacks but require the pattern value("--cp-token", fallback) so the fallback is visibly secondary; and move genuine visualization colour ramps (em-spectrum, blackbody) into named, commented data tables with a per-file exemption marker, the way DemoIllustration.astro is exempted today.

findings.title: units.test.ts computes its expectations from the constants under test, and arcsecToRad is asserted only to be positive
findings.evidence: units.test.ts:28-35: `const rad = AstroUnits.arcsecToRad(1); expect(rad).toBeGreaterThan(0); expect(AstroUnits.radToArcsec(rad)).toBeCloseTo(arcsec, 12);` — sign plus round-trip, no value. I computed the independently known figure: pi/(180*3600) = 4.84813681e-6 rad per arcsec, and grepped the repo for 4.848 — nothing asserts it anywhere. A factor-of-two or arcmin/arcsec confusion in arcsecToRad passes both assertions as long as radToArcsec is wrong by the inverse factor. Same pattern at :7-10, where the expected km/s is `AstroConstants.LENGTH.KM_PER_AU / AstroConstants.TIME.YEAR_S`, built from the same two constants the function divides, and at :39-41, `expect(AstroUnits.evToErg(1)).toBeCloseTo(AstroConstants.PHOTON.ERG_PER_EV, 20)`, which compares a function to the constant it returns. sanity.test.ts contributes `it("runs unit tests", () => expect(1 + 1).toBe(2))` to the suite count.
findings.scenario: Someone edits AstroUnits.arcsecToRad to divide by 60 instead of 3600 and fixes radToArcsec to match. Both units tests pass. parallax-distance's diagram geometry (logic.ts:45 converts arcsec to radians) and telescope-resolution's diffraction limit are then wrong by 60x, and the only thing standing between that and a student is whichever per-demo test happens to pin a number in degrees.
findings.fix: Replace the self-referential expectations with literals and a cited source: assert arcsecToRad(1) toBeCloseTo 4.84813681e-6 at 1e-14, auPerYrToKmPerS(1) toBeCloseTo 4.74057 km/s, evToErg(1) toBeCloseTo 1.602176634e-12. Delete sanity.test.ts. Adopt the rule repo-wide: a conversion or constant test must compare against a number written down from an external source, never against the module's own arithmetic.

findings.title: The lint gate truncates its report to 10 diagnostics while the repo carries hundreds of standing warnings, and .astro is unlinted
findings.evidence: `"lint": "biome check --max-diagnostics=10 && ..."` while `"lint:biome"` — not in any gate — uses --max-diagnostics=2000. biome.jsonc records the standing warning load in its own comments: noNonNullAssertion "331 occurrences", noEmptyBlockStatements "16 empty blocks, mostly swallowed catches", plus noExplicitAny, noUnusedVariables and noUnusedFunctionParameters, all at `warn`. Because they are warnings they never fail the gate, and because the cap is 10 they are what the gate prints, so a newly introduced error (noUnusedImports and noTsIgnore are the only `error` rules) is overwhelmingly likely to be buried below the cut even though the exit code still fails. Separately biome.jsonc's files.includes is `apps/**/*.ts`, `packages/**/*.ts`, `scripts/**/*.mjs` — *.astro is excluded by design, which is why the two live Unicode violations I found in .astro files (FilterBar.astro:62, DemoCard.astro:73) had no linter looking at them either.
findings.scenario: A developer runs `corepack pnpm lint`, sees ten noNonNullAssertion warnings scroll past and a non-zero exit, assumes the pre-existing debt is what failed, and re-runs or moves on. The actual noUnusedImports error sits at diagnostic 47 and is never shown. Meanwhile the swallowed-catch class the config calls out as "the silent-failure class" can never block a build, including packages/physics/src/keplerSolver.ts:69 and stellarEosModel.ts:343, where a caught error turns into NaN or a silent fallback state inside a physics model.
findings.fix: In package.json, raise the gate to --max-diagnostics=2000 (or drop the flag) so the gate shows what it failed on, and add --error-on-warnings behind a separate `lint:strict` script to start ratcheting the 331+ warnings down. Promote noEmptyBlockStatements to error after auditing the catch sites — a swallowed exception in packages/physics is a correctness issue, not style. Add an .astro text scan (validate-math-formatting already walks these files; give it a sibling for the colour and link rules) since Biome cannot parse them.

findings.title: 96 waitForTimeout calls plus CI retries mean a timing-flaky test is reported green, and the suite's own infrastructure notes record both
findings.evidence: I counted 96 `waitForTimeout` calls across apps/site/tests/*.spec.ts against 771 test() declarations. layout-budget.spec.ts:162 and :232 each wait a flat 600 ms per demo before measuring geometry, for all 20 demos in both of its loops. playwright.config.ts:21 sets `retries: process.env.CI ? 1 : 0`, so a test that fails on timing and passes on retry is reported as passing. The config also uses the single fixed port 4321 with `reuseExistingServer: !process.env.CI`, which CLAUDE.md records as a live hazard ("Never run two Playwright runs at once: they share port 4321 and test-results/ is wiped at start") and which scripts/agent-hooks/ blocks a second concurrent run to work around. site-links.spec.ts:33 documents the measured consequence: its crawl "exceeded 30s and failed in two of three full runs while passing every time in isolation", attributed to eight workers contending on one preview server. layout-budget.spec.ts's own comments record two allowances raised purely because Linux CI fonts measure wider than macOS (eos-lab 520 to 600 px, stars-zams-hr 40 to 56 px), so the ratchet's thresholds are platform-coupled.
findings.scenario: A render path gets slower than 600 ms on the CI runner under eight-worker contention. layout-budget measures before the layout settles, reports readouts below the fold, fails, is retried, happens to win the race, and reports green. The ratchet's whole value — detecting drift — is lost in the noise, and the signal that something got slower is discarded rather than recorded.
findings.fix: Replace the flat waits with condition-based waiting: have each demo set a data attribute (data-rendered, or the existing data-scroll that initScrollAffordance already publishes) once its first layout pass completes, and await that instead of 600 ms. Set retries: 0 for the geometry and layout specs so a timing failure is a failure. Make the port configurable per run (PLAYWRIGHT_PORT already exists in the config) so two runs cannot collide, rather than relying on a hook to block the second one.

findings.title: Moon orbit endpoints are derived from angular-size extremes, implying a = 380,824 km and e = 0.0667
findings.evidence: `ORBIT_MIN_ANGULAR_SIZE_DEG: 0.49, ORBIT_MAX_ANGULAR_SIZE_DEG: 0.56` feed `moonOrbitPeigeeApogeeKm` (angularSizeModel.ts:203-212). Recomputed: perigee = 3474/(2 tan(0.28 deg)) = 355,436 km; apogee = 3474/(2 tan(0.245 deg)) = 406,213 km. Their midpoint is 380,824 km, but `DISTANCE_TODAY_KM` is 384,400 km — the interpolation's centre is 3,576 km (0.93%) short of the semi-major axis it should equal. Since `moonDistanceAtOrbitAngleDeg` computes r = a_mid - A cos(angle), the implied orbit has a = 380,824 km and e = A/a = 25,389/380,824 = 0.0667, against the Moon's e = 0.0549 (21% high). This is why the model's inverse puts "Moon (Today)" at 98.1 deg instead of 90 deg (the code comment at main.ts:285 records the 98 deg without explaining it). The two values are also *extreme* perigee/apogee (which occur in different months), not the mean perigee 363,300 km / apogee 405,500 km that average to 384,400 km.
findings.scenario: A student in Station Mode adds the "Moon perigee/apogee" row set and records perigee = 355,436 km, labelled simply "Perigee"; they compute (perigee + apogee)/2 = 380,824 km and find it disagrees with the 384,400 km the same demo calls the Moon's distance. Asked why "Today" sits at 98 deg rather than halfway round the orbit, neither the UI nor the model notes can answer.
findings.fix: Invert the ownership: make `a = AstroConstants.MOON.DISTANCE_TODAY_KM` and `e` the stored constants (e = 0.0549), derive perigee = a(1-e) = 363,300 km and apogee = a(1+e) = 405,500 km, and label the orbit slider as eccentric anomaly E (which is what r = a(1 - e cos E) already makes it). Keep 0.490/0.560 deg only as the separately labelled extreme apparent sizes. Add a model test asserting (perigee + apogee)/2 == DISTANCE_TODAY_KM to within 1 km — the current test (angularSizeModel.test.ts:65-67) only checks perigee > 350000 and apogee < 420000, which this defect satisfies.

findings.title: The "thumb at arm's length" rule is stated as 2 deg but the demo's own thumb preset computes 1.64 deg
findings.evidence: Preset `thumb`: `diameter: 0.00002` km (2 cm), `distance: 0.0007` km (70 cm), `description: "Thumb at arm's length ≈ 2°"`. Recomputed: theta = 2 atan(0.00002/(2 x 0.0007)) = 1.6369 deg, displayed by `formatAngleDisplay` as "1.64 deg". The sidebar callout (index.html:73) states "Thumb at arm's length ≈ 2°". The discrepancy is 22%. The cause is the 70-cm arm: a 2-cm thumb needs d = 0.0573 km... i.e. 57.3 cm to give exactly 2.00 deg, and 60 cm gives 1.91 deg. (The same 70 cm is used for the `quarter` preset.)
findings.scenario: A student reads the sidebar tip "Thumb at arm's length ≈ 2°", selects "Your thumb" to check it, and the demo answers 1.64 deg. The demo contradicts the mnemonic it is teaching, and the student cannot tell which number is wrong.
findings.fix: Set the thumb preset's distance to 0.0006 km (60 cm, a realistic arm's length) giving 1.91 deg, and change the callout and description to "$\approx 2^{\circ}$ (about $1.9^{\circ}$ here)" so the stated rule and the computed number agree. Rewrite the `≈ 2°` in the description as ASCII or LaTeX, since it is the kind of string that leaks into UI.

findings.title: formatDiameterAuto skips parsecs, so the Pleiades' 4 pc diameter reads "3.999 x 10^-3 kpc"
findings.evidence: The ladder is cm -> m -> km -> AU -> kpc -> Mpc (the doc comment at line 110 admits the omission). With sigFigs = 4 as used by `render()` (main.ts:769), I reproduced the readouts: Pleiades diameter 1.234e14 km -> `3.999 x 10^-3 kpc` (true 4.00 pc); Orion Nebula 2.469e14 km -> `8.001 x 10^-3 kpc` (true 8.00 pc). `formatDistanceAuto` does have a pc rung (logic.ts:97), so distance and diameter use different ladders for the same physical dimension. The logic tests (logic.test.ts:226-255) check cm, m, km, kpc and Mpc and never exercise the AU or pc range, so the gap has no coverage.
findings.scenario: A student selects the Pleiades to compare a star cluster with a galaxy. The diameter readout says 3.999 x 10^-3 kpc. Nobody writes a 4-parsec cluster that way, and the student cannot recognise the familiar scale or compare it with the parsec distances the very next readout shows.
findings.fix: Insert a pc rung in `formatDiameterAuto` matching `formatDistanceAuto`: after the AU branch, `if (abs < 1000 * KM_PER_PC) return { text: formatSci(km / KM_PER_PC, sigFigs), unit: "pc" };`. Update the doc comment and add tests for a 4-pc and a 0.3-pc diameter.

findings.title: Unit tests assert the Unicode output verbatim, pinning the contract violation instead of catching it
findings.evidence: `expect(formatSci(1.5e8, 3)).toBe("1.50 × 10⁸")` (line 161), `expect(formatSci(0.00012, 3)).toBe("1.20 × 10⁻⁴")` (164), `expect(formatSci(6779, 3)).toBe("6.78 × 10³")` (177), `expect(formatSci(-1.5e8, 3)).toBe("-1.50 × 10⁸")` (181), plus the whole `toSuperscript` block (130-148) asserting every Unicode superscript digit. The demo's own design-contracts.test.ts has no KaTeX/Unicode assertion at all, and its one architecture test (line 204) only checks that main.ts does not declare `function angularDiameter` — it passes with `FULL_MOON_DEG = 0.533` hardcoded two lines away.
findings.scenario: Anyone converting formatSci to KaTeX, as the project's math invariant requires, will see five tests go red and may conclude the Unicode output is the intended contract and revert.
