The test suite actively defends the defect, which is the failure mode recorded in this project's memory ("five green tests that pinned the bug instead of catching it").
findings.fix: When formatSci is converted to LaTeX, rewrite these assertions to expect `1.50 \times 10^{8}` and delete the `toSuperscript` tests along with the function. Add a design-contract assertion to this demo that index.html, main.ts and logic.ts contain no `&#x`/`\u` escape in the ranges the math validator forbids — the guard the build-level validator structurally cannot provide.

findings.title: Model tests are round-trip self-consistency and would pass with the formula wrong
findings.evidence: Line 42 `expect(Math.abs(backThetaDeg - thetaDeg)).toBeLessThan(1e-10)` round-trips angularDiameterDeg against its own inverse; line 86 round-trips the orbit angle; line 103 round-trips the recession time. All three pass identically if the forward law is theta = 2 atan(D/d) or theta = atan(D/d), because the inverse is derived from the same expression. Only two of the 18 presets are checked against an external value: Sun 0.53313 +/- 0.005 (line 20) and Moon 0.5178 +/- 0.01 (line 29). Nothing tests the Sky View constant, the FOV mapping, the stage radius mapping, or the 16 remaining presets' angular sizes against published values.
findings.scenario: A refactor that drops the factor of 2 (theta = atan(D/(2d))) halves every angle. The Sun test fails, but a refactor touching only the orbit or recession helpers — or the rendering constants, which have no tests at all — is validated entirely by round-trips that cannot detect a wrong law. This is how the 0.533 Sky View constant reached production with a full green suite and a physics review declaring no errors.
findings.fix: Add an independent-value table test: for every preset, assert theta against a hand-computed constant in the test file (Sun 0.53313, Moon 0.51780, Venus 60.3 arcsec, Mars 25.6 arcsec, LMC 10.74 deg, SMC 5.21 deg, M42 66.8 arcmin, ISS 53.5 arcsec), with the source for each in a comment. Add one asymmetric non-round case (e.g. D = 1234 km, d = 56789 km -> theta = 1.2449 deg) so a dropped factor of 2 or a radian/degree slip cannot round-trip away. Add a test that the demo's Sky View reference constant equals the Moon preset's theta.

findings.title: angularDiameterDeg returns a hard 180 deg for a NaN distance, hiding the domain error
findings.evidence: `if (!Number.isFinite(distanceKm) || distanceKm <= 0) return 180;` — a non-finite input and a zero/negative input are collapsed into one answer, 180 deg, a physically meaningful value. Traced by hand: `angularDiameterDeg({ diameterKm: 3474, distanceKm: NaN })` returns 180, which `render()` passes to `formatAngleInUnit` ( -> "180.0 deg"), to `renderStage` (clamped radius 130, `--wide` class) and to `renderSkyView` (fov clamped to 60, objR 138) — a fully rendered, confident, wrong page. The model test at line 11 pins `distanceKm: 0 -> 180` but no test covers NaN. By contrast `distanceForAngularDiameterDeg` correctly returns `Number.NaN` for a bad diameter (line 28).
findings.scenario: Any future caller that can produce NaN — a parsed query parameter, an imported state payload, a new preset with a missing field — gets a page showing "180.0 deg" and a hemisphere-filling object instead of the em-dash the formatters already know how to display. The NaN guard in `formatAngleDisplay` (logic.ts:34) is dead code because the model never emits NaN.
findings.fix: Split the guard: `if (!Number.isFinite(distanceKm)) return Number.NaN;` then `if (distanceKm <= 0) return 180;`, matching the sibling function's convention. The display layer already renders NaN as an em-dash. Add a test asserting NaN in -> NaN out.

findings.title: "Exact geometry" overstates 2 arctan(D/2d), which is exact for a flat disk and not for the spheres every preset uses
findings.evidence: Model notes tab: "Exact geometry: $$\theta = 2\tan^{-1}\left(\frac{D}{2d}\right)$$", echoed by angular-size.md:27 ("the exact geometric relation") and the model doc comment (angularSizeModel.ts:15). For a sphere of diameter D whose centre is at distance d, the tangent lines give theta = 2 arcsin(D/(2d)), not 2 arctan. The arctan form is exact for a flat disk facing the observer. Magnitudes: at the Sun's D/(2d) = 4.652e-3 the two differ by 1.4e-7 deg (negligible); at the slider extremes (1-cm object at 0.1 m, D/(2d) = 0.05) arcsin gives 5.7345 deg against arctan's 5.7249 deg, a 0.17% difference.
findings.scenario: A student who has met the arcsin form in a textbook, or an instructor checking the model notes, finds the demo asserting that the arctan form is "exact" for the Sun, the Moon and the planets — all spheres. The numerical consequence is invisible at every preset, but the claim of exactness is wrong, and "exact" is the word the demo uses to distinguish this from the small-angle approximation it also shows.
findings.fix: In the Model notes tab and in angular-size.md:27 say "exact for a disk of diameter $D$ facing the observer; for a sphere the tangent construction gives $\theta = 2\sin^{-1}(D/2d)$, which differs by less than $0.2\%$ anywhere in this demo's range." Mirror the same note in the angularSizeModel.ts doc comment. No code change needed.

findings.title: Panel translucency contract is violated and its contract test was weakened from the golden reference to let it pass
findings.evidence: Design-system invariant 4 requires demo-specific panels to use var(--cp-instr-panel-bg) plus backdrop-filter: blur(8px). I grepped the demo's style.css: it contains no --cp-instr-panel-bg and no backdrop-filter anywhere; its panels use color-mix(in srgb, var(--cp-bg1) 94%, transparent) (style.css:38, 72, 348, 388) and 97% (style.css:161, 239), i.e. 94-97% opaque, so the starfield behind them is effectively invisible. The golden reference asserts the contract literally - moon-phases/design-contracts.test.ts:106 requires /\.viz-panel[\s\S]*?background:\s*var\(--cp-instr-panel-bg\)/ and :109 requires a backdrop-filter - and moon-phases/style.css:11,17-18 satisfies it. binary-orbits' 'Panel translucency' describe block replaced both with weaker checks: 'canvas background uses token-based radial-gradient' and a negative 'CSS does not override panel backgrounds with opaque colors' (design-contracts.test.ts:200-206), which a 97%-opaque color-mix passes.
findings.scenario: The instrument layer's starfield is drawn and then hidden behind near-opaque panels, so the demo reads as museum-layer chrome rather than an instrument and looks inconsistent next to moon-phases. The contract test reports green, so the migration checklist records the demo as compliant and the drift is never surfaced.
findings.fix: In apps/demos/src/demos/binary-orbits/style.css replace the color-mix(var(--cp-bg1) 94%/97%, transparent) panel backgrounds with var(--cp-instr-panel-bg) (or --cp-instr-panel-bg-muted for nested cards) and add backdrop-filter: blur(8px) with the -webkit- prefix, exactly as moon-phases/style.css:11-18 does. Then restore the two real assertions from moon-phases/design-contracts.test.ts:106-111 in place of the weakened pair, targeting .rv-panel, .control-group, .cp-live-insight and .integrity-panel.

findings.title: K means both RV semi-amplitude and kinetic energy in the same instrument, including as adjacent bar labels
findings.evidence: The readouts panel uses K for the spectroscopic semi-amplitude - 'RV semi-amplitude of $M_1$ ($K_1$)' and '($K_2$)' (index.html:264, 268) - and, in the same panel, for kinetic energy: 'Kinetic energy of $M_1$ ($K_1$)' and 'Kinetic energy of $M_2$ ($K_2$)' (index.html:294, 298) plus 'Total kinetic energy ($K$)' (index.html:302). drawEnergyView labels its bars 'K1', 'K2', 'K' (main.ts:961-963) with no qualifier, and the export emits both 'RV semi-amplitude K1 (km/s)' and 'Kinetic energy K1 (Msun AU^2/yr^2)' (main.ts:2287, 2293). The virial copy '2K + U' (index.html:313, main.ts:1017) uses the energy sense while the spectroscopy panel's $K_1/K_2 = M_2/M_1 = q$ (index.html:427) uses the amplitude sense. The project's symbol-discipline rule is written for D and d, but the same hazard applies: K is the standard symbol for the RV semi-amplitude in binary-star spectroscopy.
findings.scenario: A student in the Energy view reads 'K1 = 0.85' off a bar, carries it to the RV view's 'K1 / K2 = q' relation, and computes a mass ratio from kinetic energies. Units would catch them if the bars carried units, but the bar labels do not (and are currently off-canvas anyway), and the export puts both meanings of K1 in one list.
findings.fix: Rename the energy quantities to T (or E_kin) throughout: index.html:294-302 labels, main.ts:961-963 bar labels, main.ts:1615-1617 readout wiring, main.ts:2293-2295 export names, the virial copy to 2T + U, and the energyScaleCueForControl text in logic.ts:503-517 where it refers to |E|. Keep K reserved for the RV semi-amplitude.

findings.title: The K1 amplitude bracket is drawn at a phase where the primary RV curve is at 12.5 percent of its peak
findings.evidence: annotateAmplitude draws a bracket from the zero line to yFromVelocity(amplitude) at a fixed x, and it is called as annotateAmplitude("K1", model.k1KmPerS, ..., margin.left + plotW * 0.74) and annotateAmplitude("K2", ..., margin.left + plotW * 0.88) (main.ts:914-917). xFromPhaseCycle maps x = margin.left + (phaseCycle/2)*plotW (main.ts:752), so x-fraction 0.74 is phaseCycle 1.48, i.e. phase 9.299 rad = 3.016 rad mod 2pi, where sin = 0.1253: the primary curve is at 0.125*K1 there, not at its peak (which falls at x-fractions 0.125 and 0.625). The K2 bracket at 0.88 lands at phase 4.775 rad where sin = -0.998, so rv2 = +0.998*K2 - that one does coincide with the secondary's peak, which makes the mismatch look like an oversight rather than a convention.
findings.scenario: A student looking at the RV view sees a bracket labelled K1 spanning from the zero line to a height no part of the primary curve reaches at that x, while the K2 bracket sits neatly on the secondary's crest. The visual lesson 'K is the half-amplitude you read at the extremum' is undermined for the primary, and during the challenge students are told to click near the extrema while the annotation points somewhere else.
findings.fix: Place each bracket at its own curve's extremum instead of a hardcoded x. Compute the peak phase per curve (phaseCycle 1.25 for the primary where rv1 = +K1, phaseCycle 1.75 for the secondary where rv2 = +K2 with the current sign convention) and pass xFromPhaseCycle of that, nudging the two labels apart horizontally only for legibility.

findings.title: Three places assert the shared-period invariant without computing anything, including a readout labelled 'check'
findings.evidence: evaluateInvariants' sharedPeriod entry sets lhs: model.periodYr, rhs: model.periodYr and isTrue: nearEqual(model.periodYr, model.periodYr) (logic.ts:376-381) - a value compared with itself, true for any finite period. updateReadouts hardcodes periodSharedCue.textContent = "P1 = P2 (shared period)" (main.ts:1597), a constant string behind the label 'Shared-period check' (index.html:239-242). updateDebugPanel's 'P1 - P2' row is fed delta: 0 literally (main.ts:1276-1281) behind the label $P_1 - P_2$ (index.html:365). The e2e test pins the constant string rather than any computation: 'shared-period cue states P1 equals P2' asserts #periodSharedCue contains 'P1 = P2' (spec.ts:441-443).
findings.scenario: A student working the 'What must be true?' discrimination task selects P1 = P2, and the panel confirms it - but the confirmation is self-referential. If orbitalPeriodYrFromAuSolar were wrong (a bad exponent, say), all three displays would still report the invariant as verified, and the only test would still pass. The demo teaches that these panels are live verifications ('These live checks should stay true as you drag controls', index.html:308).
findings.fix: Either compute the two periods independently and compare them - derive P1 = 2*pi*a1/v1 and P2 = 2*pi*a2/v2 from the model's own a1, a2, v1, v2 and feed those as lhs/rhs to the sharedPeriod invariant, the readout and the debug row (that is a real, non-trivial consistency check) - or relabel all three so they read as a stated property rather than a check. Add an assertion that the sharedPeriod invariant reports false when handed a mutated model with mismatched periods.

findings.title: System velocity readout is hardcoded to 0.0 km/s with no control, in the panel and in the export
findings.evidence: index.html:287-290 renders a readout 'System velocity ($v_{\rm sys}$)' with a km/s unit span, and the only writer is vsysValue.textContent = formatNumber(0, 1) (main.ts:1614). The export carries it too: { name: "System velocity v_sys (km/s)", value: formatNumber(0, 1) } (main.ts:2292). There is no control for it anywhere in index.html, and BinaryOrbitState (logic.ts:132-141) has no field for it. The design-contracts test asserts the element merely exists (design-contracts.test.ts:177, expect(html).toContain('id="vsysValue"')).
findings.scenario: A student sees a readout that never moves and cannot tell whether v_sys is a model output pinned by the barycentric frame or a control they have failed to find. It also implies the demo models a systemic velocity offset - the thing that in real spectroscopy you must fit out before measuring K - when it does not, so the one observable most responsible for RV-curve bookkeeping is present as decoration.
findings.fix: Either make it real - add a 'System velocity' slider in km/s, add vsysKmPerS to BinarySystemState, and offset both RV curves and the Doppler shift by it, which would also make the RV view's zero line pedagogically meaningful - or delete the readout from index.html:287-290, the write at main.ts:1614, the export row at main.ts:2292 and the contract assertion at design-contracts.test.ts:177. Making it real is the higher-value option and pairs naturally with the spectrum-view fix.

findings.title: Turning off Auto-fit pushes the system off-canvas above about 5 AU, and the unit test pins that behaviour
findings.evidence: computeTargetViewScale returns the constant FIXED_VIEW_SCALE_AU_PER_PX when autoScale is false (logic.ts:524), and that constant is 1/84 (logic.ts:34), i.e. 84 px per AU, with no clamping against the canvas size. computeOrbitScreenRadii then returns r1Au/viewScale (logic.ts:557-560). The separation slider runs to 100 AU (logic.ts:21), so at a = 100 AU with q = 1 the orbit radii are 50 * 84 = 4200 px on a canvas whose min dimension is clamp(440px, 72svh, 860px) (style.css:142) - both stars and both orbit circles are drawn thousands of pixels outside the visible area, leaving only the barycenter dot and the sightline. Even a = 10 AU with q = 1 gives a 420 px radius, already off a 520 px canvas. The unit test 'uses a constant fixed-view scale so screen radii grow monotonically with separation' (logic.test.ts:293-313) asserts only farRadius.r1Px > nearRadius.r1Px at r up to 15 AU (1260 px on a declared 600 px canvas) and never that anything stays on screen.
findings.scenario: A student unchecks 'Auto-fit view' - a visible, documented toggle - at any separation past the slider's lower third and the orbit view goes blank except for a dot and a dashed line, with no empty state, no off-screen indicator and no hint to re-enable auto-fit. They reasonably conclude the demo crashed.
findings.fix: Keep the fixed scale as a pedagogical 'same scale across systems' mode but make it honest: clamp the fixed branch of computeTargetViewScale so the larger orbit stays inside the canvas, and when the clamp bites draw an on-canvas note plus an edge marker showing the direction of the off-screen body. Then strengthen the test to assert max(r1Px, r2Px) <= 0.5 * canvasMinDimensionPx across the full separation range rather than only monotonicity.

findings.title: Dead code: orphaned JSDoc block ends logic.ts and two computed locals in drawEnergyView are never read
findings.evidence: logic.ts is 605 lines and the file ends at line 605 with a closing */ of a JSDoc block that documents a function that no longer exists: lines 600-605 read 'Logarithmic visual scaling factor for orbit rendering. / Returns a smooth, bounded multiplier in [0.68, 1.22], decreasing as separation increases from min to max.' - there is no declaration after it (bodyPositions closes at line 598). Nothing in the file or in main.ts produces a multiplier in [0.68, 1.22]; the camera now uses computeTargetViewScale/stepViewScale. In main.ts, drawEnergyView computes baselineY = margin.top + (maxMagnitude/(2*maxMagnitude))*plotH (main.ts:958) and, inside the bar loop, const y = yFromEnergy(Math.max(0, bar.value)) (main.ts:995); neither is referenced again.
findings.scenario: A maintainer reading logic.ts believes a log visual-scaling helper is still part of the camera contract and either reimplements it or wires it back in alongside computeTargetViewScale, reintroducing the two-owners problem the camera refactor removed. The stale doc is also the kind of thing that makes an otherwise accurate file untrustworthy.
findings.fix: Delete logic.ts:600-605 and the two unused locals at main.ts:958 and main.ts:995 (the latter in the same edit as the bar-label y fix). If any of the three is meant to come back, leave a one-line TODO naming the owner instead of an orphaned contract.

findings.title: Demo default is 5778 K while the model's solar reference is 5772 K, so the Sun reads L/L_sun = 1.004 on first load
findings.evidence: main.ts:89-95 `const state = { temperatureK: 5778, ... }`; blackbodyRadiationModel.ts:16 `TSunK: 5772`; the "Sun" preset is `data-temp-k="5772"` (index.html:58) and Station Mode's step text and sequence rows also use 5772 (main.ts:582, 616). Recomputed: (5778/5772)^4 = 1.004164, and formatNumber(1.004164, 3) = "1.004". So the demo opens showing the Sun at 1.004 solar, and clicking the Sun preset changes the number to 1.000 for no reason the reader can see. (The physics test at blackbodyRadiationModel.test.ts:32 independently uses 5778, a third copy of the solar temperature.)
findings.scenario: A student opens the demo, reads 5778 K and L/L_sun = 1.004 as the Sun's own values, then clicks the "Sun" preset and watches the number drop to 1.000 - a 0.4% change with no visible cause, which looks like a bug in the demo rather than a 6 K difference between the effective temperature and the reference.
findings.fix: Set `temperatureK: BlackbodyRadiationModel.CONSTANTS.TSunK` at apps/demos/src/demos/blackbody-radiation/main.ts:93 so the default, the preset and the ratio denominator are one value, and change the 5778 in packages/physics/src/blackbodyRadiationModel.test.ts:32 to the same constant. Whether the shared solar value should be 5772 K (the IAU nominal effective temperature) or 5778 K is Anna's call to confirm, but it must be one number in one place.

findings.title: Thirteen hardcoded rgba() literals in main.ts sit outside the no-color-literals invariant, which scans only .astro/.css/.html
findings.evidence: main.ts has 13 `rgba(` literals: the gradient endpoints at lines 252 and 271 (`"rgba(20, 0, 40, 0.12)"`, `"rgba(15, 0, 0, 0.06)"`), the ten spectral stops at lines 255-264, and the non-visible strip fill at line 379 (`"rgba(20, 10, 20, 0.6)"`). scripts/validate-invariants.mjs:104 defines `const colorLiteralExts = new Set([".astro", ".css", ".html"])` and the `apps:no-color-literals` check at lines 154 and 315 is gated on that set, so `.ts` is never scanned. The demo's own contract test (design-contracts.test.ts:114-133) reads only style.css. The script does carry a deliberate carve-out for spectral data colours (lines 155-157, DemoIllustration.astro), so the spectral stops are arguably legitimate - but lines 252, 271 and 379 are dark UI overlays, not spectral data, and the theme ships a light layer (packages/theme/styles/layer-paper.css:5 `[data-theme="paper"]`).
findings.scenario: The demo is viewed under `data-theme="paper"`: the UV/IR gradient ends and the non-visible band strip stay near-black dark overlays baked into main.ts, so the plot background and the EM band render as dark smears on a light page, and no gate reports it because the invariant cannot see .ts files.
findings.fix: Add `".ts"` to `colorLiteralExts` in scripts/validate-invariants.mjs:104 with an explicit, commented allowlist for spectral-data colours (the same reasoning as the DemoIllustration carve-out), then move the three non-spectral overlays at apps/demos/src/demos/blackbody-radiation/main.ts:252, 271 and 379 onto tokens read through the existing `cssVar()` helper (main.ts:112-118) so they follow the theme. Extend design-contracts.test.ts:114-133 to read main.ts as well as style.css.

findings.title: The model keeps its own 4-significant-figure copies of c, h and k instead of AstroConstants.PHOTON; flagged in the 2026-02-07 review and not fixed
findings.evidence: blackbodyRadiationModel.ts:5-7 `cCmPerS: 2.998e10, hErgS: 6.626e-27, kErgPerK: 1.381e-16`, while packages/physics/src/astroConstants.ts:61-68 defines `PHOTON.C_CM_PER_S: 2.99792458e10` and `PHOTON.H_ERG_S: 6.62607015e-27` with a comment stating they are "Kept here so demos/models share a single source of truth." I measured the resulting spread by recomputing B_lambda both ways: the model is high by 2.03e-3 at (300 nm, 5772 K), 1.02e-3 at (1200 nm, 3000 K), 2.07e-3 at (50 nm, 34000 K) and 2.57e-3 at (0.05 cm, 2.725 K) - up to 0.26%, harmless numerically but a live divergence. docs/reviews/blackbody-radiation.md:66 logged this on 2026-02-07 as issue 2; the constants are unchanged.
findings.scenario: A student compares this demo's spectral radiance against the em-spectrum or spectral-lines demos, which draw from AstroConstants, and gets a 0.1-0.26% mismatch on the same physical quantity with no stated reason; more importantly, a future constants update to astroConstants.ts silently leaves this model behind.
findings.fix: In packages/physics/src/blackbodyRadiationModel.ts, import AstroConstants and define `cCmPerS: AstroConstants.PHOTON.C_CM_PER_S`, `hErgS: AstroConstants.PHOTON.H_ERG_S`, adding K_ERG_PER_K, SIGMA_ERG_PER_S_CM2_K4 and WIEN_CM_K to AstroConstants.PHOTON if they are not there yet so all four live in one place. Because this shifts every plotted radiance by up to 0.26%, propose the exact constant set to Anna before landing it.

findings.title: Canvas redraw is wired to a click on #tab-explore, so keyboard tab navigation can leave a 1x1 stretched canvas; four demos repeat the same fork
findings.evidence: main.ts:552-554 `tabExploreEl?.addEventListener("click", () => window.requestAnimationFrame(() => render()))`. packages/runtime/src/tabs.ts drives keyboard tab switching through its own `onKeydown` handler (ArrowLeft/Right/Home/End -> `activateTab` then `.focus()`); focusing an element fires no click, so keyboard tab changes never reach that listener. Traced consequence: while the Explore panel is `hidden`, `resizeCanvasToCssPixels` (main.ts:97-110) reads a 0x0 bounding box and sets `canvas.width = Math.max(1, ...) = 1`, destroying the bitmap; the CSS at style.css:111-116 then stretches that 1-pixel bitmap to the full `width: 100%` box. The same `#tab-explore` click fork appears in eos-lab/main.ts:1422, hydrostatic-equilibrium-explorer/main.ts:915 and spectral-lines/main.ts:99, while binary-orbits and conservation-laws use ResizeObserver instead - so there is a correct shared pattern and this is a four-way divergence from it.
findings.scenario: A keyboard-only student arrows to the Understand tab, rotates their tablet or resizes the window (the resize listener at main.ts:551 fires render() while the panel is hidden, setting the canvas to 1x1), then arrows back to Explore. No click is dispatched, render() never runs, and the spectrum appears as a single smeared column of pixels until they touch another control.
findings.fix: Replace the click listener at apps/demos/src/demos/blackbody-radiation/main.ts:552-554 with a ResizeObserver on #spectrumCanvas that calls render() whenever its box becomes non-zero (the pattern already in binary-orbits/main.ts and conservation-laws/main.ts), and guard resizeCanvasToCssPixels (main.ts:97) to return early rather than resize when the measured rect is 0x0. Better still, have packages/runtime/src/tabs.ts dispatch a `cp:tab-activated` CustomEvent from activateTab so all five demos drop their per-demo forks.

findings.title: Inline mass-temperature relation tints the histogram, disagreeing with the HR dot colours it is meant to match at the low-mass end
findings.evidence: main.ts:908-910 `function massToApproxTemperatureK(massMsun: number) { return 5772 * massMsun ** 0.55; }`, used at line 864 to colour every bar, with the stated purpose at line 906 "so the mass axis and the HR diagram share a colour language". I evaluated both routes through the demo's own `temperatureToRgb`: at 0.1 Msun the bar uses T = 1627 K -> rgb(255,116,0) while the HR dot uses the Tout value 2812 K -> rgb(255,171,96); at 0.2 Msun, 2382 K -> rgb(255,154,59) versus 3299 K -> rgb(255,187,129). At 100 Msun the relation gives 72,665 K, clipped by temperatureToRgb's 40,000 K ceiling, against the Tout value of 46,692 K. The two agree only near 0.5-1 Msun. Every star's real temperatureK is already on the ClusterStar objects the function is iterating past.
findings.scenario: The first two or three histogram bins are the tallest bars on the plot and the ones a student is told to read. They are drawn a visibly deeper orange than the same stars' dots on the HR diagram, so the colour cue the caption promises links the two panels actively mismatches where the population is densest -- and the relation is a fitted equation living in demo code, which the architecture invariant forbids.
findings.fix: Delete `massToApproxTemperatureK` from apps/demos/src/demos/cluster-census/main.ts and tint each bar from the stars actually in it: carry the median `temperatureK` of the binned stars (ignoring remnants) alongside the counts from `countIntoBins`, or fall back to `ZamsTout1996Model.effectiveTemperatureKFromMassMetallicity({ massMsun: centresMsun[i], metallicityZ: 0.02 })`. No new physics either way.

findings.title: starClusterModel duplicates postMainSequenceTrack's end-of-life test, making its white-dwarf branch unreachable from clusters
findings.evidence: starClusterModel.ts:190 `const isRemnant = ageMyr >= totalLifetimeMyr(massMsun);` and `totalLifetimeMyr` (stellarLifetimeModel.ts:307-309) returns `timeToGiantBranchMyr(massMsun) * (1 + POST_BGB_FRACTION)` -- numerically identical to the `end` computed inside postMainSequenceTrack (line 361). So the branch at lines 363-368, which returns a cooling white-dwarf point for progenitors below 8 Msun, can never be reached through sampleStarCluster: line 195 takes the remnant path first and emits luminosityLsun = 0, temperatureK = 0, stellarRadiusRsun = 0. The branch is live for the other consumer, hrInferencePopulationModel.ts:261, which is why stars-zams-hr shows a white-dwarf cooling sequence and cluster-census does not. Two demos built on the same module disagree about whether an old cluster has white dwarfs.
findings.scenario: An instructor shows stars-zams-hr (white-dwarf sequence at bottom left, one of the three structures a CMD is read for) and then cluster-census at 12 Gyr (no white dwarfs, grey dots in the spatial panel whose star card nonetheless says phase "white dwarf"). The in-demo copy at index.html:431 is honest about this, but the duplicated lifetime test is what forces the inconsistency, and any future fix has to be made in two places.
findings.fix: In packages/physics/src/starClusterModel.ts, drop the `isRemnant` pre-check and let postMainSequenceTrack own the stage decision: call it first, and treat a null return past t_MS as "remnant with no photosphere" (neutron star or black hole). That makes `totalLifetimeMyr` a single owner, lets the white-dwarf branch reach cluster-census, and removes the need to keep the two expressions in step. Changing what an old cluster's HR diagram shows is a scientific choice, so propose it before landing.

findings.title: main.ts holds ten untested pure functions that the architecture invariant puts in logic.ts, and nothing constrains the HR axis orientation
findings.evidence: .agents/references/invariants.md:45 states "Pure UI logic goes in each demo's logic.ts (tested); main.ts is thin DOM wiring." main.ts is 1,491 lines against logic.ts's 451, and the following DOM-free pure functions live in main.ts and therefore have no unit test: `measuredAxisPadLeft` (332), `sceneSizePx` (409), `clusterPlotRadiusPc` (446), `niceScaleLength` (459), `hrRanges` (528), `padRange` (561), `isPlottable` (572), `decadeTicks` (581), `massToApproxTemperatureK` (908), `starTypeLabel` (1005), `phaseLabel` (1021). logic.test.ts:257-259 does assert that projectToPixels's `invert` flag maps min to pixelHigh, but nothing asserts that drawHrDiagram passes invert=true for temperature (line 632) and false for luminosity (line 648): swapping those two arguments would mirror the HR diagram and leave every unit test, every design-contract test and every e2e case green -- cluster-census.spec.ts's only axis assertion is that KaTeX rendered the titles (line 320-324).
findings.scenario: A refactor flips the temperature axis so cool stars sit on the left. Every gate passes. Students read a mirrored HR diagram, and the panel hint "same stars, hotter to the left" (index.html:235) becomes false with nothing to catch it. More broadly, `hrRanges`/`padRange`/`decadeTicks` decide what the plot shows and are unreachable from any test.
findings.fix: Move the eleven functions listed above from apps/demos/src/demos/cluster-census/main.ts into logic.ts and add unit tests (hrRanges on an empty population, padRange's minimum-span path, niceScaleLength across decades). Then add one e2e assertion of orientation: at a known draw, read the overlay or a data- attribute carrying the pixel x of the hottest and coolest plotted stars and assert hot < cool.

findings.title: Colour literals in demo TypeScript escape the no-color-literals gate, and the remnant grey is duplicated
findings.evidence: scripts/validate-invariants.mjs:104 `const colorLiteralExts = new Set([".astro", ".css", ".html"]);` -- the `apps:no-color-literals` rule (lines 315-324) never looks at .ts. cluster-census draws its entire cluster panel, HR diagram and histogram from TypeScript, so the gate has no coverage of this demo's actual colours. Concrete literals: main.ts:506 `ctx.fillStyle = "rgba(10, 14, 24, 0.65)"` (a panel plate that should be `--cp-instr-panel-bg`); main.ts:428 `rgb: remnant ? [150, 158, 176]` and main.ts:1046 `"rgba(150, 158, 176, 0.7)"` (the same remnant grey written twice, in two formats); main.ts:310-314 five hex fallbacks in `readPalette` ("#3a4358", "#e8edf7", "#93a0b8", "#7fd4e8", "#f2b544"). CLAUDE.md's design-system section states "no hardcoded color values in demo code". The per-demo contract test at design-contracts.test.ts:199-207 checks only style.css.
findings.scenario: A token change to --cp-instr-panel-bg or the remnant swatch updates the CSS and the HTML legend swatch but not the canvas, so the scale-bar plate and the remnant dots drift away from the legend that is supposed to explain them -- and because the remnant grey exists in two places, half of it moves when someone fixes one.
findings.fix: Widen `colorLiteralExts` in scripts/validate-invariants.mjs:104 to include ".ts", then in apps/demos/src/demos/cluster-census/main.ts route the three literals through `readPalette` by adding `panelPlate` (var(--cp-instr-panel-bg)) and `remnant` entries, and introduce the remnant colour as a token in packages/theme/styles/tokens.css so the HTML swatch and the canvas read the same value. Expect the widened gate to surface literals in sibling demos; land it as its own change.

findings.title: A 140-character census sentence is re-announced on every slider input event, with no coalescing
findings.evidence: `setLiveRegionText` (liveRegion.ts:1-18) writes textContent immediately with no debounce or rAF coalescing on the changed-text path. main.ts:950-961 calls it from `renderReadouts`, which `update()` (1205) calls on every `input` event from countSlider (1219), slopeSlider (1224), ageSlider (1271), fehSlider (1259) and meclSlider (1265). Each slider is a 1000-step (or 250/400-step) range input, and `censusAnnouncement` (logic.ts:285-290) produces roughly 140 characters, e.g. "800 stars drawn from the Maschberger mass function at age 0 Myr. Heaviest star 18.3 solar masses, no star has left the main sequence yet, 0 giants, 0 remnants." The region is `role="status" aria-live="polite" aria-atomic="true"` (index.html:188), so each change queues a full re-read. Holding an arrow key on countSlider steps once per repeat (about 30/s) and each step changes N by about 0.3 percent.
findings.scenario: A screen-reader user holds the right-arrow key on the "Number of stars" slider to go from 800 to 4,000. The polite queue fills with dozens of near-identical 140-character sentences; the user hears the first few seconds of one announcement after another and cannot reach the final value's reading without waiting the queue out or navigating away.
findings.fix: Add coalescing inside packages/runtime/src/liveRegion.ts: keep the latest pending text and flush it on a trailing timer (about 400ms) so a drag or key-repeat produces one announcement at rest. It belongs in the shared runtime, not per demo -- every demo in the repo calls it the same way. Changing the announcement cadence is a UX choice worth confirming before landing.

findings.title: The interactive canvases are declared role="img", which hides their keyboard interaction from assistive technology, and a contract test requires it
findings.evidence: index.html:210-215 and 239-244 give #clusterCanvas and #hrCanvas `role="img"` together with `tabindex="0"`, and main.ts:1171-1172 binds ArrowLeft/ArrowRight/Escape handlers to both via `bindKeyboardSelection`. `role="img"` declares the element a static graphic with no interactive children, so a screen reader announces it as an image and the arrow-key affordance exists only inside the aria-label prose. Nothing exposes the current selection as an accessible value: the per-star detail goes to #starCard (aria-live="polite", index.html:320), a separate region. design-contracts.test.ts:271-276 asserts `role="img"` is present on both canvases, so the contract pins the weaker pattern in place.
findings.scenario: A screen-reader user tabs to the HR diagram, hears it announced as an image with a long description, and has no indication that left/right arrows select stars -- the aria-label text is the only hint and it arrives as one long run of prose after the role. The keyboard path main.ts:1110-1142 was built specifically so the per-star detail is reachable without a pointer, and the role undercuts it.
findings.fix: In apps/demos/src/demos/cluster-census/index.html change both canvases to `role="application"` with an `aria-roledescription` naming them ("HR diagram, interactive"), or wrap each in a focusable element with an explicit widget role and keep role="img" on the canvas itself. Then relax design-contracts.test.ts:271-276 to accept either role while still requiring a 20+ character label. This changes how every demo's canvas is announced, so settle the pattern once rather than per demo.

findings.title: Station Mode drops the giant count: getSnapshotRow returns a field with no matching column
findings.evidence: main.ts:1440 `giants: String(cluster.postMainSequenceCount),` inside the object returned by `getSnapshotRow`, but the `columns` array declared at main.ts:1421-1429 is case / law / n / age / heaviest / turnoff / remnants -- there is no `giants` column. packages/runtime/src/demoModes.ts:650-655 passes the row straight to `addRows`, and the table and CSV are rendered from `columns`, so the field is silently discarded. Station step 3 (main.ts:1419) is "Return to the open-cluster preset and raise the age, watching the turnoff fall", and the giant branch growing is the other half of that observation.
findings.scenario: A student works through Station Mode, raises the age, watches the giant count climb on screen, then copies the CSV to hand in -- and the giant count is not in it. They cannot answer a question about the giant branch from their own recorded data, and the omission looks like their mistake.
findings.fix: In apps/demos/src/demos/cluster-census/main.ts:1421-1429 add `{ key: "giants", label: "Giants" }` between turnoff and remnants. Optionally tighten the StationRow type in packages/runtime/src/demoModes.ts so a key with no column is a type error rather than a silent drop.

findings.title: The export's "Below the ZAMS model range" row is structurally always zero, and the matching exhibit note describes stars that are never drawn
findings.evidence: main.ts:1373 exports `{ name: "Below the ZAMS model range", value: formatCount(cluster.outsideModelCount) }`. `outsideModelCount` is incremented only at starClusterModel.ts:221 when `ZamsTout1996Model.validity` fails, which for metallicityZ = 0.02 means massMsun < 0.1. main.ts:240/254/265 sets `minMassMsun: CENSUS_MIN_MASS_MSUN = 0.1`, and both samplers are bounded below by it (maschbergerMassMsun clamps at initialMassFunctionModel.ts:90; kroupaMassMsun is monotone from loMsun, which I verified: at u = 0 it returns lo exactly and the mass increases with u). So the row prints 0 for every reachable control setting. cluster-census.spec.ts:226 asserts only that the label string reaches the clipboard, never the value. The matching exhibit note (cluster-census.md:47) still describes those stars "appearing in the cluster and the histogram".
findings.scenario: A student copies results, sees a readout named "Below the ZAMS model range: 0", and spends time looking for the control that changes it. There is none. Worse, the permanent zero reads as positive evidence that the model's lower domain limit has been tested, when in fact the sampler never visits it.
findings.fix: Remove the row from the export in apps/demos/src/demos/cluster-census/main.ts:1373 (or keep it only if a future control re-opens the 0.08-0.1 Msun range), correct cluster-census.md:47, and relax cluster-census.spec.ts:226 so it does not pin a label for a quantity that no longer varies.

findings.title: Dead API surface: ClusterScene's highlight methods are never called, and logic.ts's solar symbols are never imported
findings.evidence: clusterScene.ts declares `setHighlight` (56, 359) and `getHighlight` (57, 365) plus the `highlightId`/`highlightPinned` state they maintain (161-162). Grepping apps/demos/src, apps/site/src and packages/*/src for those names returns only the declarations -- main.ts keeps its own `hoverId`/`pinnedId` (352-353) and draws the ring on the 2-D overlay (main.ts:513-516), so the scene's highlight state is written and never read. Separately, logic.ts:314-315 exports `MSUN_SYMBOL` and `LSUN_SYMBOL`; they are absent from main.ts's import list (lines 24-54) and from every other source file, and they are kept alive only by design-contracts.test.ts:358-359 asserting the escape "☉" appears in logic.ts and by logic.test.ts:388-390. logic.ts also redeclares a `CensusStar` interface (128-135) that is a subset of `@cosmic/physics`'s `ClusterStar`.
findings.scenario: A maintainer adding a second highlight behaviour wires it through `setHighlight`, sees no visual change, and loses time before discovering the overlay owns selection. The symbol exports are worse as evidence: a contract test cites them as proof the demo uses real solar glyphs on its canvas tick labels, when no canvas label in the demo uses them.
findings.fix: Delete `setHighlight`/`getHighlight` and the two state variables from apps/demos/src/demos/cluster-census/clusterScene.ts (lines 56-57, 161-162, 359-365). Either use MSUN_SYMBOL/LSUN_SYMBOL in the canvas axis context they were written for or delete them from logic.ts and drop the assertions at design-contracts.test.ts:358-359 and logic.test.ts:388-390. Replace logic.ts's `CensusStar` with a `Pick<>` over the imported `ClusterStar`.

findings.title: The Potential view leaves an orphan Sun glyph on an otherwise empty plot for radial motion, and the e2e test for that case cannot see it
findings.evidence: main.ts:651-657 toggles display for exactly [potentialCurve, potentialAllowed, potentialZero, potentialEps, potentialDrop, potentialBody] and then `if (!profile) return;`. #potentialSun is not in that list and main.ts:663 (its only write, `potentialSun.setAttribute("cx", ...)`) sits after the early return - grep confirms potentialSun appears at only main.ts:118 and 663. So setting the speed slider to 0 (radial, profile = null) hides every other mark while the Sun stays visible at its last cx = box.width/2 and its HTML-fixed cy. The e2e test at apps/site/tests/conservation-laws.spec.ts:996-1004, named 'radial motion hides the energy bar and the plot rather than drawing nonsense', asserts only `#energyBarK` and `#ueffCurve` are hidden; it never looks at #potentialSun or #potentialCurve.
findings.scenario: Student sets speed factor 0 (reachable: the slider's min is 0), switches to the Potential tab, and sees a blank panel with a single glowing Sun floating near the top centre and nothing else - no curve, no energy line, no body. The test suite stays green.
findings.fix: Add potentialSun to the display list in main.ts:651-653, and extend the spec at conservation-laws.spec.ts:996 to assert #potentialCurve and #potentialSun are hidden in the Potential view under radial motion.

findings.title: The Sun glyph in the Potential view is pinned to a fixed pixel height in a plot whose vertical axis is energy, placing it at +7.6 AU^2/yr^2
findings.evidence: index.html:71 `<circle id="potentialSun" class="orbit__mass" cx="0" cy="12" r="8">`; main.ts:663 sets cx only, and `setAttribute("cy")` never names potentialSun (grep over main.ts gives only particle, ueffDot and potentialBody). The y axis is energy: logic.ts:520 `yPx = (e) => ((eHi - clamp(e, eLo, eHi)) / (eHi - eLo)) * heightPx`. For the default circular orbit (M=1, r0=1) I computed uEffMin = -19.7392, eLo = 1.12*uEffMin = -22.1079, eHi = -0.45*uEffMin = 8.8826; at heightPx = 300, y = 12 px corresponds to +7.6430 AU^2/yr^2, while y(0) = 86.0 px and y(eps) = 277.1 px. index.html:64 captions the panel 'Height is energy per unit mass, not depth in space.'
findings.scenario: Under a callout that says height is energy, the Sun is drawn above both the zero line and the total-energy line, at the top of the clipped centrifugal barrier. The intuitive reading is that the Sun sits on a peak and the planet lies in a valley below it - gravity inverted - which is the opposite of the intuition the landscape metaphor is there to build.
findings.fix: In main.ts:659-667 either place the Sun on the energy axis at a defined value (e.g. profile.yPx(eLo), at the floor of the window, so it reads as the bottom of the well) or replace the circle with an axis marker outside the plot area (a tick plus '$r=0$' under the x axis), and say in index.html:64 that the barrier is clipped at the top of the window.

findings.title: formatTimeScale has no year branch, so the Step caption reads "577.8 months" instead of "48 years"
findings.evidence: logic.ts:251-260: `if (days >= 60) { const months = days / (DAYS_PER_YEAR / 12); ... return `${...} months`; }` - the largest unit is months, with no year case. main.ts:490-491 feeds it `anim.characteristicYr / STEPS_PER_ORBIT`. I evaluated the function verbatim: for M=1, r0=1, f=1.41 the period is 770.335 yr so one Step is 48.146 yr and the caption reads 'Each Step = 577.8 months of orbital time'; at f=1.40 (T = 125 yr) it reads '93.7 months'. The caption is shown whenever captionTimeLine returns 'step', i.e. under prefers-reduced-motion (logic.ts:334-337, main.ts:492-494).
findings.scenario: A student with reduced motion enabled sets the speed factor to 1.41 - the value play_steps step 3 names - and the stage caption tells them each Step covers 577.8 months. They have to divide by 12 to learn it is 48 years.
findings.fix: Add a years branch at the top of logic.ts:251-260: when days >= 2*DAYS_PER_YEAR return years to one decimal (or whole years when within 0.05), then fall through to the existing months/days/hours ladder. logic.test.ts already has a formatTimeScale block to extend.

findings.title: Reader-facing model notes are maintained twice and have already drifted apart
findings.evidence: conservation-laws.md:28-31 carries three model_notes (teaching units; 'Orbit type is determined by conserved specific energy and angular momentum'; 'Escape at sqrt(2) ... the slider steps from 1.41 to 1.42'). index.html:295-309 carries a separate 'Model notes' accordion with five different bullets (teaching units; the body starts at r0 on +x tilted from tangential; what the green arrow means; paths beyond 6 r0 are clipped and the window stays between 1.5 r0 and 50 AU; zero speed means radial infall). Only the units line is common; the other seven bullets exist in exactly one of the two places. main.ts:800-804 then holds a third, shorter copy for the clipboard export.
findings.scenario: A student who reads the exhibit page never learns that the drawing clips at 6 r0 or that the start is tangential from +x - the two facts needed to interpret what they are about to see. A student in the demo never reads the escape/slider-step note. Any correction to one copy silently leaves the other two wrong, which is how they diverged.
findings.fix: Make conservation-laws.md:28 the single source and render it into the demo: either have the build inject the frontmatter model_notes into index.html's accordion (the same path used for the export notes in main.ts:800-804), or move the demo-only bullets into the frontmatter and have the exhibit page and the demo render one list. Add a contract test asserting the demo's accordion bullets match the frontmatter array.

findings.title: effectivePotentialPlot and potentialProfile are near-duplicate 50-line functions differing only in the x mapping
findings.evidence: logic.ts:402-446 (effectivePotentialPlot) and logic.ts:503-553 (potentialProfile) each: run the same guard (`!(rpAu > 0) || !(rMaxAu > rpAu) || !(uEffMinAu2Yr2 < 0) || !Number.isFinite(epsAu2Yr2)` and the width/height check), call potentialEnergyWindow, call curveStartAu, define the same yPx, build the curve with the same `for (let i = 0; i <= samples; i++)` sweep from rMin to rMaxAu, build allowedD with the same sweep from rpAu to rEnd closed back to eps, and return the same six fields plus xPx/yPx. The only real differences are xPx (linear in r from rMin vs. signed and centred) and the mirrored half()/allowed() wrappers. The two also disagree on sample count for no stated reason (120 vs 90).
findings.scenario: A correction to the allowed-region path, the energy window or the curve start has to be made twice. Any fix applied to one view and not the other produces two drawings of the same orbit that disagree - exactly the class of defect that put the conflicting readiness claims in this repo's history.
findings.fix: Extract one builder in logic.ts that takes `xPx: (rAu: number) => number` plus an optional mirror flag and returns {curveD, allowedD, epsYPx, zeroYPx, rpXPx, raXPx, yPx}; have both exported functions supply their own xPx and share one samples constant. Both already have logic.test.ts coverage to hold the behaviour.

findings.title: exportResults scrapes three values out of the DOM instead of the model, so the export inherits whatever the screen rounded to
findings.evidence: main.ts:793-798: `{ name: "Specific kinetic energy K (AU^2/yr^2)", value: kValue.textContent ?? "—" }`, the same for uValue, and `{ name: "Speed v (km/s)", value: vKmSValue.textContent ?? "—" }` - while every other row in the same object comes from the model (`o.epsAu2Yr2` at 4 digits, `o.hAbsAu2Yr` at 8, `formatEccentricity(..., 6)`, `formatPeriapsis(..., 6)`). So K and U leave at 4 decimals and v at 3 while e, |h| and r_p leave at 6-8, and if a render bug ever wrote the wrong text into #kAu the export would copy it verbatim with no way to tell.
findings.scenario: A student exports a snapshot to check that K + U = eps at 6 figures, as the eps and |h| columns invite, and finds K and U truncated to 4 decimals - the sum no longer closes at the precision the neighbouring columns advertise. The export is also the only artifact that leaves the page, so a display bug becomes a data bug.
findings.fix: In main.ts:778-806 recompute the instantaneous state from the model - call ConservationLawsModel.conicPositionAndTangentAu + instantaneousSpeedAuPerYr + specificEnergyPartsAu2Yr2 at anim.nuRad, as renderBody does - and format K, U and v there with the export's own digit counts. The design-contracts test at design-contracts.test.ts:251 already asserts the export uses the shared formatters for e and r_p; extend it to K, U and v.

findings.title: turningPointsText promises a turnaround the body never makes on an open orbit started outbound, and the allowed region shades a leg it never travels
findings.evidence: logic.ts:449-455 returns `Turns around once, at ${rp} AU, and does not come back.` for any orbit with non-finite raAu. But for an open orbit the start is nu0 = el.nuRad (conservationLawsModel.ts, initialOrbit), and I traced the sign: with r = (r0, 0) and v = (v sin a, v cos a), the eccentricity vector gives omega = -nu0, so a positive (outward) direction puts nu0 > 0 - past periapsis already. I computed M=0.3, r0=3, f=1.6, dir=+55: nu0 = +97.473 deg, so the body only moves outward and never reaches r_p = 1.1417 AU. PRESETS.escape and PRESETS.hyperbolic (main.ts:144-145) set `directionDeg: null`, deliberately keeping whatever direction the student left, so this is reachable by setting the direction positive and then clicking Escape or Hyperbolic. logic.ts:429-434 and 533-541 shade the allowed region from rpAu outward in both cases, including the inbound half.
findings.scenario: Student sets the direction to +55 degrees, clicks Hyperbolic, switches to the Potential view and reads 'Turns around once, at 1.14 AU, and does not come back' in the status line and the plot's accessible name, with a shaded region reaching in to 1.14 AU. The body starts at 3 AU moving outward and never goes near 1.14 AU. The same text is also the plot's aria-label (main.ts:576-581), so a screen-reader user has only this description.
findings.fix: In logic.ts:449-455 take nu0Rad as an argument and, for an open orbit with nu0Rad > 0, say the body started past its closest approach at r_p and is on the way out. Clip the allowed path in logic.ts:429-434 and 533-541 to the arc the body will actually cover (start radius outward) for that case.

findings.title: The exhibit's "closed system and stated assumptions" learning goal has no support: the restricted two-body idealisation is never stated anywhere a student reads
findings.evidence: conservation-laws.md:14-17 claims the goals 'Identify quantities that remain constant under specific assumptions' and 'Connect ‘conserved’ to ‘closed system’ and stated assumptions'. Every readout in the demo is per unit mass (index.html:95-96 'Energy per unit mass AU$^2$/yr$^2$', 162 'Angular momentum per unit mass $|h|$'), which is only meaningful under a test-particle approximation with the primary held fixed - and the central mass is indeed held fixed at (300, 300) forever (index.html:47; nothing in main.ts moves #centralMass). Neither the demo's three accordions (index.html:279-344) nor the frontmatter model_notes (28-31) nor the export notes (main.ts:800-804) ever say the orbiting body's mass is negligible, that the primary does not recoil, that the motion is planar, or that there is no drag. The title at conservation-laws.md:2 is 'Conservation Laws: Energy & Momentum' but no linear momentum appears anywhere in the instrument, and the misconception at line 19 ('Energy is always conserved in the same form without exceptions') has nothing dissipative in the demo to test it against.
findings.scenario: A student asked on an exam to name the assumptions behind h = r v_t being conserved has read nothing in the exhibit that states them; worse, a student who notices the Sun never moves while the planet swings past at 65 km/s has no copy telling them that is an idealisation rather than a bug.
findings.fix: Add one bullet to conservation-laws.md:28 model_notes and to index.html's Model notes accordion naming the idealisation (central mass fixed, orbiting mass negligible so every quantity is per unit mass, planar, no drag), and either retitle to 'Energy & Angular Momentum' at conservation-laws.md:2 or drop the unaddressed 'same form without exceptions' misconception at line 19.

findings.title: The review of record says "Issues Found: None" and cites code that no longer exists, yet content_verified: true points at it
findings.evidence: docs/reviews/conservation-laws.md:56 'None. All physics equations, rendering chains, coordinate conventions, and orbit classifications are correct.' Its evidence column is stale: line 22 attributes the speed law to `logic.ts:188-190`, which is now inside viewRadiusAu (`const closedFit = ... Math.max(raAu, r0Au) * 1.1`); line 23 attributes `nuSpeedRadPerYr = hAbs/(r*r)` to `main.ts:231-232`, which is now renderTrail's `const o = validOrbit()`; line 45 analyses `classifyOrbit()` in logic.ts, which the demo's own contract test (design-contracts.test.ts:232-237) asserts no longer exists - grep for classifyOrbit across the demo and packages/physics returns only that assertion. The physics moved to packages/physics/src/conservationLawsModel.ts, which the review never mentions. conservation-laws.md:4 sets `content_verified: true` and line 12 sets `parityAuditPath`, with lastVerifiedAt 2026-09-11.
findings.scenario: The next reviewer (human or agent) reads a dated review that claims zero defects, cannot resolve a single one of its line citations, and either re-derives everything from scratch or trusts a verdict about deleted code. That is how the four P1s in this report survived a review that declared the demo clean.
findings.fix: Rewrite docs/reviews/conservation-laws.md against the current file layout (packages/physics/src/conservationLawsModel.ts and twoBodyAnalytic.ts for the equations, apps/demos/.../logic.ts for the drawings), record the findings in this report, and quote code rather than line numbers so the next move does not invalidate it. Keep readiness: candidate; it should not advance to launch-ready until the four P1s are closed, and the readinessReason at line 11 should stop implying the readouts are student-checkable while v is in km/s.

findings.title: Three consecutive arrow-key presses on the mass and radius sliders announce the same value while the orbit changes
findings.evidence: The mass and r0 sliders carry log10 values with step 0.01 (index.html:230, 236), so one arrow press changes the physical value by 10^0.01 = 1.0233, i.e. 2.33%. main.ts:386-393 renders and announces them at two decimals: `massValue.textContent = formatNumber(controls.massSolar, 2)` and `r0Slider.setAttribute("aria-valuetext", `${formatNumber(controls.r0Au, 2)} AU`)`. At the low end of the range that is below the display resolution: slider -1.00, -0.99, -0.98 give r0 = 0.1000, 0.1023, 0.1047, all of which format to '0.10'; only -0.97 (0.1072) reads '0.11'.
findings.scenario: A screen-reader or keyboard-only student at r0 = 0.1 AU presses Right twice and hears '0.10 AU' three times in a row while the drawn orbit and the energy readouts change each time. They cannot tell whether the control responded.
findings.fix: Give formatNumber-backed control readouts a significant-figures mode (3 s.f.) rather than fixed 2 decimals for the mass and r0 sliders in main.ts:386-393, so 0.10 / 0.102 / 0.105 / 0.107 are distinguishable, and keep the same string in the visible value and the aria-valuetext.

findings.title: The wave-spacing bracket length is not proportional to the lambda_obs it is labelled with, and stops responding above 1606 nm
findings.evidence: `spacingForNm = (nm) => clamp(18 + ((nm - 300) / 600) * 34, 14, 92)` (main.ts:768-771), i.e. spacing_px = 1 + 0.0566667 * nm, then clamped. The bracket drawn from bracketStart = 620 to bracketStart + obsSpacing is labelled `lambda_obs = <value> nm` (main.ts:822-827). I computed drawn-vs-physical ratios against lambda_0 = 656.3 nm: at v = +300 km/s physical 1.0010 / drawn 1.0010 (fine); at v = +100,000 km/s physical 1.4146 / drawn 1.4037; at z = 2 physical 3.0000 / drawn 2.4090 (saturated at the 92px cap); at z = 10 physical 11.0000 / drawn 2.4090 — identical to z = 2; at z = -0.8 physical 0.2001 / drawn 0.3666 (floored at 14px). Saturation sets in at nm = (92-1)/0.0566667 = 1606 nm and at nm = (14-1)/0.0566667 = 229 nm.
findings.scenario: A student drags z from 2 to 10. The bracket label climbs from "lambda_obs = 1968.94 nm" to "lambda_obs = 7219.30 nm" while the bracket itself does not move a pixel, and the wave underneath keeps the same crest spacing. They measure the picture with a ruler against its own label, find a factor-of-3.7 disagreement, and learn that the drawing is decorative. At the blue end the drawn spacing overstates lambda_obs by 83%.
findings.fix: In apps/demos/src/demos/doppler-shift/main.ts:768-771 make the mapping strictly proportional (spacing_px = k * nm) with k chosen from lambda_0 so the rest bracket lands near 38px, and when the result would exceed the drawable width, hold the spacing and draw an explicit "off-scale" marker instead of silently clamping — the spectrum comparator already does this at main.ts:704-708.

findings.title: Mystery challenge leaks whether the hidden element is Fe through the enabled state of the line-density checkbox
findings.evidence: Traced the control flow. startMystery (main.ts:1178-1198) sets `state.selectedElement = target.element` and render() then disables the element chips and forces aria-pressed false (main.ts:980-986) so the answer is hidden. But render() also computes `const denseAvailable = state.selectedElement === "Fe" && lineCatalog().length > 10;` and applies `showAllLines.disabled = !denseAvailable` (main.ts:1008) plus `lineDensityWrap.title = denseAvailable ? "" : "Dense line catalog unlocks when Fe is selected."` (main.ts:1014-1016). Neither is gated on `state.mystery.active`. CHALLENGE_ELEMENTS is ["H","He","Na","Ca","Fe"] (main.ts:171), so the checkbox is enabled for exactly one of the five possible answers.
findings.scenario: A student starts a Mystery Spectrum round and glances at the "Show all element lines (dense Fe catalog)" checkbox. If it is live, the answer is Fe; if it is greyed out with the tooltip "unlocks when Fe is selected", Fe is eliminated. One in five rounds is solved without looking at a single line, and the other four are reduced from five options to four — defeating the predict-check-explain loop the exhibit's play_steps build on.
findings.fix: In apps/demos/src/demos/doppler-shift/main.ts:1008-1016 force `showAllLines.disabled = true` and a neutral title whenever `state.mystery.active && !state.mystery.revealed`, so the control carries no information about the hidden element. Add an e2e assertion that the checkbox's disabled state and title are identical across several challengeSeed values.

findings.title: Mystery scenarios 2 and 3 pose questions the checker never grades, then assert the ungraded inference is correct
findings.evidence: All three Challenge entries share the same predicate. Scenario 2's prompt is "Determine the sign and regime of radial velocity from the shifted pattern" (main.ts:1095) but its check is `const correct = payload.guessedElement === payload.targetElement && payload.guessedMode === payload.targetMode;` (main.ts:1103) — MysteryCheckState (main.ts:1061-1066) carries only element and mode, with no velocity-sign or regime field at all. On success it returns "Correct. Your mode/element inference is consistent with the measured shift direction." (main.ts:1107), asserting agreement with a shift direction that was never examined. Scenario 3's prompt is "High-z case. Compare non-rel and relativistic predictions before deciding" (main.ts:1114) with the identical element/mode-only check (main.ts:1120). The design-contract test only counts prompts (`expect(promptCount).toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(3)`, design-contracts.test.ts:84), so it cannot see that the three checks are the same.
findings.scenario: A student drawn into Scenario 2 reads the prompt, works out the sign and regime, guesses the element right and the sign wrong, and is told "Correct. Your mode/element inference is consistent with the measured shift direction." The feedback certifies a reasoning step the checker never read, so a wrong sign is confirmed as right.
findings.fix: In apps/demos/src/demos/doppler-shift/main.ts, either add the fields each prompt asks for to MysteryCheckState (guessedSign, guessedRegime) with per-scenario checks, or rewrite prompts 2 and 3 to ask only for element and mode and drop the "consistent with the measured shift direction" wording at :1107. Replace the prompt-count assertion in design-contracts.test.ts:78-85 with unit tests that call each scenario's check() with a deliberately wrong sign and assert it fails.

findings.title: The unit test named "computes relativistic z from velocity" passes identically with the non-relativistic formula
findings.evidence: The assertion is `expect(synced.z).toBeCloseTo(0.001001, 4)` for syncPhysicalFromVelocity(300). toBeCloseTo(x, 4) admits |diff| < 5e-5. I computed both candidates at v = 300 km/s: z_rel = 1.001193e-3 and z_nonrel = beta = 1.000692e-3, which differ by 5.0e-7 — a hundred times inside the tolerance. The test would stay green if syncPhysicalFromVelocity (logic.ts:84-97) passed relativistic: false. Note the neighbouring test at logic.test.ts:36-40 does discriminate (z = 0.158 gives 43,665 km/s relativistic vs 47,367 km/s non-relativistic), so the suite proves the inverse direction but not this one.
findings.scenario: Someone flips `relativistic: true` to false in syncPhysicalFromVelocity while refactoring. Every z readout and the entire z slider mapping silently become non-relativistic; preset 8's z = 2 would map to 599,585 km/s instead of 239,834. The test whose name promises to catch this stays green, which is the failure mode the project already logged (five green tests pinning a bug).
findings.fix: In apps/demos/src/demos/doppler-shift/logic.test.ts:32 pick a velocity where the two formulas separate beyond the tolerance — e.g. syncPhysicalFromVelocity(60000) with `expect(synced.z).toBeCloseTo(0.2223, 4)` (relativistic) and an explicit `expect(synced.z).not.toBeCloseTo(0.2001, 3)` (non-relativistic) — and keep a low-velocity case only as a continuity check.

findings.title: No test in either suite constrains shift direction, so the inverted arrow and a sign flip pass all gates
findings.evidence: Read every assertion in both files. apps/site/tests/doppler-shift.spec.ts checks only plumbing: `not.toHaveText("0")`, `toContainText("+")`, toBeVisible/toBeHidden/toBeEnabled, and "- Element: Na" in the clipboard. The one physical number is `toContainText("+0.158")` after preset 7 (:96). Nothing asserts lambda_obs > lambda_0 for v > 0, nothing reads #lambdaObsValue or #deltaLambdaValue against a computed value, and nothing touches the wave diagram. logic.test.ts never imports directionSummary (logic.ts:262) at all, and no test covers wavelengthToFraction, wavelengthToRgbString, axisTicks, formatNumber or formatSigned. design-contracts.test.ts is string-presence only — e.g. `expect(main).toContain("initStarfield")`. Consequently the inverted arrow at main.ts:846 has been open since 2026-09-03 with every gate green.
findings.scenario: The sign convention is inverted anywhere in the chain — directionSummary, the arrow, or shiftedWavelengthNm — and the full suite still passes. The demo ships teaching blueshift for recession, which is exactly the state it is in today.
findings.fix: Add to apps/demos/src/demos/doppler-shift/logic.test.ts a direction block asserting directionSummary(+1000).keyword === "redshift" and (-1000) === "blueshift", and extract the arrow geometry into logic.ts so its endpoints can be asserted relative to the observer x. Add to apps/site/tests/doppler-shift.spec.ts one numeric assertion per sign: after preset 4 (-301 km/s) expect #deltaLambdaValue to start with "-" and #lambdaObsValue to be below 656.463; after preset 5 (+1000) expect the opposite.

findings.title: Three role="radiogroup" chip groups have no arrow-key handling or roving tabindex
findings.evidence: Spectrum mode (index.html:102-105), Formula selector (:107-110) and Mystery mode guess (:170-173) each wrap two `<button role="radio" aria-checked=...>` elements in a `role="radiogroup"`. Searched packages/runtime/src for radio keyboard support: initTabs handles ArrowRight/ArrowLeft but only for role="tab" (packages/runtime/src/tabs.ts:96), and nothing in the runtime or in main.ts binds keydown to these groups — main.ts:1282-1287 binds click only, and the document keydown handler (main.ts:1548) has no arrow cases. So all radios are in the tab order (the ARIA pattern requires one) and arrow keys do nothing inside a group.
findings.scenario: A screen-reader user hears "Formula selector, radio group, Non-relativistic, radio, checked, 1 of 2" and presses ArrowRight, which is how the announced role says to change a radio selection. Nothing happens. They have no indication that Tab-then-Enter is required, and the formula toggle — one of the demo's two primary physics controls — reads as broken.
findings.fix: Add a shared `initRadioGroups(root)` to packages/runtime that binds ArrowLeft/ArrowRight/Home/End within each `[role="radiogroup"]`, sets tabindex="0" on the checked radio and "-1" on the rest, and dispatches click on the newly selected one; call it from main.ts beside initTabs (main.ts:1643). All three groups here then conform without per-demo code.

findings.title: Emission-mode strips show a 26%-opacity continuum rainbow instead of a dark background
findings.evidence: drawSpectrumStrip (main.ts:546-572) always paints the full wavelength-coloured gradient first (`ctx.fillStyle = grad; ctx.fillRect(...)`, :556-557), then for emission mode overlays `ctx.fillStyle = "rgba(4, 8, 14, 0.74)"` (main.ts:563-565). Alpha 0.74 leaves 26% of the rainbow visible, so the "emission" strip is a dimmed continuum with brighter lines on top rather than dark sky with bright lines. The gradient is also built from only 48 stops across the domain (main.ts:548), which at the default 80-2200 nm window is one stop every 44 nm — about 8 stops across the entire visible band.
findings.scenario: A student toggles Emission and Absorption to learn the difference and sees two strips that both carry a visible continuum; only the line colour changes. The defining feature of an emission spectrum — no continuum between the lines — is not shown, and misconception "all spectra have a rainbow underneath" is reinforced by the picture.
findings.fix: In apps/demos/src/demos/doppler-shift/main.ts:546-572 branch before painting: for emission fill the strip with the dark background only (alpha 1.0) and skip the gradient entirely; keep the gradient for absorption. Raise the gradient stop count to scale with the domain span (one stop per ~10 nm) so the visible band is smooth when zoomed.

findings.title: computeReadoutContext runs four to five times per render, rebuilding the line catalogue each time, including every animation frame
findings.evidence: Traced one render() call: main.ts:971 (`formulaLimitIndicator.hidden = !computeReadoutContext().formulaFallbackApplied`), then updateReadouts at :1035 calls it again (:932), then drawWaveDiagram at :1036 calls it (:763), then drawSpectrumComparator at :1037 calls it (:730). Each call runs lineCatalog() — which for H regenerates the Bohr series via SpectralLineModel.seriesTransitions and for Fe maps a 34-entry dense array — plus selectRepresentativeLine twice and six DopplerShiftModel calls. drawSpectrumComparator additionally calls lineCatalog() through displayLines() and again through its own representative lookup, and render() calls it a sixth time at :1003 for denseAvailable. The wave animation calls drawWaveDiagram on every requestAnimationFrame (main.ts:1047-1050), so the catalogue is regenerated ~60 times a second while idle.
findings.scenario: On a low-end classroom Chromebook with Fe + Show all selected, every animation frame regenerates and re-sorts the catalogue and recomputes the full readout context; the sweep stutters and the drag feels laggy. Worse for correctness: six independent copies of the same derived state can drift if any call site passes a different argument, which is already true — drawSpectrumComparator derives its representative line from displayLines() (the strongest-8 subset) while computeReadoutContext derives it from the full catalogue, so the arrow and the readout can disagree for a catalogue where the global strongest line is not in the top 8.
findings.fix: Compute the context once per render in apps/demos/src/demos/doppler-shift/main.ts:render() and thread it into updateReadouts, drawWaveDiagram and drawSpectrumComparator as a parameter; hold the last context in a module variable for the animation frame to reuse, recomputing only when state changes. Have drawSpectrumComparator use the context's representative line instead of its own lookup at main.ts:682.

findings.title: Shadow radii are evaluated at Earth's centre distance, putting the total/annular boundary 6,400 km too close
findings.evidence: `solarEclipseTypeFromBetaDeg` passes `distanceFromBodyKm: dEarthMoonKm` (eclipseGeometryModel.ts:217), i.e. the Moon-centre-to-Earth-centre distance, so the Moon's umbral cone is sampled at Earth's centre rather than at the sub-lunar surface point, which is R_E = 6371 km nearer. Setting r_u = 0 in the model's formula gives d_crit = R_m x AU / (R_s - R_m) = 1737.4 x 149597870.7 / 694262.6 = 374,370 km, whereas the physically correct boundary adds Earth's radius: 380,741 km. Recomputed with node. The same substitution appears for the lunar case at line 183 (there the Moon is a full Earth-radius farther from the shadow's source, so the error has the opposite sign).
findings.scenario: Latent today because only three distance presets exist and all three are classified the same way under either convention (363,300 -> total, 384,400 and 405,500 -> annular). It bites the moment the dropdown becomes a continuous slider, as the exhibit copy implies ("Earth-Moon distance is selectable (km)"): every distance from 374,370 to 380,741 km would be labelled "Annular solar" when the real eclipse is total — a 6,400 km band, about 13% of the perigee-apogee range.
findings.fix: In packages/physics/src/eclipseGeometryModel.ts:217 and 183, pass `distanceFromBodyKm: dEarthMoonKm - earthRadiusKm` for the Moon-casts-shadow case and `dEarthMoonKm` for the Earth-casts-shadow case, documenting that the solar cone is evaluated at the sub-lunar point. Pin it with a test asserting `solarEclipseTypeFromBetaDeg({betaDeg: 0, earthMoonDistanceKm: 378000})` is "total-solar" and 382000 is "annular-solar".

findings.title: The statistics challenge asserts a canned, incorrect conclusion that its own fixed-distance simulation cannot produce
findings.evidence: `checkEclipseStatistics` returns `correct: true` with the sentence `"Total eclipses are the rarest type!"` appended unconditionally to whatever counts came back (logic.ts:583-590). Two problems. First the claim is wrong: among solar eclipses annular (~33%) outnumber total (~27%) and partial are the most common, and among lunar eclipses total (~35%) are not the rarest. Second the simulation cannot test it: `simulation.earthMoonDistanceKm` is captured once at launch (main.ts:1468) and never varied, and `solarEclipseTypeFromBetaDeg` decides total-vs-annular from the sign of the umbral radius, which depends only on that fixed distance. So a run at the default `mean` distance yields solar.total = 0 for every eclipse in 1,000 years, and a run at `perigee` yields solar.annular = 0. The challenge prompt asks "Are total eclipses more common than partial?" (main.ts:938).
findings.scenario: A student runs the default 10-year simulation, sees "Solar: 0 total" in the table, and is then told "Correct! ... Total eclipses are the rarest type!" — learning both that total solar eclipses essentially never occur and that the demo rewards an answer its own data contradicts.
findings.fix: Let the Moon's distance vary over the anomalistic month in `stepSimulation` (apps/demos/src/demos/eclipse-geometry/main.ts:1117) — d(t) = a(1 - e cos M) with a = 384,400 km, e = 0.0549, P_anom = 27.5545 d is one line and makes total and annular both reachable (this is a scientific assumption for Anna to approve). Then in logic.ts:583 derive the closing sentence from `args.counts` instead of hardcoding it, e.g. name the largest and smallest bins by their actual values.

findings.title: The beta curve escapes its panel above 7 deg tilt while the marker stays clamped, so the marker detaches from the curve
findings.evidence: `buildBetaCurvePath` applies no vertical bound: `const y = args.panelCenterY - beta * args.yScale` (logic.ts:75), with `BETA_Y_SCALE = 20` px/deg (main.ts:388), while the marker IS bounded: `const markerY = clamp(-args.betaDeg * BETA_Y_SCALE, -140, 140)` (main.ts:404). The drawn axis spans y = -140 to +140 (index.html:198), i.e. +/-7 deg, but the tilt slider allows up to 10 deg (index.html:76). At tilt = 10 deg the curve peaks at y = -200 and +200 in panel coordinates; with the group transforms translate(520,40) + translate(30,180) that is absolute y = 20 and y = 420 in a `viewBox="0 0 920 420"` — the top lobe overlaps the panel title at y = 40 and the bottom lobe runs through the "Schematic" caption at y = 392 and off the canvas. The marker meanwhile stops at +/-140, 60 px away from the curve it is supposed to sit on.
findings.scenario: A student drags the tilt slider past 7 deg to explore "what if the orbit were more tilted". The sinusoid grows out of its frame and over the caption text, and the Moon marker visibly separates from the curve, so the panel now shows the Moon's latitude at two different values at once.
findings.fix: In apps/demos/src/demos/eclipse-geometry/main.ts:388 scale the panel to the current tilt — `const BETA_Y_SCALE = 120 / Math.max(1, state.orbitalTiltDeg)` — so the curve always fills the axis, and label the axis ticks with the resulting degree values; or add `clip-path` to the beta panel group and remove the marker clamp at main.ts:404 so the two agree. Lower the tilt slider max to 7 deg only if the 10 deg range is not pedagogically wanted.

findings.title: Stage text is fixed at 11 px in a 920-unit viewBox, so every SVG label is about 4 px tall at 320 px width
findings.evidence: `.stage__svg { width: 100%; max-width: 960px; height: auto; }` over `viewBox="0 0 920 420"` (style.css:72-75, index.html:139), with `.stage__label { font-size: 11px }`, `.stage__note { font-size: 11px }` and `.stage__band-label { font-size: 11px }` (style.css:98-106, 225) and `.stage__title { font-size: 15px }` (style.css:93). Those sizes are in user units, so at a 320 px viewport the scale factor is 320/920 = 0.348 and 11 user units render at 3.8 CSS px (titles at 5.2 px). CLAUDE.md records that `/play/` routes are not covered by reflow.spec.ts, and apps/site/tests/eclipse-geometry.spec.ts has no viewport test, so nothing catches this.
findings.scenario: A student opens the demo on a phone in a lecture hall. "Sun direction", "Earth", "asc. node 210 deg", "solar zone", the beta value label and the 0/180/360 axis ticks are all sub-5 px and unreadable, leaving two unlabelled diagrams; the readout strip is the only usable part of the stage.
findings.fix: Give the stage text viewport-relative sizing in apps/demos/src/demos/eclipse-geometry/style.css — e.g. `font-size: clamp(11px, 1.6cqw, 15px)` with `container-type: inline-size` on `.stage`, or set the SVG font sizes in `rem` with `vector-effect`-style non-scaling text — and add a 320 px-width case for `/play/eclipse-geometry/` to apps/site/tests/reflow.spec.ts asserting no horizontal page scroll and a minimum computed label size.

findings.title: Named colour literals in demo CSS and five unreachable exports across the demo and the physics model
findings.evidence: Token purity: `.stage__sunDir { stroke: color-mix(in srgb, white 20%, transparent) }` (style.css:115) and `.stage__betaZero { stroke: color-mix(in srgb, white 30%, transparent) }` (style.css:165) hardcode the colour `white` instead of a `--cp-*` token, and `.stage__node:hover { filter: drop-shadow(0 0 8px var(--cp-accent)) }` (style.css:142) hardcodes glow geometry instead of using a `--cp-glow-*` token. The demo's own guard only looks for `rgba(` and `#hex` (design-contracts.test.ts:104-121), so named colours pass. Dead code: `getSimSummary` (main.ts:1057) and the `formatSimSummary` it wraps have no caller — `renderSimTable` replaced them; `yearsToSlider` (logic.ts:506) is exported and tested but never used; and `betaFromDeltaLambdaDeg`, `isSarosRelated`, `isExeligmosRelated`, `SAROS_CYCLE_DAYS` and `EXELIGMOS_CYCLE_DAYS` in packages/physics/src/eclipseGeometryModel.ts:5-6, 43, 230, 237 have no consumer anywhere in apps/demos or apps/site. Also `eclipseThresholdsDeg` returns a `_debug` object (eclipseGeometryModel.ts:148-151) in its public contract.
findings.scenario: The two `white` literals ignore the museum/instrument layer split, so the Sun-direction and beta-zero guides keep the same contrast in both layers and under high-contrast mode instead of following the token system; and a reader of the model cannot tell which of its fifteen exports the demo actually depends on, which is how the stub-versus-real test drift above went unnoticed.
findings.fix: Replace `white` with `var(--cp-text)` or a new `--cp-guide-line` token in apps/demos/src/demos/eclipse-geometry/style.css:115 and 165, swap the hover filter at line 142 for `var(--cp-glow-accent-teal)`, and extend the colour-literal check in design-contracts.test.ts:104 to flag CSS named colours. Delete `getSimSummary` + `formatSimSummary` + `yearsToSlider`, and either wire the saros helpers into a "Saros" readout or remove them and `_debug` from the model's exported surface.

findings.title: The chirp overlay compresses 18 decades of wavelength into 1.3, with no reader-facing caveat
findings.evidence: logic.ts:301-302 sets minFreq = 3 and maxFreq = 60 cycles across the bar and sweeps exponentially in x (logic.ts:308-315), so the drawn wavelength shrinks by a factor 20 (1.30 decades) from left to right while the axis beneath it shrinks by 18 decades. The only statement of this is a source comment at logic.ts:286-290 ("not physically literal"); the canvas is `aria-hidden="true"` (drawn into `#spectrumWaveCanvas`, index.html:94) and no caption, legend or model note mentions it. The design-contract test only checks that the canvas element exists (design-contracts.test.ts:113-115) and the logic test only checks the function's arity (logic.test.ts:572-577).
findings.scenario: The demo's stated purpose is to show how extreme the dynamic range of the spectrum is. A student compares the drawn wave at the visible band with the drawn wave at radio, sees roughly a factor of ten, and concludes radio waves are about ten times longer than light rather than about 10^6 times longer. Nothing on screen contradicts them.
