findings.fix: Either make the overlay honest over a declared sub-range (draw the true wave only inside a small window around the marker and label the window), or add a visible caption under the bar stating that the wave is schematic and the real wavelength ratio across the bar is 10^18. The caption is the cheaper fix and should land either way.

findings.title: Reader-visible micrometre unit is the ASCII string "um" instead of rendered LaTeX
findings.evidence: logic.ts:139 returns `unit: "um"`, which main.ts:243 writes into `#readoutWavelengthUnit` via textContent, and main.ts:231 / 261 / 282 interpolate into the band range, the telescope list and the molecular-band list. CLAUDE.md's math-authoring table says for "Astro/TS that emits reader-visible strings: LaTeX only. Render it with ... renderMath() from @cosmic/runtime in the demos", and lists the canvas as the only ASCII exemption. These are DOM text nodes, not canvas. scripts/validate-math-formatting.mjs cannot catch it because FORBIDDEN_UNICODE_MATH (line 33) only matches Unicode glyphs, and "um" is pure ASCII. Separately em-spectrum.md:29 promises "nm/$\mu\mathrm{m}$/mm/m for $\lambda$; Hz for $\nu$; eV/keV/MeV for $E$", but the demo also renders km, pm, fm, kHz through EHz, and erg -- three unit families the public note does not list.
findings.scenario: A student at 316 um sees the readout "316 um" where the exhibit page beside it renders a typeset mu. In the Lines panel they read "CO2 ~15 um band - 15.0 um". The symbol for micro is not u, and the mismatch teaches a wrong notation while the model notes claim otherwise.
findings.fix: Return a LaTeX token from the formatters (e.g. `unit: "\\mu\\mathrm{m}"`) and render the unit spans with renderMath() from @cosmic/runtime in main.ts:242-247, or keep plain text in logic.ts and map unit keys to LaTeX at the render boundary. Then correct em-spectrum.md:29 to list every unit family the demo can actually show.

findings.title: The Convert panel is a second, disconnected wavelength state and its convertLock is dead code posing as a mutex
findings.evidence: main.ts:192-195 holds the instrument state (`state.wavelengthCm`), while main.ts:408-458 maintains three independent inputs that never call setWavelengthCm and are never initialised from state -- they start empty and typing in them moves nothing on the bar, the band card or the readouts. Tracing main.ts:394-457 line by line: `convertLock` is assigned, used only as the guard `if (convertLock) return` at the top of the same three handlers, and cleared before each handler returns, with no await anywhere; programmatic `.value` assignment in setConvertInputs (main.ts:396-406) does not dispatch an `input` event, so no handler can ever observe a truthy lock. It is unreachable state. docs/reviews/em-spectrum.md nevertheless credits it: "A mutex lock (convertLock) prevents circular updates."
findings.scenario: A student types 656 in the wavelength field to put H-alpha on the spectrum. Frequency and energy update, the bar does not move, the band badge still says whatever it said, and the marker is somewhere else entirely. The demo now holds two different answers to "what wavelength am I looking at?" with nothing on screen distinguishing them.
findings.fix: Drive the Convert inputs from the single state: have each handler call setWavelengthCm(...) and have renderReadouts (main.ts:234-251) write the three inputs back, guarded by a document.activeElement check so the field being typed in is left alone. Delete convertLock, which then has no job, and correct the review line that cites it.

findings.title: Static Objects and Lines lists are torn down and rebuilt on every slider input, and two of four object fields are never shown
findings.evidence: setWavelengthCm calls renderLists(lambdaCm) on every `input` event (main.ts:355, 373-376). Inside renderLists, only the telescope loop reads lambdaCm (main.ts:256); the object loop (main.ts:265-270) and the line loops (main.ts:272-284) are lambda-independent yet are cleared with `innerHTML = ""` and rebuilt each time -- roughly 30 elements per slider tick. The object renderer emits only `${obj.name} - ${obj.why}`, dropping the `bands` and `telescopeExamples` fields that packages/data-spectra/src/emSpectrumObjects.ts:28-96 supplies for all 17 entries. Atomic lines render as `${nm.toFixed(3)} nm` (main.ts:276), e.g. "656.281 nm", sub-picometre precision with the `medium: "air"` field (atomicLines.ts) never shown.
findings.scenario: em-spectrum.md:34 lists the play step "Match bands to a type of astronomical observation", but the Objects panel shows no bands, so the step cannot be completed from the demo. Meanwhile an assistive-technology user reading the Lines list while dragging the slider has the list destroyed under them on every arrow key.
findings.fix: Render the Objects and Lines lists once at init and leave them alone; keep only the telescope "Now:" state in the per-change path and update it by toggling a class/aria-current on existing nodes instead of rebuilding. Show obj.bands and obj.telescopeExamples, and either drop to one decimal on line wavelengths or label them as air wavelengths.

findings.title: The wavelength slider is inverted and exposes a meaningless aria-valuenow; no change is announced
findings.evidence: index.html:22-29 declares `min="0" max="1000"` under the label "Wavelength $\lambda$", and main.ts:348 / 374 map the raw value to axis position percent x 10, where position 0 is the longest wavelength. Increasing the slider therefore decreases the labelled quantity: ArrowRight at value 571 (520 nm) moves toward shorter wavelengths. aria-valuenow stays the raw 0-1000 position with no physical meaning; only aria-valuetext is set (main.ts:250). setLiveRegionText is imported (main.ts:6) but called only in handleCopyResults (main.ts:315, 317), so no wavelength or band change is ever announced -- the whole figure is aria-hidden (index.html:84, 93, 100, 108) and `.spectrum` carries aria-label on a div with no role (index.html:82), where the label is ignored.
findings.scenario: A screen-reader user arrows through the slider. Each press announces a wavelength that moves the opposite way from the number, the band never changes audibly even when crossing from visible into ultraviolet, and no part of the spectrum figure has a text alternative.
findings.fix: Either invert the mapping so increasing slider value increases lambda, or keep the layout and set role="slider" semantics with aria-valuemin/max/now expressed in the physical quantity. Call setLiveRegionText(status, ...) from setWavelengthCm with the new wavelength and band -- debounced, and outside any animation frame, per the project's live-region rule. Give `.spectrum` role="img" with an aria-label that states the axis range and the current position.

findings.title: Named colour literals in demo CSS slip past both the build invariant and the demo's own contract test
findings.evidence: style.css:98-99 styles the band highlight with `background: color-mix(in srgb, white 18%, transparent)` and `border: 1px solid color-mix(in srgb, white 35%, transparent)`, and style.css:81 adds `inset 0 1px 0 color-mix(in srgb, white 6%, transparent)`. CLAUDE.md invariant 7 requires token purity and invariant 5 forbids colour literals, but scripts/validate-invariants.mjs:115 defines `rxColorLiteral = /#[0-9a-fA-F]{3,8}\b|\brgba?\(|\bhsla?\(/gi`, which matches neither `white` nor any other CSS colour keyword; the demo's own guard (design-contracts.test.ts:75-93) tests the same two shapes. The band highlight is the one visual that marks the selected band, and it is styled outside the token system.
findings.scenario: The highlight is a fixed white wash that ignores the instrument layer's accent tokens, so a theme change silently leaves it mismatched, and the gate reports green. The same loophole lets any future `white`, `black` or `red` into any demo's CSS.
findings.fix: Replace the three `white` keywords with instrument tokens (e.g. var(--cp-accent-ice) or var(--cp-instr-panel-border)) in style.css:81, 98, 99, and extend rxColorLiteral in scripts/validate-invariants.mjs:115 with a CSS named-colour alternation so the gate can see this class of violation across all demos.

findings.title: The visible-band highlight is ~1.5% wide with a 999px radius and 1px borders, so the demo's headline point is nearly invisible
findings.evidence: renderBandHighlight (main.ts:212-219) sets width = pos(lambdaMin) - pos(lambdaMax); I recomputed the visible band as 57.890% - 56.416% = 1.474% of the bar. style.css:93-101 gives `.spectrum__highlight` `border-radius: 999px`, `height: 100%` (80px) and a 1px border on each side. At a typical 800px bar that is an 11.8px-wide element whose corner radius saturates at height/2 = 40px, collapsing it into a lozenge whose two 1px borders are a sixth of its width. The gradient comment at logic.ts:222-223 states the intent plainly: "The visible band is genuinely ~1.5% of this axis. Rendering it at its true width is the point: the demo exists to show how narrow it is."
findings.scenario: A student selects Visible to see how narrow their eyes' window is and gets a faint rounded sliver roughly the width of the marker line, with the 2px marker sitting inside it. The single most important comparison in the demo is the one hardest to see.
findings.fix: Clamp the highlight's rendered width to a minimum of about 6px in main.ts:216 while keeping it centred on the true band, drop border-radius to 4px for narrow bands in style.css:97, and add a leader line or callout tying the sliver to the band name so its narrowness reads as deliberate rather than as a rendering glitch.

findings.title: Unit tests re-assert the implementation: band bounds are only checked for internal contiguity and the chirp only for arity
findings.evidence: logic.test.ts:458-471 ("adjacent bands have matching boundaries") asserts only `BANDS.radio.lambdaMinCm === BANDS.microwave.lambdaMaxCm` and its five siblings -- every assertion passes with microwave at 0.1-1 mm, so the test cannot detect the P0 band-definition error; no test compares any boundary to a conventional value or to any named source. logic.test.ts:399-405 asserts band centres lie inside their own bands, which is true by construction of the geometric mean. logic.test.ts:572-577 is the entire coverage of drawSpectrumWave: `typeof === "function"` and `drawSpectrumWave.length === 3`. There is no test that formatter output avoids exponential notation (I showed "1.99e-22 erg" and "3.00e+4 EHz" are produced), none for tick-label alignment, none for the convert handlers, and the e2e spec's assertions are existence-and-nonempty throughout (apps/site/tests/em-spectrum.spec.ts:142-161 asserts only toBeTruthy on each readout, and :222-232 only that converted values are > 0, which would pass with c or h wrong by any factor).
findings.scenario: All suites are green while the axis labels are off by 72x, the microwave band contradicts its own examples, and the marker label never renders. The tests encode what the code does, so the next change to the band table or the formatters will also pass unexamined.
findings.fix: Add value-level tests: bandFromWavelengthCm(12.236) === "microwave" and bandFromWavelengthCm(0.10632) === "microwave" (oven and CMB peak); photonEnergyEvFromWavelengthNm(656.281) close to 1.8892 with a tight tolerance; a sweep asserting no formatter output matches /e[+-]\d/; and a geometry test that each declared tick wavelength maps to its rendered percentage. Add an e2e assertion that #markerLabel has a non-zero bounding box.

findings.title: Telescope coverage ranges are wrong by one to three decades and drive a factual "Now:" claim
findings.evidence: VERITAS is given wavelengthMinCm = 1e-15, wavelengthMaxCm = 1e-12 (emSpectrumTelescopes.ts:38-46). I converted with E = hc/lambda: that is 124 MeV to 124 GeV. VERITAS is a ground Cherenkov array sensitive from about 85 GeV to 30 TeV, i.e. lambda 1.46e-15 down to 4.13e-18 cm -- the stated range excludes the entire TeV band the entry's own `science` field advertises ("Very high energy gamma rays") and extends three decades into Fermi's MeV territory where VERITAS has no sensitivity. Chandra is given 1e-9 to 1e-6 cm = 0.124 to 124 keV against a real 0.1-10 keV (1.24e-8 to 1.24e-6 cm), a decade too hard. Fermi is given 1e-14 to 1e-10 cm = 1.24 MeV to 12.4 GeV against a real 20 MeV to 300 GeV. FAST is given a 21 cm short limit although it tunes to 70 MHz-3 GHz (10 cm-4.3 m). main.ts:256 turns these into a claim: lambda inside [min, max] prefixes the entry with "Now: ".
findings.scenario: A student parks at 1.24 GeV (lambda = 1e-13 cm) and the Telescopes panel says "Now: VERITAS", asserting that a ground Cherenkov array observes GeV photons. Dragging to the TeV photons VERITAS actually detects is impossible, because they are off the axis. At 100 keV the panel says "Now: Chandra".
findings.fix: Recompute each entry's wavelength bounds from the instrument's published energy or frequency coverage and store the source in the meta.provenance notes: VERITAS 4.1e-18 to 1.5e-15 cm, Chandra 1.2e-8 to 1.2e-6 cm, Fermi 4.1e-16 to 6.2e-12 cm, FAST 1e1 to 4.3e2 cm. Add a dataset contract test asserting each range round-trips to the documented energy or frequency limits.

findings.title: Exhibit copy promises unit-conversion practice the Convert panel does not provide
findings.evidence: em-spectrum.md:38 reads "then use the Convert panel to practice unit conversions." The panel has exactly three fixed-unit fields -- Wavelength (nm), Frequency (Hz), Photon energy (eV) at index.html:157-169 -- with no unit selects, so it practices converting between physical quantities, not between units. docs/audits/migrations/em-spectrum-parity.md flags this as its own P0 ("Exhibit copy currently says 'practice unit conversions' ... but the migrated Convert panel does not implement unit toggles yet") and offers restoring the legacy selects or revising the copy; neither has been done. The same section's second P0, updating apps/site/src/content/instructor/em-spectrum/model.md, is also open: lines 17-18 still point at `demos/_assets/em-spectrum-model.js` and `demos/em-spectrum/em-spectrum.js`, files that do not exist in this repo.
findings.scenario: A student reads the exhibit page, opens the demo expecting to practise nm-to-um and Hz-to-GHz conversions, and finds three fields locked to one unit each. An instructor following the model notes to read the implementation is sent to two paths that do not exist in the repository.
findings.fix: Take the parity audit's Option B now and the cheaper half of Option A later: change em-spectrum.md:38 to "to convert between wavelength, frequency and photon energy", and update instructor/em-spectrum/model.md:17-18 to cite packages/physics/src/photonModel.ts, packages/data-spectra and apps/demos/src/demos/em-spectrum/. Add unit selects as a separate change if the legacy capability is wanted back.

findings.title: The slider's markup start value disagrees with the demo's initial wavelength, so the thumb jumps on load
findings.evidence: index.html:28 hard-codes `value="520"`, which the mapping at main.ts:374 reads as axis position 52% -- that is lambda = 10^(6 - 0.52*18) = 1.32e-3 cm, about 13 um, far-infrared. The real initial state is 520 nm (main.ts:193, AstroUnits.nmToCm(520)), whose position I computed as 57.13%, and main.ts:348 rewrites the slider to round(57.13*10) = 571 once setWavelengthCm runs at main.ts:469. The literal 520 looks like "520 nm" but is in position-times-ten units, which is how it came to be wrong.
findings.scenario: On first paint, before the module executes, the thumb sits at 52% and then jumps to 57%. Anyone editing the markup will read 520 as nanometres and set an unrelated position.
findings.fix: Set index.html:28 to value="571" and add a comment that the units are axis-position percent times ten, or better, drop the literal and have main.ts derive both the slider range and its initial value from LAMBDA_MIN_LOG / LAMBDA_MAX_LOG so the markup carries no duplicated number.

findings.title: Degeneracy branch switches produce discontinuous jumps in P_deg,e at x_F = 0.3 and a hard zero at T/T_F = 8
findings.evidence: electronPressureFiniteTDynePerCm2 picks the non-relativistic integral when `xF < 0.3` (line 616) and the relativistic one otherwise, with no blending. I evaluated both branches on the same states (mu_e = 2, T = 2e7 K): at rho = 5.0e4 (x_F = 0.2950) the non-relativistic branch gives excess 1.78332e20 and the relativistic 1.71913e20 dyne cm^-2; at rho = 5.4e4 (x_F = 0.3027) they give 2.04516e20 and 1.96833e20. So crossing the threshold steps the displayed value down by 2.9-3.1% while density increases -- locally non-monotonic in a readout shown to 5 significant figures. Separately, the `chiZeroT >= 8` shortcut at line 608 returns exactly n_e k_B T, so the excess is forced to 0: at rho = 1e-2, T = 2e5 K (chi = 15.9) the FD excess is 1.6217e9 dyne cm^-2 but the card reads 0.0000e+0, and at chi = 7.96 it reads 1.0762e9 -- a 100% step at the threshold. (The chi <= 1e-3 zero-T cut is clean: 2.62016e22 vs 2.62020e22, 1e-5 relative.)
findings.scenario: A student sliding density upward through x_F = 0.3 watches P_deg,e tick DOWN by 3% at one slider step and concludes the model is noisy or that degeneracy pressure is non-monotonic in density. A student in the weakly degenerate regime sees P_deg,e reported as exactly zero and concludes degeneracy pressure vanishes identically above T/T_F = 8 rather than becoming negligible.
findings.fix: Use the relativistic integral everywhere (it reduces correctly to the non-relativistic result at small x_F and I measured its quadrature error at 0.015%), which removes the x_F = 0.3 seam and the duplicated solver; or, if the two-branch structure is kept for pedagogy, blend them over x_F in 0.25-0.35 and expose the seam in the method label. Replace the hard `chiZeroT >= 8` zero with the FD integral plus a display rule that renders values below a stated fraction of P_tot as "negligible" rather than as 0.

findings.title: Regime grid is point-sampled at (n-1) spacing but painted as n cells, offsetting the colour fill from the dashed analytical boundaries by up to 0.125 dex in density
findings.evidence: evaluateRegimeGrid samples grid POINTS: `dRho = (logRhoMax - logRhoMin) / Math.max(1, yCells - 1)` with `logRho = logRhoMin + j * dRho` (logic.ts:467, 470), so with yCells = 80 over 20 dex the samples sit 0.2532 dex apart, j=0 at -10 and j=79 at +10. drawExactGrid paints them as CELLS of a different pitch: `cellH = pa.h / grid.yCells` = 0.25 dex, with `y = pa.y + (grid.yCells - 1 - j) * cellH` (regimeMap.ts:197, 206). Cell centre for row j is therefore log rho = -10 + (j+0.5)*0.25 while the sample is at -10 + j*0.2532: j=0 is drawn centred at -9.875 for a sample taken at -10.0 (+0.125 dex), j=79 at +9.875 for a sample at +10.0 (-0.125 dex). The same mismatch in temperature is +/-0.03 dex. drawBoundary and drawMarker use the exact logRhoToY mapping, so the dashed boundaries and the crosshair are right while the colour fill is shifted.
findings.scenario: A student compares the dashed gas/degeneracy boundary with the colour change behind it near the top or bottom of the map and finds them separated by about a cell -- roughly a 30% discrepancy in the density at which the model says the channels cross. With the crosshair sitting on the dashed line, the cell under it can read the other colour.
findings.fix: Make the two conventions agree. Either sample cell CENTRES in evaluateRegimeGrid (logic.ts:465-470) and the worker (regimeWorker.ts:44-45) -- dRho = range/yCells with logRho = logRhoMin + (j+0.5)*dRho -- keeping drawExactGrid as is, or keep the point sampling and draw each cell centred on its sample by offsetting x and y by half a cell and using pitch range/(n-1). Add a unit test that the channel reported by evaluateRegimeGrid at a given (logT, logRho) matches the cell drawExactGrid paints at that pixel.

findings.title: Design-system literals relocated from CSS into TypeScript, frozen at first paint, and panels bypass --cp-instr-panel-bg
findings.evidence: main.ts:420-424 defines the five channel colours as hex literals (gasColor "#34d399", radColor "#f472b6", degColor "#a78bfa", totalColor "#fbbf24", markerColor "#fbbf24") and main.ts:429-437 pushes them onto .cp-demo__stage as --eos-* custom properties under the comment "keeps hex out of CSS" -- so the canonical value for four reader-visible channel colours lives in a demo's TypeScript, not in packages/theme tokens.css, and nothing in packages/theme can reference or test them. regimeMap.ts:146-156 then re-declares the same four as fallbacks and adds `text: "rgba(255,255,255,0.78)"`, `grid: "rgba(255,255,255,0.15)"`, `marker: "#fbbf24"`, `preset: "#ffffff"`, with more at :422 and :444 and "#fff"/"#fbbf24" in mechanismViz. resolveColors caches into `cachedColors` on first call and returns early forever (regimeMap.ts:133-134), so a token or theme change after first paint is never picked up. Separately, grep finds no `var(--cp-instr-panel-bg)` anywhere in style.css -- the demo's panels use `color-mix(in srgb, var(--cp-bg1) 90%, transparent)` (style.css:218, 263, 299, 452, 499) instead of the token the Panel Translucency Contract names, and the one backdrop-filter is blur(6px) (style.css:381) where the contract specifies 8px.
findings.scenario: An instructor asks for the degeneracy channel to be recoloured for a projector. The change has to be made in main.ts:422 and again in regimeMap.ts:149 and the mechanismViz violet constants, with no token to change and no test that catches a missed copy -- so the uPlot curve, the regime-map fill and the mechanism animation drift to different violets. A later light-theme or token change silently does not reach the regime map at all, because cachedColors was frozen on first render.
findings.fix: Promote the four channel colours to real tokens in packages/theme tokens.css (e.g. --cp-channel-gas/-rad/-deg/-total) with entries in vars.ts and packages/theme/src/tokens.test.ts, delete the hex declarations in main.ts:420-424 and the fallbacks in regimeMap.ts:146-156, and read them through resolveCssColor. Make resolveColors re-read on each render (or invalidate the cache on a theme change) instead of caching permanently, and switch the demo's panel backgrounds in style.css to var(--cp-instr-panel-bg) with blur(8px).

findings.title: 22 hardcoded rgba()/hex colors in main.ts bypass the token system, which the no-color-literals gate cannot see because it only scans .astro/.css/.html
findings.evidence: `grep -c 'rgba(\|#[0-9a-fA-F]{6}' main.ts` returns 22 — e.g. main.ts:676 `ctx.fillStyle = "rgba(8, 12, 22, 0.76)"`, :753 `"rgba(242, 140, 140, 0.12)"` for the dark-matter fill band, :759 `"rgba(255, 206, 115, 0.95)"` for V_total, :772 `"rgba(132, 210, 255, 0.85)"` for V_visible, :813 `ctx.fillStyle = "#fff2cf"`. CLAUDE.md's token hierarchy says "Every visual property flows from the token system — no hardcoded color values in demo code", but scripts/validate-invariants.mjs:104 sets `const colorLiteralExts = new Set([".astro", ".css", ".html"])`, so the `apps:no-color-literals` rule at line 318 never reads a .ts file and these 22 pass the build. The repo already has the fix pattern: apps/demos/src/demos/keplers-laws/main.ts:148-158 `resolveCanvasColor(value)` resolves `var(--cp-celestial-earth)` through getComputedStyle for canvas use, and eight demos call getComputedStyle for the same reason. galaxy-rotation's style.css is clean (color-mix over tokens throughout) — only the canvas code forks.
findings.scenario: A token change in packages/theme — a new instrument accent, a contrast fix, a light-mode variant — updates the SVG schematic and every panel but leaves the rotation plot on last season's palette, and no test or build gate reports it. The same literals mean the plot cannot respond to a high-contrast or light theme at all.
findings.fix: Copy `resolveCanvasColor` from apps/demos/src/demos/keplers-laws/main.ts:148-158 into packages/runtime (it is duplicated across demos already) and resolve a `canvasColors` map once at startup from --cp-celestial-* / --cp-accent-* tokens, then replace the 22 literals in apps/demos/src/demos/galaxy-rotation/main.ts. Separately add ".ts" to colorLiteralExts in scripts/validate-invariants.mjs:104 so the gate covers demo code — expect other demos to light up.

findings.title: ctx.font is set to a string containing var(), which the canvas font setter cannot resolve, so all three label font assignments are discarded
findings.evidence: main.ts:661, :795 `ctx.font = "11px var(--cp-font-sans, ui-sans-serif)"` and main.ts:820 `ctx.font = "12px var(--cp-font-sans, ui-sans-serif)"`. var() substitution happens only for declarations in a CSS rule at computed-value time; the canvas 2D `font` setter parses its argument as a standalone CSS font shorthand, and the spec requires an unparseable value to be ignored with the attribute left unchanged. So every one of these assignments is a no-op: the inset title, the "M_dark = M_vis near X kpc" annotation and the "R (kpc)" / "V (km/s)" axis titles render at whatever font was last valid — the 10px sans-serif initial value, since no valid font is ever set in this file. The same mistake appears 18 times repo-wide, four of them in doppler-shift/main.ts.
findings.scenario: The axis titles and the dark-dominance annotation render two points smaller than intended in the browser's default sans-serif instead of the demo's sans token, so the plot's only text is the least legible text on the page — worst on a projector at the back of a lecture hall, which is the demo's stated station use.
findings.fix: Resolve the font family once the same way colors should be resolved: read `getComputedStyle(document.body).getPropertyValue("--cp-font-sans")` (or getComputedStyle(canvas).fontFamily) into a module constant and build the string as `11px ${fontFamily}`. Apply at apps/demos/src/demos/galaxy-rotation/main.ts:661, 795, 820; the same fix is owed repo-wide and belongs in packages/runtime beside the canvas colour helper.

findings.title: rotationCurve re-implements four of the model's own methods inline, with different NaN behavior from the methods it duplicates
findings.evidence: galaxyRotationModel.ts:549-553 inside rotationCurve: `const vTotalKmS = Math.sqrt(vBulgeKmS ** 2 + vDiskKmS ** 2 + vHaloKmS ** 2);` duplicates vTotalKmS (line 462); `const vVisibleKmS = Math.hypot(vBulgeKmS, vDiskKmS);` duplicates vVisibleKmS (line 399); `const baryonFraction = masses.total > 0 ? masses.visible / masses.total : 0;` duplicates baryonFraction (line 509). The copies are not equivalent: vTotalKmS:470 guards `if (!Number.isFinite(vBulge) || ...) return NaN` and returns 0 at R = 0, while the inline copy has no guard; and darkVisRatio at line 552 returns NaN when visible === 0 whereas the neighbouring baryonFraction returns 0 for the same degenerate case, so the two dimensionless mass readouts disagree about how to report an empty galaxy. The demo consumes only rotationCurve (main.ts:206-213), so every plotted and exported number comes from the copies, not from the tested methods.
findings.scenario: The next correctness fix to vTotalKmS or vVisibleKmS — say the a_N fix this audit recommends, or a future halo truncation change — lands in the method, passes galaxyRotationModel.test.ts which calls the methods directly, and never reaches the plot, because main.ts reads rotationCurve's private copies. This is precisely how GR-1's spherical benchmark survived.
findings.fix: In packages/physics/src/galaxyRotationModel.ts:540-556, have rotationCurve call `this.vTotalKmS`, `this.vVisibleKmS` and `this.baryonFraction` instead of recomputing them, and pick one convention for the degenerate ratio (NaN or 0) in both darkVisRatio and baryonFraction. Add a test asserting row-by-row equality between rotationCurve output and the direct method calls for all four presets — the existing one (test:264) checks only vVisibleKmS.

findings.title: Two physics tests cannot fail: one asserts an identity true by construction while claiming to check the readout, the other's name contradicts its own range
findings.evidence: galaxyRotationModel.test.ts:270-280, titled "dark mass inferred from the curve gap is zero when the halo is empty", comments "M_dark from V^2 R / G must agree with the model's own mDark10 readout" and then asserts `((vTotal*vTotal - vVisible*vVisible) * radiusKpc) / G_GALAXY` is 0 to 9 decimals. Since vTotalKmS is defined as sqrt(vBulge^2+vDisk^2+vHalo^2) and vVisibleKmS as hypot(vBulge,vDisk), that expression is identically vHalo^2*R/G = 0 whenever haloMass10 = 0 — it is the definition, not a check, and it cannot fail no matter what the displayed equation does. The displayed equation uses M_vis(<R), not vVisible^2R/G, and I recomputed the real disagreement as 0.000 vs 1.421e10 Msun at R = 10 kpc for that same preset; this test is why the P0 above stayed invisible. Separately test:91 is named "MOND velocity at 30 kpc is near 187 km/s" but asserts `expectCloseToRange(vMond, 175, 185)`, a window that excludes 187; the true value I computed is 179.81 km/s.
findings.scenario: A reviewer greps the test suite for the M_dark relation, finds a green test whose title and comment say exactly what they wanted checked, and ships the demo with an on-screen equation that overstates dark matter by 42%. The 187-vs-175-185 test teaches the next reader to trust the name over the assertion.
findings.fix: Rewrite packages/physics/src/galaxyRotationModel.test.ts:270-280 to assert the relation actually displayed: compute `vTotal^2 * R / G - enclosedMass10().visible` and assert it does NOT equal masses.dark for the no-dark-matter preset (pinning the known disk-geometry gap with explicit expected values at R = 5, 8, 10 kpc), so any change to the equation card or the mass model trips it. Fix the title at test:91 to match the computed 179.8 km/s and tighten the range around it.

findings.title: The solar-system inset's planet points are pure R^(-1/2) values, not planetary speeds, so the inset demonstrates the Keplerian law with data generated from it
findings.evidence: main.ts:606-612 hardcodes `{ rNorm: 0.387, vNorm: 1.607 }, { 0.723, 1.176 }, { 1.0, 1.0 }, { 1.524, 0.809 }, { 5.203, 0.439 }`. I checked each against both pure Kepler and the real orbital speeds: r^(-1/2) gives 1.6075, 1.1761, 1.0000, 0.8100, 0.4384 — matching the hardcoded values to 3-4 decimals — while the actual mean speeds normalized to Earth's 29.78 km/s are 1.5903, 1.1760, 1.0000, 0.8083, 0.4385. So Mercury is plotted at 1.607 rather than its true 1.590, and every dot lies on the dashed Keplerian reference line drawn at main.ts:633-640 by construction. The inset also has no axis labels or tick values (only the title at main.ts:656), and the two series use different x normalizations — planets in AU, the galaxy in R/8.2 kpc (main.ts:618) — with nothing on screen saying so.
findings.scenario: A student reads "Solar System vs Galaxy", takes the five dots for measured planetary data, and concludes that observations confirm Keplerian decline — when the dots were computed from the law they are shown confirming. Mercury's plotted value is 1.1% off its real speed. With no axis labels the student also cannot tell that the galaxy curve's x axis is in units of 8.2 kpc while the planets' is in AU.
findings.fix: In apps/demos/src/demos/galaxy-rotation/main.ts:606-612, use the measured mean orbital speeds (47.36, 35.02, 29.78, 24.07, 13.06 km/s normalized to Earth) so the dots are data that happen to land on the law, and cite the source in a comment. Add x and y tick labels to the inset and state both normalizations in the title, e.g. "Solar System (R/1 AU) vs Galaxy (R/8.2 kpc), V normalized".

findings.title: A Unicode math operator reaches reader-visible copy, and the math validator's forbidden-glyph regex cannot catch it
findings.evidence: index.html:241 `<summary>Dark matter ≠ dark energy</summary>` — a Unicode math operator in rendered text, which CLAUDE.md forbids by name alongside ×, −, ≈ and ∝ ("Every equation, symbol, unit and operator that a reader sees is authored as LaTeX"). It ships because scripts/validate-math-formatting.mjs:33 `FORBIDDEN_UNICODE_MATH = /[°☉µμ′″×−∝≈∞αβγ...]/u` omits ≠, and also ≤ ≥ ± ÷ √ → ∂ ∇ ∑ ∏ ∫ ⟨ ⟩ · ‖. The regex does cover the Greek block and the sub/superscript digits, so this is a hole in the character class rather than a missing scan root — apps/demos/src/demos/ is in SCAN_ROOTS at line 20.
findings.scenario: The glyph inherits whatever the surrounding CSS does to it — exactly the failure CLAUDE.md documents for 2026-09-05, when an inherited text-transform turned 94 KaTeX nodes' ν into N and μ into M with every test green. A ≠ under a font-feature or transform change degrades silently, and because the validator's class omits it, every future ≠, ≤, ≥ and ± in any scanned surface ships the same way.
findings.fix: Write `$\neq$` at apps/demos/src/demos/galaxy-rotation/index.html:241 (the page already loads KaTeX and calls initMath), and extend FORBIDDEN_UNICODE_MATH at scripts/validate-math-formatting.mjs:33 with ≠ ≤ ≥ ± ÷ √ ∂ ∇ ∑ ∏ ∫ · ‖ ⟨ ⟩. Run the validator after extending it — other demos will have the same glyphs, and that sweep is the point.

findings.title: compact-toy preset radius 0.12 Rsun is off the radius slider's step grid
findings.evidence: HYDROSTATIC_PRESETS["compact-toy"].radiusSolarRadius = 0.12. index.html:137 `<input id="radiusSlider" type="range" min="0.1" max="20" step="0.05" ...>`, so the allowed values near 0.12 are 0.10, 0.15, 0.20, 0.25 (I enumerated the grid from the min as step base). main.ts:1310 `radiusSlider.value = state.radiusSolarRadius.toFixed(2);` assigns "0.12"; the range control's value sanitization snaps an off-step value to the nearest allowed one, 0.10. main.ts:1316 `radiusValue.textContent = state.radiusSolarRadius.toFixed(2)` still prints 0.12, and the model keeps 0.12 because state is never read back from the slider. The other three off-baseline presets (0.5, 4.8, 1.0) are all on the 0.05 grid, so compact-toy is the only one affected.
findings.scenario: A student clicks 'Compact toy star'. The readout says R = 0.12 Rsun, the slider thumb sits at 0.10, and a screen reader announces 0.10. One Right-Arrow press fires input with value 0.15, so the radius jumps 0.12 -> 0.15 and the central pressure drops by (0.12/0.15)^4 = 0.41 in a single keystroke — the student cannot step through the compact regime at all.
findings.fix: Either change the preset to a grid value (0.10 or 0.15 Rsun — Anna's call, since it sets how extreme the 'compact toy' case is) or change index.html:137 to step="0.01" so 0.12 is reachable and arrow-key nudges are fine-grained near small radii. Add a logic test asserting every preset's massSolarMass and radiusSolarRadius lie on the corresponding slider's step grid.

findings.title: One-sided clamp hides that the 0.06R shell patch extrapolates to negative pressure near the surface
findings.evidence: `const pressureOuterDynePerCm2 = Math.max(0, localPoint.pressureDynePerCm2 - 0.5 * pressureDifferenceDynePerCm2);` — clamped — while pressureInnerDynePerCm2 (line 369) and pressureDifferenceDynePerCm2 are not. logic.ts:627 fixes shellThicknessCm = 0.06 * radiusCm. I recomputed the uniform sun-like balanced patch: at r/R = 0.96, P_in - P_out = 1.549e14 = reported dP (consistent); at r/R = 0.99, P_out clamps to 0 so P_in - P_out = 1.066e14 while pressureDifferenceDynePerCm2 still reports 1.598e14; at r/R = 1.00 the figures are 8.068e13 vs 1.614e14 and the patch spans 0.97R to 1.03R, i.e. 3% of it lies outside the star. The crossover is r/R = 0.9705 balanced and 0.9646 over-supported (solving 0.375(1-x^2) = 0.0225x and 0.027x) — all reachable since shellRadiusSlider is min 0 max 100 step 1.
findings.scenario: A student drags the shell to r/R = 0.99 or 1.00. The hero's avgPressure (main.ts:424) is then computed from a clamped outer pressure, so the arrow-length mapping is driven by numbers that no longer satisfy P_in - P_out = dP, and nothing on screen says the 'thin patch' is now thicker than the local pressure scale height and sticking out of the star.
findings.fix: Make the patch thickness adaptive instead of a fixed 0.06R — e.g. min(0.06R, 0.2 * P/(rho g)) so it stays thin against the local scale height — and return a `patchExceedsSurface` / `pressureFloorApplied` flag from localShellPatchBalance instead of silently clamping, so main.ts can show a state banner at large r/R. The thickness rule is a modelling choice and needs Anna's approval before it becomes load-bearing.

findings.title: taskPrevAlt / taskNextAlt are permanently hidden dead controls duplicating taskPrev / taskNext
findings.evidence: index.html:234 `<div id="guidedTaskActions" class="task-actions" hidden>` containing #taskPrevAlt and #taskNextAlt; main.ts:1367 `guidedTaskActions.hidden = true;` unconditionally on every render, so the container is never shown. main.ts:1371-1375 still maintain `taskPrevAlt.disabled = atFirstStep` and `taskNextAlt.disabled = atLastStep`, and main.ts:1851-1853 bind click listeners to both. Note taskNextAlt's disabled rule omits the prediction gate that taskNext carries (`atLastStep || (student && predict && !predictionChecked)`), so the dead copy would also bypass the gate if it were ever unhidden. Related dead code: buildSummaryCards destructures `supportFactor` and `netDirection` (main.ts:757) and no branch uses either; and the `netBalanced ? "hero-arrow--net" : "hero-arrow--net-unbalanced"` ternary (main.ts:499) sits inside the `netBalanced === false` branch, so "hero-arrow--net" is unreachable.
findings.scenario: A future edit that removes the `hidden` attribute or the forced-hidden line surfaces a second Back/Next pair that lets a student skip the prediction gate the guided flow depends on, and today the duplicate markup plus listeners mislead anyone reading the step-navigation logic.
findings.fix: Delete #guidedTaskActions and its two buttons from index.html, and remove taskPrevAlt/taskNextAlt, their q() lookups, their disabled lines and their click listeners from main.ts; drop the unused supportFactor/netDirection params from buildSummaryCards and the unreachable hero-arrow--net ternary.

findings.title: Tests re-assert the implementation's own formula and never check P(r) against dP/dr
findings.evidence: Lines 35-39: `const expectedCenter = (3 * constants.gravitationalConstantCgs * solarMassG**2) / (8 * Math.PI * solarRadiusCm**4); expectRelativeClose(pressureCenter, expectedCenter, 1e-12);` — the expectation is the implementation's formula (hydrostaticEquilibriumModel.ts:143-147) retyped, so a wrong coefficient copied into both sides passes at 1e-12. The central-toy centre is only checked as `> uniform centre` (line 82). Nothing anywhere asserts that pressureProfile* is the integral of pressureGradient*, and the 'monotonic profiles' test (lines 119-128) uses toBeLessThanOrEqual / toBeGreaterThanOrEqual, which a flat or constant profile would satisfy. I did the missing check myself: central differences of P(r) match the stated dP/dr to 2e-8 relative at r/R = 0.23, 0.37, 0.71, 0.93 for both models, and Simpson quadrature of 4*pi*r^2*rho matches enclosedMassCentralToyG to 5e-15 — so the code is correct, but the suite does not establish it.
findings.scenario: A coefficient typo in pressureProfileCentralToyDynePerCm2 (say 4x^4 written as 3x^4) would leave the Pressure tab plotting a curve inconsistent with the Gradient tab the student is told to compare it against, with every test green — exactly the 'green tests pinned the bug' pattern this repo has already hit.
findings.fix: Replace the tautological central-pressure assertion with an independent one (a hand-computed literal, or a finite-difference check that -(P(r+h)-P(r-h))/(2h) equals rho(r)*g(r) within 1e-6 at r/R = 0.23, 0.37, 0.71, 0.93 for BOTH models), add a quadrature check of enclosedMass* against the trapezoid sum of 4*pi*r^2*rho, and tighten the monotonicity test to strict inequalities where the model is strictly monotone.

findings.title: Local gravity readout is hidden at exactly the step whose prompt asks about gravity
findings.evidence: main.ts:1467 `readoutGravityCard.hidden = guidedStep.id === "compactness";` inside the student-mode branch. GUIDED_STEPS[3] (logic.ts:318-326) is `compactness`, whose prompt is "Hold mass fixed and shrink radius. How do the gravity problem and the required central pressure scale respond?" and whose noticeBody is "Compactness makes support harder". compactness is also the first step where showReadoutStrip is true (logic.ts:443), so this is the student's first sight of the readout strip and the gravity card is the one thing missing from it. Related: the gravity card's secondary line (main.ts:1565) is `r/R=0.55 shell`, a location rather than a value, yet it is gated on state.showNormalizedValues ('Show solar-normalized values').
findings.scenario: A student is asked how the gravity problem responds to shrinking the radius, drags the radius slider, and the local-gravity number is not on screen. They can only infer it from the profile plot's Gravity tab, which the guided flow has pointed away from (compactness focuses the Pressure tab).
findings.fix: Delete the `guidedStep.id === "compactness"` special case in main.ts:1467 so the gravity card follows showReadoutStrip like the others, and move the `r/R=... shell` annotation out of the showNormalizedValues branch (it is a location label, not a normalized value) into the card label.

findings.title: CGS export writes toFixed(4) on values near 1e19, producing 24-character numbers with four meaningless decimals
findings.evidence: logic.ts:238-242 formats every conservation row with `.toFixed(4)`, and lines 215-219 convert them to CGS when units === '201'. I recomputed the Earth-like case: h = 6.283185307 AU^2/yr -> 4.4558e19 cm^2/s, and `(4.4558e19).toFixed(4)` yields the literal string "44558106312230166528.0000" — the trailing digits are float64 representation noise, followed by four decimal places on a quantity known to about 10 significant figures. Total specific energy gives "-4435806888114.9482". The UI readouts escape this because formatReadoutNumber switches to exponential above 1e6 (logic.ts:52-54), but the export path never calls it.
findings.scenario: An ASTR201 student in 201 (CGS) mode clicks Copy results and pastes into their lab writeup. The angular momentum row reads 'Angular momentum h (cm^2/s): 44558106312230166528.0000'. They either transcribe 20 digits of false precision into a calculation or conclude the tool is broken; an instructor grading the sheet cannot tell the significant figures from the noise.
findings.fix: Route the export through the same formatter as the UI: in logic.ts:238-242 replace `.toFixed(4)` with `formatReadoutNumber(value, 4, 'auto')` (it already lives in the same file and switches to exponential above 1e6), or pass the UI's current notation mode into buildExportPayload so the export matches what the student sees on screen. Add a logic.test.ts assertion that the 201-mode h row matches /^4\.4558e\+19$/ rather than a 20-digit integer.

findings.title: Reader-visible units and solar-mass symbols are authored as ASCII instead of KaTeX, which the Unicode-only validator cannot catch
findings.evidence: CLAUDE.md's math table requires LaTeX only for 'Demo HTML, site pages, components, layouts, authored content'. Authored ASCII math remains at index.html:257 (`1.0 M_sun`), 268 (`0.1 M_sun to 10 M_sun.`), 444 (`mm/s^2`), 467/472/477 (`AU^2/yr^2`), 482/487 (`AU^2/yr`) and 513 (`AU / yr / M_sun`), and main.ts:591 writes `${state.massSolar.toFixed(1)} M_sun` into #massDisplay as plain textContent on every update. scripts/validate-math-formatting.mjs tests for Unicode glyphs, so `M_sun` and `s^2` pass it. The readout unit divs are overwritten with real KaTeX by setMathLabel/updateUnitLabels (main.ts:501-516) once JS runs, but #massDisplay and the two hints never are.
findings.scenario: In Newton mode the mass field reads 'Star mass M_*: 1.0 M_sun / 0.1 M_sun to 10 M_sun.' while every other quantity on the same panel is typeset. A student reads 'M_sun' as a variable named M with a subscript 'sun' rather than the solar-mass unit, and the panel's own label right above it uses the typeset $M_*$ — two notations for the same star in adjacent lines. If scripts are blocked or fail, the readout units also fall back to 'mm/s^2' and 'AU^2/yr^2'.
findings.fix: Author them as LaTeX: index.html:257/268/513 become `$M_{\odot}$` forms, index.html:444/467/472/477/482/487 become `$\mathrm{mm}/\mathrm{s}^2$` etc. (matching the TeX already in main.ts:502-505 so the pre-JS and post-JS text agree), and main.ts:591 should use renderMath() from @cosmic/runtime like setMathLabel does rather than writing textContent. Then extend scripts/validate-math-formatting.mjs to flag bare `_sun`, `_odot` and `^2`/`^3` in reader-visible demo HTML, not just Unicode glyphs.

findings.title: An invisible canvas is resized and redrawn every animation frame with a mapping mirrored from the SVG, and the prior review mis-describes it
findings.evidence: style.css:45-52 gives #orbitCanvas `opacity: 0` and `pointer-events: none`, so nothing it draws is ever seen. Yet update() calls drawOrbitCanvas on every frame (main.ts:619), and that function calls getBoundingClientRect(), recomputes the fit, may reassign canvas.width/height, and fills an arc (main.ts:278-322) — a forced layout read per frame for no output. Its mapping is also the opposite handedness from the SVG: `px = cx + rAu*Math.cos(thetaRad)*scale` (main.ts:315) with xMin = -ra - pad and xMax = rp + pad (306-307) puts perihelion on the RIGHT, whereas orbitalToSvg puts it on the LEFT. docs/reviews/keplers-laws.md:94 calls this 'cosmetic' and states 'the Canvas dot appears on the opposite side of the star from the SVG planet' — which is not what happens, because the layer is not displayed at all. The same review's note at line 88 describes the old linear-true-anomaly wedge interpolation, which main.ts:443-454 has since replaced with mean-anomaly sampling.
findings.scenario: Two ways to lose. Someone profiling the demo finds a per-frame layout read and a canvas resize check producing nothing. Or someone makes the layer visible (the CSS comment at style.css:414 says the two layers are deliberately kept 'registered', so that is the stated intent) and a second planet appears mirrored across the star from the real one, since the two mappings disagree. Meanwhile the demo's physics review asserts a visible symptom that cannot occur and reports a fixed defect as open, so it cannot be trusted as the audit artifact for this demo.
findings.fix: Decide and act. If the canvas has no job, delete #orbitCanvas from index.html:30, the .orbit-canvas rules from style.css:45-52, drawOrbitCanvas and its call site from main.ts (278-322, 619), and the resolveCanvasColor probe at main.ts:148-159 that exists only to feed it. If it is meant to carry a trail, make it visible and change main.ts:315 to `px = cx - rAu*Math.cos(thetaRad)*scale` with xMin/xMax swapped so it matches orbitalToSvg (or whichever handedness the mirror finding settles on). Either way correct the two stale statements in docs/reviews/keplers-laws.md (lines 88 and 94).

findings.title: The a slider's initial position disagrees with the initial state, and .sr-only is redefined locally although the theme defines it
findings.evidence: index.html:224 sets the a slider to value="250"; I computed logSliderToValue(250, 0.3, 40) = 10^(log10(0.3) + 0.25*(log10(40) - log10(0.3))) = 1.01943 AU, while state.aAu starts at 1 (main.ts:125) and #aDisplay reads '1.00 AU'. valueToLogSlider(1, 0.3, 40) = 246, so the markup is four steps off. The same mismatch follows every preset, since applyPreset sets state.aAu = a exactly but the slider to the rounded step (main.ts:674-678). Separately, style.css:295-304 redefines `.sr-only` although packages/theme/styles/demo-shell.css:27 already defines it and the demo imports the full chain; only one other demo does this. The static readout placeholders are also pre-computed for the wrong state: index.html:438 says 29.8 km/s and 444 says 5.93 mm/s^2, both correct for a circular 1 AU orbit, while the demo actually opens at perihelion r = 0.983 AU where I computed 30.29 km/s and 6.14 mm/s^2.
findings.scenario: Student presses ArrowRight once on the semi-major axis slider expecting a nudge from 1.00 AU and lands on 1.0268 AU — a 2.7% jump with no step in between, and the period readout moves by 4% for one keypress. If scripts are slow or blocked, the panel shows 29.8 km/s and 5.93 mm/s^2 for a state whose true values are 30.3 and 6.14, numbers a student could copy.
findings.fix: Set index.html:224 to value="246", and in applyPreset (main.ts:674-678) set state.aAu back from the rounded slider position (`state.aAu = logSliderToValue(sliderValue, 0.3, 40)`) so the control and the state never diverge. Delete the local .sr-only block at style.css:295-304 and rely on demo-shell.css. Update the index.html:438/444 placeholders to the perihelion values (30.3, 6.14) or blank them so nothing wrong is readable pre-hydration.

findings.title: The Full and New presets animate the Moon backward through its cycle
findings.evidence: `shortestAngleDelta(fromDeg, toDeg) = ((toDeg - fromDeg + 540) % 360) - 180` returns -180 for the exact antipode in both directions: I computed shortestAngleDelta(0, 180) = -180 and shortestAngleDelta(180, 0) = -180. animateAngle (main.ts:396) tweens `normalizeAngle(start + delta * t)`, so going from Full (0) to New (180) the Moon passes alpha = 0 -> 315 -> 270 -> 225 -> 180, i.e. backward through the waxing phases, and New to Full passes 180 -> 135 -> 90 -> 45 -> 0, backward through the waning ones. Since alpha advances with time in this model (days = ((alpha - 180) mod 360)/360 * 29.53), both are reversed. logic.test.ts:147 even records the value as expected -- "(0, 180) -> -180 (ambiguous; formula yields -180)" -- without noticing it is a direction, not a tie.
findings.scenario: A student at Full Moon clicks the New Moon preset, or presses key 1, and watches the Moon run around the orbit the wrong way for 400 ms while the lit limb grows on the waxing side and the timeline reads WAXING. The animation teaches the reverse of the lunar cycle at exactly the two phases students click most.
findings.fix: In apps/demos/src/demos/moon-phases/animateAngle (main.ts:384-412) choose the forward arc when the two angles are antipodal: use `let delta = shortestAngleDelta(start, targetDeg); if (Math.abs(Math.abs(delta) - 180) < 1e-9) delta = 180;`. Better, since every caller is a time-forward jump, tween the positive direction by default (`delta = ((targetDeg - start) % 360 + 360) % 360`) and reserve the shortest path for the Step-backward button. Add a logic test asserting the tween's midpoint angle is 90 when going 0 -> 180.

findings.title: The export reports rise/set to the minute while the screen says "~8 PM" and the model's neglected 5.1 deg tilt moves it by 26 min
findings.evidence: formatClock (riseSetViewModel.ts:9-15) rounds to whole minutes and renders "HH:MM", and exportPayload.ts:56-57 ships those as "Moon rise time (local solar time)". main.ts:336 renders the same number through formatApproxTime, which rounds to the nearest hour and prefixes "~". At 45 N on the June solstice with a full moon I computed rise = 19.71 h: the UI shows "Rises ~8 PM" and the export shows "19:43" for the same state. The model's own docstring lists what is dropped -- "circular orbits, zero ecliptic latitude, local solar time, no refraction or parallax, and no lunar orbital tilt". I quantified the largest of those: perturbing the declination by the Moon's +/-5.145 deg ecliptic latitude moves the same rise from 19:17 to 20:12, a 55 min spread, so minute-level digits are false precision by a factor of about 25.
findings.scenario: A student copies results into a lab writeup, records "Moon rise 19:43", then compares it with an almanac or their own observation and finds a 30-50 min discrepancy they cannot account for -- because the export's two digits imply a precision the model does not have and neither the export notes nor the readout states the omission. Worse, the same student's screenshot says "~8 PM", so their table and their figure disagree.
findings.fix: In apps/demos/src/demos/moon-phases/riseSetViewModel.ts round formatClock to the nearest 15 min (or drop to the same whole-hour "~H AM/PM" form main.ts uses) so the export and the readout cannot disagree, and add to exportPayload.ts's notes: "Rise/set is good to about +/-30 min: the model drops the Moon's 5.1 deg ecliptic latitude, refraction and parallax." Show the same caveat beside #rise-set-text, which currently states no assumptions at all -- with Advanced off it is silently an equator, equinox number.

findings.title: The speed control is labeled 1x/5x/10x, with no units and no reference the multiplier is against
findings.evidence: index.html:456-460 offers `<option value="1">1x</option>`, `5x`, `10x`. animation.ts:4-7 turns that value into `degreesPerSecondFromSpeed = (360 / synodicMonthDays) * speed`, so speed = 1 advances 360/29.53 = 12.19 deg per wall-clock second, i.e. one synodic DAY per second -- a time compression of 86,400x, not 1x. The invariants require "Units in variable names and on every label, readout and export"; `animationSpeed` (main.ts:277) carries no unit in its name either, and main.ts's two fallbacks disagree (`|| 5` at line 277, `|| 1` at line 726).
findings.scenario: A student reads "1x" as real time and concludes the Moon visibly moves around its orbit in half a minute, or cannot answer "how long does this animation represent?" -- a question the timeline's own "Day 0 of 29.53" invites. Nothing on the page connects the transport speed to the 29.53 d period the demo is teaching.
findings.fix: Relabel the options in apps/demos/src/demos/moon-phases/index.html to their actual units -- "1 day/s", "5 days/s", "10 days/s" -- and rename the variable to animationSpeedDaysPerSecond in main.ts with one fallback value used in both places. The select's visible label can then read "Speed (days per second)", which also makes the 29.53 d cycle time computable from the screen. apps/site/tests/moon-phases.spec.ts:270 asserts the inputValue "5", not the label, so it is unaffected.

findings.title: `d` is used as the unit symbol for days, which the project reserves for distance
findings.evidence: index.html:531 `14.8d`, and exportPayload.ts:54 `{ name: "Days since new (d)", ... }`; logic.ts:281 also writes "Day N of 29.53" with no unit at all. CLAUDE.md is categorical: "Symbols in UI copy, model notes, exports and docs: D = physical diameter, d = distance. Never reuse D/d for other quantities -- name them." The invariants file repeats it. This demo is the golden reference the remaining demos are told to copy, and the exhibit sits next to parallax-distance and angular-size, where d is a distance in the same readout styling.
findings.scenario: A student moves between angular-size (where the readout d is a distance in km) and moon-phases (where d is days) within one lab and reads one as the other; or an instructor copying this demo's readout markup as the golden pattern propagates the collision. The Station Mode column header "Days since new (d)" lands in an exported table beside other demos' d columns.
findings.fix: Either write the unit out in apps/demos/src/demos/moon-phases/index.html:531 and exportPayload.ts:54 as "days" (the readout__unit span is styled for short strings but "days" fits the existing "%" / "deg" pattern), or amend the D/d rule in CLAUDE.md and .agents/references/invariants.md to carve out the SI day symbol explicitly. Pick one and make it the same everywhere -- the current state is the rule being silently broken in the reference implementation.

findings.title: No 320 px reflow coverage for this demo, and the Moon's drag target is 22 px there
findings.evidence: `const PLAY_ROUTES = ["play/conservation-laws/"];` with the comment at lines 49-50: "Play routes are added one demo at a time, for demos at `candidate` readiness or above whose `/play/` page has been separately verified not to scroll sideways at 320px." moon-phases is at `readiness: candidate` (moon-phases.md:10) and is not in the list, so the horizontal-scroll check has never run against it. Touch targets: #orbital-svg has viewBox "0 45 400 280" with CSS `width: 100%; height: auto` (style.css:89-94), so in a ~290 px-wide panel at a 320 px viewport the scale is 290/400 = 0.725 and the draggable Moon (MOON_RADIUS = 15, logic.ts:11) renders 2*15*0.725 = 21.8 CSS px across -- under the 24 px WCAG 2.5.8 minimum and far under 44 px. The eight timeline buttons are worse in a different way: at widths under 700 px style.css:393 hides their text, leaving a 20 px icon in a button with 4 px of vertical padding, about 28 px tall.
findings.scenario: A student on a phone -- the likeliest device for a station exhibit -- tries to drag the Moon, repeatedly misses a 22 px target, and has no visible alternative (the "Focus Moon" keyboard path is useless on touch and the drag-hint only says "Drag the Moon"). If anything on the page overflows at 320 px, nothing in CI would report it.
findings.fix: Add "play/moon-phases/" to PLAY_ROUTES in apps/site/tests/reflow.spec.ts once a 320 px pass is confirmed, following the file's own one-demo-at-a-time rule and its `scrollTo(2000,0)` then `scrollX > 0` method rather than scrollWidth. Enlarge the hit area without changing the drawing: add a transparent `<circle r="26" fill="transparent" pointer-events="all">` as the first child of #moon-group in index.html (26 in a 400 viewBox is about 38 px at 320 px wide), and raise `.timeline-phase` padding to reach a 44 px min-height under the 700 px breakpoint in style.css.

findings.title: ASCII and Unicode math in reader-visible copy where the KaTeX-only invariant requires LaTeX
findings.evidence: index.html:248 `Chord: AU | deltaPhi deg` — "deltaPhi" and "deg" spelled out in HTML, where the rule is `$\Delta\phi$` and `$^{\circ}$`. index.html:231 and main.ts:864, 873 render "deltaTheta" in prose into SVG text. main.ts:719, 727, 742 build labels like `Now 37deg`, `A 37deg`. main.ts:927 and 931 emit `±` directly into HTML (`\` ± ${...}\``) — a Unicode math operator that should be `$\pm$`; FORBIDDEN_UNICODE_MATH in scripts/validate-math-formatting.mjs:33 does not include U+00B1 and could not see the escape anyway, which is exactly the escape case .agents/references/invariants.md warns about. The validator does scan apps/demos/src/demos (SCAN_ROOTS, line 20), so these pass only because they are ASCII or an uncovered codepoint.
findings.scenario: A student reads "deltaPhi 106.0 deg" and "Measured shift deltaTheta = 159.73 mas" in a course whose notation is $\Delta\phi$ and $\Delta\theta$, and sees a bare "±" rendered in the body font beside a KaTeX label — the same inconsistency class that in September 2026 let an inherited text-transform turn $\nu$ into "N" across 14 demos, because a glyph in a string cannot be checked.
findings.fix: In apps/demos/src/demos/parallax-distance/index.html:248 write `$\Delta\phi$` and `$^{\circ}$`; in main.ts replace the `±` template literals (927, 931) with `renderMath("\\pm")` from @cosmic/runtime, and render the phase labels as "Now 37" plus a degree mark set in HTML rather than inside SVG text (or keep SVG text ASCII and add a note in CLAUDE.md's surface table extending the canvas exemption to SVG <text>, so the rule and the code agree). Add U+00B1 and U+2260 to FORBIDDEN_UNICODE_MATH in scripts/validate-math-formatting.mjs:33 and make the scanner decode \uXXXX escapes before matching.

findings.title: Units in every readout sub-line sit outside cp-readout__unit, breaking the Readout Typography Contract
findings.evidence: The six main values wrap units correctly (e.g. index.html:242 `mas`), but every `cp-readout__sub` line puts the unit in bare text: line 243 `Signed: mas`, 248 `... AU | ... deg`, 253 ` arcsec | ... mas`, 258 ` ly`, 263 ` ly`. CLAUDE.md invariant 3 is unqualified: "Units MUST be separated into `` elements. Values render in amber monospace, units in ice-blue." The contract test checks only `unitSpans.length >= 5` (design-contracts.test.ts:155-158), which the six main values already satisfy, so the nine unwrapped sub-line units are invisible to it.
findings.scenario: Half the numbers in the readout strip — the signed shift, the chord, the phase separation, the arcsec parallax, both ly distances — render their units in body text at body colour while the other half render ice-blue, so the strip reads as two different components, and a student scanning for "which number is in arcsec" loses the colour cue the design system trains them on.
findings.fix: In apps/demos/src/demos/parallax-distance/index.html wrap each sub-line unit: `mas` etc. on lines 243, 248 (AU and the degree mark), 253 (arcsec, mas), 258 and 263 (ly). Then raise the contract test (design-contracts.test.ts:155) from a count to a rule: assert that no `cp-readout__sub` block contains a bare unit token (mas|arcsec|AU|pc|ly) outside a `cp-readout__unit` span.

findings.title: Live region is force-re-announced on every slider input tick, so dragging distance or sigma floods a screen reader
findings.evidence: `distancePcRange` fires `input` per step and calls setDistancePc (main.ts:1249-1251), which ends in `setLiveRegionText(status, "Distance updated. Capture A and B again.")` (main.ts:951); the sigma slider does the same at main.ts:1324. packages/runtime/src/liveRegion.ts:1-18 does not debounce — when the text is unchanged it deliberately clears `textContent` and re-sets it on the next frame specifically to force a repeat announcement. So a drag across the 49,990-step distance track queues one forced re-announcement per step on an `aria-live="polite"` `aria-atomic="true"` region (index.html:159). Each of those input events also runs clearCaptures(false) (main.ts:947).
findings.scenario: A screen-reader student arrows the sigma slider from 1.0 to 5.0 mas: 40 input events, each one forcing "Measurement uncertainty updated. Capture A and B again." The speech queue never drains long enough for them to hear the readouts they are changing, and on the distance slider the same message repeats indefinitely while any pointer drag is in progress.
findings.fix: In apps/demos/src/demos/parallax-distance/main.ts, announce on commit rather than on every tick: keep render() on `input` and move the two setLiveRegionText calls (951 via a new flag on setDistancePc, and 1324) to `change` handlers on #distancePcRange and #sigmaMas, or debounce them behind a ~400 ms trailing timer. Announce the resulting value too ("Distance 25.0 parsecs, captures cleared") so the message carries information.

findings.title: The scatter cloud implies 2-D isotropic, repeatable measurement noise; the model is 1-D along the axis and deterministic
findings.evidence: renderScatter (main.ts:522-536) lays 8 points from the fixed SCATTER_TEMPLATES table (main.ts:101-110) at angles 18-332 deg and radius scales 0.35-0.94 around the marker — a 2-D cloud, drawn from the same template for A and B at the same radius, so the two epochs' "scatter" is pixel-identical. The actual noise is one scalar along the measurement axis (`applyAxisNoiseToOffset`, logic.ts:196-203), and it is a deterministic hash of (epochLabel, phase rounded to 0.1 deg, distancePc, sigmaMas) (logic.ts:170-192), so re-capturing at the same settings reproduces the identical measurement exactly. The error circle (index.html:214-215) is likewise a circle for a 1-D sigma.
findings.scenario: Student is asked to "take repeated measurements and see the scatter": they press Capture A five times at the same phase and get the identical reading every time, because the noise is a hash of the settings. Meanwhile the picture shows a 2-D cloud of eight points identical for A and B, so they read it as five realisations of an isotropic error — and conclude that the perpendicular direction carries measurement error too, when the model has none there.
findings.fix: In apps/demos/src/demos/parallax-distance/main.ts, draw the uncertainty 1-D to match the model: replace the circle and the 8-point template with an along-axis error bar of half-length sigma*exaggeration*pxPerMas (and drop SCATTER_TEMPLATES and renderScatter). For repeatability, add a draw counter to the noise key in logic.ts:175 and a "Re-measure" button, so pressing capture again gives a genuinely new draw while the sequence stays reproducible per session.

findings.title: The design-contract architecture test greps for an import string instead of checking that physics is not re-implemented
findings.evidence: design-contracts.test.ts:150-162, under the heading "Architecture compliance": `expect(mainTs).toContain('from "@cosmic/physics"')`, `expect(mainTs).toContain('from "./logic"')`, and two negative checks that main.ts does not define formatNumber or clamp. All four pass today while logic.ts owns the longitude propagation, the separation, the alignment criterion, the classification and the year-to-day conversion (see the architecture finding above). The test only inspects main.ts and never reads logic.ts, so the file where the re-derived physics actually lives is outside the contract's field of view.
findings.scenario: The invariant "demo code never re-derives equations" is reported as enforced and green while the demo owns five equations. The next demo copies this contract file as the migration checklist tells it to, inherits the same blind spot, and the architecture drift spreads with full test coverage.
findings.fix: In apps/demos/src/demos/planetary-conjunctions/design-contracts.test.ts, read logic.ts as well and assert the absence of physics there -- no Math.sqrt of a cubed semi-major axis, no 2*pi*t/P propagation, no hardcoded second-per-year or AU constants -- and assert that the physics names the demo uses are imported from @cosmic/physics rather than defined locally. A grep for an import line is not a contract.

findings.title: Speed is labelled as a bare multiplier ("10x") but the quantity is days per real second
findings.evidence: index.html:36-40 renders `Speed` with `10x`, and the export repeats it at main.ts:369 as `{ name: "Speed multiplier", value: speedSlider.value + "x" }`. The code says what it really is -- main.ts:265-266: "// Advance simulation: speed multiplier in days per real second" then `elapsedDays += dtSec * speed;`. So "10x" means 10 simulated days per wall-clock second, not ten times anything the student can see. The project invariant requires units on every reader-visible number, and this control is the only place in the demo where a quantity carries no unit.
findings.scenario: Student reads "Speed 10x" and takes it to mean the animation is ten times faster than some baseline, so they cannot predict how long to wait for an opposition. A student trying to reason that one Mars opposition should take 780/10 = 78 s has to reverse-engineer the unit from the day counter, and the exported payload records "10x" with no way for an instructor to reconstruct the run.
findings.fix: In apps/demos/src/demos/planetary-conjunctions/index.html change the value span's trailing text to the real unit (days per second) and add an aria-valuetext in main.ts so the slider announces the unit; change the export entry at main.ts:369 to "Time rate (days per real second)". Also delete the now-redundant input listener at main.ts:345-347, since tick() already rewrites speedValue every frame.

findings.title: The separation readout does not say it is heliocentric, in a demo about how things look from Earth
findings.evidence: index.html:132-135 labels the readout just "Angular separation" with unit deg, and main.ts:200,247 fills it from `angularSeparationDeg(earthAngle, targetAngle)` -- the difference of two heliocentric longitudes. The model notes do qualify it (index.html:166, "the heliocentric angular separation") and logic.ts:117-119 warns that the function name is historical, but the readout a student actually watches does not. The exhibit's own learning goal and predict_prompt are about separation as seen from Earth, which is a different number: at the inferior conjunction of Venus the heliocentric separation shown is 0 deg while the Earth-centred elongation from the Sun is also near 0, but at a Mars opposition the readout shows 0 deg where the Earth-centred elongation is 180 deg.
findings.scenario: Student watches the separation readout fall to 0.0 deg at a Mars opposition and concludes that Mars and the Sun are 0 deg apart in the sky -- that is, that Mars is behind the Sun and invisible -- which is the exact opposite of an opposition, when Mars is up all night. The misconception the exhibit lists (that a conjunction means the bodies are close) is reinforced rather than corrected.
findings.fix: Relabel index.html:133 as the heliocentric longitude difference (matching the two lambda labels directly above it), and add the Earth-centred elongation as a second readout computed from the two positions. Those two numbers side by side are the whole lesson the exhibit copy promises.

findings.title: Alignment announcements fire into the live region every few seconds with no way to stop them
findings.evidence: main.ts:204-211 calls setLiveRegionText from inside render(), which runs on every animation frame; the call is gated to the rising edge, so it fires once per alignment, but the alignment rate is set by the speed slider. At the slider maximum of 100 days per second (index.html:38) the synodic periods I computed give an announcement every P_syn/100 seconds: Saturn 3.8 s, Jupiter 4.0 s, Venus 5.8 s, Mars 7.8 s. The same region (index.html:70, role="status" aria-live="polite" aria-atomic="true") also carries the copy-results feedback. Because there is no pause control, the stream cannot be stopped without leaving the page.
findings.scenario: Screen-reader user raises the speed to reach an opposition sooner. From then on the demo interrupts them every four seconds with "Opposition 7 at day 2643", overriding whatever they were reading, and because there is no pause button the only escape is to navigate away or reload with the slider back down.
findings.fix: Once the playbar lands (see the time-control finding), stop announcing during continuous playback and announce on explicit user action -- a step, a scrub release, or a pause -- or coalesce to at most one announcement every few seconds. The copy-results status should also move to its own region so a pending alignment message cannot swallow "Copied results to clipboard".

findings.title: The diagram's accessible name never changes, so no non-visual user learns what is on the stage
findings.evidence: index.html:76: `<svg id="conjunctionSvg" class="conjunction" viewBox="0 0 600 600" role="img" aria-label="Orbital diagram showing Earth and target planet">`. Declaring role="img" makes the whole drawing a single opaque image whose alternative text is that one fixed sentence; main.ts never touches the attribute (no setAttribute on conjunctionSvg anywhere in the file). The selected planet, the two longitudes, whether an alignment is in progress, and the amber alignment ray that appears at index.html:90 are all invisible to that label. The target's name is in a `<text>` element (index.html:102) which role="img" hides from assistive technology.
findings.scenario: Screen-reader user tabs to the stage, hears "Orbital diagram showing Earth and target planet", and switches to Saturn. The label is identical. They have no indication that the drawing changed, that Earth's ring is now a sixth of its previous size, or that an alignment ray is currently drawn.
findings.fix: In apps/demos/src/demos/planetary-conjunctions/main.ts, update the SVG's aria-label from the render step whenever the selection or the alignment state changes -- naming the target, the two longitudes in degrees and whether the bodies are currently aligned -- throttled to meaningful changes rather than written every frame.

findings.title: The prior physics review records "Issues Found: None" and the parity audit it gates on is an empty stub
findings.evidence: docs/reviews/planetary-conjunctions.md:49-51: "## Issues Found -- None. All physics equations, synodic period calculations, coordinate conventions, and conjunction detection logic are correct." Line 15 of the same table stamps the counting defect CORRECT: "Conjunction detection: separation <= threshold (5 deg) ... with rising-edge counting ... CORRECT", and line 36 calls the 1-day guard sufficient -- neither notices the 1.39%-of-P_syn lead I measured above. Its line citations have also drifted: it cites logic.ts:174-177 for orbitToSvg (now 223-233), logic.ts:184-192 for orbitRadiusPx (now 239-247) and twoBodyAnalytic.ts:269-275 for synodicPeriod (now 285-291). The exhibit's readinessReason (planetary-conjunctions.md:11) blocks promotion on "parity ... signoff", and parityAuditPath points to docs/audits/migrations/planetary-conjunctions-parity.md, which is six "Pending detailed parity review" lines -- for a demo with no legacy counterpart (`ls ~/Teaching/astr101-sp26/demos/` shows planetary-climate-sandbox, nothing for conjunctions), so that gate can never be satisfied as written.
findings.scenario: Whoever next triages this demo reads "Issues Found: None" on a dated physics review and promotes it toward launch-ready without re-deriving anything, shipping the "yr days" readout and the early event announcements to a class. The parity gate that was supposed to catch it cannot close, because there is nothing to establish parity against.
findings.fix: Replace the verdict in docs/reviews/planetary-conjunctions.md with the defects above and refresh its line citations. In apps/site/src/content/demos/planetary-conjunctions.md, keep readiness at experimental and status at draft, and restate readinessReason in terms of gates that can actually close -- the alignment-day detector, the elapsed-time unit, a time control, and the from-Earth view the copy promises -- then either fill in docs/audits/migrations/planetary-conjunctions-parity.md with the intentional deltas of a from-scratch demo or drop parityAuditPath.

findings.title: Plot tick and axis labels render at 3.5-4.2 CSS px at phone widths
findings.evidence: index.html:269 gives the plot `viewBox="0 0 1000 400"` and style.css:154-159 sets `.retro__svg { width: 100%; height: auto }`, so the whole viewBox scales uniformly with the container. At a 320 px viewport the scale factor is 320/1000 = 0.32, so the y-grid and t-grid labels set at `font-size: 11` (main.ts:627, 652) render at 3.5 CSS px and the axis titles set at `font-size: 13` (main.ts:662, 671) render at 4.2 px. The 900 px breakpoint (style.css:475) collapses the grid to one column, which makes the plot full-width but does not change the uniform scaling. CLAUDE.md records that `/play/` routes are not yet in reflow.spec.ts, so there is no test.
findings.scenario: A student opens the exhibit on a phone in lab, can see the shape of the curve and the pink band, and cannot read a single axis number - so they cannot report the day a retrograde starts or ends, which is exactly what the station worksheet (main.ts:1682) asks them to record.
findings.fix: Set a minimum rendered text size by sizing SVG text in a unit that does not scale with the viewBox (apply `font-size` via CSS in px on the `<text>` elements with `vector-effect`-style non-scaling behaviour, or switch the plot to a fixed-height viewBox whose width tracks the container). Add `/play/retrograde-motion/` to apps/site/tests/reflow.spec.ts at 320 px and assert a minimum computed font size on the axis labels.

findings.title: Tooltip trigger buttons are 21.6 px, under the WCAG 2.2 target-size minimum
findings.evidence: style.css:109-111 sets `.retro-tip__trigger { inline-size: 1.2rem; block-size: 1.2rem }`. The root font size is `--cp-text-md: 1.125rem` applied to `html` in packages/theme/styles/tokens.css:163 and :338, which resolves to 18 px, so 1.2rem = 21.6 px square - below the 24 x 24 CSS px minimum of WCAG 2.2 SC 2.5.8. There are two such triggers (index.html:207-214 and :242-249). By contrast the transport buttons do comply: packages/theme asserts `min-height: 44px` on `.cp-playbar__btn` (components.test.ts:139).
findings.scenario: A student on a touch device tries to tap the "?" next to "Relative angular speed proxy" or next to the plot title, misses, and instead hits the surrounding label or the accordion. The two inline explanations of the demo's least self-evident readouts are the hardest things on the page to reach.
findings.fix: Raise `.retro-tip__trigger` in style.css:109-111 to at least `1.5rem` (27 px) square, or keep the 21.6 px visual circle and add a transparent `::before` hit area padded out to 24 px, which preserves the compact look. Add the check to the a11y spec so it does not regress.

findings.title: Zodiac ring is labelled sidereal but uses tropical sign midpoints at exactly 30 deg spacing
findings.evidence: logic.ts:241-243 comments "The 12 zodiac constellations with their approximate ecliptic longitudes. These are sidereal positions (not tropical)." The values that follow (:244-257) are Ari 15, Tau 45, Gem 75 ... Psc 345 - the exact midpoints of the twelve 30-degree TROPICAL signs, which is what logic.test.ts:615-620 pins ("labels are evenly spaced at 30-degree intervals"). The model's longitudes are referred to the J2000 mean equinox (the Standish elements at retrogradeMotionModel.ts:33-42), so they are tropical/J2000 longitudes, and the real IAU constellation boundaries along the ecliptic are strongly unequal (Virgo spans about 44 deg, Scorpius about 7 deg) and offset from the like-named signs by roughly 24 degrees of precession.
findings.scenario: A student turns on the zodiac ring to answer "which constellation is Mars in right now?", reads off Leo because the planet sits between 120 and 150 deg, and is wrong - at that longitude Mars is in Cancer, because the constellation Leo begins about 24 deg further along than the sign Leo. The demo teaches the astrological sign grid while labelling it with constellation abbreviations.
findings.fix: Either relabel the ring honestly as tropical SIGNS (and say so in the checkbox label and model notes), or replace the twelve equal midpoints in logic.ts:244-257 with the actual IAU ecliptic constellation boundaries and place each label at its own span's centre - then update logic.test.ts:615-620, which currently asserts the uniform 30 deg spacing and would block the correct data.

findings.title: The lambda arc can be shown without its 0 deg baseline and carries no numeric value
findings.evidence: index.html:122-129 exposes "Show 0 deg reference axis" (#showReferenceAxis) and "Show lambda angle arc" (#showLambdaArc) as two independent checkboxes. main.ts:864 draws the +x reference ray only when `state.showReferenceAxis` is true, while main.ts:1014 draws the arc whenever `state.showLambdaArc` is true. Both default to unchecked (index.html:119, 123, 127, confirmed by spec.ts:578-580). The arc label is the bare string at main.ts:1036 with no value. Separately, both checkbox labels are reader-visible math written in ASCII ("0 deg reference axis", "lambda angle arc"), as is the SVG axis label "0 deg" at main.ts:877 and the Sky View label at main.ts:1147.
findings.scenario: A student checks only "Show lambda angle arc" - the natural single choice when the readout says lambda - and gets an arc floating in space with no visible ray to measure it from and no number on it.
