findings.evidence: `rollupOptions` sets only `input` (line 35); there is no `output.manualChunks`. Rollup therefore groups every module shared by two or more of the 20 HTML entries into one chunk and names it after an arbitrary member — which is why the 287,754-byte KaTeX-plus-runtime-plus-physics chunk every demo loads is called `stellarLifetimeModel-yTTURjSP.js`, after a stellar-evolution model that `angular-size` and `parallax-distance` have no use for. Its sibling CSS chunk, `stellarLifetimeModel-D2lIc1rk.css` (28,839 B), is in fact KaTeX's stylesheet.
findings.scenario: Nobody can reason about the payload from the build output. A reviewer looking at `/play/angular-size/`'s asset list sees a 288 KB chunk named after a stellar-lifetime model and cannot tell whether that is a code-splitting bug, an accidental import, or (as it is) mostly a LaTeX renderer — so the real finding above went unnoticed through several audits. Any future split also silently re-partitions when one demo's imports change.
findings.fix: Add an `output.manualChunks` that names the boundaries the architecture already has: one chunk for `katex`, one for `@cosmic/runtime`, one for `@cosmic/physics`, leaving per-demo code in its entry. The names then describe the payload, and a chunk growing becomes visible in `ls -S` instead of hiding inside a mislabeled blob.

findings.title: Lexend ships a license for a font that does not exist, and fonts.css declares a face for the missing file
findings.evidence: `src: url("/fonts/Lexend.woff2")`, but `ls apps/site/public/fonts` lists only Inter.woff2, Outfit.woff2, SourceSans3.woff2 and SourceSans3-Italic.woff2 — no Lexend.woff2 anywhere in the repo. `Lexend-LICENSE.txt` (4,436 B) nevertheless ships in `public/fonts` and is one of the 7 tracked files there, and `grep -rn "Lexend" packages apps` finds no `font-family` reference outside this dead file.
findings.scenario: Harmless today because nothing imports fonts.css. It matters as evidence: the licenses directory claims a typeface the project does not use, which is exactly the kind of thing an attribution audit of a publicly deployed teaching site flags, and it misleads anyone deciding which fonts are load-bearing.
findings.fix: Remove the Lexend `@font-face` block and `apps/site/public/fonts/Lexend-LICENSE.txt` in the same change that removes fonts.css.

findings.title: Every dataset declares license "UNSPECIFIED" and the gate passes it
findings.evidence: All 8 datasets across the three data packages carry the literal `"license": "UNSPECIFIED"` — data-astr101/manifest.json:19, data-spectra/manifest.json:24,44,65,84, data-telescopes/manifest.json:26,46,65. scripts/validate-datasets.mjs:70-75 puts "license" in `requiredStrings` and checks it only with `isNonEmptyString`, so the placeholder satisfies the gate: `const requiredStrings = ["id", "title", "description", "unitsPolicy", "license"];`. The gate is green on every dataset in the repo while no dataset has a license.
findings.scenario: A colleague at another institution adopts the parallax demo for their ASTR 101, or a reviewer evaluates the IUSE submission for reusability. They open the manifest to find the terms and read "UNSPECIFIED" — which legally means all rights reserved, not permissive. Nothing in the repo tells them whether they may redistribute `nearbyStars`, and `pnpm lint` reports no problem, so no one on the project ever sees the gap either.
findings.fix: Change the license check in scripts/validate-datasets.mjs:70-75 from a non-empty-string test to membership in an allowlist of real SPDX identifiers (plus an explicit `"license-pending"` sentinel if a staging state is needed), then fill in each of the 8 datasets. For the derived ones this means naming the upstream terms (NIST ASD is public domain; Gaia/Hipparcos data are CC BY).

findings.title: Measured catalog parallaxes are labeled "project-authored" with no citation
findings.evidence: The values are published measurements to 0.1 mas: Proxima Centauri 768.5, Alpha Cen 747.0, Barnard's Star 548.3, Wolf 359 419.1, Sirius 379.2, Procyon 284.6, Vega 130.2 (lines 30-39). These are the Hipparcos/van Leeuwen and Gaia figures, not teaching approximations. packages/data-astr101/manifest.json:16-18 declares `"kind": "project-authored"` with notes "Approximate values curated for teaching examples; not a single upstream catalog." The same `"kind": "project-authored"` appears on all 8 datasets (data-spectra/manifest.json:21,41,62,81; data-telescopes/manifest.json:23,43,62) including one whose own notes say wavelengths are "anchored to NIST strong line tables" (data-spectra/manifest.json:22) — which is by definition derived-from-upstream, not authored.
findings.scenario: A student computes d = 1/p for Barnard's Star, gets 1.824 pc, and asks where 548.3 mas came from and what its uncertainty is. There is no answer in the repo: no catalog, no epoch, no error bar, and the manifest actively asserts the project made the number up. A four-significant-figure parallax with no uncertainty and no source is exactly the kind of number a student should be taught never to accept, presented by the teaching resource itself.
findings.fix: Add a `provenance.kind` enum to scripts/validate-datasets.mjs (e.g. `project-authored` | `derived` | `upstream`) and require `source`, `citation` and `accessed` fields whenever kind is not `project-authored`. Then set starsNearby to the catalog actually used (Gaia DR3 or van Leeuwen 2007 Hipparcos reduction), add a `parallaxErrorMas` field, and reclassify the NIST-anchored line list as derived.

findings.title: KaTeX CSS and fonts are vendored into both apps with no MIT notice
findings.evidence: `copyKatexBundle` (lines 50-56) copies only `katex.min.css` and the `fonts/` directory, and `main()` (lines 70-78) runs it into apps/site/public/assets/katex, apps/demos/public/assets/katex and apps/demos/src/assets/katex. `ls apps/site/public/assets/katex/` returns exactly `fonts` and `katex.min.css`. A repo-wide find for LICENSE files under apps/*/public returns only the three font licenses in apps/site/public/fonts — no KaTeX notice anywhere. KaTeX is MIT, which requires the copyright and permission notice to accompany all copies or substantial portions.
findings.scenario: The site ships ~60 redistributed font binaries plus a third-party stylesheet with the upstream notice stripped, on a university resource whose README advertises a careful dual-license model. Anyone auditing redistribution compliance (an institutional review, a journal software statement, an IUSE reviewer) finds the one thing MIT actually asks for is missing — and the same omission is replicated into three output directories by a script that runs on every build.
findings.fix: Add a `copyFile(path.join(distDir, "..", "LICENSE"), path.join(targetKatexDir, "LICENSE"))` to `copyKatexBundle` so the notice travels with the bundle into all three targets, and add a top-level THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md listing KaTeX (MIT), the three OFL fonts, three.js and uPlot with their terms.

findings.title: Outfit font ships with no license; a Lexend license ships with no font
findings.evidence: apps/site/public/fonts contains Inter.woff2 + Inter-LICENSE.txt, SourceSans3.woff2/-Italic.woff2 + SourceSans3-LICENSE.txt, Outfit.woff2 (14,760 bytes) with no Outfit license, and Lexend-LICENSE.txt whose first copyright line reads "Copyright 2018 The Lexend Project Authors ... with Reserved Font Name 'RevReading Lexend'" — for a font that is not in the directory and is not tracked by git. Outfit is the project's display face: packages/theme/styles/tokens.css:155 sets `--cp-font-display: "Outfit", ...` and Layout.astro:44 preloads it, so it is the one font on every page heading.
findings.scenario: The site redistributes its primary display typeface with no license text, while shipping to every visitor the license of a different typeface it does not use. A reader who follows Lexend-LICENSE.txt is told about a Reserved Font Name that has nothing to do with the file being served, and the OFL's requirement that the license accompany the font is unmet for the font that actually ships.
findings.fix: Add Outfit-LICENSE.txt (Outfit is OFL-1.1, Copyright 2020 The Outfit Project Authors) and delete Lexend-LICENSE.txt, or restore Lexend.woff2 if the headings were meant to be Lexend — packages/theme/styles/fonts.css:19 still expects it, which suggests a half-finished font swap.

findings.title: Instructor pages grant adaptation rights the repo license does not give
findings.evidence: Line 63 renders, on every instructor-notes page: "Teaching notes for this exhibit. Free to adapt for your own course." LICENSE-CONTENT.md licenses "original written content, instructional materials, figures, and visual assets" under CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 — NonCommercial and ShareAlike, with attribution required. The page text states none of those three conditions and the word "Free" implies none apply.
findings.scenario: An instructor at a for-profit institution, or one bundling the notes into a paid course pack, reads the page and reasonably concludes the material is theirs to adapt. The NonCommercial clause forbids exactly that, ShareAlike obliges them to relicense their derivative, and BY obliges attribution. The most prominent licensing statement a reader actually encounters contradicts the repository's own terms — and it is the instructor pages, the ones most likely to be reused, that carry it.
findings.fix: Replace the sentence with the real terms and a link: "Free to adapt for your own course under CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 — credit Cosmic Playground, no commercial use, share adaptations under the same license." Hoist the string into one component so it cannot drift from LICENSE-CONTENT.md.

findings.title: PR events share the pages concurrency group and cancel in-flight deploys
findings.evidence: The workflow triggers on `push: branches: [main]`, `pull_request: branches: [main]` and `workflow_dispatch` (lines 3-8), and declares a single workflow-level `concurrency: group: pages` with `cancel-in-progress: true` (lines 15-17). The group key is a constant — it contains no `github.ref` or `github.event_name` — so a PR's verify run and a main push's verify+deploy run compete for the same slot and cancel each other. GitHub's own Pages starter workflow uses `cancel-in-progress: false` on this group for precisely this reason.
findings.scenario: Anna pushes a fix to main; the verify job starts its ~several-minute gate chain. She opens or updates a PR while it runs. The main run is cancelled — including, if the timing lands there, after `upload-pages-artifact` and inside `deploy-pages`. The run's conclusion is "cancelled", not "failed", so no failure notification fires and nothing retries it; main's newest commit silently never reaches the site, and the deployed page keeps serving the previous commit with no signal that it is stale. CLAUDE.md already records the symptom ("Pushing to main cancels an in-progress deploy") as a gotcha to live with rather than a config bug.
findings.fix: Key the group by ref and exclude PRs from the deploy slot: `group: pages-${{ github.ref }}`, and set `cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' }}` so superseded PR runs are still cancelled while a main deploy always runs to completion.

findings.title: The visual regression suite runs in neither workflow, so 3.34 MB of baselines gate nothing
findings.evidence: All five screenshot tests are tagged `@visual` (apps/site/tests/binary-orbits.spec.ts:854,861,871,and the two rvPanel tests at 395,427). The `desktop` project has `grepInvert: /@visual/`, `mobile` has `testMatch: /reflow\.spec\.ts/`, and only the `visual` project greps them in (config lines 34,41,51-53). Both workflows run `corepack pnpm -C apps/site test:e2e`, which apps/site/package.json defines as `playwright test --project=desktop --project=mobile` — the visual project is never selected. `scripts/gates.mjs:16` runs the same command. The 10 tracked baselines total 3,336,135 bytes. The config comment at lines 45-50 states the cause (darwin-only baselines fail on the Linux runner) and the remedy, but no CI job runs them today on any platform.
findings.scenario: A token change, a layout edit or a theme refactor visibly breaks the binary-orbits orbit rendering or its RV panel. Every gate goes green — lint, typecheck, unit, build, desktop E2E, mobile reflow — and the broken drawing deploys to students. The only suite that could have caught it is a manual `test:e2e:visual` on Anna's Mac, which is not in `pnpm gates` and not in CI, so it is skipped exactly when it matters.
findings.fix: Either regenerate the baselines on Linux in the mcr.microsoft.com/playwright container and add `--project=visual` to the nightly workflow (where a failure costs nothing and does not block a deploy), or delete the 10 baselines and the five tests so the repo stops carrying 3.34 MB of binaries that assert nothing. Carrying them un-run is the worst of the three options.

findings.title: pages:write and id-token:write are granted workflow-wide to the job that installs dependencies
findings.evidence: `permissions: contents: read / pages: write / id-token: write` is declared at workflow scope (lines 10-13), so both jobs inherit it. The `verify` job then runs `corepack pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` (line 40), `pnpm lint`, `pnpm test`, `pnpm build` and `playwright install --with-deps chromium` — thousands of transitive packages' code, plus any dependency lifecycle scripts, executing in a token context that can publish to GitHub Pages and mint an OIDC identity token. Only the `deploy` job needs those two scopes; `actions/deploy-pages@v4` is its single step.
findings.scenario: One compromised transitive dependency (or one typosquat landing in a future `pnpm install`) runs during the verify job with `pages: write` and `id-token: write` in the environment. It can publish arbitrary content to the live student-facing site, or exchange the OIDC token with any cloud provider that trusts this repository. The blast radius is entirely avoidable: the install/test job has no legitimate need for either scope.
findings.fix: Set the workflow default to `permissions: contents: read`, and move `pages: write` + `id-token: write` down into the `deploy` job only. The Pages artifact upload in `verify` needs just `contents: read` plus the actions cache; `upload-pages-artifact@v3` does not require `pages: write`.

findings.title: No dependency build-script allowlist, so install scripts run unreviewed under pnpm 9
findings.evidence: pnpm-workspace.yaml contains only `packages: - "apps/*" - "packages/*"` — no `onlyBuiltDependencies` and no `neverBuiltDependencies`. package.json:5 pins `"packageManager": "pnpm@9.0.0"`, and pnpm 9 runs dependency install scripts by default (the deny-by-default `onlyBuiltDependencies` gate arrived in pnpm 10). pnpm-lock.yaml carries 39 `requiresBuild`/`hasBin` markers, so there are packages in the tree that do run build steps. `packageManager` also has no integrity hash, so corepack fetches pnpm 9.0.0 — the first 9.x release — without verifying it against a pinned digest.
findings.scenario: `corepack pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` in CI executes the postinstall of any dependency that declares one, inside the job that (per the previous finding) holds pages:write and id-token:write. A frozen lockfile pins *which versions* install, not *what their install scripts do* — so the lockfile gives no protection against this class at all, and nothing in the repo records which packages are even allowed to build.
findings.fix: Add `onlyBuiltDependencies:` to pnpm-workspace.yaml listing just the packages that genuinely need to build (esbuild and the Playwright browser fetch are the likely ones), and append the integrity hash to the packageManager field (`pnpm@9.x.y+sha512.…`). Bumping off 9.0.0 to a current 9.x or to pnpm 10 gets deny-by-default for free.

findings.title: pre-bash-guard misses force-push-by-refspec, `git -C` staging, and the gates path to Playwright
findings.evidence: Three verified gaps against what CLAUDE.md claims the hooks block. (1) Line 26 matches only `--force`, `--force-with-lease` and `-f`, so `git push origin +main` — a force push by refspec, the most destructive command in the list — passes. (2) Every git rule anchors on `\bgit\s+add` / `\bgit\s+commit` / `\bgit\s+push` (lines 22-27), so any global option between the verb and the subcommand defeats them: `git -C /path add -A` does not match `\bgit\s+add\b`. (3) The Playwright concurrency check at line 33 tests the command text for `/\btest:e2e\b|\bplaywright\s+test\b`, but `corepack pnpm gates` — the documented way to run all five gates, which invokes e2e at scripts/gates.mjs:16 — contains neither string, so the one guard protecting against two runs sharing port 4321 and wiping test-results/ does not fire on the most likely command.
findings.scenario: Two agents work the repo concurrently (as they are now). One runs `corepack pnpm gates`; the guard sees nothing to match and allows it; the second run's startup wipes test-results/ and collides on port 4321, and both suites report garbage. Separately, an agent reaching for a force push after a failed `--ff-only` land types the refspec form and rewrites main's history with no prompt — the exact outcome the rule at line 26 exists to prevent.
findings.fix: Add `/\bgit\s+push\b[^;&|]*\s\+[\w./-]+(?::|$|\s)/` for refspec force pushes; change the three git anchors to `\bgit\b(?:\s+-[^\s]+(?:\s+[^\s-][^\s]*)?)*\s+(?:add|commit|push)\b` so global options cannot slip through; and add `\bpnpm\s+gates\b|\bgates\.mjs\b` to the Playwright-detection regex at line 33. Worth adding a fourth rule for writes under ~/Teaching/astr101-sp26, which CLAUDE.md and .agents/references/invariants.md both call read-only and which no hook guards.

findings.title: Nightly E2E installs Chromium without system deps and uploads nothing on failure
findings.evidence: Line 39 runs `playwright install chromium`, where deploy.yml:57 runs `playwright install --with-deps chromium` on the same ubuntu-latest image. The nightly job also ends at line 41 with the test command — it has no `upload-artifact` step for apps/site/playwright-report, which deploy.yml:60-66 does have under `if: failure()`.
findings.scenario: The nightly fails for a missing shared library rather than a product regression and leaves no report behind. There is nothing to read the next morning and no way to tell an environment failure from a real one, so the signal gets ignored — which is how playwright.config.ts:45-50 records the last nightly breakage going unaddressed from 2026-03-11.
findings.fix: Add `--with-deps` to line 39 and copy the `if: failure()` upload-artifact block from deploy.yml:60-66 into the nightly job.

findings.title: packages/theme/styles/fonts.css has root-absolute URLs and a missing font, invisible to every gate
findings.evidence: Line 19 is `src: url("/fonts/Lexend.woff2") format("woff2");` — a file that does not exist in apps/site/public/fonts and is not tracked by git. Lines 7, 28 and 36 likewise use root-absolute `url("/fonts/...")`, which .agents/references/invariants.md forbids outright ("Never write root-absolute internal links") because GitHub Pages serves the site under /cosmic-playground/. Nothing imports the file: a repo-wide grep for "fonts.css" across apps, packages and scripts returns zero hits, and Layout.astro:44-73 declares its own @font-face through `withBase()` instead. The file is nonetheless a public entry point — packages/theme/package.json exports `"./styles/*"`. scripts/validate-invariants.mjs cannot see it: its base-path rules scan apps/site/src, apps/site/src/content and apps/demos/src, and the comment at line 114 says the color rule "intentionally targets only app-layer files (apps/site and apps/demos), not packages/theme".
findings.scenario: Someone adds `@import "@cosmic/theme/styles/fonts.css"` — the obvious move for a new demo or a station-card stylesheet. On localhost at the /cosmic-playground/ base it already fails; on Pages all four faces 404 and every page falls back to system fonts. `pnpm lint` and `pnpm build` stay green, because no gate scans packages/theme for the base-path invariant the project calls non-negotiable.
findings.fix: Delete fonts.css (Layout.astro already owns font loading correctly) or rewrite it with relative `url("../fonts/...")` and drop the Lexend block. Either way, add packages/theme/styles to the base-path scan roots in scripts/validate-invariants.mjs so the invariant is enforced wherever reader-visible CSS lives — and wire .agents/skills/cosmic-site-content/scripts/check-basepath.mjs into `pnpm lint`, since it exists but no gate, script or workflow references it.

findings.title: Instructor and station index pages are indexable while their detail pages are noindex
findings.evidence: Only one page in the site passes the prop: `apps/site/src/pages/instructor/[slug].astro:56` (`<Layout ... noindex>`), which Layout.astro:46 turns into `<meta name="robots" content="noindex, follow" />`. The four sibling instructor-facing pages do not — instructor/index.astro:27, for-instructors/index.astro:20, stations/index.astro:23, stations/[slug].astro:26. There is no robots.txt in apps/site/public (it holds only assets, fonts, play).
findings.scenario: The instructor landing page is indexed and links to every noindex detail page with `follow`, so a search for a demo title surfaces the instructor index — the directory of the pages that were meant to stay out of results — along with every printable station card. The protection is half-applied, which is weaker than applying it nowhere and documenting that instructor material is public.
findings.fix: Pass `noindex` from the four remaining pages, or decide instructor material is openly indexable and remove it from [slug].astro so the policy is uniform. Either way add apps/site/public/robots.txt stating the intent, since a static site has no other place to say it.

findings.title: 2.9 MB of dead tracked binaries, including an unrelated personal dashboard
findings.evidence: Three groups. (1) Five snapshots carry no project-name segment (binary-orbits-default/-mobile-default/-q0p2/-rv-inclination-30/-rv-sb1-darwin.png, 1,605,734 bytes); all three Playwright projects are named, so the default snapshot path template always inserts `{-projectName}` and these pre-naming baselines can never be matched by any current run — the live ones are the `-visual-darwin` siblings. (2) `.playwright-mcp/your-colors.png`, `teal-comparison.png` and `muted-palette.png` (1,273,157 bytes) are tracked even though .gitignore lists `.playwright-mcp/` — gitignore does not untrack files already in the index. (3) `dashboard.html` (97,651 bytes, mode 0400, `<title>Productivity</title>`, committed in 33a6f91) is an unrelated personal productivity dashboard that preconnects and loads from fonts.googleapis.com and fonts.gstatic.com. Total: ~2.9 MB of a 8.56 MiB pack.
findings.scenario: A reviewer or adopter clones a resource whose README promises a careful static teaching site and finds a locked-down personal dashboard at the repo root pulling fonts from Google, 1.6 MB of baselines no test can use, and three color-comparison screenshots the project's own .gitignore says should not be there. On the first `--update-snapshots` run the orphans silently stay behind, so they grow stale indefinitely while still looking authoritative.
findings.fix: `git rm --cached` the three .playwright-mcp PNGs and dashboard.html (keeping the local copies), and `git rm` the five orphaned baselines. None affects the build: no dist, build or public/play path is tracked, so the output pipeline is otherwise clean.

findings.title: Astro 4, Node 20 and pnpm 9.0.0 with no engines field or .nvmrc
findings.evidence: apps/site/package.json pins `"astro": "^4.16.0"` — a caret on a major line superseded by Astro 5, which is where security and dependency fixes land. deploy.yml:34 and nightly-e2e.yml:23 pin `node-version: 20`, whose maintenance window has closed. There is no `.nvmrc` anywhere and no `engines` field in any of the 11 package.json files, so a local build uses whatever Node happens to be on PATH while CI uses 20. apps/demos also carries a type/runtime skew: `"three": "0.185.1"` exact against `"@types/three": "^0.180.0"`, five minor versions apart on a library that changes API surface every minor.
findings.scenario: Two distinct failures. A CVE lands in Astro 4's build or dev server and there is no patched 4.x to move to, forcing a major upgrade under time pressure on a live student-facing site. Separately, `pnpm typecheck` validates clusterScene.ts against three 0.180's declarations while Vite bundles 0.185 — a signature changed in between typechecks clean and breaks only at runtime in the browser, which is the one place this repo has no coverage for the WebGL demo.
findings.fix: Add `.nvmrc` plus an `engines.node` range so local and CI agree, align @types/three to the pinned three version, and schedule the Astro 5 upgrade as its own branch with the full gate chain. A Dependabot or Renovate config on a weekly cadence would have surfaced all three.

findings.title: Validators self-silence on a repo path containing a space
findings.evidence: Four of the five build validators guard their entry point with `if (import.meta.url === \`file://${process.argv[1]}\`)` — validate-datasets.mjs:209, validate-invariants.mjs:507, validate-physics-models.mjs:84, validate-plot-contract.mjs:118. `import.meta.url` is percent-encoded; `process.argv[1]` is not. The comparison therefore fails for any path containing a space or other encodable character, and because the guard's body is the only thing that calls `main()`, the script then exits 0 having run no checks at all. Today's path, /Users/anna/Teaching/cosmic-playground, has no spaces, so the guard works — this is latent, not active.
findings.scenario: The repo is cloned into a path with a space ("Google Drive", "My Documents", a CI workspace derived from a branch name with a space) or run from a worktree under such a path. `node scripts/validate-datasets.mjs` prints nothing and exits 0; build.mjs:40-44 treats all four as passed; `pnpm lint` and `pnpm build` go green with the dataset, invariants, physics-model and plot contracts never evaluated. A silent gate is worse than a missing one, because the summary says the contract held.
findings.fix: Replace the guard in all four files with `if (process.argv[1] && import.meta.url === pathToFileURL(process.argv[1]).href)` using `pathToFileURL` from node:url, which encodes both sides the same way.

findings.title: Welcome recommender sends "Stars" students to eos-lab, a demo withheld from the catalogue for incomplete physics
findings.evidence: welcome.astro:9-15 hardcodes `{ key: "Stars", label: "Stars", start: "eos-lab" }` and the click handler (line 156-158) sets `resultLink.href = withBase('exhibits/' + startSlug + '/')`. welcome.astro imports only Layout, TopicIcon and withBase — it never calls `listedDemos()`, whose own doc comment states "Every listing surface (home, explore, topics, stations, instructor) must go through this" (apps/site/src/lib/catalog.ts:19-27). eos-lab.md:11-12 sets `unlisted: true` with `unlistedReason: "On hold. The equation of state is incomplete: finite-temperature Fermi branches are implemented, but the neutron-rich and pair-dominated regimes are not, so the regime map is only trustworthy over part of the plane it draws. There is also no instructor bundle. Withheld from the catalogue until the EOS is complete and independently checked."` eos-lab.md also carries `levels: [ASTR201]`, while welcome.astro asks only student-or-instructor and never asks level.
findings.scenario: An ASTR 101 student opens /welcome/, clicks Student, clicks Stars, and is handed a degenerate-electron-pressure lab that the project itself has pulled from every catalogue surface because its regime map is wrong over part of the plane it draws. The student reads a regime boundary the maintainer does not believe, and nothing on the path warns them: the badge on the exhibit page says "experimental", not "withheld".
findings.fix: Derive the welcome map from the collection instead of hardcoding it: `listedDemos(await getCollection('demos'))`, filter by topic and the student's level, sort by `readinessRank` (apps/site/src/lib/readiness.ts:73) and take the first. That change alone drops eos-lab (unlisted) and prefers launch-ready over experimental everywhere. Add a test that every slug a welcome chip can produce is in `listedDemos`.

findings.title: Homepage "Start here" sequence is two experimental drafts; the only launch-ready demo is in neither the hero nor the recommender
findings.evidence: index.astro:25 `const featuredOrder = ["keplers-laws", "retrograde-motion", "binary-orbits"]`, rendered under "Start here" with the lead "Work through them in order for the best experience" (index.astro:88-92). keplers-laws.md: `status: draft`, `readiness: experimental`, `lastVerifiedAt: "2026-02-04"`, readinessReason "Core demo behavior is implemented, but parity and launch-gate signoff are still pending." retrograde-motion.md: identical readiness and reason. binary-orbits.md: `readiness: candidate`, reason "Still to come: the page is wider than a phone screen." Across all 20 demo files `grep -h '^readiness:' | sort | uniq -c` gives 11 experimental, 8 candidate, 1 launch-ready; the launch-ready one is parallax-distance, which has `featured: false` and appears in no welcome chip.
findings.scenario: A student arriving at the homepage with no instructor direction is told to work through three demos in order. Demo 1 was last verified 2026-02-04 (8.5 months before today) and its own frontmatter says parity signoff is pending; demo 3 is admitted to be wider than a phone screen, which is the device most students will use. The one exhibit that passed the September 2026 audits with nothing open is never offered.
findings.fix: Make `featured` a derived property, not a hand-set boolean: require `readiness === 'launch-ready' || readiness === 'candidate'` for a slot in "Start here", and add a build-time check in the gates that fails if any featured demo is `experimental` or `stub`. Feature parallax-distance as step 1 until the orbital demos clear their launch gates.

findings.title: Welcome's "Data & Inference" chip recommends a demo that is not tagged Data & Inference, and its sibling link cannot reach it
findings.evidence: welcome.astro:13 `{ key: "DataInference", label: "Data & Inference", start: "conservation-laws" }`. conservation-laws.md declares `topics: [Orbits]` — DataInference is absent. The same click handler then sets the alternate link to `topics/datainference/` (welcome.astro:160-161), a page built from the demos whose topics include DataInference, which are cluster-census, doppler-shift, galaxy-rotation and parallax-distance. parallax-distance.md declares `topics: [DataInference]` and is the only launch-ready demo in the repo.
findings.scenario: A student picks "Data & Inference", is launched into an orbital energy-and-momentum instrument, then clicks "See all Data & Inference exhibits" and finds a list that does not contain the exhibit they were just sent to. The topic taxonomy and the recommender disagree, so neither can be trusted, and the site's actual flagship inference demo is skipped.
findings.fix: Same fix as the eos-lab routing defect: derive the recommendation from `listedDemos` filtered on `topics.includes(key)` and ordered by `readinessRank`. For DataInference that yields parallax-distance. Add an assertion that `demos.find(d => d.slug === startSlug).data.topics.includes(key)` holds for every chip.

findings.title: No plot in the project is readable by assistive technology: static labels, no live updates, and zero data-table alternatives
findings.evidence: galaxy-rotation/index.html:207 `<canvas id="rotationCanvas" role="img" aria-label="Rotation curve showing velocity versus radius for galaxy model">`. `rg -n 'setAttribute("aria-label"' apps/demos/src/demos/*/main.ts` returns hits only in doppler-shift, retrograde-motion, spectral-lines, keplers-laws and eos-lab — galaxy-rotation is absent, so that label is the same string whether the dark-matter halo is on or off. `grep -c '<table' apps/demos/src/demos/*/index.html` returns 0 for all twenty demos: there is no textual or tabular alternative to any curve anywhere. WCAG 2.2 SC 1.1.1 classifies charts as non-text content requiring a text alternative, and the conventional remedy is an equivalent data table (Kendo UI, https://www.telerik.com/kendo-jquery-ui/documentation/controls/charts/five-tips-for-accessible-charts-with-dataviz; Oracle's 2026.01 VPAT tests exactly this and self-reports "Partially Supports", https://www.oracle.com/ae/corporate/accessibility/templates/t2-17240.html). PhET's answer to the same problem is "interactive description" plus sonification — a live-updating description of state, not a fixed alt text (https://clixplatform.tiss.ac.in/phet/en/accessibility/prototypes.html).
findings.scenario: A screen-reader student is assigned galaxy-rotation, toggles the dark-matter halo, and hears the identical sentence both times. The flat-versus-Keplerian contrast — the whole point of the exhibit, and the evidence for dark matter — is unavailable to them. The same holds for the Planck curve in blackbody-radiation, the U_eff(r) curve in conservation-laws, the longitude plot in retrograde-motion and the regime map in eos-lab.
findings.fix: Add a shared `plotDescription()` to @cosmic/runtime that each render() calls to rewrite the plot's accessible name with the three or four numbers that define the current curve (e.g. "V_flat = 215 km/s, halo on, rises to 215 km/s by 6 kpc then flat to 20 kpc"), and a collapsed `<details><table>` of the sampled series beside each plot, built from the same array the renderer draws. Make both a line in the design-contract test template so new demos inherit them.

findings.title: binary-orbits' primary orbit canvas has no role, no accessible name and is not hidden — a featured demo's main view is invisible to AT
findings.evidence: binary-orbits/index.html:209 `<canvas id="orbitCanvas" width="520" height="520"></canvas>` — no `role`, no `aria-label`, no `aria-hidden`. The sibling canvases on lines 213, 218 and 223 all carry `aria-label` ("Radial velocity versus phase", etc.), so the omission is an oversight, not a decision. binary-orbits.md sets `featured: true`, so this is step 3 of the homepage starter sequence. Same class of defect: em-spectrum/index.html:94 `<canvas id="spectrumWaveCanvas" class="spectrum__wave">` is unnamed, and keplers-laws/index.html:30 marks its orbit canvas `aria-hidden="true"` with no stated text equivalent.
findings.scenario: A screen-reader student working the recommended starter sequence reaches binary-orbits, tabs through the controls, and the central 520x520 view of the two stars orbiting their barycenter is announced as nothing at all — not even as an image to be skipped. They can read the radial-velocity canvas's name but not the thing it is derived from.
findings.fix: Give it `role="img"` plus an aria-label that render() rewrites from the current mass ratio, separation and phase, as the other three canvases should also do. Add `expect(html).toMatch(/<canvas(?![^>]*aria-hidden)[^>]*aria-label=/)` for every non-starfield canvas to binary-orbits/design-contracts.test.ts and promote it into the golden template at moon-phases/design-contracts.test.ts.

findings.title: telescope-resolution's only visualization is a bare <canvas> with an aria-label but no role, so the name is dropped
findings.evidence: telescope-resolution/index.html:155 `<canvas id="canvas" class="stage__canvas" width="420" height="420" aria-label="Point-spread function view">`. `grep -c 'role="img"' apps/demos/src/demos/telescope-resolution/index.html` returns 0. A canvas with no role maps to a generic container, for which an author-supplied accessible name is not exposed by AT, so the label is inert. telescope-resolution/main.ts contains no `setAttribute("aria-label")` call, so even if the role were fixed the name would never change as the aperture, band, binary separation or seeing sliders move. This canvas is the entire observable of the demo: the readouts panel (index.html:163-171) gives θ_diff, θ_eff and the separation, but whether the two stars are resolved is only shown by the drawing.
findings.scenario: A student using a screen reader sets D = 0.1 m and a 2 arcsec separation, then D = 10 m, and gets three numbers but no statement of the thing they were asked to judge — resolved or not. The Rayleigh criterion is the learning objective and it is conveyed only pictorially.
findings.fix: Add `role="img"` and have render() rewrite the label with the verdict and the numbers behind it ("two sources 2.0 arcsec apart, θ_eff = 1.2 arcsec: resolved"), and surface the same verdict as a visible readout so sighted and AT students read the same claim.

findings.title: No URL-shareable instrument state: an instructor cannot link a class to a configured demo, a student cannot hand one back
findings.evidence: The only parameter any demo reads from its URL is the concept/math toggle: `getModeFromUrl` (packages/runtime/src/index.ts:76-80) reads `?mode=`, and `resolveInitialMode` (line 96) is the only consumer. A repo-wide `rg -n 'URLSearchParams|location.search|history.replaceState|pushState'` over apps/ and packages/ excluding tests returns five hits, all of them either the explore page's filter state (apps/site/src/pages/explore/index.astro:624-686, apps/site/src/lib/exploreFilter.ts:247-267) or binary-orbits/main.ts:388 reading `?debug`. No demo serializes slider values, presets, captures or view state, and no demo restores them. apps/site builds with `output: "static"` (.agents/references/invariants.md), so this must be done client-side — which is exactly how the explore filter already does it, so the pattern exists and was simply never applied to the instruments.
findings.scenario: An instructor wants the class to start galaxy-rotation at V_flat = 215 km/s with the halo off, or to put the exact state that produced a disputed readout into a discussion post. There is no way to express either: they must write prose instructions and hope twenty-four students set eight sliders identically. A student who finds a surprising result cannot show anyone the state that produced it; the Copy-results text (formatExportText, index.ts:142) prints the parameters as prose with no way to restore them.
findings.fix: Add `encodeState`/`decodeState` to @cosmic/runtime over each demo's existing controls object (every demo already has one — e.g. conservation-laws' `controls`), write it to the hash with `history.replaceState` on change (debounced), and read it at init before presets. Reuse it for Copy results so the exported text carries a restore link, which turns the export into a submittable artifact.

findings.title: The homepage advertises a Predict/Play/Explain cadence that no instrument implements
findings.evidence:
index.astro:84-86: "Every demo follows the same three-phase cadence. Commit to a prediction, explore the model, then reconcile what happened." PPEVisual.astro:22 elaborates: "Before touching a slider, commit to a prediction." The schema does require a `predict_prompt` per demo (apps/site/src/content/config.ts:48), and the exhibit page renders it as a paragraph (apps/site/src/pages/exhibits/[slug].astro:105), but nothing captures a prediction: the only commitment point in the whole project is a printed blank on the station card, `
Prediction (1 sentence):
` (apps/site/src/pages/stations/[slug].astro:80). `rg -il predict apps/demos/src/demos/*/index.html` matches only 7 of 20 demos, and in those it is prose, not an input. A student who opens /play// directly — which is what every in-demo nav link and playlist "Launch demo" button does — never meets the predict prompt at all.
findings.scenario: A student follows the homepage's framing, opens a demo, and finds no place to commit to anything; the slider is right there and the answer appears the instant they move it. The gap the copy calls "where learning lives" is never created, because nothing was committed before the reveal. PhET's research is explicit that the scaffolding has to live in the sim's controls, feedback and representations rather than in surrounding text (https://arxiv.org/pdf/1306.6544).
findings.fix: Either implement the commitment — a one-question prediction gate in the demo shell that takes a choice or a number, locks it, and shows it alongside the result for the reconcile step (galaxy-rotation already has the right UI shape at index.html:168, a "Outer behavior guess" radiogroup) — or change the homepage and PPEVisual copy to describe what exists: the prompt lives on the exhibit page and the printable station card.

findings.title: telescope-resolution ships a permanently disabled Challenges button
findings.evidence: telescope-resolution/index.html:108 renders `<button id="challengeMode" class="cp-utility-btn" type="button" aria-label="Challenges" title="Challenges" disabled>` and main.ts:473 then hardcodes `challengeModeEl.disabled = true;` unconditionally — there is no branch that re-enables it (the only other `.disabled =` assignments in the file are line 351 for the separation slider and line 395 for the AO toggle, both state-driven). It is the only demo that ships this button disabled. STATUS.md notes that disabled range sliders in galaxy-rotation also "have no style (form.css:79-178) and no hint", so a disabled control in this project gives the reader no explanation either.
findings.scenario: A student sees a trophy icon in the toolbar, tries to click it, and nothing happens, with no tooltip saying why or when it will work. In a demo whose readinessReason already says signoff is pending, a visibly broken control is the first thing they learn about the project's reliability.
findings.fix: Remove the button from index.html until the challenge set exists (the ChallengeEngine wiring can be added with it), rather than rendering a control that cannot be used. If it must stay, give it a visible reason via the existing popover pattern.

findings.title: About page claims three modes per demo; Challenge Mode is in 9 of 20 and Station Mode in 18 of 20
findings.evidence: about.astro:21 renders the stat tile { value: "3", unit: "modes per demo", label: "Station / Challenge / Export" }; :94-96 says "Each demo ships with Station Mode ..., Challenge Mode ..., and Export"; :189 says "Every demo includes a Station Mode". Counted against code: `grep -rl 'new ChallengeEngine'` over apps/demos/src/demos returns 9 demos (angular-size, doppler-shift, eclipse-geometry, galaxy-rotation, hydrostatic-equilibrium-explorer, moon-phases, retrograde-motion, seasons, spectral-lines); 11 have none. `station: {` appears in 18 of 20 main.ts files — em-spectrum/main.ts and planetary-conjunctions/main.ts have no createDemoModes call at all, so they have neither Station Mode nor the Help dialog.
findings.scenario: An instructor reads the about page while choosing demos for a lab rotation, builds a 6-station activity around "Challenge Mode for self-assessment", and discovers in class that 11 of the 20 demos — including blackbody-radiation, keplers-laws, binary-orbits, cluster-census and stars-zams-hr — have no Challenge Mode, and that em-spectrum and planetary-conjunctions have no Station Mode either, so there is nothing for students to export from those two stations.
findings.fix: Either make the claim per-demo (derive the badge from the demo's own content entry and show which of the three modes it has, the way readiness.ts already derives card badges) or restate the about copy as "the shared instrument gives every demo Export; Station Mode on 18 and Challenge Mode on 9, listed per demo". Do not fix this by adding thin Challenge sets to 11 demos just to make the number true.

findings.title: Math mode is dead in all 20 demos: every call site passes hasMathMode: false
findings.evidence: resolveInitialMode (index.ts:96-107) returns "concept" whenever hasMathMode is false, and createInstrumentRuntime.setMode (index.ts:178-182) coerces the same way. All 20 demos pass hasMathMode: false — grep over apps/demos/src/demos/*/main.ts returns 20 hits and zero `true` (angular-size:165, binary-orbits:2091, blackbody-radiation:76, cluster-census:194, conservation-laws:153, doppler-shift:143, eclipse-geometry:213, em-spectrum:148, eos-lab:373, galaxy-rotation:223, hydrostatic-equilibrium-explorer:954, keplers-laws:1007, moon-phases:287, parallax-distance:1149, planetary-conjunctions:357, retrograde-motion:181, seasons:239, spectral-lines:146, stars-zams-hr:253, telescope-resolution:58). `grep -rn 'setMode("math")\|=== "math"'` over the demos returns nothing: no demo ever reads the mode it stores.
findings.scenario: A student or instructor opens /play/keplers-laws/?mode=math expecting the equations view the runtime API implies; resolveInitialMode silently rewrites it to "concept" and the URL parameter is ignored. Meanwhile each of the 20 demos writes a localStorage key (cp:<slug>:mode) on every setMode call for a value that can only ever be "concept". The next person who wants an equations view will reasonably assume the plumbing works and build on top of a path that has never been exercised.
findings.fix: Delete Mode, getModeFromUrl, getModeFromStorage, setModeInStorage, resolveInitialMode, the hasMathMode/storageKey arguments and the 20 call-site arguments, or implement math mode in one demo and keep the API with that live consumer. Keeping an unexercised mode API is what makes the "three modes" matrix above unverifiable.

findings.title: No demo encodes its configuration in the URL, so no run is shareable or reproducible
findings.evidence: The only URL reads anywhere in apps/demos/src/demos are getModeFromUrl's `url.searchParams.get("mode")` (index.ts:71, dead per the finding above) and binary-orbits/main.ts:388 `new URLSearchParams(window.location.search).has("debug")`. `grep -rn 'history.replaceState\|history.pushState'` over the 20 demos returns nothing: no demo ever writes its state to the URL. Persistence is limited to three hand-rolled first-run flags (eos-lab/main.ts:1570 "eos-lab-toured", retrograde-motion/main.ts:474 ONBOARDING_STORAGE_KEY, seasons/main.ts:441 SCRUB_HINT_STORAGE_KEY); no demo persists its physics state.
findings.scenario: An instructor finds the eclipse configuration that produces an annular eclipse and wants to put it in a lab handout. There is no way to do it — no link, no saved state, no run id. They must write prose instructions ("set beta to 0.4 deg, nearest node 12 deg") and hope 30 students reproduce them identically. The same gap means a student cannot send a TA the state that confused them, and a grader cannot re-open the configuration a submitted export came from.
findings.fix: Add one runtime module (serializeDemoState/applyDemoState) that round-trips a flat Record<string,string|number|boolean> through searchParams with history.replaceState on change, and have each demo pass its existing state object. The demos already keep state in one `state` object and already have an updateControlsFromState()-style rehydrator, so the per-demo change is two calls. Start with parallax-distance (the one launch-ready demo) and the 5 canonical-playbar demos.

findings.title: Exported results carry no demo identity or provenance
findings.evidence: formatExportText (index.ts:130-168) emits exactly: "Cosmic Playground — Results Export (v1)", `Timestamp: <iso>`, then Parameters / Readouts / Notes. There is no demo name, no slug, no page URL and no model or physics version. All 20 demos route through it (createInstrumentRuntime.copyResults, index.ts:193-195). Station Mode's CSV is worse: toCsv (demoModes.ts:300-313) emits the column header row and nothing else — no demo name, no timestamp, no units row.
findings.scenario: A student pastes exports from angular-size and parallax-distance into one lab document. Both begin with the identical two header lines, and the only way to tell them apart is to recognise the parameter names. A grader receiving 30 such documents cannot attribute a table to a demo, and cannot tell whether two tables came from the same build of the physics. The pilot quality bar (docs/specs/cosmic-playground-pilot-quality-bar.md, section D) lists timestamp, parameters, readouts and notes but never asked for identity, so the gate is satisfied while the artefact is unusable for its stated purpose.
findings.fix: Add `demo: string` (slug) and `source: string` (page URL) to ExportPayloadV1 and print them as two header lines in formatExportText; emit the same two lines as comment rows above the CSV header in toCsv. Once the URL state module from the previous finding exists, the `source` line becomes the reproducible run an instructor can hand out.

findings.title: em-spectrum ships at readiness: candidate with none of the shared mode surface
findings.evidence: apps/site/src/content/demos/em-spectrum.md declares `readiness: candidate` and `status: beta`. Its utility toolbar (index.html:44-66) contains exactly two controls: #copyResults and the nav popover trigger — no station button, no help button, no challenges button. em-spectrum/main.ts has no createDemoModes call (`grep -c 'station: {'` and `'help: {'` both return 0), so there is no Station Mode, no Help dialog and no shortcut table, and `grep -ci 'what to notice'` on its index.html returns 0 — it is one of only two demos (with stars-zams-hr) lacking that block. It is also one of only two demos with no preset affordance at all.
findings.scenario: A student lands on /play/em-spectrum/ from an Explore card that shows no readiness badge beyond candidate. They press ? expecting the help table every other demo advertises and nothing opens; they press g for Station Mode and nothing opens; there is no "What to notice" to orient them and no preset to start from. They have a slider and a spectrum, and the only shared affordance is Copy results — which will copy a table they were never told how to produce.
findings.fix: Either drop em-spectrum to `experimental`/`draft` until it has createDemoModes (station + help) and a "What to notice" block, or add those three things. The same check applies to planetary-conjunctions (experimental today, so correctly labelled, but it has the same gap). A build gate in scripts/validate-play-dirs.mjs asserting that any demo at candidate or above has #btn-help/#help, a station button and a "What to notice" marker would stop this recurring.

findings.title: The playbar — the most-used gesture in the product — exists in four incompatible forms
findings.evidence: Five demos use the canonical five-button transport #btn-play / #btn-pause / #btn-reset / #btn-step-back / #btn-step-forward (doppler-shift, galaxy-rotation, moon-phases, retrograde-motion, spectral-lines — each with 6-7 .cp-playbar occurrences in index.html). The rest hand-roll it: conservation-laws uses #play/#pause/#reset/#step (one-directional step only), keplers-laws uses #play/#pause/#reset with no step, parallax-distance uses a single #playPauseOrbit toggle, eclipse-geometry uses #animateMonth/#animateYear with no play/pause/reset/step at all, seasons uses #animateYear, planetary-conjunctions has only #reset. accessibility.spec.ts:89-95 is the receipt: the ANIMATED_DEMOS table has to carry a per-demo playSelector and already lists three different ones ("#play", "#btn-play", "#animateMonth"). Five demos also override .cp-playbar in their own style.css on top of packages/theme/styles/components/playbar.css (moon-phases:202 and :370, retrograde-motion:269 and :459, doppler-shift:172, galaxy-rotation:129 and :202, spectral-lines:137).
findings.scenario: A student does the moon-phases station first and learns the transport: play, pause, step one frame back, step one frame forward, reset. At the next station (eclipse-geometry) none of those buttons exist — there is "Animate month" and "Animate year" and no way to step or reset. At keplers-laws play and pause are there but stepping is gone. Each station costs the student the first minute re-learning the transport, and because five demos restyle .cp-playbar the bar does not even look the same between the ones that do share the markup.
findings.fix: Promote the five-button transport to a runtime module (createPlaybar in packages/runtime) that emits the markup and binds play/pause/step/reset against a {play, pause, stepBy, reset} adapter, and delete the five per-demo .cp-playbar overrides into playbar.css. Migrate in this order: keplers-laws and conservation-laws (already have 3-4 of the buttons), then parallax-distance (launch-ready, currently a lone toggle), then eclipse-geometry and seasons (replace animateMonth/animateYear with presets that set the rate). ANIMATED_DEMOS then collapses to a slug list with one selector.

findings.title: Challenge Mode has five incompatible presentations, and one demo's Challenges button is permanently disabled
findings.evidence: The 9 ChallengeEngine demos present it five ways: (1) a modal behind #btn-challenges in the utility toolbar (angular-size, moon-phases, retrograde-motion); (2) a #challengeMode utility-toolbar button (eclipse-geometry, seasons); (3) a #challengeModeBtn .cp-button--outline inside the controls panel labelled "Mystery Curve Challenge" (galaxy-rotation/index.html:156); (4) an always-present #challengeCard inside the drawer, labelled "Checkpoint deck" (hydrostatic-equilibrium-explorer/index.html:623-634); (5) an inline #mysteryPrompt panel with no discoverable launcher (doppler-shift/index.html:158, spectral-lines/index.html:165). Separately, telescope-resolution — which has no ChallengeEngine — ships the #challengeMode star button with the `disabled` attribute hardcoded in markup (index.html:108) and disabled again at runtime (main.ts:473 `challengeModeEl.disabled = true;`).
findings.scenario: A student who learned on moon-phases looks for the star icon in the toolbar. On galaxy-rotation it is a text button halfway down the controls panel; on hydrostatic-equilibrium-explorer it is a card they have to scroll the drawer to find; on doppler-shift there is no launcher at all and the challenge is simply the state the demo is already in. On telescope-resolution the star icon is present but greyed out, so the student concludes the feature is broken rather than absent — a visible dead affordance is worse than no affordance.
findings.fix: Pick presentation (1) — the #btn-challenges toolbar button opening the shared dialog — and make the engine mount its own UI, the way createDemoModes already mounts Help and Station. Remove the #challengeMode button and the two disabling lines from telescope-resolution entirely rather than leaving it disabled. A validate-play-dirs assertion that a challenges button exists only when the demo constructs a ChallengeEngine would prevent the next dead button.

findings.title: HTML entities and \uXXXX escapes bypass the math-formatting gate, including five in the golden-reference demo
findings.evidence: FORBIDDEN_UNICODE_MATH (line 33) is a literal-codepoint character class, and it is tested against the raw file text (lines 114 and 119) with no entity decoding. I confirmed with node that `°`, `°`, `α`, `θ`, `×`, `≈` and `≈` all pass the regex as source while their decoded characters all match it. Live instances: moon-phases/index.html:74, :85, :86, :100, :536 (`α`) and :101 (`0°`, `180°`) — the golden reference; angular-size/index.html:73 (`°`, `≈`), :273, :277 (`θ`); eclipse-geometry/index.html:284, :285 (`°`); retrograde-motion/index.html:393 (`×`); eos-lab/index.html:160 (`≈`). The same blind spot covers escapes: seasons/main.ts:253-254 writes shortcut rows `{ key: "← / →", action: "Step ±1 day" }`. The gate also only forbids Unicode; it never requires LaTeX, so ASCII math in reader-visible HTML passes too (stars-zams-hr/index.html:319, :323 render `L/L_sun` and `R/R_sun` in .cp-readout__unit spans, which CLAUDE.md reserves for canvas and uPlot labels only).
findings.scenario: This is the exact failure CLAUDE.md records from 2026-09-05: an inherited text-transform uppercased 94 KaTeX nodes and turned frequency into "N". A raw α has no KaTeX node to check, and `α` has none either — so moon-phases' "In this model: α = Sun-Moon-Earth angle" (index.html:100) is one CSS rule away from reading "A = Sun-Moon-Earth angle" with every test green, in the demo every other demo is copied from. The gate reports clean, which is why these nine instances have survived.
findings.fix: Decode HTML entities and \uXXXX/\xXX escapes before testing FORBIDDEN_UNICODE_MATH, then fix the nine call sites to $\alpha$, $^{\circ}$, $\theta$, $\times$, $\approx$, $\leftarrow/\rightarrow$, $\pm$. Separately, add a positive check that .cp-readout__unit content in HTML is either a plain ASCII unit word (K, AU, deg) or LaTeX — never a bare ASCII transliteration of a Greek or solar symbol.

findings.title: WCAG 1.4.10 reflow is tested on 1 of 20 /play/ routes, with a known candidate-readiness failure excluded rather than fixed
findings.evidence: PLAY_ROUTES = ["play/conservation-laws/"] (reflow.spec.ts:55) — one demo. The comment immediately above it (lines 49-54) records the reason the list is short and names a live failure: "binary-orbits is candidate but currently DOES scroll sideways at 320px (its drawer accordions take their minimum from unbreakable KaTeX display equations), so it stays out until that is fixed." The cause is in the shared shell: .cp-accordion is used by 15 of the 20 demos (binary-orbits has 32 occurrences, eos-lab 40, doppler-shift/galaxy-rotation/spectral-lines/hydrostatic 20 each). The one launch-ready demo, parallax-distance, is not in PLAY_ROUTES either. docs/specs/cosmic-playground-pilot-quality-bar.md section G requires "No horizontal scrolling at ~360px width".
findings.scenario: A student opens /play/binary-orbits/ on a phone — the common case for a lecture warm-up — and the page scrolls sideways, so readouts and the right-hand controls are off-screen and the drawer text is unreadable without panning. This is a WCAG 1.4.10 failure on a demo the site labels candidate, it is already known, and the gate that would have caught it was narrowed around it. Because the trigger is the shared accordion's intrinsic minimum width, the same failure is latent in 14 other demos nobody has measured.
findings.fix: Fix the cause once in the shell: give .cp-accordion__body a min-width: 0 and make .katex-display scroll inside its own overflow-x container (the accordion body, not the page), then add all candidate-and-above /play/ routes to PLAY_ROUTES in one change. The per-demo exclusion list disappears with the cause.

findings.title: keplers-laws' Help dialog advertises shortcuts under a rule that is false for half of them
findings.evidence: The dialog subtitle is "Keyboard shortcuts work when focus is not in an input field." (main.ts:1015) and the table lists `Space -> Play/Pause` and `Home/End -> Perihelion/Aphelion` (main.ts:1023-1024). Those three keys are bound only on elements.planetGroup (main.ts:891-930) — the SVG group with role="slider" tabindex="0" at index.html:139-145 — so they fire only while focus is inside the orbit graphic. The document-level handler (main.ts:934-972) handles only k/K, n/N and 1-6, and it returns early when the event target is inside `input, select, textarea, button, a, summary, [contenteditable], [role=button]`. So Space works only in one specific place, which is the opposite of the stated rule.
findings.scenario: A student presses ? to learn the controls, reads "shortcuts work when focus is not in an input field", clicks on empty page background and presses Space. Focus is on body, the planetGroup handler never fires, and the browser scrolls the page instead of starting the animation. The student concludes the help text is wrong — which it is — and stops trusting it on the other demos too, where it happens to be accurate. The same split exists in seasons, which binds Space on document (main.ts:1322-1370) and so does match its own help text.
findings.fix: Bind Space, Home and End on document in keplers-laws with the same guard as k/n/1-6 (keeping the planetGroup handler for the arrow-key nudges, which genuinely are a slider interaction), or split the help table into "anywhere on the page" and "while the planet is focused" sections. Prefer the first: a transport key that works in only one focus location is not a product-level shortcut.

findings.title: stars-zams-hr puts units in three different places in one readout panel, and the mass readout has no unit at all when hidden
findings.evidence:
Three unit placements in six readouts. (a) Unit inside the LABEL, inverting the label -> value -> unit hierarchy of design-system invariant 3: index.html:315 `
Effective temperature K
`, and the same at :319 (`L/L_sun`) and :323 (`R/R_sun`). (b) Unit baked into the value STRING: main.ts:895 `selectedMass.textContent = state.revealMassColors ? `${formatNumber(star.mass, 3)} M_sun` : "Hidden until revealed";` — so the unit renders in the amber monospace value colour, not the ice-blue unit colour, and the Mass label at :327 carries no unit span. (c) No unit anywhere: when revealMassColors is off the Mass readout reads "Hidden until revealed". The ASCII `L/L_sun`, `R/R_sun` and `M_sun` in reader-visible HTML also violate the KaTeX-only rule, which reserves ASCII for canvas and uPlot labels; CLAUDE.md's own example of the correct form is $L/L_{\odot}$.
findings.scenario: A student reads the panel and sees temperature, luminosity and radius with their units set in the muted label row and mass with its unit in the amber value row — three visual conventions for the same thing on one screen. Worse, main.ts:892-894 writes luminosity to 4 decimal places (formatNumber(star.L, 4)) and effective temperature to 0, so the panel claims 0.0001 L_sun resolution on an interpolated ZAMS grid: false precision the pilot quality bar section E explicitly forbids. The student copies "L = 1.0000" into a lab table as a measured value.
findings.fix: Move the three units out of the labels into cp-readout__unit spans after the value; give Mass a $M_{\odot}$ unit span and have main.ts:895 write only the number; write all four units as LaTeX. Then fix the significant figures: luminosity and radius to 2-3 significant figures, not 4 decimals, matching what the underlying fit actually resolves. The significant-figure choice is a pedagogical decision, so propose the digits rather than picking them.

findings.title: The drawer is a tab strip in some demos and a stack of details accordions in others — two keyboard models for the same region
findings.evidence: Counted over the 20 index.html files: 4 demos present the drawer purely as a .cp-tabs strip with no accordions (angular-size, eclipse-geometry, parallax-distance, seasons); 11 present it purely as <details class="cp-accordion"> stacks (binary-orbits 32 occurrences, em-spectrum 8, keplers-laws 16, planetary-conjunctions 8, stars-zams-hr 16, telescope-resolution 12, blackbody-radiation 12, cluster-census 12, conservation-laws 12, and others); 5 mix both. The two have different keyboard models: initTabs (packages/runtime/src/tabs.ts:88-110) implements roving tabindex with ArrowLeft/ArrowRight/Home/End, while a <details class="cp-accordion"> is Tab-to-summary then Enter or Space, one stop per panel. em-spectrum/index.html:150-155 even labels an accordion's meta text "tabs" while implementing it as a details element.
findings.scenario: A keyboard-only student learns on eclipse-geometry that the drawer panels are reached with arrow keys from one tab stop. On keplers-laws the same region is 16 separate tab stops they must Enter individually, and arrow keys do nothing. A screen-reader user gets "tab, selected, 1 of 4" on one demo and "disclosure triangle, collapsed" on the next for content that occupies the same place and serves the same purpose. The em-spectrum label reading "tabs" over a details element actively misannounces what it is.
findings.fix: Choose the tab strip for the drawer (it has the better keyboard model, one shared implementation in tabs.ts, and the smaller tab-order footprint) and convert the 11 accordion-only demos, starting with the ones whose drawer has 3-5 panels. Keep <details> only for genuinely optional long-form prose inside a panel. Fix em-spectrum/index.html:153's "tabs" meta text either way.

findings.title: The demo-shell-variants spec no longer describes the CSS it governs
findings.evidence: The spec's "Invariant DOM contract (all variants)" (line ~27) mandates `<aside class="cp-demo__controls">` and defines exactly three variants: instrument, triad, viz-first. In code: 11 demos use .cp-demo__sidebar instead of .cp-demo__controls (angular-size, eclipse-geometry, moon-phases, parallax-distance, retrograde-motion, seasons use it exclusively; eos-lab and hydrostatic-equilibrium-explorer carry both), and demo-shell.css:62-63 has to select on both. demo-shell.css:300-311 declares the data-shell attributes "Backward compatibility ... They are no-ops now", yet 7 demos still carry one, and conservation-laws/index.html sets data-shell="orbit" — a fourth variant the spec never defines, implemented at demo-shell.css:354-432 with its own grid, its own mobile block and its own readouts scroll states. seasons/style.css:3-25 goes further and redefines bare .cp-demo grid-template-areas in both breakpoints, adding a `context` area absent from the shared grid.
findings.scenario: Someone authoring demo 21 reads the spec, writes cp-demo__controls and data-shell="triad", and gets a layout the CSS treats as a no-op while the class they chose is the minority spelling. Someone else reading only the CSS adds a fifth bespoke data-shell value because orbit set the precedent, and the "variants are layout-only, add a variant rather than a per-demo grid" guardrail erodes one demo at a time — seasons has already crossed it with a global .cp-demo override that any future demo on the same page structure would inherit.
findings.fix: Rewrite the spec to describe the unified grid as built (one grid, five named areas, optional regions collapsing to 0) and name sidebar vs controls as one spelling with the other removed. Scope seasons' grid override to a demo-specific class and declare `context` in the shared grid or fold it into shelf. Decide explicitly whether orbit is a sanctioned variant (then document it) or conservation-laws-specific (then scope it), and delete the data-shell attributes from the 6 demos where they are no-ops.

findings.title: First-run onboarding exists on 3 of 20 demos, each hand-rolled, with nothing in the runtime
findings.evidence: Three mechanisms, three storage keys, zero shared code: eos-lab/main.ts:1570 and :1588 gate a multi-step tour on localStorage "eos-lab-toured" (and CLAUDE.md records that this tour blocks clicks in E2E unless the key is pre-set); retrograde-motion/main.ts:474 and :1750 gate an #onboardingStep flow on ONBOARDING_STORAGE_KEY; seasons/main.ts:441-460 gates a scrub hint on SCRUB_HINT_STORAGE_KEY. packages/runtime/src contains no onboarding or tour module. eos-lab is also the only demo with a #startTour button in its utility toolbar, so the gesture that replays the tour exists in exactly one place. The remaining 17 demos open cold: their orientation is whatever the "What to notice" accordion says, which is collapsed-or-open depending on the demo and absent entirely from em-spectrum and stars-zams-hr.
findings.scenario: A student following a 6-station rotation gets a blocking modal tour on eos-lab, a dismissible step strip on retrograde-motion, a one-line hint on seasons and nothing on the other three. They cannot replay any of them except on eos-lab, because the other two only check their key on load. In the 17 cold demos the ten-second question "what am I supposed to do here?" has no answer in the viewport, and the one demo that does answer it loudest is the one whose tour had to be special-cased in the E2E suite.
findings.fix: Standardise on the cheapest pattern that works for all 20: a non-blocking first-run callout in the controls panel — one sentence of what to try plus a button that applies the demo's first preset — with one runtime module owning a single `cp:<slug>:onboarded` key and a replay affordance in the utility toolbar for every demo. Retire the blocking eos-lab tour (which is also an E2E liability) and the two one-off hints into it. Pair it with a "What to notice" block in em-spectrum and stars-zams-hr so the 10-second question is always answered on-page.

findings.title: Eleven of twenty demos hide sidebar content behind an invisible-scrollbar scroller
findings.evidence: The measurement is recorded in the shell's own comment (demo-shell.css:137-154): "Measured 2026-09-04 at 1440x900: 11 of 20 demos hide sidebar content behind this scroller -- 4,205px of it, up to 882px in one demo -- and every one reported a 0px scrollbar gutter, meaning an overlay scrollbar that is invisible until you happen to scroll." The cause is structural: .cp-demo__controls/.cp-demo__sidebar is capped at `max-height: calc(100svh - 2 * var(--cp-space-4))` with `overflow: hidden` (demo-shell.css:62-74) and its .cp-panel-body gets `overflow: auto` (:155-163). The mitigation is a mask-image fade keyed on a data-scroll attribute published by initScrollAffordance; the comment itself calls it "an affordance, not a fix".
findings.scenario: A student on a 1440x900 laptop opens eos-lab (8 range inputs) or galaxy-rotation (7) and sees a controls panel that looks complete and ends cleanly. Up to 882px of controls — in the worst case most of the demo's parameter space — is below the fold behind a scrollbar that does not render until they happen to scroll inside that panel. They do the activity with the top three sliders and never discover the rest, and the gradient fade reads as a visual style rather than as "there is more here".
findings.fix: Treat panel overflow as a layout budget violation rather than an affordance problem: for the 11 demos, move secondary controls into the drawer or behind a popover until the sidebar fits at 900px height, which is what the layout-budget spec exists to enforce. Add the measured overflow per demo to apps/site/tests/layout-budget.spec.ts as a failing threshold so the number cannot grow silently.

findings.title: Help shortcut tables teach four different spellings for the same arrow-key gesture
findings.evidence: Aggregating the `{ key, action }` rows across the 18 demos with a shortcut table: ? and g are consistent (17 each), but the arrow-key gesture is written four ways — "← / →" and "↑ / ↓" (seasons/main.ts:253-254), "Left / Right", "Left/Right (or Up/Down)", "Shift + arrow keys" and "Shift + arrow" in others. Play/pause is "Space" in 5 tables (keplers-laws:1023, retrograde-motion:1654, parallax-distance:1165, seasons:255) and "p" in spectral-lines:2096 — and spectral-lines actually binds both (main.ts:861 handles " " and :2196 handles "p") while advertising only p. Preset keys are "1-8" in doppler-shift:1448, "1-4" in galaxy-rotation:1345 and "1–8" elsewhere, mixing an ASCII hyphen and an en dash for the same range notation.
findings.scenario: A student reading two help tables in one session cannot tell whether "Left / Right" and "arrow keys" are the same control, or whether p and Space are alternatives or different demos' choices. In spectral-lines they learn p, carry it to doppler-shift where it does nothing, and never discover that Space would have worked in both.
findings.fix: Add a SHORTCUTS constant to packages/runtime exporting the canonical rows (help, station, play/pause, step, reset, presets) with one spelling each, rendered as LaTeX arrows rather than escapes, and have each demo spread the ones it binds. The table then cannot drift from the bindings, and the ← escapes disappear with it.

findings.title: galaxy-rotation model notes claim the deep-MOND asymptote; the code plots the simple interpolating function
findings.evidence: index.html:374 (reader-visible model notes): "The MOND curve shows the deep-MOND asymptotic limit ($a \ll a_0$) where $V^4 \approx G\,M\,a_0$." The plotted series is `row.vMondKmS` (main.ts:767, and main.ts:690 for the y-domain). `packages/physics/src/galaxyRotationModel.ts:446-458` defines `vMondKmS` as the simple-nu solution a = aN/2*(1+sqrt(1+4*a0/aN)), v = sqrt(a*R) — not the asymptote. The asymptote has its own function, `vMondDeepKmS` (galaxyRotationModel.ts:436, returns (G*M*a0)^0.25), and a grep of all non-node_modules .ts files shows it is referenced only from galaxyRotationModel.test.ts:94 and :159 — dead code in production. Traced the full chain index.html -> main.ts:767 -> model. Logged as GR-3 "open" in docs/reviews/galaxy-rotation.md on 2026-09-03 and still open 50 days later; the demo carries `readiness: candidate` and `content_verified: true` in apps/site/src/content/demos/galaxy-rotation.md.
findings.scenario: A student reads the model note, takes the flat outer curve as the $V^4 = GMa_0$ baryonic Tully-Fisher relation, and reports that reading in a lab write-up. The curve they measured is the full interpolating function, which the review measured as 24% different at 8 kpc and 55% at 2 kpc, so the number they extract for $a_0$ or for the implied baryonic mass is wrong by those factors — and the demo's own `logic.ts:229` already says "full interpolation", so the page contradicts itself.
findings.fix: Rewrite index.html:374 to say the curve is the simple interpolating function and that the flat $V^4=GMa_0$ form is its far-field limit, or add a second trace from the already-written `vMondDeepKmS` and label both. Either way the note and the trace must name the same function; then clear GR-3 in docs/reviews/galaxy-rotation.md rather than leaving it to be rediscovered.

findings.title: spectral-lines states a Balmer limit 0.1 nm from the one its own model computes
findings.evidence: index.html:351: "The Balmer series limit (364.6 nm)...". The model computes the limit from the reduced-mass Rydberg: `BOHR.RYDBERG_EV: 13.598434599` (spectralLineModel.ts:36) and `lambda_limit = hc/(RYDBERG_EV/n_lower^2)` (spectralLineModel.ts:289-294). Recomputed both ways with node: 4/1.0967758e5 cm = 364.705 nm, and 1239.8419/(13.598287*0.25) = 364.705 nm. So the demo is vacuum throughout and its computed limit is 364.70 nm, while the prose prints 364.6 nm, the air value. Logged as SL-4 "open" in docs/reviews/spectral-lines.md (2026-09-03) and in STATUS.md's 2026-09-10 diagnosis list; the demo is `readiness: candidate`, `content_verified: true`.
findings.scenario: A student reads 364.6 nm in the prose, then reads the series-limit label the demo itself draws from the model, and gets two different numbers for the same quantity with no explanation. The careful student concludes the instrument is unreliable; the less careful one records 364.6 nm as the vacuum Balmer limit, which it is not.
findings.fix: Replace the hardcoded 364.6 in index.html:351 with the model's own `seriesLimitNm(2)` value rendered at runtime (364.70 nm), or state 364.6 nm explicitly as the air wavelength and say the demo works in vacuum. Hardcoding either number again re-opens the drift.

findings.title: spectral-lines credits the NIST Atomic Spectra Database for ad hoc strengths and rounded air wavelengths
findings.evidence: logic.ts:560 and index.html:497 both tell the reader "Multi-element line data from the NIST Atomic Spectra Database (strongest lines only)", and index.html:489 badges the panel "Bohr + NIST". The actual table is inline in `packages/physics/src/spectralLineModel.ts:119-157+` as literals with `relativeIntensity` values on a round 0.05 grid (He I 388.9 at 0.45, 447.1 at 0.35, 471.3 at 0.25, Na D2 589.0 at 1.00, D1 589.6 at 0.95) — illustrative weights, not NIST relative intensities, and the wavelengths are air values rounded to 0.1 nm inside a demo that is vacuum throughout. The demo imports nothing from `@cosmic/data-spectra` (its only imports are @cosmic/runtime and @cosmic/physics, main.ts:1-4), so the one dataset package that does carry per-entry `medium:` and a provenance block (packages/data-spectra/manifest.json: "representative air wavelengths anchored to NIST strong line tables", license UNSPECIFIED) is bypassed. Logged as SL-5 "open" 2026-09-03.
findings.scenario: An instructor or a reviewer follows the on-screen NIST attribution to the NIST database to check a line strength, finds Ha:Hb:Hg:Hd = 0.50:0.33:0.25:0.20 against Case-B 1.00:0.35:0.16:0.09, and has no way to tell which other numbers in the exhibit are real. The data contract exists to prevent exactly this, but it only governs packages/data-*, so `validate-datasets.mjs` structurally cannot see this table.
findings.fix: Move the element catalogue into `packages/data-spectra` with its existing `medium:`/provenance/license fields, import it in spectral-lines, and change the three UI strings to say the wavelengths are representative air values anchored to NIST strong-line tables and the strengths are illustrative. Extend `scripts/validate-datasets.mjs` (or add a sibling) to flag literal line/row tables of more than N entries living outside packages/data-*, so the contract covers the place the data actually is.

findings.title: stars-zams-hr ships an inline evolution model that starts 28% below the ZAMS the same demo draws
findings.evidence: `buildEvolutionTrack` is defined in the demo at main.ts:311 and called at main.ts:675. Its main-sequence luminosity is `const luminosityLsun = msL * (0.72 + 0.85 * fraction)` (main.ts:333), so at `fraction = 0` the marker is drawn at 0.72*L_ZAMS — 1 - 0.72 = 0.28, i.e. 28% below the population's own Tout-based ZAMS, which the same page plots. A second, divergent copy of the post-main-sequence model exists in `packages/physics/src/hrInferencePopulationModel.ts` (`stageProperties`). CLAUDE.md states "All physics models MUST come from @cosmic/physics — no inline equations in demo code"; no validator enforces it (scripts/ holds validate-invariants, -math-formatting, -datasets, -physics-models, -plot-contract, -play-dirs; none scans demo code for inline physics, and validate-physics-models.mjs only checks that every packages/physics/*Model.ts has a test and an export). Logged as HR-4 "open" 2026-09-03.
findings.scenario: A student sets the evolution slider to t = 0, expecting the marker to sit on the main sequence the plot shows, and it sits visibly below it. The demo's lesson is that a star begins life on the ZAMS; the drawing says it begins 28% under it. Because the coefficients live in demo code, the physics tests in packages/physics pass and cannot see the discrepancy.
findings.fix: Delete `buildEvolutionTrack` from main.ts and drive the track from `hrInferencePopulationModel.stageProperties`, with a test asserting the track's t=0 luminosity equals the population's ZAMS luminosity for the same mass. Then add the missing guardrail (the execution board already specs it as `scripts/validate-demo-architecture.mjs`, CP-008, never written) so a future inline copy fails the build instead of a review.

findings.title: The plot contract gates an architecture that was never built and has since been replaced
findings.evidence: The contract mandates `packages/runtime/plots/plotEngine.ts` + plotTypes/plotDefaults/plotUtils, the `mountPlot`/`PlotSpec`/`PlotController` API (lines 112-138), and forbids direct Plotly use. Verified: `packages/runtime/src/plots` does not exist (ls: No such file or directory); `packages/runtime/src/` holds 17 files, none of them a plot engine.
