A repo-wide grep for `mountPlot` outside node_modules returns only docs and the validator's own regex — no implementation and no call site. Plotly is not a dependency anywhere (apps/demos/package.json ships `uplot: ^1.6.31` instead), and the one charting demo imports it directly: `apps/demos/src/demos/eos-lab/uplotHelpers.ts:7` `import uPlot from "uplot"`. So `scripts/validate-plot-contract.mjs` passes vacuously: its Plotly regexes can never match and its `mountPlot` axis-metadata branch is unreachable. Meanwhile `apps/site/src/content/demos/eos-lab.md` declares `plotContractVersion: 1`, a schema field (content/config.ts:38) asserting conformance to a contract with no implementation. docs/backlog.md already records "validate-plot-contract.mjs cleanup — references deleted Plotly architecture", but the spec, the PRD sections that cite it (5.8.5, 8.11), and the frontmatter were never updated.
findings.scenario: A future plot demo is written against uPlot per the eos-lab precedent, the green plot-contract gate certifies it, and none of the things the contract exists to guarantee — runtime-owned theming, keyboard reachability, reduced-motion, mobile layout, axis units matching exports — is actually checked for it. The demo's own design-contracts.test.ts:151 asserts only `not.toContain("plotly")`, which is true of every file in the repo.
findings.fix: Decide which is true and make the docs match: either rewrite the plot contract around uPlot with a real runtime-owned wrapper and point the validator at that, or delete the plot contract, delete `scripts/validate-plot-contract.mjs` and its test, drop `plotContractVersion`/`plotParityAudit` from content/config.ts and eos-lab.md, and remove the plot rows from PRD 5.8.5/8.11 and site-spec 9.5. The second is smaller and matches what shipped.

findings.title: Two specs mandate packages that do not exist, and the invariants file records the opposite as fact
findings.evidence: Site spec 9.3 requires a minimum `packages/ui` component set: Slider, Toggle, Select, Tabs, Callout, Badge, Readout, ParameterTable, Button, IconButton, Modal, Tooltip. CLAUDE-CODE-MIGRATION-PROMPT.md Phase 2 (lines 168-240) specifies `<cp-readout>` and the remaining components as web components, and §3.2 step 1 instructs "Replace custom HTML elements with @cosmic/ui components". PRD 5.7.1 lists "Demo uses shared UI primitives (@cosmic/ui components where available)" as an acceptance criterion, and PRD 5.1.4/5.3.1 additionally mandate an `@cosmic/renderer` Canvas2D abstraction. Verified: `packages/ui` contains exactly three files — package.json, tsconfig.json, and src/index.ts whose entire content is `export const PACKAGE_NAME = "@cosmic/ui";`. A grep for `@cosmic/ui` across the repo finds only those two self-references: nothing imports it. `packages/` holds data-astr101, data-spectra, data-telescopes, math, physics, runtime, theme, ui — no renderer. `.agents/references/invariants.md` states flatly "`packages/ui` exists but nothing imports it, and there is no renderer package", i.e. the file agents are told to read first contradicts the site spec and the PRD.
findings.scenario: An agent (or a new contributor) follows CLAUDE.md to docs/specs/, reads site-spec 9.3 and the migration prompt's Phase 2 as binding, and spends a session building a web-component library nothing asked for — or worse, blocks a demo's promotion on an acceptance criterion (PRD 5.7.1) that cannot be met because the package is empty.
findings.fix: Resolve in one direction and in one place. Either delete packages/ui, strike site-spec 9.3, migration-prompt Phase 2, PRD 5.1.4/5.3.1/5.7.1's @cosmic/ui line, and PRD 10's "@cosmic/ui (Stub — Needs Implementation)" entry, recording in the spec that theme + semantic HTML is the chosen pattern (which PRD 8.6 already half-says); or keep the goal and mark those sections "not started" so they stop reading as current requirements.

findings.title: Per-demo review Status columns are stale, so the existing backlog cannot be trusted
findings.evidence: GR-1 is recorded as severity P1, Status **open**: "The 'visible matter only' benchmark (galaxyRotationModel.ts:401-404) is built as a spherical sqrt(G M_vis(<R)/R)". It is fixed: `galaxyRotationModel.ts:418-433` defines `vVisibleKmS` returning `Math.hypot(vBulge, vDisk)`, exactly the fix the review prescribes, and line 550 uses the same composition in the curve builder. The fix is also recorded in docs/audits/2026-09-03-comprehensive-adversarial-audit.md §9 "Follow-up (2026-09-04)" — in a different file, under a different ID (P2-2/GR-1), while the review that owns the finding still says open. Conversely GR-3, SL-4, SL-5, HR-4 and HR-5 are marked open and I verified all five are still open in code. So the Status column is right in some rows and wrong in others, with no way to tell which without reading the code.
findings.scenario: Anyone folding docs/reviews/ into a tracker imports GR-1 as open work and spends a session re-fixing a fix, or trusts the column the other way and ships a demo with GR-3 still live. This is the precise failure the audit brief describes as "rediscovered rather than folded in" — the reviews already cost the project their findings twice.
findings.fix: Make the review file the single owner of each finding's status: when a fix lands, update the row in docs/reviews/<slug>.md in the same commit (the audit remediation log can link to it, not duplicate it). Add the demo's open-finding IDs to the readiness gate so a demo cannot sit at `candidate` with an open P1/P2 physics-copy row.

findings.title: content_verified: true is a public claim backed only by a file-existence check
findings.evidence: The legacy migration contract (docs/specs/cosmic-playground-legacy-demo-migration-contract.md, "Definition of done" item 4) says `content_verified: true` only after "the exhibit/station/instructor copy is reviewed against the migrated UI and exports". The gate at validate-play-dirs.mjs:200-230 only tests `/^content_verified:\s*true\s*$/m` and then that `docs/reviews/<slug>.md` exists — it never reads the review's verdict or its open rows. Result, measured across all 20 demo content files: 19 carry `content_verified: true` (only planetary-conjunctions is false), while `lastVerifiedAt` is 2026-02-02 for nine of them (angular-size, blackbody-radiation, eclipse-geometry, em-spectrum, moon-phases, seasons, telescope-resolution) — eight months stale — and galaxy-rotation and spectral-lines carry `true` with the open P0-class copy defects above.
findings.scenario: An exhibit page tells a visiting instructor the content has been checked against the instrument, and the model notes on that instrument contradict the drawing (findings 1-3). The badge converts an unverified claim into a verified-looking one, which is worse than no badge.
findings.fix: Extend the gate: `content_verified: true` requires (a) the review file exists, (b) it has no row whose Status is "open" at P0/P1, and (c) `lastVerifiedAt` is not older than the newest commit touching that demo's index.html / logic.ts / main.ts. Flip the nine stale ones to false until re-checked.

findings.title: Three documents define "ready" differently, and the one on the page is the most permissive
findings.evidence: readiness.ts:48 renders `candidate` to the reader as "near-ready" with the accessible name "Readiness: candidate -- ready to assign, pending final review". PRD 8.5 defines the same state as "passes migration gates, awaiting launch hardening verification", with promotion to launch-ready requiring "all Section 6.1 launch gates pass with no open P0/P1 blockers". docs/specs/cosmic-playground-pilot-quality-bar.md is a third, independent definition — a 7-section exemplar checklist (A-G) whose own scope note says "it is acceptable that many library demos remain stubbed or incomplete", so it grades a different thing again and is reachable from neither of the other two. Measured consequence: galaxy-rotation and spectral-lines are both `candidate`, i.e. announced to instructors as "ready to assign", while carrying the open physics-copy defects in findings 1-3. Nothing checks PRD 8.5's transition rule — there is no validator reading review status (see previous finding), so the rule exists only in prose.
findings.scenario: An instructor filters Explore by readiness, takes the "near-ready" demos as assignable next week, and assigns galaxy-rotation. The badge's own wording authorizes that; PRD 8.5's rule, if it were enforced, would not.
findings.fix: Pick one vocabulary. Keep `readiness` (readiness.ts already argues well for it), move PRD 8.5's transition rules into the same file as executable predicates, soften the `candidate` aria text to match PRD 8.5 ("passes migration gates; not yet cleared for class use"), and either fold the quality bar's A-G checklist into the launch-ready predicate or mark the quality bar superseded.

findings.title: Three documents carry stale migration orders naming slugs that never existed
findings.evidence: Migration prompt §3.3 lists a 14-demo order containing six slugs that are not in the repo: `parallax` (actual: parallax-distance), `blackbody` (blackbody-radiation), `photon-energy` (no such demo), `spectral-lines` is there but `eclipses` (eclipse-geometry), `two-body` (binary-orbits) and `hr-diagram` (stars-zams-hr) are not. Verified against `ls apps/demos/src/demos/`: 20 demos, all built, all present in apps/site/public/play/. CLAUDE.md carries a different 13-item order whose item 2 is "angular-size — similar complexity" as though pending; angular-size is `readiness: candidate`, migrated since February. docs/backlog.md still reads "retrograde-motion — multi-body, next in migration order" with conservation-laws, binary-orbits and planetary-conjunctions listed as remaining; all four are migrated (conservation-laws was refactored and promoted to candidate on 2026-09-11 per STATUS.md). Neither the prompt nor CLAUDE.md's order mentions the seven demos added since: cluster-census, doppler-shift, eos-lab, galaxy-rotation, hydrostatic-equilibrium-explorer, spectral-lines, stars-zams-hr.
findings.scenario: An agent asked to "continue the migration" reads CLAUDE.md's order, starts on angular-size, and re-migrates a candidate-grade demo; or follows the prompt's `photon-energy`/`two-body` names and creates duplicate slugs beside em-spectrum and binary-orbits, which would then both satisfy validate-play-dirs.
findings.fix: Delete the order from all three places and replace it with one pointer to the readiness table the content files already define (`readiness` + `readinessReason` across apps/site/src/content/demos/). An order is a derived view; it should be read from the schema, not typed three times.

findings.title: Site spec 9.2 requires ?mode=math in the URL and localStorage for every demo; neither exists
findings.evidence: Site spec 9.2 item 1: every demo must support `concept` (default) and `math` modes, "Mode reflected in URL query (?mode=math) and persisted in localStorage." Verified: a grep for `mode=math` or `?mode=` across apps/demos/src/demos returns nothing, and `packages/runtime/src/demoModes.ts` contains no `localStorage`, `location.search`, `URLSearchParams` or `history.` reference at all — `createDemoModes` (demoModes.ts:701) does something else entirely (help/station/challenge wiring). The frontmatter field that advertises the feature is `has_math_mode`, and it is `true` for exactly 1 of 20 demos (hydrostatic-equilibrium-explorer) — yet it drives a visible "math mode" pill on exhibit pages (exhibits/[slug].astro:55) and is passed to cards on four more surfaces (index.astro:128, explore/index.astro:250 and :318, topics/[slug].astro:150).
findings.scenario: An instructor links a lecture slide to `/play/keplers-laws/?mode=math` expecting the derivation view, and gets the default demo with the query silently ignored — and no way to deep-link a mode at all. The nineteen `has_math_mode: false` values also make a schema-required field carry no information.
findings.fix: Either implement mode in @cosmic/runtime once (URL param read on load, written on change, mirrored to localStorage) and set `has_math_mode` honestly per demo, or strike 9.2 item 1 from the site spec, drop `has_math_mode` from content/config.ts and the five render sites, and record the decision. Do not leave the pill rendering from a field nothing implements.

findings.title: Every spec says "Draft", so binding contracts and never-started suite PRDs read alike
findings.evidence: Read the Status line of all 27 files in docs/specs/: 24 say "Draft" with varying parentheticals, and three (CLAUDE-CODE-MIGRATION-PROMPT.md, cosmic-playground-codex-skills.md, cosmic-playground-roadmap.md) have no Status line at all. The parentheticals do not separate the categories: the enforced data contract says "Draft (enforced)", the dead plot contract says "Draft (proposed for enforcement)", and cosmology-suite-prd.md (1,270 lines), galaxies-suite-prd.md (883), galaxy-merger-demo-spec.md (690), data-viewer-spec.md (639), stellar-demo-02-opacity-diffusion-memo.md (229) and cosmic-playground-authoring-kit-spec.md (134) all say "Draft" too. Verified not started: a grep for `data-viewer`, `galaxy-merger`, `opacity-diffusion` or `authoring-kit` across apps, packages and scripts returns zero hits, and apps/site/src/pages holds 15 .astro files with no data-viewer route. Classification by evidence: implemented — site-spec (mostly), data-contract, model-contract, theme-spec, legacy-migration-contract, and the six shipped per-demo specs (doppler-shift, galaxy-rotation, spectral-lines, stars-zams-hr, blackbody-radiation-v2, binary-orbits-spectroscopy); partially — PRD, stellar-structure-suite-prd (eos-lab unlisted + hydrostatic-equilibrium-explorer exist; opacity-diffusion does not), authoring-kit (scripts/new-demo.mjs only), demo-shell-variants; not started — cosmology-suite-prd, galaxies-suite-prd, galaxy-merger-demo-spec, data-viewer-spec; contradicted by the code — plot-contract, CLAUDE-CODE-MIGRATION-PROMPT, roadmap/execution board; superseded — pilot-quality-bar (by the readiness vocabulary).
findings.scenario: An agent told to "read the specs" ingests 51,971 lines in which an enforced invariant and a speculative 1,270-line cosmology PRD carry identical authority, then either builds unasked-for scope or treats a live contract as aspirational. This is the root cause of most of the other findings in this report.
findings.fix: Add one required front-matter line to every file in docs/specs/ with a closed vocabulary — `Lifecycle: enforced | implemented | partial | not-started | superseded-by <path>` — and a one-line index in docs/specs/README.md (which does not exist today) listing each file and its lifecycle. Move `not-started` suite PRDs to docs/specs/future/ so a directory listing already separates them.

findings.title: keplers-laws reports acceleration in mm/s^2, which CLAUDE.md forbids outright
findings.evidence: logic.ts:140-142: the non-201 branch computes `{ value: AstroUnits.auPerYr2ToMPerS2(args.accelAuDerYr2) * 1000, unit: "mm/s^2" }` — AU/yr^2 converted to SI m/s^2 and then scaled to millimetres, while the 201 branch next to it uses the CGS `auPerYr2ToCmPerS2`. The SI converters it calls are exported from packages/physics/src/units.ts:76-89 (`auPerYr2ToMPerS2`, `mPerS2ToAuPerYr2`) alongside the CGS sibling at :91. CLAUDE.md: "ALWAYS use CGS units... NEVER use SI units (meters, kg, Joules)", and the invariants file repeats it. Logged as P2-11 in the 2026-09-03 audit and listed under §9 "Still open". Nothing enforces it: no validator scans for SI unit strings or SI converter calls.
findings.scenario: An ASTR 101 student copies results from keplers-laws and an ASTR 201 student copies the same readout, and the two lab notebooks carry accelerations in mm/s^2 and cm/s^2 — a factor of 10 apart, in a course whose stated convention is CGS everywhere. The export rows inherit the same unit string, so the mismatch propagates into worksheets.
findings.fix: Change the 101 branch to CGS (`auPerYr2ToCmPerS2`, unit "cm/s^2"), choosing a display scale if cm/s^2 reads awkwardly, and delete the two SI converters from units.ts so the forbidden path cannot be taken again. Add an invariant that fails on the literals "m/s^2", "mm/s^2", "m/s", "kg" and "J" in demo reader-visible strings.

findings.title: The active execution board's P0/P1 tickets name files that were never created
findings.evidence: The board is headed "Status: active". Verified against the filesystem: CP-004 (P0) targets `scripts/validate-content-verification.mjs` + its test — neither exists (scripts/ holds build, gates, copy-katex-assets, import-astr101-sp26, new-demo, and the six validate-* pairs; no content-verification one); CP-008 (P1) targets `scripts/validate-demo-architecture.mjs` — does not exist, which is why finding 4's inline physics ships; CP-006 (P1) targets `packages/runtime/src/demoBootstrap.ts` — does not exist (the shipped equivalent is `createInstrumentRuntime` at packages/runtime/src/index.ts:175, under a different name the board never mentions); CP-002 (P0) targets `.github/workflows/pr-ci.yml` — does not exist, and is now unnecessary because deploy.yml's `verify` job runs on every event (its own comment records the fix). So one P0 is superseded, one P0 and two P1s are abandoned, and the board still says active.
findings.scenario: A session picks up the board, writes `pr-ci.yml` as specified, and lands a second CI workflow that duplicates `verify` and doubles the Pages concurrency contention that CLAUDE.md already warns about. Meanwhile the two guardrails that would catch live defects (CP-004, CP-008) stay unbuilt because nothing distinguishes them from the superseded ticket.
findings.fix: Mark the board superseded and move the two tickets that still matter — the content-verification gate (finding 8) and the demo-architecture gate (finding 4) — into STATUS.md's open list with their real target paths. Record that CP-002 was satisfied by deploy.yml's verify job and CP-006 by `createInstrumentRuntime`.

findings.title: Shell-variants spec defines three layout variants; the code ships a fourth and calls the mechanism legacy
findings.evidence: The spec's opt-in mechanism allows exactly `data-shell="instrument"` (default), `"triad"` and `"viz-first"`. Verified in the demos: the values actually used are `viz-first`, `triad` and `orbit` — the last undocumented, and the one carrying the newest work (packages/theme/styles/demo-shell.css:354-430 and layer-instrument.css:201-230 implement it for the conservation-laws orbit stage landed 2026-09-11). demo-shell.css:302 heads the block "Backward compatibility: data-shell attributes", so the implementation treats the spec's mechanism as legacy while the spec presents it as the way to opt in. Separately, PRD 5.2.2 pairs `data-shell` with `data-layout`; a grep for `data-layout` across apps and packages (html/css/ts) returns zero hits — it was never implemented.
findings.scenario: A new demo sets `data-shell="instrument"` per the spec and gets the default rules with no variant styling, or copies `data-layout` from PRD 5.2.2 and gets a no-op attribute. The reader of either document cannot tell that `orbit` is the live pattern.
findings.fix: Update the spec to the three values the CSS implements (triad, viz-first, orbit), document what `orbit` is for and that omitting the attribute is the default, and drop `data-layout` from PRD 5.2.2. One `SHELL_VARIANTS` list in packages/theme with an invariant rejecting unknown `data-shell` values would keep the spec and the CSS from drifting again.

findings.title: Doc indexes contradict their own directories, and five trackers compete for the live backlog
findings.evidence: The reviews index table lists 13 files; the directory holds 22. Missing from the table: cluster-census.md, doppler-shift.md, galaxy-rotation.md, hydrostatic-equilibrium-explorer.md, spectral-lines.md, stars-zams-hr.md, eos-lab-2026-09-03.md, 2026-09-04-layout-audit.md and 2026-02-07-seasons-eclipse-physics-review.md — i.e. six of the eight demos whose reviews carry the open findings above are absent from the index pointing at them. docs/audits/README.md says the 2026-09-03 audit covered "All 19 demos"; there are 20 (19 listed plus eos-lab, `unlisted: true`). docs/README.md lists four subdirectories and omits curriculum/, grants/, migration/ and reviews/. Trackers, all live in the tree: STATUS.md (1,071 lines, genuinely current, carries `next:`/`blocker:`/`due:` for the brain), TASKS.md (an untouched template — three empty sections with HTML comments), CHANGELOG.md (one bullet, "Initial monorepo scaffold", under "Unreleased"), docs/backlog.md (stale migration order, see finding 10), and docs/migration/2026-02-02-demo-migration-dashboard.md ("Snapshot (current repo state): Cosmic Playground demo slugs: 13" against today's 20, and lists spectral-lines and doppler-shift as "Missing from Cosmic Playground (needs migration)" though both ship).
findings.scenario: Anyone looking for "what is true now" opens TASKS.md or the migration dashboard first — both read as authoritative trackers and both are wrong by months — and plans from a 13-demo repo that has 20 demos, or reports progress from a CHANGELOG that has recorded nothing since the scaffold.
findings.fix: Keep exactly STATUS.md (live state + open backlog) and docs/reviews/<slug>.md (per-demo findings with accurate Status). Delete TASKS.md and docs/backlog.md after folding their live items into STATUS.md; mark docs/migration/2026-02-02-demo-migration-dashboard.md historical (it is dated, so leave it as a snapshot but say so in its title); either maintain CHANGELOG.md per release or delete it; regenerate docs/reviews/README.md and docs/README.md from the directory listing, and fix "19 demos" in docs/audits/README.md.

findings.title: `.cp-playbar` cannot wrap and the mobile shell gives it a bare `1fr` track, so four demos lay out ~580-650px wide on any phone
findings.evidence: `.cp-playbar` (playbar.css:5-16) is `display: flex` with `gap: var(--cp-space-2)` and NO `flex-wrap`. Its items cannot shrink below min-content (default `min-width: auto`). `demo-shell.css:323` sets the mobile layout to `grid-template-columns: 1fr` — not `minmax(0, 1fr)` — so the single track's automatic minimum is the widest item's min-content width. Computed floor, from the declared values (root font-size is 18px because `tokens.css:337` sets `html, body { font-size: var(--cp-text-md) }` = 1.125rem; `--cp-text-sm` = 15.75px; box-sizing is content-box on these pages, see the separate finding, so `min-width: 44px` + 1px borders = 46px per button, and `.cp-select{min-width:84px;padding:12px 16px;border:1px}` = 118px): 5 x 46 (btn) + 165 (`.speed-control` = "Speed" + select) + 113-142 (`.cp-playbar__phase`, `white-space: nowrap`, min-width 10ch) + 6 x 8 (gaps) + 24 padding + 2 border => 583px (doppler-shift, galaxy-rotation), 611px (spectral-lines, whose phase text is "Sequence paused"), and 621px for moon-phases, whose `.playbar-transport` (moon-phases/style.css:207) is its own no-wrap flex row carrying 5 buttons + speed select + a `Focus Moon` `.cp-button`. Add the shell's `padding: var(--cp-space-4)` (demo-shell.css:52, not reduced on mobile) for a page floor of 615/643/653px. The glyph-advance assumptions (0.5em sans, 0.6em mono) are the only estimated inputs; everything else is declared. The two demos that DID fix this did it per-demo: `seasons/style.css:385` adds `flex-wrap: wrap` to `.seasons-instrument-bar` plus `min-width: min(340px, 100%)` on the scrub, and `retrograde-motion/style.css:269` sets `flex-direction: column` with row restored only inside `@media (min-width: 1025px)`.
findings.scenario: A student opens /play/galaxy-rotation/ on a 390x844 iPhone. `.cp-demo`'s single grid track sizes to the playbar's 583px min-content, so the page lays out 615px wide in a 390px viewport. The stage, the readouts and the right half of the transport sit off-screen; dragging the radius slider changes a velocity readout the student has to scroll sideways to see, and the horizontal scroll position resets nothing, so they lose the stage every time they check a number. Same on moon-phases (653px), spectral-lines (643px), doppler-shift (615px).
findings.fix: At the shell level: `demo-shell.css:323` -> `grid-template-columns: minmax(0, 1fr)` (the orbit variant at line 416 already does this), and add `flex-wrap: wrap` to `.cp-playbar` in `playbar.css:5` plus `flex: 1 1 auto; min-width: 0` on `.cp-playbar__timeline`. Then add `flex-wrap: wrap` to `moon-phases/style.css:207` `.playbar-transport` or replace it with the shared component. Both halves are needed: `minmax(0,1fr)` stops the TRACK growing, `flex-wrap` stops the bar painting outside it.

findings.title: seasons' Earth-orbit drag and retrograde-motion's timeline scrub have no `touch-action`, so a phone cancels them into a page pan
findings.evidence: `touch-action` appears in exactly two places in the whole repo (verified with `grep -rn touch-action` excluding node_modules/dist/public): `packages/theme/styles/components/bottom-sheet.css:40` and `apps/demos/src/demos/cluster-census/style.css:231`. seasons binds Pointer Events to the orbit dot (`seasons/main.ts:1231-1242`: pointerdown/pointermove/pointerup/pointercancel/lostpointercapture) and `startOrbitDrag` (main.ts:1177-1189) does `setPointerCapture` and `event.preventDefault()`. `preventDefault()` on `pointerdown` does NOT suppress touch scrolling — only `touch-action` does — so the browser starts its pan, fires `pointercancel`, and the registered `pointercancel` handler calls `stopOrbitDrag`. retrograde-motion/main.ts:1240-1252 is the same shape on `plotSvgEl` and does not even call `preventDefault`. Contrast the three demos that use legacy touch events and DO work: moon-phases/main.ts:512-516 and 553 (`touchstart` registered `{passive:false}` with `event.preventDefault()` in `startDrag`), keplers-laws/main.ts:766-771, eclipse-geometry/main.ts:1561 and 1616 — `preventDefault()` on `touchstart` does suppress the scroll for that gesture.
findings.scenario: A student on a phone presses the Earth dot on /play/seasons/ and drags it around its orbit to see how the subsolar latitude changes through the year. After a few pixels of movement Chrome/Safari decides the gesture is a vertical page pan, dispatches `pointercancel`, and `stopOrbitDrag` runs: the dot snaps back, the page scrolls, and the demo's headline interaction is unusable. Identical on /play/retrograde-motion/ when scrubbing the timeline to find the stationary points.
findings.fix: Add `touch-action: none` to the two drag surfaces (`#earthOrbitDot` in seasons/style.css, `#plotSvg` in retrograde-motion/style.css), matching the pattern and the comment already at cluster-census/style.css:230-232. Better: put `touch-action: none` on a shared `.cp-draggable` class in `packages/theme` and apply it wherever a drag is bound, so the next ported demo inherits it.

findings.title: No `.katex-display` containment rule reaches any demo page: 11 demos' display equations are unbreakable boxes with nothing to clip them
findings.evidence: `apps/site/src/styles/global.css:289-300` contains `.katex-display { overflow-x: auto; overflow-y: hidden; max-width: 100% }` with the comment "a multi-part relation like the three pressure laws renders 575px wide and forced a 320px viewport to scroll (WCAG 1.4.10)". `/play/<slug>/` is the demo's own standalone HTML (galaxy-rotation/index.html:7-8 loads only `./style.css` and `../../assets/katex/katex.min.css`), and `apps/demos/src/shared/stub-demo.css:1-16` imports 16 theme stylesheets but NOT `prose.css` — and `grep -c cp-prose` is 0 in all 20 demo index.html files, so `prose.css:83`'s `.cp-prose .katex-display` would not match anyway. `packages/runtime/src/math.ts:31` registers `{ left: "$$", right: "$$", display: true }`, which emits `span.katex-display`. Counting `$$` tokens in each index.html: binary-orbits 7 equations, hydrostatic-equilibrium-explorer 7, spectral-lines 7, blackbody-radiation 4, galaxy-rotation 4, angular-size 3, doppler-shift 3, seasons 2, cluster-census 1, parallax-distance 1, telescope-resolution 1. Only one scoped patch exists: `binary-orbits/style.css:128` `.cp-live-insight :where(.katex-display) { overflow-x: auto }` — which does not cover binary-orbits' own seven accordion equations at index.html:396-428, e.g. `$$f(m) = \frac{P K_1^3}{2\pi G}, \qquad M_1\sin^3 i,\; M_2\sin^3 i.$$`. reflow.spec.ts:49-51 independently records that binary-orbits "currently DOES scroll sideways at 320px (its drawer accordions take their minimum from unbreakable KaTeX display equations)".
findings.scenario: A student opens the 'How the masses follow' accordion on /play/binary-orbits/ at 390px. KaTeX renders the mass-function relation as one ~500-575px box with no scroll container, so it widens the accordion, widens the `1fr` grid track, and widens the page; the right-hand side of the equation — the part that says what is actually measured — sits off-screen with no affordance saying so. Same on hydrostatic-equilibrium-explorer, whose seven display equations include the three pressure laws that produced the measured 575px.
findings.fix: Move the `.katex-display` block (global.css:289-305, including the `:focus-visible` ring and the `padding-block: 2px`) into `packages/theme/styles/components/prose.css` unscoped, or into a new `packages/theme/styles/katex.css`, and import it from both `stub-demo.css` and the site's global.css. Then delete the five redundant per-demo wrappers: binary-orbits:128, conservation-laws:170 and :397, doppler-shift:306, galaxy-rotation:156, eos-lab:569.

findings.title: Demo pages never get `box-sizing: border-box`; the only three fixes are per-element and gated behind `min-width: 1025px`
findings.evidence: `box-sizing: border-box` appears in the shipped CSS exactly four times (exhaustive grep over *.css/*.html/*.astro excluding node_modules, dist and public/play): `apps/site/src/styles/global.css:15` (the site's universal reset, which demo pages do not load), and three per-element patches — `eos-lab/style.css:918`, `parallax-distance/style.css:440`, `stars-zams-hr/style.css:685`. All three sit inside `@media (min-width: 1025px)` / `@media (min-width: 1081px)` blocks (eos-lab:911, parallax-distance:433, stars-zams-hr:674), so they are inactive on every phone. Their own comments show the authors knew: parallax-distance:437 "The stage sizes as content-box, so without this the 12px padding and 1px border sit outside the height"; stars-zams-hr:683 "Without this the cap lands on the CONTENT box and the stage ends up 26px taller than it reads". Consequence under content-box: every `width: 100%` element with padding overflows its container by padding+border — `form.css:3-19` gives `.cp-input, .cp-select, .cp-textarea, .cp-demo select` `width: 100%` with `padding: 12px 16px` and a 1px border, i.e. +34px over the box they are told to fill, in every one of the 20 demos.
findings.scenario: At 320px the shell's 16px padding leaves 288px, and a `.cp-panel` adds its own 16px each side, so a sidebar `<select>` is told it is 100% of ~256px and lays out at 290px. It overflows its panel, and because the mobile track is `1fr` (auto minimum) it widens the page too. Every unit picker, preset select and text input in the set inherits the same 34px error, and the three demos that noticed fixed it only above 1025px.
findings.fix: Add `*, *::before, *::after { box-sizing: border-box }` at the top of `packages/theme/styles/tokens.css` (which both `global.css` and `stub-demo.css` import first), then delete the three now-redundant per-element patches so no one concludes box-sizing is a per-element decision. Re-check the three stage height caps after the change, since they were authored against content-box.

findings.title: All three Playwright projects are `devices["Desktop Chrome"]`: no test in the suite has touch, so no touch defect can ever be caught
findings.evidence: playwright.config.ts:30-55 defines three projects — `desktop` (Desktop Chrome, 1280x720), `mobile` (Desktop Chrome, 320x512, `testMatch: /reflow\.spec\.ts/`) and `visual` (Desktop Chrome, 1280x720). None sets `hasTouch` or `isMobile`, and none uses a `devices["Pixel ..."]`/`devices["iPhone ..."]` descriptor. `grep -rn "hasTouch|isMobile|tap()|touchscreen|dispatchEvent.*touch" apps/site/playwright.config.ts apps/site/tests/*.ts` returns nothing but those three `devices[` lines. So the "mobile" project is a narrow desktop browser: `TouchEvent` is not constructible, `pointerType` is always "mouse", `@media (hover: hover)` still matches, and `touch-action` is never exercised. It also runs ONLY reflow.spec.ts, so none of the 20 per-demo specs ever runs at a phone width.
findings.scenario: The seasons and retrograde-motion drag defects above, the eos-lab hover-only readout, and every `:hover`-gated affordance are all green in CI today and will stay green through any future regression, because the only narrow-viewport project in the config cannot generate a touch.
findings.fix: Add a fourth project `use: { ...devices["Pixel 7"] }` (hasTouch, isMobile, touch pointer, 412x915) with a `testMatch` covering reflow.spec.ts plus a new `touch.spec.ts`, and write that spec to assert the gestures: `page.touchscreen.tap()` on each playbar button, and a `locator.dragTo()`/`touchscreen` swipe on each drag surface asserting the demo's state actually changed and the page's `scrollY` did not.

findings.title: reflow.spec.ts covers 1 of 20 `/play/` routes, so 19 demo instruments have no reflow gate at all
findings.evidence: Confirmed by reading. `CONTENT_ROUTES` (reflow.spec.ts:54-61) = `MUSEUM_ROUTES` (9 routes: "", explore/, playlists/, topics/, for-instructors/, instructor/, about/, glossary/, welcome/) + `exhibits/<slug>/`, `stations/<slug>/` and `instructor/<slug>/` for all 20 slugs read from `src/content/demos` (`ls apps/site/src/content/demos/*.md | wc -l` = 20) + `PLAY_ROUTES`, which is literally `["play/conservation-laws/"]` (line 52). That is 70 routes, 69 of them museum/content pages and exactly one instrument. The spec's own comment at 46-51 explains why: play routes are added "one demo at a time ... whose /play/ page has been separately verified not to scroll sideways at 320px", and names binary-orbits as a known failure. conservation-laws is also the only demo with 0 `$$` display equations and no `.cp-playbar` — i.e. the one demo that could pass.
findings.scenario: Every finding in this report that shows as horizontal overflow — the four playbar demos, the eleven demos with uncontained display equations, the content-box selects — is invisible to the gate, because the gate looks at the one instrument that happens to have neither trigger.
findings.fix: Keep the ratchet shape but invert the default: iterate all 20 slugs and mark the known-failing ones with `test.fail()` (or a `KNOWN_REFLOW_FAILURES` set), so the list shrinks visibly and a newly-fixed demo fails loudly the way layout-budget.spec.ts does. That also records which demos are broken instead of leaving it implicit in a one-element array.

findings.title: layout-budget.spec.ts measures only 1440x900, and its own comments record that single-viewport sampling already missed two regressions
findings.evidence: Both test loops hard-code `page.setViewportSize({ width: 1440, height: 900 })` (lines 145 and 220) and assert `readoutsBelowFold` and `sidebarOverflowPx` against the `BUDGETS` ratchet. The spec's own comments admit the sampling gap twice: line 118-121 on stars-zams-hr — "at 1280x720 they switched off ... the stage grew to 856px with all ten readouts 329px past the fold ... This test only samples 1440x900, so it never saw it" — and line 125-128 on retrograde-motion, "all 12 at 1920x1080, 1366x768 and 1280x720, which this test's single 1440 sample could not see". There is no phone-width equivalent anywhere in apps/site/tests, and the `mobile` Playwright project's `testMatch` excludes this file.
findings.scenario: The mobile shell sets `.cp-demo__stage { min-height: clamp(360px, 56svh, 560px) }` (demo-shell.css:340). On a 390x844 phone that is 473px of stage before the playbar, readouts, controls and shelf; every readout is below the fold on every demo, and no gate measures it, so the readouts-below-the-fold defect that this whole ratchet exists to prevent is 100% unmeasured on the device students actually use.
findings.fix: Parameterise the two loops over `[[1440,900],[390,844]]` and give `BUDGETS` a per-viewport entry (`{ desktop: {...}, phone: {...} }`), seeded from whatever the first phone run measures. Add it to the `mobile` project's `testMatch`.

findings.title: eos-lab's regime-map readout is `mousemove`-only: no touch and no keyboard path to the temperature/density it reports
findings.evidence: `regimeMapCanvas` gets exactly three listeners: `click` (main.ts:1357, sets state.temperatureK / state.densityGPerCm3 from the tap point), `mousemove` (1371, the only code that populates and positions `regimeTooltip` with `T = ... K, rho = ... g/cm^3`) and `mouseleave` (1392, hides it). There is no `pointermove`, no `focus`/`blur`, and no `tabindex` on the canvas (`grep -n tabindex eos-lab/index.html` returns only the three `compare*Eq` divs at lines 373/387/401, not the regime map). Compare the demos that got this right: cluster-census/main.ts:1085-1097 pairs a `pointermove` hover with a `pointerup` tap-to-pin (and bindKeyboardSelection), and spectral-lines/main.ts:887-891 pairs the orbit hover with `focus`/`blur`.
findings.scenario: A student on a phone taps the regime map to place the star at a given temperature and density. The tap sets the sliders but `mouseleave` never fires on touch, so either no tooltip appears (iOS Safari dispatches no `mousemove` for a tap) or one appears and sticks on screen over the map. Either way the per-point T and rho the map is there to teach is unavailable, and a keyboard user cannot reach it at all.
findings.fix: Switch `mousemove`/`mouseleave` to `pointermove`/`pointerleave` + `pointercancel`, make the tooltip also render on `pointerup` so a tap shows the value it just set, and give the canvas `tabindex="0"` with arrow-key traversal plus `focus`/`blur` tooltip handling, mirroring cluster-census' `bindKeyboardSelection`.

findings.title: Stage height floors are unconditional in px, so every demo overflows its own viewport in landscape
findings.evidence: The mobile block sets `.cp-demo__stage { min-height: clamp(360px, 56svh, 560px) }` (demo-shell.css:340); `min-height` beats `max-height` in CSS, a fact this repo already records at binary-orbits/style.css:580. The per-demo mobile floors are the same shape: binary-orbits/style.css:530 `clamp(340px, 58svh, 620px)`, retrograde-motion/style.css:454 `clamp(340px, 52svh, 580px)`, conservation-laws/style.css:74 `height: clamp(270px, calc(100svh - 28rem), 760px)` (28rem = 504px at the 18px root, so on a phone the subtrahend exceeds the viewport and the 270px floor always wins). A grep for `@media` with `orientation` or any height condition across packages/theme/styles, apps/demos/src/demos and apps/site/src/styles returns exactly one hit in the whole repo: `spectral-lines/style.css:502 @media (max-height: 768px)`.
findings.scenario: A student rotates to landscape to see more of the orbit — the natural thing to do with a wide diagram. On a 844x390 iPhone the 56svh term evaluates to 218px, so the 360px floor wins: the stage alone is 92% of the screen height and the playbar, readouts, controls and 'What to notice' are all below the fold, with no indication they exist. conservation-laws is worse, pinning a 270px stage in a 390px-tall viewport by a `calc` that can never win.
findings.fix: Make the floors height-aware: `min-height: min(360px, 70svh)` instead of `clamp(360px, 56svh, 560px)` — the `min()` form respects a short viewport where `clamp()`'s lower bound cannot. Add one `@media (orientation: landscape) and (max-height: 500px)` block in demo-shell.css that drops the stage floor and un-stacks the controls beside it, and delete the per-demo px floors that would override it.

findings.title: The slider thumb — the primary control of every instrument — is 20x20 on a 6px track, under the WCAG 2.2 2.5.8 minimum size
findings.evidence: `.cp-range, .cp-demo input[type="range"]` is declared `height: 6px` (form.css:84) with `::-webkit-slider-thumb { width: 20px; height: 20px; margin-top: -7px }` (form.css:114-120) and the matching `::-moz-range-thumb` at 156-158. So the draggable thumb is 20x20 CSS px and the track you tap to jump the value is 6 CSS px tall. Honest reading of 2.5.8: this is below the 24x24 minimum, but it most likely passes via the Spacing exception — sidebar controls are separated by `.cp-panel-body { gap: var(--cp-space-3) }` (12px, stub-demo.css:18-21) plus a ~26px label row from `.control` (control.css:36-40), giving >24px offset between adjacent thumbs. It is still roughly half of Apple's 44pt and Google's 48dp guidance, on the control a student uses hundreds of times per session. I did not find a clear 2.5.8 violation anywhere in the set: `.cp-playbar__btn` and `.cp-utility-btn` are both `min-width/min-height: 44px` (playbar.css:24-25, utility-toolbar.css:20-21), `.cp-chip` computes ~26px tall (chip.css:13-16 with `--cp-text-sm` = 15.75px, `line-height: 1`), `.cp-tab` ~37px (tabs.css:11-20), and retrograde-motion's annotation close button is `2rem` = 36px (retrograde-motion/style.css:369).
findings.scenario: A student on a phone tries to set the dark-matter concentration on galaxy-rotation. Their fingertip covers ~45px; the thumb is 20px on a 6px band, so they repeatedly grab nothing, or land on the track and jump the value past where they wanted. Every slider-driven demo in the set shares the geometry.
findings.fix: Grow the thumb to 24x24 and raise the hit area without changing the visual track: keep `height: 6px` on the painted track but add `padding-block: 9px; background-clip: content-box` (or wrap the input in a 44px-tall `.cp-range-hit` label), and bump the thumb to 24px with `margin-top: -9px`. Then add a token test in `packages/theme/src/tokens.test.ts` asserting the thumb is >= 24px so it cannot regress.

findings.title: `.cp-toggle`'s switch is 36x20, making the whole toggle a 20px-tall target
findings.evidence: `.cp-toggle input[type="checkbox"]` is `appearance: none; width: 36px; height: 20px` (toggle.css:23-27) with a 14x14 `::after` knob (toggle.css:42-44). The wrapping `.cp-toggle` label is `display: inline-flex; align-items: center; font-size: 0.85rem` (toggle.css:14-21) = 15.3px text at the 18px root, so the label's own line box is shorter than the switch and the composite target height is the switch's 20px (+2px border) — under the 24x24 minimum. Clicking the label text does toggle it, which widens the target horizontally but not vertically.
findings.scenario: A student taps a 'Show vectors'-style toggle on a phone and misses the 22px-tall band, hitting the panel behind it; nothing happens and there is no feedback explaining why.
findings.fix: Set `min-height: 24px` on `.cp-toggle input[type="checkbox"]` (and grow the knob to 18px with the checked `translateX` adjusted from 16px to 14px), or give `.cp-toggle` `min-height: 44px; align-items: center` so the whole row is the target.

findings.title: MobileNav's `min-width: max-content` overrides its own viewport cap, because min-width beats max-width in CSS
findings.evidence: `.mobile-nav__panel` declares `min-width: max-content` (line 127) immediately followed by `max-width: calc(100vw - 2 * var(--cp-space-3))` (line 128), with the comment "size to content, capped at the viewport". CSS resolves a min-width/max-width conflict in favour of min-width, so the cap is advisory only: whenever the longest nav link's max-content width exceeds `100vw - 24px`, the panel wins and pushes past the viewport. `.mobile-nav__link` is `padding: var(--cp-space-3) var(--cp-space-4)` with `font-size: var(--cp-text-md)` (lines 142-147) = 20.25px at the 18px root, so each link costs its text plus 32px, inside a panel with another 24px of padding. Today's labels are short enough that reflow.spec.ts passes at 320px, so this is a latent trap rather than a live break — but the rule does not do what its comment says, and the component's own history (lines 70-74) is a previous instance of this panel forcing horizontal scroll at 320px.
findings.scenario: Someone adds a nav item such as 'Instructor resources' or a longer playlist name. At 320px the cap is 296px; the link needs ~230px of text plus 32px padding plus 24px panel padding = 286px, and the next label of similar length crosses it. `min-width: max-content` then widens the open panel past the viewport and the page scrolls sideways again — and reflow.spec.ts will catch it only if the spec opens the `<details>`, which it does not.
findings.fix: Replace line 127 with `width: max-content` (which the max-width does cap) and keep line 128, or write `min-width: min(max-content, calc(100vw - 2 * var(--cp-space-3)))`. Add a case to site-header.spec.ts that opens the nav at 320px and asserts the panel's `getBoundingClientRect().right <= 320`.

findings.title: moon-phases hides all eight phase names below 700px, leaving eight near-identical 20px circles
findings.evidence: `@media (max-width: 700px)` sets `.timeline-phase span { display: none }` and `.phase-icon { width: 20px; height: 20px }` (style.css:392-401). The eight timeline buttons (`grep -c 'class="timeline-phase"'` = 8) are `flex: 1; min-width: 0; padding: 4px 2px` in a `justify-content: space-between` strip with `gap: var(--cp-space-1)` (style.css:267-287). The accessible name survives (each button has `aria-label="New Moon"` etc., index.html:474-481) and the computed target is roughly 29x30px, so this is not a 2.5.8 or 1.1.1 failure — it is the pedagogical content that is gone. The rule is the right instinct (it prevents the `white-space: nowrap` labels at style.css:304-307 from overlapping at ~30px per button) but trades away the vocabulary the demo exists to teach, and 20px is too small to distinguish waxing crescent from waning crescent.
findings.scenario: A student on a phone works through the phase strip trying to learn which drawing is called 'waxing gibbous'. The names are hidden, the icons are 20px, and the only way to recover a name is a hover (impossible) or a screen reader. On the device most students will use, the phase-naming objective is unreachable.
findings.fix: Keep the labels and let them wrap instead of disappearing: drop `white-space: nowrap` from `.timeline-phase span`, allow two lines at `font-size: 0.6rem`, and show four phases per row by giving `.timeline-strip` `flex-wrap: wrap` with `flex: 1 1 22%` on the buttons. Keep the icons at 24px.

findings.title: CLAUDE.md's reflow gotcha prescribes the assertion reflow.spec.ts deliberately rejected, and will mislead the next agent
findings.evidence: CLAUDE.md's Verification gotchas say: "Reflow: test whether the page actually scrolls (`scrollTo(2000,0)`, then `scrollX > 0`), not `scrollWidth`." reflow.spec.ts computes `canScrollSideways` exactly that way (lines 72-74) and then explicitly does NOT assert it, with a measured justification at lines 118-129: "On routes with a wide table or display equation, Chromium propagates the CLIPPED descendant's scrollable overflow up to the root scroller, so the viewport can be dragged sideways into a region that is provably empty -- `document.elementFromPoint` out there returns <html> ... Setting `overflow-x: clip` on html/body does not suppress it." It asserts the better pair instead: no unclipped element with `right > 320` (line 109), and `document.body.getBoundingClientRect().width <= 321` (line 115). On the audit's own question — what the right assertion is — the spec is right and CLAUDE.md is stale: `scrollX > 0` false-positives on legitimately clipped scrollers, `scrollWidth` false-positives via the same propagation, and the widest-unclipped-element + body-layout-width pair is the one that answers 1.4.10.
findings.scenario: An agent adds a new reflow check (say for the `/play/` routes this audit recommends), follows CLAUDE.md, asserts `scrollX === 0`, and gets a failure on any route holding a wide table or display equation inside a correct `overflow-x: auto` scroller. It then 'fixes' the CSS by removing a legitimate scroll container — reintroducing real overflow to silence a phantom one.
findings.fix: Rewrite the CLAUDE.md gotcha to the spec's actual contract: "Reflow: assert (a) no element whose nearest `overflow-x: auto/scroll/hidden` ancestor is absent has `right > viewport`, and (b) `body.getBoundingClientRect().width <= viewport + 1`. Do NOT assert `scrollX > 0` or `scrollWidth` — Chromium propagates clipped descendants' overflow to the root scroller (see reflow.spec.ts:118)."

findings.title: spectral-lines' per-orbit energy is reachable only by hover or Tab, neither of which exists on a phone
findings.evidence: Each Bohr orbit gets `mouseenter` (main.ts:866), `mousemove` (876) and `mouseleave` (886) to show/hide the energy tooltip, plus `focus`/`blur` (887-891) and `click` -> `selectOrbitLevel(n)` (859). The code comment at main.ts:897-900 states the design intent plainly: "Thinned, the ladder below pushes labels off their own rings, so keep only the active pair ... Every other level's energy is still one hover or Tab away on the orbit itself." On touch there is no hover, and tapping a `tabindex="0"` SVG `<circle>` does not reliably move focus (iOS Safari in particular). The information is not lost — `aria-label` carries "Select orbit n=N, energy X eV" (main.ts:855) and tapping selects the level, which surfaces it in the readout — but the on-diagram affordance the comment relies on is mouse- and keyboard-only.
findings.scenario: A student on a phone wants to compare the n=4 and n=5 energies before choosing a transition. Both labels are suppressed and neither tooltip can be opened, so the only route is to tap each ring in turn and read the readout — losing the side-by-side comparison the hover was designed to give.
findings.fix: Call `showOrbitTooltip` from the existing `click` handler as well (dismissing on the next tap elsewhere or on a timeout), so a tap both selects the level and shows its energy in place. Switching `mouseenter`/`mousemove`/`mouseleave` to `pointerenter`/`pointermove`/`pointerleave` costs nothing and makes the stylus/trackpad path work too.

findings.title: Twelve of twenty demos have no media query below 800px, and two have none at all
findings.evidence: Counted per demo (`grep -c '@media'` and `grep -c '@media (max-width: [3-7][0-9][0-9]px)'` over each `style.css`): zero `@media` of any kind in angular-size and em-spectrum; zero phone-width (<=799px) rules in binary-orbits, blackbody-radiation, cluster-census, conservation-laws, eclipse-geometry, keplers-laws, planetary-conjunctions, retrograde-motion, seasons, telescope-resolution, plus the two above — 12 of 20. Only 8 have any phone-width rule (doppler-shift, eos-lab, galaxy-rotation, hydrostatic-equilibrium-explorer, moon-phases, parallax-distance, spectral-lines, stars-zams-hr). Meanwhile 16 of 20 have a `@media (min-width: 1025px)` block adding desktop refinements. The only mobile adaptation the other twelve receive is the shell's single `@media (max-width: 1024px)` stack (demo-shell.css:321-342), which reorders the four grid areas into one column and does nothing about the width of their contents.
findings.scenario: A student opens /play/eclipse-geometry/ or /play/keplers-laws/ on a phone and gets the desktop composition linearised: multi-column stage grids, `aspect-ratio` drawings sized from the full width, and readout rows laid out for a 1440px column, none of which has ever been looked at below 1024px. The effort ratio — 16 demos with desktop-only refinements, 8 with any phone rule — is the defect, not any one rule.
findings.fix: Treat the phone as the base case rather than the fallback: once the shared playbar/box-sizing/KaTeX fixes land, walk the twelve demos at 390px with the new touch Playwright project and add the one or two rules each actually needs. Give the shell a reduced mobile gutter (`padding: var(--cp-space-2)` below 480px) so demos are not fighting for 32px of a 320px viewport.

findings.title: Golden-reference printable station card swaps First and Third Quarter against the demo's own model
findings.evidence: The printed data table template reads `| First Quarter | 90 | 0.50 | 50 | Waning |` (line 46) and `| Third Quarter | 270 | 0.50 | 50 | Waxing |` (line 48). packages/physics/src/moonPhasesModel.ts:6 bins 67.5-112.5 deg as "Third Quarter" and :10 bins 247.5-292.5 deg as "First Quarter". I recomputed waxingWaningFromPhaseAngleDeg: at 90 deg, daysSinceNew = ((90-180+360) mod 360)/360 x 29.53 = 22.15 d > 14.765, so "Waning"; at 270 deg, 7.38 d, so "Waxing". The model's names and the waxing/waning column are both correct; only the station card's phase names are swapped. The row is also self-contradictory on its own terms: a first quarter moon is waxing by definition. Lines 14 and 31 of the same file give the correct cycle order (New -> First Quarter -> Full -> Third Quarter), which confirms the table alone is wrong. CLAUDE.md records this exact trap: "Moon phase convention: 0 = full, 90 = third quarter, 180 = new, 270 = first quarter" and "a waxing/waning swap passed because tests checked only full and new moon".
findings.scenario: A student prints the moon-phases station card (the Print worksheet button at stations/[slug].astro:33), reads the pre-filled row "First Quarter, 90, 0.50, 50, Waning", then drags the Moon to 90 deg in the demo and sees the readout say "Third Quarter". Either they trust the printed sheet and write down the wrong phase name on the four custom rows they must fill in (45, 135, 225, 315 deg), or they conclude the instrument is broken. Graded against the sheet, the correct answer is marked wrong. This is the card CLAUDE.md names as the golden reference that every other demo copies.
findings.fix: Swap the two phase names: line 46 becomes Third Quarter at 90 deg (Waning) and line 48 becomes First Quarter at 270 deg (Waxing). Then add the quarter phases to the word bank at line 63, which currently says only "quarter phases are at $90^{\\circ}$ and $270^{\\circ}$" without naming which is which. Add a content gate that reads each station card's prefilled table and asserts every row against MoonPhasesModel (and the equivalent model for other demos), so a hand-typed answer table cannot drift from the physics again.

findings.title: No pre/post instrument exists for any demo, so learning gain cannot be measured at all
findings.evidence: All 17 assessment banks follow the same post-only shape: "Clicker prompts" / "Short-answer checks" / "Exit ticket". `rg -ci 'exit ticket'` returns 1-3 per bank; no bank contains a matched pair of items administered before and after. `rg -ni 'LSCI|TOAST|Astronomy Diagnostic|concept inventory|pre/post|pretest' apps/site/src/content/` returns zero hits. docs/plans/next-session-learning-outcomes.md:40-45 specified exactly this work ("LSCI -> moon-phases, ADT -> seasons, retrograde-motion, TOAST -> angular-size, parallax-distance. Write 2-3 pre/post questions per demo") and it was never done; docs/curriculum/cosmic-playground-curriculum-guide.md:1191 only says "Compare pre/post concept inventory (if used)". 3 of 20 demos have no assessment bank at all (cluster-census, eos-lab, stars-zams-hr).
findings.scenario: Anna runs the suite for a semester and is asked, by a Cottrell/NSF-IUSE reviewer or a curriculum committee, whether the demos teach. She has clicker tallies from a single post-instruction moment and no baseline, so she cannot compute a normalized gain, cannot separate the demo's effect from the lecture's, and cannot say which of the 20 demos is worth the class period. docs/curriculum/astro-201-course-redesign.md:820 commits to ">0.3 normalized gain" as a success criterion that no shipped instrument can evaluate.
findings.fix: Add an `assessments` content collection whose schema requires, per demo, a single `pre_post_item` (stem, 4 options, key, the misconception each distractor diagnoses) plus an `exit_check` and a 3-level `rubric`. Seed it with the 20 items in the first recommendation below. Make the pre/post item the *same* text in both administrations and store it once. Gate promotion to `readiness: candidate` on the item existing.

findings.title: For Instructors page promises assessment rubrics; zero rubrics exist anywhere in the content
findings.evidence: Line 100 reads "Deeper notes: activities, assessment rubrics, model details, and known limitations." `rg -ni 'rubric' apps/site/src/content/` returns zero hits across all 20 demos, 19 station cards, 6 playlists, 4 hubs and 85 instructor files. Line 39 likewise tells instructors to "Read the instructor notes for timing, misconceptions, and assessment tips" and line 114 labels every card "{n} misconceptions targeted" -- including cards for cluster-census and stars-zams-hr, which have no instructor bundle at all (find apps/site/src/content/instructor -type f shows 17 slugs; eos-lab, cluster-census and stars-zams-hr are absent) and so land on the "Instructor notes not written yet" scaffold at instructor/[slug].astro:128.
findings.scenario: An instructor evaluating whether to adopt the suite reads "assessment rubrics" on the one page written for them, plans a graded lab around it, opens any of the 19 Instructor Notes cards and finds none. For cluster-census and stars-zams-hr the card is visually identical to moon-phases' but leads to a page that admits it is a scaffold. The page's own promise is the reason they stopped evaluating further.
findings.fix: Either write one shared 3-level rubric (claim / evidence / model limitation) in instructor/_shared and link it from each bundle, or change line 100 to name what is actually there ("activities, clicker items with answers, model details, and known limitations"). Separately, render a visible "notes not written" state on the cards at line 108-118 for the three slugs with no bundle, computed from the instructor collection rather than from the demo's misconceptions array.

findings.title: Station card override discards predict_prompt, play_steps and explain_prompt, so 13 of 18 printed cards have no Predict step
findings.evidence: Line 58 is `{StationOverride ? (<section>{<StationOverride />}</section>) : (<>...Predict / Play steps / Parameter table / Explain / Claim + evidence...</>)}` -- the authored markdown *replaces* the structured worksheet rather than composing with it. All 18 demos with an authored card take the override branch, so entry.data.predict_prompt, play_steps and explain_prompt never render for them. Counting "predict" case-insensitively in each override: 13 of 18 return 0 (angular-size, blackbody-radiation, cluster-census, eclipse-geometry, em-spectrum, eos-lab, hydrostatic-equilibrium-explorer, keplers-laws, moon-phases, parallax-distance, retrograde-motion, seasons, telescope-resolution). for-instructors/index.astro:72 advertises "One-page printable cards with controls, parameters, and the PPE flow for each demo" and :40 instructs "Have students follow the Predict -> Play -> Explain loop at each station".
findings.scenario: An instructor follows the Quick start, prints the moon-phases, seasons and angular-size cards for a station rotation, and hands out three worksheets with no prediction box -- the one step that makes the activity a predict-observe-explain cycle rather than slider-fidgeting. The predict_prompt is authored and schema-required for all 20 demos and is simply never shown. Every future authored card silently loses it too, which is why this keeps recurring.
findings.fix: Compose instead of replace: render the Predict section (predict_prompt + blank), then the override body, then Explain and Claim+Evidence. Keep the Parameter table inside the override's control. Add an E2E assertion that every /stations/<slug>/ page contains a Predict heading and the demo's predict_prompt text.

findings.title: Playlist pages render no readiness badge, and the flagship ASTR101 playlist marks three experimental demos Required
findings.evidence: The journey step at lines 84-106 renders title, a Required/Optional pill, time_minutes, goal, note and three buttons -- and never calls readinessBadge. DemoCard.astro:72 does call it, so Explore and exhibit pages warn and the playlist does not. astro-101-core-concepts.md lists 6 required demos; eclipse-geometry, telescope-resolution and blackbody-radiation are all `readiness: experimental`, whose own ariaLabel in readiness.ts:48 is "usable, still being revised". solar-system-geometry (use_case: lab) requires eclipse-geometry and planetary-conjunctions, both experimental. earth-sky-starters requires eclipse-geometry.
findings.scenario: An instructor picks "Astro 101 Core Concepts" from the For Instructors page because it is the one labelled for their course, sees "6 required", prints the cards and assigns it. Half the required sequence is demo content the project itself classifies as still being revised, and the only surface that says so is the page they did not visit. If any of those three changes mid-semester, the assignment changes under them.
findings.fix: Render readinessBadge(entry.data.readiness) in the journey step header beside the Required pill, and surface readinessReason as the badge's title. Then add a content gate that fails the build when a playlist step has `required: true` and the demo's readiness is `experimental` or `stub` -- either promote the demo or mark the step optional.

findings.title: A lab playlist built around Station mode requires a demo that has neither Station Mode nor a station card
findings.evidence: solar-system-geometry.md has `use_case: "lab"`, `audience: "For inquiry labs (Station mode)"` and instructions "Work through the demos in order and complete station artifacts for each." Line 20 lists planetary-conjunctions with `required: true`. apps/demos/src/demos/planetary-conjunctions/main.ts contains no `station:` config (grep -c returns 0; every other demo except em-spectrum returns >=1), and apps/site/src/content/stations/planetary-conjunctions.md does not exist, so /stations/planetary-conjunctions/ falls back to the generic template with the "Generic station template" warning at stations/[slug].astro:95. planetary-conjunctions also has no station_params, so the parameter table prints two rows of blanks. em-spectrum has the same Station Mode gap and is `required: true` in light-and-measuring-the-universe.
findings.scenario: The lab is running, students rotate to station 4, and the instruction sheet says to collect rows in Station Mode and export the table. There is no Station Mode button on planetary-conjunctions and the printed card is the generic fallback with two blank rows. The station produces no artifact, so one fifth of the lab cannot be graded and the instructor improvises in front of 30 students.
findings.fix: Three options, cheapest first: (a) demote planetary-conjunctions to `required: false` in solar-system-geometry and em-spectrum in light-and-measuring-the-universe, and say in the note that these two have no Station Mode; (b) author stations/planetary-conjunctions.md with a synodic-period data table (pairs, P1, P2, measured recurrence, 1/P_syn = |1/P1 - 1/P2|); (c) add the station config to both demos. Then gate: a playlist with use_case "lab" may not have a required step whose demo lacks a `station:` config.

findings.title: No ASTR201 sequence exists, and six demos appear in no playlist at all
findings.evidence: All six playlists have intended_level 101 (astro-101-core-concepts, earth-sky-starters, planetary-conjunctions-starter, solar-system-geometry) or mixed (light-and-measuring-the-universe, orbits-and-gravity). None is "201", although the schema allows it (config.ts:107). Taking the union of all playlist demo slugs gives 14; the six that appear in zero playlist are cluster-census, doppler-shift, eos-lab, galaxy-rotation, hydrostatic-equilibrium-explorer and stars-zams-hr -- which is every ASTR201-only demo (eos-lab, hydrostatic-equilibrium-explorer, stars-zams-hr) plus the three heaviest inference demos. Only orbits-and-gravity ("mixed", use_case self-study) reaches past descriptive 101 content.
findings.scenario: An ASTR201 instructor opens For Instructors, reads "Curated sequences with timing, required/optional markers, and instructions", finds six sequences none of which targets their course, and the three demos written specifically for 201 are in none of them. They either hand-build a sequence with no prerequisite information (there is no prerequisites field in the schema) or they do not adopt. The 201 course redesign in docs/curriculum/astro-201-course-redesign.md has no playlist to point at.
findings.fix: Ship the four ASTR201 blocks in the sequence recommendation below as playlists with intended_level "201". Add `prerequisites: z.array(z.string()).default([])` to the demos schema and a build gate that fails a playlist whose step precedes one of its own prerequisites -- that single gate would also catch finding 11.

findings.title: Nothing a student submits carries a demo identifier, a timestamp or the parameters that produced it
findings.evidence: toCsv (lines 304-315) emits exactly one header line of column labels plus the rows: no demo slug, no timestamp, no parameter block, no name field. Line 670 calls it with `{ columns, rows: state.rows }` for the Copy CSV button, and the only other path is window.print() at line 677. There is no Blob or a.download anywhere in demoModes.ts, so there is no file to upload to an LMS. Challenge Mode results are never persisted: challengeEngine.ts exports only ChallengeResult/Challenge/ChallengeStats/ChallengeOptions types with no storage, and the only localStorage writes in the repo are the theme key (runtime/src/index.ts:92), eos-lab-toured, a seasons scrub hint and a retrograde onboarding flag. 8 demos have no Challenge Mode at all (blackbody-radiation, cluster-census, conservation-laws, em-spectrum, keplers-laws, parallax-distance, planetary-conjunctions, stars-zams-hr). `rg -ni 'lms|canvas module|turn in|submit|gradebook|scorm|lti'` over apps/site/src/content and pages finds no submission guidance of any kind.
findings.scenario: 30 students paste 30 CSV blocks into a Canvas text-entry assignment. Each block is a bare header plus rows -- no demo name, no date, no slider settings. The instructor cannot tell a galaxy-rotation table from a binary-orbits one, cannot verify a student used the assigned configuration, and cannot detect a table copied from a classmate. Challenge Mode, the only self-check, leaves no trace at all, so the one piece of evidence that a student engaged is unrecoverable.
findings.fix: Prepend a provenance block to the CSV: `# demo,<slug>` / `# exported,<ISO timestamp>` / `# parameters,<k=v;...>` / `# name,` (blank for the student to fill), and add a download button alongside Copy CSV using a Blob and a `<slug>-station-<date>.csv` filename. Have createDemoModes write the challenge summary (items attempted, items correct, timestamp) into the same CSV footer so the submitted artifact covers both modes.

findings.title: levels: [Both] on 16 of 20 demos while their objectives are major-level, so the level filter misleads
findings.evidence: Counting the levels field across all 20 demos: 16 are [Both], 3 are [ASTR201] (eos-lab, hydrostatic-equilibrium-explorer, stars-zams-hr) and exactly 1 is [ASTR101] (planetary-conjunctions -- which is also the one with no station card and no Station Mode). binary-orbits is [Both] with goals "Connect barycentric motion to spectroscopic observables through RV amplitudes $K_1$ and $K_2$" and "Relate circular-orbit energies ($K$, $U$, $E$) to separation scaling and virial balance". spectral-lines is [Both] and demands the Rydberg formula. retrograde-motion is [Both] and states "Identify stationary points as times when $d\\tilde{\\lambda}/dt = 0$". galaxy-rotation is [Both] and asks for baryon fraction reasoning. None of these is an introductory non-major objective, and no demo provides a 101 and a 201 variant of its goals.
findings.scenario: A gen-ed ASTR101 instructor filters Explore to ASTR101 and gets 17 of 20 demos, including virial balance, the Rydberg formula and a time derivative of apparent longitude. They assign binary-orbits to non-majors on the strength of the tag, and the exhibit page's stated learning goals are objectives their students cannot meet. The field that exists to prevent exactly this carries almost no information because [Both] is the default nobody revisited.
findings.fix: Split `learning_goals` into `goals_101` and `goals_201` (either may be empty) and derive `levels` from which arrays are non-empty, so the tag cannot disagree with the objectives. Write the 101 goals as the qualitative claim and the 201 goals as the quantitative one -- binary-orbits 101: "Explain why the lighter star moves faster around the barycentre"; 201: "Infer the mass ratio from $K_1$ and $K_2$ and compare to the model value".

findings.title: A demo required in three playlists states in its own frontmatter that it does not announce results to screen readers
findings.evidence: seasons.md readinessReason: "Close to ready: the day-night boundary is fixed and the page works on a phone. Still to come: announcing results to screen readers, and the direction Earth is drawn orbiting." seasons is `required: true` in astro-101-core-concepts, earth-sky-starters and solar-system-geometry (the lab playlist). angular-size.md and em-spectrum.md carry the same sentence; angular-size is required in solar-system-geometry and em-spectrum in light-and-measuring-the-universe. Surveying index.html, 14 of 20 demos have exactly one aria-live region and it is `id="status" class="cp-status" role="status" aria-live="polite"` -- the Copy results confirmation from the quality bar, not the readouts. Only cluster-census, keplers-laws, retrograde-motion, seasons, spectral-lines, eclipse-geometry, binary-orbits and eos-lab add a second live region, and in seasons it is a contextMessage, not the readout values.
findings.scenario: A screen-reader student is assigned the earth-sky-starters sequence. On seasons they tab to the day-of-year slider and press arrow keys. The drawing changes and the day-length and noon-altitude readouts update silently; the only thing their screen reader ever announces is "Copied results to clipboard". There is no non-visual path to the core observation the station card asks them to record, which makes a required graded step inaccessible. This is documented in the demo's own public copy, so it is a known gap being assigned anyway.
findings.fix: Wire each demo's primary readout group into a polite live region distinct from #status, debounced and phrased as a sentence ("Day length 14.2 hours, noon altitude 71 degrees"), and add a per-demo design-contract test asserting the readout container is a live region. Until then, mark seasons, angular-size and em-spectrum optional in the playlists and name the accommodation in the instructor bundle.

findings.title: The ASTR101 playlist teaches telescope resolution and Wien's law before wavelength is introduced
findings.evidence: The ordered demos array is moon-phases, seasons, eclipse-geometry, parallax-distance, telescope-resolution (required, 5th), blackbody-radiation (required, 6th), em-spectrum (optional, 7th), angular-size (optional, 8th), and the instructions say "Move in order through required demos first." telescope-resolution's physics is $\theta_{\min} = 1.22\lambda/D$ and its goal is "Connect resolution limits to diffraction qualitatively"; blackbody-radiation's goal is "Relate temperature to Planck-curve shape and Wien peak shift". Both require wavelength, which em-spectrum introduces ("Order EM bands by wavelength and frequency") and which is both optional and last. The project's own instructor-facing playlist light-and-measuring-the-universe.md puts em-spectrum first, so the two sequences contradict each other.
findings.scenario: A 101 instructor runs the required six in the stated order. At station 5 students are asked to connect aperture and wavelength to resolving power having never met wavelength as an ordered quantity; at station 6 they are asked which way the Planck peak moves with temperature on the same footing. The two demos most dependent on a prerequisite are placed before it, and the one that supplies it is marked optional, so a time-pressed class skips it entirely.
findings.fix: Reorder astro-101-core-concepts to moon-phases, seasons, eclipse-geometry, em-spectrum (promote to required), blackbody-radiation, angular-size, parallax-distance, telescope-resolution -- or split it into the four 50-minute modules in the sequence recommendation. Encode the edge em-spectrum -> {blackbody-radiation, telescope-resolution, spectral-lines} in a new prerequisites field and gate it.

findings.title: Instructor bundle tells instructors the demos work offline; there is no service worker or cache
findings.evidence: Line 22, under "Materials and setup": "Nothing to install and no login. Works offline once the page has loaded." `rg -ln 'serviceWorker|manifest.webmanifest'` over apps/site/src, apps/demos/src and packages returns only this same markdown file -- there is no service worker registration, no web app manifest and no cache strategy anywhere in the repo. The claim is narrowly true of an already-loaded tab (there are no external origins, so nothing fetches mid-session), and false for a reload, a new tab, a late-arriving student, or a second station device.
findings.scenario: An instructor reads this, plans a station rotation on a classroom network they know is unreliable, and tells students they can keep working if the wifi drops. The wifi drops during the rotation; every student who reloads, every pair that moves to a second device, and every student arriving at station 3 gets a browser error page. The activity stops.
findings.fix: Either narrow the sentence to what is true ("No install and no login. An open tab keeps working if the network drops, but loading a demo or reloading the page needs the network") or ship a small service worker that precaches the /play/<slug>/ bundle and a manifest, and then make the claim honestly. If the claim is kept, move it to a shared setup partial so it is written once rather than per bundle.

findings.title: An instructor cannot set a demo's configuration by link: 19 of 20 demos have no URL state
findings.evidence: `rg -ln 'location.search|URLSearchParams|history.replaceState|pushState'` across apps/demos/src and packages/runtime/src matches exactly one file, binary-orbits/main.ts, and the single use at line 388 is `debugPanel.hidden = !new URLSearchParams(window.location.search).has("debug")` -- a developer toggle, not demo state. No demo reads or writes parameters in the URL, and apps/site builds with output: "static" so query parameters never reach a server. Every station card therefore has to describe the setup in prose: moon-phases.md:14 "start at New -> First Quarter -> Full -> Third Quarter", parallax-distance/assessment.md:27 "set $d_{\\rm true}=10\\,\\mathrm{pc}$, capture A/B at $0^{\\circ}/180^{\\circ}$".
findings.scenario: An instructor wants all 30 students to start blackbody-radiation at the same temperature so the clicker item has one answer. There is no link that sets it. They read the settings aloud, students mis-set them, and the class answers a dozen different questions. The same gap blocks Canvas deep links with pre-set parameters, which docs/plans/next-session-learning-outcomes.md:60 listed as a deliverable, and blocks a student from sending their configuration back as evidence.
findings.fix: Add a serializer to @cosmic/runtime: read a compact `?p=` on load, write it with history.replaceState on change (debounced), and version the encoding. One implementation in createDemoModes covers all 20 demos. Then add a Copy link to this setup button next to Copy results, and replace the prose setup lines in station cards and assessment banks with links.

findings.title: Nine of 17 assessment banks give no answer key for any open-response item
findings.evidence: Counting 'answer key' per bank: 0 in blackbody-radiation, conservation-laws, doppler-shift, em-spectrum, galaxy-rotation, hydrostatic-equilibrium-explorer, parallax-distance, spectral-lines, telescope-resolution -- nine banks, including parallax-distance, the only launch-ready demo. Four of these are 48-line files (doppler-shift, galaxy-rotation, hydrostatic-equilibrium-explorer, spectral-lines) that give 'Correct:' letters for three clicker items and then list three short-answer checks and a three-part exit ticket with no expected response. Contrast retrograde-motion/assessment.md:86, which gives "Answer key (core ideas, roughly one point each)", and blackbody-radiation/backlog.md:25, which already names the gap: "Answer keys: add suggested 'ideal student responses' to the activities protocols to reduce TA variability."
findings.scenario: Two TAs grade the same spectral-lines exit ticket question ("Why does a hydrogen lamp show a few sharp colours?"). One accepts "because hydrogen only emits some colours"; the other requires quantised energy levels. Students in the two sections get different grades for the same answer, and neither TA can defend the line. With nine of 17 banks in this state, the open-response items -- the only ones that assess the stated objectives -- are effectively ungraded.
findings.fix: Add a one-to-three-sentence ideal response plus a 3-level band (complete / partial / misconception present) to every short-answer and exit-ticket item in the nine banks, copying the pattern at retrograde-motion/assessment.md:86-106. Then require the key in the assessments schema so a new bank cannot ship without one.

findings.title: Thirteen of 17 assessment banks do not say which misconception each distractor diagnoses
findings.evidence: Only four banks label their distractors: em-spectrum, parallax-distance, blackbody-radiation and telescope-resolution, each with 6 'Misconception targeted' lines. The other 13 give a stem, four options and a 'Correct:' letter with no diagnosis -- including moon-phases, seasons and eclipse-geometry, the three demos whose frontmatter misconceptions are the best-known ones in astronomy education. conservation-laws/assessment.md has only 2 items in total (two 'Answer:' marks), the thinnest bank in the repo, for a demo whose own objectives are the vaguest (see the next finding).
findings.scenario: An instructor runs the moon-phases clicker, 40 percent of the class picks option C, and the bank does not say what picking C means. They cannot tell whether those students hold the Earth's-shadow model, the quarter-means-a-quarter-lit model, or simply guessed, so the re-teach is generic. The clicker produces a score instead of a diagnosis, which is the whole reason to use clickers.
findings.fix: Add 'Misconception targeted:' to every distractor in the 13 banks, drawing on each demo's existing frontmatter misconceptions array so the item and the exhibit page agree. Make the field required in the assessments schema and assert that every demo's listed misconceptions appear as at least one labelled distractor -- that turns the misconceptions array from documentation into an assessment contract.

findings.title: Playlist estimated_minutes drifts from the demo times it should sum, and a 72-minute sequence is labelled a lecture activity
findings.evidence: I summed time_minutes for each playlist's steps. astro-101-core-concepts: stated 72, required 66, required+optional 86. earth-sky-starters: stated 45, required 32, with optional 42. planetary-conjunctions-starter: stated 25, required 8, with optional 20 -- three times the required demo's own time. Only orbits-and-gravity (50 = 50) and solar-system-geometry (50 = 50) match exactly; light-and-measuring is 58 against 56. estimated_minutes is hand-typed with no derivation or gate, and none of the figures includes the predict-writing and debrief time the instructions themselves require. astro-101-core-concepts is `use_case: "lecture"`.
findings.scenario: An instructor plans a single 50-minute period around "Astro 101 Core Concepts" because the page says 72 minutes and they assume they can trim. The six required demos alone are 66 minutes of demo time before any prediction writing or debrief, so the period ends at station 4 with no synthesis. For planetary-conjunctions-starter the error runs the other way: a 25-minute booking for 8 minutes of required work.
findings.fix: Compute the displayed time in playlists/[slug].astro as the sum of required step times plus an explicit per-step overhead (say 4 minutes for predict and record), show required and required+optional separately, and keep estimated_minutes only as a sanity check the build compares against. Then re-scope astro-101-core-concepts into the four 50-minute modules in the sequence recommendation rather than one 86-minute block called a lecture.
